features.summary: Lets a person browse the connectors they could add to AGI Workforce (Gmail-style apps and MCP servers), with name, publisher and state, then narrow the list by search text or category. Works on Web, the Electron Desktop (same hosted web UI) and Mobile. CLI has no catalogue. Today every connector shows as coming soon except 13 named ones.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows a paged list of connector records with name, publisher, description, badge (first-party, official, verified, community), category and a state label (Connected, Needs setup, Desktop and CLI, Not available yet, Coming soon). A search box and category chips narrow it server-side. (apps/web/app/api/connectors/directory/route.ts:50-113; apps/web/features/directory/services/connectors-directory.ts:256-310)
purpose.why_it_exists: A person cannot connect an app they cannot find. The Should lines in the brief require a signed-in user to browse, search and filter a catalogue (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/055-connector-setup-and-account-management.md S55.01-S55.03). docs/product/requirements.md section 16.7 lists Directory, Search and Categories as required connector features (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:1352-1360).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on Web, Desktop (Electron shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5) or Mobile who wants to add an app to the assistant. Support staff and testers use it to check what is offered.
problems_solved: Finding which apps can be connected without knowing the exact name (search matches name, publisher, tool names and description, in that rank order). (apps/web/app/api/connectors/directory/route.ts:31-49)

Hiding unchecked or risky listings: by default only first-party and hand-checked connectors are listed; money-moving connectors that are not hand-checked and non-first-party API-key connectors are excluded. (apps/web/lib/connectors/directory/listing.ts:75-100)
Telling the person why something cannot be connected yet (coming soon, needs setup, desktop only, plan upgrade). (apps/web/features/directory/services/connectors-directory.ts:256-269)
use_cases: A person opens Settings, then Connectors, types a tool name and picks the matching connector.
A person on Mobile taps a category chip to see only one category.
A person on a plan without connectors opens Connectors and sees an Upgrade notice instead of a connect button.
A tester checks that an unreleased connector shows Coming soon, not Connect.

established.statement: A signed-in user can browse a catalogue of connectors with each entry's name, publisher and state.
Typing in the search box narrows the catalogue by name, publisher, tools or description.
The catalogue can be filtered by category.
The product must include a directory, search and categories for connectors.
Unreleased connectors show as not available, not as connectable (the code enforces it).

acceptance_criteria: With the release state unchanged, searching for a connector not on the 13-id list shows it with Coming soon and no Connect action.
Searching for a tool name of a listed connector returns that connector.
Selecting a category chip returns only entries that carry that category and the chip list shows only categories that have entries.
With the directory call failing, the list shows an error notice with a retry, not an empty list (Mobile; Web needs a check, see unknowns).
A person on a plan without the connectors capability sees an Upgrade button and no Connect on unconnected entries.
Mobile in Local app mode shows a banner to switch to Cloud and no list.
inferred: [inferred] The directory data is public by design because the route sets public cache headers and reads no session, so the 'signed-in only' line is met by where the screen lives, not by the API.
[inferred] Search runs on the server, not on a loaded copy, because the UI sends the text in the request. The brief's phrase 'on the loaded catalogue' does not match the code.
proposed: [proposed] Show an explicit error notice on Web when the connected-state call fails instead of treating all as not connected.
[proposed] Add a CLI search over the directory (agi connectors search) if parity with the other apps is wanted.

steps.what_happens: Person opens Connectors; the Settings adapter loads the connected list, custom connectors and account state.
The directory panel asks GET /api/connectors/directory with search, badge, category, connectableOnly, sort, limit, cursor.
Server rate-limits the call, parses the query (400 INVALID_QUERY if invalid), reads the cached snapshot, filters, ranks and pages.
The snapshot itself is built from registries and probes ahead of time, not per request.
Client wraps entries with Connected and state labels and applies the release lock and plan lock.
On failure the server returns 503 CONNECTOR_DIRECTORY_UNAVAILABLE and logs 'Connector directory list failed'.

data.synced: Built on the server; clients only read pages

features.summary: One page per connector showing description, publisher, whether sign-in is needed, its tools, a plain-words sentence about read or write access, the six 'Before you connect' consent points and provider links. Web and Desktop show it fully; Mobile shows tools, access sentence and consent notes too; VS Code only a tooltip; CLI lists tools through MCP info.

Brief Should lines require the operation list, a plain read/write explanation and a data-retention explanation at connect time (doc: area brief S55.04, S55.05, S55.06, S55.28). established.statement: Selecting a connector opens a detail page with description, publisher, sign-in requirement, tools and links.
The page lists operations/tools before or after connecting.
Before connecting the user sees in plain language what the connector can read and change.
At connect time the product explains what connector data it stores and for how long.
Connector detail pages are part of the leader-matching connector set.

acceptance_criteria: Open a released connector on Web: description, publisher, Sign-in row and Tools list show.
Open an unconnected catalogued connector: the access sentence and the six consent points show before Connect.
Press Connect: a dialog 'Connect <name>?' with Allow and Deny appears before any redirect.
Open the same connector on Mobile: tool names, access sentence and 'Before you connect' notes show.
Open a connected connector on Web: the capabilities panel loads the live tool list or shows an error.
Open links under More info: each opens the provider page.
inferred: [inferred] The fifth consent point covers retention (chat-bound, deleted with the chat). A longer retention policy per provider is not shown.
[inferred] Per-tool read or write flag comes from the capabilities route (readOnly field) so it exists only after connecting.
proposed: [proposed] Show per-tool read/write badges before connecting using the directory record's tool names where annotations are known.
[proposed] Give VS Code a read-only detail panel or a link to the web detail page.

features.summary: Starts the real connection from a connector's page: either the provider's own sign-in (OAuth, with a consent dialog first) or an API key form whose key is tested against the service and stored encrypted. Built on Web, Desktop (opens the system browser), Mobile and, for own MCP servers, CLI. Currently refused for connectors not yet released.

purpose.what_it_does: Web: Connect posts to /api/connectors, which answers with the path for sign-in or for a key form; the client asks the person for consent, then goes to the provider and returns to Connectors. API key: the key is sent over HTTPS, tried against the server with a test call, sealed and saved. (apps/web/features/connectors/hooks/useConnectorsSettingsAdapter.tsx:757-870; apps/web/app/api/connectors/[connectorId]/credentials/route.ts:110-250)
purpose.why_it_exists: An assistant can only act in an app after the person authorizes it. The brief requires a real authorization or credential flow (doc: area brief S55.07-S55.09).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on a plan with connectors; admins for workspace-policy limits.
problems_solved: Safe token handling: tokens and keys are stored encrypted and never in plain text; if token storage is not configured the connect is refused with 503. (route.ts:420-430; credentials/route.ts:127-129)
Wrong keys: a rejected key gives '<service> rejected that API key.' and nothing is saved. (credentials/route.ts:160-175)
Forbidden connectors: the workspace policy, plan, release and email checks run before any credential is exchanged. (apps/web/lib/services/connector-policy-gate.ts:139-215)
use_cases: Connect a Notion-style connector with provider sign-in.
Paste an API key for a key-based MCP server and see how many tools were found.
Connect on Electron Desktop where the sign-in opens in the system browser.
Connect on Mobile with an in-app browser and return to the app.

established.statement: A Connect action starts the connector's real authorization or credential flow.
Connecting an OAuth provider opens the consent page and stores the returned grant.
An API-key connector offers a form, stores the key encrypted and connects.
Connect is checked against workspace connector policy before any credential is exchanged.
A reconnected connector does not resume the interrupted turn; the person asks again.

acceptance_criteria: Press Connect on a released OAuth connector: a consent dialog shows before leaving the app.
Press Deny in the dialog: no request to the provider is made and nothing is stored.
Decline on the provider page: the app returns to Connectors with status denied and no grant row.
Submit a wrong API key: error naming the service, no row saved.
Submit a correct key: the form shows connected and the tool count; a row exists with an encrypted credential.
With token storage disabled, Connect and key save answer 503 'token storage unavailable' text.
Connect a connector not released: refused with 'Connectors are coming soon.'
inferred: [inferred] The key is checked by an MCP connection and tool listing (probeMcpServer), not by a provider-specific auth ping.
[inferred] Cancelling in the system browser on Electron leaves the list unchanged because the list reloads only on focus.
proposed: [proposed] Let the CLI complete cloud connector sign-in with a device flow instead of printing a link.
[proposed] Name the 501 device-local connectors in the directory so people do not hit the refusal.

steps.what_happens: Person presses Connect; the client posts {connectorId, authType} with a CSRF token to /api/connectors.
Server checks CSRF, rate limit, workspace access, then the policy gate (release, email, plan, kill switch, workspace policy).
Server answers 409 with oauthStartPath or credentialsPath (or 501/503/403).
Client shows the consent dialog; on Allow it requests oauth/start?mode=json.
Start route re-checks region, token storage, workspace policy; creates state and PKCE verifier; stores a pending row; returns authorizeUrl.
Browser (or system browser on Electron) goes to the provider; person approves.
Provider redirects to the callback; our server consumes the pending row, exchanges the code at the provider, encrypts and stores tokens, writes an audit event.
API key path: our server probes the connector's MCP URL with the key as a header; on success seals and saves the key and caches tool names.

data.what: Pending authorization (state hash, code verifier, requested scopes)
data.retained_or_deleted: Consumed on callback; also deleted by cleanup (oauth-store.ts:57-70,285-292); TTL default unknown
Replaced on a new key; removal on connector removal not traced

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No language model takes part. Providers are the connector's own OAuth or key service. MCP discovery contacts the server's metadata endpoints (mcp-discovery.ts).

access_and_usage.account: Signed in account; unconfirmed email is refused with a message (connector-policy-gate.ts:100-125). Mobile needs Clerk sign-in and Cloud mode.
access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace connector policy (admin 'these connectors only') is checked at start, callback and key save. Org admin not needed to connect personally.
access_and_usage.subscription: Plan check inside the gate returns plan_upgrade_required with the upgrade message for tiers not in the connectors list (connector-policy-gate.ts:180-195; billing-catalog.ts:332-351).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Custom connector count and tool count limits by plan (assertCustomConnectorCapacity, assertConnectorToolCapacity; credentials/route.ts:154,184). Rate limit buckets on routes. No per-call metering at connect.
access_and_usage.flags: CONNECTOR_RELEASE_STATE and selective list; kill-switch canUseConnectors via connectorsAllowedWithoutRequest (connector-capability.ts:68-86).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: none found in the code.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Region refusal for sensitive-data connectors (route.ts:626-635). Providers with no registered OAuth app return 501 not configured (oauth/start/route.ts:317-325).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Cloud connectors need the cloud account on every app; on Mobile Local mode blocks the screen. CLI own MCP servers (agi mcp add/login) work on the device with the token in the OS credential store; whether they need any sign-in to AGI is unknown. No payment is tied to local inference in this feature.

features.summary: A workspace admin shares one of their own custom or key-based connectors so members can use its tools in chat without ever holding the credential. Built on Web (Sharing page and settings) and Desktop (same hosted web). The share route currently refuses while connectors are coming soon, and OAuth grants cannot be shared.

purpose.what_it_does: Admin picks one of their connectors under 'Shared connectors', presses 'Share connector with organization'; members then get that server's tools in chat under an id like orgmcp-<short id>, called by our server with the owner's stored credential. Unsharing stops member access. (apps/web/features/settings/sections/OrganizationSharingSection.tsx:533-660; apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:1682-1870)
purpose.why_it_exists: Teams should authorize an app once instead of every member holding a key. Brief S55.11 requires members to use it without holding the credential (doc: area brief).
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace admins and sharing managers share; members use.
problems_solved: Key sprawl: only the owner's sealed key exists. (user-connector-tools.ts:1687-1700)
Lost control: unshare removes access and evicts caches. ([connectorId]/route.ts:96-110)
Over-sharing: share needs a sharing manager and a quota check. (org-shared-connector-service.ts:118-150; [connectorId]/route.ts:45-52)
use_cases: Admin shares a team's internal MCP server with all members.
Member asks a question; the assistant calls the shared server.
Admin stops sharing; member's next call fails with 'no longer available'.

Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no sharing screen found.

established.statement: An organization admin authorizes a connector once and members use it without holding the credential.
Members have no approval-request flow; one account per connector.
Workspace connector policy must bind at the point of connection.

acceptance_criteria: Admin shares a connector: the list shows it with an orgmcp id.
A member's chat can call a tool of the shared connector; the member never sees the key in any response.
Admin unshares: the member's next call returns 'no longer available'.
A non-admin cannot call PUT or DELETE (refused by requireSharingManager).
A second share of the same connector does not create a duplicate (on conflict update).
Sharing a connector owned by another user fails (owned check).

purpose.what_it_does: Marks each connected row with a state: connected, needs-reauthorization or not-responding, and offers a call-based Connector health panel with Responding, Degraded, Not responding or Not called yet. purpose.why_it_exists: Connections expire or the provider fails; a person must see that and fix it without guessing. Brief S55.18, S55.20, S55.21 require health, reconnect and a test (doc: area brief). Decision D-2026-09-28-24 says reconnecting does not resume the turn (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:353-359).

steps.what_happens: Every connector tool call writes an outcome (ok, failed, blocked) with duration to the call log.
GET /api/connectors reads grants and the failed-call set, then sets health per row.
Client turns needs-reauthorization or not-responding into warning rows with Reconnect.
Before a tool call our server resolves the access token; near expiry it refreshes at the provider under a lock.
If refresh is impossible or rejected, the grant is revoked and a Reconnect notification is stored; the tool result tells the chat to ask for reconnect.
Reconnect on the client reruns connect: consent, oauth/start, provider, callback.
Health panel reads /api/connectors/health and shows state and latency.

features.summary: Disconnect removes a connected app (a connector) so the assistant can no longer use it. On the web service it destroys the stored sign-in, asks the provider to revoke the token, clears tool permissions and warns when the provider did not confirm. Web, Mobile and CLI each have a different confirmation step.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person end a connector. The server soft-revokes the stored grant (the row is marked revoked and both tokens are nulled), asks the provider to revoke the token where the provider offers revocation, clears the saved tool permissions, drops cached connection state and records an audit event (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:444, apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-store.ts:770, apps/web/app/api/connectors/route.ts:880).
purpose.why_it_exists: A connected app holds a long-lived token to the person's data. The person must be able to end that access, and ending it should also end it at the provider where possible. The product requirement says revocation prevents later tool use (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md W14).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on a plan that includes connectors who connected an app on Web, Desktop (Electron shows the hosted web app), Mobile (Cloud mode) or the CLI. Support staff also have a revoke-connector support action (test: apps/web/lib/support/actions/__tests__/revoke-connector.test.ts).
problems_solved: A token stays valid at the provider after the person stops using the app.
A person cannot tell whether the provider really revoked access, so the message names where to finish removal.
Stale tool permissions would silently apply again after reconnecting, so they are cleared and the person is told if that fails.
use_cases: Disconnect Notion from Settings, Connectors on the web because the work account changed.
Disconnect a connector from the Mobile detail screen after losing a phone.
Run agi connectors disconnect <id> in a terminal to remove a connector from the account.
Run agi mcp logout <name> to forget and revoke a local MCP server token on the device.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (Electron, hosted web): Settings, Connectors, open a connected connector, button 'Disconnect' (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/ConnectorDetailView.tsx:323, packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts:288).
Mobile: Connectors, open a connected connector, bottom button 'Disconnect' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/ConnectorDetailScreen.tsx:1177-1203).

CLI: 'agi connectors disconnect <connector>' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7392) for account connectors, and 'agi mcp logout <name>' / 'agi mcp remove <name>' for local MCP servers (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5368, 5384).
VS Code and Chrome: not available. The brief marks them n/a.
prerequisites: Signed in, and the connector is currently connected.
Mobile: Cloud mode must be active; the screen loads connections only when connectors are on, the person is signed in and Cloud mode is on (ConnectorDetailScreen.tsx:470-480).
CLI account command: capability and privacy checks pass; Local and own-key modes are refused with a message (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7378-7385, 2617).
screens_and_controls: Web detail header: a 'Disconnect' button next to the Connected state (ConnectorDetailView.tsx:323).

Web fallback table panel only: a 'Disconnect' button that asks 'Disconnect <name>?' with the text 'The assistant will no longer be able to use <name>. You can connect it again later.' (packages/ui/ui/src/settings-modal/SettingsModal.tsx:1092-1099).

Mobile: native alert titled 'Disconnect <name>?' with 'Cancel' and 'Disconnect' (destructive), text 'This removes the connection and its saved tool permissions from your AGI Cloud account.' (ConnectorDetailScreen.tsx:670-676).

CLI: prompt 'Disconnect <id> from your account? Its saved sign-in and tool permissions are removed, and every surface loses it until you connect it again.' with --yes to skip (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7394-7399).
journey: Open the connector's detail page.
Press Disconnect.

Web live panel: the request is sent at once, with no confirmation dialog (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/DirectoryPanel.tsx:549, test packages/ui/ui/src/directory/__tests__/DirectoryPanel.test.tsx:659-673). Mobile and CLI ask first.
The server revokes the grant, asks the provider to revoke, clears permissions and caches.
The connector leaves the connected list. If the provider did not confirm, a warning explains where to finish removal.
feedback_and_outputs: Web: a warning toast that stays until dismissed when the provider did not confirm (apps/web/features/connectors/hooks/use-connectors.ts:143-148). Text: 'Disconnected here, but <provider> did not confirm that it revoked access, so access may remain until you remove it at <manage link or in your <provider> account settings>.' (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:476-490).

Mobile: alert '<name> disconnected' with the notice, then the app returns to the connector list; failure shows 'Could not disconnect' / 'The connector is still connected.' (ConnectorDetailScreen.tsx:686-694).
CLI: 'Disconnected <id> from your account.' plus the notice; declining prints 'Left <id> connected.' (apps/cli/src/cloud/connectors.rs, apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7400).
CLI mcp logout prints one of three results: revoked at provider, provider offers no revocation endpoint, or provider did not confirm (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5372-5382).
settings: Use in chats switch per connector ('When off, AGI cannot use this connector in any chat.') is a softer alternative to disconnecting (apps/web/features/connectors/hooks/useConnectorsSettingsAdapter.tsx:89-90).
No setting changes Disconnect behaviour.

working: Web service DELETE /api/connectors?connectorId= handles OAuth grants, GitHub App installations, directory records and custom connectors, with CSRF, rate limit and workspace access gate (apps/web/app/api/connectors/route.ts:880-897).

Grant removal is atomic: rows are locked, then marked revoked with both tokens nulled, and only the locked rows are touched (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-store.ts:770-810). Pending authorizations are cancelled first (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:444-452).

Provider revocation is best effort and never throws: the result is revoked, nothing-to-revoke or not-revoked with reason and an optional manage link (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:284-296, 343-362); the manage link exists only for discovered MCP grants (oauth-access.ts:313-341).
Tool permissions are cleared and a failure is reported as a notice (route.ts:862-865); caches are evicted and the audit event connector_removed carries a vendor status (route.ts:915-933).
GitHub: the App installation is revoked at GitHub first; on failure the connector stays connected and the API answers 502 or 503 (route.ts:935-985).
Disconnect is not blocked by the connectors release switch: the DELETE handler checks only access and CSRF (route.ts:880-897) [inferred from reading the handler; no assertConnectorsReleased call].
Mobile: confirmation alert, then the shared client runtime DELETE (packages/client/client-runtime/src/connectors/runtime.ts:342-349; apps/mobile/services/connectors.ts:160).
CLI: agi connectors disconnect asks first, refuses to proceed non-interactively without --yes, and treats success false as an error (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2573-2600, apps/cli/src/cloud/connectors.rs).
CLI agi mcp logout revokes the stored token at the provider with a 30 second limit, then deletes the local token (apps/cli/src/mcp/mod.rs:1331-1375, crates/agiworkforce-mcp/src/oauth/flow.rs:786).
incomplete: The HTTP result carries only success and an optional vendorNotice string, so a client cannot tell 'revoked' from 'nothing to revoke'; both show no message (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:476-490, apps/web/features/connectors/hooks/use-connectors.ts:143-148). The brief expects the three outcomes to be reported.

Web and Desktop Disconnect has no confirmation in the live directory panel, although the fallback panel has one (DirectoryPanel.tsx:549 vs SettingsModal.tsx:1092). AGENTS.md section 9 requires the shared confirm primitive for an action the user cannot undo.
Mobile uses a native alert instead of the shared useConfirmAction primitive (ConnectorDetailScreen.tsx:670); acceptable on a native surface [inferred], but it is a different primitive.
agi mcp logout and agi mcp remove run without a confirmation prompt (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5368-5395).
disconnected_or_disabled: Internal Tauri desktop build: the connectors store calls the local command mcp_oauth_disconnect, which removes the local MCP server, local tokens and saved key and emits connector:disconnected; the lines read show no call to ask the provider to revoke (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sys/commands/mcp_oauth.rs:1521-1612, apps/desktop/src/stores/connectorsStore.ts:58). Tauri is retained internal code, not the public Desktop (AGENTS.md section 5).
Connectors are released only for 13 listed ids; the global state is coming_soon (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:12-27). Disconnect still works for rows that exist.
not_available: VS Code and Chrome: no disconnect control (brief marks n/a).

Disconnecting a single account of a connector: the store functions accept an account key but no route or screen passes one (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:444, apps/web/app/api/connectors/route.ts:880).

established.statement: Disconnect removes the stored grant and the connector is no longer available to the assistant.
Revoking removes the stored grant and asks the provider to revoke the token.
Revocation prevents subsequent tool use, and a revoked connector can be reconnected.
Revocation, policy changes and account switching must converge on every Cloud surface.
The connectors settings must include Disconnect/uninstall.
An action a user cannot undo asks first, names the consequence, and uses useConfirmAction in @agiworkforce/ui.

acceptance_criteria: Pressing Disconnect on web shows a confirmation that names what stops working before any request is sent.
After confirming, GET /api/connectors no longer lists the connector and the next chat turn cannot call its tools.
When the provider offers revocation, the grant row has revoked_at set and both token columns null.
When the provider does not confirm revocation, the person sees a notice that says where to remove access (manage link or account settings).
Saved tool permissions for the connector are gone after disconnect; if clearing fails the person is told.
Mobile and CLI ask before disconnecting; CLI without --yes and without a terminal refuses.
A GitHub disconnect that cannot revoke the App installation leaves the connector connected and shows the error.
inferred: The web result should report all three revocation outcomes, not only the failure one [inferred from brief S55.23].
Disconnect should work when connectors are switched off globally so people can always remove access [inferred from the handler having no release check].
proposed: [proposed] Route the web Disconnect through useConfirmAction in DirectoryPanel, using the wording already used in SettingsModal.
[proposed] Return the revocation status in the DELETE response and show 'Access revoked at <provider>' on success.
[proposed] Add a confirmation to agi mcp logout and agi mcp remove, or document why local token removal is exempt.
[proposed] Call the provider revocation endpoint from the Tauri disconnect path or document that the internal build skips it.

steps.what_happens: Person presses Disconnect; on web the hook sends DELETE /api/connectors?connectorId=<id> with a CSRF token.
Server checks sign-in, CSRF, rate limit and workspace access.
Server cancels pending authorizations, locks and soft-revokes the grant rows (tokens nulled), returning the captured tokens.
Server asks the provider's revocation endpoint to revoke each captured token; a refusal, timeout or missing endpoint is reported, not thrown.
Server evicts cached connections, purges cached MCP responses, deletes saved tool permissions and writes the audit event.
Response {success, vendorNotice?} returns; the client removes the row and shows a persistent warning if a notice came back.
CLI account path: after the prompt, the CLI sends the same DELETE to the service; the MCP path revokes at the provider from the device and deletes the local token.

aliases: agi mcp allow, ask, block, unset
features.summary: Each tool of a connected app can be set to Allow, Ask or Deny. The server checks that setting before every connector call. Tools are grouped as Read-only tools and Write and delete tools. There is no single read-only switch. Destructive tools always ask. Mobile uses per-tool controls and the label Block.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores a per-tool verdict per user and applies it in the chat tool loop: a Deny verdict blocks the call, Allow runs it, Ask pauses for approval. Group rows for read-only and write tools set a default for the whole group (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/connector-tool-permissions.ts:255-268, apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-call-gate.ts:68-137).
purpose.why_it_exists: A connector can change real data. People need to say which actions run unasked, which need approval and which never run, and the server must enforce that rather than trust the client. The product requires per-tool permissions (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 16.7).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people with connected apps on Web, Desktop (hosted web), Mobile; CLI users for local MCP servers.
problems_solved: Unwanted automatic writes or deletes.
Needing approval for every harmless read.
An injected instruction making the assistant send or delete data: destructive tools cannot be set to always run, and a saved Allow still asks for them.
use_cases: Deny all 'Write and delete tools' of a Gmail connector so it can only read.
Allow read-only tools of a project tracker so searches run without prompts.
Reset all permissions of a connector after a mistake.
On the CLI, block one tool of a local MCP server.

(apps/web/features/connectors/hooks/useConnectorsSettingsAdapter.tsx:96, 1242-1250). Opens a dialog titled '<name> - Tool Permissions'.

CLI: 'agi mcp allow|ask|block|unset <server> [tool]' for local MCP servers (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5320-5357).

VS Code and Chrome: not marked.
prerequisites: Connector connected. Web: 'Use in chats' switch on.
Mobile: Cloud mode active and signed in.
Tool list: the live catalog loads from the connector; if it fails, known tools are shown.
screens_and_controls: Web dialog: legend Allow ('Always run without asking'), Ask ('Needs approval each time'), Deny ('Never run this tool'); a group row per category with 'Allow all', 'Ask all', 'Deny all' (read-only and write); one row per tool with three buttons; 'Always asks: destructive' text on critical tools with Allow disabled; Recent calls log; 'Reset all to default' button (apps/web/features/connectors/components/ToolPermissionsPanel.tsx:52-100, 246-404).

Reset confirmation: 'Reset every tool permission?' with the sentence that unrecognised tools go back to asking and that the action cannot be undone; confirm label 'Reset permissions' (ToolPermissionsPanel.tsx:53-62).

Mobile: groups 'Read-only tools' and 'Write and delete tools', each tool row has Allow, Ask, Block and a per-tool reset button; no confirmation on reset, no group buttons (ConnectorDetailScreen.tsx:91-98, 120-123, 1086-1156).
CLI prints for example '<tool> now asks before it runs' and notes that managed rules come first (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5337-5357).
journey: Open the connector's tool permissions.
Wait for tool discovery (spinner 'Discovering connector tools').
Choose Allow, Ask or Deny for a tool or a group.
The choice is saved to the account at once; a spinner shows while saving and an error appears if it was not saved.
In chat the saved level is applied before the tool runs.
feedback_and_outputs: Pressed state on the chosen button (aria-pressed).
Error text 'That permission was not saved, so the assistant still follows the level shown here. Try again.' (apps/web/features/connectors/stores/tool-permissions-store.ts:31-32).

In chat: an approval request for Ask, and for Deny the tool result 'Tool is blocked by this account's connector permissions and was not executed' (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:4162-4166).
Mobile alerts 'Could not update permission' and 'Could not reset permission' (ConnectorDetailScreen.tsx:523, 547).
settings: Account default 'Tool approvals': options ask_every_time, auto_approve_read_only, autonomous (packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts:3-11). The default is ask_every_time; cloud accounts default to autonomous per CLOUD_ACCOUNT_DEFAULT_TOOL_APPROVAL_POLICY (line 13).
A workspace can forbid autonomous approvals (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-approval-policy.ts:29-37).
'Use in chats' switch per connector (useConnectorsSettingsAdapter.tsx:89).

working: Verdicts stored in connector_tool_permissions with levels always-allow, needs-approval, blocked, mapped to allow, ask, deny (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/connector-tool-permissions.ts:25-35); API GET, PUT, DELETE at /api/connectors/permissions with CSRF, rate limit and audit event connector_setting_changed (apps/web/app/api/connectors/permissions/route.ts:42-131).
Category rows read_only and write act as defaults for tools without their own row; an undeclared tool counts as a write tool (connector-tool-permissions.ts:255-268; tool-metadata.ts:876-904).

The gate is a ranked table: saved Deny first; saved Allow second (with the injection-risk escalation first); saved Ask; then the account default policy; manual approval; auto (tool-call-gate.ts:68-137). A denied tool returns a blocked result and is not run (tool-loop.ts:4162-4166).

A critical tool: Allow is refused by the API with 422 critical_tool_always_asks, a saved allow still asks at decision time, and the UI disables Allow (connector-tool-permissions.ts:45-80, 238-252; permissions/route.ts:96-105; ToolPermissionsPanel.tsx:96-98, 138-150).

Undeclared connector tools ask under every approval policy unless the person saved Allow for them; a saved Allow on an undeclared tool is stored (test: apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.permission-matrix.test.ts:190; apps/web/app/api/connectors/permissions/__tests__/route.test.ts:429).
Each save advances a permission generation and revokes conversation grants so a card shown earlier cannot restore an older choice (connector-tool-permissions.ts:84-87, 140-215).
Reset all calls DELETE on the server, with a confirmation through useConfirmAction (ToolPermissionsPanel.tsx:362-376, tool-permissions-store.ts:115).
Connector permissions are loaded only when the model supports tools (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-approval-policy.ts:84-99).
Lockdown mode denies every connector tool (connector-tool-permissions.ts:388).
Mobile edits the same account rows through the shared runtime (packages/client/client-runtime/src/connectors/runtime.ts:353-370).

CLI: per-server and per-tool allow, ask, deny rules in a user policy file; a workspace block beats a user allow; an MCP tool with no workspace root defaults to Ask (apps/cli/src/platform/policy/engine.rs:223-260, 376-430; apps/cli/src/agent/tools.rs:76-95).
incomplete: There is no single 'read-only mode' switch. The nearest control is Deny all on the 'Write and delete tools' group (web) [inferred]. Brief S55.26 lists web and desktop done, CLI missing.
The read-only grouping is based on built-in tool metadata only (apps/web/app/api/connectors/[connectorId]/capabilities/route.ts:93-94), so unknown tools sit in the write group.
Mobile labels the deny level 'Block', has per-tool controls only, and no confirmation before reset; web labels it 'Deny' (ConnectorDetailScreen.tsx:91-98).

The draft statement 'a tool the app does not recognise defaults to Ask even if set to Allow' is not what the code does: an explicit Allow for an undeclared tool is honoured; the code asks only when no verdict is saved, or the tool is critical, or injection escalation applies.
disconnected_or_disabled: Connectors are in coming_soon state with 13 released ids (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:12-27), so most connectors cannot be connected and have no permissions to edit.
not_available: CLI: no read and write grouping and no account-level connector permissions (account connectors are only listed and disconnected) (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7377-7408).
VS Code and Chrome: no tool permission panel found.
Internal Tauri desktop: no tool permission panel found in apps/desktop/src (searched by name).

established.statement: A connector can be set to read-only so its write operations are blocked (S55.26).
The user controls whether write actions run automatically, need approval, or are blocked (S55.27).
Connectors must include per-tool permissions.
Writes requiring approval cannot execute before that approval; source permissions and workspace policy apply to direct API calls too.
Reset is destructive and goes through the shared confirm primitive.

acceptance_criteria: Setting a tool to Deny makes the next call return the blocked result and nothing runs.
Setting a tool to Allow lets a non-critical tool run without a prompt; the same for a group default.
Trying to Allow a critical tool is refused with the reason shown and the tool still asks.
With no saved verdict and the default policy, every connector tool asks.
Reset all asks first and, once confirmed, deletes the server rows so tools ask again after reload.
The same saved levels appear on Web and Mobile for one account.
An account whose workspace forbids autonomous approvals cannot get skip-approval behaviour.
inferred: Deny on the write group should be explained in the UI as read-only mode [inferred from brief S55.26 and the category rows].
Mobile should offer group controls like the web [inferred from parity requirement, not stated in code].
proposed: [proposed] Add a one-tap 'Read only' control that sets Deny on the write group and shows it as a single state.
[proposed] Use the same label (Deny or Block) on every surface.
[proposed] Add confirmation to mobile per-tool reset and a reset-all.

steps.what_happens: Person opens Tool permissions; the panel fetches the connector's tool catalog and the saved verdicts.
Person picks a level; the store sends PUT /api/connectors/permissions (a category row and tool rows in chunks).
Server refuses an Allow for a critical tool, otherwise advances the generation, revokes conversation grants, upserts rows and records an audit event.
In a chat turn the server loads the user's verdicts (only when the model can call tools) and the approval policy.
When the model calls a connector tool, the gate resolves a verdict: deny blocks, allow runs, ask pauses for an approval card.
CLI: before a local MCP tool runs, the layered policy file decides; Ask opens an approval prompt on the device.

features.summary: The brief says a connector can be limited to chosen folders or repositories. The code read has no such chooser inside connector settings. What exists is narrower: GitHub reaches only repositories the GitHub App installation and the linking person can both see, and Google scopes limit file access. The CLI sandbox limits local server folders.

purpose.what_it_does: Intended: restrict what a connector can see to chosen folders or repositories. Found in code: repository access is decided on GitHub when the App is installed, then filtered to a verified list stored with the installation (apps/web/lib/github-install-app-return.ts:170-190, apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:360-405); file access for Google is capped by reviewed scopes (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/connector-scopes.ts:46-50, 242).
purpose.why_it_exists: Least privilege: an assistant that can read one project should not read a whole drive or every repository (doc: AGENTS.md section 6 minimum data).
purpose.who_uses_it: People connecting GitHub, Google Drive or similar apps, and CLI users running local file servers.
problems_solved: A member with access to one public repository must not link an organization's private repositories (migration comment in apps/web/db/neon/0188_github_installation_verified_repositories.sql).
Connectors asking for whole-drive access (forbidden scopes list in connector-scopes.ts:248-260).
use_cases: Install the GitHub App on two chosen repositories at GitHub; the assistant lists only those.
Pick files with the Google picker for a project instead of granting a full drive.
Start a local filesystem MCP server with chosen root folders in the CLI.

where_to_find_it: No control named for folder or repository selection exists in Settings, Connectors on Web, Desktop or Mobile in the files read (searched apps/web/features/connectors, apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors).
Web Code surface: chip 'Select repository' and link 'Manage repository access on GitHub' (apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts:143, 295).
Projects, Sources: a Google Drive picker for files (apps/web/features/projects/lib/google-drive-picker.ts).
CLI: the roots passed as arguments to a filesystem MCP server (apps/cli/src/mcp/mod.rs:654-700).
prerequisites: GitHub: connected through the GitHub App install flow and the Code surface available on the plan.
Drive picker: Google Drive connected and picker keys configured, otherwise status not-configured (apps/web/app/api/connectors/google-drive/picker/route.ts:25-33).
screens_and_controls: Code repository chip lists repositories from /api/github/repositories with search, a truncation notice 'More repositories exist. Search to narrow the list.' and the link to manage access at GitHub (apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts:285-295).

GitHub connector detail in connectors settings shows an On/Off switch for pull request review per installation, not a repository chooser (apps/web/features/connectors/hooks/useConnectorsSettingsAdapter.tsx:1197-1233).
journey: Install the GitHub App and choose repositories on GitHub (outside service).
Return to the product; the link step stores the repositories the person can reach.
In Code, choose a repository from the list; connector tools act only on those repositories.
feedback_and_outputs: Repository list with Private marker; messages 'Repositories could not be loaded.' and 'These installations could not be read:' (code-surface.ts:285-290).
Message 'This GitHub connection was made before repository access was checked. Reconnect it to list its repositories.' for old links (apps/web/lib/github-app.ts:665).
settings: None for folder or repository choice inside connector settings.

working: GitHub installations store verified_repositories and writable_repositories at link time; consumers use only that set, and NULL means list nothing (apps/web/db/neon/0188_github_installation_verified_repositories.sql, apps/web/db/neon/0413_github_installation_writable_repositories.sql, apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:360-405).
GitHub connector tools resolve the installation by the repository's full name against the verified set (apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:395-405).
Repository catalogue endpoint lists, searches and caps at 500 repositories (apps/web/app/api/github/repositories/route.ts:25-30).

Google Drive scope ceiling admits drive.file, drive.readonly and drive.metadata.readonly and forbids whole-drive scopes (connector-scopes.ts:46-50, 248-260); the picker route hands the signed-in person's token to the Google picker so they choose files (apps/web/app/api/connectors/google-drive/picker/route.ts).
CLI: a stdio filesystem server's chosen roots are the writable folders of its sandbox; every other directory argument is read-only (apps/cli/src/mcp/mod.rs:654-700).
incomplete: Which folder or repository a connector may use is not editable from connector settings after connecting; the GitHub choice is made at GitHub.

The Google picker belongs to Projects, not to connector limits; it does not restrict later connector calls [inferred from the route and its caller apps/web/features/projects/components/SourcesPanel.tsx].
disconnected_or_disabled: Connectors are in coming_soon state with 13 released ids (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:12-27); GitHub and Google Drive are not in that list, so they cannot be newly connected in the current release state.
not_available: Mobile: no folder or repository chooser found (brief says done; cited lines are connect handlers, apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/index.tsx:676).
Web connectors settings: the cited lines apps/web/app/api/connectors/route.ts:522 and useConnectorsSettingsAdapter.tsx:530 are connect and load code, not a chooser.
CLI: no per-connector limit for account connectors (brief: missing).

steps.what_happens: Person installs the GitHub App and chooses repositories on GitHub.
After return, the server asks GitHub which repositories the linking person can reach and stores lowercased owner/name lists on the installation row.

features.summary: When a chat tool needs a connector that is not connected, expired, or lacks a permission, the tool returns a marker that the app turns into a card that offers Connect or Reconnect and lists the scopes. Each connector step is labelled with the provider name. CLI prints a sign-in command.

purpose.what_it_does: Server tools answer with agi_connector_authorization_required, naming the connector, tool, reason (not_connected, authorization_expired, insufficient_scope, authorization_unavailable), a connect URL and scopes. Clients show a card with a Connect or Reconnect link and a Retry button (apps/web/lib/connectors/connect-required.ts:52-70, packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ConnectorConnectCard.tsx:15-40). Tool steps are labelled '<Provider> · <Tool>' (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/mcp-tool-name.ts:44-52).
purpose.why_it_exists: The assistant should not fail silently or invent data when a connector grant is missing; the person must see what to grant and where the data came from.
purpose.who_uses_it: People chatting on Web, Desktop (hosted web), Mobile and the CLI with connectors.
problems_solved: A task stops with a vague error when a token expired or lacks a scope.
People cannot tell which service supplied a fact.

CLI: the MCP transport returns an authorization fault with the challenged scope; the CLI stores it and tells the person to run agi mcp login.

features.summary: Reaching a service on a private network is allowed only on the CLI. Web refuses private or unsafe addresses for custom connectors. The CLI lets remote MCP servers on the LAN connect and lets a local server opt in to reach this computer's services with allowLocalNetwork. The internal Tauri desktop blocks private addresses.

purpose.what_it_does: Decides whether a connector may reach an address on a private network. Our web servers refuse private targets; the CLI on the user's own machine allows them, so a person can use an MCP server on their LAN or on localhost.
purpose.why_it_exists: A hosted service that fetched private addresses would be an attack path (SSRF) into our infrastructure, while a developer on their own machine legitimately needs local servers such as a database or Ollama.
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using the CLI with local or LAN MCP servers; web users who try to add a custom connector with a private URL and are refused.
problems_solved: Cloud servers must not reach private networks.
Local developer tools need to reach services on the same computer or LAN.
use_cases: Add a company LAN MCP server to the CLI.
Start a local database MCP server with allowLocalNetwork set so it can reach the database.
Try a private URL as a custom connector on the web and get a clear refusal.

where_to_find_it: CLI: 'agi mcp add <name> --url <url>' for a remote server; 'allowLocalNetwork' in a stdio server entry (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2128-2160, apps/cli/src/mcp/mod.rs:141-150).
Web and Desktop (hosted web): Settings, Connectors, 'Add custom connector' refuses private addresses (apps/web/lib/mcp-url-validation.ts:5-26).
Mobile and Chrome: no private-network control found.
VS Code: not marked.
prerequisites: CLI: nothing beyond a registered server; a project server asks for approval again when allowLocalNetwork is turned on (apps/cli/src/mcp/mod.rs:144-146).
Web: an https URL that resolves to a public address.
screens_and_controls: CLI launch approval shows '(it can reach services on this computer, such as databases and Docker)' when allowLocalNetwork is set (apps/cli/src/mcp/consent.rs:783-785).
Sandbox start hint names the options: sandbox false, allowLocalNetwork true, or the environment switch (apps/cli/src/mcp/mod.rs:718-727).
Web error text '<field> targets a private or unsafe network address' (apps/web/lib/mcp-url-validation.ts:19-21).
journey: CLI: register a server with agi mcp add (URL or command).
If it is a stdio server that needs local services, set allowLocalNetwork true in its entry and approve the launch.

Web: validation error text above.
settings: allowLocalNetwork (stdio server entry flag, default off).
sandbox flag per server and the MCP sandbox environment switch (apps/cli/src/mcp/mod.rs:722-726).

working: CLI remote MCP transports do not validate URLs by default: the knob validate_urls defaults to false so LAN servers stay reachable (crates/agiworkforce-mcp/src/config.rs:70-72, 99-100, 192); no CLI code sets it true (grep of apps/cli/src found none).
Cleartext http is refused for non-loopback hosts when credentials are sent (crates/agiworkforce-mcp/src/transport/http.rs:603-607, crates/agiworkforce-mcp/src/security.rs:80-100).
The OAuth flow always validates endpoints it fetches, anchored on the configured server URL (crates/agiworkforce-mcp/src/security.rs:1-9).
A sandboxed stdio server reaches only external addresses by default; allowLocalNetwork lets it reach loopback and Unix sockets (apps/cli/src/mcp/mod.rs:640-651).

Web custom connector URLs must be https, resolve to a public hostname and carry no embedded credentials (apps/web/lib/mcp-url-validation.ts:5-30); the egress policy also blocks private targets at tool execution (apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:1560-1570).

Internal Tauri desktop sets validate_urls true, so private and link-local addresses are blocked there (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/core/mcp/transport.rs:910; crates/agiworkforce-mcp/src/security.rs:14-70).
incomplete: There is no supported setup for a private network from the cloud (no tunnel, agent or relay found); CLI works only because it runs on the person's own machine.

Brief citations apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1337 and apps/cli/src/mcp/registry.rs:261 do not point at private-network code (lib.rs:1337 is a Projects subcommand region; registry.rs:261 is entry description code); the real code is listed above.
disconnected_or_disabled: Loopback is allowed by validate_server_url even when validation is on (security.rs:33, 53).
not_available: Web, Desktop (Electron), Mobile, Chrome: no private-network connector setup, by design of the egress policy.
VS Code: not marked.

established.statement: Where offered, a connector can reach services on a private network through a supported setup (S55.32).
Desktop egress funnels through egressGuard; Rust transports use the host-owned egress policy.
Security behavior fails closed; validate at trust boundaries.

acceptance_criteria: On web, a custom connector URL with a private IP or a name that resolves to one is refused and not saved.
On web, an http URL is refused.
On the CLI, a remote MCP server at a private LAN address connects.
On the CLI, a stdio server without allowLocalNetwork cannot reach loopback services inside the sandbox; with it, it can.
Turning on allowLocalNetwork for a project server asks for approval again.
The internal Tauri build refuses a private address.
inferred: The product treats 'private network' as the user's own machine and LAN reachable only from the CLI; no other supported setup exists [inferred from code search].
The CLI default of not validating URLs is deliberate for LAN use (comment in security.rs:3-6).
proposed: [proposed] State in the CLI docs and in agi mcp add output that LAN addresses are allowed.
[proposed] If cloud connectors to private services are wanted, design a device-side bridge with consent rather than loosening the egress policy.

features.summary: Lets the assistant search, read, draft and send email in a connected Gmail or Outlook account from chat. Sends and drafts wait for approval. The code is complete on the server, but Gmail and Outlook are not released (connectors are 'coming soon'), so no app can use it until that changes.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the chat assistant mail tools. For Gmail it uses Google's hosted mail server (search_threads, get_thread, get_message, list_drafts, create_draft) plus three AGI tools: send_draft, read_attachments and create_draft_with_attachments. For Outlook it uses a built-in Microsoft Graph adapter with search_mail, read_mail and send_mail. purpose.who_uses_it: People on a paid plan who connect a mailbox on the web app and then ask for mail help in chat on any app. [code] (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:351)

Writing a reply or new mail as a draft the person can review in their own mailbox
Reading what a PDF or Office attachment says without opening it

established.statement: With an email account connected, the assistant can search the mailbox by sender or subject and return matching messages.
The assistant can open and read the full content of a specific email or thread.
The assistant can create a draft (new or reply) in the connected mailbox for the user to review.
The assistant can send an email from the connected account, after approval.
The assistant can read attachments on an email and attach files when composing.
Labels and folders: not applicable on any app.
gmail.send sends a draft after the user approves that specific send; gmail.compose creates drafts the user reviews.
send_draft is a non-reversible external send that asks under every approval policy.
Gmail public readiness must not be claimed from offline tests; the real consent, read and draft journeys must pass on the review build first.

acceptance_criteria: With Gmail released, configured and connected on a paid plan in Cloud mode, 'find the last email from X' runs search_threads and the answer matches the real mailbox.
Asking for a draft shows an approval prompt naming the action; after Allow, the draft appears in Gmail Drafts with the right recipient, subject and body, and nothing is sent.

Asking to send always shows an approval prompt, even with 'Skip approvals' and even after 'Always allow' was set on other tools; refusing it sends nothing and the assistant does not claim the mail was sent.
With an expired or revoked grant, the chat shows a Reconnect card and the assistant does not claim success.
With no Gmail connected, no Gmail tool runs and the assistant does not invent mail.
A draft with a file the user did not own is refused with 'is not a file in this account.'
On a model whose provider may train on inputs, Gmail tools are withheld and the chat tells the user to pick another model.

Per-plan limits for mail actions do not exist beyond the paid-plan gate and the connector tool count ceiling. [code] (apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:2441) [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Declare tool metadata for Gmail's label tools or hide them from the catalog, so a failing tool is not offered.
[proposed] Add an Outlook draft tool after the owner decides on Mail.ReadWrite.
[proposed] Show the full recipient list and body in the approval card for every mail write on every app.

steps.what_happens: The person types the request in chat on the app; the app sends the turn to our servers.
The server checks release, paid plan and the connectors kill switch for the turn; if any fails no connector tools are offered.
The server builds the tool list: Google's hosted mail tools plus the three AGI mail tools, but only for a connected, released Gmail and only if the turn is limited to no-training models.
The chosen model decides to call a tool; the gate allows, asks or denies using saved levels, approval policy and tool metadata.
For 'ask', the app shows the approval prompt and posts the decision back; CLI prompts in the terminal.
Google's hosted tools run on Google's server with the user's token; the three AGI tools call the Gmail API directly with a 20 second timeout and no redirects.
The result is fenced as untrusted, returned to the model, the conversation is marked as holding Google data, and the step shows on the device.

steps.what_happens: The person types a request in chat on web, mobile, Chrome, CLI or VS Code. Desktop shows the web app.
The client sends a Cloud chat turn to AGI's chat endpoint.
The server checks the plan, the release state and the operator kill switch.
The server loads the saved per-tool permissions and the account approval policy.
The server asks each connected, released vendor MCP server for its tools using the person's stored token, then trims to the plan's tool limit.
The model picks a tool. The server checks the gate; an undeclared tool needs approval, so the run pauses and the client shows an approval card.
The person decides on the device; the decision is sent to the approve endpoint.
The server calls the vendor MCP server; the vendor creates or reads the record.

aliases: Code, pull requests, CI and deployments
features.summary: Lets the assistant search code, read and review pull requests, report CI status and view or start deployments. It works two ways: through hosted connectors in a Cloud turn (GitHub App adapter, pinned GitHub MCP server, Vercel MCP server, all unreleased today), and through the local GitHub CLI on the coding apps (CLI review command, VS Code review and create commands).

purpose.what_it_does: On hosted surfaces the assistant fetches a pull request diff, posts an issue comment or a pull request review through a GitHub App installation, and can use the pinned GitHub MCP server and Vercel MCP server for search, status, logs and deploys. On the coding apps, the CLI reviews a pull request with the local gh tool, reads review threads and failing checks, and VS Code starts a review prompt or opens a pull request.
purpose.why_it_exists: Developers want review help, build status and deploy control inside the assistant, as Claude and ChatGPT offer (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md, D-2026-09-28-08).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers on a paid managed plan for hosted connectors; any CLI or VS Code user who has the GitHub CLI installed and signed in for the local path.
problems_solved: Reading a long diff and writing review notes by hand.
Finding out why a build failed without opening the CI site.
Checking or starting a deployment from chat.
use_cases: Run `agi review --pr 128 --post` to review a pull request and post the result.
In the CLI use /pr-comments to read review threads and failing checks, or /autofix-pr to fix them.
In VS Code run 'Code: Review a Pull Request' with a number or branch.
In a Cloud chat, ask the assistant to read a pull request diff or comment on an issue after approving.

features.summary: Meant to let the assistant query a connected database, analyse a Snowflake or Databricks warehouse added by account URL, and create a dashboard in an analytics tool, all through vendor MCP servers in a Cloud turn. Today none of these connectors is in the released list, custom connectors are blocked by the release gate, and no read-only guard for queries exists in the code read.

purpose.what_it_does: Database and warehouse vendors publish MCP servers with query tools. AGI connects to them with the person's sign-in, offers their tools to the model and asks for approval before calls. Snowflake and Databricks are added by pasting the account's MCP server URL, because each account has its own address (apps/web/lib/connectors/account-url-connectors.ts:10-31).
purpose.why_it_exists: Analysts and developers want answers from their data inside chat. The founder decision says Snowflake and Databricks are added by account URL, and the Google-hosted BigQuery server is not pinned because it needs a broader scope than the read-only ceiling (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md, D-2026-09-28-08).
purpose.who_uses_it: Analysts, developers and data teams on a paid managed plan.
problems_solved: Copying SQL results into chat by hand.
Hunting for the right warehouse endpoint format.
Letting a model touch data without a human check.
use_cases: Ask a question; the assistant runs a query through a database MCP server and shows the table.
Add a Snowflake MCP server URL and ask about sales by region.

steps.what_happens: The person adds the warehouse by URL in Connectors; the browser or phone sends it to AGI.
The server validates host suffix and path and stores the encrypted connection.
In a chat turn the server dials the vendor MCP server and lists its tools, only if the connector is released and the host approved.
The model proposes a query; the run pauses for approval on the device.
The vendor runs the query on the person's warehouse and returns rows.
The server fences the result and gives it to the model, which writes the answer.

steps.what_happens: Bank link: the person opens Plaid Link in the browser (web) or an in-app browser (mobile, hidden).
AGI exchanges the public token with Plaid, encrypts the access token and saves a bank item.
In a chat turn, bank tools are added only if released, granted, Plaid is configured and the turn is not from mobile.
The model calls a bank tool; AGI asks Plaid for balances or transactions now, per bank, skipping excluded accounts.
The text is fenced as untrusted bank data and returned to the model.
Phone: the Cloud run emits a device-step-requested event for the phone's device id; the phone checks the id, asks OS permission, reads or writes the calendar and returns the result.
The result goes back to the run so the model can answer.

The directory lists some vendors, but the release gate keeps them off, and the messaging catalog entries cannot be connected. Native messaging code was not found.

purpose.what_it_does: Nothing is promised to users yet. The aim is for the assistant to retrieve licensed research, look up products, make bookings, control media and read or send messages through connected services.
purpose.why_it_exists: ChatGPT and Claude are moving toward consumer actions; the brief lists these as wave 3 items that are not built (doc: audit/partial/056-concrete-integration-families.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: No one today. Intended for consumers on paid managed plans.
problems_solved: Not applicable yet.
Future: ordering, booking and messaging from chat.
Future: reading licensed research the user already pays for.
use_cases: Future: 'book a table for two on Friday'.
Future: 'play my focus playlist'.
Future: 'send this to Sam on WhatsApp'.
Future: 'summarise the licensed report I have access to'.

features.summary: The assistant can search the web for current facts, open one page it found, and read PDF or Office files. Searches and pages show as cards with their sources. Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome use the AGI server; CLI and VS Code use the CLI's own search with the user's key or Managed mode.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the model two tools. web_search returns up to 5 titled, linked snippets for a query. url_fetch (web_fetch in the CLI) downloads one page and returns its readable text. The server version also extracts text from PDF and Office files, but the prompt that tells the model so is not live yet. Results are shown as sources under the answer. [inferred from] (apps/web/lib/web-search/web-search-tool.ts:54) (apps/web/lib/url-fetch/url-fetch-tool.ts:501) (apps/web/lib/prompts/prompt-manifest.ts:282)
purpose.why_it_exists: A model's training data is old. Looking things up lets it answer about recent events and cite what it read, so the person can check it. (doc: docs/product/definition.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone chatting on Web, Desktop, Mobile or the Chrome extension; developers using the CLI or VS Code; API callers.
problems_solved: Stale or invented facts
No way to check where an answer came from
Needing to open a cited PDF or Word file by hand
use_cases: Ask for today's news on a topic and see the search and its sources.
Paste a web address and ask for a summary of that page.
Ask the CLI to look up a library's current docs while coding.
Ask about a cited PDF report and have the assistant read it (server code reads it; the model is not yet told it can).

steps.what_happens: The app sends the chat turn to the AGI completions endpoint with web search enabled (Mobile sets web_search and web_fetch flags).
The server decides which tools to offer, then the model asks for web_search.
The server checks the per-turn budget (3, or 10 in AGI Work) and withholds a repeated query.
The server decides how the call is paid: Free plan counts against 20 per 30 days; paid plans and automated callers (API, CLI, VS Code, AGI Work, research, scheduled) are charged to credits.
The server calls the search provider and gets results.
Results are wrapped as untrusted content, turned into sources, and sent to the model and to the client as cards.
url_fetch downloads one page through a guarded fetch, extracts text or PDF or Office text, and returns up to 20,000 characters.
In the CLI, the search runs from the person's machine with their own Brave or Tavily key; in Managed mode AGI runs the search.

data.what: Tool results over the cap are stored in full and replaced by a reference

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The search itself is done by a separate search provider (Perplexity in the registry), not by the chat model, so any model that can call tools can use it. Some providers also offer native search that the server collects and shows the same way. The Composer turns web search off when the selected model has no honest search path (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:1690). In the CLI the chat model is independent of the Brave or Tavily key.

access_and_usage.account: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome and API need a signed-in account to reach the server. CLI own-key mode needs no AGI account for search (own Brave or Tavily key) [inferred from mod.rs:420].
access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace website allow and deny rules filter sources and fetches (apps/web/lib/web-search/web-search-tool.ts:116-130). CLI fetch follows only hosts the user approved for redirects (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/web/mod.rs:200).
access_and_usage.subscription: Free plan: 20 searches per rolling 30 days; other plans and automated callers are charged to credits (apps/web/lib/web-search/search-budget.ts:32, :133-143). Whether any paid plan name has a search ceiling: none found in the files read.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: 5 results per call, 15 s per call, 3 searches per turn (10 AGI Work), 5 fetches (15 AGI Work), 10 s per fetch, 20,000 characters of page text (cites above). Billing key space is search:<requestId>:<call> (apps/web/lib/web-search/search-budget.ts:~170).
access_and_usage.flags: Tool description version 2 is on the internal channel (routing-policies.json:157-163). Search kill switches: none read; a general capability gate exists (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:543-545) (unknown whether search is covered).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Needs a tool-capable model for web_search, or a model with native search. The composer turns search off otherwise (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1690).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Server search uses one provider registered in web-search-providers.json; native search depends on the model provider. CLI supports Brave and Tavily only (mod.rs:444-448).
access_and_usage.local_mode: CLI: web_search, web_fetch and browser tools are refused in Local privacy mode with a message to create an explicit BYOK or Managed continuation (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs:725-737). Mobile on-device chat: no search wiring found (unknown). Desktop local models: unknown.

features.summary: The assistant can find, read, write and edit files. On Desktop it works inside a folder the person granted, through device steps. In the CLI and VS Code it works in the project folder. On Web, Mobile and Chrome it works in a cloud sandbox that is switched off today. Web also searches the person's uploaded files.

purpose.what_it_does: Provides four jobs. Search: find files by name or by text. Read: return a file's text. Write: create or replace a file. Edit: replace one exact passage without rewriting the file. There are three families: server file search over uploaded files and project knowledge (search_files, open_file), device steps on the Desktop's granted folders (device_*), CLI tools (read_file, write_file, edit_file, glob, grep), and cloud sandbox tools (read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_files) that need the sandbox switch. (apps/web/lib/server/tools/file-search-tool.ts:64) (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/device-steps.ts:131-165) (apps/web/lib/e2b/execution-tools.ts:14-19)
purpose.why_it_exists: Work on documents and code needs the assistant to touch real files, with the person in control of which folder it may reach. (doc: docs/product/definition.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop users with a granted folder, developers in the CLI and VS Code, Web users asking about files they uploaded, and later Web, Mobile and Chrome users once the sandbox is on.

steps.what_happens: The Desktop shell declares its granted folders and capabilities in a request header; only the desktop and mobile surfaces are believed.
The server offers only the device tools the declaration allows (no folder, no workspace tools).
The model calls a device tool; the server plans the step, pauses the turn and sends x_device_step_request back to the app.
The Desktop runtime checks the capability, may prompt, and performs the read, write, edit, glob or grep inside the folder.
The result (up to 24,000 characters) returns to the server and the turn resumes.
Sandbox path: tool call goes to a cloud sandbox from an outside provider after the policy and switch checks.
CLI path: the CLI reads or edits files on the person's machine after permission checks.

The sandbox tools replace provider-native code tools so any model can use them (apps/web/lib/e2b/execution-tools.ts:1-9). The sandbox itself is an outside provider; its name is hidden from users by a redaction function (apps/web/lib/e2b/execution-tools.ts:278-284).

features.summary: The assistant can run code or a shell command and show the output. Desktop runs commands in a granted folder after the person approves each one. CLI and VS Code run them locally. Web, Mobile and Chrome run code in a cloud sandbox, which production has not switched on; Mobile and Chrome have no shell.

steps.what_happens: The app asks for code execution on the turn (Web/Mobile send code_execution true when allowed).
The server resolves which execution tools exist: sandbox tools if ready and streaming, else provider-native code tool, else it marks the turn unavailable and tells the model.
A hold for the likely cost is reserved before the turn.
On a call, the server checks the sandbox switch and the account policy, then runs the code in the cloud sandbox.
Output is capped at 100,000 bytes, vendor names are replaced by 'sandbox', and an overflow copy is stored.
Desktop shell: the server hands the step back; the desktop asks the person to approve the exact command, runs it in the folder and returns output and exit code.
CLI shell: the CLI checks saved permissions, workspace policy and approval, then runs the command locally.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Any model that can call tools can use the sandbox tools; some provider routes use their own code tool when the sandbox is off (anthropic, google, openai) (apps/web/lib/e2b/execution-tools.ts:216-235). The model decides the code; the sandbox is an outside compute provider whose name is redacted from user text. Desktop and CLI shell are independent of the model.

features.summary: The assistant can drive the person's paired Chrome browser (open, click, type, read, screenshot) and, on Desktop, see and control the whole screen after the person grants it. CLI and VS Code can drive the browser through the CLI bridge; Chrome has its own steps. Web and Mobile cannot.

purpose.what_it_does: Provides browser steps (read page, navigate, click, type, screenshot, download, console, network) and screen steps (screenshot, zoom, move, click, drag, scroll, type, key, wait, open app). Browser steps go through the Chrome extension paired to the Desktop; screen steps use the desktop runtime. (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/device-steps.ts:21-60, :214-262) (apps/desktop/electron/browser/browserSteps.ts:19, :75)
purpose.why_it_exists: Many tasks live in web pages and apps with no API. Controlling them lets the assistant finish those tasks while the person stays able to stop it.
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop users, CLI and VS Code developers, Chrome extension users.
problems_solved: Repeating clicks and form entry
Testing a web app by looking at its console and network
Working in apps with no connector
use_cases: Ask Desktop to open a page and read its text.
Ask the assistant to fill a form in the signed-in browser.
Ask it to open Notes and type a list on the Mac.
Ask the CLI to check a page's console errors during a test.

steps.what_happens: The Desktop declares its granted capabilities; the server offers only those tools.
The model calls a device tool; the server validates arguments against limits and plans the step; risky steps get a review sentence.
The turn pauses and sends x_device_step_request to the app.
The app asks the desktop runtime, which prompts the person where required and runs the step.
Browser steps go to the paired Chrome extension, whose reported address is checked against workspace rules.
The result (text or a screenshot, up to 24,000 characters of text) returns and the turn resumes.
An audit event records the tool and its status (not content).

steps.what_happens: The server decides at request time whether to offer the image tools: surface, plan, storage and default provider must all be ready.
The model calls generate_image or edit_image.
The server checks that the user's message asked for a picture and for an edit that a source image exists.
The server runs the image pipeline with the image provider, which is an outside service, using account credits.
The image is saved to the person's Library and an image card is returned.
The app renders the card in the transcript.
CLI: the CLI sends the prompt to the person's AGI account and saves files in the working folder.
