features.summary: The product turns an uploaded audio file into text through an API endpoint. There is no chat tool for transcription and none for speech. A separate read-aloud endpoint turns text into speech, but the model cannot call it. Dictation in the composer reuses the same transcription handler and is outside this area.

purpose.what_it_does: Accepts a multipart upload (field file, optional model and language), checks account, plan, spend and file rules, sends the audio to one transcription provider and returns the text. The same handler also serves composer dictation. Speech generation is not offered to the model as a tool; a read-aloud endpoint exists for the apps (apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts:40-48,102).
purpose.why_it_exists: Developers who use the AGI API with an API key, and the first-party apps, need speech to text with the same entitlement, quota and spend rules as chat. The brief asks for a transcription endpoint beyond composer dictation (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/057-tool-catalog-and-invocation-experience.md S57.19).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers calling the API with an API key or a session token, and the web and phone apps through the dictation route (apps/web/app/api/voice/transcribe/route.ts:10,29).
problems_solved: Getting text from a recording without running a model locally.
Charging and limiting speech to text through the same subscription and credit system as chat.
Rejecting files that are not audio before any provider spend.
use_cases: A developer posts a recording with an API key and gets the transcript back.
A signed-in person dictates into the web composer, which calls the dictation route that reuses this handler.
A Free-plan person uses the free voice allowance for dictation (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:594,624-660).

where_to_find_it: API: POST /api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions, listed in apps/web/public/openapi.json under Inference (apps/web/public/openapi.json:2662-2665).
Web and Desktop (hosted web app in Electron): no visible tool card; transcription is reached only through dictation in the composer, which is outside this area.
Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no transcription tool card found. Whether each one calls the dictation route is unknown (only apps/web files matched a search for the audio path).
Read aloud: Web uses apps/web/lib/hooks/useTTS.ts:10 and Mobile uses apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/serverSpeech.ts:10, both on /api/voice/speech.
prerequisites: A signed-in account or an API key with the inference:write scope (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:297; apps/web/public/openapi.json:2675).
Audio no larger than 25 MB in an accepted audio type (route.ts:398-411).
Adult eligibility for non-API-key callers (route.ts:307-312).
screens_and_controls: No chat screen or tool card exists for transcription or speech generation (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/057-tool-catalog-and-invocation-experience.md S57.19, S57.20).
The API takes file, model and language form fields (apps/web/public/openapi.json:2683-2695).
journey: 1. The caller sends a multipart POST with the audio file.
2. The server checks CSRF, rate limit, identity, spend and policy gates.
3. The server checks size, type and the first bytes of the file.
4. The server reserves credit, or grants free voice seconds on a Free plan.
5. The audio goes to the transcription provider.
6. The server settles the cost and returns the transcript.
feedback_and_outputs: On success the OpenAI-style transcription response (openapi lists 200 'Transcription').
Errors: 400 missing file, 413 over 25 MB, 415 unsupported type or non-audio bytes (route.ts:380-460), 429 rate limited (apps/web/public/openapi.json:2745-2760).
settings: Admission is by plan and workspace policy; there is no per-user setting for this endpoint found.

The model field is honoured only if it is a live speech-to-text model of the one provider; otherwise the default slot voice_transcription is used (route.ts:520-529; apps/web/public/openapi.json:2688-2691).

working: Transcription endpoint with rate limit, CSRF, API-key scope, spend gate, org policy gate, size and type checks, content sniff and upload scan (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:288-480).
Credit reservation and settlement for paid plans; free voice allowance grant for Free plan (route.ts:594-660,780-815).
Dictation route reuses the same handler (apps/web/app/api/voice/transcribe/route.ts:10,29).
Read-aloud speech endpoint with a 4,000 character cap, voice and speed fields (apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts:40-48).
incomplete: Transcription is pinned to a single provider; the code throws if the voice_transcription slot is not that provider's speech-to-text model (route.ts:500-505). Provider agnosticism does not apply here.
disconnected_or_disabled: Speech generation is not connected as a model tool on any app; the read-aloud endpoint is not under /api/llm/v1 (no speech route found in that folder listing: audio, chat, credits, embeddings, models).
not_available: Transcription chat tool card: not available on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome (brief S57.19 lists api only).
Speech generation tool: not applicable on every app (brief S57.20).

steps.what_happens: The caller uploads the audio with a CSRF token or API key; rate limit and identity are checked.
Spend, adult-eligibility, managed-compute and workspace policy gates run before the body is read.
Size, MIME type, first-byte sniff and an upload scan run on the bytes.
Credit is reserved (paid) or free voice seconds are granted (Free plan).
The audio is forwarded to the transcription provider and dropped; nothing stores it.
Usage is settled from provider token counts or the estimate, and a log line is written.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: One provider only: the voice_transcription slot must resolve to that provider's speech-to-text model or the handler throws (route.ts:500-505). A caller may name a live speech-to-text model of that provider; anything else falls back to the slot default (apps/web/public/openapi.json:2688-2691). The provider's training policy is checked against the person's privacy setting (route.ts:506-518). Read-aloud speech uses the voice_speech slot (apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts:102).

access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace policy gate for provider, model and feature audio_transcription (route.ts:333-352). Spend limit gate (route.ts:355).
access_and_usage.subscription: Managed compute access is evaluated against the subscription (route.ts:574-586). A developer API key on the Free plan is refused (route.test.ts:423).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: 25 MB cap; credit reservation by estimated audio seconds; voice_minutes tier allowance for paid plans; free voice allowance seconds on Free (route.ts:594-660). Rate limit bucket audio-transcription (route.ts:294).
access_and_usage.flags: Dictation route has a kill switch test (apps/web/app/api/voice/transcribe/__tests__/route.kill-switch.test.ts); the flag name is unknown.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Only the provider's live speech-to-text models; other model ids fall back to the default.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: One provider; refused when privacy settings keep content away from providers that may train (route.ts:506-518).
access_and_usage.local_mode: The handler is a server endpoint, so it is Cloud only. No on-device transcription path was opened in this area; unknown whether Mobile or Desktop dictation has a local alternative (see SYS-voice-and-media).

features.summary: The assistant can save, search and forget remembered facts, and create scheduled tasks. In the hosted chat route these are three memory tools and one create_schedule tool, offered only when the message asks for them. The CLI and VS Code use their own file-based memory tool and cron tools that act on the signed-in account.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a model save one fact about the person, search saved facts, delete saved facts after approval, and create a scheduled task with a name, prompt and repeat rule. In the CLI and VS Code the schedule tools also list and delete (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs:839-880).
purpose.why_it_exists: So a person can say remember this, forget this, or run this every morning, in chat, without opening Memory or Schedules screens.
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people on Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome through the hosted route; CLI and VS Code users through the CLI tools.
problems_solved: Keeping lasting preferences across chats.
Removing a remembered fact on request, with consent.
Turning a chat request into an unattended recurring task.
use_cases: Say 'remember that I prefer short answers' and the assistant saves one sentence.
Say 'forget my old address' and the person approves the deletion.
Say 'every weekday at 9 send me a briefing' and a scheduled task appears in Schedules.
In the CLI, run cron_list to see the account's schedules.

features.summary: The assistant can ask a clarifying question with choices, ask the person to approve a plan or decision, and hand a job to another agent. The hosted chat shows a question card on Web, Mobile and Chrome and then ends the turn. The CLI and VS Code have ask_user (question or approval), plus task and agent tools for delegation.

purpose.what_it_does: Hosted route: the model calls ask_clarifying_questions to render up to four questions with two to four options each, plus an 'other' answer. CLI and VS Code: ask_user asks a question or an approve or decline decision and waits; task and agent run a sub-agent and return its result to the parent turn.
purpose.why_it_exists: To ask when information is missing instead of guessing, to get consent before a decision, and to split work across agents.
purpose.who_uses_it: People who send vague requests, and developers using the CLI or VS Code.

steps.what_happens: The server offers ask_clarifying_questions for short, non-action messages on web, mobile or chrome when the client declares clarify.v1.
The model calls it; arguments are normalised and validated; a card is built and sent in the stream.
The turn ends. The person answers on the card; the answer is posted and the card settles.
CLI: ask_user asks the surface through the approval broker or a typed prompt and returns the reply as the tool result.
CLI: task and agent spawn sub-agents and return their output to the parent.

features.summary: When more tools are connected than fit in one turn, the server sends only the most relevant tool schemas and lists the rest by name and a short summary. The model calls load_connector_tools by exact name or keyword to load more. The CLI has a separate tool_search tool with its own ranking.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps the prompt small as the connected tool count grows. Hosted: ranks tools against the turn, admits schemas up to a byte budget, defers the rest, and offers load_connector_tools. CLI: keeps niche tools deferred and loads them with tool_search.
purpose.why_it_exists: Large tool catalogs must not be dumped into every prompt (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:650-653).

problems_solved: Prompt bloat and cost from many connected tools.
A relevant tool being missed by ranking.

features.summary: Every tool call appears in the transcript with its arguments, a running then done or failed status, a result preview and full detail on expand. Failed calls show an error and return to the model. Results over the inline limit are kept up to a cap for 24 hours and read back with read_tool_result. Records of calls exist but differ per app. Cost per call is not shown.

purpose.what_it_does: Renders tool calls as cards (web and desktop through the shared ToolCallCard, mobile through ToolCallTimeline, Chrome through side-panel bubbles, VS Code through its webview, CLI through the TUI). Replaces oversized results with a reference. Records connector calls in a log and session approvals in the developer sessions.
purpose.why_it_exists: So people can see and trust what the assistant did, and so long outputs do not fill the context.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who uses tools; developers who debug runs.
problems_solved: Not knowing what a tool did.
Big outputs exhausting context.
Finding which connector calls worked.
use_cases: Watch a web search card run, then open it to see the query.
See a failed fetch card with its error.
Ask the assistant to read the rest of a large result.

3. The person opens the card to see the request and response, and closes it again.

6. After a failure the person uses 'Try again', which re-runs the whole turn.

features.summary: Shows the MCP servers a person has connected, what tools each offers, the protocol version, transport, server name and version, and compatibility notices. Web reads one catalog route. CLI and VS Code show a text report. Mobile shows tools only. The Tauri desktop shows local servers; its cloud connector list has no inspector.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists configured MCP servers and, for one server, shows its tools (with parameters and risk tier), resources, prompts, apps, protocol, transport, server identity and any compatibility warning or partly failed discovery. (apps/web/app/api/connectors/[connectorId]/capabilities/route.ts:56-119; apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorCapabilitiesPanel.tsx:45)
purpose.why_it_exists: A person needs to see what an assistant can do through a server before trusting it, and to learn why a server shows fewer tools than expected (rejected tool names, old handshake, deprecated transport). The panel's own copy says this (apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorCapabilitiesPanel.tsx:19-35).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who connects an MCP server: web and Desktop (hosted web app) users, mobile users in Cloud mode, developers using the CLI or VS Code, and workspace admins checking what members connect. [inferred]
problems_solved: No way to tell what a connected server offers.
Silent loss of tools whose names or schemas the product refuses (rejectedTools list) (apps/web/app/api/connectors/[connectorId]/capabilities/route.ts:85).
Old or deprecated protocol and transport are explained instead of failing silently (apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorCapabilitiesPanel.tsx:25-30).
use_cases: Web user opens a custom connector and reads its tool list and protocol line.
Developer runs agi mcp get docs to see the server name and its tools.
VS Code user clicks the info button on a server to read protocol, capabilities, instructions and recent output.
Mobile user opens a connector to see its tools and set tool permissions.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings modal > Connectors; open a connected connector; the detail footer shows the panel with label 'Live MCP capabilities' (apps/web/features/connectors/hooks/useConnectorsSettingsAdapter.tsx:1191; apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorCapabilitiesPanel.tsx:213). Desktop (public) shows the hosted web app, so it gets the same screen (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).

Tauri desktop (internal build): Settings > Connectors tab shows the cloud connector gallery and a 'Tool Management' workspace with tabs Servers, Bundle Registry, Tools, Credentials, Configuration; 'Connected Tools' lists local servers (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/tabs/Connectors/index.tsx:10; apps/desktop/src/features/mcp/MCPWorkspace.tsx:80).

Mobile: Settings > Connectors (screen title 'Connectors'); tap a connector; the 'Tool permissions' section lists its tools (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/index.tsx:832; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/ConnectorDetailScreen.tsx:1024).
CLI: agi mcp list, agi mcp get <name>, and in a session /mcp list, /mcp tools [server], /mcp info <server> (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5149; apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:1568-1710).

VS Code: command surface 'MCP servers' picker; the info button opens a read-only document with the report (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/capabilityManagement.ts:770; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/mcpServerDetails.ts:31).
Chrome: not applicable; no MCP server list was found in apps/extension.
prerequisites: Web, mobile and Tauri cloud list: signed in to a cloud account (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/index.tsx:809-818).

Web custom connectors currently need connectors to be released; the release constant is 'coming_soon' (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:14), so custom connector capabilities answer 404 today (apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:2083).
Mobile: Cloud mode must be active (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/index.tsx:429).
CLI and VS Code: the local agi command line; VS Code needs a CLI that offers the inspect capability (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/capabilityManagement.ts:776-777).
screens_and_controls: Web panel chips: protocol label ('MCP <version>', 'MCP stateless' or 'MCP initialize handshake'), 'Tasks', '<n> App(s)'; groups Tools, Resources, Templates, Prompts; click a tool to open a detail with parameters ('required'/'optional'); 'Close'; 'Compatibility' section with Protocol, Server supports, Transport, Server rows; 'Retry discovery' button (apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorCapabilitiesPanel.tsx:30-60, 213-378).

Mobile: 'Loading tools...', 'Could not load the tool list' with 'Try again', per-tool permission rows, 'Recent calls', health card (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/ConnectorDetailScreen.tsx:1030-1175).
CLI get prints name, status, transport, target, file, rules, then connects (20 second limit) and prints server identity, 'about', and 'Tools (n):' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5192-5310).
VS Code details: Health, Connection (live/probe), Protocol, Server, Capabilities, error, 'checked at', Instructions, Output (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/mcpServerDetails.ts:31-63).
journey: Open the surface for your app (see where_to_find_it).
See the list of servers; on web and mobile the list is the connected connectors.
Open one server.
The app asks the server what it offers (web: GET capabilities route; CLI: connect then list tools; VS Code: mcp/inspect request).
Read tools, protocol and compatibility notes.
If discovery failed or is partial, use 'Retry discovery' (web) or 'Try again' (mobile) or re-run the command (CLI).
feedback_and_outputs: Web: loading text 'Discovering live MCP capabilities…'; error text 'Live capabilities could not be loaded.'; empty text 'This connector answered but offers no tools, resources or prompts yet...'; partial text 'Unavailable during discovery: <names>.' (apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorCapabilitiesPanel.tsx:19-27, 170-180, 365-376).
CLI: 'could not connect: <error>' or 'did not answer within 20 seconds', 'It offers no tools.' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5262-5300).
VS Code: 'Not reported' for missing fields, 'No output from this server yet' style text from translation keys (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/mcpServerDetails.ts:31-63).
settings: Web: 'Use in chats' switch beside the panel decides if the connector is usable in chats (apps/web/features/connectors/hooks/useConnectorsSettingsAdapter.tsx:89-93); see F058-05.
CLI: --mcp-config and --strict-mcp-config choose which config files are read (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:402-407).

working: Web list route GET /api/connectors/custom returns the user's custom connectors with signedIn flag and directory link (apps/web/app/api/connectors/custom/route.ts:50-78).

Web capabilities route returns protocolEra, protocolVersion, supportedVersions, transport, serverInfo, capabilityKeys, tasksSupported, rejectedTools, tools (name, title, description, parameters, visibility, hasApp, readOnly, riskTier), resources, resourceTemplates, prompts, apps, discoveryErrors; 404 for an unknown connector, 503 'Connector is temporarily unreachable' when the catalog has no entry for it (apps/web/app/api/connectors/[connectorId]/capabilities/route.ts:56-119).

Web panel renders protocol label, transport label, server name and version, legacy handshake notice, deprecated transport notice, rejected tool notices (apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorCapabilitiesPanel.tsx:45-95).
Web client caches a catalog for 30 seconds and validates it with a schema (apps/web/features/connectors/hooks/use-connector-capabilities.ts:12-40).

Mobile fetches the same route and validates it, and shows tools grouped by category (apps/mobile/services/connectors.ts:241-249; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/ConnectorDetailScreen.tsx:388-410).
CLI agi mcp list/get and /mcp list/tools/info/logs work against the registry and live session (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5149-5310; apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:1687-1760).

VS Code picker lists servers with status, transport and scope, and shows tools, prompts, resources and a details document (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/capabilityManagement.ts:670-870).
Tauri desktop lists local servers through the mcp_list_servers command (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sys/commands/mcp.rs:781).
incomplete: Mobile shows tools only; protocol, transport, resources, prompts, apps and rejected tools from the catalog are not rendered (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/ConnectorDetailScreen.tsx:1123; search of catalog usage found only tools).

CLI get and /mcp info show protocol version and capability names but not resources, prompts, rejected tools or supported-version diagnostics (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5192-5310; apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:1714-1760).
VS Code report shows protocol and capability names only; no compatibility warnings (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/mcpServerDetails.ts:31-63).
Tauri desktop cloud connector list has no capability panel; ConnectorCapabilitiesPanel is used only by the web adapter (found by search of apps/desktop/src and apps/web).
disconnected_or_disabled: On web, custom connector capabilities are switched off while connectors are 'coming_soon': the loader returns null for any id not in the selective list, so the route answers 404 (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:14-33; apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:2083). Thirteen directory connectors are selectively released (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:16-30).
not_available: Chrome extension: no MCP server list found.
Plan cap display: no UI element that shows the number of allowed custom connectors was found; the cap is only in server error text (apps/web/lib/services/free-plan-entitlements.ts:69-82).

established.statement: The user can see a list of the MCP servers configured for their account or workspace, on web, desktop, mobile, CLI and VS Code.
Connecting a server discovers its tools and the user can see them (web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code).
The user can inspect protocol, tools, resources, prompts and extensions; brief marks mobile as missing.
The product reports protocol or schema version mismatches or partial compatibility; web and desktop done, mobile, CLI, VS Code missing.
Shared UI must not assume one surface's routing or billing model.

acceptance_criteria: With one connected custom server that supports tools, the web panel lists every tool the server published except app-only tools.
A server on the old handshake shows the legacy handshake notice; a server on the deprecated SSE transport shows the transport notice.
A tool with a name the model cannot call appears in a rejected notice and not in Tools.
An unknown connector id returns 404; an unreachable one returns 503 with 'Connector is temporarily unreachable'.
Mobile detail shows the same tool set as the web panel for the same connector.
CLI agi mcp get prints identity and tools within 20 seconds or a clear failure line.
With no servers, each app shows its empty text and no error.
inferred: Mobile and CLI should show the same compatibility facts the route already returns; the data exists on the client for mobile (apps/mobile/services/connectors.ts:241).
The brief's 'done' for desktop applies to the hosted web app in Electron, not the Tauri build. [inferred from doc: AGENTS.md section 5]
proposed: [proposed] Render protocolEra, transport, rejectedTools and discoveryErrors on mobile from the data it already fetches.
[proposed] Show the plan's custom connector cap next to the list.

steps.what_happens: Web or mobile client calls GET /api/connectors/<id>/capabilities with the user's session.
The route applies a rate limit, checks the connector id pattern, resolves the user and workspace.
The server loads the connector row, opens the MCP connection and discovers tools, resources, prompts and apps (a runtime cache exists).
The MCP server itself answers the discovery requests.
The route strips fences from server text, computes riskTier and returns JSON with Cache-Control private, no-store.
CLI and VS Code instead start or connect to the server on the user's machine (stdio) or call the remote URL directly, then list tools and negotiated protocol.

features.summary: Lets a person connect a new MCP server. Web and mobile add a remote server by https address through one cloud route. The CLI and VS Code register a local command or a remote URL in a local registry. Web add is refused today because connectors are marked coming soon.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates a saved MCP server entry. On web, desktop and mobile it posts name, address and optional credentials to the cloud route, which checks policy and plan, probes the server, encrypts any token and stores a row. On CLI and VS Code it writes an entry to the local registry file. (apps/web/lib/connectors/custom-connector-creation.ts:63-170; apps/cli/src/installs.rs:27-66)
purpose.why_it_exists: The assistant can only use tools from servers the person has connected, and the directory cannot list every server. [inferred]
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers and power users who run or own an MCP server; admins who want to forbid it use the organization policy. [inferred]
problems_solved: Using a private or in-house MCP server in chat.
Connecting from any app without editing config files (web, mobile).
Local stdio servers on a developer's machine (CLI, VS Code).
use_cases: Paste https://mcp.example.com/mcp with a token in web Settings.
Run agi mcp add docs --command node --arg server.js.
Add a remote SSE server from the VS Code picker.
Mobile user adds a server by URL and an optional auth token.

established.statement: The user can register a local (stdio) server that the product starts (CLI done; VS Code listed missing).
The user can add a remote MCP server by URL with optional credentials and it becomes available to the assistant.
Where offered, an MCP server on a private network can be reached through a supported route (CLI done; web, desktop, mobile, chrome missing).
A developer can connect an in-development server such as localhost through a developer-mode flow (CLI done).
The web add route checks CSRF, rate limit, workspace access and allowCustomConnectors before reading the body; a refused request writes nothing.
Never route Local data silently to cloud; consent and visible label required for crossing.

acceptance_criteria: On a plan with room and connectors released, posting a valid https URL returns 201 with toolCount.
A free plan gets a refusal naming the plan before any network call.
A request with a private IP URL is refused as 'targets a private or unsafe network address'.
With allowCustomConnectors off for the workspace, the request returns 403 and no row is written.
Adding the same URL twice is refused with 'You already have a custom connector for this URL.'
A token and OAuth client id together are refused.
agi mcp add with --command writes the entry and agi mcp list shows it as enabled.
A bad JSON body returns a validation error.

proposed: [proposed] Provide a safe private-network route (agent on the user's network) for cloud users; today web refuses private hosts by design.
[proposed] Add header and environment entry to the mobile and web add flows to match CLI.

steps.what_happens: Client sends POST with name, url, optional authToken or OAuth client id and secret and the CSRF header.
Route checks CSRF, rate limit, workspace access gate and the connector policy (including allowCustomConnectors) before parsing the body.
Create step validates input, plan capacity and URL, checks policy for that host, then probes the server over MCP.
The MCP server answers the probe (tool and capability counts).
A row is inserted with the sealed credential; an audit event is recorded; the external resource is recorded best effort.
If sign-in is required the client opens the OAuth start route and the provider consent page.
CLI path: the command validates the name and URL or command, edits ~/.agiworkforce/mcp.json atomically and prints the path; nothing leaves the device.

features.summary: Sets how a server is reached and authorized: token or OAuth sign-in on web, desktop and mobile; address, environment and headers in the CLI and VS Code; per-project servers from .mcp.json in the CLI and VS Code. Web has no editor for an existing server and no project scope.

purpose.who_uses_it: Developers and workspace members who connect servers that need authentication. [inferred]

OAuth sign-in and revoke for remote servers.
Repository-specific servers that should not run elsewhere.

Complete OAuth sign-in after adding a server that publishes a protected resource.
agi mcp add --env KEY=VALUE for a stdio server.
Check .mcp.json into a repo so teammates get the server after approving it.

Web and mobile read a call log table for health states 'Responding', 'Degraded', 'Not responding'; CLI and VS Code connect and report responding plus recent server output lines (apps/web/lib/connectors/health.ts:20-60; apps/cli/src/app_server/surfaces.rs:838-875).

steps.what_happens: The panel reads the catalog; the user selects a resource or prompt; the selection is stored in session storage and announced by a window event.
The composer merges it into state (four resources at most) and attaches it as mcpContext when sending.
The chat request reaches the server, which resolves the connectors named and loads the context through the user's connector handle.
The MCP server returns the resource contents or the prompt result.
The server clips, escapes and fences the text as untrusted reference material and adds it to the model's context.
The model answers using that context.

features.summary: A workspace administrator publishes MCP server addresses so every member of the workspace gets those servers in their connector list without adding anything. The web admin page at /workspace/mcp lists, publishes, unpublishes and retires them. Today the server code refuses publishing and re-publishing because connectors are marked 'coming soon'.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person with the policy.manage permission keep a list of MCP servers (https address, name, optional description) that belongs to the workspace. A published server is offered to every member automatically. Members never see or hold its credentials (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceMcpServers.tsx:237-240).
purpose.why_it_exists: Before this, a workspace that ran its own MCP gateway had to ask every member to add it by hand, and a member who left took their copy away. Nothing said 'this server belongs to the workspace', so nothing could be audited, retired or handed over (apps/web/db/neon/0250_organization_mcp_servers.sql, header comment).
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace administrators and owners (people with policy.manage) publish. Every member of the workspace consumes the result through their connector list.
problems_solved: Members do not have to find, add and configure a company MCP server themselves.
A published server survives the administrator who made it leaving (row belongs to the workspace).
Retiring is an update, not a delete, so the audit trail and the short id are kept and never reused.
A server the workspace's own host policy would block is refused at publish time instead of failing for every member.
use_cases: An IT admin publishes the company's internal MCP gateway so all staff can use its tools.
An admin saves a server as a draft (unpublished) while checking it, then publishes it to everyone.
An admin retires a server that was decommissioned so every member loses it at once.

where_to_find_it: Web: workspace console, left nav item 'MCP servers' (hint 'Servers this workspace publishes to its members'), route /workspace/mcp, page title 'MCP servers' (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceConsoleNav.tsx:101-105; apps/web/app/workspace/mcp/page.tsx:12-18).

Desktop: the public Electron desktop shows the hosted web app, so the same page is reached inside the desktop window (doc: apps/desktop/README.md). The Tauri source under apps/desktop/src has no reference to this page: unknown whether any Tauri screen exists.
Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no screen found; the brief marks them not applicable.
prerequisites: Signed in to a workspace (organization).
To change anything: the policy.manage permission (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/mcp/route.ts:138-142).
To publish or re-publish: connectors released on the server (see gaps; currently not released).
screens_and_controls: Card 'Workspace MCP servers' with explanation 'A published server appears in every member's connector list without them adding it. Members never see or hold its credentials.' (WorkspaceMcpServers.tsx:234-240).
List 'Published MCP servers': each row shows name, URL and a state label 'Published to everyone', 'Draft, not yet published' or 'Retired' (WorkspaceMcpServers.tsx:129-132,254-269).
Row buttons for managers on non-retired rows: 'Unpublish' or 'Publish to everyone', and 'Retire' (WorkspaceMcpServers.tsx:270-292).

Retire confirmation dialog 'Retire <name>?' with buttons 'Retire for everyone' and 'Keep it published'; text says every member loses the server at once and that publishing again gives a new id (WorkspaceMcpServers.tsx:209-221).

Add form 'Add a server': fields 'Name members will see', 'Server URL' (https://mcp.example.com), 'Description' (optional), button 'Publish' (shows 'Checking the server…' while working), note 'The server is checked once before it is published.' (WorkspaceMcpServers.tsx:299-356).
journey: Admin opens 'MCP servers' in the workspace console.
The page loads the list (spinner text 'Loading workspace MCP servers…').
Admin types a name and an https URL, optionally a description, and presses 'Publish'.
The server contacts the MCP server once to check it (probe) before saving; the button reads 'Checking the server…'.
On success the form clears and the list refreshes with the new row labelled 'Published to everyone'.
To stop offering a server the admin presses 'Unpublish'; to remove it for good presses 'Retire' and confirms.
feedback_and_outputs: Empty list: 'This workspace has not published an MCP server yet.' (WorkspaceMcpServers.tsx:250).
Load error: 'We could not load this workspace's MCP servers' with a 'Try again' button (WorkspaceMcpServers.tsx:161-178).
Publish error shown in red under the form via toUserMessage (WorkspaceMcpServers.tsx:334-342).

Server messages include: not https, host blocked by workspace policy, server could not be reached, needs authorization first, edge-blocked, already published at that URL, limit of 32 reached (route.ts:98-103,168-177; org-mcp-servers.ts publishOrgMcpServer).
Permission refusal text: 'Your workspace role does not allow publishing an MCP server to this workspace.' or '...changing this workspace's MCP servers.' (route.ts:141,241).
settings: Workspace connector policy (allowed hosts) is read at publish time and must permit the URL (route.ts:150-151).
No per-member setting: membership is the grant (apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:1703-1707).

working: GET lists servers, the caller's canManage flag and the workspace revision, with ETag headers (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/mcp/route.ts:123-129,108-121).

POST publishes: CSRF check, rate limit, policy.manage check, connectors-released check, revision check, https and host-policy check, a live probe of the server, insert, audit event, optional idempotency key (route.ts:131-229).
PATCH publishes, unpublishes or retires, writes an audit event and returns the refreshed list (route.ts:231-297).
Every successful change records an 'admin_policy_changed' audit event with resourceType organization_mcp_server, severity warning (route.ts:192-204,263-275).

A workspace is capped at 32 non-retired servers; duplicate URL per workspace is refused by a unique constraint (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/mcp/org-mcp-servers.ts MAX_ORG_MCP_SERVERS; apps/web/db/neon/0250_organization_mcp_servers.sql unique constraint).
Members' connector list and tool calls include published, non-retired rows, with no credential header (apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:1709-1735,1825-1830).
Admin page with confirm-before-retire using useConfirmAction (WorkspaceMcpServers.tsx:143,209-221).
incomplete: Un-retire through the API: PATCH with retired:false is accepted but the SQL only ever sets retired_at, never clears it, so a retired row stays retired (org-mcp-servers.ts updateOrgMcpServer, 'retired_at = case when $4::boolean then coalesce(retired_at, now()) else retired_at end'). The page tells admins to publish again instead.

Optimistic concurrency: the server enforces If-Match when sent, but the web page's send() never sends If-Match, so two admins can still overwrite each other from the page (WorkspaceMcpServers.tsx:70-83; route.ts:147-148).

Published servers are read by members with a null credential header, so a server that needs authorization can pass the admin's probe but may fail for members: not confirmed either way (user-connector-tools.ts:1712-1714).
disconnected_or_disabled: Publishing and re-publishing are switched off in the current build: assertConnectorsReleased throws 'Connectors are coming soon.' because CONNECTOR_RELEASE_STATE is 'coming_soon' (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:12; apps/web/lib/connectors/connector-capability.ts:27-29; route.ts:143,245). Retiring and unpublishing still work (test: route.test.ts 'still lets an administrator retire a server').

Whether members actually receive published servers also depends on the same connector release and plan gate (apps/web/lib/connectors/connector-capability.ts:44-52): exact member-side outcome while coming-soon is unknown.
not_available: Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no admin screen for this (brief S58.15 lists web and desktop only).
No per-member or per-group targeting: a published server goes to every member (WorkspaceMcpServers.tsx:238).

established.statement: An organization admin maintains a catalog of approved MCP servers that members can use (web done, desktop done).
A change requires policy.manage; otherwise it is refused with a message naming the workspace role.
Publishing or un-publishing-to-restore calls assertConnectorsReleased first.
Each change writes an admin_policy_changed audit event.
A change is checked against the workspace revision (when the caller states one) so two edits do not overwrite each other.
Founder decisions list the remaining product rules for connectors; no document under docs/product or docs/decisions describing this catalog was found.
established.source: search of docs/product and docs/decisions (no match for the org catalog)

acceptance_criteria: A member without policy.manage who calls POST or PATCH gets 403 with the workspace-role message and no row changes.
With connectors released, POST with an https URL that the server answers publishes the row, returns 201, and writes one admin_policy_changed audit event.
POST with an http URL, a host the connector policy blocks, or an unreachable server is refused and no row is written.
PATCH with retired:true removes the server from every member's connector list and the page shows 'Retired'.
A request carrying a stale If-Match returns a conflict naming the expected and current revision.
While connectors are 'coming soon', POST and PATCH published:true return 403 'Connectors are coming soon.' without contacting the server; retire still succeeds.
The 33rd non-retired server is refused with a limit message.
inferred: The web page should send If-Match from the revision it loaded so the 'two edits do not overwrite each other' rule holds for page users, not only API callers [inferred].
Retire should be the only way a server leaves the list, because the confirmation names it as irreversible [inferred from the dialog text].
proposed: [proposed] Make un-retire either work (clear retired_at with a new id policy) or remove retired:false from the schema.
[proposed] Have the page send If-Match and show the conflict message with a reload action.
[proposed] Decide and document how a published server that needs authorization is credentialed for members.

steps.what_happens: Admin presses 'Publish'; the page sends POST with a bearer token and CSRF header.
Server checks CSRF, rate limit (settings-org-patch), resolves the workspace and requires policy.manage, then assertConnectorsReleased.
Server validates the body, compares the workspace revision when If-Match was sent, reads the connector policy, and requires https plus an allowed host.
Server connects once to the MCP server to count its capabilities; an unreachable, edge-blocked or authorization-needing server is refused.
Server inserts the organization_mcp_servers row and writes the admin_policy_changed audit event; replies 201 with the server and capability counts.
When a member's chat turn or connector list runs, the server adds published non-retired rows of the member's workspace to the connectors they reach, after a public-hostname safety check.

features.summary: When an MCP tool result includes an app, the chat shows it as a small page inside a sandboxed frame. The app can ask to call tools (with approval), read resources, resize, and use device features after consent. Only the signed-in owner can load it. It is built on web and the Electron desktop; mobile shows plain text only; VS Code and Chrome have nothing.

purpose.what_it_does: A tool result that points to an MCP App resource becomes an interactive card (kind 'mcp-app.v1'). The web chat loads the app HTML from the server's resource, runs it in a sandboxed iframe behind a relay page, passes it the tool input, tool result and theme, and brokers its calls back to the server's tools through our servers.
purpose.why_it_exists: MCP Apps let a tool show a chart, form or dashboard instead of only text. Earlier desktop prototypes were cut because they did not follow the standard host contract; this host was built end to end (doc: docs/decisions/wire-or-cut.md section 'MCP Apps Host Boundary').
purpose.who_uses_it: People chatting with a connector or MCP server that ships an app, and server authors whose apps run in chat.
problems_solved: Rich results instead of long text.
Safe execution of third-party HTML: separate origin, strict CSP, no credentials in the app.
The app acts as the signed-in person without ever holding a token.
Device features need a visible 'Allow once'.
use_cases: A connector returns a chart; the person sees it and can resize it.
An app button calls a server tool; the person approves 'This App wants to run <tool>'.
An app asks for the camera; the person chooses 'Allow once' or 'Deny'.

where_to_find_it: Web chat: inside an assistant message after a tool call whose result has an app; the card has frame title '<tool> interactive result' (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/cards/McpAppCard.tsx:431-441).
Desktop: the Electron desktop shows the hosted web app, so the same card appears (doc: apps/desktop/README.md). The Tauri source has no card (no match under apps/desktop/src).
Mobile: card testID 'interactive-card-mcp-app' shows the result as text with a notice, not an interactive app (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/cards/McpAppCard.tsx).
VS Code, Chrome: nothing found.

A connected MCP server that returns an app (tool metadata with a ui:// resource).
On production web: a separate sandbox origin configured (NEXT_PUBLIC_MCP_APP_SANDBOX_ORIGIN) or the card shows plain text.
A saved (non-temporary) chat for buttons that send messages is an Answer-UI rule, not MCP App (InteractiveCardBlock.tsx:60-73).

Tool ask bar: 'This App wants to run <tool name>.' with 'Allow once' and 'Deny' (McpAppCard.tsx:470-498).
Notice with warning icon and the plain tool text when the app cannot run (McpAppCard.tsx:418-430).

The server runs the tool; if the result has an app and a user id, it stores the payload and emits the card (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:2969-3002).

working: Server builds the 'mcp-app.v1' card and saves payload (tool-loop.ts:2969-3002; apps/web/lib/connectors/mcp-state-store.ts saveMcpAppPayload).
Payload over 2 MB (input plus result JSON) is not saved, a warning is logged, and the message shows text only (mcp-state-store.ts:9-10,28-35).
Task-binding failure returns 'The MCP server started a task, but its secure task binding could not be persisted.' (tool-loop.ts:2944-2958).

Sandbox: relay page with strict CSP, inner frame sandbox 'allow-scripts allow-forms', no cache (apps/web/app/api/mcp-apps/sandbox/route.ts).
Production requires a separate origin, else the plain text fallback (McpAppCard.tsx:111-118,242-248; apps/web/lib/validate-env.ts:458-490).

Device permissions (camera, microphone, geolocation, clipboard) are withheld until 'Allow once' (McpAppCard.tsx:54-90,259-266).

Connector endpoint authorises each widget call for the viewer, enforces deny, asks for approval on non-allow or critical tools, audits (apps/web/app/api/connectors/[connectorId]/mcp/route.ts:57-80,130-150).
incomplete: Theme is read once when the bridge is created; no code updates the app when the theme changes (McpAppCard.tsx:273-275) [inferred from absence of any host-context update call].
Display mode is only 'inline' (McpAppCard.tsx:276-277).

disconnected_or_disabled: Connectors are 'coming soon' in the current release state, which gates connector tool turns (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:12; connector-capability.ts:44-52). Effect on MCP App cards: unknown.
Without NEXT_PUBLIC_MCP_APP_SANDBOX_ORIGIN in production the app never runs; the card shows text (validate-env.ts:462-471).
not_available: VS Code: no MCP App rendering found.
Chrome extension: none found.
CLI: not in scope.
Tauri desktop source: no MCP App code found under apps/desktop/src.
Local-mode MCP servers: the card reads resources through the cloud connector route only (McpAppCard.tsx:129-145).

established.statement: A tool result that ships an MCP App renders as an interactive panel inside the chat (web done, desktop done, mobile/VS Code/Chrome missing).
The host initializes the embedded app with the standard handshake before it runs.
The host passes tool input, result and host context (theme, display mode) to the widget.
The widget can call server tools and read resources through the host, with approval for tool calls.
The widget can request a new height and the host resizes within limits.
The widget acts as the signed-in user without handling credentials.
An app's payload and actions are authorized for the viewing user only.
Embedded Apps need the standard host contract end to end; arbitrary HTML via private formats was cut.

acceptance_criteria: A tool result with an app shows a 'Loading MCP App…' line and then a frame on a deployment with a dedicated sandbox origin.
With no dedicated origin in production the card shows the notice and the tool's plain text and never runs the app.
A payload over 2 MB is not stored and the message carries text only.
Resource HTML over 2 MB shows "This app's content is too large to display." and the plain result.
A widget tool call that needs approval shows 'This App wants to run <tool>.'; Deny returns 'The user declined this MCP App tool call.'
An app that requests camera or location gets nothing until 'Allow once' is pressed.
A resize request of 5000 results in a height of 1000; of 10 results in 180.
Another user requesting the payload id gets 404.

Mobile 'missing' for S58.17 to S58.23 is accurate for interactivity; mobile shows text only [inferred from code].

steps.what_happens: The assistant calls an MCP tool; our server runs it on the connector.
If the result has an app and a user id, the server stores input and result (limit 2 MB) and puts a card with only an opaque payload id and ids in the message.
The browser fetches the payload by id; the server returns it only to its owner.
The browser asks our connector route to read the ui:// resource; our server reads it from the MCP server.
The MCP server supplies the HTML and its declared CSP and permissions.
The browser loads the relay page from the sandbox origin and runs the app in a nested frame; the handshake passes tool input, result and host context.
App calls are proxied: callTool (approval first if required), readResource, lists; each hits our connector route and an audit event is recorded.

features.summary: A web page can publish its own tools, either by registering them in the browser (navigator.modelContext) or by marking forms with tool-name. The Chrome extension finds them when the page loads, keeps them per tab, updates the list when the page changes, and lets the browser agent list them with discover_site_tools and call them after approval.

purpose.what_it_does: The extension's page script discovers site tools, validates and size-limits them, sends them to the background worker, and refreshes the list when the page changes. The browser agent has two actions: discover_site_tools (no arguments) and call_site_tool (always needs approval).
purpose.why_it_exists: Pages can offer structured actions that are safer and more reliable than clicking around. The product keeps them as their own category, separate from connectors and from plain browser automation (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md line 180 notes the leaders distinguish site tools, browser automation and connected APIs).
purpose.who_uses_it: People using the Chrome extension's browser agent on pages that publish tools, and site owners who publish them.
problems_solved: The agent can use a page's own actions instead of guessing at buttons.
Tool declarations are treated as untrusted, so a page cannot grant itself permission.
The list stays correct as the page changes or the person navigates.
use_cases: A shop page publishes 'add_to_cart'; the agent discovers and calls it after approval.
A page with a form marked tool-name='search' lets the agent search through the form.
A page adds a tool after login; the list updates without reloading.

The side panel is sent a WEBMCP_TOOLS_CHANGED message, but no code that listens for it in the extension source was found (apps/extension/src/background.ts:2294-2296).

After the call the extension checks the page did not change and returns the page's claimed result, flagged as unverified.

steps.what_happens: The content script waits 1 s after load, discovers tools (forms and navigator.modelContext) and sends them to the background worker.
The worker checks the sender tab is still current, normalizes and size-limits the list, stores it per tab and informs listeners and the native host.
When the page changes, a debounced observer or toolschanged event re-discovers; a changed list is sent again.
The browser agent loop asks the model (through the cloud gateway) what to do; the model may choose discover_site_tools.
The worker re-discovers from the page, verifies the tab and URL did not change, and returns the list.
For call_site_tool the person approves; the extension re-checks, calls the page's tool, then verifies the document did not change.

features.summary: When the agent wants to run a tool that needs a decision, the run pauses and shows a card. The person allows it, so it runs, or denies it, so it does not run and the model is told. On Managed Cloud the pause is a saved checkpoint that expires after 24 hours; local apps ask on the device.

purpose.what_it_does: Pauses a run at a tool call that needs a decision, shows the call, and carries the answer back: Allow runs that call and the run continues, Deny skips it and tells the model it was refused (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:3163, :3168).
purpose.why_it_exists: The product's rule is that no sensitive action happens without the user's approval (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 9.7, 'Approvals').
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using a tool-using chat, a Work run or a coding session on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code or Chrome.
problems_solved: The agent cannot send, write or run something the person did not see.
A denied call is not retried silently: the model gets a clear 'denied' result (tool-loop.ts:3163).
A run that waits for a person is saved, so closing the tab does not lose it (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1908).
use_cases: Web chat: the agent wants to call a connected app; the person presses Allow once on the card.
Mobile: the agent wants to run a connector tool; the person presses Deny and types what to do instead.
CLI: a shell command needs approval; the person presses y or n in the overlay.
VS Code: the editor is in the background; the person presses Allow once in the notification.

where_to_find_it: Web, and Desktop (the public Desktop shows the hosted web app, per AGENTS.md section 5): a card inside the assistant message. Plain tool card buttons: 'Allow' and 'Deny' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/ToolCallCard.tsx:419 via TOOL_APPROVAL_ACTION_LABELS). 4. The person presses Allow or Deny. Web posts the decisions to POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions/approve once every call of the step has a decision (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:5494).
5. The server claims the checkpoint, rechecks workspace and permission rules, and resumes the run (approve/route.ts:220, :560).

established.statement: A single tool call that needs approval can be approved or denied and the run continues accordingly.
A pending action that is allowed then runs.
A denied action does not run and the model is told it was denied.
Approval prompts show the action, target, provider/tool, risk, scope and available choices.
Approval and permission cards are part of the transcript experience; approval state is a typed durable event.

acceptance_criteria: A call that must ask shows a card and the run does not continue until a decision.
Allow runs exactly that call; the result appears in the transcript.
Deny leaves the call unexecuted and the model receives the denied message.
An answer after the checkpoint expired is refused with 410 and the card shows expired.
Two devices answering the same approval: the second gets 409 and a plain message.
If the server cannot resume, an error is shown and the same approval can be answered again.

Every decision on any app should reach one history; today only cloud approvals do [inferred from approve/route.ts:631].

steps.what_happens: Tool gate returns ask for a call; the loop saves a checkpoint and streams an approval request, then ends the stream.
The client shows the card and keeps decisions in memory until every call of the step is decided.
Client posts decisions; server runs managed-compute, workspace-policy and spend gates, parses the body and blocks secrets in guidance.
Server claims the pending checkpoint (24 hour window, exact decision set) and sets a lease.
Server rebuilds the request, forces approved calls to rejected if the saved permission store now denies them, and resumes the loop.
Approved tools run; denied tools get a fixed 'did not run' result; the stream continues to the client.
CLI and Electron device prompts never leave the machine: answer is stored locally and the tool runs on the device.

features.summary: A run can pause on several tool calls at once. The server only resumes when it gets one decision for every pending call, then resumes once. Tasks screens apply one Approve or Deny to all calls. The CLI has Allow All and Deny All for the rest of a turn.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person answer all pending calls of one run together so the run resumes a single time (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1964-1972).
purpose.why_it_exists: A model can ask for several tools in one step; asking one by one would need many resumes, and the server refuses a partial answer.
purpose.who_uses_it: People managing background work on Web, Desktop, Mobile, VS Code and the CLI.
problems_solved: No half-answered step: the server rejects a decision set that does not match the pending set (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1964).
No repeated prompts for the rest of a CLI turn (apps/cli/src/tui/approval_broker.rs:325-326).

purpose.what_it_does: Remembers approvals at three levels (once, for the chat, always), stores per-tool Allow/Ask/Deny, lists past decisions and revokes saved choices (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/connector-tool-session-grants.ts:272, apps/web/app/api/connectors/permissions/route.ts:131).
purpose.why_it_exists: Asking for every repeated safe action is tiring, while some actions must always ask; the person needs control and a record (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md section 9.3, 'Do not use one generic approval setting').
purpose.who_uses_it: Regular users of connected apps, workspace admins, CLI users.
problems_solved: Repeated prompts for the same tool.
No way to block one tool of a connector.
No audit trail of what was approved.
use_cases: Allow Read-only tools of a connector once for all chats, keep Write and delete tools on Ask.
Press Allow for this chat on a mail tool for one conversation.
Open Approval history to see what was approved yesterday.
Reset a tool to default after changing one's mind.

journey: 1. A card appears; the person picks a scope.
2. For a destructive tool a confirm dialog names what cannot be undone.
3. The decision is sent; the server stores the grant before resuming (approve/route.ts:403).
4. Later calls to that tool follow the saved verdict.
5. To undo: open the connector panel, press Reset, or set Ask or Deny; the next call asks again.

working: Three scopes once, session, always are on the wire; the server offers session only for a rememberable connector tool in a saved chat, and always only if the tier is not critical (connector-tool-session-grants.ts:272-287; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/tool-approval-resume.ts:11-16).

Workspace rules merge with member rules; the stricter wins (connector-tool-permissions.ts:503-540).
Temporary chats ignore standing allows and cannot remember (connector-tool-permissions.ts:464-495).
Approval history lists tool_approval_decided audit rows, newest first, 50 per page by default, up to 100 (settings/approvals/route.ts:20, :90).
CLI saves rules to permissions.toml and refuses open-ended or multi-line rules (permissions.rs:104, :373-431, :445).
Electron stores 'always' grants in desktop-permissions.json and keeps high-risk grants to the session (permissionManager.ts:50, permissionCore.ts:57-62).
incomplete: Web has two 'for this chat' behaviours: plain cards keep the allowance in page memory and auto-approve later calls until reload (chat-tool-allowance-store.ts:10, MessageBubble.tsx:2354); reviewed connector cards save a server grant that lasts until the chat is deleted or reset (tool-approval-presentation.ts:31).
History shows only decisions made through the cloud approve route (approve/route.ts:631); CLI and Electron local decisions were not found in it [inferred].
The brief cites CLI history at lib.rs:2835 and exec/tools/mod.rs:988; those lines are about hosted conversation adoption and a confirm prompt, not history. CLI history is not established.

established.statement: A session allow stops asking until the session ends.
The user can set allow, ask or deny per connected app and per tool, and the runtime enforces it.
Permission choices persist across sessions and devices until changed.
The user can review a history of past approval requests and their decisions.
The user can revoke a saved always allow (or folder or site grant) so the action asks again.
The remembered scope differs per approval domain; do not use one generic setting.

acceptance_criteria: After Allow for this chat on a reviewed tool, the next call in that chat runs without a card; in another chat it asks.
Always allow is not offered for a critical tool; PUT allow for a critical tool returns 422.
After Reset or DELETE the next call asks.
A per-tool Deny blocks the call even under Skip approvals.
History shows the decision with tool name and time within one page load.
A workspace Ask or Deny wins over a member allow.
inferred: Plain cards should use the same server grant as reviewed cards [inferred from the two mechanisms].
proposed: [proposed] One 'for this chat' mechanism with the same lifetime on every card.
[proposed] One history that also includes local CLI and Desktop decisions.

steps.what_happens: Card offers only the scopes the server reviewed; destructive tools ask for a second confirmation.
Decision approved-for-session or approved-always is posted with the resume request.
Server plans scoped approvals, checks the permission generation, saves the grant, rereads and confirms policy still agrees, then resumes.
Each later call is gated by saved level, grants, workspace rules and the policy (tool-call-gate ranks).
History read pulls audit rows for the user.
CLI and Electron save rules in local files; nothing is sent.

features.summary: Limits where the agent may act. On Desktop and CLI the person grants folders. On Web a workspace admin lists sites web search and fetch may read. The CLI has domain: rules and asks before fetching unknown or private hosts. Chrome has an approved sites list. Mobile has neither.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps file and web access inside what the person or workspace allowed (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/pathGuard.ts:108; apps/web/lib/url-fetch/url-fetch-tool.ts:552).
purpose.why_it_exists: Agents that read files or fetch pages could reach private data or internal networks; requirements call for approval on new or sensitive domains and for file and network operations outside safe defaults (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 9.7).
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop and CLI developers, workspace admins, browser-task users.
problems_solved: File access outside a granted folder.
Reading blocked websites.
Fetching internal addresses or cloud metadata services.
use_cases: Desktop: pick a project folder; revoke it later.
Admin: allow only a short list of sites for web search in a workspace.
CLI: add domain:docs.example.com to always allow fetches there.
Chrome: approve a site once for a task or always.

journey: Desktop: 1. Choose a folder; 2. the app lists it as a root; 3. later file or shell actions ask under that folder; 4. press revoke to remove the root, which first stops work in it.

The public Desktop is Electron showing the web app (AGENTS.md section 5), so whether this gap applies to the public Desktop is unknown.

established.statement: The agent can touch only folders the user granted, and the user grants or revokes each folder.
The user can allow or block specific websites the agent may act on or fetch, and it is enforced.
Desktop cloud chats are bound by workspace site rules; local and own-key desktop turns with hosted search are not (known gap).
Browser actions on new or sensitive domains and file, shell and network operations outside safe defaults need approval.

acceptance_criteria: A file tool targeting a path outside every granted folder is refused.
Revoking a folder stops later access and asks again after re-granting.
A blocked site is refused by fetch and absent from search results.
The CLI asks before fetching a private-network address and does not offer an open-ended allow.
With an allow list set, a host not on it is refused.
inferred: Website rules should also apply to personal accounts [inferred from connector-policy-service.ts:87 returning null without a workspace].
Local and own-key desktop search should carry the same rules [inferred from S59.06 note].
proposed: [proposed] A per-user site list for accounts without a workspace.
[proposed] Withhold hosted search on local turns or pass the lists to the provider.

Web and Mobile cloud accounts start on Skip approvals unless a value was saved; the safe default only applies on errors or when the workspace forbids skipping. The CLI, VS Code and Chrome have their own mode lists.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores an account-wide default policy and applies it in the tool gate, together with per-tool saved rules, workspace limits and a safety escalation (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-call-gate.ts:68-128, packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts:3-8).
purpose.why_it_exists: People want to choose between safety and speed; the two leading assistants offer similar modes (doc: AGENTS.md section 10 says compare ChatGPT and Claude).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every user of tools; admins who forbid skipping approvals.

working: Gate: ordered ranks; a saved Deny wins, then a saved Allow, then a saved Ask, then the account policy for read-only tools, then ask in manual mode (tool-call-gate.ts:68-128).

Ask every time: nothing is auto-approved. Read-only policy: only declared, reversible read tools without an egress path are auto-approved; device and browser command tools never are. Skip approvals: everything except destructive or unknown tools (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-metadata.ts:1083-1100; test apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.permission-matrix.test.ts:190).

A workspace that does not permit Skip approvals turns a stored Skip back into Ask every time, not into the read-only policy (tool-approval-policy.ts:93-100; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-approval-policy.ts:48-62).
A read of the policy that fails falls back to Ask every time (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-approval-policy.ts:66).
Lethal-trifecta escalation: untrusted content plus a private source plus an egress call asks even under Skip approvals, and denies if unattended and cannot pause (tool-call-gate.ts:78-110, :130-136).
CLI Plan mode is a real read-only profile; Default, Auto (edits allowed), Bypass and headless modes map to profiles (apps/cli/src/permissions.rs:303-340).
VS Code carries four developer modes; Chrome four browser modes (developer-session.ts:25, askBeforeActing.ts:5).
incomplete: No global read-only mode that refuses write, send and execute tools exists on Web: the 'read-only' policy only skips asking for reads, and per-connector 'Write and delete tools' = Deny is a manual preset (tool-metadata.ts:1083, ToolPermissionsPanel.tsx:57). CLI Plan mode is the real one; VS Code 'Plan' is plan-then-approve (webviewContent.ts:66).

The default is inconsistent: Web and Mobile cloud use Skip approvals when nothing is saved (apps/web/shared/types/toolApprovalPolicy.ts:29, :45; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/tool-approvals/toolApprovalPolicyOwner.ts:181) while the shared constant is Ask every time (tool-approval-policy.ts:11) and Mobile tags Ask as 'Recommended' (auto-approve.tsx:28).
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile Local mode stores a policy on the phone (toolApprovalPolicyOwner.ts:86; apps/mobile/stores/settingsStore.ts:122) but no reader outside settings code was found by search; the composer control is hidden in Local (ComposerApprovalModeControl.tsx:26).
not_available: Read-only mode on Mobile (brief lists none).

features.summary: Lets a person change or steer a pending agent action instead of only allowing or denying it. Redirect (typed guidance sent with the decision) works on all six apps in different forms. Edit works only for file content in VS Code through the local CLI runtime. Editing a command, recipient or text is not built anywhere.

purpose.what_it_does: Redirect: the person types a note with Allow or Deny, and the agent receives it and continues with that guidance. Edit: before a file write or edit runs, the person changes the proposed file text and the edited version is written.
purpose.why_it_exists: A plain Deny stops the agent without saying why. A note lets the person correct course without restarting. Edit lets the person fix a small mistake in a proposed file change without a second round trip. Brief items S59.21 and S59.22 define both.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone approving agent tool calls: Cloud chat and Work users on Web, Desktop, Mobile and the Chrome extension, and developers in the CLI and VS Code.
problems_solved: Denying with no reason leaves the model guessing what to do next.
Approving a nearly right file change forces a deny and a re-ask.
Long-running Cloud runs would otherwise need a new message to redirect them.
use_cases: On Mobile the person taps Add guidance, types 'use the staging address instead', and presses Deny; the agent continues with that.
In the CLI the person presses Tab on No, types what to do instead, and presses Enter.
In VS Code the person presses Review change, edits the proposed file in the diff, then presses Allow once and the edited text is written.
On the Tasks page the person types guidance and presses Approve to steer a Cloud run.

journey: 1. The agent asks to run a tool and pauses.
2. The person opens the approval card (or the Approvals popover, Tasks page, notification, or CLI overlay).
3. Redirect: the person types a note. Edit (VS Code only): the person presses Review change and edits the proposed file in a diff tab.
4. The person presses Allow or Deny (CLI: Tab, type, Enter).
5. The note or edited text is sent with the decision.
6. The agent continues. With a note on a denied call it is told to follow what the user says next; the card shows the decision.

established.statement: Redirect: instead of just denying, the user can tell the agent what to do instead and the agent continues with that guidance.
Edit: before approving, the user can edit the proposed action (command, recipient or text) and run the edited version.
Approval prompts must show the action, target, provider/tool, risk, scope and available choices.

acceptance_criteria: On Web, open Approvals, type a note, press Deny: the request body has guidance and the transcript shows 'Applied your guidance'.
On Mobile, tap Add guidance, type, press Allow once: the resume request carries the text; the card shows 'Decision saved: Allowed'.
In the CLI, Tab on No, type a note, Enter: the tool does not run and its output ends with the note line.
In VS Code, Review change, edit the proposed file, Allow once: the file on disk holds the edited text.
A note of 4001 characters is refused or cut at 4000 on each app.
A note holding a secret is blocked or redacted before the model sees it (Cloud).
Pressing Edit on a command approval (any app) is not offered, and no control claims otherwise.
inferred: [inferred] Guidance should also be offered on the Web inline card and on the Mobile Tasks sheet so every approval surface behaves the same.
[inferred] An edited approval should be shown to the model as edited, as the CLI already does.
proposed: [proposed] Add an 'Edit' control for command, recipient and text arguments, with a typed edited-arguments field in the approve request and a re-check of risk on the edited value.
[proposed] Update the brief rows S59.21 to partial for VS Code and CLI app-server.

steps.what_happens: Person types a note or edits file text and presses Allow or Deny in the app.
Cloud: the app posts run id, one decision per pending call and optional guidance to the approve endpoint.
Server checks managed compute, organization policy and spend limit, screens guidance for secrets, then claims the pending checkpoint.
Server resumes the same run; the tool loop builds the tool results and the guidance message and calls the model again.
The model provider answers with the next step.
CLI and VS Code local: the note or edited text goes to the local tool process and is appended to its result; nothing leaves the device for the prompt.

features.summary: A pending approval waits a limited time that differs by path: 24 hours for Cloud tool approvals, 15 minutes for device steps, 10 minutes in the CLI, 30 minutes for Cloud Code sessions. After a decision the same run resumes and the transcript shows ran or denied. Late answers are refused with an expiry message.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores a paused run as a checkpoint, accepts one decision before it expires, refuses late or duplicate answers, resumes the same run, and shows what was decided and what happened.
purpose.why_it_exists: An agent cannot wait forever and a stale approval must never run an action the user no longer expects. Resuming the same run avoids restarting the work.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who approves agent actions on any app, and engineers who debug stuck approvals.
problems_solved: Stale approvals running late.
Two devices answering the same approval.
Lost progress when a person decides after leaving.
Unclear outcome after pressing Allow.
use_cases: Answer an approval in a Web chat 5 minutes later; the run continues in the same message.
Come back the next day; the Cloud approval is older than 24 hours and the server refuses with an expiry message.
A CLI prompt left alone for 10 minutes ends as 'did not run'.
After Deny, the transcript marks the tool denied and the model is told it was denied.

Cloud: signed-in account; the run must still be pending.

Expired card text: 'This approval request expired or is no longer active.' with 'Send a new message to try again.' (ToolCallCard.tsx:371; ToolCallTimeline.tsx:362).
Web popover expired text: 'This request expired. Open the conversation to rerun the turn.' (ApprovalInbox.tsx:224).
Device step expired text: 'This step waited too long for <device>. Ask again on that device.' (ToolCallCard.tsx:362).

journey: 1. The agent pauses on an approval. The server saves a checkpoint in state pending.
2. The card shows waiting buttons.
3. The person presses a decision for every pending call.
4. The server claims the checkpoint (state resuming, with a lease) and resumes the same run.
5. The card changes: denied calls show 'You denied this tool.', approved calls show running and then their result.
6. When the turn ends the checkpoint is completed. If it expired first, step 4 returns 410 and the action does not run.
feedback_and_outputs: Web denied tool: error 'You denied this tool.' and result 'The user denied permission to run this tool.' (useChatStream.ts:5601).
Mobile denied tool: 'You denied permission to run this tool.' (chatExecutionStore.ts:4439); allowed or denied saved line (ToolCallTimeline.tsx:396).
VS Code outcomes 'Allowed once.', 'Allowed for the rest of this session.', 'Denied.', 'The turn ended before this was answered.' (webviewContent.ts:7040-7046).

Model is told: 'The user denied permission to run this tool.' style result (tool-loop.ts:6600).

working: Cloud TTL constant 24 hours (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:457) applied when claiming (1935-1946), when listing pending approvals (478-490) and in the mobile status route (apps/web/app/api/mobile/agent-status/route.ts:66).

Expired claim throws CloudAgentApprovalCheckpointExpiredError, mapped to 410 'This approval request expired and can no longer be resumed.' (route.ts:145). Unknown run 404, duplicate or already answered 409 'This approval is already being resumed.' (route.ts:148-151).

The claim moves the checkpoint to resuming with a lease and the run to running in one transaction (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1966-1992); the approve route asks for an 86,400 second lease (route.ts:227); failures release it back to pending (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:2027-2050).
The resumed turn continues the same run, session, turn and event sequence (route.ts:560-580) and completes the checkpoint through predecessorApproval.
Device step checkpoints expire after 15 minutes (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:515; packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/device-steps.ts:428; tool-loop.ts:7735).

CLI TUI prompt expires after 600 seconds and records a Timeout decision (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:38,1658,8396); the app-server waits 600 seconds (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:120,6975).
Cloud Code session approvals expire after 30 minutes and answer 409 (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-agent-service.ts:964; apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/[sessionId]/agent/approvals/route.ts:42).

Web client closes the card on 404, 409, 410 (useChatStream.ts:5843); Mobile treats 404, 409, 410 as terminal (chatExecutionStore.ts:501); Tasks pages map 409 and 410 to clear messages (TasksPage.tsx:175-184; apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/service.ts:26,93-95).
Transcript receipts: Web, Mobile, VS Code and CLI show denied and allowed results as listed above; the server writes audit event tool_approval_decided per call (route.ts:631).
incomplete: The brief says a lease expires on its own if a resume stops. For approval checkpoints the claim selects only state pending (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1935) and a resuming row answers 409; only caller checkpoints reclaim an expired lease (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1853). Whether another process repairs a stuck resuming approval was not found.

Web and Mobile 'expired' in a chat card is client state (not live in memory, or superseded by a newer turn), not the 24-hour clock (useChatStream.ts:1138; MessageBubble.tsx:1010; chatExecutionStore.ts:791). A reloaded card older than 24 hours can show buttons until the server answers 410 [inferred].
No remaining-time display was found on any app.
disconnected_or_disabled: apps/desktop/src (Tauri) is internal; Desktop public window uses the hosted web code.
not_available: Configurable wait times: none found.
Brief says device approvals last 15 minutes: the 15 minutes belongs to device-step checkpoints, not to approvals.
Chrome expiry handling beyond the generic stream error: not established.

established.statement: A pending approval expires after a set time, the UI shows it expired, and the action cannot run from it.
After the user intervenes the same run resumes where it stopped.
After a decision the transcript shows what was decided and what happened (ran, result or denied).
Approval is bound to the exact pending action, expires, and cannot be replayed or retargeted.
Approvals bind to stored commands; denial performs no action.

acceptance_criteria: A Cloud approval older than 24 hours answers 410 with the exact message and no tool runs.
A second answer to the same approval answers 409.
After Allow, the same run id continues in the same assistant message.
After Deny, the tool shows denied and the model receives a denied result.
A CLI prompt left 10 minutes ends with the 'did not run' line.

steps.what_happens: Tool loop hits a call that needs approval and saves a checkpoint (messages, request, pending calls, event cursor) in state pending.
The app shows the waiting card from stream events or from the persisted projection.
Person decides every pending call; the app posts the resume.
Server checks the 24 hour window, locks the row, checks decisions match exactly, sets resuming with a lease, sets the run running.
Server applies connector permission denials, then resumes the turn on a durable workflow or inline fallback.
Model provider returns the next step; events stream back; checkpoint is completed.
CLI path: modal waits up to 600 seconds, then the broker records Timeout.
