features.summary: An approval raised on one signed-in device can be answered on another through the Tasks page, a chat, Mobile Tasks, or VS Code cloud tasks, and the first device follows the result. VS Code offers Allow once, Deny and Open chat from a notification. Desktop banners and a Mobile notification also exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows pending Cloud approvals on any signed-in device, accepts the first answer, refuses later ones, and lets the first device pick up the result. Raises notifications so a person can answer without opening the app.
purpose.why_it_exists: Agents often pause while the person is away from the device that started the run. Answering from a phone or an editor notification keeps work moving.
purpose.who_uses_it: People who start Cloud runs or local coding sessions and then move between devices.
problems_solved: Run waits because the person is away from the original device.
Two devices answering one approval.
Missing a pause because no alert was shown.
use_cases: Start a Cloud task on Web, answer its approval on Mobile Tasks.
VS Code window is in the background; press Allow once on the notification.
Open Tasks, filter 'Needs you', approve all pending calls of one run.
Desktop banner offers Approve for a low-risk reversible command.

Chrome: no other-device approval surface found.

established.statement: An approval raised on one device can be answered from another signed-in device, and the first device sees the result.
When an approval is needed the user is notified and can approve or deny from the notification.
Remote projection of approvals is projection only; the host remains authority.
Start a task, close its tab and observe the same durable task from a fresh browser; approval is bound to the exact pending action.

acceptance_criteria: Raise an approval on Web, approve it on Mobile Tasks; the Web chat shows the run continuing within about 10 seconds.
A second approve on a different device shows the already-answered message and does not run twice.
VS Code unfocused: banner offers Allow once, Deny, Open chat; a question offers Open chat only.
Press Allow once on the banner: the local tool runs and the card shows Allowed.
Desktop banner offers no Approve for a high-risk or irreversible request.
Mobile notification Review opens the app at the run.
Chrome behaviour is recorded as unverified until tested.

[inferred] Notification actions should never allow a high-risk call, as the Desktop rule does.
proposed: [proposed] Add push to the Web follower instead of polling.
[proposed] Offer Approve and Deny actions in the Mobile notification for low-risk reversible calls, using the Desktop rule.

features.summary: While the agent drives the screen or a browser tab, the person can press Take over to pause it, use the screen themselves, then hand control back. Built on Desktop (Electron) and Chrome. On Desktop the agent is told to look again before carrying on. Chrome ends the task after 15 minutes without a hand back.

purpose.what_it_does: Pauses the agent's control of the computer or a browser tab on request or when the person starts using it, and lets the person hand control back so the task goes on.
purpose.why_it_exists: A person must always be able to stop an agent that controls their screen and fix things by hand. Product requirements list a manual takeover path.
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop and Chrome users running computer use or browser tasks.
problems_solved: Agent stuck on a login or captcha the person must do.
Person needs to correct something the agent got wrong.
Agent clicking while the person is typing.
use_cases: Desktop: press Take over, sign in to a website, press Hand back.
Chrome: the agent hands the page over to enter a password; the person presses Continue.
Desktop: move the mouse during a run and the agent pauses by itself.
Chrome: leave a taken-over tab for 15 minutes and the task ends.

where_to_find_it: Desktop (hosted web UI in Electron): floating status bar 'AGI is using your computer' with buttons 'Take over' and 'Stop'; when paused 'Paused. You have the screen.' with 'Hand back' and 'Stop' (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/ComputerUseControlBar.tsx:31,53; mounted in DesktopHostMount.tsx:55).
Desktop tray menu: 'Hand Back Screen Control' while the screen is taken (apps/desktop/electron/tray.ts:152). The stop shortcut also takes the screen back (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1794).

Chrome side panel: browser-task bubble button 'Take over' / 'Hand back' (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:1587) and computer-use panel buttons 'Take over' and 'Continue' (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/computerUsePanel.ts:1227,1234).
Chrome page: in-page run dock with 'Stop' and 'Take over'; while paused the dock shows 'You have the page.' (apps/extension/src/features/content/browserRunOverlay.ts:55,76-78).
prerequisites: Desktop: computer use turned on in settings and permission granted, macOS or supported OS (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/computerUseSession.ts:81-99,263-265).
Chrome: an active browser or computer-use run on a tab.
screens_and_controls: Take over, Hand back, Stop (Desktop bar).

Native confirmation 'Hand the screen back?' with buttons 'Keep control' and 'Hand back' (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/computerUseSteps.ts:138-150), reached through computer_hand_back (dispatcher.ts:2606-2607).
Chrome Take over, Hand back or Continue, Stop; banner 'You have the page.'
journey: 1. The agent is controlling the screen or tab.
2. The person presses Take over (or moves the mouse or types).
3. The agent pauses; its next screen step waits.
4. The person uses the screen.
5. The person presses Hand back (Desktop asks to confirm) or Continue (Chrome).

steps.what_happens: Person presses Take over; the web host calls the Electron runtime command computer_take_over.
The session moves to paused, the stop shortcut is released and the agent's next screen step waits.
Person presses Hand back, confirms in a native dialog; the phase returns to active and held steps are released.
The held step is refused unless it only observes; if a resume is owed the chat sends a resume prompt to the model.
The model (Cloud, own key or local, as the chat uses) takes a fresh screenshot and decides the next step.

features.summary: Lets a signed-in person on a paid plan describe a goal, optional constraints and a wanted deliverable, then start an AGI Work run (a tool-using Cloud agent run) instead of a plain chat turn. Found in the web and desktop composer Work mode, the mobile New task sheet and the Chrome side panel toggle. CLI and VS Code do not start it.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns a typed goal into a structured request (work_mode agiwork plus agi_work_goal with goal, constraints, deliverable, excluded tools). The server then plans the work, asks for plan review when requested, and runs tools (web search, fetch, code execution, file creation) as a durable Cloud run that shows up in the Tasks list. [inferred from the code path below]
purpose.why_it_exists: A plain chat turn answers once. Multi-step work (research a topic, build a report or file) needs a stated objective, scope and expected output so the agent can plan and the person can check the result. (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:635 lists AGI Work run as composer-mode dispatch on web, desktop and mobile.)
purpose.who_uses_it: Paying users (Pro plan and above) on web, desktop (which shows the hosted web app) and mobile; Chrome extension users on a qualifying plan.
problems_solved: The person can state the outcome they want and the boundaries once, instead of steering through many chat turns.
The run is a recorded, resumable task that survives closing the tab (AGI Work is the only mode that expects to outlive the tab, apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:4730-4738).
The wanted deliverable and constraints are passed to the planning step and the agent, so the plan targets them.
use_cases: Research three competitors and write a one-page comparison (the mobile sheet placeholder text, apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/components/StartWorkSheet.tsx:133).
Build a spreadsheet or report file from public sources with code execution switched off.
Re-run a finished task: mobile prefills the sheet with the original goal (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/CloudTasksScreen.tsx:596-616).
Start work from a project so the task has that project's sources.

Type the goal. Optionally add constraints and a deliverable (web/desktop, mobile).

established.statement: The user can open a dedicated entry to describe and start an agentic work task (not a plain chat turn) and it starts a real agent run. Status in brief: web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code done; Chrome missing.
The user states the objective of the task; it is stored with the run and shown back.
The user can specify what deliverable the task should produce and the run receives it. Brief: web, desktop, mobile done; CLI, VS Code, Chrome missing.
Each work task shows a readable title in the task list.
AGI Work run is a composer-mode dispatch, live on web, desktop and mobile; N/A on CLI and VS Code.
Work (and the other Cloud destinations) is Cloud only on mobile; Local shows only what works on the phone with no account.

acceptance_criteria: A paid account on web can switch to Work, send a goal, and the request carries work_mode agiwork and agi_work_goal.goal equal to the message.
An empty or whitespace goal never creates a run (mobile: no conversation is created, start-cloud-work-run.test.ts); a goal over 2000 characters is refused by the server, not silently cut.
Empty constraints or deliverable are stored the same as missing ones (agiwork-plan.ts:37-46).
A free account sending work_mode agiwork gets HTTP 403 and no run starts; the Work toggle is hidden or reset to Chat.
After a successful start the run appears in the Tasks list with a title and the goal card shows the goal text, constraints and deliverable.
On mobile a rejected send shows 'This task could not be started' and the sheet stays open.
inferred: The brief says the run record stores the objective; in code the objective is stored in the goal journal event and the work_plans row, not in the run row. [inferred from cloud-agent-run-service.ts:755-790 and work-plan-steps.ts:29-36]
Web, desktop and Chrome Work sends always stop for plan review first; mobile New task does not. [inferred from useChatStream.ts:4669-4670 and chatExecutionStore.ts:3451]
proposed: [proposed] Send constraints, deliverable and excluded tools from Chrome, and send the plan-review flag from the mobile New task sheet so all surfaces behave the same.
[proposed] Put maxLength on the mobile sheet fields to match the server limits.
[proposed] Store a short readable title on the run itself so every surface shows the same title.

steps.what_happens: Person types the goal in Work mode (web/desktop/Chrome) or fills the New task sheet (mobile). The client builds the goal object.
Client posts to the Cloud chat completions endpoint with work_mode agiwork, the goal, and a plan-approval flag (web, Chrome) or none (mobile sheet).

Server applies Work mode (stream on, tool switches from excluded tools), creates a run row, opens the work_plans row and starts the tool loop, which emits the goal event first.
The planning model call and the work model calls run on the routed provider.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The model is the one the person picked (web footer picker, mobile selected cloud model or the tier default). Routing treats Work turns as the 'agentic' task type (request-processor.ts:1040). The server calls the routed provider for the planning turn and every work step, with failover. No model identifiers are written here; they come from the model catalog (doc: AGENTS.md section 4).

access_and_usage.account: A signed-in managed Cloud account is required. Free trial and free accounts are refused with 403 free_trial_feature_unavailable (request-processor.ts:4405-4419). Web hides the toggle for free trial (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1062-1066).
access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace feature gate 'work' is applied to Work requests (request-processor.ts:3181 workspaceFeaturesForChatRequest); tool approvals follow the account policy (see F060-06). Role rules inside a workspace: not traced.
access_and_usage.subscription: agi_work belongs to pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium and enterprise (billing-catalog.ts:341,354). A lower plan gets 403 agi_work_plan_required with requiredTier pro (request-processor.ts:1486-1503).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Runs are metered in managed usage credits; a Work turn takes a 86,400 second usage lease instead of 900 (request-processor.ts:1526-1536). When credits are used up the composer shows a WorkUsageCard (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5080-5110). Exact credit price per run: unknown.
access_and_usage.flags: Capability kill switch canUseAgiWork (kill-switches.ts:31, request-processor.ts:5217-5219); capability gate in the client via useCapability('canUseAgiWork') (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1057); user setting defaultWorkMode.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Work needs a model that can call tools; the server decides tool capability per model (request-processor.ts, clarify offer uses resolvedModelCaps.tools at 5598-5602). Which catalog models are excluded: unknown.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Work runs use the managed Cloud route. Whether an own-key provider can run Work on web: not traced (unknown). Web plan-decision code refuses to resend for Local or own-key conversations (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:6322-6334), which suggests Work is Cloud only there. [inferred]
access_and_usage.local_mode: Mode:local cannot start AGI Work. Mobile forces a Cloud model for the run (startWork.ts:38-42), and Work is listed as Cloud only on mobile (doc: docs/decisions/2026-11-13-founder-decisions.md:91-96). Local inference on mobile and desktop stays free of any subscription; Work is a Cloud feature behind a paid plan. Web own-key and desktop local routes: unknown.

features.summary: Before an AGI Work run starts, the person can pick what it may read (project, files, connectors, folder), switch web search or code execution off, pick the model and the reasoning effort. Web and desktop have all of these; mobile has only a model and a project; Chrome has model and effort. Only desktop can let the run use the computer.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person bound a Work run: which sources it can use, which of two tool groups stay on (web search with fetch, code execution), whether device steps may run on this computer (desktop), which model runs it and how much reasoning effort it uses.
purpose.why_it_exists: Work runs act with tools and spend usage credits. Scope controls reduce surprise and cost and keep private sources out unless chosen. (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:768-780 requires approval prompts for cloud spend and for sending local context to a provider.)
purpose.who_uses_it: Paid users on web, desktop and mobile; Chrome users for model and effort.
problems_solved: Keep a task from searching the web or running code when the person does not want that.
Choose a stronger or cheaper model for one task.
Let the desktop app use approved local folders and apps, or keep the whole task in the cloud.
use_cases: Draft a report from a project's files only: select the project, turn off web search.
Analyse a spreadsheet in a chosen working folder on desktop with 'Use this computer' on.
Run a quick low-effort task on a fast model.
Run a long research task with high effort.

established.statement: While composing a task the user can choose which sources it may use (project, files, connectors). Brief: web, desktop, CLI, VS Code done; Chrome missing (mobile not listed).
The user can choose which tools the task may use before it runs. Brief: mobile and Chrome missing.
The user can choose where the task executes (cloud sandbox versus this computer or another device). Brief: only desktop done.

Approval prompts are required for sending local workspace context to a provider and for Cloud spend or usage-credit actions.
Model and provider choices come from the generated catalog, never from literals in consumers.

steps.what_happens: Person sets sources, tool switches, place, model and effort in the composer.
Client builds the request. On desktop the host context decides whether the device-host header is attached.
Server maps excluded tools to tool flags, routes the turn (task type agentic) to the chosen or auto-picked model, and builds the tool list.
If the model calls a device tool, the run pauses with a device checkpoint and waits for the desktop to run the step, then resumes.
Model calls run on the routed provider with the chosen effort.

features.summary: No person-facing spend cap, time limit or completion condition exists for AGI Work on any app. Only the CLI local agent has a per-turn spend cap (/budget and --max-budget-usd). The Cloud run is bounded by fixed system limits (100 steps, 120 tool calls, a 4-minute invocation clock with automatic continuation) that the person cannot set.

purpose.what_it_does: Intended: let the person cap what a task may spend and how long it may run, and name when it counts as finished. Today: the CLI stops a turn at a credit cap; the Cloud run stops at built-in limits.
purpose.why_it_exists: Agent runs can loop and spend credits. A cap, a clock and a definition of done keep cost and quality predictable. (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:768-780 requires approval for cloud spend or usage-credit actions.)
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI users for the cap; every Work user is protected by the system limits without choosing them.
problems_solved: Runaway cost on a long agent turn (CLI).
A run that never stops: system step, tool and time limits end or checkpoint it.
use_cases: In the CLI type /budget 20 to stop each turn at 20 credits.
Run the CLI one-shot with --max-budget-usd 1.5 so the run stops with a budget_exhausted status.
A Cloud Work run that reaches 100 steps stops with a clear error.

where_to_find_it: CLI: slash command /budget <credits>, /budget off, /budget alone (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:1429-1456) and flag --max-budget-usd (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:489-491).

features.summary: A running Work task shows its plan steps with a status (Not started, In progress, Done, Failed, Stopped), the step currently running, and read-only tool calls that run together grouped as 'parallel'. features.summary: A Work run can stop to ask the person something or to get permission. Clarifying questions are a card whose answers go back as the next message. Tool approvals and connector input pause the run durably; the person approves or denies (or answers a form) and the run resumes. Many Cloud accounts default to auto-approve, so prompts may not appear.

purpose.what_it_does: Offers a clarify card when a request is ambiguous, pauses the run when a tool needs approval or a connector needs input, and resumes the run with the person's decision.
purpose.why_it_exists: The agent should not guess on ambiguous goals or take risky actions without consent. (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:768-780 lists approval prompts for connector writes, shell, files, sending context to a provider and cloud spend.)
purpose.who_uses_it: Work users on web, desktop, mobile, CLI (local agent approvals), VS Code and Chrome.
problems_solved: Wrong assumptions on vague goals.
Unwanted writes, sends or purchases.
A connector that needs a missing value.
use_cases: The agent asks 'Which market?' with options and an 'Other' answer.
Approve a file write the agent wants to do.
Deny a send-email tool call and add guidance.
Fill a connector form on mobile while away from the desk.

steps.what_happens: The loop meets a tool the policy gates; it saves an approval checkpoint (messages, pending calls) and emits x_tool_approval_request; the run state becomes awaiting_input.
Client shows the card (chat, Tasks, mobile, VS Code) and the person decides, optionally adding guidance.

Client posts run_id and decisions to /approve; the server runs auth, managed compute gate, organisation policy gate and the workspace spend gate, claims the checkpoint, restores the request and resumes the loop.
The loop executes only approved calls (re-running every guard), adds denial results for rejected calls, and continues; the provider is called again.
Clarify: the model calls ask_clarifying_questions, the turn ends; the person answers; the answer is saved on the message and sent as the next user turn.

data.what: Approval, input and device checkpoints (pending calls, input requests, request state)
data.synced: Yes, shown on every surface that lists the run
data.retained_or_deleted: Pending only for 24 hours (approval, input) or 15 minutes (device); later retention: not traced

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The model decides when to ask or call a gated tool. Model quality affects how well questions are phrased (clarify service filters delivery-style questions). Approvals do not depend on a provider; resumed turns use the same routed provider.

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in owner of the run; approve and resume-input go through the auth gate.
access_and_usage.permissions: Policy: ask_every_time, auto_approve_read_only, autonomous; autonomous needs workspace permission (organizationPermitsAutonomousToolApprovals, tool-approval-policy.ts:80-95).
access_and_usage.subscription: Approvals have no plan gate found beyond Work. Free accounts cannot run Work, so no Work approvals.

features.summary: Lets a person change course on a running Work task in the cloud. They can queue a message the agent reads at its next step, pause at a step boundary, resume with optional guidance, or stop the run for good. Web, mobile, VS Code and Chrome reach it through the shared run API; the CLI and Chrome have only parts.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the person four controls over a cloud Work run (an AGI Work task that runs on our servers): send a message into the run (steer), ask it to pause, resume a paused run (optionally with guidance), and stop it. Each control is a call to the managed run API. The agent honours steer and pause at its next step, and a stop at its next step or at once if the run is waiting on a person.
purpose.why_it_exists: Work tasks run for minutes with the app closed. Without these controls the only choices are wait or lose the work. The product direction asks that Cloud work can be steered from another surface (doc: docs/product/definition.md:139).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people with a Work task in flight, on web, the Tauri desktop build, mobile, VS Code and Chrome. The CLI has its own local-turn controls.
problems_solved: A task heads the wrong way and the person would otherwise have to cancel and restart.
The person needs to stop spending on a run without destroying its progress (pause keeps a checkpoint).
A run is parked waiting on an approval or answer and must be ended from any device.
use_cases: Type 'use the 2024 figures only' into the steer box while a research-style Work task is running.
Pause a long task, type new guidance in the box under the paused row, press Resume.
Press Stop on a task that is heading the wrong way.
On a phone, pause a task from the detail sheet, then resume it later.

journey: 1. Start a Work task (see the start-of-task features). It appears on the list as Queued or Running.
2. Open the task. While it works the detail panel refreshes itself every 4 seconds and shows 'Updating automatically'.
3. To steer: type in 'Message the agent' and press Send. The message shows in the queue. At its next step the agent reads it and the journal shows a completed progress line.
4. To pause: press Pause. The badge changes to 'Pausing'. At the next step boundary the run becomes Paused. To change your mind before it pauses, press 'Keep working'.
5. To resume: optionally type guidance under the paused row, press Resume. The list is re-read and the run shows Resuming then Running.
6. To stop: press Stop. A run waiting on you is cancelled at once; a working run stops at its next step and shows Cancelled.
7. If the task finished before the agent read a queued message, press 'Send as new message' to move it into the chat.
feedback_and_outputs: Steer failure keeps the draft and shows an alert: 'Your message was not sent. The task keeps working without it.' or the server's text (TaskSteerSection.tsx:40-45).

Pause failure toast: 'Could not pause the task. It is still working.'; resume failure: 'Could not resume the task. It is still paused.' or 'Another device already resumed this task.'; stop failure: 'Could not stop the task. Check its activity before retrying.' (TasksPage.tsx:336-430).

Server refusals: pause 409 'Only a task that is still working can be paused. This one is waiting on you or has already stopped.'; steer 409 texts for a full queue, a Code task, or a non-working run (pause/route.ts:58-62; steer/route.ts:74-88).
Cancelled run keeps partial output; the assistant turn is marked stopped (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/stopped-run-turn.ts).
settings: Layout List or Board is remembered per device in browser storage key agi-tasks-layout (TasksPage.tsx:~88-99).

working: Steer: POST /api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/{runId}/steer validates 1 to 4,000 characters, blocks or redacts secrets, then appends to the run's pending_steer list (max 10) only while the state is queued, planning, running or resuming and no pause or cancel is pending (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/[runId]/steer/route.ts:50-90; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:2798-2853; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/cloud-agent-runs.ts:81).

The agent reads queued steers at the top of every loop step and again before ending its answer on a Work turn, adds them as user messages and journals a 'steer:<id>' progress line (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:6736-6738,7436-7453,5309-5324).

Pause: POST .../pause sets pause_requested_at only for executor-held states (queued, planning, running, resuming) with no cancel pending, else 409 (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:2727-2744; pause/route.ts:41-62).

At the next step boundary the tool loop emits task-state-changed paused and lifecycle paused, saves a 'pause' checkpoint (messages, event cursor, completed steps) and sets the run to paused (tool-loop.ts:6702-6735; cloud-agent-run-service.ts:2928-3028; apps/web/lib/workflows/start-cloud-agent-workflow.ts:435-466).

Resume: POST .../resume first withdraws a pause not yet reached; otherwise runs the managed compute, organization policy and spend gates, blocks secrets in guidance, claims the pause checkpoint, re-checks workspace controls and the saved context policy, then continues the tool loop with the guidance as a user message (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/[runId]/resume/route.ts:157-356; tool-loop.ts:6670-6681).

Cancel: POST .../runs/{runId} records cancellation_requested_at; a run parked on a person is ended immediately and its pending checkpoint resolved; a working run is stopped at its next step; the provider call already in flight, committed tool side effects and committed connector writes cannot be undone (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/[runId]/route.ts:69-109; cloud-agent-run-service.ts:3107-3197; tool-loop.ts:6698-6701).
Shared UI wires all four controls for web and the Tauri desktop build (TasksPage.tsx:336-430,788-826; TaskSteerSection.tsx).
Mobile wires steer, pause, resume, stop (with confirmation) and send-as-new-message (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/store.ts:390-483; CloudRunSteerSection.tsx; CloudTasksScreen.tsx:626-635,846-847).
VS Code wires steer (input box) and stop (modal confirmation) (cloudRunDetail.ts:265-333).

Chrome wires stop with an inline confirmation and confirms the run reached a terminal state (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/tasksSheet.ts:90-122; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedRunControl.ts:429-449).

CLI: while a turn runs, typed lines queue ('type to queue a message') and are sent after the turn; Esc or Ctrl-C cancels, saves the partial turn and returns queued lines to the composer (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2064-2074,7274-7275,8482,8756-8761; apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8618-8629).
CLI app-server host exposes cloud/turn/stop and cloud/turn/resume for a paused run (crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/developer_session.rs:166-167; apps/cli/src/app_server/cloud_turns.rs:512,590).
incomplete: Mobile pause shows only for state running, and mobile resume sends no guidance (CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx:588-606; apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/service.ts:89-91).

A queued steer can be withdrawn only after the run has ended; while the run is open the server answers 'It stays queued until the task reads it' (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:2892-2900; steer/[steerId]/route.ts:61-65).
Web Stop fires with no confirmation although a cancelled run cannot be resumed (TasksPage.tsx:826; cloud-agent-run-service.ts:3195).
disconnected_or_disabled: The inline (non-durable) completions path passes cancellation and steer readers to the tool loop but no pause reader or pause checkpoint saver, so a pause requested on a run executing there would not be honoured (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:1088-1095; tool-loop.ts:6702). Which runs take that path is unknown.
The Board layout of the shared page passes steer and stop handlers but its row controls live in TasksBoard.tsx, which was not opened.
not_available: Pause: not available on VS Code (detail client picks only getRun, resumeRun, cancelRun, steerRun; cloudRunDetail.ts:35-38), Chrome, or the CLI terminal UI (no pause for a turn; 'Pause' in lib.rs:1572,1676 pauses schedules and triggers).
Resume of a paused cloud run: not available on VS Code or Chrome. CLI resume (/resume, /load) reloads a saved local session (apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:177; registry.rs:200).
Resume of a stopped (cancelled) run: not possible; CLOUD_AGENT_RUN_CANCELLATION states resumable false (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:3195).
Steer from Chrome: not available. Steer into a Code task is refused with a pointer to its Code session (steer/route.ts:74-78).

established.statement: The user can redirect a running task with new guidance without starting over, on all apps.
The user can pause a running task at a step boundary and it keeps its work.
The user can resume a paused or stopped task from where it left off.
The user can stop a running task and the run is cancelled on the server.
Cloud work can be steered from another surface while the trusted host stays authoritative for local access.
Chat lifecycle actions including stop must preserve message lineage after reload.
An action a user cannot undo asks first, and the question names the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: Steering a Running task shows the message as queued, and after the next step the journal has a 'steer:' progress line with the same text.
A message of 4,001 characters or an empty one is refused; a message containing an API key pattern is blocked with the secret message.
Pause on a Running task returns 202 and the row shows 'Pausing'; within one step the state is Paused and Resume continues from the saved step count.
Pause on a task waiting on approval returns 409 with the 'Only a task that is still working...' text.
Stop on a task waiting for approval makes it Cancelled at once and a later resume attempt fails.
Every Stop on every app asks first and names what is lost (cannot be resumed).
A second device resuming the same pause gets 'Another device already resumed this task.' and no second run starts.
inferred: Pause, steer and stop are entitlement-free once a run exists, because no plan check was found in those routes [inferred from the route code].
A Local session has no cloud run, so these controls do not apply to it [inferred from DesktopTasks.tsx:51-53].
proposed: [proposed] Ask before Stop on web and Tauri, like mobile, VS Code and Chrome.
[proposed] Add Pause and Resume (with guidance) to VS Code and Chrome, and guidance to mobile resume.
[proposed] Allow withdrawing a queued steer while the run is live, or say plainly in the UI that it cannot be taken back.

steps.what_happens: Person presses Send, Pause, Resume or Stop; the app calls the managed run client with the account token and, on web, a CSRF header.
The route rate-limits (bucket llm-completion), checks CSRF, opens a user-scoped database connection and validates ids.
Steer: secret-handling gate, then an update appends the message to pending_steer if the run is in an executor-held state with no pause or cancel pending and fewer than 10 queued.
Pause and cancel only set timestamps (pause_requested_at, cancellation_requested_at); an audit event agent_run_lifecycle_changed is written.

The executor (tool loop, running in the durable workflow or inline) checks cancel, then pause, then takes steers at each step; on pause it saves a checkpoint and stops; on cancel it ends the turn as cancelled.
A run parked on a person (awaiting input, approval or paused) is cancelled directly by the route, its pending checkpoint failed and a cancelled event journaled.

Resume claims the pause checkpoint, rebuilds the request from the checkpoint, runs the model through the tool loop again with the guidance as a user message, and streams events; the client discards the stream and re-reads the list and journal.
The shared page polls the run journal every 4 seconds while the selected run is live and shows the new state.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: These controls are model-agnostic: they act on the run row and the loop, not on a model. A steer or guidance becomes a user message to whatever model the run already uses. Resume continues under the model selection saved in the pause checkpoint (test: apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/[runId]/resume/route.test.ts:319). If the first model fails, the loop can fail over to another (tool-loop failover option, start-cloud-agent-workflow.ts:423-429). Provider and billing details are in SYS-inference-providers.

access_and_usage.account: A signed-in AGI account is required on every app. Rows are scoped to the owner (user_id) and to the active workspace for steer and withdraw (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:2809,2893).
access_and_usage.permissions: Web requires a CSRF token for cookie sessions on steer, withdraw, pause and cancel (pause/route.test.ts:73; steer/route.test.ts:229). A cross-tenant run answers 404, not 403 (pause/route.test.ts:65).
access_and_usage.subscription: Starting a Work run needs the canUseAgiWork capability (agi_work, plans pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise; billing-catalog.ts:341,354). Steer, pause and cancel routes contain no plan check. Resume runs the managed compute gate, the organization policy gate and the spend-limit gate and settles a Free-plan reservation if the continuation cannot start (resume/route.ts:165-189; resume/route.test.ts:392-432).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Steer: 4,000 characters, 10 queued per run. Pause, steer, withdraw and cancel share the llm-completion limit (30 per minute per user, fail closed); reading a run uses agent-run-follow (120 per minute) (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:359,374). A resumed turn takes a managed turn slot and managed usage reservation (resume/route.ts:420-424,286-312).
access_and_usage.flags: Mobile: FEATURES.cloudTasks (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:10). No other flag found for these controls.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: None found in the code for steer, pause or cancel. Resume re-renders under the saved model selection.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: none found in the code for steer, pause, cancel. Whether an own-key (BYOK) turn creates a run record at all is unknown.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Local mode has no cloud run: the Tauri Tasks panel is not shown in local privacy mode and says local sessions are not listed (DesktopShellV3.tsx:790; DesktopTasks.tsx:51-53). The CLI controls in this page act on a local turn and need no subscription or sign-in (tui_app.rs:2074).

features.summary: After a Work task ends, the person can run it again from a loaded draft: web and the desktop build offer 'Re-run this task', mobile offers 'Run again'. On web a failed or stopped plan step offers 'Retry from this step', which sends a new message for that step onward. There is no one-click restart that resumes the same run.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns a finished or failed Work task into a new task. 'Retry from this step' starts a new Work turn whose plan begins at the failed step. 'Re-run this task' (web, Tauri desktop) and 'Run again' (mobile) put the original goal back into the composer or start sheet so the person can edit and send it.
purpose.why_it_exists: A task can fail on step 3 of 5, or the person wants the same job again next week. Rewriting the goal is slow and loses constraints and deliverable.
purpose.who_uses_it: People with a finished, failed or cancelled Work task on web, desktop and mobile.
problems_solved: Retyping a long goal with its constraints and deliverable.
Redoing earlier plan steps that already succeeded.
Seeing exactly what will be sent before a re-run starts.
use_cases: Step 4 of a report failed; press 'Retry from this step' to run steps 4 onward.
Open last week's finished task and press 'Re-run this task', then change the date range.
On mobile open a completed task and press 'Run again' to review the request in the start sheet.

where_to_find_it: Web chat: on a Work message whose run has finished, a card 'Retry a step' shows the first failed or stopped plan step and the button 'Retry from this step' (apps/web/features/chat/components/work-session/AgiWorkPlanReview.tsx:51-79; mounted at apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:2644).

Web /tasks and Tauri Tasks: in the detail panel 'Goal' box, button 'Re-run this task', shown only when the task is not live, is a Work task, the host supplies rerunWork and the journal has a goal (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TaskDetailPanel.tsx:567-581; TasksPage.tsx:665).
Desktop (public Electron app): the hosted web app, so the web controls (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
Mobile: task detail sheet, button 'Run again' (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/components/CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx:608-616).
VS Code: only the chat command 'agi-workforce.retryLastMessage' that resends the last chat message (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/chat/retry.ts:4,55-72).
CLI: '/branch' or '/fork' copies the current local session; '/continue' asks the model to continue its last answer (apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:491; apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:185).
Chrome: none found.
prerequisites: Signed-in account; Work available on the plan (canUseAgiWork) for web and desktop composers (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:1057-1062; apps/desktop/src/features/v3/DesktopShellV3.tsx:254-259).
For 'Re-run this task': the task has a Goal entry in its journal and is not live.
For mobile 'Run again': the task is settled and has a conversation (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/taskActions.ts:15-17).
screens_and_controls: Retry card text: '<n>. <step description> · Failed|Stopped' with the button 'Retry from this step' (AgiWorkPlanReview.tsx:65-77).

Web re-run toast: 'Loaded this session's goal, constraints and deliverable into a new Work chat. Edit them if you like, then send to run it again.' (apps/web/features/tasks/components/TasksPage.tsx:68-70).
Tauri re-run toast: 'Loaded this task into a new AGI Work chat. Edit it if you like, then send to run it again.' (DesktopTasks.tsx:34-36).
Mobile start sheet opens with the original request prefilled; failures show alerts 'Could not run it again' (CloudTasksScreen.tsx:600-624,831).
journey: 1. Open a finished task or the failed Work message.
2. Web retry: press 'Retry from this step'. A new Work message 'Retry step N: <description>' is sent with the plan from step N onward.
3. Re-run: press 'Re-run this task' (web, desktop) or 'Run again' (mobile).
4. The composer or start sheet opens with the goal; web also restores constraints, deliverable and the tools that were switched off.
5. Edit if needed and send. A new run starts and appears in the task list.
feedback_and_outputs: Web re-run navigates to /chat with the draft and Work mode on and shows a success toast.
Mobile shows an alert if the original request cannot be found or loaded (CloudTasksScreen.tsx:609,618-621).
If the trial allowance is used up, web retry opens the upgrade dialog instead of sending (WebChatPage.tsx:6358-6361).
settings: Composer Work scope (constraints, deliverable, excluded tools) in the chat store (apps/web/features/tasks/components/TasksPage.tsx:56-65).

working: Web retry: the card appears for the first failed or cancelled plan step once the message stops streaming; the handler sends a new agiwork message with the original goal and the plan sliced from that step (AgiWorkPlanReview.tsx:51-56; apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:6363-6378).

Web re-run: rerunWork writes the goal to the pending draft, sets Work mode and the scope (constraints, deliverable, excluded tools), navigates to /chat and shows a toast (apps/web/features/tasks/components/TasksPage.tsx:53-71).
The goal text, 'Constraints:', 'Deliverable:' and 'Tools off:' lines are parsed from the goal journal entry (TaskDetailPanel.tsx:203-219,575).
Tauri re-run: builds a draft of goal plus Constraints and Deliverable lines and appends it to a new chat in Work mode (DesktopTasks.tsx:22-39; DesktopShellV3.tsx:797-802).

Mobile 'Run again': finds the user message nearest the run's start time across conversation pages, closes the sheet and opens the start sheet with it (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/taskActions.ts:19-47; CloudTasksScreen.tsx:600-624).
CLI '/branch' and '/fork' fork the saved local session into a new managed session named by the person or branch-<time> (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:1381-1426).
incomplete: 'Retry from this step' is a new turn, not a resume of the failed run's checkpoint, so earlier context is whatever the conversation holds (WebChatPage.tsx:6368-6374).
Tauri re-run drops the excluded tools that web restores (DesktopTasks.tsx:25-32 vs TasksPage.tsx:60-62 in apps/web/features/tasks/components).
Mobile re-run carries only the request text; constraints and deliverable are not carried (taskActions.ts:19-47) [inferred from the code returning message content only].
disconnected_or_disabled: The Tauri build re-run hook is only wired when the shell passes onRerunWork, which it does (DesktopShellV3.tsx:797); the public Electron app shows the web page instead.
not_available: No one-click 'restart with the same inputs' that starts immediately: every re-run is a draft the person must send.
No separate 'Duplicate' control exists on web or desktop; 'Re-run this task' covers both (TaskDetailPanel.tsx:579).
Retry step and re-run: not found on Chrome. Retry step: not found on mobile, VS Code or the CLI.
VS Code retry.ts resends the last chat message only; it is not a task restart (retry.ts:38-53).
Whether the Tauri desktop chat shows the plan retry card: unknown.

established.statement: After a step fails, the user can retry just that step and the task continues.
The user can restart a finished task with the same inputs.
The user can duplicate a task into a new editable task.
Product behaviour is shared by contracts; each surface owns only transport, permissions and presentation.

acceptance_criteria: A Work message with a failed or stopped plan step, not streaming, shows 'Retry from this step' on that step only.
Pressing it sends 'Retry step N: ...' with the plan starting at step N and the original goal.
Pressing it with the trial allowance used up opens the upgrade dialog and sends nothing.
'Re-run this task' is hidden while the task is live and when the host cannot start a run.
After 'Re-run this task' on web, the draft holds the goal and the constraints, deliverable and tool switches of the original.
Mobile 'Run again' is shown only for settled tasks and opens the start sheet with the original request; a missing request shows an alert.
inferred: A re-run creates a new run row with no link to the old one [inferred: nothing in the transport or draft code stores the source run id].
proposed: [proposed] Resume a failed step from the run's own checkpoint so earlier work is not re-sent.
[proposed] Carry excluded tools on Tauri and constraints and deliverable on mobile.
[proposed] Offer a plain 'Duplicate' that opens an editable copy and a 'Restart' that starts at once after a confirmation.

aliases: Save a task as a routine or a skill
features.summary: A finished Work task can become a routine: web and mobile open a prefilled schedule form from the task's goal. Saving a task as a skill by user action is not found on any app; the CLI instead learns skills on its own after repeated tool patterns. Desktop (Tauri), VS Code and Chrome have no routine control.

purpose.what_it_does: On web, 'Save as routine' opens the Schedules page with the task's goal, constraints and deliverable as the prompt. On mobile, 'Make it a routine' opens the new-schedule screen with the task's prompt and model. The CLI writes learned skill files by itself after it sees the same tool pattern in several sessions.
purpose.why_it_exists: A job done once is often wanted weekly. Re-creating it as a schedule by hand loses the exact wording.
purpose.who_uses_it: People who repeat a task; CLI users who want repeated procedures captured.
problems_solved: Retyping a goal into a schedule form.
Remembering the original constraints.
Capturing a repeated tool procedure without writing a skill file by hand.
use_cases: Turn a finished 'watch competitor prices' task into a weekly schedule.
On a phone, tap 'Make it a routine' on a completed task.
Use the CLI for several similar jobs and find a learned skill saved under the config folder.

Desktop (public Electron app): the hosted web app, same button (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
Desktop (Tauri): no button, the transport has no saveAsRoutine (apps/desktop/src/features/tasks/DesktopTasks.tsx:16-41).
Mobile: task detail sheet, button 'Make it a routine' (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/components/CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx:627-634).

Schedules on the account; the schedules page waits for billing to load and takes the plan tier (apps/web/features/schedules/components/SchedulesPageWithProjects.tsx:41-62). Which plans may create schedules: unknown.

features.summary: When a Work task ends, the person sees its result text, the files it produced with a download link, its cost, and, if it stopped short, how many plan steps were done and which remain. Web, the desktop build, mobile and VS Code show this; Chrome and the CLI show far less.

purpose.what_it_does: Reads the task's event journal and shows a final answer ('Result'), the produced files ('Outputs' on web, 'Files' on mobile, 'Outputs' in VS Code), the failure reason when it failed, cost and tokens, and for a task stopped by step limit, timeout, cancel or failure a count of steps done and a list of steps remaining.
purpose.why_it_exists: A person returns to a long task and needs to know what it produced and what is missing without reading the whole transcript.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who started a Work task, from any app, including a different app than the one that started it.
problems_solved: Finding the answer among many progress lines.

Knowing whether the task finished or stopped short, and what is left.

steps.what_happens: The executor produces files in a sandbox or via a provider; at the end of the turn it saves them as library assets and journals artifact-produced events.
At the end the loop advances the plan to done, stopped or failed and emits the final task state (ready_for_review, partial, timed_out, failed or cancelled).
The client reads the run journal in pages of 500 up to 8 pages and rebuilds the activity, plan, outputs and result from the events.
Pressing a file link requests /api/files/{id}; the server checks owner and allowance and returns or redirects to the bytes.
Mobile downloads the file to the device and opens the share sheet.

features.summary: A list of the account's Work tasks with title, state and time, kept on our servers so any signed-in app can open the same task. Web and the desktop build offer filters, a board view and unread marks; mobile has filters and search; VS Code and Chrome show the active tasks. Sharing opens the chat's share flow on web and mobile.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists the person's Work runs from the server, 25 at a time, newest update first, named by the conversation title. Selecting one opens its detail with a live journal. 'Share task' shares the task's chat as a link. Because runs live on the server, a task started on one device can be followed, answered and stopped from another.
purpose.why_it_exists: Work tasks outlive the app. The person needs one place to find what is running, what needs them and what finished, from any device (doc: docs/product/definition.md:139).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who runs Work tasks, on any app.
problems_solved: Losing track of long tasks.
Not knowing a task is waiting for approval.
Moving between laptop and phone mid-task.
Showing a result to someone else.
use_cases: Open Work history and press the 'Needs you' filter to answer an approval.
Start a task on the laptop, follow it on the phone.
Search tasks on mobile by title or first prompt.
Share a finished task's chat as a link.

where_to_find_it: Web: /tasks, titled 'Work history' with the line 'Your Cloud work sessions' (apps/web/app/tasks/page.tsx; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TasksPage.tsx:546-548).

established.statement: Each work task shows a readable title in the task list, and the user can set or change it.
The user can browse past tasks with their state and open any of them.
The user can share a task (its plan, steps and results) with someone else.
A task started on one device can be followed and acted on from another device.
Cloud work can be steered from another surface.
Chrome keeps browser-task history where allowed.

acceptance_criteria: A signed-in account sees its Work runs newest-updated first, 25 per page, with a working 'Show more'.
Each row shows a title (conversation title or 'Work' fallback), a state label and a relative time.
Filter 'Needs you' shows only awaiting input, approval and paused tasks, and they sort first in the Active list.
A task started on web appears on mobile and in VS Code after refresh; an approval answered on one device is refused on the other with the 'Another device' message.
'Share task' on a finished task opens a share flow for its chat; it is absent for live tasks.
Another account's run id returns 404.
The user can rename a task on at least the apps the requirement names, or the requirement is changed.
inferred: The list is for the signed-in account only; Local sessions are not Work runs [inferred from DesktopTasks.tsx:51-53].
proposed: [proposed] Show finished tasks in VS Code and Chrome by passing all states.
[proposed] Add a rename control to the Tasks detail on web, desktop and mobile.

steps.what_happens: The page asks the managed run client for a page of runs with the chosen states and a limit of 25.
The route rate-limits (agent-run-follow), validates states, limit, cursor and search text, opens a user-scoped database, and queries runs joined to conversations.
The server returns runs and an opaque next cursor; the page appends on 'Show more'.
Selecting a run reads its journal pages; while live, the page re-reads after the last sequence every 4 s.
'Share task' navigates to the chat with share=true; the chat page opens its share flow and POSTs /api/share, which applies the external sharing gate and outbound content inspection.
On another device the same list call returns the same rows because the run lives in the database, not on the starting device.

features.summary: Shows every saved agent by name, role description and look. In the CLI it is a file-based list and a picker overlay (name drawn in one of 8 colours). On web and mobile Cloud it is a server-backed Agents page with an icon and accent colour. The brief calls web and mobile missing; the code contradicts that.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists the agents a person can use, each with a name, a one-line role (description) and a visual identity, and lets them read the full definition. Two separate systems exist. CLI agents are markdown files found on disk. Cloud agents are database rows listed by the web Agents page and the mobile Agents screen.
purpose.why_it_exists: So a person can see what specialist assistants they have and pick one without remembering file names or ids. The brief item S61.01 requires a roster by name, S61.03 a name and avatar, S61.04 a role description the user can write and read back (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/061-persistent-agents-and-agent-rosters.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI users who keep reusable agent files per project or per machine; web and mobile Cloud users who build or receive shared agents; workspace members who see agents shared with them.
problems_solved: Finding the right agent among many without opening files.
Telling agents apart at a glance by colour or icon.
Seeing which agents are mine and which were shared with me.
Reading an agent's full definition before using it.
use_cases: In the CLI, type /agents, filter the overlay by typing a word after pressing /, then Enter to switch the session to that agent.
In the CLI, run /agents show reviewer to print the full definition and the file path.
On the web Agents page, open Your agents and press Chat on an agent.
On mobile in Cloud mode, open Agents from Customize and use the All, Yours, By AGI and Shared segments.

features.summary: Lets a person make, edit, rename, delete and retire agents. CLI: markdown files managed with /agents subcommands, no versioning. Web and mobile Cloud: editor with draft, publish, version restore, pause, retire, transfer and delete. Duplication of a person's own agent was not found anywhere.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates an agent, changes its fields, renames, pauses, retires, transfers or deletes it. CLI agents are files on disk. Cloud agents are database rows with a draft, numbered published versions and sharing.
purpose.why_it_exists: Agents are saved assets that a person tunes over time. The brief requires create (S61.02), versioned configuration (S61.21), duplication (S61.23) and retirement or transfer with history (S61.24) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/061-persistent-agents-and-agent-rosters.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI developers who keep agent files; web and mobile Cloud users and workspace owners who build and share agents.
problems_solved: Starting an agent from a blank file or a plain-words description.
Changing one field without hand-editing a file.
Keeping earlier versions and restoring one on web and mobile.
Taking an agent out of use without losing its history.
Handing an agent to another workspace member.
use_cases: Run /agents create reviewer to get a template file.
Describe an agent in words at the interactive prompt and let the model draft it.
On web, edit the draft, press Publish, share with the workspace, later Restore version 2.
On mobile, retire an agent that is no longer needed and bring it back later.

established.statement: The user can create a persistent agent that is saved and appears in the roster.
Changes to an agent's configuration are versioned and can be reviewed or restored.
The user can duplicate an agent as a starting point.
The user can retire an agent or transfer its ownership, keeping its history.
The user can pause or disable an agent so it stops acting until re-enabled.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence; an agent never destroys user data on its own; removed files go to the OS Trash first.

/agents set reviewer color teal fails and lists the 8 colours; the file is unchanged.
On web, Publish with no changes since the last version is refused with 'There are no changes to publish.'
On web, Restore version N puts that version's content into the draft and does not change published_version until Publish.
A retired agent cannot be edited until brought back, and Chat is disabled on it.
Transfer to a person outside the workspace fails with 'The agent can only move to another member of the workspace it belongs to.'

steps.what_happens: CLI create: slugify the name, create the directory, refuse if the file exists, write frontmatter and body.
CLI drafting: validates the session's privacy boundary, sends the description inside <agent_request> to the session's own model with a 90 second timeout, parses JSON, saves the file.
CLI set and rename: read file, replace one frontmatter line, write, re-parse; roll back on failure.
Web save: PATCH validates the model against the catalog and updates the draft columns, only for the owner and not when retired.
Web publish: inside one transaction, compares draft with last published, inserts the next version row, sets published_version.
Web write calls require a CSRF token and pass through the rate limiter.

features.summary: Gives each agent its own instructions and lets a person talk to it. In the CLI, activating an agent switches the current session and adds its instructions as a system message. On web and mobile Cloud, Chat opens a new conversation tied to the agent, and the server adds the instructions each turn.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores an agent's instructions and applies them to a chat. CLI: the session becomes that agent (no separate thread). Cloud: each chat is a conversation row linked to the agent and every turn is run as that agent.
purpose.why_it_exists: So one assistant can behave as a reviewer, a tutor or a writing editor with stable rules, as S61.05 and S61.13 require (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/061-persistent-agents-and-agent-rosters.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI users who start with --agent or the picker; web and mobile Cloud users who press Chat on an agent.
problems_solved: Repeating the same instructions in every chat.
Keeping a specialist's rules separate from the general assistant.
Starting a chat from conversation starters.
use_cases: Run agi --agent reviewer to start reviewing as that agent.
In a running CLI session, pick an agent in /agents and keep chatting with history intact.
On web, press Chat on an agent and use one of its starters.
On mobile, start a chat with a built-in By AGI agent such as the coding partner.

features.summary: Agents reuse the tools, connectors and skills the account already has, but each can be narrowed and capped. CLI: tool allow and deny lists, MCP servers, skills, max turns and a dollar cap. Web and mobile Cloud: connector and skill selection, three tool toggles, web domain rules, a daily message limit and a monthly credit limit.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets an agent use shared account-level tools and skills while restricting which ones and how much it may spend or run.
purpose.why_it_exists: S61.08 shared tools with per-agent limits, S61.09 shared skills visible to the user, S61.20 turn and spend limits that are enforced (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/061-persistent-agents-and-agent-rosters.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI users who want a read-only reviewer; workspace owners who want an agent that cannot use the web or cost too much.
problems_solved: Stopping an agent from using tools it should not.
Capping cost per agent.
Preloading the right skills.
Limiting how many messages people can send to an agent each day.
use_cases: Set tools to Read, Grep for a reviewer and maxBudgetUsd to 0.50.
Turn off web search and code execution for a policy-bound agent on web.
Allow only two connectors for a sales agent.
Set 'Messages a day, per person' to 20 for a shared support agent.

steps.what_happens: CLI: activation intersects tools, appends disallowed tools, replaces the MCP list, sets max turns, takes the lower spend cap and preloads skills.

Cloud: before applying an agent to a chat turn the server counts today's user messages and the month's spend and refuses over the cap.

features.summary: Per-agent memory, routines, a private workspace and a responsibility list. The brief calls all four missing. The code has two partial pieces on web and mobile Cloud: routines that run as an agent (Deployments), and up to 20 reference files per agent. No per-agent memory, no private computer and no responsibility list were found.

purpose.what_it_does: Would give each agent its own memory, scheduled routines, a workspace for its files and a list of what it owns. Today Cloud agents can own scheduled routines and carry reference files; nothing else of the four is built.
purpose.why_it_exists: S61.06, S61.07, S61.10 and S61.12 describe agents that persist over time like a team member (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/061-persistent-agents-and-agent-rosters.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web and mobile Cloud users who want an agent that runs on a schedule or reads fixed files; future users of persistent agents.
problems_solved: Running the same agent on a schedule without opening a chat.
Giving an agent reference material once instead of attaching it each chat.
use_cases: Add a weekly routine that runs a research agent every Monday.
Upload a style guide as Knowledge so a writing agent always has it.
See the agent's recent chats and routines under Activity.

features.summary: CLI only. With --team or AGI_TEAM=1 the lead model can start teammates that run in their own threads and sessions, message each other and the person, and share a task list. Without teams, the model can call the agent tool to list installed agents and run one as a one-off specialist that can only narrow the parent's authority.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets several agents work on one job. A lead spawns teammates (long-lived, message-driven) or runs a named specialist once and gets its result back.
purpose.why_it_exists: S61.14 group conversation, S61.15 coordinator pattern, S61.16 specialist delegation, S61.17 inter-agent messages visible to the user (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/061-persistent-agents-and-agent-rosters.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI developers running larger tasks; the model acts as lead.
problems_solved: Splitting a big task across helpers.
Keeping a specialist's tools and limits narrower than the lead's.
Letting a helper ask the person a question and wait.
Keeping total spend under one cap.
use_cases: Start agi --team, ask for a reviewer and a tester teammate, read their reports.
Ask the lead to run the installed security-reviewer agent once on a diff.
A teammate asks the person for a decision; the person answers with /team <name> <answer>.

where_to_find_it: CLI flag --team or env AGI_TEAM=1 (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:341-344, 8291-8292).
CLI slash command /team, /team <teammate> <message>, /team stop <teammate> (apps/cli/src/teams.rs:817-870).
Model tools spawn_teammate, send_message, read_messages, team_task, list_teammates (apps/cli/src/agent/tools.rs:8-14).
Model tool agent with action list or run (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs:1150-1175).
/subagents lists configured subagents read-only (apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:258; apps/cli/src/agents.rs:1657-1700).

Web: the endpoint /api/agents/collaboration answers 410 retired (apps/web/app/api/agents/collaboration/route.ts:20-27). VS Code: read-only subagent task group (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:560). Mobile, Chrome: none found.
prerequisites: Teams: start the CLI with --team or AGI_TEAM=1 (or true). Only the lead can spawn (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:1873-1880).
Named agent for a teammate or specialist must exist with the exact installed name (chat.rs:1889-1898; agents.rs:492-497).
screens_and_controls: /team prints Team, the lead line, each teammate as working, idle waiting for a message or stopped, Shared tasks and Recent messages (apps/cli/src/teams.rs:855-905).
Messages in the chat thread are shown as '<name> asks you' with 'Answer with /team <name> <your answer>.' for the person (teams.rs:608-624).
Task states pending, in_progress, completed, blocked (teams.rs:41-58).
journey: Start agi --team.
Ask the lead to get help; it calls spawn_teammate with name, prompt and optional agent.
The teammate runs in its own thread and session, works, and sends its final reply to the lead automatically.
The lead calls read_messages with wait_seconds to collect replies; teammates and the person can message each other.
Use /team to see status; /team stop <name> to stop one.
One-off specialist: the lead calls agent with action list, then action run with name and prompt; the result returns to the lead.

Not lead: 'Only the team lead can spawn teammates.' (chat.rs:1879).
Reserved name: ''lead' is reserved; pick another teammate name' (teams.rs:415).
Bad name: 'Invalid teammate name ...: only ASCII letters, digits, '_' and '-' are allowed' (teams.rs:111-125).
Stopped teammate: 'Teammate 'x' has stopped and will not read new messages.' (teams.rs:359-363).
Unknown recipient: lists current teammates plus lead and user (teams.rs:342-357).
Run failure: 'I could not start: <error>' sent to the lead (teams.rs:690-697 area).
settings: Team mode flag and env var (lib.rs:341-344).
Teammate turn cap 15 and subagent depth 3, concurrent 7 (subagent.rs:429-453).
Transcript kept to the last 200 messages (teams.rs:12).

working: Teams: TeamManager registers teammates, mailboxes, shared tasks, a bounded transcript and spend pool (apps/cli/src/teams.rs:133-295).
spawn_teammate checks team mode, lead-only, name and prompt, optional named agent, session spend headroom, then launches (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:1866-1940).
launch validates the name against a strict safe-character check and rejects lead and user (teams.rs:412-417).

Each teammate runs on its own OS thread with its own runtime and a child session from the lead's inherited route; a route leaving the lead's privacy mode is refused (teams.rs:420-458, 687-700; apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:49-72).
Teammate reports its final reply to the lead automatically and goes idle; it wakes on new messages (teams.rs:772-806).
Messages from other agents are labelled 'another agent on your team, not the person' and the teammate brief says they never count as the person's approval (teams.rs:641-667).
send_message rejects a spoofed sender when the acting identity is known (teams.rs:915-950).
Shared task list with pending, in_progress, completed, blocked and a dependencies field (teams.rs:518-560).

agent tool: list returns a catalog capped at 200 agents and about 18 KB without prompt bodies, paths, model or permission mode (apps/cli/src/agents.rs:500-535); run is handled by the foreground subagent path with name length and prompt size (100,000 bytes) checks (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:2917-2965).
A named specialist can only narrow: model and permission overrides ignored, tools intersected, deny lists joined, max turns can only go down, MCP intersected (apps/cli/src/agents.rs:196-246).
Teammate and specialist runs are logged to subagents.jsonl (teams.rs:787-799; apps/cli/src/subagent_audit.rs:98-122).
Hooks: TeammateIdle fires when a teammate goes idle (teams.rs:567-590).
incomplete: Task dependencies are stored but add_task and update_task enforce nothing about them (teams.rs:518-560) [inferred from reading the functions].
TeamManager is in memory only; the team, mailboxes and tasks are not persisted across CLI runs (teams.rs:133-146) [inferred].
spawn_teammate in TeamManager registers the roster and its doc comment says a future version could spawn a child session; launch() does the real start (teams.rs:296-325, 412-458).
Messages from another agent only reach the lead through read_messages polling (teams.rs:1082-1150) [inferred].
disconnected_or_disabled: Team tools are not offered unless --team or AGI_TEAM is set; spawn_teammate is hidden from teammates (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:917-919, 1065-1068).
The web endpoint /api/agents/collaboration is retired (410) (apps/web/app/api/agents/collaboration/route.ts:20-27).
The agent tool is removed when the session cannot own child tasks (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:1062-1064).
not_available: Web, Mobile, Chrome, Tauri desktop: no agent teams found. Desktop BackgroundAgentsPanel lists background runs, not teams (apps/desktop/src/features/agi/BackgroundAgentsPanel.tsx).
Group conversation UI with several agents on any app other than the CLI thread.
/api/agents/communication on web was listed but its handler was not opened.

established.statement: Several agents can take part in one conversation with the user.
A coordinator agent routes work to other agents and reports back.
An agent can delegate part of a task to a specialist agent and use its result.
Agents can send each other messages that the receiving agent acts on, visible to the user.
A subagent never leaves its parent's trust boundary.
A message from another agent never counts as the person's approval.

acceptance_criteria: Without --team, calling spawn_teammate returns 'Agent teams are off. Start agi with --team or AGI_TEAM=1.'
A teammate trying spawn_teammate gets 'Only the team lead can spawn teammates.'
spawn_teammate with name lead or ../x is refused.
Sending a message to an unknown teammate fails and names who can be addressed.
A teammate's final reply appears in the lead's inbox without an explicit send.
A specialist run with an agent whose file sets a bypass permission mode still runs in the parent's mode.
The agent list for the model never contains prompt bodies or paths and holds at most 200 agents.
Stopping a teammate with /team stop makes later messages to it fail.
inferred: Dependencies should block a task from starting until they are completed [inferred from the dependencies field].
The person should be able to see teammate threads in each app that offers teams [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Persist team state or document that it is per session.
[proposed] Enforce task dependencies.
[proposed] Offer the same lead and teammate pattern on web through the Cloud agent runs, if wanted.

steps.what_happens: The lead model calls spawn_teammate; the handler checks team on, lead-only, name, prompt and named agent, and the lead's remaining spend.
launch registers the teammate and starts a thread with its own runtime and a child session built from the lead's route.
The teammate applies its named definition (narrowing only), adds a team brief, and runs a turn with the session's model.
On finish the final reply is sent to the lead, an audit line is written, spend is recorded in the pool and the teammate goes idle, waiting for messages.
A named specialist run goes through the foreground subagent manager with depth, concurrency and turn limits and returns its output to the parent.

features.summary: The plan is a status (working, idle, offline) beside each saved agent and a switch to pause or disable it. Neither exists for saved agents on any app. Only live teammates in a CLI team session have a status and a stop command, and those vanish when the session ends.

purpose.what_it_does: Planned: show whether each persistent agent is working, idle or offline in the agent roster, and let the user switch an agent off until switched back on. Today the CLI has a narrower thing: live teammates in an agent-team session carry an Active, Idle or Completed status, shown by /team, and can be stopped with /team stop. (brief S61.11, S61.19; apps/cli/src/teams.rs:24-26)
purpose.why_it_exists: A person who owns several agents needs to see which one is busy and needs a way to make one stop acting without deleting it. (brief S61.11, S61.19 'Should')
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI users who start a session with --team (or AGI_TEAM=1) and let the lead spawn teammates. Saved-agent owners on every app would use the planned version. (apps/cli/src/teams.rs:819)
problems_solved: Not knowing whether a teammate is still working or waiting for a message (apps/cli/src/teams.rs:855-857).
Stopping a teammate that is running up cost or going the wrong way (apps/cli/src/teams.rs:460-467).
Lets a user hook automation to the moment a teammate goes idle (apps/cli/src/teams.rs:566-590).
use_cases: In a team session, type /team to see 'alice: researcher, working' or 'idle, waiting for a message'.
Type /team stop alice to end a runaway teammate.
Configure a TeammateIdle hook that runs a script whenever a teammate finishes a turn.
Planned: pause a nightly-report agent for a week without deleting it. [proposed]
