features.summary: Shows the child agents (subagents) that a coding session started. The command-line app lists them with id, role, status and description. The VS Code side panel and the web Code page show a Subagents group with title and state. Nothing draws a tree. Children are started by the model, not by clicks.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person see which child agents a parent coding session spawned and what state each one is in. The command-line app prints a list (id, role, status, description). The VS Code sidebar and the web Code page (local developer sessions) show a 'Subagents (n)' group with each child's title and state. The parent-child link is only a flat list inside one session (apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:101; apps/web/features/code/components/LocalSessionPanel.tsx:174).
purpose.why_it_exists: When the model fans work out to several children, the person needs to know they exist, which are still running and which failed, otherwise work happens invisibly. The product contract says progress, including subagents, must be visible typed data (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md, rule 6).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using AGI Workforce CLI, the VS Code extension, or the local developer session view on web. Testers checking multi-agent behaviour.
problems_solved: Children run on their own threads and would otherwise be invisible (apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:700-722).
The person can see a failed or still-running child without reading the whole chat.
Runaway fan-out is bounded and the person is told why a spawn was refused (apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:609-660).
use_cases: In the CLI, ask for a review split across three files, then type /tasks to see three children running.
In VS Code, open a resumed conversation and read 'Subagents (3) · 1 running · 1 done · 1 failed'.
Check that a child that hit the spend cap or depth limit was refused with a clear message.

where_to_find_it: CLI (TUI and plain REPL): slash commands /tasks and /task, alias subcommands list and ls (apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:267-271; apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:484-530).
VS Code: the 'Subagents' collapsible group above the composer in the AGI Code sidebar (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:3176).
Web: 'Subagents (n)' group inside the local developer session panel on the Code page (apps/web/features/code/components/LocalSessionPanel.tsx:174-203, mounted at :1606).

Desktop: no desktop-specific list found. The Electron desktop starts the local runtime (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerSessionService.ts) and, per AGENTS.md section 5, shows the hosted web app, so the web group is [inferred] reachable there; not verified.
Mobile and Chrome: not available. No child-agent view found.
prerequisites: CLI: the session must be persisted, otherwise the task tool is not offered to the model (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:1064; can_own_child_tasks at :2508).
The model must decide to call the task tool; the person cannot start a child by clicking (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:2975-3070).
VS Code and web: a local developer session that ran subagents (apps/extension-vscode/src/__tests__/subagents.webview.test.ts, 'stays hidden until a session ran subagents').
screens_and_controls: CLI /tasks [list | show <id> | transcript <id> | stop <id>] (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:567).
CLI TUI line '⧉ N subagents working at once' shown while more than one task or agent cell runs (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2977-2996).

VS Code summary text 'Subagents (3) · 1 running · 1 done · 1 failed'; per row title and state label; Stop and Transcript buttons (apps/extension-vscode/src/__tests__/subagents.webview.test.ts; webviewContent.ts:3510-3545).
Web summary 'Subagents (n) · ...' and rows 'title · State'; a paused child shows 'Interrupted work is kept for review and will not restart on its own.' (LocalSessionPanel.tsx:181-196).
journey: 1. The person sends a coding request in a persisted CLI, VS Code or web local session.
2. The model calls the task (or agent) tool. The CLI starts a child on its own thread and prints '[task] Spawning subagent ...' outside the TUI (apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:709-716).
3. The person types /tasks (CLI) or opens the Subagents group (VS Code, web) to see each child.
4. The row shows running until the child finishes, then completed, failed or cancelled.
5. For details the person types /tasks show <id> (see F062-02) or opens the transcript (F062-03).
feedback_and_outputs: Empty CLI list: 'No subagent tasks in this session yet. Tasks appear here after the model calls the `task` tool to spawn a subagent.' (apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:102-106).
CLI list row: id, role, [status], description; a blank description reads '(no description)' (subagent.rs:107-115).
Failed child: status text 'failed: <error>' (subagent.rs:86-93).
VS Code and web state words: Queued, Running, Waiting for input, Interrupted, Done, Stopped, Failed (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/developer-session.ts:161-169).
VS Code and web hide the group when no child exists; the VS Code group folds when all are finished (subagents.webview.test.ts).
settings: CLI subagent limits are constants, not settings: 7 at once, depth 3, 15 turns per child (apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:429-453).
A session spend cap, when set, limits spawning (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:3005-3008).
Named agent definitions can set the child's role label and options (apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:1130; apps/cli/src/agents.rs). Their file format was not read in full.

working: CLI: /tasks list prints id, role, status, description for each child, sorted by id (apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:885-899; registry.rs:515-523).
CLI: role label is the named agent's name, else 'general-purpose' (subagent.rs:99, :693-697).
CLI: at most 7 children run at once; the 8th spawn is refused with 'Maximum concurrent subagents reached' (subagent.rs:429, :641-657).
CLI: nesting stops at depth 3 with 'Maximum subagent nesting depth reached' (subagent.rs:453, :612-619).
CLI: a session spend cap refuses new children when used up ('Session spend cap reached ...') and caps each child at an even share (subagent.rs:620-632).
CLI: a child runs on exactly its parent's provider and privacy mode and is refused if the route leaves that boundary (subagent.rs:23-70).

CLI app server publishes each child as a DeveloperChildTask (id, parentSessionId, title, state, timestamps, transcriptAvailable) to clients (crates/agiworkforce-protocol/bindings/DeveloperChildTask.ts; apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:2587-2600).
VS Code sidebar renders the Subagents group from that data (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:6258-6270).
Web local developer session panel renders the same group (apps/web/features/code/components/LocalSessionPanel.tsx:174).
incomplete: The list is flat; no app draws a parent-child tree. The link is the session itself.
VS Code and web rows carry no role label, model or cost because DeveloperChildTask has no such fields (DeveloperChildTask.ts).
Web group has no Stop or Transcript control; VS Code has both (LocalSessionPanel.tsx:187-200 vs webviewContent.ts:3519-3545).
/tasks list also prints background shell terminals under the child list (registry.rs:515-521); that is not an agent list.
disconnected_or_disabled: The task tool is removed from the model's tools when the session is not persisted (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:1063-1065).
not_available: Web (cloud chat), Mobile, Chrome: no child-agent list found.
Desktop (Tauri DesktopTasks): lists Cloud runs only, no child agents (apps/desktop/src/features/tasks/DesktopTasks.tsx).
The brief (S62.01-S62.03) marks web, desktop and VS Code as missing; code found contradicts that for VS Code and web local sessions (see gaps).

established.statement: A parent task visibly owns the child agents it spawned and the user can see that relationship.
The user sees a list of the child agents working under a task.
Each child agent is labelled with its role.
Progress, including subagents, is typed durable data and capability honesty is absolute: a disabled control is better than a no-op.
A child never leaves its parent's trust boundary.

acceptance_criteria: In a persisted CLI session with no children, /tasks prints the 'No subagent tasks in this session yet' text.
After the model spawns two children, /tasks shows two rows with id, role and status, sorted by id.
Spawning an 8th concurrent child is refused with the 'Maximum concurrent subagents' message.
A session at depth 3 cannot spawn; the message names the depth limit.
With a spend cap already used up, a spawn is refused with 'Session spend cap reached'.
In VS Code, a resumed conversation with three children shows 'Subagents (3) · ...' with state words.
A child started in a Local session never uses a cloud provider.
inferred: [inferred] Role labels should reach VS Code and web rows, since the CLI already has the role and the brief expects labels on every app.
[inferred] The Electron desktop shows the web group because it loads the hosted web app (AGENTS.md section 5).
proposed: [proposed] Add role and model fields to DeveloperChildTask so VS Code and web match the CLI list.
[proposed] Indent children under their parent turn, if a tree is wanted.

steps.what_happens: Model calls the task tool; CLI checks the session is persisted and builds a child description and prompt.
SubagentManager refuses if depth, spend cap or concurrency limit is hit, else starts a dedicated OS thread with its own async runtime.
Child session is created on the parent's exact route and privacy mode; its prompt is sent to the parent's provider (Local, own key or Cloud).

CLI /tasks reads the manager's in-memory entries; VS Code and web read the published tasks and redraw the group.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: A child uses the same model, provider and privacy mode as its parent; a named agent definition may change the model for that child (apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:1130; apps/cli/src/agents.rs:31). Route cannot leave the parent's boundary (subagent.rs:60-67).

access_and_usage.account: CLI: none required for Local or own-key sessions; a Cloud route needs sign-in [inferred from route rules]. VS Code and web group need a local developer session.
access_and_usage.permissions: Children inherit the parent's permission mode, allowed and disallowed tools, and approval sink (apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:668-683). No separate permission for viewing the list was found.
access_and_usage.subscription: No plan check on the list itself. Cloud-routed children are billed through the parent's usage (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:3129-3136).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: 7 concurrent children, depth 3, 15 turns per child, 600 s wait (apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:429-453). Spend cap divides remaining budget among children (subagent.rs:620-632).
access_and_usage.flags: none found in the code for the list; the task tool depends on session persistence (agent/mod.rs:2508).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not model specific; any model that can call tools can call the task tool [inferred].
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Child must match the parent's provider trust boundary or it fails before any request (subagent.rs:60-67).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Works. A Local session's children run on the device with Local models and are refused a cloud route (subagent.rs:19-22, :60-67). Listing needs no network.

features.summary: Shows, for each participating agent or model, its model name, status, result and (where built) usage. Mobile has Compare Models (two answers, timings). Web has Compare answers (two or three models, timings, no cost). The CLI /tasks show prints model, tokens and cost. Web and mobile Cloud runs also show model and cost.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a per-participant view: which model, is it still working, what did it answer, and what did it cost. Mobile Compare Models sends one prompt to two Cloud models side by side. Web Compare answers does the same for two or three models. The CLI /tasks show prints a child's model, input and output tokens, and credits. Cloud task cards on web and mobile show model and cost for each run.
purpose.why_it_exists: People choosing between models, or checking what a delegated agent did and spent, need the answer and the cost per participant, not one blended result. AGI is model agnostic, so showing the model is part of being honest about what ran (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md rule 5).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who want to compare models (mobile and web), developers watching child agents and their cost (CLI), and anyone reviewing Cloud work runs (web, desktop, mobile).
problems_solved: Which model gave which answer is labelled.
A slow or failed model is visible next to a working one.
Child agent spend is visible in credits, or 'on your subscription' (apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:119-146).
use_cases: On mobile, type /compare in the chat input, send a prompt, and read both answers.
On web, pick models in the Models page and press 'Compare answers'.
In the CLI, run /tasks show subagent_<n> after a child finishes to see its cost.
On web Work history, open a run and read 'Cost and usage'.

features.summary: Lets a person open what one agent or task did. CLI: /tasks transcript <id> prints a finished child's steps. VS Code: a Transcript button on each subagent row. Web and desktop: a Task details panel with progress, outputs and an Open source chat link. Mobile: the run detail sheet with streamed output.

purpose.what_it_does: Drill-down from a list of agents or tasks into one agent's own record. CLI prints one line per message or tool step (long lines clipped to 400 characters). VS Code opens it as a read-only document. Cloud run detail shows plan, progress, outputs and cost, and links to the source chat for the full conversation.
purpose.why_it_exists: The final answer alone does not show how a child got there or why it failed. A transcript lets a person audit tool use and errors (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md rule 6).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers auditing child agents (CLI, VS Code); people reviewing Cloud work runs (web, desktop, mobile).
problems_solved: See what a child did step by step.
Find why a run failed ('Why this task failed' section).
Reopen a past run's output without re-running it.
use_cases: Type /tasks transcript subagent_2 after it finished.
Press Transcript on a VS Code subagent row.
Open a failed Cloud run on web and read the failure reason.
Open a run on mobile and read its output text.

where_to_find_it: CLI: /tasks transcript <id> (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:535-546); /tasks show prints 'Its whole conversation (N steps): /tasks transcript <id>' (apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:166-172).
VS Code: 'Transcript' button on a Subagents row, aria-label 'View transcript for <title>' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:3537-3545).
Web and Electron desktop: Work history page at /tasks, select a run, panel 'Task details' (apps/web/app/tasks/page.tsx; TaskDetailPanel.tsx:428-537).
Desktop Tauri: DesktopTasks wraps the same shared panel (apps/desktop/src/features/tasks/DesktopTasks.tsx:58).
Mobile: tap a run on the AGI Work screen to open the run detail sheet; close with 'Close task' (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/components/CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx:300).
Chrome: side-panel More menu 'Tasks' sheet lists runs with Open (to the web chat) and Stop; no in-panel detail (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/tasksSheet.ts).
Web Code page subagent group: no transcript control found (LocalSessionPanel.tsx:174-203).
prerequisites: CLI: the child must have finished with a result; failed and cancelled children have no result so the command says it has not finished (registry.rs:536-541).
VS Code: the row must report transcriptAvailable.
Cloud run detail: signed-in Cloud account.
screens_and_controls: CLI /tasks transcript <id>.
VS Code Transcript button; opens a read-only document using the agi-subagent-transcript scheme (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/developerOutput.ts:10, :119).

Web Task details panel sections: Task goal, Task plan, Latest output or Result, Why this task failed, Cost and usage, Progress, Outputs, Context, buttons 'Refresh task details', 'Close task details', 'Open source chat', 'Share task' (TaskDetailPanel.tsx).
Mobile sheet: status, metadata rows, approval card, plan steps, output text, Open the conversation, Stop this task.
journey: 1. Open the list (see F062-01 or F062-04).
2. Pick one child or run.

features.summary: One overview of many Cloud agent runs. Runs that wait for the person (needs input, approval, paused) come first or have their own filter, and can be answered in place. Web and desktop: Work history page. Mobile: AGI Work screen. VS Code: Cloud tasks tree. Chrome: a Tasks sheet with Open and Stop only.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists the person's Cloud AGI Work runs from every app, shows state, model, age and cost, and lets the person approve, deny, steer, pause, resume, stop or archive without leaving the list. Waiting runs are surfaced first.
purpose.why_it_exists: Long agent runs stall when they need a decision. A single overview with a Needs you view and in-place answers keeps many runs moving (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md rule 6; docs/product/suite.md Cloud Work).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone running AGI Work or research in Cloud on web, desktop, mobile or VS Code.
problems_solved: Several runs at once are visible in one place.
A waiting approval is not buried among finished runs.
Another device may already have answered; the page says so ('Another device already answered this approval.').
use_cases: Open Work history on web, press 'Needs you', approve a pending tool call.
On mobile, open AGI Work, filter 'Needs you', open a run and tap Approve.
In VS Code, see a run under 'Needs you' and approve it from the tree.
Switch web to Board layout to see runs by stage.

Tasks or agents that need the user's input are surfaced first.
The user can unblock a waiting task inline without leaving the overview.

steps.what_happens: Client calls the run list with the chosen states and a 25-run limit.
Server reads the person's runs under row-level security and returns a page and cursor.
Client sorts needs-input runs first (web list) or filters by state (mobile, web Needs you).
On approve or deny the client posts the decision; the server applies gates, claims the pause checkpoint and continues the run in the managed service.
The continued run calls a model provider on our managed route.
Client reloads the list and re-reads the open run's journal.

features.summary: Moves work between places so the receiver continues it. In VS Code, 'Continue here' loads a cloud code session into the local chat with a clipped conversation summary, and 'Continue in the cloud' starts a cloud session from the open branch. It is device-to-device, not agent-to-agent. Summary-only handoff display does not exist.

purpose.what_it_does: VS Code only. From a cloud code session the person can pick 'Continue here', which drops a draft (recent turns plus branch) into the local chat, or 'Bring branch in', which checks out the cloud branch. The reverse command 'Continue in the cloud' creates a cloud session on the current GitHub branch and starts a task there.
purpose.why_it_exists: Work started in one place often has to finish in another; the product contract requires such moves to be explicit, with provenance, and never a background sync (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:276-283; docs/product/experience-contract.md Handoff Snapshot row).
purpose.who_uses_it: VS Code developers using AGI Code cloud sessions.
problems_solved: Carry a cloud session's context into the local editor.
Send local branch work to a cloud agent with a review step.
use_cases: Continue a cloud session in the VS Code chat.
Check out a cloud session's branch locally.
Start a cloud session from the current branch with a goal.

aliases: Fork Conversation (VS Code: Code: Fork Conversation)
features.summary: Two related things. A conversation branch copies a chat up to a chosen message into a new chat, and the original stays unchanged. A background fork exists only in the command-line app: /thread copies the session and runs a side task in parallel, /gather brings results back. Web, mobile, desktop and VS Code have branches only.

purpose.what_it_does: A branch copies a conversation up to a chosen message into a new conversation or session. The person continues in the copy, and the source is not changed. In the command-line app (CLI) a separate background-fork path starts a headless run on a copy of the session (/thread) and later pulls the finished answers into the main chat (/gather).
purpose.why_it_exists: People want to try another approach without losing the first one. The product requirements say branches are needed for safe alternate attempts, multi-track debugging and for keeping the original Local thread when a chat moves to another mode (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:687-694). The brief item S62.16 wants a side task that runs without disturbing the main one, and S62.17 wants an interactive branch (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/062-multi-agent-and-multi-model-interfaces.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Chat users on web, mobile and the Tauri desktop (branch from a reply); developers on the CLI and in VS Code (fork a session); CLI power users who run parallel threads.
problems_solved: Trying a different prompt or model path without overwriting the original chat.
Keeping a record of the point where two lines of work split (branch group, ancestry).
Running a side investigation in the CLI while the main conversation continues (/thread).
use_cases: Web: the user likes an answer, branches from it, and asks a different follow-up in the copy.
CLI: type /fork refactor-b, then later resume the copy with agiworkforce --session <id>.
CLI: type /thread check the failing tests, keep chatting, then /threads and /gather.
VS Code: fork a developer session from the session list and continue in the copy.

features.summary: In the command-line app, /advisor <question> sends one question to a stronger catalog-chosen model and prints the answer with the label '[advisor model: <name>]'. It is a side query: the conversation history is not sent and not changed. It is refused in Local mode. No other app has it.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a second opinion on a side question from a separate model, without adding the question or answer to the main conversation. The agent can also call it as a tool named advisor.
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief item S62.18 asks that the user or agent can consult an advisor model on a side question and see its answer. A one-shot call keeps the main context clean (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/advisor.rs:1-5).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using the CLI who want a second opinion mid-task.
problems_solved: Getting a stronger model's view without switching the session model.
Keeping a side question out of the main transcript and context size.
use_cases: Ask which of two designs is safer.
Check a tricky regex with a stronger model.
The agent itself calls the advisor tool for a hard decision.

where_to_find_it: CLI full-screen view and line-based view: type /advisor <question> (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6671-6680; apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:360-368).
No control in web, desktop, mobile, VS Code or Chrome (no code found).
prerequisites: A session that is not Local (own key or Managed Cloud) (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/advisor.rs:113-125).

Own key: a provider key in the environment for a catalog provider (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/advisor.rs:25-59). Cloud: signed in with a plan model available (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/advisor.rs:127-148).
screens_and_controls: Text command only. Without a question the line is 'Usage: /advisor <question>, consult a catalog-selected advisor model'.
journey: Type /advisor followed by the question.
Line view shows a spinner 'Advisor...'; full-screen view runs the call and adds a system message.
The answer appears, then the label '[advisor model: <id>]'.
Line view then prints '(advisor side query, not added to conversation)'.
Continue the main conversation; nothing from the advisor is in the history.

working: Both views parse /advisor and show a usage line when empty (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6671; apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:360).
The advisor builds a two-message prompt (system and the question only) and streams a reply with a 1024-token cap (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/advisor.rs:197-221).

The model is picked from the shared catalog: best active model by quality tier then context size, among providers with a key; for Managed it picks the best model the plan runs (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/advisor.rs:77-108).
The answer carries the model used and the label is printed (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/task_registry/mod.rs:476-490).

Not added to conversation: in the line view the result is printed to stderr only; in the full-screen view it is pushed to the display list, not the session (apps/cli/src/repl/mod.rs:515-533; apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7831-7866).

features.summary: Manage a routine that already exists. On Web, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome you can pause or resume it; Web, Mobile, CLI and Chrome can edit it; Web, Mobile, CLI and Chrome can delete it. Web and the internal Tauri desktop can share a copy as a link. Pause-until-date and Duplicate are not built anywhere.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the owner of a Cloud routine stop it without losing it (pause), start it again (resume), change its settings (edit), remove it with its run history (delete), and hand a copy of its name, instructions and timing to someone else through a link (share). On the Desktop app, Local routines have their own Pause, Resume and Remove buttons.
purpose.why_it_exists: Unattended work needs a safe off switch and a way to fix or retire it. Sharing lets a good routine spread without retyping. The brief lists these as items S63.24 to S63.29 (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/063-routines-schedules-and-triggers.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person who owns a routine; on a paid plan that allows scheduled tasks. A link recipient only reads the shared page and then makes their own copy.
problems_solved: A routine misbehaves or is not needed for a while: pause it instead of deleting it.
The timing, prompt or model is wrong: edit in place instead of recreating.
A routine is finished: delete it and its history after a confirmation that names the loss.
Someone else wants the same routine: share a link they can turn into their own routine.
use_cases: Pause the weekly review routine during a holiday, resume it when back (Web switch on the card).
Edit a daily digest prompt from the phone (Mobile card menu, Edit).
Delete an old once-only routine from the CLI with agi schedules delete.
Share a routine from Web: Share, Create link, Copy link; later Stop sharing.

where_to_find_it: Web: Scheduled page at /chat/schedules. Each card has an on/off switch labelled 'Pause <name>' or 'Resume <name>', a pencil 'Edit Schedule' button, and a 'More actions' menu with Run now, Share, Pause/Resume, Notification settings, Delete (apps/web/features/schedules/components/ScheduleCard.tsx:383, :427-500; menu order checked by apps/web/features/schedules/components/SchedulesPage.test.tsx:987).

Desktop (public Electron app): shows the hosted web page (doc: AGENTS.md section 5), so the same Web cards appear, plus an 'On this computer' section for Local routines with 'Pause' / 'Resume' and 'Remove' buttons (apps/web/features/schedules/components/LocalRoutinesSection.tsx:206, :267-296).

Desktop (internal Tauri build, DesktopShellV3): a list with 'Pause'/'Resume', 'Share schedule', 'Delete schedule' buttons and a 'Stop sharing' button once a link exists (apps/desktop/src/features/schedules/DesktopCloudSchedules.tsx:1229, :1283-1309, :1383). This is not the screen the Electron window shows.

Mobile: Schedules screen (Cloud mode only). Each card has a switch, a 'More actions' button; the menu lists Run now, Pause/Resume, Show history, Edit, Delete (apps/mobile/src/features/schedules/components/ScheduleCard.tsx:229-242, :297).
CLI: agi schedules pause|resume|edit|delete <id or name> (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1541-1585, handlers at :4413-4486).

VS Code: commands 'Code: Pause Schedule' and 'Code: Resume Schedule' on the schedules view; no edit or delete (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:621-627; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/schedules/scheduleActions.ts:233).
Chrome extension side panel Schedules section: 'Pause'/'Resume', 'Edit', 'Delete' buttons per row (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/schedulesSection.ts:905, :940-972).
prerequisites: A routine exists and belongs to the signed-in account.
Cloud mode on Mobile (the screen shows a Cloud gate otherwise) (apps/mobile/app/(app)/schedules/index.tsx:181).
CLI: not in Local or own-key mode; the client refuses with a NotManaged error (apps/cli/src/schedules.rs:230-234).
Resuming needs the routine not to be completed, expired, over its run limit, over its credit cap, or without a next occurrence (apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:1244-1273).
Free plan on the internal Tauri desktop: resuming is blocked with 'Upgrade to Basic or higher before resuming unattended runs.' (apps/desktop/src/features/schedules/DesktopCloudSchedules.tsx:696).

Web edit dialog: ScheduleForm with 'Save Changes' button and an 'Active After Save' switch (ScheduleForm.tsx:791, :808-815).
Web Share dialog: 'Create link', read-only 'Share link' field, 'Copy link', 'Stop sharing' (SchedulesPage.tsx:1527-1566).
Stop sharing confirmation: title 'Stop sharing this schedule?', button 'Stop sharing' (SchedulesPage.tsx:781-790).

Public share page /share/schedules/<token>: heading 'Shared schedule', the name, timing and instructions, and a link 'Add to my schedules' (apps/web/features/schedules/components/SharedSchedulePreview.tsx:33-56).
Mobile delete: native alert 'Delete schedule?' with Cancel and Delete (apps/mobile/src/features/schedules/deleteConfirmation.ts:9).
CLI delete: prompt that names the loss; --yes skips it; a non-interactive run without --yes refuses (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:4413-4430, :2579-2600).
VS Code pause/resume progress toasts (scheduleActions.ts:115-124).
Chrome delete: inline alert dialog 'Delete $NAME$ and its run history? This cannot be undone.' with Delete and Cancel (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:2910; schedulesSection.ts:1001-1040).

journey: Pause: toggle the switch (or choose Pause in the menu, or run agi schedules pause). The card shows 'Paused' and the next run disappears; the web shows the message 'Schedule paused.' (SchedulesPage.tsx:528-542).

Resume: toggle again. The server recomputes the next run time from now; if it cannot (finished, expired, limit, cap, no more occurrences) it answers with a conflict message that the card shows under the schedule (schedule-service.ts:1244-1273; SchedulesPage.tsx:540).

Edit: Web pencil, Mobile menu Edit (or tap the card), CLI edit with flags, Chrome Edit (name, description, prompt only). Change fields and save; the card updates and the web says 'Schedule updated.' (SchedulesPage.tsx:509-526).
Delete: choose Delete; read the confirmation; confirm. The card disappears; the web says 'Schedule deleted.' If a run is in progress the server refuses (schedule-service.ts:1305).

Share (Web, internal Tauri desktop): More menu, Share, Create link, Copy link, send it. The other person opens the page, reads it, clicks 'Add to my schedules', which opens the create form filled in; they review and save to get their own routine (SchedulesPage.tsx:803-826).
Stop sharing: press 'Stop sharing', read the warning (link dies for everyone; copies already made stay), confirm.
feedback_and_outputs: Web toasts and the action message line: 'Schedule paused.', 'Schedule resumed.', 'Schedule updated.', 'Schedule deleted.', 'Link copied', 'Sharing stopped' (SchedulesPage.tsx:508-542, :735, :776, :788).
Row error under the card on failure, ending with 'Retry the action when ready.' (ScheduleCard.tsx:361-368).
Card notices: 'Paused: it used its N cap. Raise the cap in Edit to run it again.' and 'Paused: a run needed your approval...' (ScheduleCard.tsx:336-352).
CLI prints the updated schedule list row, or 'Deleted schedule <id>.' or 'Left the schedule in place.' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:4413-4432).
Shared link format: <web origin>/share/schedules/<24-character token> (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts:326, :368-370).
settings: Web edit form: 'Active After Save' switch decides whether the routine is enabled after saving (ScheduleForm.tsx:791-801).
Share only reaches people who have the link; there is no per-person access list (apps/web/db/neon/0311_scheduled_task_shares.sql:9-20).
Workspace external-sharing rule can block Share (apps/web/app/api/schedules/[id]/share/route.ts:45-49).
Desktop Local routine create dialog has 'Keep this computer awake while running' (LocalRoutinesSection.tsx:566); not part of manage actions.

working: Web pause/resume through PATCH with an isActive boolean; resume recomputes next run and refuses terminal, over-limit, over-cap and no-occurrence cases (apps/web/app/api/schedules/[id]/route.ts:108-121; apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:1234-1289).

Web edit: PUT merges the patch over the stored routine, refuses completed or expired routines, checks the prompt for secrets, validates the model against the plan (apps/web/app/api/schedules/[id]/route.ts:74-90; schedule-service.ts:1102-1120).

Web delete: confirmation dialog, then DELETE; the server refuses while a run has status running, then deletes the routine row; runs are removed by the database cascade (SchedulesPage.tsx:1402-1425; schedule-service.ts:1291-1312; apps/web/db/neon/0009_scheduling.sql:36).

Web share: POST makes or refreshes one live share per routine, DELETE revokes it; the recipient page and GET /api/schedule-shares/[token] only resolve while the token is not revoked and the owner may run unattended work (apps/web/lib/services/schedule-share-service.ts:52-102).
Share is blocked by the workspace external-sharing rule and by the outbound secret inspection (apps/web/app/api/schedules/[id]/share/route.ts:45-62).

Share snapshot holds name, description, prompt, model, timing fields, a small allow-list of timing metadata keys, missed-run policy and retry settings; nothing else (schedule-share-service.ts:21-45; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts:328-343).
Opening a share link then 'Add to my schedules' pre-fills the create form with no project and no agent (apps/web/features/schedules/lib/schedule-form.ts:181-188; SharedSchedulePreview.tsx:20).

Mobile switch and menu pause/resume with an optimistic update and rollback path; Edit opens the create screen with the id; delete asks first and rolls the list back on failure (apps/mobile/src/features/schedules/store.ts:208-258, :262-300).
CLI pause, resume, edit (name, description, prompt, model, cron expression, time zone) and delete with confirmation (apps/cli/src/schedules.rs:460-482; apps/cli/src/lib.rs:4413-4486).
VS Code pause and resume only (scheduleActions.ts:104-127).
Chrome pause/resume, edit of name, description and prompt, and delete with an inline confirmation (schedulesSection.ts:905, :1207-1225, :1001-1040).

Electron Local routines: Pause cancels the active run; Resume asks a native confirmation and re-checks the folder grant; Remove stops the active run, then deletes the record (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/localRoutineEngine.ts:331-364; apps/desktop/electron/runtime/localRoutineService.ts:190-206).
incomplete: Edit is missing on VS Code and Local (Electron) routines; Chrome edits only name, description, prompt; CLI edits a fixed list of fields and cannot set caps, notifications, retries or missed-run policy (scheduleActions.ts:233; localRoutineService.ts:190-206; schedulesSection.ts:1221-1225; apps/cli/src/schedules.rs:460-482).

Share exists only on Web and on the internal Tauri desktop; Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome and Electron Local routines have none (searched apps/mobile, apps/cli, apps/extension, apps/extension-vscode for share routines in the schedule code; none found).
Delete does not check for a run waiting for approval; only status running blocks it (schedule-service.ts:1297-1306).
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile schedules screen shows a feature-unavailable view when FEATURES.schedules is off (apps/mobile/app/(app)/schedules/index.tsx:179).

DesktopCloudSchedules.tsx is wired into the Tauri DesktopShellV3 only (apps/desktop/src/features/v3/DesktopShellV3.tsx:40, :818); the public Electron Desktop shows the hosted web page instead (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
not_available: Pause until a chosen date: no code found on any app (search of apps and packages for pause-until and pauseUntil returned nothing about schedules; brief S63.25 says missing on all apps).
Duplicate routine: no code found; brief S63.28 says missing on all apps.
Unshare after the routine is deleted: see gaps.
Trash or undo for a deleted routine: deleteSchedule is a plain SQL delete (schedule-service.ts:1307-1311).

established.statement: S63.24: a routine can be paused and resumed without deleting it, on every app.
S63.25: the user can pause until a chosen date and it resumes by itself. Not built on any app.
S63.26: an existing routine's timing and settings can be edited and saved (done on Web, Desktop, Mobile; missing on CLI and Chrome per the brief, but code shows CLI and Chrome edit exist).
S63.27: a routine can be deleted after a confirmation and then stops running.
S63.28: one action copies a routine into a new editable routine. Not built.
S63.29: a routine or its template can be shared so another person can create their own copy.
Pause, resume and delete are required parts of scheduled work, alongside run history, notification and permission review.
established.source: doc: docs/product/requirements.md (section 20, Scheduled Tasks, Dispatch, And Automations)

established.statement: An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence; useConfirmAction is the shared surface; a mutation fired straight from onClick is a defect.

acceptance_criteria: Pausing an active Cloud routine sets it to paused with no next run; resuming sets status active and a future next-run time.
Resume of a completed or expired routine, a routine at its run limit, or one at its credit cap is refused with a message and the routine stays paused.
Delete shows a confirmation that names what is lost; confirming removes the routine and its run history; cancelling changes nothing.
Delete of a routine that has a run with status running is refused with 'Schedule cannot be deleted while a run is in progress'.
Share creates one link per routine; opening it shows name, timing and instructions without signing in; Stop sharing makes the link answer not found.
A share is refused when the workspace forbids external sharing or the secret scan blocks the content.
A person who follows 'Add to my schedules' gets a pre-filled form and no routine exists until they save.
On the Electron Desktop, Remove of a Local routine asks first and stops its active run.
inferred: After raising a credit cap on a paused routine, the routine stays paused until the owner resumes it, because the edit keeps the current enabled flag (apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:1088-1100, :1168-1181; test title at apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.test.ts:1700) [inferred].

Resume is not plan-checked on the server: setScheduleEnabled has no plan test; a Free account's routine is instead cancelled when it tries to run (schedule-service.ts:1234-1289; apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:889-915) [inferred].
Pausing a routine whose run is in progress does not cancel that Cloud run; no code in setScheduleEnabled touches runs [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add Pause until date as a resume-at time stored on the routine and cleared by the sweep.
[proposed] Add Duplicate as a client action that opens the create form with the routine's fields (same path as a shared copy).
[proposed] Revoke or list a user's shares independent of the routine so a link can be stopped after the routine is deleted.
[proposed] Make the Tauri desktop delete use the shared confirm dialog instead of window.confirm.
[proposed] Show 'Share' and 'Duplicate' on Mobile, CLI and Chrome, or record that they are web-only on purpose.

steps.what_happens: Person flips the switch or runs the command; the client sends PATCH /api/schedules/<id> with isActive.

Server checks sign-in, rate limit and CSRF, then runs setScheduleEnabled in one transaction: locks the row, refuses terminal, over-limit, over-cap, expired or no-occurrence cases, computes next run, updates scheduled_tasks.

Edit: client sends PUT; server screens the prompt for secrets, resolves the plan tier, merges the patch with the stored routine, validates (model must be eligible for the plan, caps and retry ranges) and writes the row.
Delete: client shows a confirmation; on yes sends DELETE; server refuses if a run has status running, else deletes the routine; run rows cascade.
Share: POST loads the routine, checks the workspace external-sharing rule, inspects the snapshot for secrets, then inserts or refreshes the share row with a random 18-byte token.

Recipient opens /share/schedules/<token>; the server reads the share (public, rate limited) and renders it. 'Add to my schedules' goes to /chat/schedules with the token; the page fetches the share and fills the create form.

Electron Local routine pause/resume/remove: the web page calls the Desktop host bridge (local_routine_set_enabled, local_routine_remove); the main process updates a device-stored routine list and cancels any active run. Resume shows a native confirmation.

data.what: Routine row (state, is_enabled, next_execution_at, paused_reason, settings)
data.where_stored: table scheduled_tasks in the Cloud database
data.synced: Read by every signed-in app through the API
data.retained_or_deleted: Hard delete by deleteSchedule; no trash (schedule-service.ts:1307-1311)
Removed with the routine by foreign-key cascade (apps/web/db/neon/0009_scheduling.sql:36)

data.synced: Public read by token while not revoked
data.retained_or_deleted: Revoked by setting revoked_at; the row is kept after the routine is deleted (apps/web/db/neon/0311_scheduled_task_shares.sql:15-17; schedule-share-service.ts:74-84)

data.what: Local routine records and run notes
data.where_stored: device store managed by the Electron main process (exact file or store name: unknown, not opened)
data.synced: Not synced to Cloud (no sync code found in localRoutineEngine.ts)
data.retained_or_deleted: Remove deletes the record after the active run stops (localRoutineEngine.ts:353-364); history kept to the last 20 runs (localRoutineEngine.ts:144, :519)

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Pause, resume, delete and share do not call a model. Edit validates the chosen model against the shared model catalog and the plan; an unknown id is refused, 'automatic selection' is allowed (apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:566-583). A shared copy keeps the model field of the snapshot; the recipient's plan check applies when they save.

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account required for every manage action (getUserScopedDb on each route). The public share page and GET /api/schedule-shares/[token] need no sign-in; adding a copy needs the recipient's own account.
access_and_usage.permissions: Owner only: every query filters by user_id. Share is refused when the routine belongs to a workspace that turned external sharing off (share/route.ts:45-49). A shared link only resolves while its owner account may run unattended work (schedule-share-service.ts:94-100). Workspace role rules for editing routines: none found in these files.
access_and_usage.subscription: Scheduled-task count is limited by plan at creation (assertScheduleQuota, schedule-service.ts:877-904; plan figures come from getPlanMaxScheduledTasks in packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:816, values not read). The internal Tauri desktop blocks resume on Free with an upgrade message (DesktopCloudSchedules.tsx:696, :1058). The server's pause/resume has no plan test (inferred). Plan names for the limits: unknown.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Rate limit 'chat-conversation' per user on edit, delete, toggle and share routes; 'share-view' on the public read (route files). Share tokens are 24 URL-safe characters (cloud-contracts schedules.ts:326). Pause, resume, delete and share spend no credits.
access_and_usage.flags: Mobile: FEATURES.schedules (apps/mobile/app/(app)/schedules/index.tsx:179). Others: none found.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not model dependent; edit re-validates the model id against the catalog (schedule-service.ts:566-583).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: None found in the code for these actions; scheduled runs themselves go through the managed service.

features.summary: Keeps unattended Cloud runs safe and affordable. A routine can have a run limit and a credit cap, five notification switches, and a pause for approval: when a run reaches a step that needs a person it stops, the routine pauses, and the person approves or denies in run history. Caps exist on Web only; approvals work on every app.

purpose.what_it_does: Limits how many times and how much a Cloud routine may spend (Maximum Runs, Credit Cap), lets the owner choose which events notify them and on which channel, and stops a run at a risky tool step until a person decides. The Desktop app's Local routines have their own notification switches and approvals through the coding session.
purpose.why_it_exists: Nobody watches an unattended run, so spend and risky actions need a hard edge. Brief items S63.30 to S63.32 require per-routine notification choice, budget caps and approval pauses (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/063-routines-schedules-and-triggers.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Owners of Cloud routines on a plan that allows them; Desktop users of Local routines; anyone asked to approve a step from Web, Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome or the Tauri desktop.
problems_solved: A routine loops or costs more than expected: it pauses at its credit cap.
A run wants to send data out or use a tool the owner marked 'ask': it waits instead of acting.
The owner is away: push or email says approval is needed.
Too many alerts: switch off success notices but keep failures.
use_cases: Cap a daily research routine at a number of credits for the month of runs.
Limit a one-off watch to 10 runs.
Approve from the phone a tool step a run is waiting on.
Run agi schedules approve <name> from a terminal after a notification.

journey: Set limits: open Create or Edit, expand 'Execution Limits', enter Maximum Runs and/or Credit Cap, set notification switches, save.
Wait. When the cap is reached the next due run is cancelled, the routine pauses with reason credit_cap_reached and the card says 'Paused: it used its N cap. Raise the cap in Edit to run it again.'
Raise the cap in Edit, then resume the routine.
Approval: a run reaches a step that needs approval; it stops with status needs approval, the routine pauses with reason approval_required, and a notice is queued.
Open Run History (or the CLI/VS Code/Chrome/Mobile equivalent), read the step, press Approve or Deny.
The same run resumes from its saved checkpoint, up to the 24 hour limit; the card refreshes and the message says 'Approved. The run finished.' or the status reached.
If nobody answers in 24 hours the run is cancelled with a message to resume the schedule; the owner resumes it from the card.

working: Maximum Runs validated 1 to 1,000,000; Credit Cap validated as whole credits 1 to 1,000,000 (apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:722-738).

Credit use is the sum of settled managed usage requests carrying the routine's id; a run's charges are tagged to its routine (schedule-service.ts:520-545; apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-request-service.ts:619-624; apps/web/db/neon/0301_routine_credit_cap.sql).

At run start, if the cap is reached the routine is paused (credit_cap_reached), the run slot is given back and the run is cancelled with the cap message; after a finished run that reaches the cap the routine pauses too; retries are not scheduled once the cap is reached (schedule-service.ts:2238-2253, :1714-1722, :1774-1778).

Notifications honour per-routine switches and account preferences; cancelled runs send nothing (schedule-notification-service.ts:20-95, :147).

S63.31: per routine, the user caps cost, credits or number of runs. Done on Web and Desktop; missing on Mobile, CLI, Chrome.

When the credit cap is reached the next run pauses the routine with reason credit_cap_reached; the user must raise the cap to resume.

A run that needs approval stops in awaiting_approval, the routine pauses with approval_required, a notification is queued, approving resumes the same run from a saved checkpoint, denying lets it continue without that step.
Notification and permission review are required parts of scheduled work.
A decision to add a separate notification switch for scheduled tasks to the Mobile app has been recorded.

acceptance_criteria: Saving Maximum Runs 0, 1,000,001 or a fraction is refused with the stated range message.
Saving Credit Cap 0, a fraction or above 1,000,000 is refused with the stated range message.
With a cap of N credits and N or more used, the next due run does not start; the routine is paused with the cap notice; resume and Run now are refused with the cap message.
A run that reaches an ask-gated tool stops with status needs approval and the routine shows the approval notice; pressing Approve resumes the same run id; Deny resumes it without that step.
An approval older than 24 hours is cancelled and the card tells the owner to resume the schedule.
Turning 'When failed or timed out' off stops failure notices for that routine while success notices still arrive; turning 'Email' off stops the email even if the account allows it.
Cancelled, skipped and credit-capped runs send no completion notice.
Approving with a tool call id list that no longer matches the pending ones is refused with a conflict.
inferred: The 'Credit Cap' helper says a run already started finishes, so overshoot by one run is possible; the cap is checked only before a run starts and after it ends (schedule-service.ts:2238-2253, :1714) [inferred].
Credit Cap only sums requests whose status is completed, so a run still in flight is not counted until it settles [inferred] (schedule-service.ts:520-545).
Local routines cannot spend managed credits through this path; their model may be cloud but the cap logic is not applied [inferred].

[proposed] Send a notice when an approval expires, so the owner learns the routine is still paused.
[proposed] Show the real cap or expiry message on Mobile instead of the generic cancelled text.
[proposed] Record an approval-expiry audit event like the missed-run one.

steps.what_happens: Owner saves caps and notification choices; the server validates and stores them (caps as columns, notification flags in the routine's metadata).
The sweep (cron every 15 minutes) first cancels expired approvals, recovers expired leases, then claims due routines owned by accounts that may run unattended.
Before running, the claim checks the credit cap; if reached it pauses the routine, returns the run slot and cancels the run.

The executor refuses secret-blocked prompts and accounts without managed compute access (run cancelled with a reason), picks a model route, builds the tool plan (tools that would ask are withheld or kept ask-gated), reserves managed usage, and runs the tool loop with unattended set.
The model provider is called by our servers through the managed route; usage is settled into managed_usage_requests tagged with the routine id, which feeds the cap.
If a tool call needs approval the loop returns a checkpoint; the service stores it with a 24 hour expiry, sets status awaiting_approval, pauses the routine, and queues a notification job.
The notification job reads per-routine and account preferences, records an in-app notification, queues email (respecting quiet hours), sends mobile push, and queues a developer webhook event.

The person presses Approve or Deny in an app; the app posts the decision with the pending tool call ids; the server claims the run and resumes the loop in the request (60 second limit, 40 second run budget).

Electron Local routines: the on-device engine ticks each second, starts a coding session at the due time, and marks the run awaiting_input when the session asks for approval; the person approves inside that session. Desktop notices follow the routine's flags.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: A Cloud routine uses 'automatic selection' or a catalog model eligible for the plan; the route is chosen server-side (selectScheduledRoute) and a run that resumes after approval must use the same route and a model that can still call tools, otherwise it fails with an explanatory error (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:817-822, :936-980). Provider folder names for routes: unknown, not traced. The credit cap converts spend with the shared credit conversion (microusdFromCredits) so it follows the model's priced usage, not a model name.

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account for every Cloud action; the approval route requires sign-in, CSRF and the 'llm-completion' rate limit.
access_and_usage.permissions: Owner only. Tool permission levels (always allow, ask, deny) and the account's tool approval policy decide which steps ask; a saved deny wins (tool-call-gate.ts:68-76).
access_and_usage.subscription: Free accounts: scheduled runs are cancelled by managed-compute access policy with a reason, and the Tauri desktop UI disables scheduling (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:889-915; DesktopCloudSchedules.tsx:1058). features.summary: Explains and handles runs that did not happen on time or failed. The Cloud sweep decides a run is missed when it starts more than two sweep intervals late and then runs it late once or skips it, as the owner chose, and the run history says so. Failed or timed-out runs retry with doubling waits. Holding runs for usage resets and repairing expired connectors are not built.

purpose.what_it_does: Records why an occurrence ran late or was skipped, applies the owner's 'If A Run Is Missed' choice, retries failed or timed-out runs a chosen number of times with doubling waits, and writes an audit event for missed runs. On Electron Desktop, Local routines have their own missed-run choice and a 2 minute grace.
purpose.why_it_exists: The Cloud sweep runs about every 15 minutes, machines sleep, and models fail. People need to see what happened to an occurrence instead of guessing (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/063-routines-schedules-and-triggers.md, S63.33 to S63.35).
purpose.who_uses_it: Owners reading run history on any app; operators reading audit events.
problems_solved: A routine fired hours late: the history says 'Ran late: scheduled for X, started Y later.'
A stale occurrence should not run: choose skip and see 'Skipped the run scheduled for X'.
A flaky run: retries try again before the routine moves on.
A skipped run must not use up the run limit: the slot is given back.
use_cases: Morning digest that is pointless after noon: set 'Skip it and wait for the next occurrence'.
Billing report that must still happen: keep 'Run it once, late'.
Flaky external site: Retries After A Failed Run 3, first retry after 5 minutes.
Check why a routine did not run overnight in the run history.

established.statement: S63.33: when an occurrence is missed or skipped, the run history says so and why. Done on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code; the brief lists Chrome as none.
S63.34: a run that hits the usage allowance is held and runs automatically after the allowance resets. Missing on every app.
S63.35: when a connector a routine depends on expires, the user is told on the routine and led to reconnect. Missing on every app.
A run is missed when it starts more than twice the sweep interval late; run_once runs it late, skip records it and gives the run slot back; both write an audit event.
Failed or timed-out scheduled runs retry with doubling wait up to the chosen count (0 to 5).
The note text comes from describeScheduleRunTiming in the shared contracts.
Mobile v1 only needs the pieces required for Cloud sign-in and future dispatch; Desktop and CLI carry deeper automation later.

acceptance_criteria: A scheduled occurrence started more than 30 minutes after its due time (normal mode) is treated as missed; one started within 30 minutes is not.
With 'Run it once, late' the run executes and its history note reads 'Ran late: scheduled for <time>, started <duration> later.'
With 'Skip it...' no model call happens, the run shows as skipped with the skip note, and the routine's run counter is not increased by that occurrence.
Both policies create a schedule_missed_execution audit event.
With Retries After A Failed Run 2 and first retry 5 minutes, a failed run is tried again after 5 minutes, then 10 minutes, then the routine moves on; a manual run is not retried.
A retry does not reduce the Maximum Runs allowance.
Run history on Web, Mobile, VS Code and Chrome shows the same note text for the same run.
A Local routine on Electron with skip and a due time more than 2 minutes old shows state 'skipped'.
inferred: The Chrome run list should show missed notes because it calls the shared function, but no test title for it was found [inferred] (schedulesSection.ts:1077).

A usage-allowance refusal currently surfaces as a failed run (which retries if configured) because the reservation call is not guarded in runClaimedSchedule [inferred] (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:1056; schedule-service.ts:2309-2335).
The two-sweep grace means a routine only appears missed after about 30 minutes, which is roughly two missed cron ticks [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Hold a run that hits the allowance, show 'Waiting for your allowance to reset', and run it after the reset time.
[proposed] When a connector token has expired, mark the run and the routine with a repair link to the connector screen.
[proposed] Show the skip note on CLI and Mobile with the same wording as Web.
[proposed] Tell the owner on the routine when a workspace departure stops it from running.

steps.what_happens: Vercel cron calls /api/cron/run-schedules every 15 minutes; in low-power mode it returns early after minute 15 of the hour.

The sweep cancels expired approvals, recovers expired leases, then claims due routines (enabled, active, next run due, not past expiry, under run limit unless retrying, owner allowed to run unattended and active in the workspace). The claim inserts a run row with an idempotency key built from the due time and retry number.
For each claim, the cap check runs; then missed detection compares now with the due time; skip policy finalizes the run as cancelled, run_once continues.
The executor runs the routine (model call to the provider); on error the status becomes failed, on timeout timeout, on outside cancel cancelled.

finalizeScheduleRun writes the run result and decides the next time: retry with doubling delay, or next occurrence, or completed/expired, or pause at cap; failed and timed-out runs queue a notification, cancelled ones do not.
Clients list runs; the shared function turns the stored missedExecution and skipped fields into the note text.
Electron Local routines: the on-device engine ticks every second and applies its own missed rule with a 120 second grace.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The missed and retry logic does not depend on a model. A retried or late run goes through normal route selection; retries of a failed provider call use the same managed path. Nothing in this feature switches model or provider on failure (no such code found in the retry branch).

access_and_usage.permissions: Owner reads their own runs. Workspace admin visibility of skipped work: only a server log line (schedule-service.ts:1328-1335).
access_and_usage.subscription: A run for an account without managed compute access is cancelled by the executor with a reason (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:889-915). A usage-allowance hold: none found in the code.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Retries 0 to 5; backoff 60 to 86,400 seconds, default 300; retry delay doubles with the exponent capped at 10 (schedule-service.ts:86-89, :1643-1647). Retries do not spend a run (schedule-service.ts:1381-1382). Sweep batch limits are in the cron route (not detailed).

aliases: Ask about the page you are on
Use the browser (web dialog in Desktop)
Read the active tab (CLI status line)
features.summary: The person asks a question about the web page they have open, or asks for a summary, and the answer uses that page's text. Chrome reads the page itself. Desktop and the command line read the active tab of a paired Chrome. Mobile sends a shared link to chat, where AGI Cloud may fetch it.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the assistant the text of the page the person is looking at so a free-form question or a one-tap summary is answered from that page. Each app reaches the page differently: Chrome reads it directly; Desktop, CLI and VS Code ask a paired Chrome through the Desktop browser bridge; Mobile gets a link through the share sheet.
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief items S64.01, S64.05 and S64.06 require that the assistant reads the page open in the browser and answers with it as context, with one action to summarize it. [inferred] It removes copy and paste of page text into a chat.
purpose.who_uses_it: People who read articles, docs or pull requests in Chrome and want an answer about them; developers using the CLI or VS Code with a paired Chrome; phone users sharing a link into AGI Mobile.
problems_solved: Pasting page text by hand into a chat.
Getting a quick summary of a long page.
Letting a coding agent read the page the developer is looking at without a separate browser.
use_cases: In Chrome, right-click a page and choose Summarize this page; the side panel opens, attaches the page and sends the summary request (apps/extension/src/background.ts:7452-7461, apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:16400).
In AGI Desktop, open the composer plus menu, choose Use the browser, press Read the page, Run, then Add to chat (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/BrowserToolsDialog.tsx:324-338,396-409).
In the CLI with a paired Chrome, ask a question; the model calls browser_read_page after the person approves (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs:1459-1462).
On a phone, share a link to AGI and tap Summarize this page (apps/mobile/src/features/share-preview/index.tsx:448-461).

where_to_find_it: Chrome side panel: composer plus menu item 'Add the browser page' (message key spContextItem, apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:769; menu code apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:9865-9880). Page right-click menu: 'Ask AGI about this page' and 'Summarize this page' (apps/extension/src/background.ts:7459-7460; labels apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:46,50).

Chrome in-page panel: floating launcher button on approved pages, chips Summarize, Key points, Q&A, Translate and a box 'Ask one question about this page…' (apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/pageActions.ts GENERIC_ACTIONS; apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/panel.ts:351-368; apps/extension/src/inPagePanel/setup.ts:44-66).

Desktop (hosted web app): composer plus menu row 'Use the browser', shown only when the web app runs inside the Desktop shell (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:179,1159-1171,1697-1699; apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:6019,6029-6032,7036-7040).
CLI: no screen; the model's tool call is shown as 'Read the active tab' (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs:197).
VS Code: session tools list has a 'Browser' entry described as 'Open, read and act on pages in the paired browser' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/capabilityManagement.ts:1103-1115).

Mobile: the share sheet of the phone; AGI shows a 'Shared Content' screen (apps/mobile/src/features/share-preview/index.tsx:297-305). iOS extension is titled 'Share with AGI' (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIShareExtension/ShareViewController.swift:67).
Web in an ordinary browser: not offered, because the row needs the Desktop host (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6019).
prerequisites: Chrome: the person is signed in to AGI (Managed Cloud); in-page and side panel prompts refuse with 'Sign in to use AGI Managed Cloud.' when signed out (apps/extension/src/background.ts:9135-9137). The site must be readable under the extension's site rules (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:6486-6510).

Desktop, CLI and VS Code: Chrome with the AGI extension paired to Desktop. If not paired the dialog says 'No browser is paired yet. Open Settings, Capabilities to pair the Extension with this Mac.' (BrowserToolsDialog.tsx:33-34). Pairing is done from the extension side panel with 'Connect to Desktop' and a code Desktop shows (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/BrowserPairingSection.tsx:14-18).
CLI and VS Code also need the Desktop shell running; otherwise the browser tools are not offered (apps/cli/src/browser_bridge.rs:1-3, 67; apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs:1343-1349).
Mobile: a link or text shared from another app.
screens_and_controls: Desktop dialog 'Use the browser': action buttons (Read the page, Screenshot, Click, Type, Open a page, Stop loading, Read the console, Read network activity, Download a file), 'Choose a tab' button, 'Run', 'Add to chat', 'Close', result box labelled 'Browser result', 'Recent activity' list (BrowserToolsDialog.tsx:74-84,323-446).
Chrome side panel: attach menu items and a page chip; the plus menu also has 'Add selected text' and 'Attach tabs' (side_panel.ts:14797-14809,14968-14975).
Mobile share screen: buttons 'Dismiss', 'Summarize this page', 'Ask about this page', and the main button 'Send to Chat' (share-preview/index.tsx:448-475,495-537).
journey: Chrome right-click: person chooses 'Summarize this page' -> background stores a pending 'summarize' request in session storage and opens the side panel (background.ts:7637-7650 region, 7677) -> side panel captures the active tab text, attaches it and sends the summary prompt (side_panel.ts:16400-16445).

Chrome free question: person opens the side panel, uses 'Add the browser page' or just asks; when the model needs the page it calls browser_read_page, the panel reads the tab (asking for site access if needed) and returns the text (side_panel.ts:8078-8150).

Chrome in-page: person opens the launcher, taps a chip or types a question, the panel sends the visible text of the main region to AGI Managed Cloud and shows the answer (in-page-panel/panel.ts:558-566; background.ts:9112-9190).

Desktop dialog: person opens 'Use the browser', keeps 'Read the page' selected, optionally presses 'Choose a tab', presses Run, Desktop asks before the action, the page text appears in the result box, 'Add to chat' attaches it as a text file named page-<time>.txt (BrowserToolsDialog.tsx:131-142,282-286,396-409; apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:2092-2110).

CLI: model calls browser_read_page; CLI shows an approval 'The agent wants to read the page open in your signed-in Chrome.'; on yes the Desktop bridge asks the extension (mod.rs:1459-1462).

Mobile: person shares a link, the 'Shared Content' screen shows the text, person taps 'Summarize this page' (sends 'Summarize this page.' plus the shared text) or 'Ask about this page' (puts the text in the composer to add a question) (share-preview/index.tsx:227-248).
feedback_and_outputs: Desktop dialog: result text in 'Browser result'; a spinner labelled 'Running'; a role=alert error line; activity rows with time, client, action and 'running', 'done' or 'failed: ...' (BrowserToolsDialog.tsx:102-106,317-321,405-446).

Chrome: an activity line 'Reading <host>' for each page read and 'done' on finish (side_panel.ts:8078-8100); the in-page panel shows a disclosure that up to 30,000 characters of visible text go to AGI Managed Cloud (in-page-panel/panel.ts:411-430).
Chrome answers stream into the side panel; the in-page panel replaces each answer with the next (panel.ts:420-427).
Mobile: the message goes to a new chat; the screen shows 'Opening chat…' then navigates to the chat (share-preview/index.tsx:274-282).
settings: Chrome: site approvals and blocked sites in Extension settings, Permissions; the in-page panel can be turned off there (apps/extension/src/inPagePanel/setup.ts:70-80 region; apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:6500-6501).

VS Code: the 'Browser' tool can be switched off per session (capabilityManagement.ts:1103-1129).

working: Chrome side panel reads the active tab, bounds it to 30,000 characters, strips secrets and refuses restricted or loading pages (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:6486-6537; apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/pageActions.ts:22).

Chrome chat tool browser_read_page is offered at tier 'read' or 'act' depending on site policy (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/chatBrowserTools.ts:79-90; side_panel.ts:7738-7757) and its result is fenced as untrusted data (side_panel.ts:8118-8125).
Chrome right-click items 'Ask AGI about this page' and 'Summarize this page' exist and route through the side panel (background.ts:7452-7461; side_panel.ts:16400-16445).
Chrome in-page panel reads the main region of the page and sends it with the prompt (in-page-panel/panel.ts:394-410,558-566).

Desktop dialog reads the active page of a paired Chrome and can attach it as a text file (BrowserToolsDialog.tsx:131-142,282-286). The extension returns at most 20,000 characters (apps/extension/src/features/native-bridge/desktopCommands.ts:15,120-138).

Desktop cloud turns can call device_browser_read_page (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/device-steps.ts:52-59,265-268; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:6359-6363).

CLI offers browser_read_page when a browser is paired, marks it as read-only but never pre-approved, and caps its result at 100,000 characters (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs:1048-1056,1343-1349; apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs:4795-4830).

incomplete: Mobile does not read an open browser page; it only sends the shared text and link, so the answer depends on AGI Cloud fetching that link (share-preview/index.tsx:227-236; chatExecutionStore.ts:3393). The brief's wording 'does not read the open page' is true; the claim that nothing is fetched is not.

VS Code: only the 'Browser' tool toggle was opened; VS Code spawns the CLI runtime, so page reads are the CLI's (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:2544-2575). No VS Code code that renders a page read was opened.
The in-page panel and the Chrome page chip read visible text only; frames, PDFs and file URLs: not examined.
disconnected_or_disabled: Desktop dialog is hidden in a plain browser tab because the row needs the Desktop host (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6019).
CLI and VS Code browser tools are withheld when no browser is paired (tool_catalog.rs:1343-1349; test at tool_catalog.rs:1553-1575).
not_available: Web in an ordinary browser: no page reading (brief status n/a; ChatComposerNew.tsx:6019).
Mobile: no way to read the page open in a phone browser; only share-in (share-preview/index.tsx).
Local-mode Mobile fetch of a link: no fetch code found in the local path (not opened in depth) [inferred].

established.statement: The assistant reads the page open in the user's browser and answers with it as context (S64.01).
One action summarizes the page the user is viewing (S64.05).
The user asks a free-form question and the answer uses the current page content (S64.06).
Page content is untrusted. Browser data must not enter global memory or synced chat by default.
Chrome must include page context capture, ask/act modes, per-site allow/deny prompts, prompt-injection defenses.

acceptance_criteria: In Chrome on an approved site, 'Summarize this page' opens the side panel and sends a summary request that includes that page's text.
In Chrome on a site the person blocked, the page is not read and a notice names the host.
In Desktop with a paired and connected Chrome, Read the page, Run returns title, address and text, and Add to chat attaches a file named page-<time>.txt.
In Desktop with no pairing, the dialog shows the 'No browser is paired yet' line and Run is disabled.
In the CLI with no paired browser, no browser_ tool is offered to the model.
In the CLI, browser_read_page asks for approval every time, even in a safe-reads mode.
On Mobile, a shared link shows 'Summarize this page' and 'Ask about this page'; text over 100 KB shows the truncation notice.
inferred: Answers should say when the page text was cut at the limit; Chrome does with an excerpt notice (pageActions.ts:23-24) [inferred].
Mobile Local mode should say it cannot open a link, since the on-device model has no fetch tool [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Show in the Mobile share screen whether the link will be fetched by AGI Cloud, so the person knows the page itself leaves the phone.
[proposed] Let the CLI and the Desktop cloud tool take a tab id, as the Desktop dialog already does.

steps.what_happens: Chrome: the person asks; the side panel reads the active tab's text in the browser and attaches it.
Chrome: the page text, question and history go to AGI Managed Cloud for the answer.
Desktop dialog: the web app asks the Desktop shell to run browser_read_page; Desktop asks permission and shows a per-action dialog.
Desktop sends the command to the paired Chrome extension over the local bridge; the extension reads the tab and returns up to 20,000 characters.

Desktop cloud turn: the chat request names device browser capabilities; the server adds device tools; the model asks for device_browser_read_page; the page text then goes back to the server as a tool result.
CLI: the model calls browser_read_page; the person approves; the CLI sends the command to the Desktop shell, which uses the paired Chrome. The text goes to whichever model the CLI session uses.
Mobile: shared text is bounded to 100 KB, wrapped in a shared_via_intent tag and sent as a chat message; in a cloud turn with a link the server may fetch the link.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Chrome always uses AGI Managed Cloud with automatic model choice for in-page prompts (apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/panel.ts:93-96 provider pill; background.ts:9160-9163). Desktop cloud turns use the Cloud route. The CLI uses whatever model the session is configured for (not opened). No page read depends on a particular model; model-side tool support gates Chrome chat tools (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:8771).

access_and_usage.account: Chrome needs an AGI sign-in (apps/extension/src/background.ts:9135-9137). Desktop dialog: no account check found in the dialog code. Cloud turns need a signed-in Cloud account [inferred]. CLI and Mobile: not opened.
access_and_usage.permissions: Desktop asks for a capability grant once and shows a dialog 'Use the paired browser?' with Cancel and Allow once for each dialog action (dispatcher.ts:2092-2110, 2175-2205). Chrome acts only on sites approved in the extension (BrowserToolsDialog.tsx:31-32). CLI asks each time (mod.rs:1459-1462).
access_and_usage.subscription: none found in the code for the page read itself. Chrome returns 'plan_required' and 'quota_exceeded' outcomes from the server (apps/extension/src/background.ts:9041-9044); which plans: unknown.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Page text: 30,000 characters in Chrome (pageActions.ts:22), 20,000 returned to Desktop (desktopCommands.ts:15), 100,000 for CLI result (tool_catalog.rs:1056), 4 chat tool calls per handoff and 64,000 characters per tool result in Chrome (chatBrowserTools.ts:22-24). Mobile share text 100 KB (share-preview/index.tsx:43). Usage metering of the chat turn: server side, not opened.
access_and_usage.flags: none found in the code for Chrome; Desktop row appears only with the Desktop host (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6019); CLI tools appear only when paired (tool_catalog.rs:1343).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Chrome offers chat page tools only if the selected model supports tools (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:8769-8773 region). Others: none found in the code.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Chrome in-page: Managed Cloud only (panel.ts:93-96). Desktop dialog and CLI: no provider involved in reading.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Desktop dialog works without any model because it only reads the page and attaches a file (BrowserToolsDialog.tsx:131-142). The CLI tool works with a local model if the session uses one [inferred, CLI model path not opened]. Chrome chat has no Local mode. Mobile Local mode sends the shared text to the on-device model; no fetch of the link was found [inferred].

features.summary: Text the person highlights on a web page becomes context for a question. In Chrome it attaches to the next message, or is handed to AGI Desktop, VS Code or the CLI after a preview and approval. On a phone, shared text arrives through the share sheet.

purpose.what_it_does: Moves a highlighted passage into the assistant's context. In Chrome the passage is attached to the side-panel composer, or sent after an explicit approval to AGI Desktop (quoted draft in the composer), VS Code (composer prefill through a vscode:// link) or the CLI (a copied command with an agi-context link). On Mobile the iOS share sheet and Android share intent carry selected text into AGI.

features.summary: The person chooses which open tabs the assistant sees. Chrome has an 'Attach tabs' picker and an @ mention menu that add several tabs to one message. Desktop's 'Use the browser' dialog has a 'Choose a tab' list that reads one tab at a time. The CLI always reads the active tab. No dedicated compare action exists.

Copying text from several tabs by hand.
