features.summary: The agent reviews the current changes or a pull request and lists findings with file and line, scans for security problems, reads pull request comments and fixes them, and looks into failed checks. Each app does part of this: the CLI most, the Web GitHub app reviews pull requests on its own, VS Code and Desktop use prompts.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives review help at several points. The CLI reviews a diff, a commit, a branch comparison or a hosted pull request and can post the review. The Web GitHub app reviews pull requests when opened or when mentioned. The CLI can fetch pull request feedback and failing checks for the agent. VS Code and the CLI have security review prompts.
purpose.why_it_exists: Review catches defects before merge. Founder decisions record that the CLI, VS Code and cloud Code review pull requests (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:381-382).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers and reviewers; repository owners who install the GitHub app.
problems_solved: Slow first-pass review.
Missing review comments in large changes.
Forgetting to address every comment or failing check.
use_cases: Run agi review before committing.
Mention the app on a pull request to get a review.
Run /autofix-pr on the branch to address comments.
Run a security review of pending changes in VS Code.

where_to_find_it: CLI: 'agi review' with --base, --commit, --pr, --post, a prompt and --model (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:782-797); slash commands /security-review, /pr-comments, /autofix-pr, /ultrareview (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:301-314).
Web: GitHub app comments on pull requests; the install link on the Code page (apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts:30-31).

Desktop: the 'Review code' button in the changes panel (apps/web/features/code/components/LocalChangesPanel.tsx:259) and per-turn review pane 'Review changes' (apps/web/features/code/local-code.ts:1519).
VS Code: 'Code: Review a Pull Request' and 'Code: Security Review of Pending Changes' (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:572, 577).
Mobile: read findings in a Desktop session view; mobile pull request review is missing in the brief (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/067-coding-capabilities-and-developer-workflows.md S67.21).
prerequisites: CLI pull request review needs the GitHub CLI installed and signed in (apps/cli/src/review.rs:154-157).
Web review needs the GitHub app installed, ownership verified, and pr_review_enabled for the installation (apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts:322-336).
Web tasks need a plan that includes AGI Code (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-github-task.ts:236).
screens_and_controls: CLI review flags --base, --commit, --pr, --post (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:782-797).
Desktop 'Review code' button is disabled while a turn runs (apps/web/features/code/components/LocalChangesPanel.test.tsx:183).
Review pane comment box 'What should change here?', 'Add comment', 'Send to the agent', 'Discard comments' (apps/web/features/code/local-code.ts:1540-1546).
journey: CLI: run agi review; the diff is gathered with hardened git, sent as one turn, and the result printed; with --pr --post it is posted as a pull request comment.
Web: open or update a pull request on an installed repository, or comment with the app mention; the review arrives as a pull request review with line comments.
CLI feedback: run /pr-comments to list unresolved threads; /autofix-pr to change code, which must be on the pull request branch.
VS Code: run the command, enter a number or branch, read the answer in chat.
feedback_and_outputs: Review output: overall explanation, severity clean, minor, major or critical, issues with file, line, description, suggestion (apps/cli/src/review.rs:21-36).
If the diff is over 100,000 bytes only the start is reviewed and the output says the review is partial (apps/cli/src/review.rs:113-136).
'No changes to review.' when the diff is empty (apps/cli/src/review.rs:48-50).
Feedback fetch says what was not read instead of claiming an empty result (apps/cli/src/pr_feedback.rs:365-380).
Web comments: reply texts for quota reached, binary diff, no diff, prompt-injection skip (apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts:396-400, 506-540).
settings: review_model in CLI config (apps/cli/src/review.rs:60-63).
Installation review model and enabled flag (apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts:322-336).
Env GITHUB_PR_REVIEW_MONTHLY_CAP, default 100 (apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts:59-61).
Product requirements list 'Autofix pull request' and 'Create pull request automatically' (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:1384-1385).

working: CLI review gathers staged, unstaged and untracked diffs, a commit, a base comparison, or reads a pull request with gh; revisions starting with a dash are refused; git runs with diff drivers off (apps/cli/src/review.rs:225-283).
CLI review shortens a large diff and says so, and sensitive untracked files are named but not sent (apps/cli/src/review.rs:113-136, 286-300).
CLI post_review posts with gh pr review --comment (apps/cli/src/review.rs:174-186).

CLI feedback fetch pages through review threads, reviews and comments (up to 20 pages) and checks, reports unread parts, and fences the text as untrusted (apps/cli/src/pr_feedback.rs:7-9, 212-300, 380-440).
/autofix-pr refuses when the checkout is on another branch (apps/cli/src/pr_feedback.rs:344-362).

Failing checks are fetched with gh pr checks and included in the feedback prompt, so the CLI can look at failed CI (apps/cli/src/pr_feedback.rs:284-300, 391-396). The brief says CLI CI investigation is missing; this is a partial counter-finding: it lists failing check names and links but no log reading was found.
Web webhook verifies the signature, drops duplicates, ignores bots, and only lets owner, member and collaborator mentions start a review (apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts:228-236, 51-55).
Web reviews on opened, reopened, synchronize and ready_for_review, never on drafts (apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts:276-281, 296-304).
Web review has a 5 minute debounce and a rolling 30 day cap per installation, and skips when a prompt-injection pattern is found (apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts:57-61, 356-420, 528-540).
Web review runs a correctness and a security pass over each chunk and drops findings that name lines the diff lacks (apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/__tests__/automated-review.test.ts:107-115).
Web: a mention on a pull request with a coding task runs a cloud session whose goal includes failed checks (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-github-task.ts:264-285; apps/web/lib/github-app.ts:1287).
VS Code security and pull request review prompts that read git and say not to edit files (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/editor-utilities/editorUtilities.ts:171-192).
incomplete: Desktop and Mobile have no dedicated review engine found; they ask the session agent (apps/web/features/code/components/LocalChangesPanel.tsx:259). The brief's code references for security scanning in apps/cli/src/app_server/surfaces.rs:1116 and developer_host.rs:890 did not show scanning code where I opened them; unknown.

Web review of review comments (respond to feedback): a mention task does not read earlier review comments; its context is the pull request body and failed checks (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-github-task.ts:140-170).
CI investigation reads failed check output, annotations and a log tail on Web (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-github-task.ts:98-120) but needs the sandbox switch.
disconnected_or_disabled: Web review and tasks are skipped unless the managed-compute private beta gate is on and, for tasks, the sandbox is ready (apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts:477-483; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-github-task.ts:221).
not_available: Mobile pull request review (brief: missing).
Respond to feedback on Desktop, Web, Mobile, VS Code (brief); a general session can still be asked by prompt [inferred].

established.statement: The agent reviews current changes and reports issues with file and line references.
The agent reviews a pull request by fetching its diff and posts or shows findings.
The agent scans for security problems and reports them; explains each finding in plain language with its location.
The agent reads review comments on a pull request and changes code to address them.
The agent investigates a failed CI run: reads logs, finds the cause, proposes a fix.
The CLI, VS Code and cloud Code review pull requests.

acceptance_criteria: agi review on a dirty folder lists issues with file and line, or says 'No changes to review.'
A diff above 100,000 bytes yields a review that says it is partial.
agi review --pr N --post adds a comment to the pull request.
A failing gh call shows an error, not an empty list.
A mention from a non-member does not start a review.
Opening a draft pull request starts no review; marking it ready does.
/autofix-pr on the wrong branch refuses and names the branch to check out.
A review of a diff holding prompt-injection phrases is skipped with a comment.
inferred: Findings should be plain language; the review prompt asks for explanation fields but quality depends on the model. [inferred]
Security scan results should carry the same file and line format. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Read CI job logs in the CLI, not just check names.
[proposed] Include earlier review comments in the Web mention task so it can respond to feedback.
[proposed] Add a Desktop review button that uses the same review engine as the CLI.

steps.what_happens: CLI reads the diff with hardened host git, or asks gh for a pull request diff.
The diff, cut to 100,000 bytes, goes to the configured review model in one turn.
The CLI prints the findings; with --post it sends them to GitHub through gh.
GitHub sends a webhook; our server verifies the signature, dedups, applies the author check, rate and quota checks, and mints an installation token.
The server fetches the diff, screens it for prompt injection, resolves the owner's plan and runs the review pipeline with the owner billed.
The review is posted back to the pull request as a review with line comments, unless nothing new was found.
For a coding mention, a cloud session runs a turn in the sandbox, commits, pushes and opens a pull request.

features.summary: The agent's edits show up as reviewable changes. On Desktop the person reads each file's diff, stages or reverts single files or hunks, applies a worktree to the folder, or discards a file. In the CLI, a patch is approved before it applies and agi apply applies a stored diff. Mobile has a cloud changes sheet with a file tick-list.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows what the agent changed as diffs and lets the person choose what stays. Choices are per file or per hunk: stage, revert, discard, or include in a commit. A worktree session's changes can be applied to the main folder. Rewind goes back to before a turn.
purpose.why_it_exists: The person stays in control of code that lands in their repository. The brief requires patches to be reviewable and that only the chosen ones are applied (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/067-coding-capabilities-and-developer-workflows.md S67.24, S67.25).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who lets an agent edit code on Desktop, CLI, VS Code or a cloud session.
problems_solved: Accepting a whole large change blindly.
Undoing one bad edit without losing the good ones.
Reviewing a phone-started change.
use_cases: Stage only the files that look right and revert the rest.
Revert one hunk the agent got wrong.
Apply a worktree session's changes to the main folder.
Pick files on the phone and press Commit and push.

established.statement: The agent proposes a change as a reviewable patch before or as it applies it.
The user picks which proposed patches are applied, and only those are applied.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence.
A file an agent removes goes to the operating system Trash first.

acceptance_criteria: After an agent edit, the changes panel lists the file with its status and counts.
Discard asks first, names the file, and then restores it to the committed version.
A conflicted file cannot be discarded.
In the review pane, staging one hunk stages only that hunk.
Revert shows which files change before it runs.
Apply to local copies the worktree changes into the main folder and leaves files the person changed since alone.
agi apply with a bad patch exits non-zero and lists conflicts.
On the phone cloud sheet, committing with no file chosen is refused.

steps.what_happens: After a turn the changes panel asks the desktop shell for the working tree changes; the shell runs git inside the approved folder.
The person previews and picks a stage, revert or apply; the desktop checks git.write and asks the folder CLI to do it with a preview first.
Discard: the person confirms, the shell checks git.destructive and restores, removes or cleans the chosen files.
CLI: the agent calls apply_patch; the person approves the file list; the patch is applied with git apply in the folder.
Mobile cloud sheet: the phone calls our server to read changes, discard files, commit chosen files, and open a pull request.
Commit and push of a cloud session talk to GitHub through the installation.

features.summary: Lets the coding agent, or the person, commit a session's changes, create a branch and open a GitHub pull request. Four separate paths exist: the Desktop and local-folder panel, the Cloud sandbox panel on Web, the CLI agent's git tools and its app-server pull request call, and a VS Code command. Mobile has no control of its own.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns the edits an agent made into a commit, a branch and a GitHub pull request. The Desktop local panel pushes the checked-out branch from the person's own computer and then asks the AGI web service to open the pull request through the AGI GitHub App (apps/web/features/code/components/LocalPullRequest.tsx:70-87). The Web Cloud panel commits and pushes from the managed sandbox and opens the pull request (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-session-service.ts:2114, 2758). The CLI agent has typed git tools (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/git_tools.rs:135-168) and an app-server pull request call that uses the gh program (apps/cli/src/app_server/pull_request.rs:188-290).
purpose.why_it_exists: A coding task is not finished until the change is saved in git and offered for review. The brief says: 'The agent (or user from the coding surface) commits the session's changes with a message', 'The agent creates a git branch for its work', and 'The agent opens a pull request for its branch on the code host' (brief S67.29, S67.30, S67.31).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using AGI Workforce Code on Desktop, Web (Cloud sessions), the CLI and the VS Code extension.
problems_solved: The person does not have to leave the app to commit and open a pull request.
Risky git actions are gated: hooks always run for CLI commits, a push is always approved by a person, a submodule pointer cannot be staged (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/git_tools.rs:439-450).
Pull request state and check status are shown next to the changes (apps/web/features/code/components/LocalPullRequest.tsx:49-52, 98-107).
use_cases: On Desktop, finish a session on a feature branch and press 'Push and open a pull request'.
On Desktop, with no branch checked out, press 'Create branch and open pull request' to put the changes on a new branch.
On Web, in a managed Cloud session, type a commit message, press 'Commit and push', then 'Create pull request'.
In VS Code, run 'Code: Create Pull Request' and confirm the push.

where_to_find_it: Desktop (Electron shell showing the hosted web app): the Changes panel of a local coding session shows the pull request block (apps/web/features/code/components/LocalChangesPanel.tsx:383). It only renders in a shell that has Local mode (apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/host.ts:45-47).

Web (Cloud sessions): the changes panel has a 'Commit message' field, a 'Commit and push' button and a 'Create pull request' button (apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts:182-183, 416; apps/web/features/code/components/CodeChangesPanel.tsx:444-499).

CLI: the agent calls git_stage, git_commit, git_branch_create and git_push as tools (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/git_tools.rs:135, 157, 168, 325). Pull request creation is an app-server method (git/pullRequest), not a visible CLI command in the code read (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:5836-5842).
VS Code: command palette entry 'Code: Create Pull Request' (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:262-264).

Mobile: no commit, branch or pull request control found. The brief marks it done (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/067-coding-capabilities-and-developer-workflows.md S67.29-S67.31) but the mobile code read only starts, steers and views a remote session (apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/CodeSessionsCard.tsx:57-70).
prerequisites: Desktop: a folder approved for the app, a git repository with an origin remote that uses https or ssh, and a GitHub remote for the pull request (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/gitService.ts:780-790, 913-935; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-local-pull-request.ts:14).

Desktop: the person is signed in to the web app and has connected the AGI GitHub App for the repository; otherwise the panel offers a GitHub compare page instead (apps/web/features/code/components/LocalPullRequest.tsx:152-165).
Web Cloud: the deployment has Managed Code and managed compute switched on, and a plan that reaches managed compute (apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/[sessionId]/commit/route.ts:48-70).
CLI and VS Code pull request: the gh program installed and signed in, else the call falls back to a GitHub compare link (apps/cli/src/app_server/pull_request.rs:261-318).
screens_and_controls: Desktop pull request block: button 'Push and open a pull request' (apps/web/features/code/local-code.ts:194), button 'Create branch and open pull request' when no branch is checked out (local-code.ts:227), a link chip 'Pull request #N, state, checks' (local-code.ts:398-410), link 'Open a pull request on GitHub' when the GitHub App is not installed (local-code.ts:223).
Web Cloud panel: 'Commit message' field, 'Include in the commit:' file checkboxes, 'Commit and push', 'Create pull request' (code-surface.ts:182-189, 416).

VS Code: an input box for the title, an input box for the base branch, a modal that lists up to 10 commits and asks to confirm the push (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/pullRequest.ts:44-66).
journey: Desktop: the agent changes files in the approved folder.
The person opens the Changes panel and reviews the files.
The person presses 'Push and open a pull request'. The desktop app asks for the git.write grant if not yet given (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:922-925).
The desktop pushes the branch to origin and reports the default branch (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/gitService.ts:913-950).
The web app opens the pull request through the AGI GitHub App and shows a link chip (apps/web/features/code/components/LocalPullRequest.tsx:70-87).
The panel re-reads checks every 30 seconds while they are running (LocalPullRequest.tsx:15, 98-107).
VS Code: run the command, enter title and base, review the commit list, confirm, then choose 'View' on the result message (pullRequest.ts:68-100).
feedback_and_outputs: A pull request chip showing number, state (open, draft, merged, closed) and check state (apps/web/features/code/local-code.ts:385-410).
Error text under the button with role=alert; when GitHub access is lost a reconnect action appears (LocalPullRequest.tsx:88-89, 189-198).
Missing default branch shows 'The remote has no default branch to open a pull request against.' (local-code.ts:230).
On a base branch the button is disabled and the hint 'Switch to a branch other than the default branch to open a pull request.' shows (local-code.ts:226; LocalPullRequest.tsx:175-186).
VS Code shows a created message or a 'finish on GitHub' warning with a View button (pullRequest.ts:46-55).
settings: Desktop preference worktreeBranchPrefix is used as the prefix of a new branch (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:3070-3076).
Session agent mode (plan, ask, auto, bypass) decides what the agent asks before running git tools (apps/web/features/code/local-code.ts, LOCAL_AGENT_MODE_HINTS).
Repository policy default branch is read by the CLI pull request call (apps/cli/src/app_server/pull_request.rs:62-65).

working: CLI agent git tools: git_stage, git_unstage, git_commit, git_branch_create, git_push and more, each with a permission class (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/git_tools.rs:68-340).
CLI git_commit commits only what is staged, runs hooks, and asks first when any hook would run (git_tools.rs:157-158).
CLI git_stage refuses a submodule pointer (git_tools.rs:135-137, 439-450).
CLI git_push is always asked for, whatever the approval mode (git_tools.rs:20-45, 325-327).

CLI app-server pull request plan and create: validates title (256 chars) and body (65,536), checks the push plan, requires the reviewed branch to be unchanged, pushes with approval, runs gh pr create, falls back to a compare link (apps/cli/src/app_server/pull_request.rs:61-84, 188-318).

VS Code command 'Code: Create Pull Request' calls that app-server method (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/pullRequest.ts:68-100; apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:1731-1745).

Desktop host push: refuses non-https/ssh remotes, multiple push addresses and local-path remotes, uses an empty hooks directory, and creates a slug-named branch when none is checked out (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/gitService.ts:743-760, 780-790, 913-950).

Desktop and Local-mode web panel: opens the pull request through POST /api/code/local-pull-requests, with CSRF, rate limit and an audit event (apps/web/app/api/code/local-pull-requests/route.ts:59-92).

Web Cloud: POST commit and pull-request session routes with CSRF and managed-compute gates (apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/[sessionId]/commit/route.ts:36-90; apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/[sessionId]/pull-request/route.ts).
incomplete: Web Cloud commit and pull request work only when AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1, E2B_API_KEY and a priceable sandbox rate are set; the brief records that the live check is pending (doc: brief S67.29 'Unfinished'; apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts:19-30).

Desktop: no person-facing 'commit' button was found; commits are made by the agent in the folder. The brief's 'user from the coding surface' commit is therefore unmet on Desktop [inferred from searching dispatcher.ts for commit commands, which found only staging at apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:795-798].
The Cloud commit stages every change when no files are chosen (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-session-service.ts:2157-2162), so 'only what is staged' does not hold there.
disconnected_or_disabled: Cloud commit and pull request are off until the managed Code switches are on (apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/[sessionId]/commit/route.ts:48-55).
The desktop pull request route returns 'capability unavailable' when the deployment has no GitHub App (apps/web/app/api/code/local-pull-requests/route.ts:21-27).

The agent opens a pull request for its branch on the code host.
Commit takes only staged changes, never skips hooks, asks the user first when any hook would run, and does not run when nobody can be asked.
A submodule pointer cannot be staged.

acceptance_criteria: With one staged and one unstaged file, CLI git_commit records only the staged one.

proposed: [proposed] Add a visible 'Commit' action to the Desktop Changes panel for the person, with staged-only semantics matching the CLI tool.
[proposed] Show on Mobile the session's branch and pull request link, read only.

steps.what_happens: A person comments on GitHub.
GitHub posts a signed webhook; AGI verifies the signature, filters, claims the delivery and returns 'queued'.
After the response, the task reads the installation, checks switches, workspace gate and plan.
The task reads the issue or pull request and its failed checks from GitHub.
A managed sandbox session is created and one agent turn runs with the model chosen for the plan.
Changes are committed and pushed from the sandbox; a pull request is opened and a reply is posted.

features.summary: The brief wants a goal plus a turn or time bound, with the agent looping until done or the bound hits. No goal command was found. features.summary: The agent keeps repository notes in project files, loads AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and AGI instruction files into its prompt, and uses skills and plugins a folder defines. On Desktop (local panel) and VS Code the person can save a memory and switch skills and plugins; project skills run only after the person trusts that exact set. Cloud sessions load none of this in the code read.

purpose.what_it_does: Saves a short fact into the repository's CLAUDE.md or the user's instruction file (apps/cli/src/memory.rs:243-279), loads instruction files from the working folder up to the repository root within a 10,000 token budget (apps/cli/src/compaction.rs:11-23, 172-218, 286-300), and lists and toggles skills and plugins with a trust step for project skills (apps/cli/src/app_server/surfaces.rs:105-188).
purpose.why_it_exists: Agents work better and safer with the repository's own rules, remembered facts and skills. Brief items: save repository facts and reuse them (S67.37), load AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md and follow them (S67.38), use project skills and plugins that the user can see or toggle (S67.39).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers with Desktop local sessions, the CLI and VS Code.
problems_solved: The agent forgets repository conventions between sessions.
Untrusted skills in a cloned repository could run scripts; they stay off until the person trusts that exact set (apps/cli/src/skills.rs:395-445, 529).
Files outside the folder, FIFOs and credential files are not read into the prompt (apps/cli/src/compaction.rs:160-166).

Add an AGENTS.md to a repository and have each CLI turn load it.

The desktop checks the shell grant and sends memory/add to the CLI runtime for that folder.
The CLI appends the text to the memory file directly. It does not ask the model to write it.
On the next turn the CLI reads instruction files, memory, rules and the enabled skills, and builds the system prompt.
The prompt, with that text in it, is sent to the session's model: a local model on the device, the person's own provider, or AGI Cloud.

aliases: AGI Code session (phone screen label 'AGI Code')
features.summary: A coding session keeps one id. Cloud Code sessions open by that id on web, desktop (the hosted web app), phone, command line and VS Code, with the same history, repository and branch. Model is chosen per turn by each client, and plan, checkpoints and worktree are shared only on local CLI and VS Code sessions.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person start a coding session on one app and open the same session, by the same id, on another. There are two kinds. Cloud Code sessions live in AGI's servers and are reached through /api/code/sessions. Local developer sessions live on the person's machine in the CLI-hosted store and are shared by CLI, VS Code and Desktop Code (doc: docs/product/definition.md:118-120).
purpose.why_it_exists: The product requirement is one account and one effective session per piece of work, so a person can start at a desk, check from a phone and finish in the editor without copy and paste (doc: docs/product/definition.md:118-120).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers who run coding tasks in a cloud sandbox or in a local terminal, and testers who check that clients agree.
problems_solved: No more re-describing a task on each device.
The same repository and branch are visible everywhere, so nobody works on the wrong branch.
A deleted or unreachable session gives a clear message instead of a crash.
use_cases: Start a cloud session on the web, then follow it from the phone.
Run agi code list in a terminal to find a session id, then open it on the web.
Open the same cloud session from the VS Code Sessions sheet and continue the chat there.
Open a local CLI session in the desktop app's Code view (same host store).

where_to_find_it: Web: page /code and /code/<session id> (apps/web/app/code/[sessionId]/page.tsx:11-15); the session rail lists sessions (apps/web/features/code/components/CodeRail.tsx).

Desktop: the Electron window shows the hosted web app, so it is the same /code page (doc: AGENTS.md section 5); local sessions appear in the web Code view only when it runs inside the desktop host (apps/web/features/code/hooks/use-local-sessions.ts:17-20,120).
Phone: route cloud-code and cloud-code/<session id> (apps/mobile/app/(app)/cloud-code/[sessionId].tsx:4-6); the screen title is 'AGI Code' (packages/contracts/types/src/pairing.ts:30).
CLI: agi code list, agi code show <id>, agi code open <id> (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1092-1097,1203-1214).

VS Code: command 'Code: Open AGI Code Session' (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:596-599) and the cloud tasks tree that refreshes every 15 seconds (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/cloudTasksTree.ts:10).
prerequisites: Cloud Code sessions: signed in to AGI, and the cloud Code service must be switched on for the deployment and the plan must include it (apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/route.ts:57-65).
Phone: Cloud mode and an unlocked cloud account (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/useCloudCodeAccess.ts:36-41).
CLI: Cloud (managed) mode and a signed-in account; other modes are refused (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:361-373).
VS Code: signed in to the AGI account (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/cloudCodeSessions.ts:49-55).
screens_and_controls: Web: session rail, status filters, sort (activity, created, title), search (apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts:495-505); archived banner and Unarchive on the phone (packages/contracts/types/src/cloud-code.ts:241-253).
Phone: session list with search, sort and sections per repository (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/CloudCodeSessionsScreen.tsx:90-104; apps/mobile/__tests__/CloudCodeSessionViews.test.ts).
CLI list filters: open, closed, archived, all (apps/cli/src/cloud/code_sessions.rs:7).
VS Code quick pick title is the session title; placeholder shows state, repository and branch (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/cloudCodeSessions.ts:62-77,284-290).
journey: 1. Create or find a session (web /code, phone AGI Code list, or agi code list).
2. Copy or tap the session; its id is in the address /code/<id>, the phone route, or the CLI list.
3. Open it on another client: web address, phone list row, agi code show <id> or VS Code Open AGI Code Session.
4. The client reads the session and its turns (history), repository and branch and shows them.
5. Send the next task from any client; the others see it on their next read.
feedback_and_outputs: Phone: 'That session is not available. It may have been deleted.' for a missing session, with a button back to the list (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/CloudCodeSessionScreen.tsx:79,394-418).

Phone: 'This session could not be opened' with Try again when loading fails first time; the last good view stays if a later reload fails (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/service.ts:11; useCloudCodeSession.ts:136-141).
Web: 'That session is not available. It may have been deleted.' and a redirect to Code home (apps/web/features/code/code-surface.ts:219; CloudCodePage.tsx:735-747).
CLI: a text list and show output with the page address (apps/cli/src/cloud/code_sessions.rs:224-300).
settings: Transcript view Normal or Verbose on web (apps/web/features/code/components/CodeSessionMenu.tsx:100-120).
Phone model picker feeds the model sent with each turn (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/CloudCodeSessionScreen.tsx:243-247).

working: The same session id opens the same cloud session on web (apps/web/app/code/[sessionId]/page.tsx:11-15), phone (apps/mobile/app/(app)/cloud-code/[sessionId].tsx:4-6), CLI show/open (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3146-3160) and VS Code (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/cloudCodeSessions.ts:272-300).

The session record carries repository address, base branch, working branch, state and timestamps, so every client that reads it shows the same repository and branch (packages/contracts/types/src/cloud-code.ts:99-135).

History is rebuilt from stored turns and their steps on every read, on web and phone (apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx:712-733; apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/useCloudCodeSession.ts:121-133,193-200).

Instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .agiworkforce/instructions.md, at most two) are read on the server from the cloned workspace, so every client gets the same ones (packages/contracts/types/src/project-instructions.ts:1-9; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-project-instructions.ts:27-47).

Local developer sessions: CLI prints worktree and branch in its session status lines (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:2223-2262 [status function]); VS Code lists, creates and removes session worktrees (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/sessionWorktrees.ts:14-60).
The app server advertises checkpoints, so CLI-hosted clients (VS Code, Desktop Code) can list them (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:1058,3661).
incomplete: Model: the session record has no model field; each client sends its own model with every turn (phone: useCloudCodeSession.ts:229-233; VS Code: apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/continueInCloud.ts:116-125; packages/contracts/types/src/cloud-code.ts:99-135). So two clients can run the same session with different models [inferred]. The brief marks S68.06 partial on web and desktop pending the cloud switch (doc: audit/partial/068-session-continuity-and-remote-session-product.md).

Web and desktop cloud Code is partial because the deployment switch needs AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1 and E2B_API_KEY (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts:20-28; doc: audit/partial/068-session-continuity-and-remote-session-product.md). Whether production has them set is unknown.
VS Code, CLI show and list read a snapshot; they do not stream (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/cloudCodeSessions.ts:280).
disconnected_or_disabled: Phone Remote Control to a desktop's local sessions is hidden: FEATURES.companion is false (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:16).
not_available: Worktree association (S68.05) and task plan and checkpoints (S68.07) for cloud sessions on web, desktop and phone: the cloud session record has no such fields (packages/contracts/types/src/cloud-code.ts:99-135; doc: brief S68.05, S68.07).
Chrome extension: not applicable (status n/a).

established.statement: One session identifier names the same coding session on every supported client.
Opening the session on any client shows the same conversation history, active branch and repository.
Every client associates the session with the same worktree.
Every client runs the session with the same model and the same instruction files.
Every client shows the same task plan and checkpoints.
Desktop Code, CLI and VS Code use the same session ids and transcripts; resuming appends to the same id and forking creates a new id.
Web, phone, desktop cloud and Chrome share one signed-in Cloud continuity domain; a change on one must converge on the others.

acceptance_criteria: A cloud session created on web opens by the same id on phone, CLI (agi code show) and VS Code, with the same title, repository and working branch.
The transcript on each client lists the same turns in the same order after a reload.
A deleted session id shows the 'not available' note on web and phone, not an error screen.
A failed reload after a good load keeps the last good view on phone and shows an error line.
With the cloud switch off, web and desktop show the unavailable notice and create nothing.
Opening a local CLI session in VS Code shows the same transcript and branch.
inferred: Model should be stored on the session or shown per turn so clients agree [inferred from S68.06 and the missing field].
Instruction files agree across clients only because the server reads them; a local client reading its own copy may differ [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Store the model used on each turn record and show it in every client.
[proposed] Show the worktree path and plan on cloud sessions by adding them to the session record.

aliases: Live view of a running turn
features.summary: A running cloud Code turn is shown on web and phone by reading the session every 4 seconds while the turn runs. Local sessions have real reconnect: after a drop, VS Code, desktop and the terminal remote host get the partial reply and pending approvals back. Read-only attach is declined by decision.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows what a running coding turn is doing (tool steps, commands, final message) on a second client, and lets a client that lost its connection return to the same state.
purpose.why_it_exists: A person starts a long task, closes the laptop or locks the phone, and wants to see progress and pick up where they left off.
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers running long cloud or local coding turns, and testers of reconnect behaviour.
problems_solved: Long turns are not lost when a tab closes or a phone sleeps.
A second client can see tool activity without owning the turn.
A client opened mid-turn can still answer pending approvals (local kind).
use_cases: Start a cloud task on web, watch it on the phone.
Lock the phone during a turn, unlock, see new steps.
Reload VS Code during a local turn and get the partial reply back.
Run agi code show to see what each turn did.

where_to_find_it: Web: the Code page transcript for an open session (apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx:700-757).

Phone: the AGI Code session screen; a 'Working' indicator and stop control show while a turn runs (packages/contracts/types/src/cloud-code.ts:241-253; apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/CloudCodeSessionScreen.tsx:527-532).
CLI: agi code show <id> for a snapshot (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3146); after agi code start the terminal waits for the turn (lib.rs:3365-3386).
VS Code: the Sessions quick pick (a snapshot) and the cloud tasks tree (refresh every 15 seconds) (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/cloudCodeSessions.ts:272-290; cloudTasksTree.ts:10).
Desktop and VS Code local turns: the chat panel shows the live reply and reattaches after reload (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:3085-3110).
prerequisites: A session that is running a turn.
Cloud kind: cloud switch on and plan entitled (see F068-01).
Phone to desktop Remote Control: hidden in the first release (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:16).
screens_and_controls: Phone 'Stop the task' and 'Stopping the task' labels (packages/contracts/types/src/cloud-code.ts:244-245).
Phone offline screen with Reconnect button and 'Reconnecting to <computer>…' text (apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/code/[threadId].tsx:19-44,59-62).
Web pairing note: 'It reconnects on its own while Remote Control is on' (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/RemoteControlSection.tsx:43-44).
journey: 1. A turn starts on one client.
2. A second client opens the session.
3. The second client reads the session now and again every 4 seconds while the latest turn has no stop reason.
4. New tool steps appear as the server stores them.
5. When the turn ends polling stops; on foreground return the phone reads once more.
feedback_and_outputs: Steps appear with their label and an error mark (packages/contracts/types/src/cloud-code.ts:257-264).
Phone: 'Reconnecting to <computer>…' while connecting, reconnecting or stale; '<computer> is offline' with an explanation when not (apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/code/[threadId].tsx:33-61).
VS Code local: notice 'Some live output was missed, so this answer was reloaded from the local runtime.' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:5278-5290).
settings: Transcript Normal or Verbose on web (apps/web/features/code/components/CodeSessionMenu.tsx:100-120).
None found for the poll interval; it is a constant.

working: The cloud turn writes one step row per finished tool call, so a poll sees progress (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-agent-service.ts:757-780).
Web polls every 4 seconds while the latest stored turn has no stop reason, and skips a read while the page's own turn is pending (apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx:182,699-757).

Phone polls every 4 seconds when ready, the app is active and a turn or busy session exists; it waits for a slow poll before asking again (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/useCloudCodeSession.ts:35,175-193; test apps/mobile/__tests__/CloudCodeSessionPolling.test.tsx).
Phone reloads on foreground (useCloudCodeSession.ts:159-163).

Local kind: thread/reconnect returns the running turn id, partial reply, next delta index, next event sequence, and pending approvals and questions (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:3943-4010).

VS Code attaches to a running local turn on reload and recovers missed output (ChatStateManager.ts:3085-3110,5255-5290); desktop does the same through toPanelActiveTurn (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerSessionService.ts:2600-2640,2667-2676); the terminal remote host also answers reconnect (apps/cli/src/tui/remote_host.rs:448-470).
incomplete: The cloud view is polling, not streaming; the phone and web show steps only after the server stores them [inferred from the poll design].
VS Code cloud sheet and agi code show are single reads (cloudCodeSessions.ts:280; apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3146).

CLI wait for the first cloud turn uses a 330-second request limit while the server turn limit is 800 seconds (apps/cli/src/cloud/code_handoff.rs:14; packages/contracts/types/src/cloud-code.ts:259-266), so a long turn may outlast the CLI wait [inferred].
disconnected_or_disabled: Phone Remote Control (companion) screens are hidden by FEATURES.companion = false (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:16).
not_available: Read-only attach (S68.10): not built on any app by decision D-2026-09-28-03 (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:166).
Attaching to a turn running in another process on CLI, VS Code, desktop: not built by decision (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:88).
Chrome: not applicable.

established.statement: Tool activity of a running turn streams to every attached client.
After a dropped connection the client reconnects and resumes the same session state.
A client may attach read-only (S68.10) - declined, not built.
Attaching to a turn run by another process is not built on CLI, VS Code, desktop.

acceptance_criteria: While a cloud turn runs, a second client shows new steps within about two poll intervals (8 seconds).
Polling stops when the turn has a stop reason, and on the phone when the app is in the background.
Returning the phone to the foreground triggers one reload.
After reloading VS Code mid local turn, the partial reply and pending approvals reappear.
No client offers a read-only attach control.
A failed poll does not blank the transcript.
inferred: Web and phone should show approvals in the same poll so a waiting turn is noticed [inferred from useCloudCodeSession.ts:121-127].
proposed: [proposed] Add server push so cloud steps show without a 4-second delay.
[proposed] Make the CLI wait limit follow the server limit constant.

features.summary: When a cloud coding agent pauses for permission, the request is stored on the server for 30 minutes and any signed-in client of the account can approve or deny it: web, phone, command line and VS Code. The same clients can send a new task and stop a running turn.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person answer an agent's permission request, send new tasks and stop a turn from whichever client is at hand.
purpose.why_it_exists: Agents ask before risky steps. If the answer only worked in the starting client, work would stall when the person moves away.
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers running cloud Code tasks across devices; testers of approval flows.
problems_solved: A task waiting on approval can be finished from the phone.
A decision on an expired request is refused clearly.
Two clients cannot both decide the same step.
use_cases: Approve a command from the phone while away from the desk.
Run agi code approvals in a terminal and agi code approve <handle>.
Reject a step from the VS Code Sessions quick pick.
Stop a runaway turn from the phone.

where_to_find_it: Web: approval cards in the session on the Code page (apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx:2649).
Phone: an 'Approval required' card under the transcript (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/CloudCodeSessionScreen.tsx:535-541).
CLI: agi code approvals, agi code approve <handle>, agi code reject <handle> (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1218-1224).
VS Code: Sessions quick pick shows 'Approval required' with 'Approve and continue' and 'Deny' rows (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/cloudCodeSessions.ts:178-205).
prerequisites: A cloud session whose latest turn is waiting for approval.
Cloud switch on and the account's plan allowed (see access).
Approval not older than 30 minutes (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-agent-service.ts:957-966).
screens_and_controls: Phone buttons use the labels 'Approve and continue' and 'Deny' (packages/contracts/types/src/cloud-code.ts:247-250; packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts:30-31; CloudCodeApprovalCard.tsx:50-58).

Phone first-run notice 'Code sessions use your approval setting' (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/components/CodeApprovalNotice.tsx:13).
journey: 1. The agent hits a step needing permission and the turn stops with 'awaiting approval'.
2. The server stores an approval row (command, reason) valid for 30 minutes.
3. A client lists approvals (web and phone on each read; CLI agi code approvals; VS Code when opening the session).
4. The person taps Approve and continue or Deny.
5. The client sends turn id, step index and decision; the server resumes the same turn and returns its result.
6. Other clients see the new state on their next read.

settings: Tool approval policy synced on the phone (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/components/CodeApprovalNotice.tsx:9,17-19; route /(app)/settings/auto-approve at line 14).

Decision body needs turnId, a non-negative integer stepIndex and decision approve or reject (route.ts:80-94).
Decision runs rate limit, CSRF check, deployment gate, then managed compute access for the account (route.ts:62-69,97-106).
An expired approval gives a conflict error (route.ts:42; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-agent-approval-service.ts:29-34,305-316).
Pending approvals are retired when their turn is no longer suspended (cloud-code-agent-approval-service.ts:85-97).

Phone, web, CLI and VS Code all call listApprovals/decideApproval (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/useCloudCodeSession.ts:126-127; apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx:775,1522; apps/cli/src/cloud/code_sessions.rs:118-145; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/cloudCodeSessions.ts:243-270).

Stop is recorded on the server and audited (apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/[sessionId]/agent/cancel/route.ts:56-59); CLI cancel uses the same endpoint (apps/cli/src/cloud/code_handoff.rs:500-508).
The CLI decision is idempotent by a key built from session, turn, step and decision (code_sessions.rs:136).
incomplete: The list route has no deployment gate, but the web page reads approvals only when it may run (route.ts:46-57; CloudCodePage.tsx:770).

Attaching to a turn running in another process on CLI, VS Code, desktop: declined (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:88).

established.statement: An approval pending in the session shows on every attached client and can be answered from any of them.
A client attaches with full control: send turns, stop, approve.
Attaching to a turn running in another process is not built for CLI, VS Code, desktop; work moves by reviewed hand-off.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: An approval created by a turn shows on web, phone, CLI and VS Code for the same account.
Approving on one client resumes the turn; a second decision on the same step gets a conflict.
A decision after 30 minutes is refused as expired.
With the cloud switch off the decision returns 'Managed Code is not enabled for this deployment'.
The phone does not reload while a decision is pending and hides that card.
Send is blocked while a turn runs; Stop works only while a turn runs.
A decision for an account without managed compute access is refused by the access gate.
inferred: Two clients racing on one approval resolve to one success and one conflict [inferred from the 'already decided' conflict in cloud-code-agent-approval-service.ts:316].
Stop should confirm what is lost [inferred from AGENTS.md section 9]; the phone stop has no confirmation in the code read.
proposed: [proposed] Show who decided an approval on the other clients.
[proposed] Add a confirmation naming what a stop discards.

steps.what_happens: The agent turn stops and an approval row is inserted with a 30 minute expiry.
A client lists approvals for the session.
Person chooses Approve or Deny; client posts turn id, step index and decision.
Server checks rate limit, CSRF, deployment, subscription and workspace access, then resumes the turn.
The resumed command runs in the cloud sandbox.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The decision itself uses no model. The resumed turn uses the model of the turn (stored with the turn; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-agent-service.ts:661-683). The plan tier is passed to the resume for metering (approvals route.ts:107-115).

aliases: Who owns execution and handing control
features.summary: For local sessions, one program at a time holds a writer lease on the session file. The terminal warns about a second writer; the app server, VS Code and the desktop Code view refuse, name the holder and offer Take over. Control also moves with 'Continue in VS Code'. A standing owner label exists only in the CLI.

purpose.what_it_does: Tells which program is writing a local coding session and lets the person move control to another client on purpose.
purpose.why_it_exists: Two programs appending to one session file lose each other's turns. A lease stops the clash and names the writer.
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers who use the same local session from the terminal, VS Code and the desktop app.
problems_solved: Two clients writing at once and leaving duplicate copies.
Not knowing which program has the session.
A crashed program that never released the session.
use_cases: Open a terminal session in VS Code and take it over.
See 'Writing: ...' in the terminal status.
Move a web Code session to VS Code with Continue in VS Code.
Hand the session back before running it in the terminal.

journey: 1. Client A holds the lease while it works.
2. Client B tries to send a turn.
3. B is refused with the holder's label, or sees the held notice.

working: A lease file per session records holder id, label, process id, times; stale when expired or the process is gone (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/writer_lease.rs:19-41).

The app server refuses a turn while another live process holds the lease, takes over on request, releases on request but not while a turn runs, and emits writer change notifications (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:1838-1890,4011-4063).
A clean exit releases leases (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8556; writer_lease.rs:85-89).

aliases: Hand a local session to the cloud
features.summary: On the command line, agi code handoff sends a local session to a new cloud Code session after showing what moves and what stays, and agi code start sends a new task. VS Code's 'Continue in the Cloud' starts a new task from the open repository. Web, desktop and phone have no hand-off.

purpose.what_it_does: Moves coding work from the person's machine to cloud execution, after a review that names the repository and branch, the task or session record that move, and the files and settings that stay.
purpose.why_it_exists: Long work can run while the laptop is closed, but nothing may leave the machine without the person seeing it first (doc: docs/product/definition.md:120).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers with a GitHub repository who want cloud execution of a local task.
problems_solved: Surprise uploads: the review lists moves and stays.
Cloud work starting from code that GitHub does not have.
Local or own-key sessions silently reaching our cloud.
use_cases: Run agi code start "fix the failing test" in a checkout.
Run agi code handoff to continue a local session in the cloud.
In VS Code, run Code: Continue in the Cloud, type a task and confirm.

where_to_find_it: CLI: agi code start <task> and agi code handoff [session] (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1163-1196).

VS Code: command palette 'Code: Continue in the Cloud' (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:592-595) and the Sessions sheet on the Cloud tab (doc: audit/partial/068-session-continuity-and-remote-session-product.md, S68.16 note).
Web, desktop, phone: not available.
prerequisites: Cloud (managed) mode and a signed-in account (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:361-379).
A git checkout of a GitHub repository with the branch on GitHub (apps/cli/src/cloud/code_handoff.rs:209-280).
For handoff: no unpushed commits, and a saved local session in this folder that is in Managed mode (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3209-3218; code_push.rs:40-93).
Cloud Code switched on for the deployment and plan (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-session-open.ts:44-53).
screens_and_controls: Review text: 'Hand this task to a cloud Code session:', 'What moves to the cloud', 'What stays on this machine', 'Access:' (apps/cli/src/cloud/code_handoff.rs:412-433).
Prompt 'Hand this session to the cloud?' default no; '--yes' or '-y' skips it; '--model'; '--json' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1163-1196,3238).

VS Code input box 'Continue in the cloud' with the prompt about the branch, then a modal review with a 'Continue in the cloud' button (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/continueInCloud.ts:14,109-131).
journey: 1. Push the branch to GitHub and commit what should travel.
2. Run agi code handoff (or start).
3. The CLI inspects git, checks GitHub access, picks the cloud model and prints the review.
4. Answer the prompt (or pass --yes).
5. The CLI sends the record, the server opens a session and returns a seed prompt.
6. The first cloud turn runs; Ctrl-C stops it and keeps the session.
7. The result and the session address print; bring the branch back later (F068-06).
feedback_and_outputs: Moves list includes the repository and branch on GitHub 'as of your last fetch', and the task with 'Trusted hosts' network access; for handoff also 'this session's handoff record: its goal, the approvals you gave, its plan and architecture notes, the files it changed, the checks it ran and this folder's path' (code_handoff.rs:333-351).
Stays list includes unpushed commits, changed and untracked files, and local settings (code_handoff.rs:352-389).

Refusals: '<branch> has N commit(s) that are not pushed ... push first' (lib.rs:3209-3214); 'Nothing was handed off: this run cannot ask for confirmation. Re-run with --yes.' (lib.rs:3234-3235); 'Nothing was handed off.' on a No answer (lib.rs:3238-3240).
Warning 'Uncommitted changes stay on this machine; the cloud session works from the pushed branch.' (code_push.rs:174-178).
VS Code: refusals about no GitHub remote, detached HEAD, no upstream (continueInCloud.ts:24-36) and 'sign in to AGI Cloud' (line 103).
settings: Default cloud model from config default.cloud_model, else a coding model the plan includes (lib.rs:1171-1176 doc comments).
Network access is fixed at 'trusted' (code_handoff.rs:11).

working: agi code handoff: inspect git, refuse unpushed commits, find the local session in this folder, admit only Managed mode, review, confirm, post to /api/code/sessions/handoff, then run the first cloud turn (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3197-3268).
agi code start: validate task (max 8000 characters, no null byte), review, confirm, create session, run first turn (lib.rs:3270-3331; code_handoff.rs:9,95-110).

Server admits a hand-off only when it is fresh, for the same account, of a supported protocol and addressed to managed Code; otherwise 422 with a refusal reason (apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/handoff/route.ts:60-110; test apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/handoff/route.test.ts).
A retried hand-off reuses the session by request id (route.test.ts 'gives the same request id to the same handoff so a retry reuses the session').
Private repositories need the GitHub app; otherwise the session clones it as public and the review says to connect GitHub on the Code page (code_handoff.rs:390-404).
The CLI turns the 422 refusal reasons into plain text (code_push.rs:118-133,141-164).

VS Code shows a modal review with repository, branch, model, network, what moves and stays, unpushed and uncommitted counts (continueInCloud.ts:60-85; packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/vscode.json:228-235), creates the session and runs the first turn (continueInCloud.ts:142,164).
incomplete: VS Code creates a new session from a freshly typed task; it does not use the hand-off endpoint and so sends no session record (continueInCloud.ts:142-164; apps/web/__tests__/api/routes-without-callers.test.ts:160-161 says the CLI posts there). The brief marks it partial.
CLI first-turn wait is 330 seconds while the server turn limit is 800 seconds (code_handoff.rs:14; packages/contracts/types/src/cloud-code.ts:259-266) [inferred risk].
Unpushed commits are listed under 'stays' in the review but block only handoff; agi code start does not block on them (code_handoff.rs:353-359; lib.rs:3209-3215 vs 3281-3290).
disconnected_or_disabled: Cloud session creation needs the deployment switch; without it the server refuses with 'Managed Code is not enabled for this deployment. Use the desktop app for local code.' (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-session-open.ts:44-48).
not_available: Web, desktop and phone hand-off and transfer review: not built (doc: brief S68.16, S68.18). Phone creates new cloud sessions only.
Summary-only transfer and transcript branch (S68.28, S68.29): declined (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:164-168).

established.statement: The user explicitly hands a local session to cloud execution, seeing what moves.
Before a transfer the user reviews which files, context and environment move.
Moving context between local and cloud is an explicit, provenance-preserving handoff with payload preview, secret scanning, consent and a new destination record.
Cloud handoff must not overwrite local context.
Summary-only and transcript-branch options are not built.
No local, BYOK or managed move happens silently; a Local to BYOK move is an explicit fork.

acceptance_criteria: agi code handoff with an unpushed commit exits with the 'push first' error and sends nothing.
Without a terminal and without --yes, nothing is sent.
The review lists the repository and branch, the task or record, and the files that stay, before any request.
A Local or own-key session is refused with a message naming the mode.
A private repository not in a GitHub installation shows the connect-GitHub line.
With the cloud switch off, the server refuses and no session is created.
Repeating the same handoff reuses the same cloud session.
inferred: Secret scanning of the handoff record should happen before upload; not found in the CLI path read [inferred from definition.md:120].
proposed: [proposed] Offer hand-off on web and desktop for local sessions.
[proposed] Make VS Code send a real session record through the hand-off endpoint.

features.summary: A cloud session's work comes back as a git branch. The terminal does it with agi resume --teleport (checks out the branch and loads the history). VS Code does it with a cloud-task link or the Sessions sheet 'Bring the branch in'. Web and desktop offer 'Continue in VS Code'; desktop continues cloud sessions through the hosted Code page.

purpose.what_it_does: Moves the result of a cloud Code session into the person's local checkout, and lets the person keep working on a cloud session from the desktop app.
purpose.why_it_exists: Cloud work ends as a branch and a transcript; the person needs both locally to review and finish. The leaders do the same through a terminal command (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:342-350).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers who start tasks in the cloud and finish in a local editor or terminal.
problems_solved: Cloud branch and local checkout drift apart.
Overwriting uncommitted local work when switching branch.
Starting the local review from scratch.
use_cases: Run agi resume --teleport in the repository to pull the cloud branch and history.
Click Continue in VS Code on a cloud session's changes panel.
In VS Code open a cloud session and pick 'Bring the branch in'.
Continue a cloud session in the desktop app's Code page.

prerequisites: The cloud session has a working branch pushed to GitHub and a GitHub repository (apps/cli/src/cloud/code_teleport.rs:134-150,167).
A local clone of that repository (not a fork) is open (code_teleport.rs:100-115).

journey: 1. The cloud session works and pushes its branch.
2. In the terminal run agi resume --teleport (or in VS Code open the session or the link).
3. The tool checks the repository, the branch name and the working tree.
4. It fetches the branch and checks it out (CLI fast-forwards only).
5. The CLI imports the cloud history into a local session named code-<id> and resumes it.
6. New work stays local until pushed.

established.statement: Results of cloud work come back into the user's local workspace.
From the desktop app, the user continues a coding session that runs in the cloud.
A cloud session's result comes local through the CLI and VS Code; the desktop hands a cloud session to VS Code or the terminal and adds no native pull.
Cloud handoff must not overwrite local context.
Anything that could discard local work names the files at risk and asks first.

acceptance_criteria: agi resume --teleport in the right repository checks out the cloud branch and opens a session with the cloud turns.
It refuses a dirty tree, a fork, an invalid branch name, and a session with no branch, each with its message.
Opening a vscode cloud-task link never changes the checkout by itself.
Bring the branch in on a dirty tree asks 'Switch anyway' and lists the files; No leaves it untouched.
A link with no branch or no repository changes nothing and says why.
The web button is absent when the session has no repository or working branch.
With cloud Code off, the web Code page shows the unavailable notice.

features.summary: A paired AGI Mobile phone follows, steers, stops and answers approvals for coding sessions running on the person's own computer, and can ask that computer to start a new session in a folder the computer has approved. The computer decides every time. In the v1 phone build the whole phone side is switched off.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a phone talk through the relay to a computer that runs AGI Code sessions (the Desktop app, a terminal running the command line, or VS Code). The phone lists the computer's sessions, opens one, sends guidance, interrupts a turn, answers the agent's approval and question prompts, reads diffs, and starts a new session by sending a task text and a folder choice. The computer re-checks that the folder is allowed on every command. [inferred from apps/mobile/src/features/companion/remote-code/service.ts:15-117 and apps/desktop/electron/remote/remoteControlService.ts:219-280]
purpose.why_it_exists: Work that must run on the person's own machine (their files, their tools) should still be reachable when they are away from the desk. The brief states: 'From the phone, the user continues a coding session that runs on their local machine' (S68.14) and 'starts a new session on a remote machine inside a folder that machine allows' (S68.24). (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/068-session-continuity-and-remote-session-product.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: A person with a paid plan who has AGI Desktop (or the command line, or VS Code) signed in on a computer and AGI Mobile on a phone, on the same account. [inferred from apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:57-78 and apps/web/app/api/pair/claim/route.ts:55-67]
problems_solved: A long agent turn on the computer waits for an approval while the person is away; the phone can answer it.
The person wants to start a task on the computer without walking back to it.
A phone must never get more reach than the person allowed on the computer: folders and approvals are decided on the computer.
use_cases: Follow a running refactor on the Desktop app from the phone and send one line of guidance.
Allow or deny an agent's approval request from the phone; a risky one opens a native dialog on the computer first.
Describe a task in the phone's 'New session on this computer' box, pick an approved folder and start it.
Press stop on a runaway turn from the phone.

where_to_find_it: Phone (AGI Mobile): 'Remote' screen (Companion), cards 'Your computers' and, once connected, a code sessions card with 'New session on this computer' [apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/index.tsx:270; apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/CodeSessionsCard.tsx:47]. Also the 'New session' sheet of the Cloud Code screen offers 'the paired computer' [apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/components/NewCloudCodeSessionSheet.tsx:346-352; doc: docs/decisions/2026-11-13-founder-decisions.md:143-150]. Both are switched off in v1: FEATURES.companion and FEATURES.dispatch are false [apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:12,16], the Remote screen then shows 'Remote isn't available in this build' [apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/index.tsx:183; apps/mobile/src/shared/components/FeatureUnavailable.tsx], and the Cloud Code computer section returns nothing [apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/components/CodeDevicesSection.tsx:190].

Computer: Desktop app Settings, Capabilities, 'Remote Control', button 'Pair a phone' [apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/RemoteControlSection.tsx:293; apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/DesktopSetupChecklistView.tsx:52]. VS Code: command 'agi-workforce.remoteControl' [apps/extension-vscode/src/features/remote-control/index.ts:12-18].

Web: no folder-start screen. The page /code/computer ('Your computer') sends a task to Desktop as a dispatch task, not a code session in a chosen folder [apps/web/app/code/computer/page.tsx; apps/web/features/remote-dispatch/components/RemoteComputerPage.tsx:53].
prerequisites: Signed in to the same account on phone and computer, on a paid plan [apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:68; packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:332-352].
Phone is paired and its status is 'connected' (feature F068-09). A request is not sent otherwise [apps/mobile/src/features/companion/remote-code/service.ts:20].
The computer's app is open (not asleep, not quit) and Remote Control is on. [apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/code/[threadId].tsx:19-20]

Desktop: the folder is approved and the agent has the shell-execute grant for it [apps/desktop/electron/runtime/agentAccess.ts:15-26]. VS Code: the folder is an open workspace folder and the workspace is trusted [apps/extension-vscode/src/features/remote-control/remoteControlService.ts:99-105,229-231]. Command line: only the folder where 'agi remote-control' runs [apps/cli/src/remote_control/host.rs:782-786].

The computer must advertise the capability 'code-session-start' or the phone offers no start box [apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/DesktopInfoCard.tsx:80; apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/AccountComputersCard.tsx:106-107].
screens_and_controls: Radio list of approved folders with branch name; text box 'Describe a task for AGI Code' (labelled 'Task for a new AGI Code session'); button 'Start session' (shows 'Starting…') [apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/CodeSessionsCard.tsx:47-117].
Text 'No approved folder can run a session right now.' when no folder is available [CodeSessionsCard.tsx:50].
Session view with steer, stop and approval controls [apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/CodeSessionView.tsx; remote-code/service.ts:42-60,91-117].

Computer: native dialog 'Allow this phone?' with buttons 'Cancel' and 'Allow this phone' at pairing [apps/desktop/electron/remote/remoteControlService.ts:196-203]; a second native sheet when a phone approval needs the computer's own confirmation [remoteControlService.ts:85,116-190].
journey: 1. Pair the phone with the computer (F068-09).
2. Open the Remote screen; the phone asks the computer for its sessions and folders ('code.sessions.list') [apps/mobile/src/features/companion/components/CodeSessionsCard.tsx:171-173].

3. Pick an approved folder, type a task, press 'Start session'. The phone refuses an empty task or one over 8000 characters [apps/mobile/src/features/companion/remote-code/service.ts:62-65; packages/contracts/types/src/remote-code.ts:46].

4. The request travels through the relay to the computer, which checks the folder is still approved, starts a session and a first turn, and answers with the new thread id [packages/platform/utils/src/remoteControl/codeRemoteController.ts:651-696; apps/desktop/electron/remote/remoteControlService.ts:257-262].
5. The phone opens the new session screen. It can steer, interrupt, answer approvals and read diffs [useCodeSessionStart.ts:22-30; CodeSessionsCard.tsx:41-44].
6. An approval that the computer reserves for itself opens a native dialog on the computer and waits two minutes; the phone is told it is waiting [remoteControlService.ts:85,116-190].

Check it there.', 'The session could not be started on this computer. Try again, or start it there.', 'Too many sessions were started from the phone just now. Wait a few minutes.' [packages/platform/utils/src/remoteControl/codeRemoteController.ts:48-53].

Approval held on the computer: 'This needs to be allowed at your computer. A dialog is open there now.' and, if the screen is locked, 'This has to be allowed at your computer, and its screen is locked. Unlock it and answer again.' [remoteControlService.ts:90-103,132-136].

Offline: '<name> is offline' with 'Remote access stops while the computer is asleep, offline, or has AGI Desktop closed...' and a 'Reconnect' button [apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/code/[threadId].tsx:19-22,48-57].
settings: Computer side: the folder grant (shell-execute) per approved folder [agentAccess.ts:15-26]; Remote Control on/off in Capabilities [RemoteControlSection.tsx].
Phone side: no per-feature setting found for starting sessions. Notifications are a separate feature (F068-10).

working: Desktop host accepts 'code.session.start' for an approved folder, checks it again on each command, refuses unapproved folders, rate-limits starts to 10 per 10 minutes and 8 running at once [apps/desktop/electron/remote/remoteControlService.ts:73-83,229-263; packages/platform/utils/src/remoteControl/codeRemoteController.ts:44-46,651-696,746-756].
Desktop advertises 'code-sessions' and 'code-session-start' to the phone at pairing [packages/platform/utils/src/remoteControl/remoteControlHost.ts:681].

Phone code sends list, attach, detach, steer, interrupt, start, history, approval and question requests with a protocol version and request id; refuses an over-long task or guidance (2000) before sending [apps/mobile/src/features/companion/remote-code/service.ts:15-117; packages/contracts/types/src/remote-code.ts:27-46].

Phone start UI exists (folder radios, task box, Start button) and is reused in the 'Your computers' sheet and the Cloud Code new-session sheet [CodeSessionsCard.tsx:19-130; AccountComputersCard.tsx:61-88,282-284; NewCloudCodeSessionSheet.tsx:346-352].
Approval hold dialog on the computer: two-minute limit, refused when the screen is locked or no window can open [remoteControlService.ts:85,116-190].

established.statement: The user can continue, from the phone, a coding session that runs on their local machine.
From another client the user starts a new session on a remote machine inside a folder that machine allows.
A phone reaches a folder only while the person at the computer has allowed the agent to run there; nothing a phone sends raises a prompt that grants access.
A phone's approval that the computer reserves must be confirmed in a native dialog on the computer; with the screen locked or no answer within two minutes it is dropped and the agent keeps waiting.
Remote Control comes with paid plans only.
In Local mode the phone shows only what works with no account; Remote is Cloud only because pairing needs a signed-in account and the relay.
A session on the computer opens on the phone as a conversation; New session offers the cloud or the paired computer.

acceptance_criteria: With a paired phone and an approved folder, a 'code.session.start' request creates a session in that folder and the phone receives its thread id.
A start request for a folder the computer no longer approves is refused with 'That folder is not approved for AGI Code on this computer.' and no session or turn is created.
A task over 8000 characters or empty is refused on the phone and sends nothing.
The eleventh start within ten minutes is refused with the 'Too many sessions' text.

A phone allow that needs the computer's confirmation opens a native dialog; with the screen locked the phone gets the 'unlock it and answer again' text; unanswered for two minutes the dialog closes and the agent keeps waiting.
Withdrawing the folder grant on the computer makes the next phone command for it fail at once.
With FEATURES.companion off, the phone never sends a control message and shows the 'not available' screen.
inferred: A phone with a plan that lacks Remote Control cannot start sessions because pairing is refused (403 plan_upgrade_required) [apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:57-78].

Which model and provider run the started turn is chosen on the computer, not by the phone; the request carries only rootId, text and title [apps/mobile/src/features/companion/remote-code/service.ts:62-72; codeRemoteController.ts:679-688]. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Add a web client for 'code.session.start' with a folder picker, so web reaches parity with the phone.
[proposed] Show on the phone which model and provider the started session will use before 'Start session'.
[proposed] Turn on the phone flags behind a live check once the relay is verified in production.

steps.what_happens: Person types a task and chooses a folder on the phone; the phone checks length and builds a request with version, request id and time.
The connection store signs the control message and sends it over the paired relay socket; it refuses when the pair flags are off or the status is not connected.
The relay forwards the message between the two paired devices and rechecks account, plan and switch while the pairing lives.
The computer's host parses the request, checks rate limits, lists its sessions, and finds the folder; a missing or unavailable folder returns an error to the phone.
The Desktop wrapper checks the folder is approved and the shell-execute grant is held, then starts a developer session and a first turn with the task text.
The new session's agent turn runs on the computer; the model call goes to whatever route that session uses. Which route is not decided by the phone.
The computer replies 'code.session.started' with the thread id; the phone opens the session view.

data.what: Task text, folder id, thread id, session events and diffs
data.where_stored: Session data lives on the computer's session store; the phone keeps a view in its remote-code store. Relay carries messages in transit. Phone store persistence details: unknown.
data.synced: Streamed over the relay while paired; not a cloud copy found in this code path.
data.retained_or_deleted: Computer session stays until the person removes it; phone view cleared on disconnect (connectionStore.ts:1339-1368 resets agents and dispatch tasks). Relay retention of message content: not found.

data.what: Pairing credentials and the persisted computer name

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The phone and relay do not call a model. The started turn runs in the computer's own agent session; the model and provider are chosen there. The command line host shares only Managed-mode sessions and refuses Local or own-key folders with a message [apps/cli/src/remote_control/host.rs:47,812].

access_and_usage.account: Required. The phone claims a pairing through an account-authenticated web route; the relay itself cannot tell accounts apart [apps/web/app/api/pair/claim/route.ts:37-46,55-61].
access_and_usage.permissions: Per command the Desktop checks the folder is approved and the shell-execute capability is granted for it; a worktree is covered by its source folder [apps/desktop/electron/runtime/agentAccess.ts:15-26; remoteControlService.ts:73-83]. Phone must be confirmed by the person at the computer ('Allow this phone?') [remoteControlService.ts:196-210].
access_and_usage.subscription: Remote Control needs a paid plan: basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise [packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:332-352]. Checked when pairing is created, claimed and again by the relay while the pairing lives [apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:97-123]. The feature registry also names entitlement 'developer_surfaces' and policy 'remote_control' for this feature [packages/contracts/types/src/feature-registry.json:193-199]; how the two relate: unknown.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: 10 phone starts per 10 minutes and 8 phone sessions running at once [codeRemoteController.ts:44-46]. Task up to 8000 characters, guidance 2000 [remote-code.ts:29,46]. Approval hold 120000 ms [remoteControlService.ts:85]. Pairing routes use the 'device-link' rate limit [apps/web/app/api/pair/claim/route.ts:63]. No usage metering of the start found.
access_and_usage.flags: Phone: FEATURES.companion and FEATURES.dispatch (both false) [apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:12,16]. Server: the 'screen_share' kill switch governs Remote Control [apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:29-52; feature-registry.json:187]; workspace policy 'remote_control'.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not applicable to the relay. The started session's model is the computer's choice; no model rule found in these files.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Command line host: only Managed sessions are shared [apps/cli/src/remote_control/host.rs:47]. Others: none found in the code.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Remote is Cloud only on the phone (doc: docs/decisions/2026-11-13-founder-decisions.md:96-99). The command line refuses to start Remote Control unless its privacy mode is Managed [apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:368-372; apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:1337]. Local inference on the computer is untouched by this feature; a session in Local or own-key mode on the command line cannot be shared.

Web and phone render cards; the command line prints a list. Offline explanations exist only in a few places. The phone card is switched off in v1.
