established.statement: The user sees which of their machines are available to run sessions.
Each remote machine appears as a card with name, platform and status.
Each machine advertises what it can host (local models, browser, MCP, computer use, code sessions).
When the machine is offline, the client says so and explains what that means.
Owned device listing and revocation use the current session scope; browser pairing pages never claim the browser completed a pairing.
Remote is Cloud only on the phone; in Local it is not shown.

acceptance_criteria: A computer signed in on the account appears with its name, platform and a status within one heartbeat.
A computer that stopped heartbeating shows 'Offline' after the presence window; one quit Desktop reads online for at most about two minutes.
The capability line lists exactly the capabilities the device reported.
An offline computer is not offered as a pairing or start target on the phone (row inert).
The list survives a failed refresh: old rows stay with a message.
Unlinking a device removes the row only on success.
inferred: Capability 'localModels' for Desktop should reflect real local inference when it exists, since local inference on desktop is a product requirement; the code reports false [inferred from dispatcher.ts:2298].
Offline help should appear wherever the word Offline appears [inferred from S68.25].
proposed: [proposed] Add one shared sentence for each presence state and show it under the card on web, phone and command line.
[proposed] Add 'code sessions' as a reported capability in the registry contract.
[proposed] Show a distinct error state on /code/computer instead of the empty-list message.

steps.what_happens: Each computer app sends a periodic heartbeat with its name, platform and capabilities (Desktop every 45 s, others every 5 minutes).
The server stores the row and sets remote_enabled (it can only fall back to off through heartbeat).
A viewing app asks for the list; the server runs three queries, computes presence from last seen time and returns up to 200 devices.

features.summary: The person pairs a phone (or a signed-in browser) to a computer with a short-lived code or QR, confirms it on the computer, and can end the pairing from either side or unlink the device. The relay rechecks account and plan while a pairing lives. The phone side is off in v1; command line and VS Code can also host a pairing.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates a one-time, five-minute pairing on the relay for the computer (initiate), lets a phone or browser of the same account claim it (claim), asks the person at the computer to allow that phone, then keeps a signed channel for session control. Either side ends it; unlinking a device also stops remote work and drops live relay sessions. A phone staying connected after a plan downgrade or workspace switch-off (the relay rechecks).

established.statement: The user pairs a phone or other client with a machine so it can reach that machine's sessions.
The user revokes a pairing from either side and it stops working at once.
A claim for a pairing that belongs to another account is refused (403) and audited.
Pairing is refused with 503 'Pairing is not configured' if the relay is not set up.
The relay checks account and plan again while a pairing lives.
Revoking a pairing keeps its audit trail.
No path reaches the camera before the pairing page shows what pairing allows; QR stays the default pairing.
Remote Control comes with paid plans only.

acceptance_criteria: With the relay unset, claim and initiate answer 503 'Pairing is not configured'.
A code claimed by a different account is refused with 403 and an audit event with outcome failure.
Claiming a code that already has a phone returns 409; an unknown or expired code returns 404.
Disconnecting on the computer or the phone ends the pairing; the old code no longer works.
Unlinking a device closes its live relay sockets and deletes pairings that name it.
After a plan downgrade the relay ends a live pairing within its recheck interval.
A new phone cannot connect unless the person at the computer presses 'Allow this phone'.
inferred: The claim route maps every relay 403 to 'pairing_belongs_to_another_account' although the relay also returns 403 'device_revoked'; a revoked device would be told the wrong reason [inferred from claim/route.ts:134-146 and services/signaling-server/src/index.ts:877,911].
Because the relay needs SIGNALING_STANDING_URL in production, a missing value makes it serve no pairing [services/signaling-server/src/standing.ts:40-66].

[proposed] Add a 'Stop remote work' control for one device on web settings if none exists.

steps.what_happens: Person presses Pair a phone; the page posts to initiate with CSRF.
The server checks sign-in, rate limit, workspace policy, plan and kill switch, then asks the relay to create a pairing with the account id in its metadata.
The computer connects to the relay as the 'desktop' role with the pair token; QR text 'agiw:<code>' is shown.
The phone claims through the web route; the server verifies the account then asks the relay for a phone token; the relay refuses a different account.
The relay announces the peer; the computer asks the person to allow it, then derives a signed session key and marks the phone connected.
While paired the relay rechecks standing on an interval and closes the pairing if the answer is no; if unreadable it holds up to a maximum stale time.
Revoke: either side sends end_pairing; or Unlink calls the relay revoke route which closes sockets and deletes pairings naming the device.

features.summary: The signed-in chat page of the AGI Workforce web app at /chat. A person types in the composer and gets a streamed reply. A Chat | Work toggle switches to Work mode, which runs multi-step tool tasks. Work is offered only on Premium or higher; below that the toggle is hidden and the server refuses it.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a person a place in the browser to chat with the assistant. It streams replies, shows tool activity, and lets the person switch the composer between Chat and Work. Work mode sends work_mode 'agiwork' plus an optional goal and plan with the message (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:4663-4670).
purpose.why_it_exists: The web app is the main Cloud surface and is the product that the Desktop app shows inside its window (doc: AGENTS.md section 5). Work mode exists so paid users can hand off multi-step jobs that use tools, files and reviewable results (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:329-332; packages/contracts/types/src/interaction-modes.json:50-85).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in web users. A signed-out visitor may get a limited guest chat at /chat when the guest chat is open (apps/web/app/chat/layout.tsx:18-52). Work is for Premium, Max, Ultra, Team, Team Premium and Enterprise accounts (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:341,354).
problems_solved: One place to ask questions and run tool tasks without installing anything.
Keeps paid agent work behind the plan check on the server, so hiding a button in the browser is not the only guard (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:3538-3556).
Lets a person start in Work from a direct address (/agi-work) or from a project (apps/web/app/chat/page.tsx:5-19; ChatComposerNew.tsx:1217-1231).
use_cases: Ask a quick question in Chat mode and read the streamed answer.
Switch to Work and ask for a multi-step task such as gathering sources and producing a document.
Open /agi-work to land directly in Work mode.
Open a project and start a new chat in it, which lands an eligible account in Work.

where_to_find_it: surface:web: the address /chat (new chat) and /chat/<id> (an existing chat) (apps/web/app/chat/page.tsx:1-19; apps/web/app/chat/[sessionId]/page.tsx:12-14).

surface:web: the address /agi-work is rewritten to /chat for a signed-in browser session and opens in Work mode; the address bar keeps /agi-work (apps/web/proxy.ts:109-133; apps/web/app/chat/page.tsx:5-19).
surface:web: /cowork redirects permanently to /agi-work (apps/web/next.config.ts:136).

The Chat | Work toggle sits on the composer face. Its buttons are labelled 'Chat' and 'Work' (translation keys composer.modeChat and composer.modeAgiWork) (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:316-320; packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/chat.json:169,193). Hover text for Work is 'Work: multi-step tasks with tools, files, and reviewable deliverables' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:326-329).

Other apps: the area brief gives no status for desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code or Chrome for this item (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/069-web-application.md S69.01). The Desktop app shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
prerequisites: Signed in, accepted the current terms, and passed the adult eligibility check, or the page redirects (apps/web/app/chat/layout.tsx:56-58).

For Work: a plan of Premium or higher, billing policy loaded, not a free trial, the Work capability granted, and the toggle shown only when the composer has a project picker and no image or video mode is on (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1062-1066, 6171).
screens_and_controls: Composer text box and send control (ChatComposerNew.tsx).

Interaction modes are defined in a contract: Work needs streaming, tools and agentic model abilities, per-tool approval, synced across devices, and a queued draft only when offline.
Every subscription capability on every app connects to one AGI Subscription system.

steps.what_happens: Browser loads /chat; the layout checks identity, terms and adult eligibility, then renders the chat page.
The composer decides if Work is offered from plan, billing policy and capability, and shows the toggle.
On send the client builds the request with work_mode and goal and posts it to the managed chat endpoint.
The server checks the Work plan rule (403 if below Premium), then the Work kill switch, then routes the turn as agentic.
The server opens a durable work plan when a goal is given and runs the tool loop; frames stream back.
The model call goes to the chosen provider through the managed route.

features.summary: The web app changes its navigation by window width. Under 768 pixels, navigation is a drawer opened by an 'Open navigation' button. A portrait tablet gets an icon rail that expands over the content. Wide windows and landscape tablets keep a persistent sidebar. Two code paths do this: the shared shell and the chat page.

purpose.what_it_does: Picks one of three sidebar modes (drawer, rail, persistent) from the window size and orientation, and shows the sidebar in that form (apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-shell-layout.ts:24-48).
purpose.why_it_exists: Navigation must not cover the reading column on a phone or a split-view tablet (app-shell-layout.ts:38-41 comment). The product contract also says persistent desktop sidebars become modal drawers on narrow screens (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md section 5.2, line 197).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using the web app on a phone, tablet or desktop browser.
problems_solved: Sidebar crowding the text on narrow windows.
Layout flash on first paint (SERVER_LAYOUT assumes a wide window) (app-shell-layout.ts:43-48).
Losing scroll position when rotating the device (WebAppShell.tsx:200-218).
use_cases: Phone user taps the menu button to switch conversations, then the drawer closes.
Tablet user in portrait taps the icon rail to expand navigation over the chat.
Desktop user collapses the sidebar and later widens the window; the choice is kept.
iPad in split view gets the phone-style shell because of its width (app-shell-layout test name 'treats an iPad split view as the compact shell').

features.summary: Every web conversation has its own address, /chat/<id>. A new chat starts at /chat and takes its address on the first send. Back, Forward and reload return to the same conversation, and an unsent draft comes back after reload. Other tabs do not live-update, but a tab re-reads its open chat when it regains focus.

purpose.what_it_does: Ties the open conversation to the browser address so links, history and reload work, and keeps the draft in browser storage (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:2354-2375; apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/composer-draft-storage.ts).
purpose.why_it_exists: People expect to copy a link, press Back, and reload without losing their place. The brief requires each conversation to have a URL, history to work and reload to restore the conversation and draft (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/069-web-application.md S69.03 to S69.05).
purpose.who_uses_it: All signed-in web users.
problems_solved: Lost place on reload.
No way to share a link to a conversation with yourself on another device.
Lost typed text when the page reloads.
use_cases: Reload a long chat and continue.
Open a saved /chat/<id> link on another computer.
Press Back from a chat to the previous page.
Open a second tab on the same chat and see new messages when switching to it.

Artifact links use the address query ?artifact=<id> (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactsPanel.tsx:283-290).
prerequisites: Signed in. The conversation must belong to the account.

'New chat' pushes /chat (WebChatPage.tsx:4778).

Reload; the conversation and draft return (composer-draft-storage.ts; ChatComposerNew.tsx:4150-4165).
Open /chat/<id> in a new tab; the chat loads from the server.
feedback_and_outputs: If the address names a conversation that cannot be loaded, an error toast shows the message or 'Couldn't load this conversation. Check your connection and try again.' and the page goes back to /chat (WebChatPage.tsx:2366-2381).
settings: Temporary chat settings affect whether a chat is saved (WebChatPage.tsx:2459-2470); not traced further.

working: New chat stays at /chat with nothing saved until first send (WebChatPage.tsx:2354-2356).
First send creates the conversation and replaces the address with /chat/<id>; replace, not push, so Back leaves the page (WebChatPage.tsx:2679, 5792, 6711).
Opening a conversation from the sidebar pushes history (WebChatPage.tsx:4807-4813).
Loading from the address when the conversation is not already in local state, and a failure path with toast and redirect to /chat (WebChatPage.tsx:2358-2381).
The artifact panel re-reads ?artifact=<id> on popstate (ArtifactsPanel.tsx:636-639).
Draft kept in localStorage keyed by a per-tab owner id kept in sessionStorage; earlier owner ids are copied forward and, after a reload, retired (composer-draft-storage.ts:60-95, 146-200).

features.summary: On the web chat page a person can drop files onto the window, paste text, code or files into the composer, and copy a message out. A 'Drop files here' overlay shows while dragging. Large pastes become a file. 'Attach clipboard' exists only inside the desktop host. Copy shows a toast but does not catch a clipboard refusal.

purpose.what_it_does: Moves content into and out of a message: drops and pastes go to one attachment intake that applies file count and size limits; copy writes the message text to the system clipboard (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:2301-2303; apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:2273-2283).
purpose.why_it_exists: Leaders let people drag, paste and copy; the product guidance asks for drag-and-drop, paste and per-file validation (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:259).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web chat users.
problems_solved: Attaching files without a file dialog.
Huge pastes freezing the text box (text over 10,000 characters becomes a file) (packages/platform/utils/src/composerPaste.ts:12,45-55).
Pasted code losing its formatting (fenced and undoable) (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2372-2396).
use_cases: Drag a PDF onto the chat window.
Paste a screenshot into the composer.
Paste 20 pages of text and get a 'Pasted text.txt' attachment with an undo.
Copy an assistant answer as plain text.

where_to_find_it: surface:web: the chat page composer and any place the window accepts a file drop (DragDropOverlay is mounted by the composer, ChatComposerNew.tsx:4893).
surface:web: copy control on each message with accessible name 'Copy message' (MessageBubble.tsx:3750-3751).
Desktop host only: the '+' menu row 'Attach clipboard' (ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:176, shown when showDesktopActionRows is true, ChatComposerNew.tsx:6018-6021).
prerequisites: Composer must not be disabled or the trial exhausted for paste (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2373).
screens_and_controls: Full-screen overlay: 'Drop files here', 'Release to attach to your message', and 'Up to N files' when N is more than 1 (DragDropOverlay.tsx:109-115).
Composer paste handler (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2372-2399).
Copy button; label changes to 'Message copied' (MessageBubble.tsx:3751).
journey: Drag a file over the window; the overlay appears (DragDropOverlay.tsx:27-30).
Release; the files go to the attachment intake and show as chips (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2301-2303).
Or paste: the shared decision says files, a large-text file, or plain text (composerPaste.ts:131-150).
Code pasted as text is wrapped in a code fence with an undo (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2383-2393).
Click copy on a message; the text is written and a toast says 'Copied to clipboard' (MessageBubble.tsx:2273-2282).
feedback_and_outputs: Overlay, attachment chips, notices naming refused files (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-attachments.ts:447-448).
Toast 'Copied to clipboard' and a 2-second 'copied' state (MessageBubble.tsx:2279-2286).
Notices for the clipboard attach row: 'Your clipboard is empty, so there was nothing to attach.' and a truncation notice (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2321-2328).
settings: Per-plan attachment limits come from billing policy: 'Up to N files, <size> each' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:915-922; apps/web/features/chat/lib/composer-attachment-limits.ts).

working: Window-level drag listeners with a depth counter and a Files check (DragDropOverlay.tsx:20-60).
Single intake addChatAttachments for drops, pastes, mentions and clipboard (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2301-2303, 3065, 3082).
Shared paste decision used by the web composer and other composers (composerPaste.ts:131; ChatComposerNew.tsx:2376-2379).
Large paste threshold 10,000 characters turns text into a file (composerPaste.ts:12).
Copy: user messages copy as written, assistant messages are flattened from rich blocks (MessageBubble.tsx:2274-2276).
Share fallback has a try and catch (MessageBubble.tsx:2287-2305).
incomplete: Copy: handleCopy awaits navigator.clipboard.writeText with no try and catch, so a refusal (for example no permission or no secure context) rejects with no message to the person (MessageBubble.tsx:2273-2276). Compare handleShare, which has a catch (2299-2304).
disconnected_or_disabled: 'Attach clipboard' reads the clipboard through the desktop host only (readHostClipboard, apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/runtime-client.ts:365). It is hidden in a normal browser (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6018). The draft said it works on the web; that is wrong.
not_available: Drag-and-drop and paste in other apps are not covered here; the brief gives no status for them. Only the paste decision is shared with other surfaces (composerPaste.ts in packages/platform/utils).

established.statement: Dragging files onto the chat page shows a drop overlay and attaches the dropped files to the composer.
Pasting text, code or files into the composer is handled, and a message can be copied to the system clipboard.
Support multiple eligible file types, drag-and-drop, paste, mobile pickers, attachment removal, and per-file validation.
The clipboard is read only on a person's click in the desktop host, never in the background.
The paste decision is shared so one clipboard gives the same result on web, the unified composer and the extension.

acceptance_criteria: Dragging a file over the window shows the overlay with 'Drop files here'; releasing attaches it.
Dropping more files than the plan allows attaches up to the limit and names each refused file.
Pasting an image attaches it; pasting under 10,000 characters of text inserts it as text.
Pasting over 10,000 characters attaches 'Pasted text.txt' and offers an undo.
Copy on an assistant message puts plain text on the clipboard and shows 'Copied to clipboard'.
When the clipboard write is refused, the person sees an error message (currently fails: see gaps).
inferred: The same refusal handling used by share should apply to copy [inferred from MessageBubble.tsx:2299-2304].
proposed: [proposed] Wrap handleCopy in a try and catch and show 'This message could not be copied'.

features.summary: The web chat asks the browser for the microphone for dictation and for live voice calls, explains a refusal, and retries a live call when access is later granted. A camera sharing control is built but not connected on the chat page. The feedback dialog can capture one screen frame. Screen sharing into chat is not offered.

purpose.what_it_does: Dictation records audio and sends it to our server for transcription (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-input-store.ts:218-235). Live voice sets up a WebRTC call brokered by our server (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:480-548). The feedback dialog grabs one screen frame as a picture (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:52-69).
purpose.why_it_exists: Voice is a core input path, and the product contract needs permission denied, absent microphone and transcription failure to be recoverable states (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:786 W13).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web users who dictate, talk to the assistant, or report a problem with a screenshot.
problems_solved: Typing by voice.
Hands-free conversation.
Showing support what is on screen.
Telling a person why the browser blocked the microphone and what to do.
use_cases: Click the microphone, speak, and get text in the composer.
Start voice mode and talk; fix a blocked microphone and the call retries on its own.
Open feedback and press 'Capture screen'.
Camera sharing in voice mode (built, not reachable today).

where_to_find_it: surface:web: microphone button in the composer (VoiceInputButton.tsx); title 'Voice input not supported in this browser' when unsupported (VoiceInputButton.tsx:12-13).
surface:web: voice mode entry through the composer (onEnterVoiceMode, WebChatPage.tsx:7670).
surface:web: feedback dialog button 'Capture screen' (ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:335-345); the dialog opens from the sidebar or a message (WebAppShell.tsx:615; MessageBubble.tsx:3826).
Camera button 'Share your camera' / 'Stop sharing your camera' in voice mode (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:47-48, 524-535), not rendered on the chat page (see current_implementation).
prerequisites: A browser with MediaRecorder or the needed APIs; unsupported browsers see the disabled button (VoiceInputButton.tsx:44-78).
Microphone permission in the browser.
Live voice: a plan whose policy allows voice, and the adult eligibility check (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:180-186, 311-313).
screens_and_controls: Microphone button with pressed state (VoiceInputButton.tsx:73).
Voice mode surface with orb, captions, reconnect notice (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:300-330).
Feedback dialog 'Screenshot' section with 'Capture screen' and 'Upload image' (ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:316-352).
journey: Press the microphone; the browser asks for permission.
Speak; recording stops; status becomes 'transcribing'; the text fills the composer (voice-input-store.ts:344-370).
For a live call, start voice mode; the page asks for the microphone, creates a peer connection, sends an offer to /api/voice/live/sessions and applies the answer (live-voice-session.ts:480-548).
For a screenshot, open feedback, press 'Capture screen', choose a screen in the browser picker; a preview shows with a 'Remove screenshot' button.
feedback_and_outputs: Denied: 'Microphone permission denied. Please allow access in your browser settings.' (voice-input-store.ts:450-453).
Other dictation errors: no microphone, busy, interrupted, blocked by site, and a generic one (voice-input-store.ts:454-466).
Live voice denied: 'Microphone access was denied. Allow the microphone to use voice mode.' (live-voice-session.ts:62).
Reconnect: 'Reconnecting <n> of <max>' (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:318-325).
Capture: preview image; on submit, 'Your note was sent, but your screenshot could not be stored and was not attached.' if storage dropped it (ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:143-147).
settings: Chosen microphone id (voice-input-store.ts:278 microphoneId).
Voice settings dialog in voice mode (VoiceSettingsModal).

working: Dictation: records with MediaRecorder, posts to /api/voice/transcribe, shows the text (voice-input-store.ts:298, 368; TRANSCRIBE_ENDPOINT line 16).
Mapped error messages for denied, not found, busy, aborted, security (voice-input-store.ts:441-466).
Live voice session with microphone request only when started, plus retry on granted permission (live-voice-session.ts:480-486; use-voice-session.ts:899-925).
The session ends on pagehide and retries when the browser comes back online (use-voice-session.ts:927-934).

Screen frame capture in the feedback dialog with stop of tracks in finally (ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:52-69), offered only when getDisplayMedia exists (lines 94-96); a refused picker (NotAllowedError) is silent (lines 142-148).
Camera and screen sources in the shared capture module with distinct messages for denied, busy and unavailable (packages/contracts/types/src/visual-session-capture.ts:30-91).
incomplete: Captured PNG is not size-checked on the client, while an uploaded file is limited to 4 MiB (ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:42, 120-126 versus 52-69). The server limits the data URL length (apps/web/app/api/feedback/route.ts:33). A large capture may be dropped; the person is told only after submit.
disconnected_or_disabled: Camera sharing: VoiceModeSurface shows the camera button only when it is given onVisualFrame (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:155,524). WebChatPage renders VoiceModeSurface with voiceSurfaceProps, which contains no onVisualFrame (WebChatPage.tsx:6841-6853, 7665-7668, 7793-7796). No other caller passes it outside tests. So the camera button never shows in the product. The draft said it works; that is wrong.
The camera is also hidden when the desktop host is present (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:257-258).
Screen sharing as a chat or voice source: the shared module can request a screen (visual-session-capture.ts:92-95) but the only caller uses source camera (VoiceModeSurface.tsx:259-262).
not_available: Screen or tab sharing into chat or voice on web: brief S69.09 says not applicable anywhere. A screen_share capability switch exists for remote control, not for this (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:46).

established.statement: The web app asks the browser for microphone and camera access when a feature needs them, explains a refusal, and recovers once access is granted.
A user can share a screen, window or tab with the assistant (brief status: not applicable anywhere).
Voice: permission denied, absent microphone, transcription failure, mute, interruption and exit all have recoverable states; exit releases capture and playback.
Do not claim realtime audio behaviour for a completed text-to-speech path.
The microphone is requested only when a feature needs it.

acceptance_criteria: Clicking the microphone triggers the browser prompt; after allowing, speech becomes text in the composer.
Denying shows 'Microphone permission denied. Please allow access in your browser settings.'
In voice mode with the microphone denied, the live error shows; after granting in browser settings the call restarts without pressing anything.
With no microphone attached the dictation message says no microphone found.
In the feedback dialog 'Capture screen' attaches a preview and 'Remove screenshot' clears it.
Cancelling the browser's screen picker shows no error.
inferred: Camera sharing should either be wired into the chat page or removed; dead controls are not allowed (doc: AGENTS.md section 9) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Connect onVisualFrame in the chat page to a real sink, or delete the camera control and its hook until a sink exists.
[proposed] Check the captured PNG size against 4 MiB before showing it.

steps.what_happens: Person presses the microphone; the page calls getUserMedia for audio.
Audio is recorded in the browser, then posted to /api/voice/transcribe.

aliases: Cloud code execution and file creation
features.summary: Lets the assistant run code and create files in a cloud sandbox during a chat turn. A person types /code or asks clearly to run code. A Settings switch, 'Cloud code execution and file creation', turns it off, and the server enforces that choice. If the setting cannot be read, execution is refused.

purpose.what_it_does: Offers execution tools to the model for a turn and runs them in a managed sandbox or a provider's own code tool, then returns output and files to the chat (apps/web/lib/e2b/execution-tools.ts:258-269).
purpose.why_it_exists: Data analysis, calculations and file creation need real code runs. The Settings switch gives people control over that managed compute, and the server enforces it because the client declares tools in the request (apps/web/lib/server/code-execution-policy.ts:13-19).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web users who analyse data, write scripts or generate files. Not available on Local-only or Local + BYOK plans (sandbox count is 0 there; packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:590, 607).
problems_solved: Getting exact answers from computation.
Producing files such as charts or documents.
Letting a person refuse managed compute for their account.
use_cases: Type '/code' then ask to analyse a CSV.
Ask in words 'run this Python and show the chart'.
Turn execution off in Settings for privacy.
Re-run a code block from a message through the code-runs route.

where_to_find_it: surface:web: the composer slash command '/code' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3247-3265).

surface:web: Settings, Capabilities, row 'Cloud code execution and file creation' under the heading 'Code execution and file creation' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/CapabilitiesSection.tsx:108-121).
prerequisites: Signed in; the deployment has sandbox execution on (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts:11-26); the chosen model can run code or the route can use the sandbox; plan with sandboxes (free has 2 slots, local-only and BYOK have 0; billing-catalog.ts:590, 607, 620-628).
screens_and_controls: Slash menu entry /code.
Settings switch (aria-label 'Cloud code execution and file creation').
'Artifacts' switch is forced on and disabled with the note 'Required by code execution' while execution is on (CapabilitiesSection.tsx:52, 142-151).
journey: Type /code followed by a request, or ask in words. The server may turn execution on for that turn when the words clearly ask for it (request-processor.ts:998-1013).
Send. The server checks the platform switch, then offers execution tools (request-processor.ts:6410-6419).
The model calls an execution tool; the tool loop checks the account setting first and runs the code (tool-loop.ts:2814-2840).
Results and files stream back and show in the chat; activity shows as 'executing' (useChatStream.ts:3498-3500).
feedback_and_outputs: If /code is typed on a model that cannot run code: '/code needs a model that can run code on this deployment. Switch models, then try again.' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3256-3261).
With no text after /code on a free-model hand-over: 'Type what you want after /code, then send. The command applies to that one message.' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3646-3652).
When off, the model is told execution is off and where to turn it on (tool-loop.ts:2829-2833).
The code-runs route returns a forbidden error 'Running code is turned off for this account. Turn it on in Settings, Capabilities.' (code-runs/route.ts:106-110).
settings: capabilities.cloudCodeExecution in the account's user settings; default true (apps/web/features/settings/hooks/use-capabilities-preferences.ts:67; code-execution-policy.ts:7-8, 33-36).
Settings copy says the sandbox can reach only GitHub, npm and PyPI (CapabilitiesSection.tsx:112).

working: Setting stored in user_settings under capabilities.cloudCodeExecution; absent means enabled; false means off (code-execution-policy.ts:25-37).
A failed read refuses execution (code-execution-policy.ts:43-48).
Server enforcement in the tool loop with a user-facing explanation to the model (tool-loop.ts:2814-2840) and in the code-runs route with a forbidden error (code-runs/route.ts:106-110).
Handshake feeds the setting and the deployment flag into canUseCloudExecution (apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts:282-300; capability-handshake-service.ts:95-98).
Platform kill switch: if closed, the turn is marked execution-unavailable (request-processor.ts:5226-5228, 6416-6419).
Execution tools offered only for a streaming turn when the sandbox is on and the provider routes to it; otherwise a provider's own code tool if the model supports it (execution-tools.ts:258-270).
Implicit turn-on from the words of the prompt, unless the surface is excluded (request-processor.ts:1003-1013).
Sandbox network allowlist in code: github hosts, npm and PyPI hosts (apps/web/lib/e2b/runtime.ts:104-114). This matches the Settings text.
Per-plan sandbox slots and lifetime (billing-catalog.ts:531-532, 590, 607, 620-628).
incomplete: The allowlist enforcement at the sandbox network level was not verified; only the host list in code was read.
disconnected_or_disabled: Everything is off unless AGI_E2B_EXECUTION is 1 or a sandbox key is set (gate.ts:11-26). The cutover flag decides the handshake (me/route.ts:282). Whether production has it on is unknown.
Managed compute private beta gate is separate (gate.ts:36-38; managed-compute-gate.ts).
not_available: Local-only and Local + BYOK tiers: no managed sandbox (runtime.ts:121-124; billing-catalog.ts:590, 607).
Desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: the brief gives web status only.

established.statement: From the browser a user turns on cloud code execution (/code or a skill) and the server runs code in a provider sandbox or E2B, with a Settings switch to refuse it.
An absent setting means enabled; an unreadable setting means refused.
Enforcement is on the server, because tools are declared by the client.
Code execution forces Artifacts on.
Execution tools and sandbox availability depend on a provider route or an AGI harness and must not be described as intrinsic model abilities.
Local and BYOK stay outside managed sandbox provisioning.

acceptance_criteria: With the switch on and execution available, '/code' plus a request runs code and shows output.
With the switch off, the same request returns an answer saying execution is off and pointing to Settings, Capabilities.
With the switch off, the code-runs route returns forbidden.
Turning execution on makes the Artifacts switch read 'Required by code execution' and disabled.
If the settings read fails, execution is refused with a 'temporarily unavailable' explanation.
On a model without code ability the slash command says to switch models.
inferred: The switch should also hide or grey the /code entry when off so the person is told before sending [inferred; not found in ChatComposerNew].
proposed: [proposed] Show a notice at /code time when the account switch is off, so the person does not learn only from the model's reply.
[proposed] Add a test that reads the sandbox host list and the Settings copy together so they cannot drift.

steps.what_happens: Person types /code or asks; the composer sets codeExecution true for that send.
The server may also set code_execution from the prompt text when the person did not choose.
The server reads the platform switch; if closed the turn proceeds with execution marked unavailable and the model is told.
Execution tools are added when the sandbox is on and the turn streams, or a provider tool when the model has one.
When the model calls a tool, the loop reads the account setting and refuses if off or unreadable.
The code runs in a sandbox that can reach only the listed hosts, with a per-plan slot count and lifetime.

data.retained_or_deleted: Sandbox lifetime is per plan (billing-catalog.ts:531-532); file retention unknown

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The sandbox is provider-neutral for models that route to it; otherwise the model's own provider code tool is used when the model supports it (execution-tools.ts:258-270; hosted-code-execution.ts:9-13 names two providers with hosted tools). The model catalog must have at least one model with codeExecution ability for the capability to be granted (capability-handshake-service.ts:95-98).

access_and_usage.account: Signed in. Account setting capabilities.cloudCodeExecution (default on).
access_and_usage.permissions: Platform kill switch canUseCloudExecution; workspace controls can disable it (request-processor.ts:2308-2318 reads workspace-disabled capabilities).
access_and_usage.subscription: Sandbox slots by plan: Local-only and Local + BYOK 0; Free 2; higher plans more up to a five-per-user ceiling (billing-catalog.ts:531-532, 590, 607, 620-681; runtime.ts:121-128). Free compute uses a daily platform allowance; paid plans use credit reservations (runtime.ts:121-124).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Per-plan sandbox count and lifetime; conversation timeout 10 minutes and command timeout 60 seconds in the runtime constants (runtime.ts:100-101); code-runs route max duration 300 seconds (code-runs/route.ts:42).
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_E2B_EXECUTION and E2B_API_KEY control availability (gate.ts:11-26); AGI_MANAGED_COMPUTE_PRIVATE_BETA is a separate gate (managed-compute-gate.ts:40). Handshake uses feature_flags.code_execution (me/route.ts:282).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Needs a model with tool ability and a streaming turn for the sandbox; or a model with its provider's own code tool (execution-tools.ts:258-270). The slash command refuses models without it (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3256-3261).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Sandbox routes only for providers that providerRoutesToE2B accepts (function name seen at execution-tools.ts:259; list not read).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Not available: Local and BYOK stay outside managed sandbox provisioning (runtime.ts:121-124) and their plans have 0 sandboxes (billing-catalog.ts:590, 607).

aliases: Send a task to Desktop from a browser
features.summary: Two ideas. Cloud browser, where the assistant drives a browser hosted by us, has no code on the web app. Browser control of a paired Desktop host is partly built: the page 'Your computer' (/code/computer) pairs a browser tab with Desktop, sends tasks, cancels, resends and shows status and result text. No screen view or step approval was found.

purpose.what_it_does: Cloud browser: would let the assistant navigate, click and read pages in a browser we host. Not built. Browser control: a signed-in web tab pairs with the user's own Desktop host through a one-time link and sends it tasks, then follows their status (apps/web/features/remote-dispatch/components/RemoteComputerPage.tsx:34-40; apps/web/features/remote-dispatch/lib/remote-dispatch-client.ts:225-253).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants a user to work with no local desktop or extension (S69.11) and to steer their own computer from any browser (S69.12) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/069-web-application.md). The product guide says execution environments must be told apart: built-in browser, existing browser session, cloud browser, native desktop automation (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:390).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in web users on a paid plan who also run Desktop (Electron) on a computer linked to the same account [inferred from RemoteComputerPage.tsx:97 and packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:352].
problems_solved: Start work on your own computer while away from it.
See whether a sent task was accepted, is running, finished or failed.
Stop or resend a task that was not confirmed.
use_cases: From a laptop browser, paste a pairing link and ask Desktop to run a task in an allowed folder.
Cancel a running task from the browser.
Resend a task Desktop never confirmed.

where_to_find_it: Web: Code rail item 'Your computer' goes to /code/computer; hidden when the page runs inside the Desktop shell (apps/web/features/code/components/CodeRail.tsx:88-93,120-123).
Web: the link component RemoteComputerLink exists, but no importer was found outside its own index file (apps/web/features/remote-dispatch/index.ts:1).

Desktop (hosted web app in Electron): Settings, Capabilities, 'Remote Control' section makes the pairing code and a copy-link action; the section renders nothing in a plain browser (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/RemoteControlSection.tsx:166; apps/web/features/settings/sections/CapabilitiesSection.tsx:215).
Cloud browser: nowhere on any app.
prerequisites: Signed in to the web app.
A paid plan: basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium or enterprise (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:57-76 with packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:332-340,352).

The screen share switch open and workspace policy allowing it (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:29-52).

established.statement: The assistant can drive a cloud browser for a web user without a local desktop or extension.
From a normal browser tab a user can control a paired desktop host: send work, approve steps, see its screen.
Remote Control is governed by the screen share switch and a paid plan; a pairing must not outlive a reason that would have refused it.
Execution environments (built-in browser, existing session, cloud browser, desktop automation) are distinguished.
Surface matrix lists Remote control as experimental and present on web (via the Desktop settings section), desktop, mobile and VS Code; absent on CLI and Chrome.

acceptance_criteria: A paid user pastes a valid link on /code/computer and sees 'Connected to <name>'.
A task sent from the browser appears on Desktop and its status changes appear on the card.
Cancel on an open task reaches Desktop; failure shows the cancel error.
A used or expired link shows the 'expired or already used' message.
A free-plan account or a closed screen share switch is refused with a readable message.
No cloud browser control appears anywhere on web until built.
inferred: [inferred] The brief status 'missing' for S69.12 is out of date, because the browser page exists; 'partial' fits better because screen view and approval are absent.
[inferred] Cloud browser would run on our servers or a vendor, so it would need an explicit execution boundary and plan gate; none exist.
proposed: [proposed] Add step approval and a screen preview to the browser page, or change the brief text to the narrower task-dispatch promise.
[proposed] Decide whether cloud browser is in scope; if so write a spec under docs/specs first.

steps.what_happens: Desktop creates a pairing and shows a code and secret; user copies a link containing both in the URL fragment.
Browser reads the fragment and removes it from the address bar.
Browser posts the code to /api/pair/claim with CSRF; the server checks session, rate limit, plan, policy, switch, then calls the relay with an internal secret.
Server returns a token and websocket address; the browser opens the signaling socket.
steps.evidence: claim/route.ts:166-190; remote-dispatch-client.ts:179-188 (relay code is in services/signaling-server; where it is hosted is not established)

steps.what_happens: Browser signs the task with a key derived from the code, salt and secret and sends it as a control signal; Desktop answers with a receipt and status updates.
Desktop runs the task on the computer, with the folders and apps allowed there.
steps.evidence: RemoteComputerPage.tsx:34-35 (page text); execution code in apps/desktop not read

features.summary: Web users can turn on browser push so a system notification arrives when a cloud agent run finishes, fails or needs approval, even with the tab closed. A switch in Settings, Notifications, 'Agent run updates', registers this browser. The server sends encrypted push through the browser's push service. Alerts show status, not run output.

purpose.what_it_does: Registers a browser with a push service and our server, then sends an encrypted notice when a cloud agent run changes state (apps/web/lib/services/agent-notification-service.ts:140-175; apps/web/lib/services/web-push-service.ts:346-412).
purpose.why_it_exists: A run can finish while the user is away. Without push the web user hears nothing (apps/web/db/neon/0151_web_push_subscriptions.sql:1-8). The brief asks for a system notification with the tab closed (S69.13).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web users in a browser that supports push, signed in, with cloud agent runs.
problems_solved: Missing a finished or blocked run.
Not knowing a run needs approval.
A shared browser leaking one account's alerts to the next.
use_cases: Start a long cloud run, close the tab, get 'Agent run finished'.
Get 'Approval needed' for a tool.
Turn alerts off on a shared computer.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings, Notifications, row 'Agent run updates' with a switch (apps/web/features/settings/sections/NotificationsSection.tsx:80,439-470).

Web: a one-time card 'Know when a run finishes' with 'Turn on' and 'Not now', bottom right (apps/web/features/notifications/components/WebPushOptIn.tsx:88-120; mounted at apps/web/app/AppRuntimeMounts.tsx:26).
A status note 'Browser delivery: <Allowed | Not allowed yet | Blocked | Unavailable | System settings>' sits above the rows (apps/web/features/notifications/components/BrowserNotificationStatus.tsx).
Desktop shell: the row says the desktop app uses system notifications (apps/web/features/notifications/components/WebPushToggle.tsx).
prerequisites: Signed in.
Browser with service worker, Push API and Notification (apps/web/features/notifications/lib/web-push-client.ts:34-41).
Not in the Desktop shell.
Server has a VAPID key pair configured, else nothing is offered (web-push-client.ts:74-88).
screens_and_controls: Switch 'Agent run updates'; helper text 'Completions, failures and approval requests. This browser only.' and details 'Enable separately in each browser. Alerts show run status, not run output.' (NotificationsSection.tsx:81,448-451).
Offer card with 'Turn on', 'Not now' and a Dismiss button (WebPushOptIn.tsx).
Browser permission prompt.
journey: Sign in; the offer card appears if permission is undecided, the offer was not dismissed and the server has a key (WebPushOptIn.tsx:46-67).
Press 'Turn on' (or the Settings switch). The browser asks permission.
On allow, the worker registers and the browser subscription is sent to the server.
A cloud agent run ends or needs input; a notification appears.
Click it: an open tab on the same path is focused, else a window opens (apps/web/public/sw.js:81-103).
Turn the switch off to delete the registration and drop the browser subscription.
feedback_and_outputs: Switch state and helper text: 'Registered in this browser.', 'Notifications are blocked for this site in your browser settings.', 'This browser could not be turned off. Try again.', 'Browser push is unavailable here.' (WebPushToggle.tsx).
Notification titles: 'Approval needed', 'Your agent has a question', 'Agent run finished', 'Agent run failed' (agent-notification-service.ts:98-121).
settings: Quiet hours (checked before sending, apps/web/lib/services/push-notification-service.ts:281-291).
Separate 'Reply ready' browser popup preference, a different mechanism (NotificationsSection.tsx:50).

working: Subscribe, store, delete endpoints with CSRF, rate limit, https and public-host checks (apps/web/app/api/web-push/route.ts:62-145).
Client enable/disable, account hand-over on a shared browser, re-sync of held subscriptions (web-push-client.ts:132-217).
Own Web Push sender: encryption, VAPID signing, batches of 10, 10 s timeout, prune of dead endpoints (web-push-service.ts:178-238,252-263,346-412).
Service worker shows the notice, handles click and endpoint rotation (public/sw.js:63-133).
Cloud agent run events call the sender (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:170; agent-notification-service.ts:140).
incomplete: Click on a run notice opens /tasks, not the run: sw.js says /tasks does not read the run query parameter yet (public/sw.js:31-44).
Agent-run notices only carry runId; conversation and code-session ids are used by other senders (sw.js:45-62; agent-notification-service.ts:157-165).
Migration 0151 header still reads 'NOT YET APPLIED - draft only'; applied state in each environment is not established (apps/web/db/neon/0151_web_push_subscriptions.sql:3).
disconnected_or_disabled: The standalone WebPushToggle component has no importer outside features/notifications; only the hook is used by Settings.

Chat reply and schedule notices pass web: false, so they do not push to browsers (apps/web/lib/services/chat-reply-notification-service.ts:42; apps/web/lib/services/schedule-notification-service.ts:184).
Without the three VAPID env vars the sender returns zero sends and GET returns a null key (web-push-service.ts:104-114,350-351).
not_available: Desktop shell: push disabled, OS notifications used (web-push-client.ts:26-40).
Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome extension: not this feature (mobile has its own push path).

established.statement: A user turns on browser notifications in Settings and gets a system notification when an agent run or long task finishes, even with the tab closed.
A registration moves between accounts only by a fresh endpoint; the server refuses to move it.
Notices carry no task output because they render on a locked screen.
Permission is requested only on a user click.
Quiet hours hold a push.

acceptance_criteria: Switch on: browser prompt appears; on allow a row exists in web_push_subscriptions for this user.
Switch off: row deleted and browser subscription removed, even if the server call fails.
With no VAPID key the offer card and switch offer nothing and GET /api/web-push returns publicKey null.
A second account on the same browser can turn notifications on (gets a fresh endpoint).
A finished cloud run sends a notice with no run output.
Click on a notice focuses or opens a tab.
In quiet hours no notice is sent.
inferred: [inferred] 'Opens the run' is not met: the click lands on /tasks.
[inferred] Tab-closed delivery depends on the browser's push service and OS, not on our code.
proposed: [proposed] Make /tasks read the run parameter, or send the run's conversation id.
[proposed] Fix the stale 'not yet applied' header or record the applied state.

features.summary: The web app ships an install manifest (standalone, icons, start at '/'), signed-in visitors land in chat, and a notice shows when the connection drops. The composer refuses to send offline and keeps the draft. The service worker caches nothing, so no offline reading. An /offline page exists but nothing leads to it. The brief marks both items n/a.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the site be installed from the browser and tells the user when they are offline, without losing the draft (apps/web/app/manifest.ts:4-30; apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:717,3588-3590).
purpose.why_it_exists: An installed app should open the working product, and a dropped connection should be explained, not silent (S69.14, S69.15 should-lines).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web users on desktop and phone browsers.
problems_solved: Opening the product from the home screen or dock.
Sending a message with no network and losing the text.
Not knowing why nothing happens.
use_cases: Install from the browser menu and open straight into chat.
Lose Wi-Fi mid-draft; read the notice; reconnect and send.
Open /offline to see a plain explanation.

where_to_find_it: Install: the browser's own install or add-to-home-screen action. No in-app install button or prompt handler found (search for beforeinstallprompt, no hits in apps/web).
Offline notice: banner under the header, aria-label 'Network status indicator' (apps/web/shared/components/OfflineIndicator.tsx:128-140).
Composer notice: 'You are offline. Your draft is saved here and can be sent after you reconnect.' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:717).
Page /offline titled 'No connection' (apps/web/app/offline/page.tsx:12-18).
prerequisites: A browser that supports install for the manifest.
Signed in to land in chat from '/' (apps/web/proxy.ts:124-129,208).
screens_and_controls: Offline banner with Retry when sync errors and an 'N pending' count (OfflineIndicator.tsx:148-175).
/offline page: heading "You're offline.", text, 'Retry' button reloading the page (apps/web/app/offline/OfflineStatus.tsx).
Composer send blocked with a reason while offline (ChatComposerNew.tsx:4806).
journey: Install from the browser menu; launch opens '/' standalone.
Signed in: '/' is rewritten to the chat root; signed out sees the marketing page.
Connection drops: banner appears; composer shows the offline reason.
Type a draft; pressing send shows the notice and sends nothing.
Connection returns: press send.
feedback_and_outputs: Banner text from the sync manager status (apps/web/lib/offline/offlineSync.ts:46-52).
Composer notice text above.
settings: none found in the code

working: Manifest with name, short name, description, standalone, colours, three icons, start_url '/' (apps/web/app/manifest.ts:4-30).
Signed-in '/' rewrites to chat (apps/web/proxy.ts:124-129,208).
Composer tracks online state, refuses send, keeps draft (ChatComposerNew.tsx:842,3588-3590,4806).
OfflineIndicator mounted for the whole app (apps/web/app/AppRuntimeMounts.tsx:25).
incomplete: Previously loaded content is not readable offline: the only worker caches nothing and intercepts no fetches (apps/web/public/sw.js:1-8).

Offline queue module exists (localStorage key agi_offline_queue) but no producer was found: queueMessage and queueToolExecution have no importer outside lib/offline and tests (search of apps/web). The earlier idea that the Code feature enqueues into it is wrong: use-local-session uses its own queue from client-runtime/queue (apps/web/features/code/hooks/use-local-session.ts:4,221).
disconnected_or_disabled: /offline page exists and is listed in an e2e contrast spec (apps/web/e2e/qa-14-public-route-contrast.spec.ts:106) but no link, redirect or worker fallback leads to it.
not_available: Offline read-only content; offline navigation fallback; in-app install prompt; mobile, desktop, CLI, extensions (not this feature).

established.statement: The site can be installed as a standalone web app whose launch opens the working product.
When the connection drops the app says so, previously loaded content stays readable, with an offline page for navigations.
The only worker deliberately caches nothing, because a cache would shadow streaming responses.

acceptance_criteria: Browser offers install and the installed app opens chat for a signed-in user.
Going offline shows a status banner.
Send offline shows the offline reason and keeps the text.
After reconnecting, the same draft sends.
/offline renders without sign-in.
Before claiming S69.15, loaded chats must be readable offline (currently fails).
inferred: [inferred] The brief marks both items n/a but code ships a manifest and notice; status needs updating to partial.
[inferred] Next serves app/manifest.ts as the manifest by file convention.
proposed: [proposed] Either wire /offline into a worker fallback or remove it.
[proposed] Remove the unused offline queue or connect chat to it.

purpose.what_it_does: Serves a read-only copy of a shared conversation or a published artifact from a token link, with a link-preview title, expiry text and a report link (apps/web/app/share/[token]/page.tsx:82-122; apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/page.tsx:46-97).
purpose.why_it_exists: Users share work with people who have no account (S69.20).
purpose.who_uses_it: Recipients of a link, signed in or not; owners who share.

where_to_find_it: Web: /share/<token> and /shared-artifact/<token>; links are created in the chat share dialog (apps/web/features/chat/components/share/ShareConversationDialog.tsx) through POST /api/share.

working: Public conversation read, then signed-in workspace read with admission check; expired rows give not-found (apps/web/app/share/[token]/page.tsx:27-48,78-80,100-122).

features.summary: The AGI Workforce desktop app (Electron) is an installed program that shows the hosted web app in a native window. It allows one running copy, hides instead of quitting on Mac, restores the window from the Dock, tray or a second launch, and reloads or explains a crashed page.

purpose.what_it_does: Runs the desktop app as one installed program. It owns the main window, the single running copy, what happens when the window is closed, the Dock or tray restore, quit protection and recovery when the page crashes, stops answering or cannot load. (main.ts:2570, main.ts:2722, main.ts:2770, main.ts:895)
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief says the product must run as an installed desktop app with its own lifecycle, single instance, sign-in and crash recovery (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/070-desktop-application.md S70.01, S70.04). The product spec calls the desktop a managed-cloud Electron shell (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:80).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who installs the desktop app on Mac, Windows or Linux. Engineers and testers use it to reason about launch, quit and crash behaviour.
problems_solved: A second launch would start a second copy that fights the first for sign-in, shortcuts and the tray; the lock prevents it (main.ts:2570).
A crashed or frozen page used to leave a blank window; it now reloads once and explains if it fails again (main.ts:887-893 comment, rendererRecovery.ts:63).
Closing the window on Mac would lose the page state; it is hidden so the Dock brings back the same page (windowLifecycle.ts:1-6).
Quitting during running agent work could lose it; a quit prompt asks first (main.ts:2729, quitGuard.ts).
use_cases: Open the app from Applications; it shows the last conversation route if it was an in-app route (main.ts:1089-1140, windowState.ts:95).
Click a agiworkforce-cloud link while the app runs; the first copy gets the link and comes forward (main.ts:2579).
Close the window on Mac, click the Dock icon, and the same page returns (main.ts:2722).
The page crashes; the app reloads the same page, and if it crashes again within 30 seconds shows a stopped screen with a Reload button (rendererRecovery.ts:42, shellScreens.ts:76).

where_to_find_it: Desktop only (surface:desktop). Launched from Applications, the Dock, the Start menu or the OS launcher; no in-app menu entry is needed.
Dock icon on Mac: click restores the window (main.ts:2722). Tray icon on Windows/Linux: click opens the main window (tray.ts:216).
App menu on Mac: standard Hide, Hide Others, Quit items (appMenu.ts:133-154). Windows/Linux: File > Quit (appMenu.ts:227).
Web, Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not applicable; the brief marks them n/a.
prerequisites: An installed desktop build. The window loads the hosted app from the cloud origin, so a network connection is needed to show the product (main.ts:1065 windowUrlFor uses CLOUD_APP_ORIGIN).
Sign-in happens through the user's browser and the shell draws its own sign-in screen; signed-out windows are redirected to it (main.ts:1286-1290 comment, windowPolicy.ts:98-110).
screens_and_controls: Main window with a native title bar chrome (windowChrome.ts via titleBarChrome, main.ts:1100).
Loading overlay for the first load (loadingOverlay.ts, desktopLifecycle.test.ts 'keeps loading visible through a blank paint').

Shell screens: sign-in, offline, service unavailable and crash screens (shellScreens.ts:37, :66, :76). The crash screen heading is 'This window stopped responding' with a 'Reload' action (shellScreens.ts:76-84).
Quit prompt: a warning dialog listing running coding agent turns and local commands, with a confirm and a cancel button (quitGuard.ts:1-40, main.ts:2729-2755).
Offer to move the app to the Applications folder on Mac (main.ts:1356-1371, applicationsFolder.ts).
journey: Launch the app. If another copy runs, this process quits and the first copy shows its window (main.ts:2570-2583).
The main window opens at the remembered size and place, on the last in-app route if it belongs to the current account (main.ts:1089-1140, windowState.ts:246).
If signed out, a shell sign-in screen is shown instead of the product (windowPolicy.ts:103).
Use the app. On Mac, the close button hides the window; the Dock icon shows it again (main.ts:1150-1159, :2722).
On Windows/Linux, closing the last window quits the app unless a tray icon exists; the tray is on by default, so the app then keeps running (main.ts:2770-2774, garnishCore.ts:566).
Quit with Cmd+Q, the app menu or the tray. If agent turns or local commands are running, a prompt asks to confirm (main.ts:2729-2755).
feedback_and_outputs: Offline screen when the page cannot load (offlineScreen, main.ts:1314).
Service unavailable screen on an HTTP 5xx from the product page (main.ts:1296).
Crash screen on a second fault within 30 seconds (main.ts:906-911).
Dock bounce on notifications is a separate feature (main.ts:1721).
settings: Launch at login (Settings, and File/app menu 'Launch at Login') starts the app at sign-in (appMenu.ts:140-145, launchAtLogin.ts).
Menu bar switch decides whether the tray exists, which decides whether Windows/Linux keeps running with no window (main.ts:1858, :2770).
Window size and place are remembered per display arrangement (windowState.ts, main.ts:1010).

working: Single instance lock: a second launch quits; the first gets the deep link and shows the main window (main.ts:2570-2583).
Mac close hides the main window, including leaving full screen first; quitting really closes it (windowLifecycle.ts:13-32, main.ts:1150-1159).
Dock activate shows or recreates the main window (main.ts:2722, :1373-1378).
Windows/Linux: app quits on last window close only when no tray exists (main.ts:2770-2774).

Renderer recovery: first fault reloads on the same page when it is ours; a second within 30 seconds shows the crash screen; an unresponsive page is only acted on after 10 seconds (rendererRecovery.ts:23, :42, :63; main.ts:895-940).
Faults are counted in desktop telemetry as domain 'crash' (main.ts:903).
Offline and 5xx recovery screens exist (main.ts:1296, :1314).
Quit guard asks before quitting with live agent turns, local commands or an active phone remote session (quitGuard.ts:1-40, main.ts:2729).
Test files cover the lifecycle pieces (desktopLifecycle.test.ts, windowLifecycle.test.ts, rendererRecovery.test.ts).
incomplete: The draft says 'one window'. The code supports many shell windows (File/Window > New Window), so 'one running copy, many windows' is the true model (main.ts:1457-1459).
A clean renderer exit is ignored (rendererRecovery.ts:69); no screen is shown, which is intended.
disconnected_or_disabled: On a non-packaged build the Dock icon is set from an asset (main.ts:2591-2594); this is a development convenience only.
not_available: No crash screen appears on the first fault; the window silently reloads (rendererRecovery.ts:75). The brief wording 'shows a recovery screen' fits only the second fault.
Web, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no such shell (brief: n/a).

established.statement: The product runs as an installed desktop app window with its own lifecycle, single instance, sign-in and crash recovery.
Clicking the Dock/taskbar icon restores the app; closing the last window keeps it running on macOS and quits elsewhere.
A second launch passes its link to the first copy and brings its window forward.
If the page crashes or stops responding for a long time, the app shows a recovery screen instead of a blank window.
The desktop is a managed-cloud Electron shell with approved local files and tools.
The public Desktop shows the hosted web app; apps/desktop/src does not reach the Electron window.

acceptance_criteria: Start the app twice: only one process remains and its window comes forward.
On Mac, close the window then click the Dock icon: the same page returns without a reload.
On Windows or Linux with the menu bar switch off and nothing running, closing the last window quits the app; with the tray on, the app keeps running and the tray click opens a window.
Kill the page process once: the window reloads to the same conversation; kill it again within 30 seconds: the screen titled 'This window stopped responding' with a Reload button appears.
Quit while a coding agent turn runs: a warning prompt appears and Cancel keeps the app open.
Disconnect the network and launch: an offline screen appears, not a blank window.
inferred: Because the shell loads the hosted app, even Local mode work needs the page to load; offline use of the UI is limited to the recovery screens [inferred from main.ts:1065 and main.ts:1314].
Closing a secondary window on Mac really closes it, since only the primary window has the hide-on-close handler [inferred from main.ts:1150-1159].
proposed: [proposed] Show a one-line notice when the first reload happens, so a user who loses a draft understands why.
[proposed] Record the Windows/Linux close-with-tray behaviour in the first-run help, since the tray defaults on.

steps.what_happens: The process asks the OS for the single instance lock; if refused it quits.
When ready, it registers IPC handlers, loads the last account fingerprint and creates the main window with the remembered frame.
The window loads the product page from the cloud origin through a persistent session partition.
A second launch sends 'second-instance' to the first copy, which delivers the link and shows the window.
On window close on Mac the window is hidden; on activate it is shown again.
A render fault triggers a reload or the crash screen and a telemetry count.
On quit, live work is checked; confirmation lets quit proceed and will-quit stops runtimes.

features.summary: The desktop app installs a native menu bar (File, Edit, View, History, Window, Help, plus an app menu on Mac), a Dock menu on Mac, and a tray or menu bar icon with quick actions and agent activity. The icon follows a Menu bar switch but stays while an agent runs or computer use is granted.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives native menus whose items send real actions to the main process or to the page, and a tray icon listing open, new chat, running agents, shortcuts, update check and quit. (appMenu.ts:579-593, tray.ts:166-207)
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires a native menu bar with real actions and a tray that can be turned off (S70.02, S70.03). The tray is also one of two ways to stop an agent from outside its window (main.ts:1850-1857 comment).
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop users who prefer menus, keyboard accelerators and quick access while the window is hidden.
problems_solved: Without a menu Electron shows a default menu with developer tools (appMenu.ts:12-19).
A hidden app needs a way back; the tray and Dock menu provide it.
An agent that controls the screen must always be stoppable from outside the window; the tray stays then (main.ts:1858-1864).
use_cases: Choose File > New Chat to open a chat.
Click the tray icon on Windows to open the window.
See a running agent in the tray list and click it to open that session (tray.ts:126-139).
Choose Help > Troubleshooting > Copy Diagnostics when contacting support (appMenu.ts:564-571).

where_to_find_it: Desktop only. Mac: menu bar at the top of the screen, app menu named after the app, Dock right-click menu with 'New Chat', 'New Window', 'Quick Ask' (appMenu.ts:617-623). Windows/Linux: window menu bar and the system tray.
Settings switch labelled 'Menu bar' with hint 'Show Desktop in the menu bar.' (DesktopSettingsSection.tsx:51-52, :355-361).
prerequisites: Desktop app running. The menu bar switch defaults to on (garnishCore.ts:566).
screens_and_controls: File: New Chat, New Temporary Chat, New Project, Open Folder, Close, Close All, Quick Ask, Screenshot to Chat, Stop Computer Use, Take Over Screen Control, Hand Back Screen Control; on Windows/Linux also Settings, Launch at Login, Quit (appMenu.ts:159-232).
Edit: Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All, Find submenu, Focus Follow-up (appMenu.ts:261-281).
View: Toggle Sidebar, Search, Show/Hide Terminal, Show/Hide Side Chat, tab items, Copy URL, Show Changes, Show Files, zoom items, full screen, Reload (appMenu.ts:283-415).
History: Back, Forward, Previous Chat, Next Chat (appMenu.ts:417-436).
Window: see F070-04.

Help: Help, What's New, Support, Keyboard Shortcuts, Send Feedback, Start Performance Trace, Troubleshooting (Open Logs, Copy Diagnostics, Clear Cache and Restart...), Open-Source Licenses, Check for Updates on Windows/Linux (appMenu.ts:545-577).

Tray: Open <app name>, New Chat, 'Waiting for Approval' and 'Running' session lists, 'Stop All Agents...', 'Hand Back Screen Control', 'Stop Computer Use and Revoke Access...', Quick Ask, Screenshot to Chat, Window to Chat, Dictation (each with its chord), Shortcuts submenu, 'Check for Updates...', Quit (tray.ts:141-207).
journey: Open a menu and pick an item.

established.statement: The app installs a native menu bar (File, Edit, View, History, Window, Help) whose items perform real actions.

Items that are not ready are disabled, not silent.
The tray is shown when the preference is on, or an agent runs, or computer use is granted; otherwise removed.
The tray hide preference is honoured only while there is nothing to stop.

acceptance_criteria: Every top-level menu named in the brief exists and each item runs an action or is disabled.

Menu text uses 'Settings...' on Mac and 'Settings' elsewhere (appMenu.ts:119).
proposed: [proposed] Show a hint under the Menu bar switch when it is held on by a running agent or a computer-use grant.
[proposed] Add a test that each menu item either has a handler or enabled:false.

features.summary: Six system-wide keys (Quick Ask, New Chat Window, Screenshot to Chat, Window to Chat, Dictation, Stop Agents) work while another app is in front. Quick Ask opens a small floating panel that shows the compact chat page. Conflicts are reported; Stop Agents can never be turned off.

purpose.what_it_does: Registers OS-level shortcuts, reports taken, duplicate and malformed keys, lets the user choose presets or off, and opens a 480 by 620 pixel always-on-top panel on the Quick Ask key. (shortcuts.ts:92-116, quickAsk.ts:6-7, :52-80)
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants system-wide shortcuts that are configurable and report conflicts, and a small composer over any app (S70.05, S70.06). Stop Agents is the key that halts a screen-controlling agent from any app (garnishCore.ts:95-103).
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop users who want to ask or capture without switching windows.
problems_solved: Starting a chat needs no window switch.
A key already held by another app is not silently broken; the user sees the reason (shortcuts.ts:45-63).
A web settings page cannot register an arbitrary system key; only offered presets are accepted (garnishCore.ts:192-199).
use_cases: Press the Quick Ask key in a browser, type a question and press Enter.
Press the screenshot key to attach the screen (see F070-05).
Change the Quick Ask key in Settings to another preset.
Press Stop Agents to stop running turns.

where_to_find_it: Desktop only. Settings page rows 'Quick Ask shortcut', 'New chat shortcut', 'Screenshot to chat shortcut', 'Window to chat shortcut', 'Voice shortcut', 'Stop agents shortcut' (DesktopSettingsSection.tsx:92-115).
Tray submenu 'Shortcuts' with radio choices (tray.ts:198-201). File > Quick Ask and the Dock menu 'Quick Ask' (appMenu.ts:182-187, :621).
prerequisites: Desktop app running (the main process registers the keys even with no window; unregistered at will-quit, main.ts:2763).
Page must be reachable for the panel to show content (quickAsk.ts:124).
screens_and_controls: Default chords are the first preset of each list: Quick Ask Alt+Shift+Space, New Chat Alt+Shift+N, Screenshot CommandOrControl+Shift+2, Window shot CommandOrControl+Shift+1, Voice Alt+Shift+V, Stop CommandOrControl+Alt+. (host-bridge.ts:161-168).
Select boxes list the presets, the current value if unusual and 'none' for keys that may be off (DesktopSettingsSection.tsx:158-166).
Quick Ask panel: frameless, not resizable, always on top across workspaces, hides on blur or Escape (quickAsk.ts:53-90).
journey: Press the Quick Ask key. The panel is created if needed, placed in the upper centre of the display under the cursor and focused (quickAsk.ts:139-162).
Type a prompt and press Enter in the compact chat page (apps/web/app/quick-ask/page.tsx:6-8).
If the page navigates anywhere outside /quick-ask (a full conversation, upgrade page or settings), the panel hides and the main window opens that route (quickAsk.ts:29-41, :97-114).
Press Escape or click another window: the panel hides (quickAsk.ts:81-89).
To change a key, choose a preset in Settings or in the tray Shortcuts submenu (tray.ts:73-102).
feedback_and_outputs: Notification 'Shortcut unavailable' with the key and reason, shown once per registration pass (shortcuts.ts:34, :52-63).
Settings notes: 'Already used by another Desktop shortcut.', 'Already used by another app.', 'Not a shortcut this computer can register.' (DesktopSettingsSection.tsx:150-154).
Tray heading shows the reason after the label (tray.ts:104-108).
Stop Agents shows a notification 'Agents stopped', 'Screen control is yours' or 'Nothing to stop' (main.ts:1804-1820).
settings: Six shortcut preferences, saved durably (shortcuts.ts:156).
Dictation into other apps: macOS only preference dictateIntoFocusedApp, default off (main.ts:1984, garnishCore.ts:572).

working: Registration with status registered, taken, duplicate, malformed or off (shortcuts.ts:74-90).
Duplicate detection sees through modifier spelling and order (garnishCore.ts:148-182).
Stop Agents claims its chord first and cannot be set to none; a change that leaves it unregistered is rolled back with a message (shortcuts.ts:130-169, garnishCore.ts:105-107).
The page may only choose presets, keep the current chord, or turn off a key that may be off (garnishCore.ts:192-199, main.ts:2163-2172).
Quick Ask panel is warmed up 5 seconds after launch and reloaded if the first load failed (main.ts:402, :2701, quickAsk.ts:91-96, :152-156).
Hand-off of non-Quick-Ask routes to the main window (quickAsk.ts:97-114, main.ts:2692).
Voice key dictates into the app, or into another app on macOS when enabled (main.ts:1921-1930).
incomplete: The notification shows only once per pass; later conflicts in the same session are logged only (shortcuts.ts:52-57). This matches the brief's 'warning once'.
Whether Quick Ask needs a signed-in session or shows sign-in inside the panel is not established; the panel hands sign-in URLs to the main window via the policy (quickAsk.ts:79).
disconnected_or_disabled: Brief S70.20 says cross-application dictation is not applicable anywhere, but code for it exists (dictationElsewhere.ts, main.ts:1893-1930). Whether it is shipped is unknown; it is off by default.
not_available: Custom chords outside presets from the settings page are refused (main.ts:2163-2172).
Shortcuts on web, mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not applicable.

established.statement: System-wide shortcuts (Quick Ask, screenshot, voice) work while another app is focused, are configurable and report conflicts.
A global shortcut opens a small composer over any app where the user can type and send a prompt.
A key that another app holds is reported as taken; the same key twice is reported as duplicate.
Stop Agents can never be set off; the change is rolled back if it would leave no stop key.
A prompt needing a full conversation, an upgrade page or settings opens in the main window.
The voice press must reach the main window even when Quick Ask is up or the window is hidden.

acceptance_criteria: Press each default chord from another app: the matching action runs.
Pick a chord already used by another app: Settings shows 'Already used by another app.' and one notification appears.
Pick the same chord for two Desktop shortcuts: the later one shows 'Already used by another Desktop shortcut.'
Try to set Stop Agents to none: refused with the Stop Agents message.
In Quick Ask open a link to the upgrade or settings page: the panel hides and the main window opens it.
Press Escape or click away: the panel hides.
inferred: Because chords are registered only while the app runs, they do not work after quit [inferred from main.ts:2763].
Prompts sent from Quick Ask follow the same chat pipeline as the main window since it is the same web chat root in compact mode [inferred from apps/web/app/quick-ask/page.tsx:7].
proposed: [proposed] Show the conflict notification each time a chord fails after the user changes it, not only once per pass.
[proposed] Add a test of the voice press with Quick Ask open.
