features.summary: The Window menu opens extra app windows, opens or moves a conversation into its own window, keeps the front window above others, and tiles windows. Two chat panels (Details and Research) can pop out into their own window. No separate companion window exists beyond the Quick Ask panel.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person work with several app windows, pin one above all apps, snap windows to halves and quarters, and detach the Details and Research panels. (appMenu.ts:438-543, main.ts:1457-1493, panel-windows.ts:1-25)
purpose.why_it_exists: Briefs S70.07 to S70.10 ask for a companion window, always on top, multiple windows and detachable panels.
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop users who keep a chat beside other apps or compare two conversations.
problems_solved: Keep an answer visible while working elsewhere (Always on Top).
Read two conversations at once (New Window and Move Conversation).
Arrange windows without OS tools (Move & Resize).
use_cases: Choose Window > Always on Top while reading docs in another app.
Choose Window > Move Conversation to New Window to split a chat out.
Choose Window > Move & Resize > Left & Right to tile two app windows.
Click 'Open Research in a new window' on the Research panel.

where_to_find_it: Desktop only. Window menu items: 'New Window', 'Open in New Window', 'Move Conversation to New Window', 'Always on Top', Minimize, Zoom, 'Fill', 'Center', 'Move & Resize', 'Full Screen Tile' (appMenu.ts:447-516); Mac also 'Minimize All', 'Zoom All', 'Arrange in Front', 'Remove Window from Set' and a list of windows (appMenu.ts:472-540).
Panel button label 'Open <panel> in a new window' or 'Move <panel> back to the main window' on the Details and Research panels (PanelWindow.tsx:39-41).
prerequisites: A front app window for Always on Top, Fill, Center and Move & Resize (main.ts:1487-1500).
A conversation open in the front window for Open in New Window and Move Conversation (appMenu.ts:455-461).
screens_and_controls: Always on Top is a checkbox; disabled when no app window is in front (appMenu.ts:463-469).
Move & Resize submenu: Halves (Left, Right, Top, Bottom), Quarters, Arrange layouts, 'Return to Previous Size' (appMenu.ts:477-509).
Full Screen Tile: 'Left of Screen', 'Right of Screen' (appMenu.ts:510-516).
Panel window 440 by 760, minimum 320 by 360 (windowPolicy.ts:237-243).
journey: Choose Window > New Window: a window opens on a new chat, stepped off the front window on the same display (main.ts:1073-1087, :1457).

Open a conversation, choose Open in New Window: the same conversation opens in a second window and stays in the first, but a conversation lives in one window; the one that already held it keeps it (main.ts:1467-1471, windowRegistry.ts:37-50).
Choose Move Conversation to New Window: the first window returns to a new chat and a new window shows the conversation (main.ts:1473-1479).
Choose Always on Top: the window floats above others; unchecking turns it off (main.ts:1487-1490).
On the Research panel click the pop-out button; the panel moves to a small window and back (use-detachable-panels.ts, panel-windows.ts).
feedback_and_outputs: Menu checkmarks show Always on Top state; the menu is rebuilt when it changes (main.ts:1487-1490).
Return to Previous Size is enabled only after a tile (appMenu.ts:503-507, main.ts:1527-1560).
settings: None found for always on top; it is not saved between launches [inferred from main.ts:1487-1490 where only the live window is changed].
Primary window size and place are remembered; secondary windows are cascaded and not written (main.ts:1143-1150 comment).

working: New Window, Open in New Window, Move Conversation to New Window, Always on Top and tiling are connected from the menu to main.ts functions (main.ts:2503-2560).

Frame memory: only the primary window writes its frame; minimized, full-screen or zoomed readings are not stored as sizes, a zoomed frame is stored as maximized (windowState.ts:224-240, main.ts:1010-1055).
Conversation clash: a window navigating onto a conversation another holds is sent back (windowRegistry.ts:37-86).
Detachable Details and Research panels work on the desktop: the page opens a named popup the shell allows, sized 440 by 760 (panel-windows.ts:12-14, windowPolicy.ts:237-243, :318-327).
A detached panel closes when its opener closes (windowPolicy.ts:277-282, :340-342).
incomplete: Brief S70.10 says detachable panels are missing; the code has detaching for two panels ('work' and 'research') only. Artifact and preview panels are not among DetachablePanel values (panel-windows.ts:7).
Brief cites appMenu.ts:237 and :242 as companion window code; those lines are the Find menu. No companion window code was found; the Quick Ask panel comment is the only mention (quickAsk.ts:46).
disconnected_or_disabled: Detaching is offered only inside the desktop host (use-detachable-panels.ts uses useDesktopHost).
not_available: A dedicated compact companion window: not found in the code.
Detaching artifact, preview or other side panels: not found in the code.
Windows are not restored after relaunch except the primary: not established.

established.statement: A compact companion window can stay open beside other apps.
The user can keep an app window above all other windows.
The user can open more than one app window and move a conversation into its own window.
A panel (artifact, preview, side panel) can be popped out of the main window into its own window.
A zoomed frame is not saved as a larger size.
With no conversation open, Move Conversation to New Window must not act.

acceptance_criteria: Window > New Window opens a second window on a new chat.
With a conversation open, Move Conversation to New Window leaves a new chat in the first window and shows the conversation in the second.
Always on Top keeps the chosen window above another app until unchecked.
With no conversation open the two conversation items are disabled.
Maximise then quit and relaunch: the window opens maximised, not enlarged beyond the screen.
Click the pop-out on the Research panel: the panel appears in its own window; click again and it returns.
inferred: Only one window holds a given conversation at a time [inferred from windowRegistry.ts:37-50].
Always on Top is per window and per run [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Decide if the Quick Ask panel counts as the companion window and update the brief item.
[proposed] Extend detaching to artifact and preview panels, or change the brief to say two panels.

features.summary: On the desktop app a shortcut or menu item captures the screen, or the front window of another app, and pastes it into the chat composer. Separately, a cloud model turn can see the screen and move the mouse and keyboard on macOS, only after the user turns it on and approves each task.

purpose.what_it_does: Captures the display under the cursor (or the front window of another app on macOS) to the clipboard, pastes it into the chat composer and clears the clipboard. Also runs computer use: screenshots, pointer, keyboard and app-open steps requested by the model, with stop, take over and hand back. (screenshot.ts:142-243, computerUseSession.ts:200-394)
purpose.why_it_exists: Briefs S70.19 and S70.21: capture the screen into chat, and let the assistant see and control the computer after permission with stop and take-over. The product spec lists computer use for Desktop (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:80).
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop users asking about what is on screen or delegating on-screen tasks (macOS for control).
problems_solved: Attach a screenshot without saving a file.
Let an agent act in apps that have no API, with the user able to stop it at any moment.
Prevent a screen picture from staying on the clipboard.
use_cases: Press Screenshot key, ask 'what does this error mean?'.
Press Window to Chat to send only the app in front.
Ask the assistant to fill a form in a desktop app; approve 'Allow for this task'.
Press Escape during a run to stop.

where_to_find_it: Desktop only. File > 'Screenshot to Chat'; tray items 'Screenshot to Chat' and 'Window to Chat'; shortcuts in Settings 'Screenshot to chat shortcut' and 'Window to chat shortcut' (appMenu.ts:189-194, tray.ts:179-190, DesktopSettingsSection.tsx:100-107).

Computer use: Settings section headed 'Computer use' with hint 'Let AGI see your screen and use the mouse and keyboard in apps you allow.' (ComputerUseSettings.tsx:34-35); control bar 'AGI is using your computer' with buttons 'Take over', 'Hand back', 'Stop' (ComputerUseControlBar.tsx:30-57); File > 'Stop Computer Use', 'Take Over Screen Control', 'Hand Back Screen Control' (appMenu.ts:196-212); tray 'Hand Back Screen Control' and 'Stop Computer Use and Revoke Access...' (tray.ts:151-161).
prerequisites: Computer use is off by default (garnishCore.ts:567) and must be turned on in Settings.
Computer use runs on macOS only; other systems report 'supported on macOS only' (computerUseService.ts:226-232).
Window capture needs the macOS helper, so it is macOS only too (computerUseService.ts:392-394).
macOS Screen Recording permission for screenshots and Accessibility for pointer and keyboard (computerUseService.ts:245-262, systemPermissions.ts:22-31).
A cloud chat turn on a model that calls device tools (request-processor.ts:6359-6362).
screens_and_controls: Control bar over the page with role 'status' and live region (ComputerUseControlBar.tsx:23-26).
Native dialog 'Let the agent use your screen?' with buttons 'Cancel' and 'Allow for this task' (dispatcher.ts:1950-1960).
Macros: Stop key is Escape, registered globally only while a run is active (computer-use.ts:24, computerUseSession.ts:123-132).
Settings Computer use section lists Control (Any app, Chrome), Allowed apps, Refused apps and a Stop button (ComputerUseSettings.tsx:34-60).
journey: Screenshot: press the key. The Quick Ask panel and main window hide for 300 ms, the display under the cursor is captured, written to the clipboard, the main window is shown and the composer focused, and a paste runs (screenshot.ts:190-243).
After one second the clipboard is cleared, or the earlier text restored, if it still holds the capture (screenshot.ts:92-107, :235-238).

Computer use: enable it in Settings; ask a task; the agent's screen step raises a native 'Allow for this task' prompt; a notification 'AGI is using your computer' says how to stop (computerUseSession.ts:213-218).
While running, press Escape or the Stop button to stop; Take over pauses so the user can act; Hand back resumes (computerUseSession.ts:313-340).
Moving the mouse or typing during a run pauses it automatically with a notice 'AGI paused' (computerUseSession.ts:231-238, :146-168).
feedback_and_outputs: Notifications: 'Screenshot copied', 'Screenshot copied to clipboard', 'Screenshot failed', 'Window capture failed' (screenshot.ts:114, :135-138, :217-221, :159-173).

Dialog 'Screen recording permission needed' naming System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording and asking for a relaunch, shown once per run of the app (screenshot.ts:39-52).
Notification 'AGI finished using your computer' (computerUseSession.ts:259).
Step results include the screen size and the picture (device-steps.ts:140-160 in apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib).
settings: computerUseEnabled preference (garnishCore.ts:567, computerUseSession.ts:108).
Screenshot and window shot chords (F070-03).
Allowed and refused apps lists (ComputerUseSettings.tsx:47-50).

working: Full-screen and front-window capture to chat with clipboard cleanup and destination checks (screenshot.ts:142-243).
If the chat window is gone, the image stays on the clipboard with a notice (screenshot.ts:113-116).
The paste goes only into the same page and conversation that asked (screenshot.ts:59-72, :126-134).

Computer use session: active, paused, idle phases, stop shortcut, user-input pause, take over, hand back, quiet-run timeout 2 minutes, held-step limit 10 minutes (computerUseSession.ts:37-38, :200-340).
Per-task native yes with a 5 minute idle expiry (computerUseRuns.ts:13, dispatcher.ts:1925-1963).
The computer.use grant is high risk: it never persists past the session (permissionCore.ts:57-71, capabilities.ts:66-73).
Repeat and cycle detector refuses a model stuck on the same click (computerUseLoop.ts:11-13, dispatcher.ts:585-600).
Cloud turn is offered device tools only if the shell declared them; workspace controls can withhold computer.use (request-processor.ts:3365-3379, dispatcher.ts:2252-2282).
Revoke: stopComputerUse withdraws the grant, so the agent must ask again (computerUseSession.ts:300-308).
incomplete: Screenshot to chat on Windows and Linux uses the Electron capturer; the permission message is Mac only (screenshot.ts:39-41).
Window capture fails with 'No other app window is in front' when the helper is unavailable, which includes all non-Mac systems (screenshot.ts:157-160, computerUseService.ts:392-394).
disconnected_or_disabled: Computer use is off by default (garnishCore.ts:567); a step while off is refused with a message naming Settings, Desktop app (computerUseSession.ts:53).
not_available: Computer use on Windows and Linux (computerUseService.ts:226-232).

Computer use from Local (on-device) models: not found; the device registry reports localModels false (dispatcher.ts:2298) and the declaration is sent in a cloud chat request header (host-headers.ts:44-50).
Web, Mobile, CLI, VS Code: none for screen control; the doc matrix lists Chrome extension as present for its own computer use (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:512-521).

established.statement: The user can capture the screen or a chosen window into the chat from the desktop app.
The assistant can see the screen and move, click and type after permission, with stop and take-over.
Capture copies to the clipboard, pastes into chat, then clears the clipboard if it still holds only the capture.
If the chat window is closed, the image stays on the clipboard and the user is told.
Missing screen recording permission produces a message naming it and asking for a relaunch.
Computer use can be stopped at any time; take-over pauses; hand-back resumes; revoke removes the grant.
Browser and computer use must treat external content as untrusted.

acceptance_criteria: Press the screenshot chord with the app visible: the composer receives the image of the display under the cursor and the clipboard no longer holds it a second later.
Copy text first, capture, wait: the text is back on the clipboard.
Close the main window, capture: a notice says the image is on the clipboard.
On Mac with Screen Recording denied, capture shows 'Screen recording permission needed' once.
Enable computer use and run a task: a native prompt 'Allow for this task' appears before the first screen step; Cancel makes the agent stop trying.
During a run press Escape: the run stops and the grant is withdrawn; the next task asks again.
Move the mouse during a run: the run pauses and Hand back resumes it.
inferred: The capture is taken of the display the cursor is on [inferred from screenshot.ts:209].
The per-task prompt can be shown only on the device with the native dialog, so a web page cannot approve it [inferred from dispatcher.ts:1950].
proposed: [proposed] Show on Windows and Linux a clear message in Settings that computer use is macOS only.
[proposed] Offer window capture on Windows and Linux without the helper.

steps.what_happens: A chord or menu click calls captureToChat or captureWindowToChat.
The capture is made by the OS capturer, copied to the clipboard and pasted into the composer; the file is not sent anywhere until the user sends the message.
The user sends the message; the image goes with the chat request.
For computer use the page sends a chat request with a header declaring this device's capabilities.
The cloud model asks for a device step; the page calls the local runtime; main asks for a per-task yes, then the helper takes a screenshot or acts.
The screenshot is returned to the cloud model as an image.

features.summary: The desktop app lets the user approve folders through the operating system folder dialog. Approved folders are saved across launches and can be revoked. The assistant can list, search names and contents, read, create and change files inside them after a native permission prompt.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps a list of approved folders, lets the user attach files from them, and runs file steps (list, read, name search, text search, write, edit, delete) inside them for the person or a cloud turn. (workspaceStore.ts:100-242, dispatcher.ts:2312-2380)
purpose.why_it_exists: Briefs S70.11 to S70.14. The cloud cannot reach the disk, so the device does the file work under permission prompts (device-steps.ts header comment).
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop users who want the assistant to work with local documents or code.
problems_solved: Attach local files without uploading whole folders.
Find files by name or content.
Let the assistant edit files without giving it the whole disk.
use_cases: Attach a file from a local folder in the composer.
Ask 'find invoices in this folder'.
Ask the assistant to edit a Markdown file; approve the write prompt.
Revoke a folder in Settings when a project ends.

where_to_find_it: Desktop only. Composer attach picker offers a local folder: dialog titled 'Attach from a local folder' (LocalFolderAttachDialog.tsx:25). Settings > Capabilities > 'Local access' section with 'Folders', 'Commands', 'Permissions' (LocalAccessSection.tsx:37-58). File > 'Open Folder' (appMenu.ts:174-178).
prerequisites: Desktop app (the page must run in the shell).
A folder that is not the system, the whole home folder, or where sign-ins and keys are kept (workspaceStore.ts:151-157).
screens_and_controls: Button 'Choose a folder' in the attach dialog; button 'Add a folder' in Local access (LocalFolderAttachDialog.tsx:368, LocalAccessSection.tsx:55).
Search field 'Search this folder' with placeholder 'Search names and text'; headings 'Matching names' and 'Matching text'; 'Clear search' (LocalFolderAttachDialog.tsx:34-39).
Folder chips with a remove control and a reveal action; permissions list with 'Withdraw' (LocalAccessSection.tsx:58-64).
Native permission dialog for read or write per folder; 'always' grants are saved for non-high-risk capabilities (permissionCore.ts:57-71).
journey: Open the attach picker and choose a local folder; the OS folder dialog opens (dispatcher.ts:1387-1411).
The folder is checked, saved and shown as a chip (workspaceStore.ts:145-172).
Browse or search the folder; results list names and matching text lines.
Choose a file: it is read and attached (LocalFolderAttachDialog.tsx:229-243).

Ask the assistant to change a file; the first write asks for permission for that folder; the edit then runs and any replaced file's earlier copy goes to the Trash (main.ts:2674, filesystemService.ts:614-650).
Revoke the folder in Local access: work running in it is stopped after a prompt, the folder is removed and all grants on it are withdrawn (dispatcher.ts:2316-2321, workspaceStore.ts:224-236).
feedback_and_outputs: 'That folder was not approved.' 'That folder was not removed.' 'Approved folders could not be read.' (LocalAccessSection.tsx:51-53).
'No folders are approved yet. Choose one, and Desktop asks your permission before it reads anything inside.' (LocalFolderAttachDialog.tsx:26-27).
Refusal text for a banned location (workspaceStore.ts:153-155).
'That workspace is no longer approved. Choose the folder again.' (dispatcher.ts:632).
'Workspace <name> is no longer reachable.' when the folder is gone (pathGuard.ts:119-121).
settings: Settings > Capabilities > Local access (CapabilitiesSection.tsx:12, :213).
Worktree location and shell policy are separate features.

working: Folder pick uses the OS open-directory dialog; cancel returns a message (dispatcher.ts:1387-1411).
Approved folders are saved to a file in the user data folder and loaded at start; a stored root on a banned path is dropped (workspaceStore.ts:36-90).
List roots newest first; revoke removes the root, its worktrees and every grant on it (workspaceStore.ts:100-104, :224-236).
Name search uses a glob and text search scans text files, skipping credential-named files, large and binary files (filesystemService.ts:890-957).
Reads and edits are resolved inside the root; traversal and outside-root paths are refused (pathGuard.ts:108-135).
Writes need filesystem.write; reads need filesystem.read, and a write grant implies read (dispatcher.ts:683-694, permissionCore.ts:21-24).
Replaced files keep a previous copy that goes to the Trash (main.ts:2674, filesystemService.ts:614-650).
The cloud model's file tools map to the same commands and capabilities (device-steps.ts:131-171).
Declaration to the cloud lists a file capability only when some folder is not denied (dispatcher.ts:2252-2282).
incomplete: When an approved folder is deleted on disk, the message is 'no longer reachable', not an instruction to choose again; the 'choose again' text appears only for an unknown root id (pathGuard.ts:119-121, dispatcher.ts:632).
The brief's claim that folder storage is unconfirmed is out of date: storage is confirmed in desktop-workspaces.json (workspaceStore.ts:36).
disconnected_or_disabled: Local shell execution in an approved folder (S70.15) is a separate feature; it shares the root list.
not_available: Folder access on web, mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: the doc matrix lists filesystem absent on web, mobile and Chrome and unverified for CLI and VS Code (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:522-531).

established.statement: Choosing files or folders opens the operating system's own file dialog.
A folder the user approves stays approved across launches and can be reviewed and revoked.
The user or assistant can search approved local folders by file name or content.
The assistant can create or change files in an approved folder after a permission prompt.
Search covers only approved folders; a missing approved folder tells the user to choose it again.
An agent never destroys user data on its own; a removed or overwritten file goes to the Trash first.
The desktop provides approved local files and tools.

acceptance_criteria: Choose a folder: the OS dialog opens and the folder shows as approved after relaunch.
Search a name and a word in the folder: both result lists appear; a file outside the folder never appears.
Ask the assistant to edit a file: a permission prompt appears first; after Allow, the file changes and the earlier version is in the Trash.
Revoke the folder: it disappears and the assistant gets 'no longer approved' on the next file step.
Try to approve the home folder: refused with the explanation.
Rename the approved folder on disk and search: the user sees a clear message that the folder is not reachable.
inferred: A 'once' grant is used once and removed (isSingleUse, permissionCore.ts:87-89) [inferred from names].
Search results are capped by MAX_LIST_ENTRIES and MAX_GREP_MATCHES (filesystemService.ts:896-945).
proposed: [proposed] When a root is unreachable, show the 'choose it again' action with a re-pick button.
[proposed] Show a count of grants per folder in Local access.

features.summary: In AGI Desktop (Electron) the user, or the assistant on the user's behalf, runs one program inside a folder the user approved. A native dialog asks first, the program runs in an operating-system sandbox where one exists, and output streams back live. A separate interactive terminal exists inside Code sessions.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person or the assistant start a program (for example a test run or a build) in an approved folder on the computer, see its output as it arrives, and stop it. It has two paths: a no-shell command runner (the 'Run a local command' dialog and the assistant's device steps), and an interactive terminal in Code sessions run by the AGI CLI.
purpose.why_it_exists: Developers need real programs to run on their own machine, not in the cloud. The product keeps this safe by limiting runs to approved folders, asking before each unlisted program, sandboxing, and withholding secrets from the program's environment (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/shellService.ts:220).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers and power users on AGI Desktop for macOS; the assistant acts for them when a cloud chat asks for a device step.
problems_solved: Running a command without leaving the chat
Letting the assistant run tests or builds in a project without giving it free access to the whole computer
Seeing live output and stopping a runaway command
use_cases: Type 'npm test' into 'Run a local command' and attach the transcript to the chat
The assistant asks to run a build; the user approves once
The assistant starts a dev server, reads its output, then stops it
Open a terminal tab in a Code session and type commands yourself

journey: 1. Open the composer plus menu and choose 'Run a local command'.
2. Pick an approved folder (or add one). Type one program and its arguments. Pipes, redirects and variables are not available because there is no shell (LocalCommandDialog.tsx:21).
3. Press Run. The first time for a folder the app asks for the 'shell.execute' permission.
4. Unless the program is on the allowed list, a native dialog quotes the exact command and asks.
5. Output streams into the pane; stderr is marked. Stop ends it.
6. The outcome line says 'Finished in Ns', 'Exited with code N', 'Stopped' or 'Stopped: the command ran past its time limit.' (LocalCommandDialog.tsx:52-57).
7. Optionally attach the transcript to the chat.
Assistant path: the cloud chat returns a device step; the same approvals apply; for long-running commands the assistant reads output and stops the command (device-steps.ts:172-198).

working: No-shell runner: parses one program and arguments, refuses control characters, evaluates the allow/deny policy, then asks, sandboxes and spawns with shell:false (shellService.ts:554-684, :705).
Sandbox: macOS seatbelt, Linux bubblewrap, otherwise none (shellSandbox.ts:189-203). Without a sandbox the user is asked every run, even for allowed programs (shellService.ts:604-610).

Folder pinning: before a sandboxed run the approved folder must still resolve to the same real path, not be a link, not the filesystem root and not contain the home folder; otherwise 'This folder changed since it was approved ... Choose it again to run commands in it.' (shellService.ts:359-395).
Unknown or revoked folder is refused with 'That workspace is no longer approved. Choose the folder again.' (dispatcher.ts:628-634).
Environment allowlist; loader hooks and names containing KEY, SECRET or TOKEN are withheld (shellService.ts:220, :288-295).

Limits: command up to 4,000 characters, timeout default 120 s and maximum 600 s, output capped at 1,000,000 bytes after which the run is stopped and marked truncated (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/shell.ts:44-48; shellService.ts:731-740).
Background commands: start, read (with typed input), stop, list; typed input is always asked about (shellService.ts:953-1070; dispatcher.ts:2412-2423).
Interactive terminal in Code sessions through the AGI CLI, with a plan dialog before it opens (developerSessionService.ts:1967-2054; dispatcher.ts:2810).
A server-set 'review' makes even an allowed program ask (shellService.ts:604-610, :84-90).

Shell features such as pipes, redirects and variables (LocalCommandDialog.tsx:21).

established.statement: The user or assistant can run a program in an approved folder, with approval, sandboxing and streamed output.

Commands run only in an approved folder and inside the same sandbox as agent commands; the assistant cannot type into the user's terminal; a folder that is no longer approved is refused with a message to choose the folder again.
established.source: task brief for F070-07; terminal copy at apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:643; refusal text at dispatcher.ts:632

established.statement: An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: With no approved folder, 'Run a local command' tells the user to choose a folder first and Run does nothing.
An unlisted program shows the native dialog quoting the exact command; Cancel means the program never starts.
With the network box unticked, a sandboxed program cannot reach the network; ticking it applies to that one run only.
Revoking the folder, then running, returns 'That workspace is no longer approved. Choose the folder again.'
A command that outputs more than about 1 MB is stopped and shown as cut off; one that runs past its limit shows 'Stopped: the command ran past its time limit.'
A command containing a pipe or redirect is refused with an explanation that there is no shell.
Typed input to a background command always raises 'Type into <program>?'.
The terminal opens only after 'Open terminal' is chosen in the plan dialog.
inferred: [inferred] The assistant cannot drive the user's interactive terminal because the device-step table lists only shell_run, shell_start, shell_read and shell_stop and no terminal command (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/device-steps.ts:172-198); the terminal commands are not in that file.
[inferred] The terminal shares the agent sandbox only as far as the AGI CLI enforces it; the desktop code shows the plan the CLI returns (developerSessionService.ts:1990-1999).
proposed: [proposed] Add one test that asserts the terminal's sandbox plan equals the agent command plan.
[proposed] Show the folder-changed refusal with a button that reopens the folder picker.

features.summary: AGI Desktop can host Code sessions that a paired phone watches and steers. The user starts pairing in Settings, scans a code with the mobile app, and allows the phone in a native dialog on the computer. The phone can read sessions, send turns, interrupt and answer approvals, within approved folders. Paid plans only.

purpose.what_it_does: Relays coding sessions on the computer to a paired phone over an encrypted relay so the phone can read output and diffs, start or interrupt turns and answer the agent's questions and approval requests.
purpose.why_it_exists: Long coding runs continue while the person is away; the phone lets them unblock the agent without returning to the desk.
purpose.who_uses_it: Paid-plan developers using AGI Desktop Code sessions and the AGI mobile app.
problems_solved: An agent waiting for approval while the user is away
Following a long run from the couch
Starting a new session from the phone
use_cases: Pair the phone, then approve a file edit from the phone
Read a diff on the phone
Send the next instruction to a running session
Stop Remote Control from the computer

journey: 1. Open Settings > Capabilities > Remote Control and press 'Pair a phone'.
2. The page asks the server for a one-time code (POST /api/pair/initiate) and gives it to the desktop shell (remote-pairing.ts:28-47).
3. A pairing window shows the QR code and code.
4. On the phone open the mobile app's Code screen, choose Add device and scan.
5. The computer shows 'Allow this phone?' with the code. Allow only if it is your phone.
6. Status becomes connected; the phone lists sessions in approved folders.
7. The phone reads, sends turns, interrupts and answers approvals; some approvals open a native dialog on the computer first.
8. Stop with 'Disconnect phone'.
feedback_and_outputs: Connected state with the phone's name and number of open sessions.

Messages to the phone for held approvals: 'This needs to be allowed at your computer. A dialog is open there now.', 'Nobody answered at your computer within two minutes...' (remoteControlService.ts:92-103).
Errors in red, for example 'The relay connection failed.' (remoteControlHost.ts:600).
settings: Remote Control on/off by pairing or stopping.
'Menu bar' and 'Keep computer awake' are separate; a connected phone always holds the computer awake (workKeeper.ts:28).

working: Pairing: server creates a code and relay session; desktop host registers, shows QR, and waits (remoteControlHost.ts:640-668; initiate/route.ts:47-140).

The user at the computer must allow the phone, unless the same phone identity and secret was already allowed in this session (remoteControlHost.ts:505-520). The allowed phone is remembered for this session only.
Messages must be signed with the scanned secret; nothing is sent to a phone before a signed control verifies (remoteControlHost.ts:416-424; doc: docs/decisions/wire-or-cut.md:748).
Sessions are listed and steered only for folders where the agent is allowed (remoteControlService.ts:73-80, :222-262).
Credential files are never diffed for the phone (remoteControlService.ts:249).
Approvals that main reserves need an allow at the computer, with a 120 s limit; a locked screen refuses (remoteControlService.ts:85, :132-137).
Dropped relay: status 'reconnecting' with backoff, then back to 'waiting' (remoteControlHost.ts:602-632).
Stop returns state to 'idle' and clears keys (remoteControlHost.ts:692-716).
Relay revoke or expiry ends the pairing with a message (remoteControlHost.ts:588-598).
Plan, workspace policy and kill switch checked on pairing (remote-control-gate.ts:97-123).

established.statement: The desktop app can act as a host that another device (phone) pairs with and drives remotely.

The phone is asked again before it connects; if the computer is locked, remote control refuses; if the service stops, state shows stopped, not connected; a dropped connection is shown and the phone can ask to refresh pairing.

features.summary: AGI Desktop lets the user choose to start at login, see what runs in the background and stop each item, and keep the computer from idle sleep while an agent runs. Sleep and lock handling is partial: some services react to suspend, wake or lock, but there is no general pause and resume of agent work.

purpose.why_it_exists: An app that keeps agents and phone links running must show what is active, let the user end it without quitting, and avoid being cut off by idle sleep.
purpose.who_uses_it: AGI Desktop users on macOS who run long coding sessions or routines.

features.summary: AGI Desktop on macOS checks for new versions daily and on request, downloads them in the background and installs after the user chooses 'Relaunch to update'. The Help menu can open the logs folder and copy a diagnostics summary. The user cannot pick an update channel.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps the app current through a signed feed and gives support two tools: the log folder and a copy-ready diagnostics summary.
purpose.why_it_exists: Users should not reinstall by hand, and support needs facts about the build and each part of the shell without private data.
purpose.who_uses_it: All AGI Desktop users on macOS; support staff.
problems_solved: Running an old build
Not knowing whether an update is ready
Reporting a problem with no details

Open the logs folder

Settings > General: row 'App version' with 'Check for updates' and 'Relaunch to update' or 'Download installer' (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopUpdateRow.tsx:11-16; mounted at DesktopSettingsSection.tsx:440).
A notice in the page when an update is ready (DesktopUpdateNotice.tsx:29), and a system notification with a 'Relaunch to update' button (main.ts:2454-2465).

2. A newer build downloads in the background.
3. When ready, a notice and a notification appear.
4. The user chooses 'Relaunch to update'. If agent turns or commands are running, the quit prompt asks first; declining defers the install to the next quit.
5. The app restarts on the new version.

where_to_find_it: Mobile: the whole app shell. The menu control is the round button with accessibility label 'Open navigation drawer' (apps/mobile/src/shared/components/DrawerButton.tsx:70-95).

Mobile drawer rows: Search, 'New chat', destination rows, Recents, 'See all chats', Settings (keys drawer.newChat, search, drawer.recents, drawer.seeAllChats, settings) (apps/mobile/src/features/drawer/components/DrawerContent.tsx:631-912).

Some rows need Cloud mode, a signed-in account, or a plan capability (Images, AGI Work tasks) (DrawerContent.tsx:337-345, 563-573).

Camera and scan pages: full window, no drawer.
Voice page: always dark, drawer swipe off.
journey: Open the app. On a phone the chat shows with the drawer closed.
Swipe from the left edge (40 points on iOS, 64 on Android, drag of at least 60 on iOS or 96 on Android) or tap the menu button.
Tap a chat, a destination or Settings. The drawer closes and the page opens.
In Settings, swipe from the left edge or tap Back to return one page.
On a window 1000 points wide or more, the drawer is already open at 280 points wide and the menu button is gone.

feedback_and_outputs: The drawer slides over the page with a scrim (apps/mobile/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:55-70).
The active chat row is highlighted and unread chats show a dot (DrawerContent.tsx:500-560).
Unread count shows on the menu button and is read out in its label (DrawerButton.tsx:77-84).
settings: Chat list arrangement: 'In one list' or 'By project' (drawer.inOneList, drawer.byProject) stored in the settings store (DrawerContent.tsx:358-380).
The 'More' fold and the folded Projects section remember their state (DrawerContent.tsx:352-357).

working: Drawer type is 'front' (overlay) on narrow windows and 'permanent' when the window is 1000 points wide or more (280 drawer + 720 content) (apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useResponsiveLayout.ts:3-9, 24-47; apps/mobile/src/features/shell/drawerGestures.ts:23-45).
The draft's 768 and 1024 are not the drawer switch. 768 sets the 'tablet' size class and 1024 (largest side of the screen) sets isTablet (apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useTabletLayout.ts:5-6, 40-50).
Split view is detected as a window narrower than the screen by at least 8 points on a tablet-size screen (useTabletLayout.ts:9, 51).
Settings pages turn the drawer swipe off so the edge swipe means Back (apps/mobile/app/(app)/_layout.tsx:20-22, 122).
Camera and scan are drawerType 'front' even where a sidebar is permanent. The voice route also turns swipe off (_layout.tsx:23-28, 130-134).
A leftover open state is closed when the window grows to the permanent width (_layout.tsx:30-41).

Phones are locked to portrait at app start by lockPhonePortrait (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:122, 129; apps/mobile/src/shared/hooks/useLandscapeWhileOpen.ts:23-25). A phone is any non-iPad iOS device or an Android device whose smaller side is under 600 dp (useLandscapeWhileOpen.ts:11-16).

A native Android plugin lets screens with smallest width 600 dp or more rotate and re-decides when the size changes (apps/mobile/native/android/withAGITabletOrientation.cjs:14-34).

Message list and composer keep a reading column up to 720 points wide on large windows (apps/mobile/src/shared/layout/contentColumn.ts:3-25; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageList.tsx:367-370).

disconnected_or_disabled: The Upgrade row in the drawer appears only when native purchases are available. Billing is off in the feature flags, so it is hidden in the current build. (DrawerContent.tsx:337-345; apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:6)
Companion pages are registered as drawer screens but FEATURES.companion is false. (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:16; _layout.tsx:110-114)
not_available: Hinge-aware layout on any app.

established.statement: The phone app navigates with native patterns: a swipeable drawer plus stack routes with back gestures.
On tablets the app uses a wider layout (persistent drawer, multi-column grids) and adapts to split view.
On foldables the layout adapts when the device folds or unfolds, ideally around the hinge. The brief status is not applicable anywhere.
Rotating the phone to landscape re-lays out the chat usefully.
The design contract names breakpoints: compact phone, phone, tablet, narrow desktop, desktop, wide desktop.

acceptance_criteria: On a phone, a swipe from the left edge opens the drawer and a tap on a recent chat opens it and closes the drawer.
On Settings pages the edge swipe goes Back and does not open the drawer.
With a window 1000 points wide or more the drawer is permanent and the menu button is not shown. Narrowing the window below 1000 closes any stale open state and the overlay drawer works.
Opening camera, scan or voice shows no drawer. Voice does not react to an edge swipe.
An iPhone and a small Android phone stay in portrait when turned; an iPad and an Android tablet rotate.
Opening a video or a presentation on a phone allows landscape and closing it returns to portrait.
inferred: The brief status 'done' for S71.27 conflicts with the portrait lock, so the status is either stale or means tablets only. [inferred]
A tablet in portrait between 768 and 999 points gets the overlay drawer, not a permanent one. [inferred from useResponsiveLayout.ts:24-47]
proposed: [proposed] Decide and record whether phone landscape is a product requirement. If yes, unlock rotation for the chat and re-lay out the composer. If no, change S71.27 to match the code.
[proposed] Add a posture or hinge signal for foldables only if a target device needs it.

features.summary: The message box in AGI Mobile chat. It starts at one line and grows to about six lines, then scrolls. An expand control opens a full-screen editor. Send, queue a follow-up while a reply streams, keep drafts after leaving, and keep the box above the keyboard. Mobile only.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person write, edit and send a message. Handles attachments staged in the box, queued follow-ups, draft saving, offline send rules and keyboard avoidance.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires a compact composer that grows, expands to a full-screen editor and sends (S71.02), and a keyboard-aware layout (S71.03). (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/071-mobile-application.md) The product requirements say the mobile composer must be multi-line, keyboard-safe and send on explicit action. (doc: docs/product/requirements.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who chats in AGI Mobile, in Local mode or Cloud mode.
problems_solved: A long message is hard to edit in a small box.
A reply in progress should not block the next thought.
Leaving a screen should not lose a typed message.
The keyboard must not hide the box.
use_cases: Type a short question and send it.
Paste a long email, tap expand, tidy it, send from the full-screen editor.
Type a follow-up while an answer is streaming; it sends when the answer ends.
Start a message in a chat, leave, come back and find the draft.

where_to_find_it: Mobile: bottom of every chat. Input has accessibility label 'Message input' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:2125-2130).
Expand control: label 'Expand message', hint 'Opens the message in a full-screen editor', top-right corner of the box (ChatInput.tsx:2136-2158).
Full-screen editor: input labelled 'Expanded message input' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ComposerFullScreenEditor.tsx:138).
Voice control: when the box is empty a button 'Start voice mode' replaces send (ChatInput.tsx:2278-2300; see F071-05).
prerequisites: A chat open. In Cloud mode, a signed-in account; usage allowance for Cloud turns.
For sending with files, see F071-04.
screens_and_controls: Text box with placeholder: 'What's on your mind?', 'Reply to AGI' while a thread is active or streaming, 'Work with AGI' in AGI Work mode, 'Type or hold to talk' when hold-to-talk is ready, an offline text when offline (ChatInput.tsx:1645-1662).
Plus control opens the Add to chat sheet.
Send button with states idle, streaming (acts as stop) and queued ('Sending when the upload finishes').
Queued follow-up rows 'Queued message N of M' with edit and cancel (ChatInput.tsx:1851-1905).
Expand and collapse controls for the full-screen editor.
journey: Tap the box. The keyboard opens and the chat and box move up.
Type. After the text wraps past about one and a half lines the expand control appears.
Optional: tap expand, edit in the full-screen editor, tap send there or collapse.
Tap send. The box clears at once; the message appears in the thread.
If a reply is streaming, sending queues the text as a follow-up row; it is sent when the stream ends.
If the send is refused, the text comes back into the box and the attachments are marked as not sent.
feedback_and_outputs: Light haptic on send when haptics are on (ChatInput.tsx:925-927).
Alert 'Pasted text not sent' or 'Pasted text not attached' on pasted-text failures (ChatInput.tsx:884-892, 1020-1024).
Alerts for missing files: 'File no longer available' (ChatInput.tsx:866-872).
Offline cloud alerts from the chat screen (see states).
settings: Haptics, auto-correct and spell check follow settings (ChatInput.tsx:2117-2118).
Keyboard behaviour is not user-configurable.

working: Box grows up to six lines (MAX_INPUT_LINES = 6, apps/mobile/lib/constants.ts:25; numberOfLines at ChatInput.tsx:2123) and is capped at 160 points high, then scrolls (ChatInput.tsx:2107).
Expand control shows only when the text is wrapped (more than 1.5 lines) and not while dictating or while the effort panel is open (ChatInput.tsx:150, 1533, 2136).

The full-screen editor owns no text; edits go up to the composer; it has send and collapse; keyboard avoidance with a Modal-safe mode (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ComposerFullScreenEditor.tsx:66-68; test:apps/mobile/__tests__/ComposerFullscreenEditor.test.tsx).
While streaming, send queues a follow-up; when the stream ends the first queued item is sent, and it returns to the box if refused (ChatInput.tsx:945-958, 1170-1195).
If the send opened a different conversation, the text typed after sending is prefilled into the new chat (ChatInput.tsx:1041-1068).
Drafts are stored on the device under keys 'composer-draft:' with the owner scope (local or cloud account) and attachment records (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/draftStore.ts:4, 148-186).
Keyboard: iOS pads; Android screens pad, modals shrink height; offset 0 (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/chrome/keyboardSafeComposer.ts:17-20, 40-50; apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:2282-2288).
Empty guard: nothing runs without trimmed text or an attachment (ChatInput.tsx:865).
A send held while an attachment uploads, sent when the upload settles (ChatInput.tsx:874-877, 1105-1118).
Send failure marks attachments sendFailed and restores the text (ChatInput.tsx:965-972, 1025-1040; flag cleared on the next attempt at ~1004-1006).
incomplete: Only the first queued follow-up is sent when a stream ends; later ones wait for the next stream end. (ChatInput.tsx:1172-1180) [inferred from the destructuring of the queue]
disconnected_or_disabled: Sending in AGI Work mode is blocked while usage recovery is owed (usageBlocked) (ChatInput.tsx:566, 863).
not_available: Web, Desktop, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not part of this feature.

established.statement: The composer starts as a one-line pill that grows up to a cap and can expand to a full-screen editor, then sends.
When the keyboard opens the chat screen and composer move above it rather than being covered.
Text input is multi-line capable, keyboard-safe and sends on explicit action; the composer must not resize or overlap badly on small devices; dark and light appearance.
Sending a file cannot cross Local to BYOK or Cloud without consent.

acceptance_criteria: Typing past one line grows the box; past six lines it stops growing and scrolls.
The expand control is absent for a one-line message and present for a wrapped message.
Send from the full-screen editor sends the same text and the box clears.
Sending while a reply streams shows a queued row, and the message sends after the reply ends.
Leaving the chat with text typed and returning shows the same text.
On iOS and Android the box stays fully visible with the keyboard open, in the main chat and in the full-screen editor.
Empty text with no attachment does nothing.
inferred: Local-mode chats treat the app as online so Local send never queues for the network. [inferred from isOnline={conversationExecutionMode === 'local' || isOnline} at apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:2751]
proposed: [proposed] Send all queued follow-ups in order, or show that only one goes at a time.
[proposed] Name the draft retention period.

features.summary: Actions on one message in AGI Mobile chat. Under a reply: Copy, Read aloud, Regenerate response, and a three-dot button. Long-press a message for the full menu: edit, resend, retry, branch, schedule, copy, select text, export, save as document, rate, report, delete. Double-tap a reply for a thumbs up.

steps.what_happens: A tap or long-press builds the action list from the message role, streaming state and passed handlers.
Copy and select text use the clipboard on the device.
Read aloud in Local uses the device speech engine; in Cloud it asks the server for a voice.
Rating in Cloud posts the rating and patches the message on our servers; Local keeps it in the device store.
Delete in Cloud removes the message on the server with rollback on failure; Local removes it on the device.
Export builds a PDF or text file on the device, then hands it to the OS share sheet.
Retry, Resend, Edit and Retry with Another Model start a new turn through the chat turn pipeline.

features.summary: Ways to put pictures, files and shared content into an AGI Mobile chat: the Add to chat sheet (Camera, Photos, Paste image, File, Library picks), an in-app camera page, and a share preview that opens when another app shares text, links, images or PDFs to AGI Mobile. Uploads do not resume by themselves.

purpose.what_it_does: Collects images and documents from the camera, the photo library, the Files app and the OS share sheet, checks them against mode and plan limits, and attaches them to the next message or starts a chat.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires camera intake, photo-picker intake, file-provider intake, share-sheet intake and background upload recovery (S71.06 to S71.09, S71.18). (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/071-mobile-application.md) Product requirements: selected files show chips, can be removed before send, and unsupported types show clear disabled states. (doc: docs/product/requirements.md M-US-004)
purpose.who_uses_it: People who want to ask about a photo, a document, or a web page they found in another app.
problems_solved: Ask about what the camera sees.
Send several photos at once.
Bring a PDF from a storage provider.
Send a link or selected text from a browser.
use_cases: Take a photo of a receipt and ask what it says.
Share a web page from the browser and tap 'Summarize this page'.
Attach a PDF from the Files app to a question.
Pick four photos from the library and compare them.

where_to_find_it: Mobile: the plus control in the composer opens the Add to chat sheet with rows 'Camera', 'Photos', 'Paste image', 'File' and Library picks (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:697-722, 831-854).
In-app camera page: route /(app)/camera, reached by intent links 'camera' and 'analyze_image' (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:216-217, 313-320). No visible button was found that opens it from the chat.
Share preview: opens after another app shares to 'AGI Mobile' (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:281-292, 827-845).
prerequisites: Camera and photo library permissions through the OS (purpose strings in apps/mobile/app.config.js:62-75).
Cloud sends need a signed-in account and Cloud consent (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/upload/uploadAttachment.ts:68-70).

Plus control, then Photos: pick one or more photos; the count is capped. They appear as chips.
Plus control, then File: pick one or more files; they are copied to the app cache and appear as chips.

Alternative: open the in-app camera page by an intent link; take a photo, review it, optionally type a question, send. With no chat open it starts a chat named 'Vision Analysis'. The default question is 'What do you see in this image?'.
From another app, Share to AGI Mobile. Check the preview. Tap 'Send to Chat' to start a chat with the text, or 'Add to chat' to stage files in the composer.
If an upload stops, tap retry on the chip.

Notice 'Content was truncated to 100 KB before sending.' (share-preview/index.tsx:44-46).
settings: Photos and Camera permission in the OS settings; the app offers Open Settings (chat/[id].tsx:1535-1538).
Image metadata is stripped before use; no setting.

working: The sheet's Camera opens the system camera through the image picker, then strips metadata; photos stage in the composer (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1521-1556; apps/mobile/src/features/media/photo-picker.ts:41-52).

Library photos: multi-select, ordered, with metadata removed (photo-picker.ts:26-39). Selection limit is the per-message file limit, or the plan photo limit when that is null (chat/[id].tsx:1575-1595; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/photoSelectionLimit.ts:3-5).

Paste image from clipboard (chat/[id].tsx:1558-1573).

Validation: empty files rejected; size ceilings by mode; denied extensions; HEIC refused in Cloud with advice; Local refuses Office types (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/attachmentValidation.ts:34-47, 100-126).

Cloud uploads: POST /api/uploads/presign then transfer, up to 2 retries with 1 s, 2 s waits, consent first (apps/mobile/services/api.ts:700-715; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/upload/uploadAttachment.ts:15-18, 68-83).

Shared text is cut to 100 KB, tags stripped and wrapped in <shared_via_intent> so the model reads it as data (share-preview/index.tsx:43-66).

incomplete: Interrupted uploads are only marked: when the app goes to the background in-flight uploads get an interrupted flag; the person must tap retry. No automatic resume was found. (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:1144-1147; uploadLifecycle.ts:116-130; AttachmentPreview.tsx:185)
The in-app camera page has no visible entry from the chat; it is reached by intent links. (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:216-217, 313-320)
disconnected_or_disabled: Android App Intents and quick actions are listed as not applicable in the brief (S71.23); the intent verbs camera, ask and summarize in _layout.tsx do exist but how they are launched was not traced.
not_available: Automatic upload resume on any app (S71.18).
Web, Desktop, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not part of this feature.

established.statement: The user can take a photo with the phone camera and it is attached to (or sent in) a chat.
The user can pick up to several photos from the system photo library and they attach to the message.
The user can attach a file from the OS document picker to a chat.
Sharing text, links, images or PDFs to the app opens a preview that starts a chat or stages the files.
An attachment upload interrupted by backgrounding continues or resumes automatically when the app returns. The brief marks this not applicable anywhere.
Selected files show chips, removal before send works, unsupported types show clear states, and sending a file cannot cross Local to BYOK or Cloud without consent.

acceptance_criteria: Camera, Photos, Paste image and File each add chips or show an alert that explains why not.
A denied camera permission shows 'Camera Access' with an Open Settings button.
In Cloud, selecting more files than the limit rejects the extras with a message naming the limit.
In Local, Office files are refused with advice to use Cloud.
Sharing 200 KB of text shows the truncation notice and sends at most 100 KB.
'Summarize this page' appears only when the shared text holds a web link.
An offline Cloud send with a photo keeps the photo and the text and shows the alert.
Backgrounding mid-upload leaves a chip with a retry control after return.
inferred: Upload interruption leaves the chip in a failed state until the request errors; the phase is not changed by the background flag alone. [inferred from uploadLifecycle.ts:116-130]
proposed: [proposed] Resume or restart interrupted Cloud uploads on return to the foreground, or record S71.18 as intentionally manual.
[proposed] Add a visible entry to the in-app camera or retire it in favour of the sheet camera.

features.summary: Talking to the assistant in AGI Mobile. In a signed-in Cloud chat a live two-way session runs through AGI Cloud. In Local chats, or when signed out, a turn-based bar listens with on-device speech recognition. A separate voice screen has an orb and push-to-talk. On iOS the person can choose the audio output route.

purpose.what_it_does: Starts hands-free voice. Live mode streams audio both ways over a real-time connection with tool calls and approvals. Turn-based mode turns speech into text on the phone, sends it to the selected model and speaks the answer.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants a full-duplex spoken conversation inside a chat (S71.10) and audio output route choice (S71.11). (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/071-mobile-application.md) The product requirements ask the app to tell dictation from live voice and show why voice is unavailable. (doc: docs/product/requirements.md M-US-005)
purpose.who_uses_it: People who want hands-free chat, for example while walking or driving, in Cloud or Local mode.
problems_solved: Typing is hard on the move.
People want to interrupt the assistant while it talks.
Voice should still work offline for Local answers.
use_cases: Tap Start voice mode in a Cloud chat and talk naturally, interrupting the reply.
Use turn-based voice in a Local chat with no signed-in account.
Switch to the speaker or a Bluetooth headset on iOS during a live call.
Hold the orb to talk and release to send.

where_to_find_it: Mobile chat composer: when the box is empty the send slot shows the control 'Start voice mode' (hint 'Opens hands-free voice conversation') (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:2278-2300). It is hidden when voice mode is not available on the device (chat/[id].tsx:2747).
Voice screen: route /(app)/voice, from Settings voice (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/voice/index.tsx:519) or the 'voice' intent link (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:218-224).

Live bar controls: 'Mute microphone' / 'Unmute microphone', 'Type instead' (label 'Switch to text for this chat'), 'End live voice', 'Try live voice again', 'Type a message instead' (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/LiveVoiceBar.tsx:397-418, 704-746).
Audio route picker inside the live bar, iOS only (LiveVoiceBar.tsx:721; apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/AudioRoutePicker.tsx).
prerequisites: Microphone permission; speech recognition permission on iOS (apps/mobile/app.config.js:166-170).

Live mode: a signed-in account, a Cloud chat, a native build with the real-time module, an HTTPS server, and the voice capability on (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts:21-45).
Turn-based mode: on-device recognizer; on Android needs API level 33 or higher (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/voiceInput.ts:289-292).
screens_and_controls: First use: an onboarding sheet, then a voice picker sheet (chat/[id].tsx:1720-1745).
Live bar: transcript, orb, call time, captions, pause, mute, 'Type instead', 'End live voice', tool approval Allow and Deny, 'Stop the task and keep talking'.
Turn-based inline bar: 'Start listening', mute, keyboard and exit controls (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/components/VoiceInlineBar.tsx:41-45).

Voice screen: orb with phase text 'Tap to speak', 'Listening...', 'Thinking...', 'Speaking...', in push-to-talk 'Hold to talk' and 'Release to send', a typed composer, a toggle 'Switch to push-to-talk mode' / 'Switch to hands-free mode' (apps/mobile/app/(app)/voice.tsx:65-95, 495-515, 673).
journey: Tap Start voice mode. First time: read the intro, choose a voice, continue.
In a signed-in Cloud chat the live bar opens and connects. Otherwise the inline bar opens, with a notice such as 'Live voice runs in AGI Cloud, so Local Mode stays turn based.'
Speak. The orb and captions follow; in live mode you may interrupt.
In live mode the assistant may call tools; approve or deny when asked.
End with 'End live voice' or leave the screen. The session closes and its minutes settle.
On a dropped connection the bar says 'Reconnecting live voice...' and retries up to 3 times.
feedback_and_outputs: Phase and status text in the bar: 'Reconnecting live voice...', 'Muted, tap the mic to talk', 'Speaking, talk any time to interrupt', 'Listening' (LiveVoiceBar.tsx:166-179).
Voice screen thinking line: 'Sending to AGI Cloud' for a Cloud model or 'Answering on this device' (voice.tsx:90-95).
Messages for failures: 'Microphone access was denied. Allow the microphone to use live voice.', 'The live voice connection could not be established.' and others (liveVoiceAvailability.ts:5-15).
Audio route notice: 'Could not switch audio to <route>. This call may use a different output.' (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/audioRoute.ts:70-72).
settings: Settings, Voice: input on or off, push-to-talk, speech language, voice and preview (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/voice/index.tsx).
Audio route stored as audioRoute in the settings store: Automatic, Speaker, Bluetooth, Headset (audioRoute.ts:8-25).

working: Live eligibility: only an execution mode of Cloud and a signed-in user; otherwise a reason string and the turn-based bar (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceAvailability.ts:21-28; apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:1697-1718).

Live session over WebRTC: offer sent to POST /api/voice/live/sessions, answer applied, data channel for events; ICE gathering waits up to 10 s; tool calls time out after 20 s (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceSession.ts:30, 37, 343; liveVoiceAuthority.ts:14).
Microphone denial and connection failures map to specific messages (liveVoiceSession.ts:171-176).

Reconnect: up to 3 attempts with 1 s, 2 s, 4 s waits; time extension requested before the budget ends; session settled on close (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/hooks/useLiveVoiceSession.ts:66-72, 229-293, 405-430).

Server session start checks rate limit, entitlement bundle, capability canUseVoice, plan voice permission, a voice budget (402) and a voice-minutes allowance, and opt-out of training rules (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:178-380).

Turn-based voice: on-device recognition is required (requiresOnDeviceRecognition true) and never falls back to server recognition (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/voiceInput.ts:306-312, 438, 493).
Voice screen: orb, phase labels, push-to-talk, typed fallback and file import; it ends the conversation on close (apps/mobile/app/(app)/voice.tsx:65-95, 395-425).

Audio route selection exists: four routes, iOS only, applied through the audio session category, shown in the live bar, with tests (audioRoute.ts:1-80; LiveVoiceBar.tsx:721). This contradicts the brief status 'not applicable'.

Plan or switch gate: starting voice checks the canUseVoice capability and shows 'Voice is unavailable' with the text 'It's paused while we fix an issue and will come back without an update.' when off (chat/[id].tsx:1697-1700; apps/mobile/src/lib/Capabilities.tsx:156-157).
incomplete: On Android below API 33 the voice button is hidden for chats that need turn-based voice, and startVoiceMode returns without a message if reached (chat/[id].tsx:1706; voiceInput.ts:289-292).
Audio route picker is absent on Android: audioRouteSwitchingSupported is true only on iOS (audioRoute.ts:56-58).
disconnected_or_disabled: Live voice also needs a native WebRTC module; without it the app says 'Live voice needs a native build of this app, so voice stays turn based here.' (liveVoiceAvailability.ts:5-15, 36-42).
not_available: Audio route choice on Android.
Voice on Web, Desktop, CLI, VS Code, Chrome is a separate feature; not part of this page.

established.statement: The user can hold a full-duplex spoken conversation with the assistant inside a chat.
During voice the user can choose the audio output route (speaker, Bluetooth, headset) and the session switches. The brief marks this not applicable anywhere.
The app distinguishes dictation from live voice; permission prompts use native expectations; if live voice is unavailable the app says so without broken controls.
Local inference on mobile is free of any paid subscription; sign-in is a separate question.
established.source: Product context given to this task

acceptance_criteria: Start voice mode in a signed-in Cloud chat opens the live bar and a spoken question gets a spoken answer.
In a Local chat the same control opens the turn-based bar with the notice naming Local mode.
With the microphone denied, a clear message appears and nothing is left recording.
Dropping the network shows 'Reconnecting live voice...' and ends in an error with 'Try live voice again' after 3 failures.
On iOS the audio route picker shows four routes and a switch changes the output; on Android no picker shows.
With the voice capability off, the control shows 'Voice is unavailable'.
Ending the session settles minutes and no further audio is sent.
inferred: Voice in Local mode should not depend on a paid plan; the code checks canUseVoice for every mode, so a plan document that denies voice would also stop Local voice. [inferred from chat/[id].tsx:1648, 1697-1700 and useCapability in apps/mobile/src/lib/Capabilities.tsx:126-134]
proposed: [proposed] Skip the plan capability check for on-device voice and keep the operator switch only.
[proposed] Show a message when Android below API 33 cannot start turn-based voice instead of hiding or ignoring the tap.

steps.what_happens: The person taps Start voice mode; the app checks the capability, mode and sign-in.
Live: the app asks for Cloud consent, opens the microphone, creates a WebRTC offer and posts it to our servers.
Our server picks the live model from a routing slot, checks plan and budget, reserves usage, and returns an answer to the offer.
Audio flows between the phone and the live model service; the provider behind the slot is chosen by our server.
steps.evidence: route.ts:191-210 (slot resolves to a managed provider); provider name not established

steps.what_happens: Tool calls from the live model go through our server's tool route and may wait for approval on the phone.
Turn-based: speech is recognised on the phone, sent as a normal chat turn to the selected model, and the answer is spoken.
steps.evidence: voice.tsx:272; voiceInput.ts:438, 493; reply source depends on mode (Local on device, Cloud on our servers)

steps.what_happens: On close the session settles minutes with our servers.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Live voice uses a model chosen on the server by a routing slot named in the route code, and a backend reasoning model chosen by plan (route.ts:185-230, 319-321). The provider is not named in the mobile code. Turn-based voice uses whichever chat model is selected, Local or Cloud (voice.tsx:90-95). Recognition is always on the device.

access_and_usage.account: Live voice: signed in (liveVoiceAvailability.ts:25-27). Turn-based: none in Local.
access_and_usage.permissions: Microphone (all modes); speech recognition permission on iOS; Bluetooth route selection uses the audio session (app.config.js:166-170; audioRoute.ts).
access_and_usage.subscription: Server checks the canUseVoice capability, plan voice permission (403) and voice budget (402) and voice minutes allowance; a free allowance path exists for some plans (route.ts:296-380). The phone also checks canUseVoice before starting any voice (chat/[id].tsx:1648, 1697-1700).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Voice minutes are metered per session in blocks with extensions requested before the budget ends (useLiveVoiceSession.ts:262-293; route.ts:366-372). Route rate limit 'voice-live-session' (route.ts:178).
access_and_usage.flags: Operator switch for canUseVoice (Capabilities.tsx:126-157); FEATURES flags not used by the live hook in the lines read.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Live model comes from the server slot and must keep inputs out of training when the account demands it (route.ts:325-338). Turn-based works with any chat model.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Server refuses a model that may train on user data in some cases ('model_may_train', 403) (route.ts:325-338). Provider choice is not in the app.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Turn-based voice with on-device recognition and a device voice; the answer comes from the Local model. Live mode is refused with 'Live voice runs in AGI Cloud, so Local Mode stays turn based.' The canUseVoice capability check still applies [inferred gap].

features.summary: Alerts from AGI Mobile. A signed-in phone registers a push address with AGI Cloud, which sends alerts for agent runs, research, schedules, chat replies and product updates through Expo's push service. Local notices such as 'Your reply is ready' are made on the phone. A tap opens the matching screen from an allow list.

purpose.what_it_does: Registers the device, shows alerts according to priority, account and user preferences, keeps a list of past alerts and routes taps to chats, tasks, schedules, reports and settings.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires push registration with server storage and pushes for agent, research and schedule events (S71.12), and deep links that open the right screen (S71.13). (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/071-mobile-application.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: People who start long tasks or scheduled work and want to be told when they finish or need approval.
problems_solved: Long runs finish while the app is closed.
An agent waits for approval.
Alerts for another account must not leak.
A tap must land on the right screen.
use_cases: An agent run finishes; the phone buzzes and a tap opens it.
A scheduled task completes; tap opens Schedules.
Leave a Local chat while it answers; a notice says 'Your reply is ready'.
Open the Notifications list to see missed alerts.

where_to_find_it: Mobile: Settings, Notifications (title 'Notifications') with a card 'Turn on notifications' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/notifications/index.tsx:168-190, 362).
Notifications list screen at /(app)/notifications with 'Mark all as read', 'Clear All' and 'No notifications yet.' (apps/mobile/app/(app)/notifications/index.tsx:344-431).
The menu button shows an unread pip (apps/mobile/src/shared/components/DrawerButton.tsx:77-95).
prerequisites: OS notification permission, requested only from the explicit enable button (apps/mobile/services/notifications.ts:202-221).
Remote push needs a signed-in account (apps/mobile/src/features/auth/hooks/usePushTokenAccountRegistration.ts:28-63).
A build with push entitlements; without them registration is skipped (notifications.ts:277-285).
screens_and_controls: Permission card with states: delivering, 'Turn on notifications', 'Your device is blocking notifications' (Open Settings), and 'AGI Cloud alerts cannot reach this device' for registration failures (settings/notifications/index.tsx:168-193).
Category rows with Push or Off or Blocked, quiet hours, vibration toggles, daily brief and usage reset reminders (settings/notifications/index.tsx:254-700).
Notification list: mark all read, clear on this device, tap an item to open.
journey: Open Settings, Notifications. Read the card that says what AGI will send.
Tap 'Turn on notifications'. The OS prompt appears once.
The app registers the push address with AGI Cloud with a device id and preferences.
Choose categories and quiet hours; changes sync to the server after about 0.8 s.
When an event happens an alert arrives. Tap it. The app opens the matching screen or the Notifications list.
If notifications are blocked, the card offers Open Settings.
feedback_and_outputs: Banner, sound or badge according to priority (notifications.ts:101-160).

steps.what_happens: The person taps Turn on notifications; the OS asks once.
The phone asks Expo for a push token using the project id.
The phone posts token, device id, platform, name and preferences to our servers.
Our server saves them in public.mobile_devices after a rate limit, CSRF check and ownership check.
An event happens on our servers; a producer service calls sendPushToUser, which picks devices that accept the notice now.
The server posts batches to Expo's push endpoint; Expo delivers through the platform push services.
The phone's handler decides banner, sound and badge, then stores the alert in the history.
A tap runs handleNotificationResponse and navigates with a retry until the router is ready.

features.summary: On the phone, a signed-in Cloud user opens the AGI Work screen, starts a cloud agent task with a goal, follows its runs in a list, answers the agent's question and approves or denies a pending action. Following a coding session on a paired desktop exists in code but is switched off.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person on the AGI Mobile app start an agent task that runs in AGI Cloud, watch its status and output, answer a question the agent asks, and approve or deny an action the agent wants to take. The run resumes or stops after the decision. A second, separate path for reviewing a coding session running on a paired computer is built but switched off (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:16; apps/mobile/app/(app)/companion/code/[threadId].tsx:81).
purpose.why_it_exists: Agent runs can take long and pause for the person. The brief says the user must be able to start a cloud task, answer questions and approve actions from the phone (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/071-mobile-application.md S71.14, S71.15, S71.17). The in-app list is the place where blocked runs are found.

A second device answering first is explained instead of failing silently (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/service.ts:23).

A push alert says an action is waiting; open the task and tap Approve.

established.statement: The user can answer an agent's question from the phone, by notification reply or a quick answer field.
The user can approve or deny a pending agent action from the phone and the run resumes accordingly.
The user can follow a coding session running elsewhere, review changed files and diffs, then steer or approve.
The user can start a cloud agent task from the phone and follow it in the task list.
Mobile has a Work surface at apps/mobile/app/(app)/tasks.tsx.

acceptance_criteria: With the capability granted, 'New task' is visible and an empty goal keeps 'Start task' disabled.
Starting a task with a goal creates a run that appears in the list and opens in the detail sheet.
A run waiting for approval shows Approve and Deny; Approve resumes it, Deny stops that action, and a failure shows 'Your decision could not be sent'.
A run asking a question shows the form; 'Send answer' submits and the run continues.
If another device answers first, the phone says 'Another device already answered this one'.
Without Cloud mode or sign-in, the screen offers the switch or sign-in and shows no runs.
With companion and dispatch off, no remote-coding control is reachable.
inferred: The same decision rules should hold for push-opened runs and list-opened runs, because both use openRun [inferred from apps/mobile/app/(app)/tasks.tsx:11-18].
Answer-in-notification is required by the brief but not built [inferred from the brief wording against apps/mobile/services/notificationCategories.ts].
proposed: [proposed] Add a text-reply notification action for simple questions, or change the brief to 'open the app to answer'.
[proposed] When several approvals are pending, send the person to the list filtered by Needs you.
