features.summary: AGI Mobile can be started from the iOS home screen widget, the iOS 18 control, Siri and Spotlight phrases, and the Android widget and icon shortcuts. Each opens the app on chat, camera, voice or another screen. Live Activity and Android default-assistant do not exist in the code.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the phone operating system ways to start AGI without opening the app first: a home screen widget with New chat, Camera and Voice, a control for Control Center, the lock screen or the Action Button (iOS 18 and later), Siri and Spotlight phrases for eight actions, and Android launcher shortcuts and a widget (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIWidgets/AGIWidgets.swift; apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/AppShortcuts.swift; apps/mobile/native/android/shortcuts/agi_shortcuts.xml).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires widgets, lock-screen widgets, Live Activity, system shortcuts and default-assistant integration (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/071-mobile-application.md S71.20-S71.24).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyday phone users who want one-tap or voice start; iOS users for Siri and Spotlight, iOS and Android users for widgets.
problems_solved: Starting a chat or the camera takes one tap from outside the app.
Asking a question by voice without opening the app (Ask AGI, Cloud only).
Setup help is in the app under Quick Access.
use_cases: Tap Camera on the widget to ask about a photo.
Say 'Summarize with AGI Mobile' to open the summary screen with text filled in.
Long-press the Android icon and choose Voice.
Add the iOS 18 control to the lock screen to open the app.

where_to_find_it: Mobile iOS: widget named 'AGI Mobile' (small and medium) from the widget gallery; control 'Open AGI Mobile' on iOS 18 or later (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIWidgets/AGIWidgets.swift).
Mobile iOS: Siri and Spotlight short titles Start Chat, Ask AGI, Summarize, Analyze Image, Transcribe, Translate, Scan, Set Reminder (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/AppShortcuts.swift).

Mobile Android: widget labelled 'AGI Mobile' (home screen category) and long-press shortcuts New chat, Voice, Camera (apps/mobile/native/android/widget/agi_widget_values.xml; apps/mobile/native/android/shortcuts/agi_shortcut_values.xml).
In the app: Settings row 'Quick Access' opens a 'Quick Access' page with steps (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:714-718; apps/mobile/src/features/widget-setup/index.tsx:142).
Ask from Siri switch: Settings, Account security screen, iOS only (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/account-security/index.tsx:579; apps/mobile/src/features/siri/askIntentToken.ts:113-115).
prerequisites: A build that includes the widget and intents plugins (apps/mobile/app.config.js:478-482).

Ask AGI also needs Cloud mode, a signed-in account and the Ask from Siri switch on (apps/mobile/src/features/siri/AskFromSiriSetting.tsx:36-60; apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/AskAGIIntent.swift:34-42).
Voice from the widget needs on-device speech to be guaranteed, otherwise it opens chat (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:219-225).
screens_and_controls: iOS widget small: tap anywhere for a new chat. Medium: three buttons New chat, Camera, Voice (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIWidgets/AGIWidgets.swift:46-72).
Android widget: three buttons wired to the same links (apps/mobile/native/android/widget/AGIQuickActionsWidget.kt).

Quick Access page sections Siri & Shortcuts, Share Sheet, Home Screen Widget, and on Android also Share From Any App, Act On Selected Text, App Shortcuts, Links Open In The App (apps/mobile/src/features/widget-setup/index.tsx:169-306).
journey: Add the widget or control from the system, or ask Siri.
The system opens agiworkforce://intent/<verb> (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/AGIIntentDispatch.swift:20-45).
The app root layout routes the verb to chat, camera, voice, summarize, translate, scan, analyze, transcribe or reminder screens (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:202-330).
The person continues in that screen.
feedback_and_outputs: Ask AGI replies by Siri speech or text with the answer, or one of the messages 'Ask from Siri is off...', 'Ask from Siri needs to be set up again...', 'AGI Mobile could not answer right now. Try again in the app.', 'Ask a shorter question.' (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/AskAGIIntent.swift:34-45).
Ask AGI answers are saved as a chat tagged source siri (apps/web/lib/server/mobile-intent.ts:81).
settings: Ask from Siri switch (label 'Ask from Siri'; description 'Ask AGI through Siri and hear the answer, saved as a chat.') (apps/mobile/src/features/siri/AskFromSiriSetting.tsx:61-67).
Quick Access page (help only).

working: iOS widget extension with a quick actions widget (small, medium) and a control widget on iOS 18 or later (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIWidgets/AGIWidgets.swift:6-8, 66-72).
Eight App Shortcuts with phrases (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/AppShortcuts.swift).

Intent dispatch builds agiworkforce://intent/<verb> URLs and opens them; files are staged into caches and images re-encoded (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/AGIIntentDispatch.swift:20-45, 60-100).
The root layout handles the verbs chat, camera, voice, ask, summarize, remind, share, translate, scan, analyze_image, transcribe (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:202-330).

Ask AGI runs without opening the app, calls POST /api/mobile/intent/ask with a stored token, and the server applies entitlements, safety checks and usage reservation (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/AskAGIIntent.swift:11, 30-65; apps/web/app/api/mobile/intent/ask/route.ts; apps/web/lib/server/mobile-intent.ts:116-176).

Android shortcuts (New chat, Voice, Camera) and the widget are registered by config plugins (apps/mobile/app.config.js:478-482; apps/mobile/native/android/withAGIShortcuts.cjs:9-15; apps/mobile/native/android/withAGIWidget.cjs:9-12).

Android 'Summarize', 'Ask' and the other verbs have no Android shortcut or widget; only chat, camera, voice are exposed on Android (apps/mobile/native/android/shortcuts/agi_shortcuts.xml).
disconnected_or_disabled: Lock screen widgets by widget family are not defined: the quick actions widget supports only small and medium (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIWidgets/AGIWidgets.swift:90). Only the iOS 18 control is described as available on the Lock Screen (same file, control description).
Whether the widget and control appear for a given build is determined by the plugin run at prebuild; no run was observed.
not_available: Live Activity or ongoing notification for agent tasks or voice: no ActivityKit or equivalent code found (searched apps/mobile app, src, native, services, stores).
Default digital assistant on Android: no assist or voice-command intent filter or service found (searched apps/mobile/native/android and apps/mobile/app.config.js).
Android widget on the lock screen: widget category is home_screen only (apps/mobile/native/android/widget/agi_quick_actions_widget_info.xml).
Desktop, Web, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not part of this feature.

established.statement: The user can add an AGI widget to the home screen that opens or starts a chat.
Where the OS supports it the user can place an AGI widget on the lock screen.
Where supported, a running agent task or voice session shows as a Live Activity or ongoing notification with progress.
OS-level shortcuts (Siri/App Intents, Spotlight, launcher shortcuts) can start AGI actions such as ask or summarize.
On Android the user can set AGI as the default digital assistant so the assist gesture opens it.
The widget page and Siri use the same agiworkforce://intent scheme (code rank 2 over docs).

acceptance_criteria: The widget gallery lists the AGI widget; tapping New chat, Camera and Voice opens chat, camera and voice or chat when speech is not guaranteed.
On iOS 18 the control can be added and opens the app.
Each of the eight phrases triggers its intent from Siri or Spotlight.
Ask AGI with the switch off answers with the 'Ask from Siri is off' message.
Android icon long-press lists New chat, Voice and Camera.
No Live Activity and no assistant role is offered (matches code today).
inferred: Each iOS intent that opens the app must have a matching case in the root layout; the eight verbs do [inferred from AGIIntentDispatch.swift and app/_layout.tsx:202-330].
Android needs no Ask equivalent until a similar token path exists [inferred: askFromSiriSupported returns true only on iOS].
proposed: [proposed] Add accessory widget families so the same buttons can sit on the iOS lock screen.
[proposed] Decide whether Live Activity and default assistant remain requirements; if yes, plan the native work; if no, remove S71.22 and S71.24 from the brief.

steps.what_happens: Person taps a widget button or says a phrase; the OS runs the widget link or intent.
The intent opens agiworkforce://intent/<verb>?<params>; no network is used here.
The root layout parses the link and pushes the matching screen.
For Ask AGI, the intent reads the keychain token and posts the prompt to /api/mobile/intent/ask with a 55 second timeout.
The server checks token, MFA and IP rules, age, safety, plan entitlement and usage, picks a route, generates the answer and saves a chat.
The model call goes to the provider the route selects.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Ask AGI uses a server route chosen by the unattended route selector for the account's plan; models are not named in the intent code (apps/web/lib/server/mobile-intent.ts:181-205). Other verbs open the app and use whichever mode the app is in.

access_and_usage.account: Widgets and shortcuts need no account to open the app. Ask AGI needs a signed-in Cloud account (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/AskAGIIntent.swift:34-35).
access_and_usage.permissions: The Ask token is stored in the keychain. Camera and microphone permissions apply once the target screen opens (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/permissions/registry.ts).
access_and_usage.subscription: Ask AGI resolves the entitlement bundle and refuses when the plan does not allow it (apps/web/lib/server/mobile-intent.ts:155-176).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Prompt max 2,000 characters on device (AskAGIIntent.swift:41); rate limit 'mobile-intent-ask' per token (apps/web/app/api/mobile/intent/ask/route.ts:28); usage is reserved and released (apps/web/lib/server/mobile-intent.ts:205-270).
access_and_usage.flags: Ask from Siri switch; the widget and shortcuts have no runtime flag. Plugins are always registered (apps/mobile/app.config.js:478-482).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Server route only; Ask refuses when no model keeps chats out of training (apps/web/lib/server/mobile-intent.ts:41, 189).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Consent to cloud provider sharing is required to enable Ask (apps/mobile/src/features/siri/AskFromSiriSetting.tsx:37-40; apps/mobile/src/features/siri/askIntentToken.ts:191).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Widget, control and shortcuts open the app in whichever mode it is in. Ask AGI is Cloud only: the switch is disabled in Local mode unless already on (apps/mobile/src/features/siri/AskFromSiriSetting.tsx:62-68).

features.summary: In AGI Mobile, a person downloads a model and chats with it on the device without Cloud or payment. The Storage screen shows what AGI uses, lets them remove a model, clear the cache or delete all local data, and holds the cellular download switch.

purpose.what_it_does: Downloads on-device models (Wi-Fi by default), runs chats with them locally, and shows and frees the space they use. It also offers a full device wipe (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/storage.tsx; apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/installStore.ts; apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:3037-3050).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires visible storage and removal controls (S71.28), a cellular preference (S71.29) and local chat without the cloud (S71.30). Local inference is free of any paid subscription (product rule in the task brief).
purpose.who_uses_it: Mobile users who chat offline or privately, and anyone short of space.
problems_solved: Models are several gigabytes; people need to see and remove them.
Mobile data is not used unless allowed.
One place to wipe data from the device.
use_cases: Download a model in onboarding over Wi-Fi.
Remove an unused model to free space.
Clear cache after exporting files.
Delete everything before handing over a phone.

where_to_find_it: Mobile: Settings, General, Storage; also from Data controls and from the settings home (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/general/index.tsx:197; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/index.tsx:442; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:741). Screen title 'Storage' (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/storage.tsx:381).

Model download: onboarding device-tier card ('Download model' button, 'Download over cellular too' switch) (apps/mobile/app/(public)/onboarding.tsx:746-770) and the model picker sheet (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/components/ModelPickerSheet.tsx).
prerequisites: No sign-in or plan for Local mode (see access).
A device that can run the chosen model; some are locked for low RAM or no native runtime (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/installStore.ts:117-190).
screens_and_controls: Summary line 'AGI uses X of Y on this device' with a meter, or 'Measuring…' (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/storage.tsx:112-139).
Card 'On This Device': 'Downloaded models (estimated)', 'Cache', 'Free space', and 'Try again' on failure.
Switch 'Download over cellular' ('Off waits for Wi-Fi. Models are several gigabytes.').
Card 'Downloaded Models' with a trash button per model.
Privacy card: 'Export all my data', 'Clear cache'.
Danger Zone: 'Delete everything'.
journey: Open Storage and read the totals.
To remove a model, tap its trash icon; confirm 'Delete <name>?'.
To clear cache, tap 'Clear cache' and confirm.
To wipe, tap 'Delete everything', confirm 'Delete all local data?' then 'Are you absolutely sure?'.
To download, choose a model in onboarding or the picker, optionally turn on the cellular switch, tap Download.
feedback_and_outputs: 'Deleting all local data…' overlay during a wipe (storage.tsx:311-322).
Alerts 'Model removal failed', 'Storage refresh failed', 'Wipe failed' (storage.tsx:170-185; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/useEraseDeviceData.ts:33-36).
Download errors with the real cause, such as 'This download needs Wi-Fi...' or a storage-full message (apps/mobile/services/modelDownload.ts:194-225).
settings: Download over cellular (persisted) (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/installStore.ts:379-384, 641).

working: Install states ready, download_required, downloading, failed, unavailable, locked (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/installStore.ts:56-57).

Wi-Fi only by default; cellular allowed only after the switch; the check reads the live network type before every download (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/installStore.ts:379, 521; apps/mobile/services/modelDownload.ts:194-209).
Free space is checked before the first byte with a 256 MB headroom (apps/mobile/services/modelDownload.ts:189-225).

Three install paths: GGUF files (llama.rn runtime), ExecuTorch presets, and OS system models that need no download (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/installStore.ts:117-215, 521-560; apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/localModelRuntime.ts).

features.summary: After the phone closes AGI Mobile, chats and unsent drafts are still stored on the device. If a Cloud reply was still being written, the app asks the server whether it finished, restores the answer, or says it stopped. The code does not reopen the last chat on its own after a cold start.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps chat messages and the unsent draft in encrypted phone storage, marks a reply that was streaming as stopped when the store reloads, and for Cloud chats asks the server what happened to the turn (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatMessageStore.ts:411-417, 1729-1748; apps/mobile/src/features/chat/inFlightTurnRecovery.ts).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief: after the OS kills the app, relaunching returns the user to their conversation with messages, draft and any in-flight reply (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/071-mobile-application.md S71.19).
purpose.who_uses_it: All Mobile users, in particular those who switch apps while a long Cloud answer is running.
problems_solved: No lost typing.
No chat lost to an OS kill.
No second paid answer for a turn the server is still working on.
use_cases: Type a long message, switch apps, come back after the OS closed AGI: draft is there.
Start a Cloud answer, lock the phone for a minute: the chat shows the finished answer or 'Waiting for the answer'.
A server run dies: the chat says the turn stopped.

where_to_find_it: Mobile only. Automatic; no setting. Recovery happens inside an open chat screen (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:469).
Draft appears in the chat composer (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx:462, 752).
prerequisites: Cloud recovery needs a Cloud chat and a network (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/inFlightTurnRecovery.ts:65-70, 176-185).
Storage must open; if the encrypted store cannot open, the root layout reports it (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:580-600).
screens_and_controls: Chat thread and composer; message shows a stopped state when interrupted; waiting text shown as an error line when you try to continue (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:5103).
journey: Use a chat; the app saves messages and draft as you go.
The OS closes the app.
Open AGI again; the app starts on the chat tab (apps/mobile/app/index.tsx:9-25; apps/mobile/app/(app)/index.tsx:4).
Open the chat from the list; messages and draft load from storage.
If it is a Cloud chat with an unfinished turn, the app asks the server and shows the answer, a waiting state, or the stopped message.
feedback_and_outputs: 'Waiting for the answer. It appears here when it is ready.' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/inFlightTurnRecovery.ts:20-21).
'This turn stopped running on the server and will not finish. Send it again to retry.' (inFlightTurnRecovery.ts:19-20).

working: Local chats persist to 'chat-message-store-local' and Cloud chats to 'chat-message-store-cloud' in the encrypted key-value store (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatMessageStore.ts:1729; apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatCloudMessageStore.ts:313; apps/mobile/lib/mmkv.ts:61).
Stores rehydrate after encryption opens (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatMessageStore.ts:2075).

A streaming assistant message is saved as stopped with finishReason 'stopped' in the local store (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatMessageStore.ts:411-417, 1745); the cloud store drops streaming messages from the saved copy (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatCloudMessageStore.ts:351-352).
Cloud store keeps up to 200 chats and 100 messages each, plus unsynced ones (chatCloudMessageStore.ts:325-326).
Drafts with attachments are saved under the 'composer-draft:' key prefix (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/draftStore.ts:5, 186).

In-flight recovery: asks the server for the conversation's runs, follows a recorded run, restores a finished answer, or decides running, waiting or stalled (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/inFlightTurnRecovery.ts:65-300).
Stall deadline 150 seconds and re-check every 5 seconds; re-asks when the app returns to the front or the network returns (inFlightTurnRecovery.ts:17-18, 186-200).
Continuing a Cloud answer first asks the server and refuses with the waiting message when the turn still runs (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:5095-5105).
incomplete: No code was found that reopens the last open chat after a cold start; the root route goes to the chat tab (apps/mobile/app/index.tsx; apps/mobile/app/(app)/index.tsx:4). The saved current conversation id is cleared when the chat screen unmounts (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:571-577). The brief's 'returns the user to their conversation' is therefore not established.
Only Cloud chats are checked against the server; an interrupted Local turn has no server and stays stopped (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/inFlightTurnRecovery.ts:65-70).

not_available: Other apps: n/a. Background upload recovery is a separate item and not applicable (doc: area brief S71.18).

established.statement: After the OS kills the app, relaunching returns the user to their conversation with messages, draft and any in-flight reply.
The phone does not keep writing an interrupted reply itself; it checks the server and shows what the server has.
Local, own key and Cloud are separate; nothing silently moves a Local chat to Cloud.

acceptance_criteria: After killing the app, a previously sent message and its chat are present.
An unsent draft is present in the same chat's composer.
A Cloud reply that finished on the server appears without resending.
A reply still running shows the waiting state, and resending is refused with the waiting message.
A turn with no sign of life for 150 seconds shows the stopped message.
A Local reply interrupted by the kill is marked stopped, not left spinning.

steps.what_happens: Messages and drafts are written to encrypted storage as the person uses the app.
On relaunch the storage key is opened, then stores rehydrate; streaming messages are settled as stopped.
Opening a Cloud chat whose last row is an unanswered question or an unfinished run starts the check.
The phone asks GET runs?conversationId=<id> and, with a recorded run id, reads the finished answer.
Finished: answer restored, or history reloaded. Running: re-check every 5 seconds. No life for 150 seconds: stalled message.

features.summary: AGI Mobile can require Face ID, a fingerprint or the device passcode when it opens or returns from the background, and it covers the screen while away so the app switcher shows nothing. Settings also lists camera, photos and microphone permissions. A separate switch filters sensitive content.

features.summary: Typing `agi` in the AGI Workforce CLI opens a full-screen terminal chat on the alternate screen: header, transcript, composer and status bar, with pickers and dialogs drawn over it. The user can pick a colour theme, which is saved to the project config. Plain or screen-reader mode uses a line-based mode instead.

purpose.what_it_does: The CLI's main screen. It shows the conversation, takes typed prompts, starts agent turns, streams the reply and tool steps into the transcript, and draws overlays (command palette, model, effort and theme pickers, approval dialogs) on top of the same frame. It also holds the colour theme choice and redraws at whatever size the terminal has.
purpose.why_it_exists: The requirements say the CLI must have an interactive TUI/REPL, slash commands, a model/mode selector and a tool-call trace (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:1157-1178). The brief states that running `agi` opens a full-screen UI with composer, transcript and overlays (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md S72.01).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers who work in a terminal and want a chat-style agent in the folder they are working in.
problems_solved: Gives a terminal user a chat experience without leaving the shell.
Lets approvals, pickers and dialogs appear in the same screen as the conversation.
Lets people with light or dark terminals, or colour-vision needs, choose a readable theme.
Keeps the conversation visible when the window is resized.
use_cases: A developer runs `agi` in a repo, asks the agent to explain a failing test, and watches tool steps stream in.
A user on a light terminal types `/theme` and picks a light theme, which is still there next launch in that project.
A user shrinks and enlarges the terminal window during a long answer and the transcript is still on screen.

where_to_find_it: surface:cli only. Run `agi` in a terminal (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8290-8300). No other app has this screen; the brief gives a status only for the CLI (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md S72.01).

Start view shows the text `Welcome to AGI`, the version, a `Model` line, a `Folder` line, the hint `Choose Local, Your key, or Managed with /model.`, and `Recent activity` with `/resume for more` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2748-2830).
prerequisites: A terminal that can enter raw mode and the alternate screen (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:1957-1967).

Not started with `--no-tui`, and not in plain mode (`--plain` or the AGI_PLAIN environment variable), because both send the user to the line-based REPL (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8290-8300, apps/cli/src/output.rs:43-62).
A model route that can run: Local server, own provider key, or a signed-in Cloud account. Whether the screen itself needs sign-in is unknown (see unknowns).
screens_and_controls: Four stacked areas: header, chat area, composer (grows with content), one-line status bar (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2003-2018).
Enter sends; Shift+Enter, Alt+Enter or Ctrl+J insert a new line (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4081-4106, 4118-4124).
`/` on an empty composer opens the command palette by default (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:48-57, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4132-4141).
`/theme` opens the Theme picker with seven rows: Auto, Dark, Light, Ansi, High Contrast Dark, High Contrast Light, Colorblind (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/theme_picker.rs:60-72).

`/theme <name>` sets a theme directly. Accepted spellings include dark, light, ansi, high-contrast-dark, high-contrast-light, colorblind, auto, and solarized-dark/solarized-light which map to Dark/Light (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/theme_picker.rs:85-100).
Page Up / Page Down scroll the transcript; Ctrl+L redraws the whole screen without losing the conversation (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7872-7880).
journey: 1. User runs `agi` in a project folder.

2. The CLI loads config, builds the session, starts MCP connection, managed-model discovery and local-model discovery in the background, then enters raw mode and the alternate screen (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7021-7118).
3. The start view appears with model, mode, folder and recent sessions (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2748-2830).
4. User types a message and presses Enter; the composer clears and a turn starts (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4081-4094).

5. The live frame redraws every 50 ms with streamed text, spinner and tool steps; the composer keeps accepting typed text to queue (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2060-2078, apps/cli/src/tui/motion.rs:4).
6. When the turn ends the reply stays in the transcript.

7. User types `/theme`, picks a row with the arrow keys and Enter; the whole screen recolours on the next frame and a system line says `Theme set to <name>, saved in <path>.` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5250-5280, 5232-5247).
8. User exits (Ctrl+D twice, or /exit); the terminal is restored, the session is saved, and a session cost line prints (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7150-7215).
feedback_and_outputs: System messages in the transcript for results and failures, for example `Model switch failed: ...` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5553-5573).
Out-of-band notices (for example MCP connect errors) are pushed into the transcript as system messages (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7228-7244).
A status-bar notice for short messages such as `press ctrl+d again to quit` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:3956-3968).
On exit the CLI prints session tokens and cost (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7203-7210).
settings: `[ui] theme` in config.toml, one of auto | dark | light | ansi | high-contrast-dark | high-contrast-light | colorblind (apps/cli/src/config.rs:142-146).
`[ui] reduced_motion` and plain mode reduce animation (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7110-7113).
`--no-tui` and `--plain` choose the line-based mode (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8290-8300).

working: The full-screen screen exists and is the default interactive mode (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8290-8300, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6882).
Layout is header, chat, composer and status bar, recomputed from the frame size on every draw (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:1991-2018).

The event loop polls every 50 ms, handles key and paste events, and redraws at the end of every iteration, so a resize event wakes the poll and the next draw uses the new size [inferred from the loop at apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7283-7295 and 7903; this was not run].
A unit test draws a live conversation at four sizes and checks the transcript text is still there and the welcome text is not (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:11638-11660).
Empty state: a start view with model, mode label (`Local`, `Your key` or `Managed`), folder and recent sessions (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2748-2830).
Waiting state: spinner tick, `… working, Esc or Ctrl-C to cancel · type to queue a message` hint, and queued-message count (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:2064-2078).

Theme: picker, direct `/theme <name>`, apply to the palette, and save to the project config; startup reads the saved theme and falls back to Dark if it does not parse (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5250-5280, 6372-6392, 650-657, apps/cli/src/config.rs:1263-1266).
Terminal is restored on panic and on termination signals (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:1905-1950).
incomplete: The loop has no explicit resize handler: any non-key, non-paste event is ignored and the redraw comes from the loop itself (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7283-7290). No test sends a real resize event; the only resize test draws into a test buffer.
`/theme <alias>` for the solarized spellings silently sets Dark or Light, not a solarized theme (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/theme_picker.rs:93-94).
disconnected_or_disabled: Plain or screen-reader mode does not open this screen; the line-based REPL runs instead (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8290-8300).
The area brief lists `S72.28 No-color mode` as a separate item that includes the TUI; this page only covers the theme choice and not NO_COLOR handling.

established.statement: Running `agi` in a terminal opens a full-screen interactive UI with a composer, transcript and overlays that sends turns to the agent.
The user can pick a terminal colour theme (picker or /theme <name>) and it applies and persists.
Resizing the terminal re-lays out the TUI without losing the transcript.

The CLI must include the `agi` command, an interactive TUI/REPL, slash commands, a model/mode selector, approval modes and a tool call trace, and must stay local/workspace scoped unless the user hands off explicitly.

acceptance_criteria: Running `agi` in a real terminal shows the start view with a `Welcome to AGI` line, model, folder and an input box.
Typing a message and pressing Enter shows the user message, then the reply and tool steps in the transcript.
Resizing the window between a narrow and a wide size keeps all earlier messages visible and the composer usable.
`/theme` opens a picker with seven rows; choosing one recolours the screen and prints a line naming the file it was saved in.
After picking a theme, quit and run `agi` again in the same folder: the theme is still applied.
`agi --no-tui` or `AGI_PLAIN=1 agi` does not open the full-screen screen.
After Ctrl+C or a crash path the terminal is back to normal (no raw mode, no alternate screen).
inferred: Theme and layout work on any terminal that supports raw mode and the alternate screen; terminals without them fall back to the line mode or fail at startup [inferred; no fallback was found in setup_terminal, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:1957-1967].
The saved theme is per project, not per user, because it writes the project config [inferred from apps/cli/src/config.rs:1162-1195].
proposed: [proposed] Add a test that feeds a real resize event to the event loop, not only a draw at several sizes.
[proposed] Also save the theme to the user config when no project config exists, so a theme chosen in one folder is not lost in another.

steps.what_happens: User runs `agi`. The CLI parses arguments, loads merged config, decides TUI vs REPL.
The session is built and the saved or resumed conversation is loaded; SessionStart hooks run.

In the background: MCP servers connect (stdio ones on the device, remote ones to outside services), a managed-model roster is requested, and local servers (Ollama, LM Studio) are probed with a 2.5 s timeout.
Terminal enters raw mode and the alternate screen; the first frame is drawn.
Each loop pass: poll 50 ms, read a key or paste, update state, redraw.

Enter sends the text; slash commands are handled locally, other text starts an agent turn on the session's model route (Local server on the device, own key to the provider, or Cloud through our servers).
Picking a theme sets the active palette and writes `theme` into the project config file.
On exit the screen is restored, the session file saved, memory summarised, the session pushed to the account if the session is Managed, and a cost line printed.

features.summary: Fast typing in the CLI chat screen: Up and Down recall earlier prompts (saved between runs), `@` opens a fuzzy file picker and inlines trusted files, and a small set of global keys can be rebound in `[ui.keybindings]` in config.toml. `/keybindings` lists them.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the composer shortcuts: prompt recall, file and agent mentions, global key actions (quit, cycle mode, cycle model, redraw, clear chat, clear input, open palette), plus fixed editing keys.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief asks for recall that persists, a fuzzy file picker that inlines mentioned files, and global shortcuts that can be rebound (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md S72.23, S72.24, S72.25).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers in the terminal who send many prompts and refer to files often.
problems_solved: Retyping a long prompt.
Pointing the agent to the right file without typing the full path.
Terminal or muscle-memory conflicts with default keys.
Accidentally sending a repository-controlled file's contents to the model from an untrusted folder.
use_cases: Press Up to repeat last week's prompt after restarting the CLI.
Type `explain @src/li` and pick `src/lib.rs` from the list.
Rebind open_palette to ctrl+p because `/` clashes with a habit.

where_to_find_it: surface:cli, full-screen screen: the composer at the bottom (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4081-4200).
`/keybindings` or `/keys` prints the current bindings (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6704-6706, apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:157-187).
In the command palette the `attach` item is listed with the description `Attach an image, PDF or Office file to the next message` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4510-4520).
prerequisites: For file contents to be inlined, the folder must be trusted; otherwise only the typed path goes to the model (apps/cli/src/mentions.rs:296-315, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4541-4545).
For `[ui.keybindings]` edits, access to config.toml.
screens_and_controls: Up/Down: move inside a multi-line draft first, then walk prompt history, otherwise scroll the transcript (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4179-4200).
Up after clearing a draft brings the cleared draft back first (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:1133-1148, 4181-4186).

`@` at a word boundary opens a `Files` popup; typing narrows it, arrows move, Enter inserts, Esc closes, Backspace past the `@` closes it (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/mention_popup.rs:1-60, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4160-4166).
The popup also offers agent names (prefix is AGENT_MENTION_PREFIX) (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:971-990).

Default global keys: Ctrl+D quit, Shift+Tab cycle permission mode, Alt+P cycle model, Ctrl+L redraw, Ctrl+C clear input, `/` open palette; clear_chat has no default key (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:48-57).

Fixed keys: Enter send, Shift+Enter, Alt+Enter and Ctrl+J newline, Ctrl+U delete to line start, Ctrl+V paste clipboard image, Ctrl+O toggle full tool output, Esc Esc rewind picker (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4020-4125, 3975-3990).
journey: 1. User sends a prompt; it is added to history and appended to history.txt (apps/cli/src/tui/prompt_history.rs:52-65, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7400-7405).
2. Next run, Up loads history.txt entries (apps/cli/src/tui/prompt_history.rs:15-30).
3. User types `@`; the popup opens with the workspace file list (git-aware, bounded) (apps/cli/src/mentions.rs:1-100).
4. User picks a path; it is spliced into the message at the cursor (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:993).

5. On Enter the text is resolved: each `@path` becomes a file block when the folder is trusted; images and documents are staged as attachments; skipped items get a system line `<path> was not inlined: <reason>` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4541-4580).

6. To rebind keys the user adds `[ui.keybindings]` with entries such as `open_palette = "ctrl+p"`; bad entries are refused at config load (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:157-187, apps/cli/src/config.rs:1437).
feedback_and_outputs: `nothing to interrupt · ctrl+c again to exit` after the first Ctrl+C on an empty composer (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4000-4012).
`press ctrl+d again to quit` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:3956-3968).
`cleared the composer · Up brings it back` when a non-empty draft is cleared (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:1144-1147).
`no workspace files to mention` when the list is empty (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4597-4599).
`<path> was not inlined: <reason>` for skipped mentions (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4565-4577).
settings: `[ui.keybindings]` with the keys quit, cycle_mode, cycle_model, redraw, clear_chat, clear_input, open_palette (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:21-40).
`[ui] edit_mode = "vi" or "emacs"` for the line REPL editor (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:157-187).
`agi config set ui.keybindings.<action> <value>` style keys are read by config get/set (apps/cli/src/config.rs:1480-1482).

working: Prompt history is a rustyline file history loaded from `history.txt` in the config folder and appended on each send (apps/cli/src/tui/prompt_history.rs:15-30, 52-65).
Up/Down logic: multi-line cursor, then parked draft, then history older, else scroll (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4179-4200).

Mention candidates: `git ls-files` (cached and untracked, minus ignored) with a 3 s timeout, else a bounded walk of depth 12, capped at 20,000 entries, ten most recent files first (apps/cli/src/mentions.rs:20-100).

Mention expansion: skips paths outside the workspace, files that hold credentials, files above 256 KB, and, in an untrusted folder, all file and directory contents; images and Office or PDF documents are staged as attachments (apps/cli/src/mentions.rs:296-420).
Global bindings are validated: unknown action, bare character keys, keys the composer owns, and duplicates are rejected (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:195-250).
Ctrl+C with a draft clears (parks) it; with an empty composer it arms exit for 2 seconds, and a second press quits (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:3991-4022, 44).
Ctrl+D with an empty composer also needs two presses within 2 seconds; with a draft it parks the draft instead (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:3936-3970).
While a turn is running Ctrl+D (the Quit binding) quits at once (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:3915-3922).
Pasted text is sanitised and long pastes collapse (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4617-4631).
incomplete: The brief says mentioned files are inlined; the code inlines only in a trusted folder and only up to 256 KB, listing folders up to 200 entries (apps/cli/src/mentions.rs:25-35, 296-420).
`/keybindings` lists the global actions and a few fixed keys, but not Ctrl+J, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+O (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:157-187 versus tui_app.rs:4020-4125).
disconnected_or_disabled: Ctrl+R reverse search exists only in the line REPL, not in the full-screen screen (apps/cli/src/command_registry.rs:281-282, apps/cli/src/repl/mod.rs:1070).
Clear chat is unbound by default; it only runs if the user names it (apps/cli/src/keybindings.rs:48-57).
not_available: surface:web, surface:desktop, surface:mobile, surface:vscode, surface:chrome: not part of this item.
History search in the full-screen screen: not available.

established.statement: Typing @ in the composer opens a fuzzy file picker and the mentioned files are inlined as context when sent.
Previous prompts can be recalled (Up arrow / history search) and persist across runs.
The TUI has global keyboard shortcuts, lists them with /keybindings, and lets users rebind them in config.
The CLI must stay local and workspace scoped unless the user explicitly hands off.

acceptance_criteria: Send a prompt, quit, restart, press Up: the prompt returns.
Press Up on a multi-line draft: the cursor moves up first and history only after the top line.
Type `@` after a space: a `Files` popup opens; typing `lib` narrows it; Enter inserts the path.
In a trusted folder, send `explain @small.txt`: the model sees the file text. In an untrusted folder the same send shows `was not inlined: workspace is not trusted, only the path was sent`.
Mention a file named like a credentials file: a skip line says `holds credentials, only the path was sent`.
Add `open_palette = "ctrl+p"` under `[ui.keybindings]`: Ctrl+P opens the palette and `/keybindings` shows it.
Set two actions to the same chord: config load fails with `duplicates another effective binding`.
Press Ctrl+C once on an empty composer: a notice appears; a second press within two seconds exits.
inferred: History should not be shared in a way that leaks a Local prompt to the account; in the code history.txt is local only [inferred from apps/cli/src/tui/prompt_history.rs:1-97, which has no network call].
Mention expansion must run before send so the model sees the file text [inferred from apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4541].
proposed: [proposed] Add Ctrl+R history search to the full-screen screen so both modes match.
[proposed] List Ctrl+J, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+V and Ctrl+O in `/keybindings`.
[proposed] Offer a way to keep a prompt out of history.txt (for example a leading space or a config switch).

steps.what_happens: A key event is read and dispatched; global actions are matched against the loaded bindings.
Up or Down reads in-memory history loaded from history.txt.
`@` lists files with `git ls-files` (3 s timeout) or a bounded walk, then ranks them locally.
On send, mentions are validated against the workspace, checked for credentials and size, and the file text is added to the prompt only in a trusted folder.
The expanded prompt goes to the session's model route; file text can leave the device if the route is own key or Cloud.

features.summary: Saved conversations in the CLI: list them (`/history`, `agi history`, `agi session list`), resume one (`/resume`, `agi resume [id] [--cloud]`, `-c`), branch one (`/fork`, `agi fork`, `agi session fork --at-turn`), and export a transcript (`/export`). Sessions live as files on the device; Managed sessions also appear in the account.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a user find an earlier terminal conversation, continue it, fork it into a new one, or write it to a file. Also lists and resumes conversations stored in the AGI account when the session mode is Managed.
purpose.why_it_exists: The requirements list sessions, resume and branch as CLI features (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:1157-1178). The brief asks for list, resume, branch and export (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md S72.11, S72.12, S72.13, S72.32).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers who return to long tasks, want to try a different approach from a past point, or need a record of what the agent said.
problems_solved: Losing context when the terminal closes.
Trying an alternative without changing the original conversation.
Saving an answer or transcript to a file.
Continuing a conversation started on another device in the same account.
use_cases: `agi -c` continues yesterday's work in this repo.
`/fork before-refactor` branches the current chat to try a second plan.
`/export md notes/chat.md` writes a Markdown transcript.
`agi resume --cloud <id>` picks up a conversation held in the account.

where_to_find_it: surface:cli full-screen screen: `/history` or `/sessions` open a session picker; `/resume` opens it, `/resume <id>` resumes directly; `/fork` or `/branch [name]`; `/export [md|json|answer] [path]` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5997-6052).

surface:cli shell: `agi history [--limit N] [--cloud] [--project

]`, `agi resume [id] [--cloud|--teleport]`, `agi fork `, `agi -c`/`--continue`, `agi --resume `, `agi --session `, `--fork-session`, `agi session list|pin|unpin|show|fork|archive|unarchive|delete` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:245-264, 917-980, 1920-1975).
prerequisites: For device sessions: nothing beyond a config folder.
For account sessions: a signed-in account and a Managed (Cloud) session mode; Local and own-key modes are refused for account history (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:361-373).
To branch: session saving must not be switched off with --no-session-persistence (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:1363-1370).
screens_and_controls: Session picker overlay: rows show an optional pin mark, first 8 characters of the id, date and time, message count and title; Enter resumes, Esc closes (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4300-4340, apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/session_picker.rs).
`/history search <text>` or `/history <text>` filters rows (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5997-6000).
`/export` with no path prints the text into the chat; with a path writes a file (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6033-6043).
journey: List: user types `/history`; the picker opens with active (not archived) sessions on this device.
Resume: user presses Enter on a row; the session is loaded, the transcript is rebuilt and a system line says `Resumed session <id> (<n> messages).` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4345-4399).
Branch: user types `/fork name`; the current session is saved, copied to a new session, renamed, and a confirmation names the new session (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:1353-1420).

Export: user types `/export md notes.md`; the file is created in the workspace (see gaps for the path rule) and a line says `Exported the conversation to <path>.` (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:440-471).

Shell: `agi history` prints `On this device:` then `In your AGI account:` (or the reason it cannot) and the line `Resume one with `agi resume --cloud <id>`.` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7180-7210, 2985-3014).
feedback_and_outputs: `No sessions on this device.` when the device list is empty (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7196).
`Resumed session <id> (<n> messages).`, `No session matches ...`, `Could not load session: ...` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4345-4399).
`Nothing to branch, no messages yet.` and `Cannot branch, this run was started with --no-session-persistence ...` (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:1363-1385).
`Nothing to export, no messages in session yet.`; `<path> already exists, so nothing was written. Export to a new file name.` (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:440-471, 598-607).
`Account history unavailable: <reason>` when the account cannot be read (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3009-3012).
Interrupted tool calls at resume produce a warning that their results are unknown (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8250-8262).
settings: `--no-session-persistence` turns session files off (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:1363-1370).
The session store sits under the config folder, set by AGIWORKFORCE_HOME (apps/cli/src/config.rs:480-484).

working: Sessions are JSON/JSONL files in `managed_sessions` with metadata in `managed_session_metadata` under the config folder (apps/cli/src/sessions.rs:1-10, 50, 205-235, apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/session_control.rs:18).
Listing excludes archived sessions; `agi session list --archived` shows them (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/session_control.rs:682-685, apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1920-1930).

`agi resume` with no id or `-c` continues the newest non-archived session started in this project folder; with none it says `No saved session in this project to continue.` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2536-2554, 8240-8262).
Resume by id works for device sessions and falls back to the account for an id it does not find locally (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2513-2535).
`--cloud` resolves the id against the account and copies the conversation into the device store before resuming (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2829-2871).
`--teleport` brings a cloud Code session here and checks out its branch (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2626-2660).
Fork from the screen: saves the current session, forks it, renames the fork (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:1353-1420).
`agi session fork <id> --at-turn N --as name [--force]` forks at a turn and refuses to overwrite an existing name without --force (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5691-5770).
Export formats: Markdown (default), JSON, and the last answer; Markdown and answer are sanitised for terminal escapes (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:579-624).
Export writes with create-new, so an existing file is never overwritten (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:446-471).
A resumed Cloud session is checked for routing authority and model, and refused if missing (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4383-4386).
incomplete: The TUI `/resume` takes only a local id or path; it has no `--cloud` handling, so account conversations must be resumed from the shell (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4345-4391).
The TUI picker lists every active device session, not only this project's; `-c` is project-scoped (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:4303-4325 vs apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/session_control.rs:693-698).
disconnected_or_disabled: Legacy sessions without privacy or provider authority cannot be resumed (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2546-2551).
not_available: Clipboard export: the brief says the transcript can go to the clipboard; `/export` has no clipboard write (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6033-6043, apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:433-471).

surface:web, surface:desktop, surface:mobile, surface:vscode, surface:chrome: not part of this item (brief status n/a). The CLI session store is separate from the synced app chat history by design (apps/cli/src/sessions.rs:12-30).

established.statement: The user can list saved sessions and pick one (`/history` picker in the TUI, `agi history`, `agi session list`).
The user can resume a previous session by picker, id or latest (`/resume`, `agi resume [id] [--cloud]`, `-c`).
The user can branch the current or a saved session into a new one (`/fork`, `/branch`, `agi fork`, `agi session fork --at-turn`).
The user can export the conversation transcript (Markdown/JSON) to a file or clipboard.
The CLI must include local session transcripts and resume/branch, and stay local unless the user hands off explicitly.

acceptance_criteria: After a conversation, `agi history` lists it under `On this device:`.
`/history` opens a picker; Enter loads the session and the transcript shows the earlier messages.
`agi -c` in the same folder loads the newest session; in a folder with none it says no saved session.
`/fork x` creates a new session; the original is unchanged and the fork resumes with the same messages.
`agi session fork <id> --at-turn 1` keeps only the first exchange; running it again without `--force` fails with `already exists`.
`/export json out.json` creates the file; running it again says the file already exists and writes nothing.
`/export` in an empty session says there is nothing to export.
With a Local or own-key session, `agi history --cloud` explains that nothing is sent to the account in this mode.
inferred: Export should land inside the workspace, as the draft says, but the code does not enforce that; this needs a decision [inferred from apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:446-452].
A user who forks should be told which session id to resume; the shell fork prints it, the screen fork names the session [inferred from lib.rs:5755-5762].
proposed: [proposed] Add clipboard copy to `/export` (the brief requires it) or change the brief.
[proposed] Allow `/resume --cloud <id>` from the screen.
[proposed] Keep permanent session delete behind the same named-consequence confirmation as the rest of the product (agents never destroy data on their own, doc: AGENTS.md section 9).

steps.what_happens: List: the CLI reads session files and metadata in the config folder.
`agi history` without --cloud prints device sessions, then asks the account for conversations (`pull_all` on /api/chat/sync) only if the mode is Managed and a token exists.
Resume: the session file is loaded, routing authority and model are checked, the mode is kept, and the transcript is rebuilt.
Resume --cloud: one conversation is fetched from the account and written to the device store.
Fork: the live session is saved, copied under a new id and renamed.
Export: messages are rendered to Markdown, JSON or last answer; a file is created without overwriting, or the text is shown in the chat.
At exit a Managed session is pushed to the account; if the project link is stale the push is retried unfiled.

features.summary: Controls in the CLI for which model answers, how hard it thinks, and what it may do without asking. `/model` picks or switches the model, `/effort` sets the reasoning level, `/permissions` edits allow, ask, deny and session rules, and `--mode` with `--allowedTools` set the mode for one run.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the user switch the model mid-session (Local, own key or Managed), set a reasoning effort for the next request (and save it as the project default), see and edit permission rules, and choose a permission mode.
purpose.why_it_exists: The requirements call for a model/mode selector and approval modes (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:1157-1178); the brief asks for model, effort and permission controls (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md S72.14-S72.16).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers choosing between cheap and strong models, or between a careful and a hands-off agent.
problems_solved: Changing model without restarting.
Spending less on easy tasks and more on hard ones.
Stopping repeated approval prompts for safe commands, or blocking risky ones.
Running unattended in CI with a fixed mode.
use_cases: `/model` to move from a local model to the managed roster.
`/effort high` before a hard debugging task.
`/permissions allow npm test` so tests no longer prompt.
`agi --mode plan` to have the agent only plan.

working: `/model` with no argument opens the picker from the catalog, OpenRouter cache, managed roster and discovered local models (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:3367-3378).

`/model <id>` calls switch_model_by_name: a Managed session stays on the account for a model its plan runs; otherwise provider detection is used; in a Local session an unknown id is looked up among the local servers (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:1159-1200, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5559-5570).
Established non-Local sessions refuse a model on another trust mode and say to start a new session (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:1135-1151).
Entering a managed model from Local or own-key needs a fresh session; otherwise it is refused (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:1218-1231).
Alt+P cycles only among models the session can run in the same trust mode (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5132-5200, test at 13181).

`/effort` sets the level for later sends (the level is written to the session before each send) and also saves it to the project config (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6452-6470, 8237-8238, apps/cli/src/config.rs:1144-1160). The brief says it only changes the next request; the code does both.
Whether the model takes the effort on this route is checked and a note is added if not (apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:668-675, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6470-6478).
`/permissions` reads and writes the permission store; open-ended allow rules are rejected (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:803-905).
Permission modes: default, plan, auto (accept edits), bypassPermissions, dontAsk; bypass is never read from saved config (apps/cli/src/cli_options.rs:12-45).
`--auto` is refused together with `--model` or `--provider` and applies only to managed-cloud sessions (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:467-478).
`--allowedTools` and `--disallowedTools` are applied to the session (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6931-6940).

established.statement: The user can view and switch the model mid-session from the terminal (`/model` picker or `/model <id>`).
The user can set reasoning effort (low/medium/high/max) and it changes the next request.
The user can change the permission mode and allow/deny rules from the terminal.

Local, own-key and Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing silently routes a Local chat to own key or cloud; a Local-to-own-key move is an explicit fork with consent and a visible provider label.
The CLI includes a model/mode selector and approval modes.

acceptance_criteria: `/model` opens a picker with Local, Your key and Managed sections; picking a row switches and prints a banner.
`/model unknown-id` prints `Model switch failed: Unknown model ...` and the model does not change.
In a Managed session `/model` to a model on another trust mode is refused with a message to start a new session.
`/effort high` prints `Effort set to High and saved as this project's default`, and `.agiworkforce/config.toml` holds `reasoning_effort = "high"`.
`/effort bogus` lists the valid levels.
`/permissions allow npm test` then `/permissions allow` shows the rule; `/permissions remove allow npm test` removes it.
`/permissions allow *` or another open-ended rule is refused.
`agi --auto --model x` fails with a conflict; `agi --mode plan` starts in plan mode.

Mode cycling should skip modes the session cannot use [inferred from next_available, tui_app.rs:128-134].

[proposed] Show on the locked row which plan unlocks it and offer the upgrade link.
[proposed] Update the brief to the seven effort levels and to the project-default save.

steps.what_happens: `/model` builds the list: catalog entries, cached OpenRouter models, the managed roster fetched at startup, and local models found by probing the machine.
A pick calls switch_model or enter_managed_model; trust-boundary rules decide whether it is allowed.
For a Managed model the roster must list it as available; otherwise ModelUnavailable.
`/effort` stores the level on the app, writes it to the project config file, and before every send copies it to the session with its thinking budget.
The request builder includes the effort only if the route takes it; the provider then applies it.
`/permissions` loads the permission store file, changes it and saves; session rules live only in the process.
On each tool call the session mode and rules decide whether to run, ask or refuse.

data.retained_or_deleted: `/permissions reset` clears all rules; remove clears one.

data.where_stored: The managed session file (model and routing authority) (apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/session.rs)

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The model list is not hard-coded in the screen: it comes from the shared catalog, the OpenRouter cache, the managed roster and local discovery. Cloud rows are gated by plan tier. Local and own-key rows are never gated by plan (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/model_picker.rs:199-214). Provider names shown come from the design system (apps/cli/src/design_system.rs). See SYS-model-catalog-and-routing and SYS-inference-providers.

access_and_usage.account: Local and own-key models need no AGI account. Managed models need sign-in (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:375-379).
access_and_usage.permissions: Rule edits go through the permission store; open-ended allow rules are refused; managed policy can pin the mode; bypass is never read from saved settings (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:875-880, apps/cli/src/permissions.rs:356-368, apps/cli/src/cli_options.rs:29-45).
access_and_usage.subscription: For Cloud models the CLI requires a tier of Pro or higher; Free, Basic and Byok tiers are refused for Cloud models in the CLI; flagship additions need Max, Max15x, TeamPremium or Enterprise (apps/cli/src/model_catalog.rs:938-970). Plan names are as in the code (UserTier, apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:184-198).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Usage of Cloud models is metered by the server (see F072-05). None found for switching or effort.
access_and_usage.flags: --model, --provider, --auto, --mode, --permission-mode, --allowedTools, --disallowedTools, --max-budget-usd (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:366-402, 467-478, 8188-8195).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Effort applies only where the route supports it; otherwise a note is added (apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:668-675, apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:1711). Some models reject a configured temperature and a notice is shown at startup (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7068-7078).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: A session fixed to Managed or own-key cannot switch to another trust mode; a fresh session is needed (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:1135-1151, 1218-1231).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Local models need no account or plan. In a Local session an id not in the catalog is checked against what the local servers report (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:1179-1200). Switching a Local session to a keyed or managed model is not refused in switch_model (agent/mod.rs:1144); the later send gate was not traced.

features.summary: Three commands in the CLI chat screen: `/context` shows how full the model's window is and what is in it, `/usage` shows this session's tokens and estimated cost plus the account allowance (Cloud only), and `/compact [focus]` summarises the conversation and reports before and after size.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows window fill with a bar and a list of what is in context, shows session token and cost totals and the account's credit windows, and shrinks the conversation by summarising older turns.
purpose.why_it_exists: Long agent sessions run out of context and cost money. The brief asks for a context report, a usage report from the shared ledger, and a compact command with focus text and a before/after report (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md S72.17-S72.19).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers on long tasks and anyone watching spend or allowance.
problems_solved: Surprise context overflow.
Not knowing what is eating the window.
Not knowing the remaining allowance.
Losing the thread when the chat is too long.
use_cases: `/context` before a big paste to see if there is room.
`/compact keep the API design decisions` to free space while keeping a topic.
`/usage` to see the 5-hour, weekly and monthly credit windows on a Cloud plan.

where_to_find_it: surface:cli full-screen screen and line mode: `/context` (alias `/ctx`), `/usage`, `/compact [focus]` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5820, 5995, 6498).
The header and footer also show a context meter and counts (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:11971, 13055-13143).
A shell usage command is cited by the brief (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:4049); not traced here.
prerequisites: None for `/context` and `/compact`.
For account numbers in `/usage`: a Cloud (Managed) session and a signed-in account (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:497-503).
screens_and_controls: `/context`: line `Context: [#####     ] NN%  (used K / limit K tokens)` then `In context:` rows: System prompt, Instructions, Rule, Attached file, Added directory, Conversation, MCP tools (apps/cli/src/compaction.rs:70-100, apps/cli/src/agent/history.rs:17-62).

`/usage`: this session's input, output, cache read and write tokens, estimated cost, per-model breakdown, turn count, then `Account usage` lines (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6498-6512, apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:564-640).
`/compact` and `/compact <focus text>` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7755-7768).
journey: 1. User types `/context`; the report appears as a system message.
2. User types `/usage`; the CLI blocks briefly on a separate thread while it asks the server, then prints session and account lines.

3. User types `/compact keep tests`; the CLI summarises earlier turns with the current model and prints a receipt such as `Compacted N earlier messages: ~A -> ~B tokens (P% of estimated model window).`
feedback_and_outputs: `/context` bar, percent and token counts.

`/usage` lines: `Account usage`, `Plan: <label>`, `5-hour window: X of Y credits used, Z left, resets ...`, `Weekly`, `Monthly`, optional `Flagship weekly`, purchased credits and `Add credits: <link>`; or percentages when the server reports no credits; `No allowance remaining on this plan` when exhausted (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:564-640).
`/compact` receipt: `Compacted N earlier messages: ...`, `Trimmed long tool output: ...`, or `Nothing to compact: no earlier turn could be summarized ...` (apps/cli/src/compaction.rs:112-133).
If the account cannot be read: `Account usage` then `  Unavailable: <reason>` (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:557-562).
settings: `[default] max_tokens` is the output reserve used for context and compaction (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5820-5823, apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:1030-1032).
Context-meter items in the status line settings (`/statusline`) (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6512-6520).

working: Context is measured with the shared agent-core budget over the message list and the model window minus the reserved output (apps/cli/src/compaction.rs:35-67, agent/history.rs:17-20).
If the catalog has no window for the model the CLI assumes 128,000 tokens (apps/cli/src/compaction.rs:9, 28-35).
`/usage` combines session totals from the local cost ledger with account data from `GET /api/usage` and `/api/usage/history` (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:15-17, 358-366, 520-536).
Account usage is read only for Managed sessions; Local and own-key sessions get a boundary line instead (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:497-503, test line 914).
A BYOK-tier account in Managed mode gets `this account runs in BYOK mode, so provider spend is billed by the provider` (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:343-356).
No credential: `no AGI credential, so this session runs local or BYOK, run `agi login` to see account usage` (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:343-356).
The plan shown is taken from the server answer, replacing a stale cached tier (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:358-366, test line 1130).

`/compact` runs the shared compaction with a target of half the window and an optional focus phrase, using the session's own provider and model, and then refreshes the stats (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:1018-1039, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7755-7768).
The receipt distinguishes nothing-to-compact, trimmed tool output and summarised messages (apps/cli/src/compaction.rs:112-133, tests 354-376).

steps.what_happens: `/context` counts tokens of the in-memory messages with the shared estimate and prints the report; no network.
`/usage` prints local ledger totals, then spawns a thread with its own runtime to ask the account.
The account call is allowed only for a Managed session, then sends the saved account token to `/api/usage` and `/api/usage/history` in parallel.
A 401/403-type answer clears the cached tier and the CLI prints the server's reason.

`/compact` sends the older messages to the session's model to write a summary, then replaces them in memory and in the session file. The route is the session's own: device for Local, outside service for own key, our servers for Cloud.
After compaction the stats and meter refresh.

features.summary: Connecting and managing extra capabilities in the CLI: `agi mcp ...` manages the registry of outside tool servers, `agi plugin ...` and `/plugin`, `/skills` manage plugins and skills, and `agi background ...` runs a prompt that keeps going after the terminal closes. `/tasks` lists sub-agents and shell jobs in the screen.

purpose.what_it_does: Adds and controls MCP servers (outside tools), installs and checks plugins (with integrity and signature rules), lists and toggles skills, and runs detached background agent runs with logs, stop, remove and attach.
purpose.why_it_exists: The requirements list MCP server management, hooks, skills and subagents for the CLI (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:1157-1178). The brief asks for MCP, skill, plugin and background management from the terminal (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md S72.20, S72.21, S72.31).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers extending the agent with tools and automations, and people running long tasks unattended.
problems_solved: Giving the agent access to a database or ticket system.
Installing shared team plugins safely.
Turning skills on and off.
Letting a long task finish after the laptop lid or terminal closes.
use_cases: `agi mcp add github --url https://...` then `agi mcp login github`.
`agi plugin install <git-url> --integrity sha256:<hex>`.
`/skills-toggle` to switch off a noisy skill.
`agi background start "update the changelog"` then `agi background logs <id>`.

where_to_find_it: surface:cli shell: `agi mcp add|list|get|enable|disable|allow|ask|block|unset|login|logout|remove` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2126-2213); `agi plugin list|install|info|login|configure|remove|enable|disable|update|digest|sign` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2017-2081); `agi background start|list|logs|stop|rm|attach` (alias `bg`) (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2083-2113, 909-912).

surface:cli screen: `/mcp` shows configured servers and their state; `/mcp tools [server]`, `/mcp restart`, `/mcp enable|disable <name>` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6055-6125); `/skills` lists, `/skills import <path>`, `/skills remove <name>`, `/skills-toggle` opens a toggle overlay (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6169-6215, 7011); `/plugin` or `/plugins` opens a tabbed overlay titled `Plugins (← → switch tabs · Esc close)`, with `/plugin enable|disable|remove|update|configure <name>` as text commands (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6285-6330); `/tasks` and `/background <instruction>` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5616, 5960).
prerequisites: MCP: a server command or URL; remote servers may need OAuth sign-in.
Plugin install: a source (git URL or folder) and either a publisher signature, a pinned sha256 digest, or an explicit unsafe flag.
Background: a working model route; nobody is at the terminal to approve tools.
screens_and_controls: `/mcp` list with a status per server: Connected, Starting, NeedsAuth, Disabled, Blocked, Failed, and the tool count (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6090-6118).
Skills overlay: `Skills (↑↓ navigate · Space toggle · Enter save · Esc cancel)` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6226-6232).
Plugin tabs: Installed and Marketplaces, with ✔ or ◯ per plugin and a Project or User group (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6292-6325).
`agi background list` prints one line per run; `--json` prints id, state, prompt, cwd, session id, times and exit code (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1731-1757).
journey: MCP: `agi mcp add name --command npx --arg ...` writes the registry file and prints `Registered MCP server '<name>' in <path>.`; `agi mcp list` shows enabled, disabled or blocked; `agi mcp login <name>` runs OAuth for a remote server (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5101-5160).
Plugin: `agi plugin install <source>` verifies integrity and signature, installs, prints contents (hooks, servers) and asks for settings at a terminal (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6833-6905).

Background: `agi background start <prompt>` prints the run id and the commands to see logs, attach and stop; `agi background attach <id>` resumes the finished conversation in a normal session (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1710-1730, 1783-1812).
In the screen, `/bg <instruction>` saves this conversation, starts a background run that resumes it, and opens a new conversation here (apps/cli/src/background.rs:303-340).
feedback_and_outputs: `Registered MCP server ...`, `No MCP servers registered in <path>.`, `blocked` with the policy reason (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5101-5160).

`Installed to <path> (<format> manifest), <signature label>` followed by plugin contents and a Trust row: `its hooks and MCP servers run on this computer with your permissions` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6860-6880, apps/cli/src/features/plugins/plugins.rs:530-536).
`Refusing install: ...` on integrity or signature failure (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6833-6860).
`Started background run <id>. It keeps going after this terminal closes.` and states running, finished, failed, stopped, `ended without a result` (apps/cli/src/background.rs:40-58).
`/tasks` shows sub-agent tasks and shell jobs: `list`, `show|output|stop|cancel <id>`, `transcript <id>` (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:484-560).
settings: MCP registry file `mcp.json` in the config folder (default `~/.agiworkforce/mcp.json`); project `.mcp.json` or `mcp.json` in the repo, with consent (apps/cli/src/mcp/registry.rs:63-67, apps/cli/src/mcp/consent.rs:39).
`plugins.require_signed`, `plugins.trusted_publishers` in config (apps/cli/src/features/plugins/plugins.rs:256-300, 571-580).
Disabled skills set (apps/cli/src/skills.rs load_disabled_skills).
`--mcp-config <file>` at launch (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:402-404).

working: MCP registry commands add, list, get, enable, disable, allow, ask, block, unset, login, logout, remove are implemented and read the same registry rows (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5095-5300).

The registry file is `mcp.json` in the config folder, whose root can be moved with AGIWORKFORCE_HOME; `~/.agiworkforce` is the default (apps/cli/src/mcp/registry.rs:63-67, apps/cli/src/config.rs:480-484).
In the screen, MCP connect runs in the background so a slow OAuth server cannot hold up start; until it finishes, turns run without MCP tools (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7021-7050, 7200-7222).
A project's own MCP config needs the user's consent and policy can block a server (apps/cli/src/mcp/consent.rs, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6103-6112).
Entering Local mode drops every connected remote MCP server and its tools and prompts (apps/cli/src/mcp/mod.rs:2376-2391).

Plugin install: default checks a publisher signature; `--integrity sha256:<hex>` pins a digest; `--unsafe-no-integrity` skips with a warning; an unsigned plugin installs with a warning unless `plugins.require_signed` is set, where it is refused unless `--unsafe-allow-unsigned` is given and managed settings allow it (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6845-6870, apps/cli/src/features/plugins/plugins.rs:538-580).
Plugins can be listed, shown, configured, enabled, disabled, updated, signed and digested from the shell (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2017-2081, 6780-6830).
`/plugin enable|disable|remove|update|configure` work as text commands in the screen (apps/cli/src/installs.rs:561-590).

Background runs: a detached supervisor launches a hidden `agi --print` child with the run's args; records are `run.json` and `output.log` under `<config>/background/<id>` (apps/cli/src/background.rs:6-7, 65-75, 246-300, 474-520).
States Running, Finished, Failed, Stopped and Lost are computed from the record and process checks (apps/cli/src/background.rs:40-58, 199-245).
`stop` ends the run's process group and records it as stopped; `rm` refuses a running run (apps/cli/src/background.rs:523-600).
`attach` shows the log while running, or resumes the saved conversation after it finished (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1783-1812).
`/tasks` lists sub-agent tasks and shell jobs, and can show, stop or transcript one (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:484-560, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7733-7743).
incomplete: `/skills` only lists, imports and removes; toggling is a separate `/skills-toggle` overlay that is not in the shared registry (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6169-6215, 4503-4527).
`/tasks` does not list `agi background` runs; those are listed only by `agi background list` (apps/cli/src/repl/registry.rs:484-520 reads the sub-agent manager and shell jobs).
A background run does not receive `--max-budget-usd` or other limits from `agi background start`; only model and permission mode are passed (apps/cli/src/background.rs:246-262).
The Marketplaces tab content and install flow in the screen were not traced.
disconnected_or_disabled: The decision log (2026-07-30) says `/background` and `/bg` were cut because they returned an unavailable message; the code now has a working hand-off and a durable background module, so the log row is out of date (doc: docs/decisions/wire-or-cut.md:55, apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5960, apps/cli/src/background.rs:303-340).
not_available: surface:web, surface:desktop, surface:mobile, surface:vscode, surface:chrome: not part of this item (brief status n/a). The surface matrix says the CLI has no connectors directory; third parties come in through MCP (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:357).

established.statement: The user can add, list, inspect, authenticate and remove MCP servers from the terminal and see connected tools.
The user can list/toggle skills and list/install/update plugins from the terminal.
The user can list, inspect and stop background tasks (sub-agents or long-running commands) from the terminal.
The CLI includes MCP server management, hooks and skills, subagents, and stays local unless the user hands off.
Local mode: no prompt, chat or file context should leave this device.

`agi plugin install <src> --integrity sha256:<wrong>` is refused.
`agi background start "hello"` prints an id; `agi background list` shows running then finished; `agi background logs <id>` prints output.
`agi background stop <id>` marks it stopped; `agi background rm <id>` on a running run is refused.

A plugin's hooks and servers run with the user's permissions, so the install summary must say so [inferred from plugins.rs:530-536].

[proposed] Pass a spend cap to background runs, and show it in the start message.

steps.what_happens: `agi mcp add` validates the target and writes the registry file in the config folder.
At session start the manager connects enabled servers: stdio servers start as local processes; remote servers are called over the network, with OAuth in a browser if needed.
In Local mode remote servers are dropped at once.

`agi plugin install` fetches the source (a git host or a folder), checks the integrity claim and the signature policy, copies the plugin into the plugins folder, reads its manifest and prints its contents.
`agi background start` writes a run record, launches a detached supervisor, which launches `agi --print ... -- <prompt>` in the same folder, with output to `output.log`.
The background child talks to the model through the same route as any one-shot run (Local, own key or Cloud).
`/tasks` asks the in-process sub-agent manager and the shell job list; no files.
