execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: MCP, plugins and skills are model-agnostic; the tools they add are offered to whichever model the session uses. A background run uses the model passed by `--model` or the configured default, through that model's route (apps/cli/src/background.rs:252-262). Remote MCP servers are outside services and are blocked in Local mode. See SYS-connectors-plugins-and-skills.

access_and_usage.account: MCP, plugins, skills and background runs need no AGI account for Local and own-key use. A Cloud model in a background run needs sign-in.
access_and_usage.permissions: Per-server and per-tool allow, ask and block settings (`agi mcp allow|ask|block|unset`) (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2175-2202). Project MCP configs need consent. Plugins run hooks and servers with the user's permissions, and the install summary says so (apps/cli/src/features/plugins/plugins.rs:530-536). Background runs refuse tools that need approval unless the permission mode allows them (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2092-2095).
access_and_usage.subscription: None found for MCP, plugins, skills or background runs. A Cloud model in a run follows the plan rules in F072-04.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: None found in background.rs for count, time or spend. Cloud usage of the child run is metered like any one-shot run.
access_and_usage.flags: `plugins.require_signed`, `plugins.trusted_publishers`, `--unsafe-allow-unsigned`, `--unsafe-no-integrity`, `--integrity`, `--mcp-config`, `--permission-mode` for background start.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: MCP tools are offered to any model that supports tools; a Local model without tool support loses them for the turn and the user is told through a notice (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7232-7244). Detailed per-model support was not traced.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Remote MCP servers are refused in Local mode (apps/cli/src/mcp/mod.rs:2376-2391). Managed policy can block servers (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:6103-6112).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Stdio MCP servers, installed plugins, skills and background runs with a local model work with no account. Remote MCP servers and any account call are cut off in Local mode.

features.summary: The CLI (surface:cli only) can run one prompt to the end and exit. The prompt comes from the command line, from stdin or from a pipe. The reply prints as plain text, one JSON object, or a stream of JSON events. Two code paths exist: `agi "<prompt>"` and the `agi exec` subcommand. They do not behave the same.

purpose.what_it_does: Runs a single agent turn (including its tool loop) without opening the full-screen screen, writes the result to stdout in the chosen format and ends the process. `agi "<prompt>"` goes through run_oneshot (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9146); `agi exec` has its own arm (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6239-6490). Text for the prompt can come from an argument, `-`, `--stdin`, or a pipe, and `-f FILE` adds file context (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8513-8548).
purpose.why_it_exists: Scripts, CI jobs and shell pipelines need a non-interactive way to ask the agent something and read the answer in a machine-friendly form (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md, S72.03 to S72.08).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers who script the CLI, CI pipelines, and tools that embed the CLI and read its JSON or event stream.
problems_solved: Run the agent with no human at the keyboard.
Feed command output (for example a diff) into a prompt.
Get a reply that a program can parse: one JSON object or line-by-line events.
Get only the reply text, with no spinner or cost line.
use_cases: `git diff | agi "explain this change"` prints a text explanation.
`agi --output-format json "summarise README.md" -f README.md` returns one JSON object a script parses.
`agi --output-format stream-json "fix the failing test"` streams session, delta and tool events to a dashboard.
`agi --json-events exec "hello"` streams typed lifecycle events for a CI log.

where_to_find_it: surface:cli only: command line `agi [PROMPT]`, `agi exec <PROMPT>` (alias `e`). Flags: `--raw`, `--print`, `--json`, `--output-format text|json|stream-json` (alias `--output`), `--json-events`, `--stdin`, `-f/--file`, `-q/--quiet` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:212-294, 767-780). Not on web, desktop, mobile, vscode or chrome.
prerequisites: Installed `agi` binary.
A usable route: Local model, own provider key (`agi login <provider>`), or Cloud sign-in (`agi login`). Without one the run fails with an auth error (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:868-869).
A trusted project folder: in headless use an untrusted folder stops the run with `Current project is not trusted...` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6160-6167).
screens_and_controls: No screen. Text mode shows a `Thinking...` spinner and rendered markdown, then a `cost:` line on stderr (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9496-9530).
`--raw`/`--print`: reply text only (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9463-9490).
`--output-format json` or `--json`: one pretty JSON object (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9415-9462).
`--output-format stream-json`: one JSON event per line (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9299-9412).
`--json-events`: a different, typed event stream (apps/cli/src/agent_events.rs:20-70).
journey: 1. Type `agi "<prompt>"` or `agi exec "<prompt>"`; optionally pipe text in or pass `-f FILE`.
2. The CLI loads config, checks folder trust and resolves the route (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6159-6195).
3. It reads stdin if requested or if stdin is not a terminal (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8664-8671).
4. It builds the final prompt: file context first, then `<stdin>...</stdin>` plus the prompt (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8513-8548).
5. It runs the turn and prints in the chosen format.
6. The process exits; Ctrl+C cancels the turn and exits 130 (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8633-8637).
feedback_and_outputs: Text: streamed markdown on stdout, `cost:` and `billed:` lines on stderr (apps/cli/src/output.rs:817-841).

JSON: keys type, model, response, input_tokens, output_tokens, via_subscription, cost, duration_ms, is_error, incomplete (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:601-632). On failure the error JSON (type, is_error, error, kind, hint, retry_after_seconds, reference) goes to stderr (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9457-9460, apps/cli/src/errors.rs:459-475).

Stream-json events carry a `type`: status_update (session_start, session_end, budget_exhausted), user_message, stream_event (subtype text_delta, tool_use_start), tool_result, assistant_message, error (apps/cli/src/sdk_io/protocol.rs:12-95).

`--json-events` events carry an `event` tag: spawning, ready_for_prompt, running_tool, tool_result, message_delta, turn_usage, fallback_triggered, finished, budget_exhausted, error (apps/cli/src/agent_events.rs:20-90).
settings: `updates`, `ui` and default model/provider in config.toml and environment variables AGIWORKFORCE_MODEL, AGIWORKFORCE_PROVIDER, AGIWORKFORCE_MAX_TOKENS (apps/cli/src/config.rs:1634-1670).
`--max-turns`, `--effort`, `--system-prompt` and related flags apply to one-shot runs (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6258-6260).

working: Output mode is chosen by resolve_oneshot_output_mode: JsonPretty, RawText, JsonLine or Text (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:574-592).
Stdin is read for `-`, `--stdin` or a non-terminal stdin (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7983, 8664-8671); file context first, `<stdin>` block before the prompt (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8513-8548).
`--print` with no prompt exits 1 with `--print requires a prompt argument.`; empty piped stdin with no prompt exits 1 with `No input received from stdin.` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8216-8224).

Stream-json writes session_start and user_message first, text deltas live, tool lifecycle, then assistant_message and session_end; on failure an `error` event then session_end, then exit with the failure's exit code (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9299-9412).
Stream-json carries the stop reason max_tokens or refusal when a turn was cut short (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9368-9380).
Terminal escape sequences in model text are stripped before printing (apps/cli/src/output.rs:492-496).
`--json-events` plus `exec` yields strict JSONL (apps/cli/tests/json_events_jsonl.rs, doc comment at line 1-20).
incomplete: `agi exec` does not read the top-level --output-format, --raw or --print (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6239-6490 uses only its own `--json` and the top-level `--json-events`). Its JSON object has only response, input_tokens, output_tokens, sources, incomplete (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6438-6457): no model, cost, duration or error state. S72.07 asks for those (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md S72.07).

`-p` is the short flag of `--provider` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:195), and `--print` has only a long form (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:292-294). The brief and the first draft say `agi -p "<prompt>"`; that is not what the code defines. No `-p` rewrite was found [inferred].
`--json-events` is not an alias of stream-json. The two schemas differ and clap makes them conflict (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:280-286; test apps/cli/src/lib.rs:10586-10595).
Top-level `--json-events` without `exec` sets session.json_events but still runs the Text branch of run_oneshot (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9238-9250, 9496-9530); what lands on stdout is unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: Bidirectional SDK stdin/control in sdk_io is intentionally inactive (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:150-153; test name apps/cli/src/lib.rs:10966).
not_available: No one-shot mode on web, desktop, mobile, vscode or chrome; the surface:vscode extension reaches the CLI runtime through other commands (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:26).

established.statement: A prompt can run to completion without an interactive session and the process exits (`agi exec` / `-p`).
Prompt text can be supplied on stdin via `--stdin`, `-`, or auto-detected when stdin is not a TTY.
Piped content is combined with the positional prompt and any --file context.
A one-shot run can print bare response text with no spinner, cost line or formatting (`--raw`, `--print`, `--output-format text`).
A one-shot run can emit a single JSON result with response, tokens, cost, duration and error state.
A one-shot run can stream NDJSON events: session start, user message, text deltas, tool lifecycle, final message, end or error.
stdout carries payload only; diagnostics go to stderr.

acceptance_criteria: `agi --output-format json "hi"` prints exactly one JSON object whose keys include type, model, response, input_tokens, output_tokens, via_subscription, cost, duration_ms, is_error.
`agi --raw "hi"` prints only the reply on stdout, with no spinner or ANSI colour.
`echo data | agi "summarise"` sends `<stdin>` content before the prompt.
`agi --output-format stream-json "hi"` prints one valid JSON object per line, starting with a status_update of reason session_start and ending with session_end.
`agi --print` with no prompt exits 1 and prints a message.
A failing JSON run prints error JSON on stderr and exits with the failure's class code.
`agi --output-format stream-json --json-events x` is rejected by the argument parser.
inferred: A script should treat an empty stdout plus a non-zero exit as failure in `--output-format json` mode because the error JSON goes to stderr [inferred from apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9457-9460].
`agi exec` should accept the same output flags as the top-level path [inferred from S72.07 applying to `exec`].
proposed: [proposed] Give `agi exec` the same output-format handling and JSON shape as the top-level path, or document the difference in `--help`.
[proposed] Make `-p` mean `--print` as in other coding CLIs, or remove `-p` from the brief.
[proposed] Print the error JSON on stdout as well in json mode, matching stream-json's error event.

features.summary: The CLI (surface:cli only) ends with a status that tells scripts what kind of failure happened: 1, 65, 69, 75, 76, 77 or 78, never 2. Flags let CI run without prompts: a spend cap, automatic plan approval, a no-prompt permission mode and a tool allow list. Several statuses outside the contract also exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Maps every failure to one exit class (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:246-280, 864-897), maps raw network errors to 69 or 75 (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8829-8845), and gives unattended runs a budget cap and approval policy flags (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:381-392, 487-492).
purpose.why_it_exists: A CI job must branch on why a run failed: an expired sign-in, an unreachable host and a bad input are different problems (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:240-245 comment).
purpose.who_uses_it: CI authors, script writers and wrapper tools around surface:cli.
problems_solved: Telling retryable failures (75) from permanent ones.
Telling sign-in problems (77) from plan or configuration problems (78).
Stopping a runaway unattended run by spend.
Running with no human to answer approval prompts.
use_cases: A pipeline retries on 75 and 69 and pages a human on 77 and 78.
A nightly job runs `agi exec` with `--max-budget-usd` to cap cost.
A plan-mode run uses `--auto-approve-plan` so no one has to type `/plan accept`.
A wrapper refuses to continue when status 76 says the CLI is too old.

where_to_find_it: surface:cli: the process exit status (`echo $?`); flags `--max-budget-usd <USD>`, `--auto-approve-plan`, `--mode`/`--permission-mode` (value `dontAsk`), `--allowedTools`/`--disallowedTools`, `-y`, `--full-auto` on exec (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:316-392, 487-492, 770-772). No UI on other apps.
prerequisites: A non-interactive invocation (`agi exec`, or `agi "prompt"`).
For headless file changes, a flag that permits them: `--full-auto`, `--permission-mode auto` or `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/file_ops/mod.rs:96-97).
screens_and_controls: No screen. Controls are flags only.
stderr shows the cause, for example the refusal text `...requires approval and stdin is not a terminal...` (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/file_ops/mod.rs:104-118).
journey: 1. Script runs `agi exec "<task>" --max-budget-usd 2 --mode dontAsk`.
2. The CLI runs the turn; a headless tool that needs approval is refused and marked.
3. The process ends; run_to_exit_code maps the outcome (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8797-8821).
4. The script reads the status and, in JSON modes, the `kind` field.
feedback_and_outputs: Exit status.
stderr error text; error JSON `kind` and `hint` (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:459-475).

On budget stop: the line `Budget cap reached: ... Stopping agent loop.` (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:3687-3699), plus a machine event in stream-json (status_update, budget_exhausted) or --json-events (budget_exhausted) only (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6365-6366, 9246-9250, 9279-9291).
settings: Permission mode default in config (`default.permission_mode`); a stored bypass mode is refused (apps/cli/src/cli_options.rs:27-33).

working: Seven classes with distinct codes 1, 65, 69, 75, 76, 77, 78; 2 is reserved for the parser (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:246-296).

Every CliError variant answers an exit class (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:864-897): signed out or bad key 77; config 78; plan excludes model, paywall, usage limit 78; server error or network or model unavailable 69; rate limit or retryable stream 75; context overflow 65; client too old 76.
A raw HTTP timeout maps to 75 and a connect error to 69 (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8829-8845).
A headless change that was refused makes an otherwise successful run exit 1 (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8813; apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/file_ops/mod.rs:96-118).
Ctrl+C exits 130 after killing tool processes (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8633-8637).
A closed output pipe exits 141 (apps/cli/src/broken_pipe.rs:7).
`--max-budget-usd` stops the tool loop when spend reaches the cap, checked after the first completion and after each continuation (crates/agiworkforce-agent-core/src/engine.rs:79-87, 282-290).
Teammates started by the lead get the remaining budget only (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:1901-1926).
incomplete: Budget stop returns normally, so the exit status is most likely 0, not a distinct code [inferred from crates/agiworkforce-agent-core/src/engine.rs:79-87 and tests at crates/agiworkforce-agent-core/tests/turn_loop.rs:680-730]. The brief's contract names no budget code.
Budget machine events are emitted only with stream-json or --json-events; text and json modes get none (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9246-9250 comment).
`agi update --check` exits 1 when a newer release exists (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6573-6578), a generic code outside the table's meaning.
An untrusted folder in headless use ends with a plain error (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6160-6167) that has no CliError, so it exits 1 [inferred from apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8829-8845].
`agi doctor` returns success even when checks fail (apps/cli/src/doctor.rs:49-57).
`-p` does not mean print (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:195).
disconnected_or_disabled: none found in the code.
not_available: Budget flags and exit classes exist only on surface:cli; other apps have no exit codes.

established.statement: Exit status distinguishes failure classes: 1 generic, 65 data, 69 unavailable, 75 temporary, 76 too old, 77 not permitted, 78 configuration; 2 reserved for usage.
CI scripts can drive the CLI non-interactively with machine output, auto-approval policy, spend cap and meaningful exit codes.
Code 2 is never produced by the CLI's own classes.
Paywall and usage-limit failures exit 78.

acceptance_criteria: A signed-out Cloud run exits 77.
A missing config value or plan exclusion exits 78.
A refused connection exits 69; a request timeout exits 75.
A context-overflow failure exits 65.
A headless run that needed approval for a file change exits 1 and prints the flag hint.
Parser errors exit 2 and no CliError uses 2.
With --max-budget-usd below the first completion's cost, no tool runs after it and a budget event appears in stream-json.
inferred: Every non-zero status outside the seven classes (130, 141, update --check 1) should be listed in the public contract [inferred].
A budget stop should be distinguishable by a script [inferred from S72.37 wording `meaningful exit codes`].
proposed: [proposed] Give budget exhaustion its own exit status or a field in the JSON result.
[proposed] Make `agi doctor` exit non-zero when overall status is Fail, behind a flag.
[proposed] Publish the full status table (including 130 and 141) in `--help` and docs/runbooks.

features.summary: The CLI (surface:cli only) has a plain mode and a screen-reader mode. Plain turns off colour, spinners and rules and uses the line-by-line prompt instead of the full-screen screen. Screen-reader mode also labels each line `you:`, `agi:` or `tool:`, uses numbered menus and rings a bell. NO_COLOR alone does not recolour the full-screen screen.

purpose.what_it_does: Publishes one global plain flag before anything prints and makes every output function read it (apps/cli/src/output.rs:41-59). Plain forces the line REPL (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8295). Screen-reader mode adds labels, numbered menus and a bell in that REPL (apps/cli/src/output.rs:61-81, 278-300, 346-410).
purpose.why_it_exists: A screen reader speaks one line at a time, so spinners and box-drawing rules are noise; logs and pipes also want no colour (apps/cli/src/output.rs:23-33 comment; doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md S72.02).
purpose.who_uses_it: Blind and low-vision developers, people who log terminal output, and anyone on a terminal that cannot draw the full-screen screen.
problems_solved: Animated spinners repainting while a screen reader speaks.
Not knowing who is speaking in a transcript.
Arrow-key menus a screen reader cannot use.
Missing signal when the CLI waits for input.
use_cases: `agi --screen-reader` for a daily session with a screen reader.
`AGI_PLAIN=1 agi` in a CI log viewer.
`ui.screen_reader = true` in config.toml so every launch is accessible.
`NO_COLOR=1 agi "hi"` for colourless one-shot text.

where_to_find_it: surface:cli: flags `--plain` and `--screen-reader` (global, so they work with subcommands; apps/cli/src/lib.rs:436-448); environment AGI_PLAIN, AGI_SCREEN_READER, NO_COLOR; config key `ui.screen_reader` (apps/cli/src/config.rs:163, 1470-1471, 1588-1589). Not on other apps.
prerequisites: Installed CLI.
For labels: an interactive launch (no prompt, no --stdin) because labels are turned on only then (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5974-5980).
screens_and_controls: Line REPL prompt: `you: ` with a bell in screen-reader mode, `> ` otherwise (apps/cli/src/output.rs:341-347).
Assistant lines start with `agi: `; tool lines start with `tool: ` (apps/cli/src/output.rs:292-300, 399-410).
Numbered menu and Yes/No menu answered by typing a digit (apps/cli/src/output.rs:304-340, 358-395).
In plain mode a spinner prints its message once (apps/cli/src/output.rs:245-262).
journey: 1. Start `agi --screen-reader` (or set the env var or config key).
2. The CLI publishes plain mode, then labels (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5943-5980).
3. Plain mode picks the line REPL instead of the full-screen screen (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8295).
4. Type a message after `you:`; the reply prints with `agi:`; tools print `tool:` lines.
5. When a choice is needed, type its number.
feedback_and_outputs: Bell character before the prompt (apps/cli/src/output.rs:56-58 constants).
Words instead of glyphs where a glyph carried meaning (apps/cli/src/output.rs:23-27 doc).
Banner shows `[no color]` when colour level is none (apps/cli/src/output.rs:906-912).

features.summary: The CLI (surface:cli only) signs the user in and out, shows which credentials exist, runs against a chosen folder, and reads settings from a global file, a trusted project file and environment variables. Account sign-in uses a browser device code. Provider API keys go to the OS keychain or owner-only files.

purpose.what_it_does: `agi login` runs a device-code sign-in to the AGI account (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1044-1051); `agi login <provider>` stores that provider's API key (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1267-1288); `agi logout` signs out of the account and `--all` also removes keys (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7275-7294); `agi auth-status` lists credentials (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7449-7470). `-C/--repo` moves into another folder and `--add-dir` adds extra roots (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:408-422, 5971-5972, 6080-6083). Config merges layers (apps/cli/src/config.rs:709-728).
purpose.why_it_exists: Cloud needs an account, own-key needs a stored key, and developers need per-project and per-machine settings without editing code (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md S72.10, S72.22, S72.33, S72.34).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every CLI user, and CI authors who set environment variables or an absolute home folder.
problems_solved: Getting a credential onto a headless machine without pasting a password.
Keeping keys out of plain files on macOS and Windows.
Running the CLI on a repo other than the current folder.
Overriding a model or provider for one run.
use_cases: `agi login` then approve in a browser, to use Cloud.
`agi login anthropic` to store an own-key credential.
`agi -C ~/work/api exec "run the tests"` to work in another repo.
`AGIWORKFORCE_MODEL=<id> agi exec ...` to pick a model in CI.

where_to_find_it: surface:cli commands `agi login [provider]`, `agi logout [--all] [--yes]`, `agi auth-status`; in the full-screen or line session `/login [provider]`, `/logout`, `/auth`, `/config`, `/add-dir` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5887-5890, 5981-5983; apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:527, 599-606, 636; apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:221, 332-370). Flags `-C/--repo`, `--add-dir`, `--config`. Not on other apps.
prerequisites: A browser (or the printed link) for account sign-in.
For own-key: a provider API key.
For project config: a trusted folder and managed policy that allows it (apps/cli/src/config.rs:826-844).
screens_and_controls: Account sign-in prints a link and a code and says `Waiting for authorization...` (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:489-503).
API-key prompt `Enter <Provider> API key (<ENV>)` hidden input (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1241-1250 region, interactive_api_key_login_for_provider).
`auth-status` table: Provider, Type, Status, Expires, Last used (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7449-7470).
`logout --all` asks a destructive confirmation naming the consequence (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7279-7289).
journey: 1. Run `agi login`.
2. Open the printed link, check the code matches, approve; the CLI polls until approved (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:489-540).
3. If updated terms are required the CLI prints the link to accept them (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:522-535).
4. The credential is saved and a device heartbeat is sent (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1044-1050).
5. Run `agi auth-status` to confirm.
6. Run `agi logout` to sign out; `--all` also removes saved keys.
feedback_and_outputs: Logged out message: `Logged out from N provider(s).` or `No active sessions to log out from.`, with a note when AGI Cloud did not confirm the sign-out (apps/cli/src/app_server/account.rs:670-684).
`/logout` appends `Saved provider API keys stay; agi logout --all removes them.` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:4994-5002).
`/login` result line `Login complete. Credentials saved.` (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7494-7510).
settings: ~/.agiworkforce/config.toml or $AGIWORKFORCE_HOME/config.toml (absolute path required) (apps/cli/src/config.rs:476-492, 1695-1713).
Project file .agiworkforce/config.toml (apps/cli/src/config.rs:531-542).
AGIWORKFORCE_MODEL, AGIWORKFORCE_PROVIDER, AGIWORKFORCE_MAX_TOKENS override; AGIWORKFORCE_API_BASE, AGI_PLAIN, AGI_SCREEN_READER are recorded (apps/cli/src/config.rs:1634-1670).

AGIWORKFORCE_JWT supplies a Cloud token from the environment (apps/cli/src/app_server/account.rs:122), AGI_AUTH_BASE moves the sign-in host if it resolves to a trusted host (apps/cli/src/app_server/account.rs:287-293), AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING forces files (apps/cli/src/secure_store.rs:14-17).

working: Device-code sign-in to the web origin (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:75, 133, 229; apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1015-1019).
API-key login for a fixed provider list; unknown names are refused (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1060-1290).
Sign-out revokes the device grant and clears the local credential; if revocation is unconfirmed the message says so (apps/cli/src/app_server/account.rs:651-683).
`auth-status` merges stored credentials with credentials found in environment variables (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:881-940).
Secrets go to the OS keychain on macOS and Windows and owner-only files on Linux or when AGIWORKFORCE_NO_KEYRING is set (apps/cli/src/secure_store.rs:1-21).
`-C/--repo` resolves `~`, canonicalises, requires a directory and runs before config and trust (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5871-5897, 5968-5972).
`--add-dir` registers extra roots, refuses network roots and missing folders (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6080-6083; apps/cli/src/path_security.rs:52-100).
Config order: user file, then project file (narrow-only), then environment, then managed policy (apps/cli/src/config.rs:709-728).
A project provider with a non-loopback URL needs consent (apps/cli/src/config.rs:622-690).
A repository config cannot loosen permission mode or change privacy mode (apps/cli/src/config.rs:731-780).
incomplete: Headless runs in an untrusted folder stop with an error instead of falling back to global config only (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6160-6167).

errors.rs describes `agi login <provider>` for openai and anthropic as opening a vendor subscription sign-in (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:495-499), but the code prompts for an API key for them (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1276-1279); the copy helper is not about current behaviour [inferred].
Copilot sign-in refuses with a message (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1273-1275, 1135 const).
disconnected_or_disabled: Legacy `~/.agiworkforce/auth.toml` is mentioned as a fallback source in tier_cache docs (apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:19-24); whether it is still read is unknown.
not_available: No browser-less password sign-in. Other apps use their own sign-in (SYS-authentication-and-identity).

established.statement: The CLI can sign in, sign out and show authentication status (`agi login|logout|auth-status`, `/login`, `/logout`).
The user can point a run at another repository or add extra working folders (`-C/--repo`, `--add-dir`, `/add-dir`).
Settings are read from a global config file with per-project overrides and can be displayed.
Environment variables override configuration (model, provider, max tokens, API base, plain mode) and the override is shown.
Security behaviour fails closed; a repository config must not silently route prompts to a third-party server.

acceptance_criteria: `agi login` prints a link and code and, once approved, `agi auth-status` lists an agiworkforce entry.
`agi login <provider>` stores a key; `agi auth-status` shows it with type and status.
`agi logout` removes the account sign-in but keeps provider keys; `agi logout --all` asks first and removes keys.
`agi -C <dir> exec ...` runs with <dir> as working folder; a non-directory fails with `--repo ...: not a directory`.
A relative AGIWORKFORCE_HOME is refused with a clear error.
A project config with a remote provider URL is dropped or asked about before use.
`/config` lists env overrides such as AGIWORKFORCE_MODEL.
inferred: Local mode should need no sign-in (policy: doc: docs/product/definition.md says sign-in is a separate question from payment) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Make a headless run in an untrusted folder fall back to global config and say so, or return a configuration exit code.
[proposed] Reconcile the vendor-subscription copy helper with the API-key login.

steps.what_happens: `agi login` requests a device code from the web origin.
User approves in a browser on the AGI site.
CLI polls the token endpoint, then stores the grant locally.
For own-key, a hidden prompt reads the key and saves it to the keychain or an owner-only file.
On sign-out the device grant is revoked on the server and cleared locally.
At each launch config is loaded, merged and env overrides applied.

data.what: Account device grant and refresh credential
data.where_stored: OS keychain (macOS, Windows) or owner-only file under the config folder (Linux or no-keyring)
data.synced: No; the server holds the grant it issued
data.retained_or_deleted: Removed on logout; server revoke attempted

data.where_stored: Same secure store; auth.json holds provider names only

data.synced: A separate `agi sync` command exists; not part of this feature

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Own-key login accepts these provider ids, matching folder names under packages/ai/providers where they exist: anthropic, openai, google, xai, deepseek, minimax, perplexity, qwen, moonshot, zhipu, openrouter, nvidia, plus ollama-cloud, brave and tavily (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1060-1135). Whether the Rust CLI reads the TypeScript provider packages is not shown; it uses its own models module [inferred].

access_and_usage.account: Sign-in is needed only for Cloud; Local and own-key runs need none [inferred from apps/cli/src/models/provider_dispatch.rs:395-440].
access_and_usage.permissions: Project config needs folder trust and managed policy allowance (apps/cli/src/config.rs:826-844); managed policy overrides everything (apps/cli/src/config.rs:709-728).
access_and_usage.subscription: Sign-in itself needs no plan; the plan decides which Cloud models and surfaces work (doc: docs/product/definition.md:294-301).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Device-code polling honours the server's interval and expiry (apps/cli/src/oauth.rs:511-520). Rate limits on the web endpoints: unknown.
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_AUTH_BASE only resolves if it names a trusted AGI host (apps/cli/src/app_server/account.rs:287-293).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: none found in the code.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Copilot sign-in is unavailable (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1273-1275). Unknown provider names are refused (apps/cli/src/auth.rs:1280-1283).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Local models need no login. A Local privacy setting also stops Cloud calls such as the update check and remote features (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:122-134; apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:368-373).

features.summary: The CLI (surface:cli only) is installed by a script served from the web site that verifies a signed checksum list before installing. `agi update` compares versions and can replace itself. `agi doctor` prints a local setup report. `agi completion bash|zsh|fish` prints a completion script. The CLI is partial until a first signed release is published.

purpose.what_it_does: The installer detects the platform, finds the newest release through /api/releases/cli/latest, downloads the archive and signed checksum list from GitHub, verifies them, checks the binary reports the right version, and installs it (apps/web/public/install.sh:111-300). `agi update` reads the same feed and can verify and swap the binary (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6559-6580, 4952-4992; apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:751-803). `agi doctor` runs local checks (apps/cli/src/doctor.rs:59-76). `agi completion` prints scripts from clap (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:740-743, 6631-6634).
purpose.why_it_exists: People need a safe way to install and keep the CLI current, find setup problems, and use tab completion (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md S72.26, S72.35, S72.36).
purpose.who_uses_it: New users installing the CLI, maintainers updating it, and support staff reading doctor output.
problems_solved: Installing unverified bytes.
Being on an old build without knowing.
Not knowing why the CLI fails on this machine.
Typing long commands without completion.
use_cases: `curl -fsSL https://agiworkforce.com/install.sh | bash` on a new laptop.
`agi update --check` in CI to detect an outdated runner.
`agi doctor --json` attached to a support request.
`agi completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_agi`.

where_to_find_it: surface:cli commands `agi update [--check] [--install] [-y]`, `agi doctor [--json] [--export]`, `agi completion <bash|zsh|fish>` (alias `completions`), hidden-by-deprecation `--completions <SHELL>` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:812-826, 852-858, 1067-1076, 7821-7824). Installer at https://agiworkforce.com/install.sh, served from apps/web/public/install.sh with a rewrite in apps/web/next.config.ts:238. The web surface list shows the CLI as `Coming soon` (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts:9).
prerequisites: Installer: bash, curl, openssl; tar or unzip; glibc 2.35 or newer on Linux; no musl (apps/web/public/install.sh:96-110, 147-153).
Update --install: a release for this platform (macOS or Linux, arm64 or x64), openssl and tar on a trusted PATH, write access to the install folder (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:243-253, 751-770).
At least one published signed release; today unknown (see unknowns).
screens_and_controls: Installer options `--version`, `--install-dir`, `--no-modify-path` (apps/web/public/install.sh:3-8, 59-79).
`agi update` prints Running and Published lines and a verdict (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:240-267).
`agi update --install` prints what will be replaced and asks `Install agi <version> into <dir>?` unless -y (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:4966-4985).
`agi doctor` prints `AGI doctor` with checks and an overall status (apps/cli/src/doctor.rs:132-150).
journey: 1. Run the installer one-liner.
2. It prints platform, version and directory, downloads, verifies the signature and checksum, and installs agi and agiworkforce (apps/web/public/install.sh:307-330).
3. It adds the install folder to the shell profile unless told not to (apps/web/public/install.sh:261-285).
4. Run `agi doctor` to check setup.
5. Later run `agi update`; if newer, run `agi update --install` and confirm.
6. Add completion with `agi completion zsh`.
feedback_and_outputs: Installer errors such as `No signed AGI CLI release is published yet.` (apps/web/public/install.sh:133).
Update verdicts: up to date, update available with install command, newer than published, or cannot compare (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:240-267).
Startup notice `agi <v> is available (you have <v>)...` in the full-screen screen (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:312-323).
Doctor JSON with version, generated_at, cwd, summary and checks (apps/cli/src/doctor.rs:41-47).
settings: `updates.check_on_startup` in config (apps/cli/src/config.rs:109-116); AGIWORKFORCE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:29-30, 120-134).

working: Installer verifies a signature over the checksum list against a public key pinned in the script, optionally verifies a Sigstore bundle when cosign exists, checks the archive checksum, and refuses a build that reports a different version (apps/web/public/install.sh:147-200, 250-300).
Installer refuses musl and old glibc, handles Rosetta, adds PATH to the right profile (apps/web/public/install.sh:82-110, 232-285).
With no release the feed returns 404 and the installer says so (apps/web/app/api/releases/cli/latest/route.ts:12-17; apps/web/public/install.sh:133).

The feed advertises a release only when its archives and signed manifest are publicly retrievable (apps/web/lib/releases/github-cli-releases.ts:107-150; test apps/web/lib/releases/__tests__/cli-release-reachability.test.ts).
`agi update` reads /api/releases/cli/latest with a 5 second timeout (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:26, 805-835) and `--check` exits 1 when a newer release exists (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6573-6578).

`agi update --install` verifies the signed manifest with the key built from install.sh, checks the SHA-256, verifies reported versions, swaps files with backup and rollback (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:459-470, 751-803, 640-740).
It refuses package-manager installs, desktop-bundled copies and Windows (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:196-262).
Startup update check runs in the background, only when updates.check_on_startup is true, privacy is not Local and the env switch is off (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:122-160).
`agi doctor` runs ten groups of checks and always prints a report; live network probes are skipped (apps/cli/src/doctor.rs:59-76, 682-708).
`agi completion` supports bash, zsh and fish (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:728-743).
incomplete: Per the brief, the owner must set the release signing secret, publish the first signed release and mark the CLI available (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md S72.35; doc: audit/partial/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md). The secret and release steps are in doc: docs/runbooks/cli-release.md. Whether a release exists is unknown.

`agi update --install` has no Windows path; it points to Git Bash or WSL (apps/cli/src/update_check.rs:196-203). The installer needs Git Bash, MSYS2, Cygwin or WSL on Windows (apps/web/public/install.sh:9-10).
`agi doctor` has no strict exit status (apps/cli/src/doctor.rs:49-57).
The first draft cites install.sh:31-34; the pinned key block is at install.sh:31-34 by line, and the verifier at 147-160 (apps/web/public/install.sh:31, 147-160).
disconnected_or_disabled: The brief marks the CLI partial and surface-status shows `Coming soon` (apps/web/lib/surface-status.ts:9).
not_available: No package-manager install (the runbook states the CLI ships only through the signed script; doc: audit/decisions/founder-actions.md item 9).
No binary platform signing: no Apple notarization or Windows Authenticode (doc: docs/runbooks/cli-release.md).

established.statement: The CLI can be installed via a published package or script and can check for and install updates itself.
A diagnostics command checks the local setup and prints a human or JSON report.
The CLI generates shell completion scripts for bash, zsh and fish.
The installer and updater accept exactly the same releases (same pinned key).
Releases are tags v-cli-<semver> matching Cargo.toml and are signed in the protected cli-release environment.

acceptance_criteria: With no release published, the installer exits 1 with `No signed AGI CLI release is published yet.`
With a published release, the installer verifies and installs agi and agiworkforce into ~/.agi/bin and reports PATH changes.
A tampered archive or manifest is refused and nothing is replaced.
`agi update` prints Running and Published versions and a verdict.
`agi update --check` exits 1 only when a newer release exists.
`agi doctor --json` prints valid JSON with summary and checks.
`agi completion bash` output defines `_agi()`.
inferred: The CLI status on the web must change from Coming soon only after the first release exists [inferred from the brief's unfinished note].
proposed: [proposed] Make `--check` exit 75 or a dedicated code, not 1, when the feed is unreachable, and keep 1 for outdated.
[proposed] Add `agi doctor --strict` for CI.

features.summary: The CLI (surface:cli only) can copy a cloud coding session into this repository: `agi resume --teleport [id]` checks out the session's branch and loads its history here. `agi remote-control` makes this folder available to AGI Mobile through a relay. Both need a Cloud account; the phone side is outside this area.

purpose.what_it_does: Teleport fetches a cloud Code session, checks out its working branch in a matching clone, and imports the cloud turns as a local session (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2626-2680; apps/cli/src/cloud/code_teleport.rs:119-185). Remote Control registers this folder with a pairing relay and serves the phone's requests to list, start, follow and steer sessions (apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:743-860; apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6659-6679).
purpose.why_it_exists: People start coding work in the cloud or on a phone and want to continue it where their code and tools are (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md S72.30).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers who use AGI Cloud Code sessions or AGI Mobile alongside the terminal.
problems_solved: Moving a cloud session's work onto the local checkout.
Driving a terminal session from a phone.
Avoiding unsafe branch names and repository hooks during checkout.
use_cases: `agi resume --teleport` in a clone, pick an open session, keep working locally.
`agi resume --teleport <id>` from a script that knows the id.
`agi remote-control` at a desk, then scan the code with the phone.
A phone starts a session in this folder and approves a command.

where_to_find_it: surface:cli: `agi resume --teleport [SESSION_ID]` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:915-927), `agi remote-control` alias `rc` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:894-896). Phone side: AGI Mobile, Remote, Scan (text printed by apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:700-742). Not on other apps; the surface-feature matrix lists CLI Remote control as absent, which contradicts the code (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:562-570).
prerequisites: Cloud account signed in (`agi login`) and the account privacy setting Managed; Local and own-key settings are refused (apps/cli/src/cloud/client.rs:368-373; apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:767-770).
Teleport: a clean checkout of the session's GitHub repository with a matching remote, and the branch pushed to GitHub (apps/cli/src/cloud/code_teleport.rs:119-165).
Remote Control: a paid plan (server check) and a working relay (see unknowns) (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:57-75).
screens_and_controls: Teleport picker: numbered list `1. <title>  <branch>` and `Teleport which session? ` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2677-2735); needs a terminal.
Remote Control text: `Remote Control is on for <folder>.`, a QR code, a pairing line, and warnings that anyone with the code controls sessions until stop (apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:700-742).
journey: Teleport: 1. Open a terminal in a clone of the repository. 2. Run `agi resume --teleport` and pick a session (or pass its id). 3. The CLI fetches and checks out the branch. 4. It imports the history and opens the session. 5. New work stays local; push the branch to share it.
Remote Control: 1. Run `agi remote-control`. 2. Scan the QR or paste the code in AGI Mobile. 3. Start or follow sessions from the phone. 4. Press Ctrl+C to stop.
feedback_and_outputs: After teleport: `Checked out|Updated <branch> from <remote> and loaded '<title>' (N turns). New work here stays on this computer; push the branch to share it.` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2648-2672).
Remote Control status lines: connected, phone disconnected, reconnecting, phone needs update, off (apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:700-742).
settings: AGIWORKFORCE_API_BASE selects the web origin used for pairing (apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:162-166).
Account privacy mode in config (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2617-2622).

working: Teleport validates the branch name, requires the matching GitHub remote, refuses a dirty tree, fetches with a pinned refspec while disabling the repository's hooks, then checks out or fast-forwards (apps/cli/src/cloud/code_teleport.rs:57-185).
Teleport imports cloud turns as a local session `code-<id>`, keeps a richer local copy if one exists, and preserves local-only turns (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2626-2674).
Without an id it lists the repository's open sessions and asks for a number; without a terminal it refuses and names the id route (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2677-2735).

Remote Control requests a pairing from the web app, registers over an encrypted relay URL, serves the phone, reconnects with backoff 1 to 30 seconds, and ends the pairing on a revoked or expired state (apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:22-35, 743-860).
Only Managed sessions are shared; Local and own-key sessions stay off the phone (apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:737-739, 1337-1360).
incomplete: Teleport is a one-way copy, not a live attachment: the cloud session keeps its own state and local work is not sent back (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2668-2672). S72.30 says `attach ... and continue it` (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/072-cli-and-terminal-application.md).

The relay host reached by the mobile app returns a missing deployment and the Remote Control relay needs a founder action (doc: audit/decisions/founder-actions.md:277-287); the CLI-side check of whether the host in use is the fixed one: unknown.
docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:562-570 says CLI remote control is absent; the code exists (apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs). The doc is stale.
disconnected_or_disabled: Remote Control may be hidden in the first mobile release (doc: owner decision recorded in project memory, not a repo file; treated as unknown here).
not_available: No attach to a session on another device other than via the cloud Code session list or the phone relay; no direct device-to-device attach (not found).

established.statement: The terminal can attach to a session that lives elsewhere (another device, the cloud or a running remote agent) and continue it.
Remote Control and connectors come with paid plans only.
Local and own-key sessions never travel through the account relay.
Pairing credentials must be sent only to a secure origin.

acceptance_criteria: `agi resume --teleport <id>` in a clean matching clone leaves the repo on the session's branch with its history loaded.
A branch name such as `--upload-pack=...` is refused before git runs.
A dirty working tree stops teleport with a message listing changed files.
Running teleport with a Local or own-key privacy setting is refused with a not-managed message.
`agi remote-control` prints a code and QR, and a phone connects and lists sessions.
Ctrl+C stops Remote Control and ends the pairing.
A free plan account is refused pairing with an upgrade message.
inferred: Teleport should work without GitHub for non-GitHub repositories; today it requires a GitHub repository URL [inferred from code_teleport.rs:119-128].
proposed: [proposed] Add a way to push local turns back to the cloud session, or rename the feature `copy` in copy text.
[proposed] Correct the surface-feature matrix entry for CLI remote control.

features.summary: Main chat of the AGI Workforce VS Code extension. It lives in the AGI Code activity-bar view or in an editor tab titled AGI Chat. It sends turns to a local developer runtime on the machine and shows loading, setup-needed, trust and error states with retry. Only the VS Code app has it.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the VS Code extension a graphical chat. A person types a request, the extension starts a turn on a local runtime (the AGI CLI run as an app server) for the open folder, and the reply streams back into the panel. The same chat can sit in the side panel or open as a tab beside code. It also shows what the runtime is doing: checking, needing setup, waiting for a folder, or blocked by workspace trust.
purpose.why_it_exists: Developers want to talk to the assistant without leaving the editor, with the code and the folder they already have open. The brief requires a sidebar chat, an editor-adjacent chat and clear loading, setup-needed and error states with retry (brief S73.01, S73.02, S73.28).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using the AGI Workforce VS Code extension. Testers of the extension. Not available in Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI or Chrome as this feature.
problems_solved: No need to switch to a browser or terminal to ask about code.
A setup problem (no CLI, no folder, untrusted folder) is shown as a state with a button instead of a silent failure.
A failed turn gets an error category and a retry when resending could work.
use_cases: Open the AGI Code view and ask how a function works.
Open the chat in an editor tab beside the file being changed.
Open a folder that is not trusted yet and be told to trust it before chat can start.
Hit a rate limit or provider error and press retry.

features.summary: In the VS Code extension, the chat adds what the person is looking at to each turn: the open file, the selected code and the file's problems, shown as removable chips. Unsaved and untitled text is read from the editor. Credential, ignored or excluded files are withheld.

purpose.what_it_does: Builds context from the active editor before each turn and shows it as chips above the composer. The person can dismiss a chip. The chat host reads unsaved text from the buffer, lists problems reported by language tools, and can add git changes and the latest terminal output from a menu.
purpose.why_it_exists: So the assistant sees the code in front of the person without copy and paste, and sees unsaved edits instead of a stale file on disk (brief S73.05, S73.06, S73.07, S73.10).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using the VS Code extension chat.
problems_solved: Pasting code into chat.
The model reading an old saved file instead of current edits.
Secret files being sent by mistake.
use_cases: Ask 'why does this fail' with the file and its error list already attached.
Select a function and ask for an explanation.
Ask about a new untitled scratch file.
Work in a repo where .env files must never be sent.

features.summary: In the VS Code chat composer, typing @ and a name searches workspace files, folders and code symbols. Picking a result attaches that file or that symbol's line range to the turn. Credential and git-ignored paths are not offered. Only the VS Code extension has it.

purpose.what_it_does: Offers a list while the person types @query. Results are symbols from language servers, folders and files. The chosen item travels as a workspace reference carrying a relative path and an optional line range.
purpose.why_it_exists: To point the assistant at exact code without pasting it, and to send only a symbol's lines instead of a whole file (brief S73.08, S73.09).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using the VS Code chat.

features.summary: In the VS Code extension, grey ghost-text code suggestions appear while typing (off by default, needs an AGI sign-in or key and an AGI Cloud model). Fix and Refactor on selected code ask AGI Cloud for a rewrite and apply it in place or open it in a tab. Local models are refused for suggestions.

purpose.what_it_does: Two related editor helpers. Inline suggestions send nearby code to AGI Cloud and show the answer as ghost text. Fix and Refactor take selected code, ask a model for a replacement and replace the selection if the file is unchanged and trusted.
purpose.why_it_exists: Developers expect completion while typing and one-step rewrite of a selection (brief S73.11, S73.12).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers who turn the setting on and sign in; anyone using the Fix and Refactor menu items.
problems_solved: Typing boilerplate.
Cleaning or fixing a block without leaving the file.
use_cases: Accept a suggestion for the next line.
Select a buggy function and choose Fix.
Select code and choose Refactor, then pick 'Apply inline' or 'View in new tab'.
Work in a repo that opts out of completions.

prerequisites: For suggestions: setting turned on in user settings, a first-run notice acknowledged, a browser sign-in or AGI API key, a trusted workspace, a saved file on disk, and a default model that is an AGI Cloud model.
For Fix and Refactor: a non-empty selection and an AGI Cloud default model (runInlineCommand.ts:43-60, 100-110).

working: Provider registered for file-scheme documents only after the setting is on and the notice was shown (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/providerSetup.ts:79-107).
Provider skips untitled, non-file, sensitive or secret-named, credential-path, excluded and outbound-refused documents (inlineCompletionProvider.ts:179-189).
Local default model returns no suggestion and shows a one-time notice (inlineCompletionProvider.ts:190-199).
Needs at least 3 typed characters on the line and a harmless remainder after cursor (inlineCompletionProvider.ts:29, 206-212).
Sends at most 80 lines before and 20 after, and 6000 characters before (inlineCompletionProvider.ts:30-35, 52-80).
Debounce, small LRU cache (16 entries, 15 s) and cancellation (inlineCompletionProvider.ts:36-37, 217-261).
Limit, service-unavailable and auth failures pause suggestions for a time and show one notice (inlineCompletionProvider.ts:309-334).

Fix and Refactor apply through applyLlmEdit, which refuses when untrusted, closed, or the document version changed, and then opens the result in a new tab (apps/extension-vscode/src/platform/applyEdit.ts:42-73).
With a Local default model, Fix and Refactor do not edit in place; they send a prompt to the chat instead (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/runInlineCommand.ts:100-110).
Plan mode asks before running (runInlineCommand.ts:112-123).

disconnected_or_disabled: Inline suggestions are off by default (package.json:1369-1371).

not_available: Not in other apps; n/a in the brief.

established.statement: Ghost-text inline code suggestions appear while typing and can be accepted with Tab.

features.summary: In the VS Code extension, changes the assistant proposes open in VS Code's own diff editor, where the person can edit the text and accept or reject. Suggested code blocks become reviewable in-file diffs with Accept and Reject controls, shortcuts and confirmed bulk actions. Hunk-by-hunk partial acceptance was not found.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows what the agent wants to write before it writes it. An approval request for a file change opens a native two-sided diff whose right side is editable. A code block from chat can become an in-file diff with CodeLens Accept and Reject.
purpose.why_it_exists: The person must stay in control of edits to their code (brief S73.13 to S73.15; doc: AGENTS.md section 9 says irreversible actions ask first).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using agent mode or applying code blocks in the VS Code extension.
problems_solved: Blind file writes.
Applying stale edits over newer text.
use_cases: Review an agent's proposed file edit and tweak it before approving.
Apply a chat code block to the open file as a diff.
Reject every pending change at once.
Restore changes rejected by mistake.

aliases: Continue This Session in the Terminal
features.summary: In the AGI Code VS Code extension, the person can have the last terminal command and its output explained in chat, attach that output to a chat message, ask for safe command suggestions, run a command in a terminal, and hand a chat session to the AGI CLI in a terminal. VS Code only.

purpose.what_it_does: Links the VS Code integrated terminal to the chat. It reads the latest command and output from the active terminal (when VS Code shell integration is on), sends it to chat for explanation, offers validated command suggestions, runs commands in a terminal named Code, and starts the AGI CLI in a terminal named AGI to resume the current chat session.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief says the extension should work with the integrated terminal: run, suggest and explain commands, and continue a session in a terminal (S73.16). People hit errors in the terminal and want help without copying text by hand.
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using the AGI Code extension in VS Code, in local or remote windows.
problems_solved: Copying a long failing command output into chat by hand
Not knowing what a terminal error means
Moving a chat session into the CLI without losing the session id
Running an AI-suggested command without review
use_cases: A test run fails in the terminal; the person runs Code: Explain Terminal Output and reads the cause and fix in chat.
Shell integration is off; the person pastes the output into the input box and gets the same explanation.
The person uses Code: Suggest Terminal Command, picks a validated suggestion and confirms it before it runs.
The person finishes a chat in the sidebar and runs Code: Continue This Session in the Terminal to keep working in the CLI.

where_to_find_it: VS Code only. Command Palette titles: 'Code: Explain Terminal Output' (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:335-336), 'Code: Suggest Terminal Command' (package.json:340-341), 'Code: Run Terminal Command' (package.json:325-326), 'Code: Continue This Session in the Terminal' (package.json:808-810).
Right-click menu inside a terminal: the entry for agi-workforce.addTerminalOutputToChat (package.json:1046-1050, command defined at package.json:238).
Composer context chip for terminal output, which is unavailable until a command has run with shell integration (apps/extension-vscode/src/data/composerContext.ts:347-352).
Explain Terminal Output has no editor or terminal menu entry; only the palette (no other package.json hit for explainTerminal besides the definition at line 335).
prerequisites: A trusted workspace. Explain Terminal Output refuses in an untrusted workspace (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/editor-utilities/editorUtilities.ts:142-146 with apps/extension-vscode/src/core/outboundContentGuard.ts:15).
VS Code shell integration in the terminal to read output automatically; otherwise the person pastes it (apps/extension-vscode/src/providers/terminalProvider.ts:305-323).
Continue in Terminal needs a started chat session, an open folder and an AGI CLI that runs (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:466-493).
Suggest Terminal Command needs a Cloud model; a Local model is refused (apps/extension-vscode/src/providers/terminalProvider.ts:194-197).
screens_and_controls: Input box titled 'Code, Paste Terminal Output' with placeholder 'Paste terminal output here…' (terminalProvider.ts:311-316).
Quick pick 'Code, Suggested Commands (AI-generated, verify before running)'; blocked commands show 'BLOCKED' and 'This command will NOT be run.' (terminalProvider.ts:232-255).
Modal warning 'Run the following command in your terminal?' with button 'Run Command' (terminalProvider.ts:270-274).
Warning with button 'Install AGI CLI' when the CLI cannot be found (commandSetup.ts:500-515).
Info message 'send a message first, then the terminal can pick this session up.' when there is no session (commandSetup.ts:468-473).
journey: 1. Run a command in the integrated terminal.
2. Open the Command Palette and choose 'Code: Explain Terminal Output'.
3. The extension reads the last command, its output and its exit code from the active terminal (terminalProvider.ts:283-291).
4. If nothing was captured, an input box asks for pasted output; an empty answer cancels (terminalProvider.ts:311-322).

5. The prompt 'Explain this terminal output. If it failed, say what went wrong and how to fix it.' with the output in a code fence goes to the sidebar chat and the chat view is revealed (editorUtilities.ts:142-153; apps/extension-vscode/src/extension.ts:278-290).
6. The answer streams in chat as a normal turn.
7. To continue in the CLI, run 'Code: Continue This Session in the Terminal'; a terminal named AGI opens in the folder and runs the CLI with --resume and the session id (commandSetup.ts:491-493).
feedback_and_outputs: A chat turn with the explanation.

Warnings: 'No terminal output to explain.' for empty output (editorUtilities.ts:143); the untrusted-workspace refusal text (outboundContentGuard.ts:6-7); 'The chat view is not available in this window. Reload the window and try again.' (editorUtilities.ts:31-35).

For the attach action: 'no command output has been captured in the active terminal. Run a command in a terminal with shell integration, then try again.' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/sidebarProvider.ts:328-334).
The attached context item is named 'Terminal: <terminal name>' (composerContext.ts:185).
settings: agiWorkforce.useTerminal makes 'Code: Open Chat' start the CLI in a terminal instead of the native chat (package.json:1472; apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:1126-1129). It is listed as not overridable by an untrusted folder (package.json:65).
agiWorkforce.cliPath selects the CLI that Continue in Terminal and sign-in commands run (package.json:1232).
agiWorkforce.terminal.usePythonEnvironment activates the workspace Python environment in new AGI terminals (package.json:73; apps/extension-vscode/src/platform/agiTerminal.ts:26-47).

working: Capture of the latest shell execution per terminal: command line (only when VS Code reports high confidence), output with control codes stripped, exit code, running state; dropped when the terminal closes (apps/extension-vscode/src/providers/terminalProvider.ts:82-99, 293-303, 338-345).
Capture stops growing at 8,000 characters and adds '... [output truncated]' (packages/client/ide-runtime/src/terminal.ts:4, 48).
Explain Terminal Output falls back to a paste box (terminalProvider.ts:283-323) and sends one chat prompt (editorUtilities.ts:142-153).

Add Terminal Output to Chat attaches 'Terminal: <name>' and keeps only the last 20,000 characters if longer (apps/extension-vscode/src/data/composerContext.ts:177-188; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/chat-participant/promptReferences.ts:8). [inferred] Because capture stops at 8,000 characters, this 20,000 cut is not reached by captured output.

A terminal named Code is reused only if it is open, not running a command, and inside the workspace folder; otherwise a new one is created with the workspace folder as its working directory (terminalProvider.ts:103-133).

Suggest Terminal Command asks a Cloud model for one to five commands, blocks unsafe ones in a shared validator, needs a modal confirm, and re-checks at the sink (terminalProvider.ts:190-281; packages/client/ide-runtime/src/terminal.ts:670-736).
Run Terminal Command refuses in an untrusted workspace (terminalProvider.ts:135-145).

Continue in Terminal releases the session writer, creates the AGI terminal in the workspace folder and runs the CLI with --resume and a shell-quoted session id (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:466-494; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:6515-6527).
incomplete: The first draft said the output is cut to the last part in the attach path when too long. That path exists, but capture already caps at 8,000 characters, so the two limits differ and only the 8,000 one is visible in practice [inferred] (ide-runtime terminal.ts:4; promptReferences.ts:8).

If releasing the writer fails with an error other than 'stop before terminal', the failure is only logged and the CLI still starts (ChatStateManager.ts:6519-6526). Effect on a live session is unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: Explain Error (agi-workforce.explainError, package.json:345-346) is not a terminal feature. It reads editor diagnostics around the cursor, so it is outside this feature even though the first draft listed it (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/editor-utilities/editorUtilities.ts:68-85; apps/extension-vscode/src/providers/errorExplainerProvider.ts:16-19).
Explain Terminal Output has no menu placement, only the palette (package.json search).
not_available: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI and Chrome do not have this feature (brief S73.16: status vscode only).
Output of commands run before shell integration started, or in terminals without shell integration, cannot be read; the person must paste it (terminalProvider.ts:305-309).

established.statement: The extension works with the integrated terminal: run, suggest and explain commands and continue a session in a terminal.
VS Code is a thin client over the CLI-hosted developer session; do not add a second execution or persistence owner in the extension.
Moving selected context between Cloud and a local developer session is an explicit handoff with consent where the trust boundary changes.

acceptance_criteria: With shell integration on, after a failing command, 'Code: Explain Terminal Output' sends a chat prompt containing the command line, the output and the exit code.
With shell integration off, the same command opens 'Code, Paste Terminal Output'; pasting text sends that text; cancelling or empty input sends nothing.
In an untrusted workspace, Explain Terminal Output and Run Terminal Command send or run nothing and show the trust message.
A suggested command that fails the validator is shown as BLOCKED and cannot be run even if picked.
'Code: Continue This Session in the Terminal' with no session shows the 'send a message first' message and opens no terminal.
With a started session and a working CLI, a terminal named AGI opens in the workspace folder and resumes the same session id.
A terminal outside the workspace folder is not reused for a new command; a new Code terminal is created in the folder.
inferred: Explanation of terminal text should follow the model chosen in the chat, so Local, own key and Cloud routes behave as in any chat turn [inferred from editorUtilities sending the prompt to the sidebar chat, extension.ts:278-290].
Output sent to a model should be bounded; the 8,000 character capture cap serves that [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Show a small notice when captured output was truncated, so the person knows the model saw only part of it.
[proposed] Add Explain Terminal Output to the terminal right-click menu next to Add Terminal Output to Chat.
[proposed] Align the two output limits (8,000 and 20,000) or drop the unreachable one.

steps.what_happens: VS Code reports a shell execution start and the extension reads its output stream into a bounded buffer.
The person runs Explain Terminal Output; the extension takes the active terminal's last capture or asks for pasted text.
The extension builds the prompt and hands it to the sidebar chat, which runs it as a normal chat turn.

The chat turn is run by the AGI CLI runtime started per workspace; where the model call goes depends on the chosen model route (Local, own key or Cloud). The routing itself was not traced for this feature.
For Suggest Terminal Command the extension sends the request text to the Cloud chat completion API; Local model is refused.
For Continue in Terminal, the extension releases the session writer to the CLI runtime and types the resume command into a terminal.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Explain and attach use whatever model the chat uses. Suggest Terminal Command uses the Cloud utility model only and refuses a Local model (terminalProvider.ts:194-197). No model name is fixed in this feature.

Suggest Terminal Command needs a Cloud account token (apps/extension-vscode/src/utils/api.ts, chatCompletion; exact check not traced). Continue in Terminal needs no sign-in in the extension code opened.
access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace Trust is required for explain and run (outboundContentGuard.ts:15; terminalProvider.ts:136). Credential-file content is refused only for editor documents, not for terminal text.
access_and_usage.subscription: Managed-cloud developer access needs Premium or higher; Free and Basic do not include managed-cloud VS Code access, while Local and own key stay available (doc: docs/product/definition.md:378-382). The per-command plan check for this feature was not found.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Output cap of 8,000 characters at capture and 20,000 at attach (ide-runtime terminal.ts:4; promptReferences.ts:8). Usage metering follows the chat turn; not traced.
access_and_usage.flags: none found in the code for this feature.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Explain and attach: any chat model. Suggest Terminal Command: Cloud models only.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: none found in the code, except that Suggest Terminal Command rejects a Local-route model.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Explain Terminal Output and Add Terminal Output to Chat go through the chat, so they can use a Local model [inferred]. Suggest Terminal Command is refused with a message when the selected model is Local (terminalProvider.ts:194-197, 412-418). Continue in Terminal runs the local CLI and needs no cloud call.

features.summary: AGI Code in VS Code puts its actions in the Command Palette, gives common actions keyboard shortcuts, shows a bottom-right status-bar item with the model and the mode that opens the model picker, and lets the person pick model, agent mode and reasoning effort. VS Code only.

purpose.what_it_does: Provides the command, shortcut and status-bar entry points for the extension and the controls for the model, the agent permission mode and the reasoning effort.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires every action in the Command Palette (S73.17), default shortcuts for key actions (S73.18), a status-bar item showing model and mode that opens the picker (S73.19) and a way to pick model, permission mode and effort (S73.20).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using AGI Code in VS Code.
problems_solved: Finding an action without a toolbar
Seeing at a glance which model and mode are active
Changing the model without opening the chat
Avoiding accidental high-authority modes
use_cases: Click the status-bar item, pick another model and read the scope message.
Press the shortcut for Ask About Code in the editor.
Run 'Code: Choose Agent Mode' and pick Plan before a risky change.
Change agent mode in settings and approve the runtime restart.

where_to_find_it: Command Palette: titles all start with 'Code:' (for example 'Code: Select Model', 'Code: Choose Agent Mode', 'Code: Set Agent Mode', 'Code: Set Reasoning Effort') (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:132-133, 187-188, 469-470, 474-475). The first draft said to type 'AGI Workforce'; the code shows the 'Code:' prefix and the extension display name 'AGI Code' (package.json:4).
Status bar, right side, text like '$(hubot) AGI: <model>' or '$(hubot) AGI: <model> · <mode>' (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/statusBar.ts:3-6; apps/extension-vscode/src/extension.ts:403-412).

Keyboard shortcuts (package.json:1485-1566), for example ctrl+shift+a opens chat, ctrl+shift+alt+g opens agent mode, ctrl+shift+alt+a asks about code, ctrl+shift+alt+x explains an error, ctrl+shift+alt+t runs a terminal command, ctrl+shift+alt+n starts a new conversation, ctrl+n starts a new conversation only when the chat is focused. On Mac the cmd key replaces ctrl.
Settings: agiWorkforce.agent.mode (package.json:1404) and agiWorkforce.agent.effort (package.json:1428).
prerequisites: Extension active (activates on startup finished, package.json:41-52).
For model choices beyond Local: a signed-in plan or own keys; locked choices offer an unlock or upgrade (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:1302-1380).
screens_and_controls: Status-bar item with tooltip 'Code, click to change model' (extension.ts:405).
Quick pick 'Code, Select Model' with placeholder 'Current: <model>' (commandSetup.ts:1319-1323).
Quick pick 'Code, Modes' with Ask, Auto, Plan and Bypass items (commandSetup.ts:1872-1920).
Quick pick 'Code, Effort' (commandSetup.ts:1925-1945).
Modal 'Apply the changed agent permissions?' with button 'Restart Local Runtime' (extension.ts:313-324).
journey: 1. The person clicks the status-bar item or runs 'Code: Select Model'.
2. The picker lists models grouped for the person's plan and route; unreachable, locked or boundary-crossing choices are explained instead of switched (commandSetup.ts:1302-1366).
3. If a switch would lose abilities, a modal asks 'Switch to <model>?' (commandSetup.ts:1355-1366).
4. After a switch the extension says whether this chat or new chats now use the model (commandSetup.ts:1370-1378).

features.summary: In VS Code, AGI Code signals a waiting approval or a finished or failed turn when the chat view is out of sight: an Activity Bar badge, and a pop-up with Allow once, Deny and Open chat when the editor window is not focused. A separate command lists past approval decisions from the account. VS Code only.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows a count badge on the AGI Code Activity Bar icon while the chat is hidden, raises a notification when the whole VS Code window has no focus, lets the person answer a tool approval from that notification, and offers an account-wide approval history list.
purpose.why_it_exists: A turn keeps running while its panel is hidden, so an approval could wait forever with nothing on screen (comment in apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/sidebarProvider.ts:152-159). The brief asks for pending approvals and finished tasks to be signalled when the view is hidden, and for approvals to be answerable (S73.21).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers who start an agent task and switch to another file, view or application.
problems_solved: Missed approval prompts that block a turn
Not knowing a long task ended
Reviewing which tools were approved or denied earlier
use_cases: Start an agent turn, switch to the Explorer; the chat icon shows a badge '1' when approval is needed.
Switch to another application; VS Code shows 'Allow once / Deny / Open chat' for a tool approval.
Run 'Code: Show Approval History' to see decisions made on any AGI client.

Warning pop-up with buttons 'Allow once', 'Deny', 'Open chat' for a tool approval; only 'Open chat' for a question (sessionActivityAlert.ts:36-52).
Info pop-up with 'Open chat' for a finished turn; warning pop-up for a failed turn (sessionActivityAlert.ts:54-62).

journey: 1. The person sends a message that needs an approval.
2. The chat posts an approvalRequested message to the view.
3. The provider counts it into the badge and, if the window has no focus, shows the pop-up (sidebarProvider.ts:165-178).
4. The person clicks Allow once or Deny in the pop-up, or Open chat to review in the chat.

features.summary: In VS Code, AGI Code shows which project instruction files apply (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .agiworkforce/instructions.md) and custom instructions, and lets the person view, add, test, turn off or remove skills, MCP servers and plugins through quick-pick commands run by the AGI CLI. purpose.what_it_does: Shows instruction sources in the Context panel and in 'Code: Show Instructions', and provides Command Palette surfaces to manage skills, MCP servers and plugins, with confirmation before removal.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief says project instruction files apply to turns in the session folder and can be viewed (S73.22), and that MCP servers, skills and plugins can be viewed and managed (S73.23). The product says CLI and VS Code must show the same discovered inventory (doc: docs/product/definition.md:122).

Run 'Code: Show Skills' and turn a skill off.

Settings panel capability lists (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/capabilityManagement.ts:891-960).
prerequisites: A working AGI CLI; the surfaces call it through CliCapabilityAdapter (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/surfaces/cliCapabilities.ts:260).
An open workspace folder for project files.
Removal and install actions appear only when the CLI offers installs (capabilityManagement.ts:221, 288).
screens_and_controls: Context tree items: 'Custom instructions' (host default or workspace override), one item per project file marked 'Runtime source' or 'Runtime source · preview truncated', or 'No active instructions' (contextPanelProvider.ts:229-300).

Quick pick 'Code, Skills' with rows 'Create a skill', 'Install a skill', 'Allow this folder’s project skills' and per-skill turn on or off and remove buttons (capabilityManagement.ts:220-300).
Quick pick for MCP servers with status, transport and scope, 'Test connection' and remove (capabilityManagement.ts:770-870).
Modal 'Remove the skill “<name>”?' with 'Its folder is deleted from your skills, and it stops loading in every workspace. This cannot be undone.' (capabilityManagement.ts:291-294).
journey: 1. Open the Context panel or run 'Code: Show Instructions'.
2. Read the listed files; select one to open it in the editor.
3. For tools, run 'Code: Show Skills', 'Show MCP Servers' or 'Show Plugins'.
4. Pick an item to see its actions; use the toggle, test or remove button.

features.summary: In an untrusted VS Code folder AGI Code keeps the CLI runtime, file reading, commands and inline completions off and points to Manage Trust. It also announces an updated version with a What’s new link, tells forks without native chat that @agi is unavailable, and offers an update when the server rejects an old extension. VS Code only.

purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires limited features and a Manage Trust link in untrusted workspaces (S73.27), an update flow with what changed (S73.29) and clear messages on unsupported editor versions or forks (S73.30). Opening a repository must not run its code.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone opening unknown repositories, and users of VS Code forks.

features.summary: In the Chrome extension, clicking the AGI Extension toolbar button or pressing the open shortcut opens the assistant in Chrome's side panel beside the page. If the browser has no side panel API, a small separate assistant window opens instead. There is no toolbar popup; the brief's popup item is not built.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the Chrome extension one entry point. The toolbar button or a keyboard shortcut opens the assistant (the side panel page side_panel.html) next to the current tab. A right-click action, the in-page 'Open in side panel' button and the welcome flow reuse the same opener. [inferred from shared openAssistantPanel callers] (apps/extension/src/features/surface/assistantPanel.ts:66-73; apps/extension/src/background.ts:7677-7681)
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief says clicking the toolbar button or its shortcut opens the assistant (S74.01) and a side panel hosts the assistant beside the page (S74.03). A popup for quick actions was also asked for (S74.02) but is not built. (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/074-browser-extension.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using the AGI Workforce Chrome extension (Chrome 132 or newer). (apps/extension/manifest.json:87)
problems_solved: The assistant stays visible while the person reads or works on the page, instead of covering it.
Works from the keyboard as well as the mouse.
Browsers without the side panel API still get a usable assistant window (assistantPanel.ts:48-73).
use_cases: Open the assistant while reading an article and ask about it.
Press the shortcut to open the assistant without leaving the keyboard.
Click the toolbar button on a different tab and get the panel for that tab.
On a Chromium browser with no side panel API, get a detached assistant window.
