Other apps (web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code): not applicable.
prerequisites: Chrome 132 or newer (apps/extension/manifest.json:87).
Not a private (incognito) window: the manifest sets incognito to not_allowed (apps/extension/manifest.json:9).
Using chat inside the panel needs a signed-in AGI account; opening the panel does not. [inferred from panel gate states] (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:723-726)
screens_and_controls: Toolbar button 'AGI Extension' with the AGI icon.

Shortcut Alt+Shift+K / Command+Shift+K. The person can change it in Chrome's shortcut settings. [inferred from Chrome behaviour; the options page also has a shortcut rows file apps/extension/src/features/options/keyboard-shortcut-rows.ts that was not read]
Side panel (src/side_panel.html) is the assistant itself.

journey: 1. The person clicks the toolbar button or presses the shortcut.

2. Chrome fires the action click for the active tab. The shortcut is declared as the reserved _execute_action command, which Chrome routes to the same click handler. [inferred from Chrome behaviour] (apps/extension/manifest.json:68; apps/extension/src/background.ts:7677)
3. The background worker calls openAssistantPanel with the tab id and window id (background.ts:7677-7681).
4. If the side panel API exists, Chrome opens the panel for that tab; otherwise an assistant window opens, or the existing one is focused (assistantPanel.ts:48-73).
5. The panel loads, checks the account and shows the chat or a sign-in gate. (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:723-731)
feedback_and_outputs: The side panel appears beside the page.
If opening fails the worker logs 'Opening the assistant from the toolbar failed' and shows nothing to the person. (background.ts:7678-7680)
From the in-page panel, a failure shows 'The side panel could not be opened. Use the AGI icon in the Chrome toolbar.' (apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/panel.ts:434-435)
settings: Shortcut binding is a Chrome setting; the manifest only suggests keys (apps/extension/manifest.json:68-74).
No popup setting exists.

working: Toolbar click opens the side panel for the clicked tab (apps/extension/src/background.ts:7677-7681; apps/extension/src/features/surface/assistantPanel.ts:66-72).
Panel behaviour is set so Chrome does not open the panel by itself on a click: openPanelOnActionClick false, so the click handler is the single opener (apps/extension/src/background.ts:1768-1771).
Fallback assistant window when no side panel API: opens a popup window, or focuses the one already open (assistantPanel.ts:36-64).
In the fallback window the page to work on is the last focused normal browser window (assistantPanel.ts:101-116).
The in-page panel can ask the worker to open the side panel; the worker opens it in the same synchronous turn so Chrome keeps the user gesture (apps/extension/src/background.ts:4489-4505).
incomplete: The toolbar popup (S74.02) is not built: the action block has only icons and a title, no default popup (apps/extension/manifest.json:52-60). Brief status: chrome missing.
disconnected_or_disabled: Chrome's own open-on-click behaviour is deliberately turned off (background.ts:1769).
not_available: Web, desktop, mobile, CLI and VS Code have no such feature (brief items are chrome-only).
Private windows: the extension is not allowed there (apps/extension/manifest.json:9). Messaging for this is missing (S74.26 missing in brief).

features.summary: In the Chrome extension, selecting text and right-clicking offers Ask AGI, Send to a local app, Explain, Translate and (in editable fields) Rewrite. The side panel opens with the selection attached as a chip. Ask waits for the person's question; Explain and Translate fill a prompt that the person sends. Chat uses AGI Managed Cloud.

purpose.what_it_does: Adds right-click menu items that send selected page text into the side panel as attached context, so the person can ask, explain, translate or rewrite it without copying and pasting. (apps/extension/src/background.ts:7452-7461, 7499-7600)
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief says right-clicking selected text offers assistant actions (S74.04) and the user can ask about the selection and get an answer in the extension (S74.05). (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/074-browser-extension.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: People using the Chrome extension who read or edit text on web pages.
problems_solved: No copy and paste between page and assistant.
Quick explain or translate of a passage.
Rewrite text inside a page's editable field.
Hand a selection to a local app instead of cloud chat.
use_cases: Select a confusing paragraph, right-click, choose 'Explain this'.
Select a foreign-language sentence and choose 'Translate this'.
Select text in a text box and choose 'Rewrite selection'.
Select a code snippet and choose 'Send selected text to a local app…' to review and hand it to AGI Desktop, VS Code or the CLI.

where_to_find_it: surface:chrome: Chrome right-click menu on selected text. Labels: 'Ask AGI about "%s"', 'Send selected text to a local app…', 'Explain this', 'Translate this' (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:10-20, 41-44).
surface:chrome: 'Rewrite selection' appears for editable fields (messages.json:5007-5009; apps/extension/src/background.ts:7452-7461).
Other apps: not applicable.
prerequisites: Selected text on an http or https page (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/tabContext.ts:344-350).
For Ask, Explain, Translate and Rewrite: a signed-in AGI account with chat ready (side_panel.ts:16632-16645, 16498-16504 for rewrite).
The site must not be on the person's Blocked sites list (side_panel.ts:16459-16465).
For 'Send selected text to a local app': AGI Desktop reachable through the native bridge, or VS Code or the CLI as the other destinations (apps/extension/src/features/context-handoff/index.ts:19-35).
screens_and_controls: Right-click menu items (above).
Selection chip in the composer, titled 'Selected text · <site>' (messages.json:4089-4090).
Preview card for the local-app handoff with approve, cancel, open in VS Code and copy CLI command (side_panel.ts:16678-16720).

Notices: 'Finish your current draft or remove its attachments, then select the text again.' and 'This selection couldn't be attached. Select text on the page and try again.' (messages.json, keys spSelectionDraftOccupied and spSelectionNotAvailable).
journey: 1. Select text and right-click.
2. Choose an item. The worker stores a pending request with the text, page URL and tab, then opens the side panel (apps/extension/src/background.ts:7556-7600).
3. The panel reads the request, checks that it is under 5 minutes old, belongs to this window and that the tab URL still matches (side_panel.ts:16287, 16562-16630, 16449-16460).
4. The selection is cleaned and bounded, then attached as a chip (side_panel.ts:16466-16490).
5. Ask: the cursor waits in the composer for the question. Explain or Translate: a ready-made prompt is placed in the composer and the person presses send (side_panel.ts:16491-16503).
6. The answer streams into the panel from AGI Managed Cloud.
feedback_and_outputs: A selection chip in the composer.
A notice if the draft is busy or the selection could not be attached.
A browser notification 'Context unavailable' with 'The selected context was not attached. Try again.' if saving the request failed (background.ts:7561-7571).
An answer bubble in the panel.
settings: Blocked sites list in Options (apps/extension/src/features/options/blocked-sites-section.ts).

working: Eight context menu items are built on install, three kinds: selection, editable and page (apps/extension/src/background.ts:7452-7461, 7474-7497).
Ask stores type ask-selection and opens the panel (background.ts:7556-7573).
Explain and Translate store their own types (background.ts:7611-7646).
Rewrite captures the editable target, needs a signed-in account, and shows a notification and an error request if it fails (background.ts:7499-7555).
The panel claims a request only if it targets its own window and is fresh (side_panel.ts:16562-16630).
Selection is redacted and bounded to the page text limit before attach (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/tabContext.ts:344-356).
Send to a local app builds a preview with a 5 minute life and three destinations (features/context-handoff/index.ts:15-35).
incomplete: Ask and Explain do not send by themselves; the person must send, which differs from 'gets an answer' if read as automatic. [inferred] (side_panel.ts:16449-16503)
disconnected_or_disabled: none found.
not_available: Other apps have no such menu.
Selections in browser pages that block extensions (chrome:// pages) cannot be read (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:6402-6404).

established.statement: Right-clicking selected text offers assistant actions.
The user asks about the selected text and gets an answer in the extension.
Page content is untrusted; browser data must not enter global memory or synced chat by default.

acceptance_criteria: Right-click on selected text shows the four selection items; in an editable field it also shows 'Rewrite selection'.
'Ask AGI about' opens the panel with a selection chip and an empty question box.
'Explain this' puts the explain prompt in the composer with the chip attached and does not send.
A request older than 5 minutes is ignored.
If the tab URL changed before the panel read the request, the panel shows a page-changed notice and attaches nothing.
On a blocked site the selection is refused with the blocked-site message.
If the draft already has text or an attachment, the selection is not applied and a notice explains.
inferred: The 'answer in the extension' requirement is met once the person sends. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Offer an optional send-immediately setting for Explain and Translate.
[proposed] Show an in-panel notice when the pending request expires instead of ignoring it silently.

steps.what_happens: The person selects text and picks a menu item; Chrome calls the worker.
The worker writes agi_pending_chat to session storage and opens the panel.
The panel verifies the request, blocklist and tab URL, then attaches the cleaned selection.
When the person sends, the selection and question go to AGI Managed Cloud, which picks a model and streams the answer.

For 'Send selected text to a local app', after approval the text goes to AGI Desktop over native messaging, or to a vscode link, or is copied as a CLI command; nothing goes to AGI servers in that step.

features.summary: In the Chrome extension the person can attach the current page and ask about it, or run Summarize this page, from the side panel or right-click menu. On approved sites an in-page panel offers quick chips, and on YouTube watch pages it summarises a video from its captions. Answers come from AGI Managed Cloud.

purpose.what_it_does: Reads the visible text of the current tab, bounds and redacts it, and sends it with the person's question. Offers a one-click page summary. On YouTube watch pages the in-page panel reads the video's captions and asks for a summary, key timestamps or Q&A. (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:6486-6537; apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/pageActions.ts:58-124)
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief items S74.06 (ask about the current page), S74.07 (one action summarises the page) and S74.08 (ask about a video, answer uses its content). (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/074-browser-extension.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: Chrome extension users reading articles, documents or videos.
problems_solved: No need to paste a page into a chat.
Long pages and videos can be summarised in one click.
The person sees and can remove what was attached.
use_cases: Right-click a page and choose 'Summarize this page'.
Attach the page from the plus menu and ask a specific question.
Open a YouTube video and press 'Summarize video' in the in-page panel.
Ask 'Key timestamps' for a long talk.

established.statement: The user asks a question about the current page from the extension.

The user asks about a video on the page and the answer uses its content.
Page content is untrusted and must not enter global memory or synced chat by default.

acceptance_criteria: 'Add the browser page' on a normal article shows a chip with the page title.
'Summarize this page' sends the summary prompt with the page and a summary appears.
On a chrome:// page the attach is refused with the 'does not let extensions read this page' message.
On a page still loading the attach fails with the try-again message.
On a YouTube watch page with captions 'Summarize video' returns a summary of the video.
On a video without captions the panel says there are no captions.
Text over 30,000 characters is cut and marked as an excerpt.
inferred: The 'page content must not enter synced chat by default' rule is partly met because only chats whose every turn ran in Managed Cloud are mirrored; whether page text inside them is mirrored was not checked. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Read captions in the side panel too, so video summary does not depend on the in-page overlay.
[proposed] Offer a fallback for videos with no captions.

steps.what_happens: The person attaches the page; the panel reads the tab text through Chrome scripting after checking blocklist, loading state and site access.
Text is cleaned of secret-like patterns and capped at 30,000 characters.
On send, the page text and prompt go to AGI Managed Cloud, which chooses the model and streams back the answer.
For video, the content script fetches the YouTube watch page and captions from YouTube itself, builds the transcript, then sends it as the page context.
The answer is shown; in the in-page panel each answer replaces the last, in the side panel it is saved in the conversation.

features.summary: In the Chrome extension the person attaches one or more open tabs as context, from the 'Attach tabs' picker or by typing @ in the composer. Each attached page shows as a chip that can be refreshed or removed. Several tabs are merged into one context, up to five attachments in total. There is no dedicated compare action.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person choose which open tabs of the current window feed the next message, shows each as a chip, and merges their text under Tab headings. (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/tabContext.ts:52-130; apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:1845-1870, 14968-15060)
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief items S74.09 (pick which open tabs to add), S74.10 (compare content across tabs) and S74.12 (attached context shows as a chip that can be seen and removed). The brief marks the picker and comparison missing but the code has them, see gaps. (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/074-browser-extension.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: Chrome extension users researching across several pages.
problems_solved: Compare product pages, docs or articles side by side.
See exactly which pages will be sent.
Remove or refresh one page without losing the others.
use_cases: Open three shop pages, attach them and ask which is cheapest.
Type @ and a few letters of a tab title to attach that tab.
Refresh a chip after the page changed.
Type @ and pick a project to move the chat into it.

3. Choose tabs. Chrome may ask for site access for sites not yet allowed.

steps.what_happens: The picker or @ menu lists tabs from Chrome for the current window.
Chrome shows its site access prompt for pages not yet allowed.
Each tab text is read, cleaned, capped and re-checked for change.
Snapshots are merged into one context string with Tab headings.
On send, the merged text goes to AGI Managed Cloud with the question.
The @ menu fetches the person's projects from AGI servers.

features.summary: In the Chrome extension the person keeps several separate chats. A clock icon ('Recent chats') opens a drawer to open, search, pin, rename, move to a project, archive, share or delete a chat; a new-chat icon starts another. Chats are saved in the browser and chats run only in Managed Cloud can be mirrored to the AGI account.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores each conversation locally under the signed-in account, lets the person switch between them, and organises them. Cloud-eligible chats are synced to the AGI account so they appear on other apps. (apps/extension/src/features/background/conversation-history.ts:41-60; apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:11523-11547, 12807-12960)
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief item S74.11: the user keeps several separate conversations in the extension and switches between them. (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/074-browser-extension.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: Chrome extension users who work on several topics.
problems_solved: Return to an earlier chat after closing the panel.
Keep topics apart.
Continue the same chat on the web or phone.
use_cases: Open yesterday's research chat from Recent chats.
Pin an important chat to the top.
Archive finished chats.
Search by words in a chat when the list is long.

The drawer reads the local store and, when opened, asks the account for recent chats to merge.

features.summary: In the Chrome extension, AGI asks for a site's access before it reads or acts there. A card offers 'Allow for this task', 'Always allow on this site' (acting only) or 'Decline'. In Options the person sets the Browser control mode (Auto, Ask first, Full access, YOLO), approves sites and lists blocked sites. Organisation policy can override.

purpose.what_it_does: Controls which sites the extension may read or act on. It asks Chrome for host access, keeps one-time grants temporary, keeps lists of approved and blocked sites, applies an optional organisation policy, and sets how often AGI asks before acting. (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:7785-8030; apps/extension/src/features/options/site-permission-policy.ts; apps/extension/src/features/site-policy/store.ts)
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S74.13: before reading a site the extension asks Chrome for that site's access explicitly. S74.14: the user reviews and changes which sites the extension may use and how. (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/074-browser-extension.md) Requirements ask for per-site allow/deny prompts and an allowlist/blocklist (doc: docs/product/requirements.md lines 1200-1215).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every Chrome extension user who reads pages or uses browser control; organisation admins who set a site policy.
problems_solved: No silent access to sites.
Temporary access that ends with the task.
A block list that stops AGI reading or acting on chosen sites.
Admin control over sites.
use_cases: Allow a shopping site for one task only.
Always allow a trusted internal site for browser control.
Block a banking site entirely.
Set Browser control to Ask first to confirm every action.

Options: current site with 'Add' or 'Remove', and a 'Grant full browser control' confirmation (options.ts:1380-1560).
Options: 'Blocked sites' with an input 'example.com', add and remove (messages.json:4923-4930; features/options/blocked-sites-section.ts).
Chrome's own site access prompt and chrome://extensions site access list.
prerequisites: Signed in for chat; the card appears during chat turns. Options can be opened from the panel menu (background.ts OPEN_EXTENSION_SETTINGS).
Chrome 132 or newer (manifest.json:87).
Account sites (AGI web, API and sign-in hosts) are refused for browser control (features/computer-use/accountOrigins.ts; options.ts:1527-1531).
screens_and_controls: Access card (read body: AGI can read this page's text and ordinary form values for this task, sent to AGI Cloud, passwords and payment fields excluded; act body: AGI can act through Chrome's debugger, Chrome shows a banner) (messages.json:4290-4296).
Browser control select with live description and 'Saving…' status.
Consent box for 'Grant full browser control' with headline 'This grants full DevTools-Protocol control' (features/computer-use/browserControlConsent.ts:7-18).
Notices: 'Chrome did not grant access to $HOST$', 'Skipped: you declined access to $HOST$', 'You blocked AGI on $HOST$...' (messages.json:4360-4372, 4913-4915).
journey: 1. A task needs a page. The panel checks the blocked list, then the policy (side_panel.ts:7785-7830).
2. If the site is not already allowed, a card appears in the chat (side_panel.ts:7930-7990).
3. The person chooses. For once or always Chrome shows its own site access prompt (side_panel.ts:7937-7952).

4. If Chrome grants, the task goes on. 'Once' is remembered only for the task and released after it; 'Always' adds the site to the approved list and records browser control consent (side_panel.ts:7971-7980, 7995-8010).
5. In Options the person can later add, remove, block or change the default mode.

Blocked sites (agi_site_blocklist).

Card with once, always (act scope only) and decline choices (features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:1399-1432).

not_available: Other apps have no site permission model of this kind. Private windows: extension not allowed (manifest.json:9). Per-site settings of finer scope than origin (paths) were not found.

established.statement: Before reading a site, the extension asks Chrome for that site's access explicitly.
The user reviews and changes which sites the extension may use and how.
Chrome must include per-site allow/deny prompts and allowlist/blocklist; page content is untrusted; high-impact actions need confirmation.
Auto, the default mode, stops for crucial actions; Ask first confirms every action; no mode completes a purchase.

acceptance_criteria: Asking AGI to read a not-yet-allowed site shows the access card before anything is read.
'Decline' leaves the page unread and tells the person.
'Allow for this task' lets the task read the page and, after the task, the Chrome host access is gone unless it was already there.
A site added to Blocked sites is refused everywhere with the blocked message.

features.summary: In the Chrome extension, a person gives AGI a goal, from the Computer Use tab or a chat message, and AGI clicks, types and reads on the current tab through Chrome's debugger. It runs on AGI Cloud models, only on approved sites, shows a page overlay and a step log, and can be stopped or taken over.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the Chrome extension drive the person's current browser tab to reach a goal they typed. A model on AGI Cloud looks at the page (text and screenshots), picks actions (click, type, navigate, scroll and similar), and the extension carries them out with the Chrome debugger. The person sees each step, can approve risky steps, stop the run, or take the page over and hand it back (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/agentLoop.ts; apps/extension/src/background.ts:6232-6760).
purpose.why_it_exists: Claude and ChatGPT both offer a browser agent. The brief lists three requirements for it: show clearly that the agent is acting, let the person switch into a browser-control mode with a goal, and give a visible Stop or takeover control (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/074-browser-extension.md, S74.15 to S74.17). docs/product/requirements.md:81 lists page automation as a Chrome extension duty (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:81).
purpose.who_uses_it: People using the Chrome extension signed in to AGI Cloud who want AGI to do a web task on a site they approved.
problems_solved: Repetitive multi-step web tasks (find, compare, fill) done by hand
Not knowing whether an agent is acting on a page
Needing to stop an agent or finish a login or captcha step by hand and then return control
use_cases: Type 'find the cheapest direct flight to Denver next Friday' in the Computer Use tab on an approved travel site
Ask in chat to fill a form on the open page and approve each sensitive step
Press Take over to sign in by hand, then Continue so AGI finishes the task
Run an unattended task on an already approved site with the YOLO permission mode

journey: Open the side panel and choose 'Computer Use'.

If the page is a normal site that is not yet approved, press 'Allow browser control on <host>', accept Chrome's site access prompt and read the consent text 'This grants full DevTools-Protocol control' (browserControlConsent.ts:7-17).
Type the goal and press 'Start' or Enter. The Start button is disabled until the site is ready and while a task runs (computerUsePanel.ts:1620-1650).
Chrome shows its debugging banner; the page shows the dock, pointer and corners; the label changes to 'AGI Cloud • agent running' and steps appear in the log.
Approve or skip sensitive steps in approval cards, or add extra details while it runs.
Press 'Take over' (panel or page dock) to pause; the banner says 'Your turn' and 'Choose Continue when you are done'; press 'Continue' to give the page back, or 'Stop' to end the run.
The run ends: completed, stopped (with a reason sentence), or error; the label returns to 'AGI Cloud • powered by AGI'.

A sentence per stop reason, for example 'You stopped the run.' or 'The tab this run was driving was closed.' (computerUsePanel.ts:809-835).

working: Start admission checks: goal required and at most 4096 characters, tab exists and is active, site on the allowlist, browser-control consent, signed in to AGI Cloud, permission mode loaded, model access verified (apps/extension/src/background.ts:6232-6470).

One active run with a lease; starting a new run cancels the earlier one with reason 'superseded' (background.ts:6283-6286; apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/runOwnership.ts, ComputerUseRunCoordinator.begin). The first draft said a second start is refused; the code supersedes instead. The panel disables Start while a task runs, and a start is refused while a paired desktop browser command is active (background.ts:6275-6281).

Run ends on tab closed (background.ts:7710-7718), tab URL leaving the approved page when nothing is in flight and no takeover (background.ts:7720-7745), account change (background.ts:1100-1112, called from GET_CLOUD_AUTH_TOKEN at 5038), site access withdrawn, panel closed (pagehide sends CANCEL_COMPUTER_USE with reason panel_closed, computerUsePanel.ts:1450-1470), debugger bar dismissed (background.ts:6690-6695), worker lost (see F074-11).

Stop: panel sends CANCEL_COMPUTER_USE with run id and reason; button shows 'Stopping…'; a refusal shows 'The run could not be stopped and may still be driving the tab. Close the tab to be certain.' (computerUsePanel.ts:1405-1450; background.ts:7148-7210). The page dock Stop sends AGI_CU_USER_INPUT command stop, checked against run id, top frame and tab (background.ts:6993-7015).

Take over and Continue: PAUSE_COMPUTER_USE and RESUME_COMPUTER_USE (background.ts:7088-7146). Take over lasts at most 15 minutes (USER_TAKEOVER_MAX_MS, runOwnership.ts:17), then the run ends with reason takeover_expired (background.ts:1050-1066). Continue re-checks the site is still approved; if not, the run ends as site_access_withdrawn (background.ts:7120-7134).

Automatic takeover when the person uses the page: real user input on the driven tab while no action is in flight pauses the run with 'You started using the page, so AGI stopped acting on it.' (background.ts:7020-7035; locale key cuTakeoverByInputReason).
The agent can ask the person to take over with the tool ask_user_to_take_over; in unattended mode it reports the step as unfinished instead (agentLoop.ts:1470-1500, 1550-1585).

Approval flow: actions needing approval ask the person; the request times out after 5 minutes and is treated as refused (agentLoop.ts:1320; background.ts:6570-6585). In YOLO mode an action that needs approval is not performed (background.ts:6545).

Chat-started tasks: one browser task at a time per panel ('Another browser task is already running in this panel.'), the task ties to the page and conversation present at start (side_panel.ts:7258-7300, 7340-7376). Unattended (YOLO) chat tasks need the site already approved and Chrome host access, else 'Approve <host> in Permissions before starting an unattended task on this site.' (side_panel.ts:7795-7833).

Panel safety net: if no sign of life for 90 seconds the panel asks the worker whether the run still exists and reports 'The background service stopped reporting on this run, so it is no longer being tracked here.' (computerUsePanel.ts:1020-1040, 1380-1420). A panel reopened mid-run adopts the run and says 'A browser-control run started before this panel was reopened is still active. Use Stop to end it.' (computerUsePanel.ts:1425-1450).
incomplete: The page indicator that names the driven page (sp-agent-page) follows only chat-started tasks (composerBrowserRun); a task started from the Computer Use tab is shown by the step log, the label and the on-page dock instead (side_panel.ts:10857-10885).

Many control labels in the Computer Use panel are English literals in code, not locale keys ('Stop', 'Take over', 'Continue', 'Start', 'Task', 'Clear') (computerUsePanel.ts:1190-1240, 1585-1650). Whether other locales exist for the rest of the panel: unknown.
No file records that the whole flow was run end to end against a live site; apps/extension/e2e/smoke.mjs exists but was not opened.
disconnected_or_disabled: The retained Run Autofill button in the same panel is a separate job-application feature and is not part of this feature (side_panel.ts:14058-14095).
not_available: surface:web, surface:desktop, surface:mobile, surface:cli, surface:vscode: not applicable; the brief marks them n/a (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/074-browser-extension.md:72-85).

mode:local and mode:own-key: no code path found in the extension that runs the agent loop on a local model or with a user's own provider key; the only model call goes to AGI Cloud (cloudAgentClient.ts:317-340).

established.statement: While the agent acts, the extension clearly shows it is acting.
The user switches the extension into a mode where it controls the browser for a goal they give.
A visible control stops the agent or lets the user take over.
The Chrome extension covers browser context, capture, native bridge and page automation.

acceptance_criteria: Start with an empty goal or a goal over 4096 characters is refused with 'AGI_START_COMPUTER_USE: goal is required' or 'goal must be 4096 characters or fewer'.
Start on a site that is not approved is refused and the site card offers 'Allow browser control on <host>'.
While a run is active the label reads 'AGI Cloud • agent running', the on-page dock with Stop and Take over is visible, and Start is disabled.
Pressing Stop ends the run, the panel returns to idle and the sentence 'You stopped the run.' is shown.
Pressing Take over pauses the agent, shows 'Your turn', and Continue resumes it; after 15 minutes without Continue the run ends with the take-over-expired sentence.
Closing the driven tab, navigating it away from the approved page, or changing the signed-in account ends the run with the matching sentence.
In YOLO mode a chat-started task on a site that is not approved is refused before any action.
inferred: The run-id format cu_run_ plus an identifier ties every panel and page message to one run, so a stale panel cannot control a newer run [inferred from COMPUTER_USE_RUN_ID_PATTERN and ownsRun checks].
Browser control must stay on the person's device and use the person's signed-in session only on sites they approved [inferred from the consent text and allowlist checks].

[proposed] Move the panel's English literals into locale keys.
[proposed] Decide whether browser control should have a Local or own-key route, given the product requirement that all three modes are explicit.

steps.what_happens: Person types a goal and presses Start; the panel creates a run id and sends AGI_START_COMPUTER_USE with goal, tab id and the selected model choice.
The worker checks goal length, tab, allowlist, consent, active tab, sign-in, permission mode and model access, then creates the run lease and cancels any earlier run.
Model access and usage are read from AGI Cloud with the person's token.
The loop reads the page and takes screenshots, sends them with the goal to the AGI Cloud chat completions route, and streams back tool calls.
The gateway sends the turn to a model provider chosen by AGI routing. Which provider serves a given turn is not visible in the extension.

steps.what_happens: Each tool call is checked against the approval policy; approval cards go to the panel; approved actions run through the Chrome debugger on the tab; the page dock and pointer show the action point.
Progress, usage and state events are broadcast to the panel; the run ends and the worker clears the marker, releases the debugger and sends a completed, stopped or error state.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The extension asks AGI Cloud for the models the account may use and picks one that supports tools, vision and streaming. With Auto it routes by the browser task profile and drops to another provider if one rejects the call (cloudAgentClient.ts:50-135). No model id is written here; ids come from the generated catalog.

access_and_usage.account: Sign-in to AGI Cloud is required: 'AGI_START_COMPUTER_USE: sign in to AGI Cloud before starting computer use' (apps/extension/src/background.ts:6362-6368).
access_and_usage.permissions: Chrome permissions debugger, tabs, scripting, sidePanel in the manifest; per-site optional host permission requested at approval; the site must be on the approved list and have browser-control consent; user blocked sites and site policy are checked (background.ts:6310-6340; side_panel.ts:13984-14030; apps/extension/manifest.json).
access_and_usage.subscription: The only plan-linked checks found are the models the account may use and gateway refusals: 401 asks to sign in again, 403 'AGI Cloud browser actions are not available for this account.' and 429 'AGI Cloud cannot accept this request right now. Check your usage or try again later.' (cloudAgentClient.ts:345-390). Which plans may use browser control: unknown. The extension does not read the canUseBrowserAutomation capability (grep found none in apps/extension/src).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Goal 4096 characters; 20 steps (DEFAULT_CALLER_TOOL_MAX_STEPS, packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/tool-call-limits.ts:5); take over 15 minutes; approval wait 5 minutes; panel silence check 90 seconds; max_tokens 2048 per turn (cloudAgentClient.ts:326). Usage is metered on the server through the gateway; the panel shows steps and tokens.
access_and_usage.flags: The request carries a header x-agi-managed-compute-beta and the code maps server refusals named public_launch_blocked, managed_compute_private_beta and not_private_beta to a message (cloudAgentClient.ts:333-352). Server-side flag values: unknown.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: A model must support tools, vision and streaming or the run is refused with '<name> does not support browser tools, screenshots, and streaming.' (cloudAgentClient.ts:97-100).

features.summary: Connects the Chrome extension to the AGI desktop app on the same computer. The person starts pairing in the extension's Options page and types a code the desktop app shows. The side panel shows a 'Desktop tools are optional and currently disconnected' notice with Reconnect. Desktop and CLI read the pairing state.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates a trusted link between one Chrome profile and the AGI desktop app: the extension asks the desktop bridge on the local loopback address for a pairing request, the desktop app shows an 8-character code in its own window, the person types it into the extension, and the desktop app issues a token. After that Chrome starts the desktop's native host and the extension answers browser commands from the desktop and the CLI (apps/extension/src/features/native-bridge/pairing.ts; apps/desktop/electron/browser/bridgeServer.ts:401-465).
purpose.why_it_exists: The desktop app and the CLI can use the person's browser only through the extension, and only if the person has agreed on this computer. The brief requires that the extension pairs with the desktop app and shows whether the native host is connected, with a way to reconnect (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/074-browser-extension.md:87-96).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who use both the AGI desktop app (or the CLI) and the Chrome extension on one computer.
problems_solved: Letting desktop chat or the CLI read and act in Chrome without opening an unsafe local door
Knowing whether the desktop link is up
Recovering after Chrome or the desktop app restarts
Removing a pairing from either side
use_cases: Pair Chrome once so desktop chat can screenshot the current page
See 'Paired and answering' in the desktop app before asking for a browser action
Press Reconnect in the side panel after restarting the desktop app
Unpair a browser from the desktop app before selling the computer

surface:cli: no screen; the CLI reads pairing state to decide whether to offer browser tools (apps/cli/src/browser_bridge.rs:209-251).

prerequisites: The AGI desktop app is installed and running with its local bridge listening (default port from BROWSER_BRIDGE_DEFAULT_PORT, packages/contracts/types/src/browser-bridge.ts:15).
The bridge address in the extension is a local one: localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] (apps/extension/src/background/policy.ts:310-326).
Signing in to AGI Cloud is not required to pair; a pairing made while signed out binds to the first account seen later (pairing.ts:236-250).
screens_and_controls: Options row: status text 'Not paired', 'Pairing…', 'Enter the code shown in Desktop', 'Paired' with a fingerprint, 'Pairing failed'; buttons 'Pair with Desktop' (or 'Retry Pairing'), 'Confirm Code', 'Unpair'; code field with placeholder ABCD-EFGH; unpair confirmation 'Unpair the desktop app? Browser actions that run through Desktop stop working until you pair again.' with 'Keep paired' (desktop-pairing-rows.ts:34-197; locale keys spPairing*, optPairing*).
Side panel notice with dot, text and 'Reconnect'.

Desktop web block: 'Install extension', 'Register the browser host again', 'Unpair' with confirmation 'Unpair this browser?', status 'Paired and answering' or 'Paired, not answering right now' (BrowserPairingSection.tsx:100-170).
journey: In the desktop app or web block, nothing needs doing yet.
In Chrome open the extension Options page, go to Account, find 'Desktop app', press 'Pair with Desktop'.

The extension posts to the desktop bridge /pair/request; the desktop app shows the pairing code in a dialog and the status reads 'Enter the code shown in Desktop' (valid for 2 minutes, packages/contracts/types/src/browser-bridge.ts:121).
Type the code and press 'Confirm Code'; the extension posts /pair/confirm and stores the issued token; the desktop host manifest is installed and the extension asks the worker to reconnect.
Status reads 'Paired'; desktop web block reads 'Paired and answering'.
If the link drops, the side panel shows the disconnected notice; press 'Reconnect'.
To remove, press 'Unpair' in Options or in the desktop app.
feedback_and_outputs: Status text and error text in the Options row (aria-live polite).
Side panel notice visible whenever the link is not connected.
Desktop shows fingerprint and state; CLI gets availability Paired, PairedNotAnswering, NotPaired or ShellNotRunning (browser_bridge.rs:209-251).

After an unpair that Desktop could not hear: 'Unpaired in this browser, but Desktop could not be reached to remove the pairing. It is removed the next time Desktop is open while Chrome is running, or you can remove it in Desktop's settings now.' (pairing.ts:31).
settings: Bridge address stored under key agi_bridge_url in store:chrome-storage-local (pairing.ts:300-310); no UI to change it was found.
Paired record under key agi_paired_desktop and flag connectedToDesktop (pairing.ts:21-30).

working: Pairing phases idle, requesting, awaiting-code, confirming, paired, error (pairing.ts:1-11). A failure stores the error and moves to the error phase (pairing.ts:64-68).
Only local bridge addresses are accepted, else 'Pairing is only supported with local desktop bridge' (pairing.ts:316-323; policy.ts:310-326).

Request and confirm are plain fetches with an 8 second timeout and no redirects (pairing.ts:326-352). Desktop binds the pairing to the extension id taken from the request Origin, not from the body (bridgeServer.ts:238-260, 395-400).

Desktop generates a code of 8 characters, expires it after 2 minutes, and limits attempts and pending requests (bridgeServer.ts:141-180, 322-345; browser-bridge.ts:120-121; constants MAX_PAIR_CONFIRM_ATTEMPTS and MAX_PENDING_PAIR_REQUESTS).
A pairing belongs to the signed-in account: if the account changes or signs out the pairing is released and an unpair is owed to Desktop (pairing.ts:112-125, 270-290; background.ts:1515-1545).
Connection uses Chrome native messaging to host com.agiworkforce.browser with a connect handshake carrying the pair token, a session secret and a ping (background.ts:1389, 1990-2050).
Status reaches the side panel by GET_CONNECTION_STATUS at open and CONNECTION_STATUS_CHANGED pushes (side_panel.ts:16264-16276, 15860-15868; background.ts:7428-7450).

GET_CONNECTION_STATUS tries connecting whenever the browser is paired, not connected, not already connecting and has not given up; it pings an existing connection (background.ts:5074-5108). This differs from the first draft, which said once per worker start.

Reconnect back-off: 1 s doubling to a 30 s cap; the timed delays are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 30, 30 seconds; at the 8th scheduling the delay is null, the worker gives up and logs 'Max native reconnect attempts reached; giving up until user action' (reconnect.ts:1-30; background.ts:1698-1735). The give-up flag is saved in session storage so it survives a worker restart (background.ts:1462-1472). Manual 'Reconnect' (RECONNECT_NATIVE) resets it (background.ts:1668-1698).

Permanent errors (host not found, forbidden, not allowed) stop retries, mark Desktop unpaired and release the stored pairing (reconnect.ts:10-17; background.ts:2433-2453). The first draft only said retries stop.

Unpair: the worker tells Desktop while the pairing still authorises the message. If Desktop is unreachable the unpair is recorded as owed, the pairing is released here, and the notice above shows; it is retried at most every 5 minutes. Only when the debt cannot be stored is the pairing kept, with 'Desktop could not be reached, so the pairing was kept. Try again.' (background.ts:1553-1580, 5115-5122; pairing.ts:455-495). The first draft described only the kept case.

Desktop side: bridge routes for pair request, pair confirm and a legacy token-authorised pair; unpair removes the host registration and pairing; dispatcher commands browser_pairing_state, browser_pairing_install_host, browser_pairing_unpair (bridgeServer.ts:905-958; apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:3127-3133).

CLI reads the desktop bridge file and POSTs /client/state with a local token, once per session, and offers browser tools only if paired (apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:1097-1103; browser_bridge.rs:209-251).
incomplete: The operator path with a pasted bridge token exists in code (requestPairing, storeBridgeSecret, header X-Bridge-Token) but no screen or message handler calls storeBridgeSecret; only tests do (grep of apps/extension/src). The error text still tells the person to paste the token 'here' (pairing.ts:411-417).

Desktop copy says to open the side panel and choose 'Connect to Desktop'; the extension has no such label. Pairing starts from Options with 'Pair with Desktop' (BrowserPairingSection.tsx:14-17 vs _locales/en/messages.json spPairingPair).
The side panel Reconnect button has no visible result of its own; failure only goes to the console (side_panel.ts:15646-15649).
disconnected_or_disabled: The bridge-token paste path described above.
not_available: surface:web (outside the desktop app), surface:mobile, surface:vscode: no pairing screen.
mode:local and mode:own-key as AI modes do not apply; this feature is local-only plumbing.

steps.what_happens: Person presses 'Pair with Desktop'. The extension posts its id to the bridge's pair request route on 127.0.0.1 or localhost.
Desktop creates a pending request with a random 8 character code, shows it in a native dialog, and returns only a request id, code length and lifetime.
Person types the code; the extension posts request id and code to the confirm route; Desktop checks code, extension origin and attempts, then issues a token and installs the native host manifest.
The extension stores the token and fingerprint locally bound to the signed-in account and asks the worker to reconnect.
Chrome starts the native host; the worker sends a connect with the pair token, negotiates a session secret, pings, then starts polling for desktop browser commands.
The side panel learns the state from GET_CONNECTION_STATUS and pushes; failures schedule timed reconnects or give up.
CLI and desktop chat read pairing state from the bridge; nothing in this feature calls AGI servers.

features.summary: A microphone button in the Chrome extension's chat composer turns speech into text using the browser's built-in speech recognition, and adds the words to the message box. It shows only when the account allows voice, asks the person to agree before first use, and gives a specific message for each speech error.

purpose.what_it_does: Adds the spoken sentence to the composer text. The browser's speech service does the recognition; the extension receives only the resulting text (_locales/en/messages.json key spVoiceNotice; apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/voice.ts).
purpose.why_it_exists: Claude and ChatGPT let people dictate messages. The brief requires that the user dictates a message by voice where the browser supports it (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/074-browser-extension.md:101-104; doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:68 lists Voice as present on chrome).
purpose.who_uses_it: Extension users who prefer speaking to typing, with a microphone and a Chrome that supports speech recognition.
problems_solved: Typing long messages in a narrow side panel
Hands-busy use
use_cases: Dictate a question about the open page

features.summary: Covers how the Chrome extension behaves at its edges. It explains pages it cannot use and recovers chats and browser runs after Chrome stops its background worker. It does not support private windows or tell people about updates or browser differences. It has no account switcher.

purpose.what_it_does: Tells the person when a page is off limits (Chrome pages, Web Store, blocked sites), keeps chats and browser tasks recoverable or clearly ended when Chrome stops the background worker, keeps the extension out of private windows, and handles first install. It leaves out update notices, private-window messages, browser comparison and an account switcher.
purpose.why_it_exists: Chrome extensions run as short-lived workers and cannot touch some pages. The brief lists six items: account switching (not applicable), unsupported-page explanation, update notice, private-window controls, browser differences and recovery after worker suspension (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/074-browser-extension.md:97-134).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every Chrome extension user, usually without noticing until something fails.
problems_solved: Not knowing why the extension does nothing on a page
Lost or frozen chat streams after Chrome stops the worker
A browser task that seems to run forever
Confusion in private windows or after an update
use_cases: Open the side panel on a Chrome settings page and see 'Page access unavailable'
Leave the panel open for a long chat while Chrome stops the worker and have the stream resume
Have a browser task end with a clear sentence after the worker was stopped
Install the extension and see the welcome page

The card text mentions pages an administrator restricted, but isRestrictedPageUrl tests address prefixes only; administrator policy is handled elsewhere in site policy (surface-policy.ts:36-45) [inferred].

Chat recovery (S74.28): the panel opens a port named by the client instance and sends MANAGED_CHAT_KEEPALIVE every 20 seconds while streaming; if the port drops during a cloud run with a saved run reference the run resumes, otherwise the stream ends with the restart message (side_panel.ts:6905-6990; background.ts:1857-1880).

Browser run recovery (S74.28): a marker written when a run starts is found on the next worker start; the worker stops the page input watch, detaches the debugger, ungroups the tab, and announces an error state with reason worker_restarted; the panel shows the sentence above (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/runMarker.ts:100-130; background.ts:9219-9236; computerUsePanel.ts:826-830). features.summary: Every model in the catalog is recorded as accepting text, producing text, or not. Auto routing for chat tasks only picks models with both text flags. The picker and the model list API only show chat-type models. Image, audio and video models stay out of chat lists.

purpose.what_it_does: Records, per model in the generated catalog, whether it reads text and writes text. Chat-style routing tasks require both flags, and the chat model lists (web picker, mobile picker, CLI list, VS Code picker, models API) show only chat-type models.
purpose.why_it_exists: A chat turn sent to a speech-to-text, image or video model fails or gives nonsense. The registry makes admission a data question instead of a per-app guess.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who chats on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome, and developers calling the models API. Engineers who add models to the catalog.
problems_solved: A chat turn is never routed to a model that cannot read or write text.
One catalog drives every app, so apps do not keep private lists of chat models.
Models of other kinds (transcription, speech, image, video) do not appear in chat pickers.
use_cases: A Free user chats and Auto picks a text model.
A developer lists models over the API and gets only chat-capable ones.
A CLI user prints the model list and sees context and output sizes beside capability letters.
An engineer adds a model to the curation file and it shows up in every app after sync.

steps.what_happens: A model is added or edited in the curation file and compiled into the generated registry.
The person opens a picker; the app reads the generated catalog bundled in the app and lists chat-type models for the plan.
On Web/CLI/Chrome the list of models the account may run also comes from the server.
On send, the server resolves Auto through routing policies that require textInput and textOutput, then calls the provider.
The provider returns text, streamed back to the app.

features.summary: Lets a person attach pictures and PDFs to chat. The catalog records which models read pictures and PDFs, how many pictures one request may carry, and which detail levels are accepted. Apps warn early; the server refuses a picture turn for a model that cannot read pictures instead of rerouting.

purpose.what_it_does: Checks every picture or PDF turn against the chosen model: picture ability, picture count, detail level and native PDF handling. Auto routing sends picture turns to vision models.
purpose.why_it_exists: Providers reject a request that carries media the model cannot read. Checking against the catalog gives a clear message before money or time is spent.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone attaching photos or PDFs on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, Chrome and VS Code; API developers sending image_url parts.
problems_solved: A picture sent to a text-only model is refused with a clear message.
Too many pictures are caught before sending.
A PDF goes native only where the model and route accept it; otherwise it is turned into text.
A detail value the model does not accept is refused.
use_cases: A user photographs a receipt and asks a question on Mobile.
A user attaches a PDF on Web and the model reads it natively.
A CLI user attaches a screenshot and is told to switch to a vision model.
A developer sends image_url parts with detail low or high to the API.

established.statement: The registry records image input per model; the product shows it and refuses or reroutes image turns to models that cannot read images (S76.03).
The registry records how many images a model accepts in one request and requests are checked against it (S76.04).
The registry records which models support high-detail inspection and the product requests high detail where supported (S76.05).
The registry records native PDF input per model and PDFs go natively to models that accept them (S76.06).

features.summary: Lets a person speak instead of typing and hear replies read aloud. Dictation turns a recording into text, live voice runs a spoken session, and read aloud speaks one reply. Server voice features use named registry slots. Mobile dictation uses on-device speech recognition. Audio-file understanding is a catalog flag only.

purpose.what_it_does: Provides dictation into the composer, a live two-way voice session, spoken replies, and the audio-input flag shown in model lists.
purpose.why_it_exists: Speaking is faster than typing and needed for hands-free use; the registry slots keep the voice models swappable without app edits.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web, Desktop and Mobile users; CLI users who dictate a prompt; API callers who transcribe audio.
problems_solved: Typing is slow on phones.
Voice models change; slots avoid editing callers.
Privacy settings can stop voice from using providers that may train on content.

A Mobile user starts a live voice conversation.
A user taps read aloud on a long answer.
A CLI user records a prompt and transcribes it with a local whisper command or the managed service.

It refuses with model_may_train when the privacy setting blocks a training provider (same file:505-522), caps audio at 25 MB (line 398-421), and meters voice minutes or a free voice allowance (lines 586-640).

steps.what_happens: Web records audio in the browser with MediaRecorder and posts it to /api/voice/transcribe.
The server checks the kill switch, sign-in, size, type, privacy, plan, allowance, then calls the speech-to-text provider with the slot model.

features.summary: Lets a model call tools (search, files, connectors, code) and keep going for several rounds in one turn. A model whose catalog entry has no tool calling gets no connector or MCP tools and answers in a single turn. Parallel read-only tool calls run only on routes that declare support.

purpose.what_it_does: Offers tools only to models flagged as able to call them, runs a loop of model, tool, result up to a step limit, and runs read-only tools in parallel where the route allows.
purpose.why_it_exists: A provider rejects a request that carries tool definitions for a model that cannot take them. The flag avoids that failure and lets agent features work.
purpose.who_uses_it: Users of search, files, connectors, code execution and agent modes on every app; API callers who send a tools array.
problems_solved: Models without tools are not sent tool definitions.
Multi-step tasks finish in one turn.
Read-only tools run side by side to save time.
use_cases: Ask a question that needs web search; the model calls search and answers.
Connector tool reads a calendar and replies.
CLI agent runs several read-only tools in parallel.
API caller sends tools and receives tool calls.

where_to_find_it: Web: 'Tools' chip on a model card (ModelCatalogue.tsx:105); tool controls in the composer (search, connectors, code run).

features.summary: API-only. A developer can ask for JSON, or JSON that matches a schema. Streaming is refused with these formats. A schema request on a model without the json flag is refused. A reply that breaks the schema is refused with an error. No app has a JSON switch.

purpose.why_it_exists: Developers need parseable output. The registry says which models and routes can do it so the server does not forward an impossible request.

problems_solved: Answers that cannot be parsed.

Validate a model's reply against a contract in CI.

features.summary: Lets a person choose how hard a reasoning model thinks, from Direct up to Maximum, showing only levels the model accepts and the plan allows. The server ignores an invalid effort and caps it by plan. Models that reject sampling settings get them dropped or the request refused.

purpose.what_it_does: Reads each model's supported effort levels and default from the catalog, shows only those in each app, and sends the chosen level. Also stops sampling settings (top_p and similar) from reaching models that reject them.
purpose.why_it_exists: Effort levels differ by model, and sending a level or sampling value a model rejects causes provider errors. Plan limits also cap effort.
purpose.who_uses_it: Users who trade speed for depth on any app; API and CLI developers.
problems_solved: Showing a level the model cannot use.
Provider 400 errors for unsupported sampling values.
Effort above the plan's allowance.
use_cases: Pick Quick for a fast answer and Deep for a hard problem.
Free user sees higher levels marked as plan-gated.
CLI user passes --effort and the CLI maps it to the nearest supported level.
API caller sends top_p to a model that rejects it and gets a clear 400.

steps.what_happens: The app reads the model's effort ladder from the bundled catalog and shows only supported levels, marking plan-gated ones.
The chosen level is sent with the request (field effort).
The server validates the level against the model, clamps by plan and workspace cap, builds the provider thinking settings.
The server refuses unsupported sampling-style parameters; adapters omit sampling for flagged models.
CLI maps effort to the nearest supported level and sends it to the provider or the managed route.
The provider reasons with the given effort and answers.

aliases: Per-model file and media size limits (not built)
features.summary: Each chat model has a context window (how much it can read) and an output limit (how long its reply can be). The server trims or summarises old chat history to fit, refuses a turn that cannot fit, and caps reply length. Pickers show the sizes. Per-model file, picture, audio and video size limits do not exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores two numbers per model in the model catalog (contextWindow, maxOutputTokens) (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:654-655). Uses them to show limits in pickers, to warn before a model switch, to shrink saved history before a Cloud turn, to refuse a message that cannot fit, and to choose how many reply tokens to ask for (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:5879-5882, 6702-6752).
purpose.why_it_exists: A model that is sent more than it can hold fails or silently loses text. A fixed reply cap would cut long answers at the same point for every model. The registry brief states: the registry records each context window, the product shows it and trims or refuses over-long requests; requests are capped by the output limit and it is shown (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/076-model-capability-registry.md S76.28, S76.29).
purpose.who_uses_it: People chatting on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI and VS Code who pick models or keep long chats; developers calling the chat completions API; QA and support staff diagnosing 'message too long' errors.
problems_solved: Long chats do not fail when the model is switched to a smaller one: history is summarised or dropped with a marker (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/context-window.ts:16-19).
A single message that cannot fit is refused before any provider call, and the credit reservation is released (request-processor.ts:6728-6752).
Reply length follows the model instead of one fixed number (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1516-1550).
People can compare models by size before choosing (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ModelCatalogue.tsx:262-263).
use_cases: A user on Web opens the model picker, opens a model card and reads 'Context ceiling' and 'Output ceiling' before choosing it.

A user with a very long chat switches to a model with a smaller window; the composer warns that older messages will be left out of the next reply (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/model-compatibility.ts:178-186).
A developer sends an oversized prompt to the API and receives HTTP 400 with code message_too_long (request-processor.ts:3311-3325).
A CLI user lists models and sees context and output sizes beside each id (apps/cli/src/provider.rs:250-265).

where_to_find_it: Web (and the public Desktop, which shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5): model picker, open a model card; rows 'Context ceiling' and 'Output ceiling' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ModelCatalogue.tsx:262-263).

Mobile: Context details sheet shows 'About N of M tokens (P%)' for the chat (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ContextDetailsSheet.tsx:93) and a context warning chip (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ContextWarningChip.tsx). The model row itself does not show context or output sizes: ModelRow.tsx has no context or output field, and formatContextWindow in apps/mobile/lib/models.ts:147 has no caller outside its definition (searched apps/mobile).
CLI: the models listing prints '<id> <N>K ctx <N>K out' per managed cloud model (apps/cli/src/provider.rs:250-265).

VS Code: model quick pick description ends with 'N context' and 'N output' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts:286-294); switching warns with text such as 'holds X of context instead of Y, so a long chat may be trimmed' (modelConstants.ts:347-364).
Chrome extension: no context or output display found (searched apps/extension for contextWindow and maxOutputTokens).
prerequisites: A chat model in the catalog with the numbers filled in; a model without them shows no row (ModelCatalogue.tsx:265 filters null values).
Cloud trimming needs a Cloud chat turn; Local and own-key runs are handled by each app (see access_and_usage).
screens_and_controls: Web: model card rows 'Context ceiling' and 'Output ceiling' (read only).

Web composer: a compatibility notice when the conversation exceeds the model budget, text 'This conversation is about X tokens and <model> holds Y. Older messages will be left out of the next reply.' (model-compatibility.ts:179-185).
Mobile: Context details sheet with percent used and breakdown rows (contextBudgeter.ts:52-67) and warning chip.
CLI: models listing; interactive '/compact' summarising compaction (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:1015-1018).
VS Code: model quick pick and a pre-switch warning.
journey: 1. The person opens the model picker or the models listing and reads the sizes.
2. The person picks a model; if it is smaller than the previous one the app warns (Web composer notice, VS Code warning).
3. The person sends a message; the app sends the history to the server (Cloud) or to the local runtime.
4. On Cloud the server estimates tokens, compacts or trims history to the budget, and refuses only if the latest message alone cannot fit (request-processor.ts:6702-6752).
5. The model replies up to the output cap chosen for the turn (request-processor.ts:5879-5882).
6. If refused, the person sees 'This message is too long for the selected model. Shorten it or send it in parts, or choose a model with a larger context window.' (request-processor.ts:3313-3320).
feedback_and_outputs: Error text above with HTTP 400 and code message_too_long (request-processor.ts:3317-3325).

In the history sent to the model, a marker line '[Earlier messages in this conversation were omitted to fit the model context window.]' replaces dropped turns, or a short summary replaces them when compaction runs (context-window.ts:16-17, context-compaction.ts:411-468).
Mobile percent-used readout; CLI notice 'Context compacted' or 'Context unchanged, nothing earlier could be summarized' (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:1230-1235).
API: /v1/models returns context_window and max_output per model (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/models/route.ts:55-57, 112-114).
settings: Server switch AGI_CONTEXT_COMPACTION_ENABLED: '0', 'false' or 'off' turns summarising compaction off and leaves mechanical trimming (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/context-compaction.ts:38, 59-62).
CLI config key max_tokens (default 8192) (apps/cli/src/config.rs:185-186, 288-290).
Temporary chats are never summarised, they are trimmed mechanically (context-compaction.ts:433-441).

working: Catalog fields contextWindow and maxOutputTokens exist on each model (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:654-655).
Web model card shows both limits (ModelCatalogue.tsx:262-263).

Server fits history to the window before each Cloud turn: budget is window minus reply allowance minus a fixed 2,048 reserve, with a floor of 1,024 (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/model-compatibility.ts:9-10, 47-53).

Server compacts old turns into a summary when the plan drops messages, the conversation is saved and not temporary, and compaction is on; otherwise it trims mechanically (context-compaction.ts:433-441).
Server refuses a turn whose latest user message cannot fit, releases the managed-usage reservation, and returns code message_too_long (request-processor.ts:6728-6752).

Output cap when the caller names none: the model's declared maximum, bounded by the window and by a product ceiling of 8,192 tokens; 4,096 when the catalog has no value; 1,024 for non-text models (model-catalog.ts:1525-1550).

For Auto, router and free-promotion turns on non-API surfaces the adaptive response budget takes the smallest of the depth ceiling, the caller's max_tokens and the model's limit (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:3675-3680, 5863-5882; packages/ai/routing/src/response-budget.ts:196-214).
API /v1/models publishes context_window and max_output (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/models/route.ts:112-114).
Composer pre-switch check uses the same budget function as the server (model-compatibility.ts:42-53, 176-186).
Mobile computes a context budget with warn at 70 percent and compact at 80 percent of the window (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/contextBudgeter.ts:82-96).

CLI summarising compaction uses the model's window from its catalog (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:1031, 1190-1195) and maps a provider overflow to a context_overflow error with the model's limit (apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:350-355).
CLI listing and VS Code quick pick show sizes (provider.rs:250-265; modelConstants.ts:286-294).
incomplete: Per-model file, picture, audio and video size limits are not in the registry; the web composer checks only plan-level byte limits (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:944-955, 921; packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:757).

For a fixed model on the API surface the caller's max_tokens is passed through; no clamp to the model's maximum was found in request-processor.ts (lines 5879-5882) and no per-adapter clamp was found for OpenAI-style routes. Anthropic's translator does resolve a value from the model's maximum (packages/ai/providers/anthropic/src/translate.ts:395). Whether upstream providers reject it is unknown.

Mobile local models get a made-up output limit, a quarter of the window between 1,024 and 8,192 (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/service.ts:152-153, 163); the output value is not shown anywhere (searched apps/mobile).
Mobile unknown-model fallback uses 4,096 as the window (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/contextBudgeter.ts:36-43).
Desktop (Tauri, internal) keeps contextWindow and maxOutput in its model store (apps/desktop/src/stores/modelStore.ts:42-67); whether a screen shows them is unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: apps/mobile/lib/models.ts:147 formatContextWindow is exported but nothing calls it (searched apps/mobile excluding node_modules).
Summarising compaction is disabled when AGI_CONTEXT_COMPACTION_ENABLED is 0, false or off (context-compaction.ts:59-62).
not_available: Per-model maximum file, image, audio and video sizes on every app and the API (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/076-model-capability-registry.md S76.30).
Chrome extension display of limits and its own trimming: none found in apps/extension.

established.statement: The registry records each model's context window; the product shows it and trims or refuses over-long requests accordingly.
The registry records each model's output-token limit; requests are capped by it and it is shown.
The registry records per-model maximum file, image, audio and video sizes and uploads are checked against the chosen model.
Model IDs and limits come from the generated catalog, never a literal in a consumer.
Local, own-key and Cloud stay separate; Cloud trimming must not route a Local chat to Cloud.

acceptance_criteria: Given a model with a 200K window, the Web model card shows 'Context ceiling' and 'Output ceiling' with rounded K or M values.
Given a Cloud chat whose latest message alone exceeds the window budget, the API returns HTTP 400 with code message_too_long and no credit is kept.
Given a long saved chat on a smaller model, the turn is sent with a summary or the omission marker and succeeds.
With AGI_CONTEXT_COMPACTION_ENABLED=0 the same turn is trimmed with the omission marker and no summary call is made.
A request with no max_tokens to a fixed text model asks the provider for at most 8,192 tokens.
The Web composer warns before sending when the conversation exceeds the selected model's budget.
The CLI listing prints a context size and an output size for every managed cloud model.
An upload larger than a chosen model's media limit is refused (required by S76.30; currently fails, see gaps).
inferred: The output limit shown in the picker is the catalog value, not the capped 8,192 value used for a turn [inferred from ModelCatalogue.tsx:263 versus model-catalog.ts:1525].
Token counts are estimates, not provider counts, so the real window can be hit slightly before or after the estimate [inferred from estimateTokens use in model-compatibility.ts:22-30].
proposed: [proposed] Clamp a caller's max_tokens to the registry maximum on every surface including the API, and say so in the response.
[proposed] Add per-model input size fields (file, image, audio, video bytes and counts) to the catalog and check them in the composer and on upload routes.
[proposed] Show context and output sizes on the Mobile model row, as the brief says Mobile is done.
[proposed] Remove or use the unused formatContextWindow on Mobile.

steps.what_happens: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI or VS Code shows catalog sizes and (Web composer, VS Code) compares the old and new model.
The app sends the chat history to the Cloud chat completions route.
The server picks the reply cap: the caller's max_tokens if given, otherwise the model-based cap, adjusted by the adaptive budget for Auto turns.
The server plans a trim, and compacts the dropped span into a summary through a cheaper managed route, unless temporary chat or switch off.
If the latest user message still cannot fit, the server returns 400 message_too_long and releases the reservation.
Otherwise the provider is called with the fitted messages and the cap (provider may be an outside service).
CLI and Mobile run their own budgeting and compaction on the device before or around the request.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Limits come from the catalog row of the chosen model, whatever provider serves it. Summaries are written by a cheaper managed route chosen by resolveEconomyRoute, not the chat model (request-processor.ts:6713-6720). Provider adapters read the cap and send it in their own field (packages/ai/providers/google/src/translate.ts:176, ollama translate.ts:115, openai translate-responses.ts:296).

access_and_usage.account: Cloud chat needs a signed-in account. Showing limits on Web needs no extra account step beyond the picker; CLI listing of managed models says 'public' or 'authenticated' (apps/cli/src/provider.rs:243-253).
access_and_usage.permissions: No separate permission for this feature found in the code. Organization model policy decides which models are offered at all.
access_and_usage.subscription: Not gated by a plan itself. Which models a plan can pick decides which limits a person can use. A message refused for length releases its reservation, so no credits are kept (request-processor.ts:6736-6748).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Reply cap enters the pre-flight cost estimate (request-processor.ts:5912-5921). Compaction uses a managed summary call that is metered through the same managed-usage path (request-processor.ts:6713-6720). Plan-level attachment byte limits come from the billing catalog (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:757).
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_CONTEXT_COMPACTION_ENABLED (server). adaptiveResponseBudgetEnabled is derived from the request (Auto, router or promotion), not a flag (request-processor.ts:3675-3680).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Applies to text chat models. Non-text models get a 1,024-token cap (model-catalog.ts:1534). Models without catalog numbers fall back to 4,096.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Provider adapters may apply their own rules (Anthropic derives max_tokens from the model, packages/ai/providers/anthropic/src/translate.ts:395). Which providers reject over-large caps is unknown.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile local models use their own window and a derived output value (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/service.ts:152-163, 203-204); the Cloud trimming, message_too_long and compaction do not run because no server is called [inferred]. Local-mode behaviour when a local chat overflows its window: the Mobile budgeter marks status 'compact' (contextBudgeter.ts:92-96); what the local runtime then does is unknown. Desktop local inference: unknown.

features.summary: A person makes a picture from a text prompt, or edits attached pictures, using an image model from the catalog. The server checks the plan, safety rules and spend limit, picks the model's image API, and refuses edits on models that cannot edit. Up to three guide pictures can join one edit on Web and Mobile.

purpose.what_it_does: Sends a prompt, and optionally a source picture, a mask and up to three reference pictures, to the Managed Cloud image route. The server resolves the catalog image model, the image API family, and returns images stored in the account library (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:255-270, 333-349).
purpose.why_it_exists: Image models differ in what they can do (one image or four, editing or not, transparent background or not). The catalog names each model's image API so each app can offer only what works (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-media.ts:57-74; doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/076-model-capability-registry.md S76.14-S76.16).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people on a plan that includes image generation using Web, Desktop (hosted web app), Mobile in Cloud chats, or the CLI image command.
problems_solved: A person cannot pick an image model that the server cannot run: the picker lists only admitted models (apps/web/lib/services/media-model-availability-service.ts:156-185).
Edits to a model that cannot edit are refused before credits are reserved (managed-image-generation.ts:681-696).
Unsafe prompts and uploads are refused before any charge (managed-image-generation.ts:272-322, 592-651).
Retries do not charge twice: the idempotency key settles the same reservation (apps/cli/src/cloud/image.rs:437-440).
use_cases: On Web the person turns on image mode, picks an image model, types a prompt and gets a picture.
On Web the person attaches a photo and chooses Edit, Variation or Mask edit to change it.
On Mobile the person attaches up to four pictures; the first is edited, the others guide it (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/actions/resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:195-200).
In the CLI the person runs 'agi image "a red kite" --aspect 16:9 -n 2' and finds files on disk and in the account library (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1107-1112).

where_to_find_it: Web and public Desktop: composer plus menu row 'Create image' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:160); model picker 'Select image model' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:6763); catalog chip 'Image out' (ModelCatalogue.tsx:143-146).

Web editing: attach a picture while image mode is on; choose 'Edit', 'Variation' or 'Mask edit' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:282-286); the card offers 'Revise this image' and 'Mask image' (apps/web/features/chat/components/ImageGenerationCard.tsx:603, 796).

CLI: command 'agi image' with flags --out, --aspect, --size, --quality, --transparent, --count/-n, --model/-m, --again, --retry, --save-defaults, --clear-defaults, --last, --list-models (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1110-1160).
VS Code and Chrome: not available (no image command or UI found).
prerequisites: Signed in with an adult-eligible account (apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:43-50).
A plan that includes image generation: pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium or enterprise (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:341, 356).
The 'canUseImages' capability open (route.ts:104-112).

journey: 1. The person turns on image mode (Web 'Create image', Mobile 'Create image' or '/image', CLI 'agi image').
2. The person picks an image model, or accepts the default.
3. The person types a prompt; optionally attaches a source picture (and a mask or guide pictures).
4. The app checks locally: plan, sign-in, online, model can edit if a picture is attached (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3755-3763; resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:160-190).
5. The app sends the request to the image route with an idempotency key.
6. The server runs the gates, reserves credits, calls the image provider and saves the images.
7. The person sees the picture in chat (or the file path in the CLI) and can revise or download it.
