established.statement: The registry records image-generation models and image requests are admitted only for models that generate images.
The registry determines which image models accept a source image, and edit requests are refused for models that cannot edit.
The registry records which models accept several reference images for one edit, and the product uses it.
Subscription capabilities connect to one AGI Subscription system; the image route checks plan, organization policy and spend limit before reserving credits.
Local, own-key and Cloud are separate; nothing routes a Local chat to Cloud silently.

acceptance_criteria: Choosing an image model and sending a prompt returns at least one image and saves it to the account library.
Attaching a picture with a model whose image API cannot edit shows the 'cannot edit' notice (Web, Mobile) or returns 422 (API).
Requesting n greater than the model's maximum returns 400 unsupported_image_count with max_images.
Sending more than three reference images returns a validation error; sending reference_images with operation other than 'edit' is refused.
A Free-plan account is refused with the plan message and no credits are reserved.
Mobile in Local mode shows the 'requires_cloud' alert and sends no request.
The CLI '--transparent' on a model without edit support fails with the message naming '--list-models'.
A prompt that fails safety checks returns 422 content_policy_violation and charges nothing.
inferred: Whether a model accepts several references should be a registry field, not the image-API edit list [inferred from the brief's wording 'registry records which models accept several reference images'].
Mobile should read the same edit signal as Web (supports_edit from availability) [inferred from ChatComposerNew.tsx:1367-1371].
proposed: [proposed] Add explicit registry flags for editing, mask edit, transparent background and maximum reference images per model.
[proposed] Make Mobile use the availability endpoint's supports_edit, like Web and the CLI.
[proposed] Add edit and reference options to the CLI image command.
[proposed] Correct the brief status for S76.16.

steps.what_happens: The app checks the plan, sign-in, network and edit support, and builds the request (source picture and guides as base64 or stored asset ids).
The request goes to POST /api/media/image/generate with an Idempotency-Key.
The server rate-limits, checks adult eligibility, managed compute, organization policy and spend limit.
The server validates the body, moderates the prompt, resolves the catalog model and provider, checks mismatch, model policy, training opt-out and image count.
The server reads and safety-checks source, mask and reference pictures, then refuses edit on a model whose image API cannot edit.
The server checks the canUseImages capability, reserves credits, and creates a durable job.
The job calls the image provider (generations or edits endpoint) and stores the results.
The app shows the result and polls status when async.

features.summary: A person makes a short video from a prompt, or from one first-frame picture or up to a few guide pictures. The server checks the plan, the model's listed durations, sizes and ratios, and generated audio against the catalog. Video editing and music are not built. No app has an audio switch.

purpose.what_it_does: Sends a prompt and options (duration, resolution, aspect ratio, optional pictures) to the video route, which validates them against the chosen model's catalog data, reserves credits and runs a long job (apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:439-479, 1194-1230).
purpose.why_it_exists: Video models differ in lengths, sizes and audio. Validating against catalog data stops invalid and costly requests (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/076-model-capability-registry.md S76.17, S76.19).
purpose.who_uses_it: People on the highest paid plans (Max 15x and Enterprise tiers by code) using Web, Desktop (hosted web app) or Mobile in Cloud chats.
problems_solved: Invalid duration, size or ratio is refused with a clear message (route.ts:454-475).
Audio is refused for a model that cannot make it (route.ts:469-471).
A model that cannot take input pictures refuses them with a clear message (route.ts:764-800).
use_cases: Web: person picks a video model, ratio, quality and length, types a prompt.
Web: person attaches an image to animate it, or several as guides.
Mobile: person chooses 'Create video' and types a prompt; the app picks sizes from the model.
API: developer posts prompt, duration_secs, resolution, aspect_ratio, optional generate_audio.

journey: 1. Person turns on video mode ('Create video').

features.summary: Streaming sends a reply as it is written; every app does this for chat. Prompt caching lets the provider reuse the unchanged start of a long prompt to cut cost and wait. The server turns it on by default for the apps, off for plain API calls, and off for temporary chats and zero-retention workspaces.

purpose.what_it_does: Streaming: the chat route returns server-sent events when stream is true (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:635). Caching: the server decides whether a turn may be cached and under whose scope, and adapters mark cacheable parts (request-processor.ts:2822-2843, 6685-6692).
purpose.why_it_exists: Streaming lets people read while the model writes. Caching lowers the cost of resending the same long prefix on every turn. First-party apps resend the whole conversation, so caching is on by default for them (request-processor.ts:2808-2818).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who chats on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code; the Chrome extension for browser actions; developers using the API.
problems_solved: Long waits before any text appears.
Paying full input price for repeated prefixes.
Cached prefixes leaking across users: the cache key is scoped to organization and user (packages/contracts/types/src/prompt-cache-plan.ts:26-33, 103-110).
Cache kept where privacy forbids it: temporary chat and zero-retention turns never cache (request-processor.ts:2830-2837).
use_cases: A person watches a reply appear on Web.
A long coding chat reuses its cached system prompt and tools turn after turn.
A developer calls the API with stream true to get events, or leaves it false to get one JSON body.
A user opens a temporary chat; nothing is left in a cache.

where_to_find_it: All apps: replies appear as they are written; no switch. Web: apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts; Mobile: apps/mobile/services/streaming.ts; VS Code: apps/extension-vscode/src/utils/api.ts; CLI: stream defaults to true in config (apps/cli/src/config.rs:182-185, 284-286); Chrome browser actions request streaming (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/cloudAgentClient.ts:324).
Caching: no user control. Model rows hold the numbers; none is shown in pickers (searched ModelCatalogue.tsx and the Mobile row).
API: 'stream' and 'use_prompt_cache' request fields (request-processor.ts:635, 807).
prerequisites: A chat model. Cloud for server caching rules.
screens_and_controls: Stop button during a stream (handled by the chat turn pipeline; not read here).
CLI: config key stream (default true).
journey: 1. The person sends a message.
2. The app sends stream true (apps) and use_prompt_cache true (Web, Desktop).
3. The server decides cache use from privacy class and surface.
4. The provider streams tokens; the server relays events.
5. The app renders text as it arrives.
6. On the next turn the same prefix is a cache hit and costs less.
feedback_and_outputs: Incremental text.

API error for streamed JSON: "response_format type 'json_object' requires stream: false. A streamed response is delivered before it can be validated as JSON, so the guarantee could not be kept." (request-processor.ts:867-875).
Office creation without streaming: 'Office file creation requires a streaming chat request.' (request-processor.ts:5461-5470).
Web search on some providers without streaming: 'Web search on this provider requires a streaming chat request. Set stream: true.' (request-processor.ts:5691-5698).
Usage and cost reports include cached tokens (not read in detail).
settings: API fields stream (default false) and use_prompt_cache (request-processor.ts:635, 807).
Web and Desktop send use_prompt_cache true (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:4680, 5032; apps/desktop/src/api/cloudApi.ts:895).
Temporary chat and organization zero-retention setting turn caching off (request-processor.ts:2830-2837).

working: Streaming transport in Web, Mobile, VS Code, CLI (grep hits for text/event-stream and stream true in each app's client).
The chat route's default stream is false; work mode 'agiwork' forces stream true (request-processor.ts:635, 1467).

Prompt cache decision: first-party surfaces default to cached, API keys must opt in, privacy classes 'temporary' and 'zero_retention' always disable (request-processor.ts:2822-2843; packages/contracts/types/src/prompt-cache-plan.ts:94-101).
A cache plan builds a tenant-scoped key and records skip reasons temporary_chat, zero_data_retention, no_stable_prefix, unscoped_tenant (prompt-cache-plan.ts:18-24, 35-50).
Provider adapters use the plan: Anthropic and OpenAI translators (packages/ai/providers/anthropic/src/translate.ts; packages/ai/providers/openai/src/translate.ts).

Route cache class per route in the registry: provider_implicit_prompt_cache, provider_explicit_prompt_cache, gateway_prompt_cache, gateway_response_cache, no_provider_cache (packages/ai/model-registry/schema/registry.schema.json:483-491).

Auto routing keeps a previously used route when it keeps a cache: it tolerates up to 25 percent extra cost for it, and no extra for a route with no cache (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:735, 1165-1180).

Model rows carry promptCacheMinimumTokens and cachePolicy (write multiplier, read discount, minimum life, explicit breakpoints) (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:717, 771-776); the registry also has a promptCaching capability (registry.schema.json:825-827).
The Chrome browser-action client requires the model to have streaming, tools and vision (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/cloudAgentClient.ts:98-103).

features.summary: Managed Cloud routing checks each route of a model before use. It refuses routes outside the required region, routes without zero retention when required, and routes whose provider may train on inputs when the user opted out. It ranks the rest, and pickers hide or label retired models.

purpose.what_it_does: In Managed Cloud (our servers), every candidate route of a model is tested against the region, data-retention, no-training, organization-policy and lifecycle rules. Routes that pass are ranked by health, credential, observed penalty, expected cost and default flag. The model pickers drop retired models, show a 'Retiring' or 'Leaves on' notice before the date, and mark degraded models as temporarily unavailable. (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1040-1115, 1137-1160, 1349-1360)
purpose.why_it_exists: People and workspaces need to keep data in a region, keep it out of provider training, and avoid models that are going away. The registry stores these facts per provider and route, so routing can enforce them instead of each app guessing. (brief: S76.34, S76.35, S76.37, S76.38; packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1040-1115)
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person who turns on the training setting; workspace admins who set a region, zero retention or a model policy; every person who opens a model picker.
problems_solved: A person's chat is not sent to a provider whose terms may allow training, when they opted out (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1112-1114).
A workspace pinned to a region is not served from a route that does not publish that region (packages/ai/routing/src/route-ranking.ts:53-58).
A workspace that requires zero retention gets a refusal rather than a quiet reroute (apps/web/features/settings/sections/WorkspacePolicySection.tsx:664-665).
Retired models stop being offered and past-date models are refused (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:2009-2013; packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1357-1359).
use_cases: A Free user turns on 'Only use models that do not train on your chats'. The web catalogue then lists only Auto and models whose provider keeps inputs out of training. (apps/web/app/api/models/catalogue/route.ts:81-86)
An admin requires zero data retention. Routes that are not zero-retention are refused. (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1099-1111)
A workspace pins its data to a region and a route that does not publish it is not used. (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1063-1070)
A model nears retirement and the picker shows when it leaves. (apps/web/features/models/lib/model-presentation.ts:43-58; apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/retirement.ts:18-28)

The model catalogue is requested; entries whose provider may train are removed, Auto stays (apps/web/app/api/models/catalogue/route.ts:81-86).
The person sends a chat. The server reads the training, retention, model-policy, region and US-only rules (apps/web/lib/server/managed-cloud-routing/admission.ts:136-152).
Routing admits only passing routes and ranks them (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1137-1160).
If no route passes the request is refused with a reason such as no_training_route or no_route (apps/web/lib/server/managed-cloud-routing/admission.ts:271-277).

Refusal for media and voice with the same setting (apps/web/lib/server/provider-training-opt-out.ts:18-22).
Picker tags: 'Temporarily unavailable', 'Coming soon', 'Retiring <date>', 'Retired <date>' (apps/web/features/models/lib/model-presentation.ts:30-33, 55-57).
settings: keepOutOfProviderTraining (user privacy setting)

workspace data region

working: Region admission: the deployment's home region check passes an unpublished region, and a pinned workspace's check refuses an unpublished region, on both route and model (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1054-1070; packages/ai/routing/src/route-ranking.ts:37-58).

Zero retention: a route passes if retention class is zero retention, or conditional with the harness feature implemented, or the provider is in an override set (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1099-1111).

No-training: both the vendor and the transport must keep inputs out of training; a provider with no recorded policy is refused (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:177-189, 1112-1114, 1374-1376; packages/ai/model-registry/generated/registry.ts:166-169).
Organization model policy is checked for both the vendor and the transport (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1073-1087).

Route ranking: health, then credential, then observed penalty, then expected cost, then default route, then route id; a preferred (warm cache) route is kept only within a cost ceiling (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1137-1170).

Lifecycle: models not live, deprecated, or past their deprecation date are rejected in routing; the managed request carries retiredModelKeys from modelsPastDeprecationDate() (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1353-1359, 1710-1720; apps/web/lib/server/managed-cloud-routing/routing-request.ts:109).
Picker list drops deprecated or past-date models (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:2009-2013; packages/ai/routing/src/model-picker.ts:126-134).
Catalogue marks a model temporarilyUnavailable when every route is degraded (apps/web/lib/server/model-catalogue.ts:240).
The API sets zeroDataRetentionOnly on the canonical request (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/canonical-request.ts:209-210).
Policy read failures fail safe: training opt-out reads as on; unreadable retention, region or model policy refuses the call (apps/web/lib/server/managed-cloud-routing/policy-source.ts:24-30, 54-64).
incomplete: The Rust resolver's route admission, eligibility and ranking show only lifecycle availability/deprecated, commercial status, selectable, harness and feature checks, and rank by cost, default and id; no region, retention, no-training, retired-date or health ordering was found in it (crates/agiworkforce-model-registry/src/lib.rs:788-846, 847-856, 976-983). The comments in auto.ts say the TypeScript and Rust route order is a contract (packages/ai/routing/src/route-ranking.ts:66-70), so this difference is notable.

The brief marks region, retention and route differences done on all six apps, but the code opened enforces them in the server path; the per-app lines in the brief point to generic picker files (brief: S76.34, S76.35, S76.38). Per-app enforcement outside the server path is unknown.

The catalogue server projection comments say a past-date model is dropped, yet the models page helper can still label 'Retired <date>' for an entry that stays selectable (apps/web/features/models/lib/model-presentation.ts:36-41); which entries reach it was not traced.
disconnected_or_disabled: observed-health ranking bands are behind a flag (enableObservedHealthRanking / observedHealthRankingEnabled) (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1290-1292); its default value is unknown.
not_available: Own-key (BYOK) and Local modes: the region, retention and no-training rules were found only in the managed Cloud request builder (apps/web/lib/server/managed-cloud-routing/routing-request.ts:96-125). Applying them to own-key or local was not found.

Desktop and CLI runtimes resolving against their own credentials are outside the server rules: auto.ts says the excluded-provider rule governs the server path, not a desktop or CLI runtime (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:207-210).

established.statement: Routes outside the required region are refused: the registry records model and provider residency regions.
The registry records provider and route data retention, and routing honours zero-retention requirements.
The registry records lifecycle stage, deprecation and retirement; pickers and routing exclude or label models accordingly.
The registry records route-dependent capabilities, cache class, retention and price per route, and routing ranks routes by them.
Local, own-key and Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing may silently route Local data to BYOK or Cloud.
Security behaviour fails closed; routing metadata is centralized and never inlined at a call site.

acceptance_criteria: With the training setting on, the web catalogue contains only Auto entries and models whose provider keeps inputs out of training.
With the training setting on and only may-train providers available, a chat is refused with the no-training message, not sent.
With a workspace region pinned away from the deployment region, a route that publishes no region or a different region is never selected.
With zero data retention required, a route with a non-zero retention class is refused and a conditional route passes only if its harness implements the per-request feature.
Of two admissible routes for one model, the healthy, credentialed, cheaper one ranks first; equal routes order by default flag then id.
A model past its deprecation date does not appear in the picker and a pinned request for it is refused, not resolved to another model.
A model within 30 days of leaving shows a leaving date in the web and mobile pickers.
When the policy cannot be read, the call is refused, not routed unfiltered.
inferred: [inferred] Every app that sends chat through the cloud API gets the region, retention and no-training rules because the checks run on the server.
[inferred] The brief's 'done' for CLI, VS Code and Chrome means the server enforces the rules for their cloud traffic, not that each app has its own rule.
proposed: [proposed] Add region, retention and no-training fields to the Rust resolver or document that it is outside this rule, so the TS and Rust results agree.
[proposed] Show a clear reason in each app picker when a model is hidden by the training setting.
[proposed] Decide and document whether own-key mode must honour the zero retention and region settings.

steps.what_happens: The person switches on the training setting; the value is written to user settings under the privacy namespace.
The picker asks for the catalogue; the server filters out models whose provider may train, keeps Auto, and returns a private 15-second cached list.
A chat turn reads the training, conversation training state, retention, model policy, workspace region and US-only rules.
The request is built with retiredModelKeys, excluded transports, region and the policy fields.
resolveAutoRoute checks models then routes, then ranks the passing routes; the first becomes the answer and the rest become failover of the same model.
The request is sent to the provider with zeroDataRetentionOnly set when required.
Pickers on mobile and CLI compute leaving labels from the catalog's deprecation date on the device.

aliases: Feature availability (brief S78.01, S78.07, S78.09-S78.12, S78.24)
features.summary: Decides whether a feature or model is allowed for this person on this app. The server builds a capability document from model, plan, app and settings layers. Each app reads it. The server checks again on every model route. The person also chooses where a request runs: on the device, with their own key, or on AGI Cloud.

purpose.what_it_does: Combines four layers (model, tier/plan, surface/app, settings) into one 'granted or denied, and why' answer per capability (packages/contracts/types/src/capability-handshake/types.ts:7-26). The server also enforces plan access, workspace model policy, training opt-out, US-only routing and age eligibility on the request itself (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:5330-5351, 5049-5066, 4709-4715). The person picks the processing path (Local, own key, Cloud) in the composer or CLI.
purpose.why_it_exists: A control hidden only in the UI can be bypassed, and a control shown without a server check can promise what the plan does not include. One shared answer keeps six apps saying the same thing, and the server refusal is the real gate (brief S78.07). The AGENTS.md trust rules say Local, own key and Cloud are separate boundaries and nothing may silently cross them (doc: AGENTS.md §6).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in or signed-out person using any of the six apps. Workspace owners and admins set the policy that binds members. Support and engineers read the denial codes.
problems_solved: A free or lower plan sees a model it cannot use and gets a late failure.
A workspace admin switches off a feature or model and members can still reach it from another app.
A temporary server outage disables features that work on the phone.
Local data is sent to the cloud without the person choosing it.
use_cases: A Free-plan user opens the model picker on web and sees plan-locked models marked as locked, then the server refuses a forced request with model_not_available and names the required plan.
A workspace admin blocks a provider; a member's request on any app is refused with a policy reason.
A user on the CLI starts in Local mode and must run /continue-with-cloud to move the chat to AGI Cloud.
A person on the Pro-or-higher plan turns on 'Only use AI providers based in the US' in Privacy settings.

Server refuses a model not in the plan: 403 model_not_available with requiredTier (request-processor.ts:5330-5351).
Server refuses Deep Research for plans without it: 403 plan_upgrade_required with required_plans (request-processor.ts:1503-1524).
Workspace model policy is read once and evaluated again on the primary model and fallback candidates; unreadable policy fails closed with 503 (request-processor.ts:4690-4693, 5049-5070).
Training opt-out read failure routes only to no-training models and logs a warning (request-processor.ts:3615-3631, 4694-4700).

US-only preference flows into the routing policy (request-processor.ts:4709-4715) and the preference test says it is enforced (apps/web/app/api/me/routing-preferences/__tests__/no-unenforced-control.test.ts:7-20).
Owner/admin gate on team changes: requireTeamAdminAccess (apps/web/app/api/settings/team/route.ts:139); Workspace policy page is read-only for others (WorkspacePolicySection.tsx:314-319).
CLI maps plan to a routing bucket (apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs:244-251) and caches the plan 300 seconds (tier_cache.rs:43).
CLI explicit path change: /privacy-mode refuses Local to BYOK or Cloud and points to /continue-with-byok or /continue-with-cloud (claude_parity.rs:480-517).
VS Code resolves plan and capability document and revalidates on signals (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/tierResolver.ts:48-54, 73; tierRevalidation.ts:12-18).

Age gate: minimum age 18 (packages/contracts/types/src/account-eligibility.ts:1); web terms step records acceptance and handles an age refusal from the server (RecordTermsAcceptance.tsx:106-113; apps/web/app/api/terms/accept/route.ts:165); mobile stores a device age verdict and refuses minors (ageGate.ts:128-170).
incomplete: Environment-gated models: environmentAvailability returns {configured:false} on web, mobile and VS Code, so a model that requires an environment is always locked there (apps/web/features/chat/lib/model-plan-admission.ts:19-21; apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/service.ts:80; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts:44).
The shared platform matrix covers only web, desktop and mobile (packages/contracts/types/src/capabilities.ts:139-143); CLI, VS Code and Chrome use their own plan logic instead of one resolver.
Role restriction status exists only for web, desktop and mobile in the brief (S78.10); CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no role control found.
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile does not fetch the remote capability list unless the app is in Cloud mode, the cloud is unlocked and an account is present (apps/mobile/src/lib/Capabilities.tsx:39-45).
On mobile, purchase wording depends on NATIVE_PURCHASES_AVAILABLE; when off, plan locks say 'Not included in your plan' (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/service.ts:65-72, 193).
not_available: No own-key choice found in the mobile model picker: mobile app mode is only 'local' or 'cloud' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/store/appModeStore.ts:5). The brief marks mobile processing path done; the own-key leg is unverified.
No own-key chooser found in the web composer footer; BYOK appears there only as a recovery link and a privacy label (apps/web/features/chat/lib/freeCapacityRecovery.ts:17; ChatComposerNew.tsx:2071).
Chrome: brief marks processing-path choice not applicable (brief S78.24).

established.statement: One resolver combines model, plan, surface and operator switches and the controls read it.
Plan entitlements are checked in the UI and again on the server for every route that runs a model.
Workspace policy (feature switches, model policy, retention) restricts members on every surface.
Owner and admin controls are withheld from other members and refused server-side.
Regional restrictions are enforced and visible to the user.
Age or account eligibility is checked at sign-up or first run, with restricted behaviour for ineligible users.
The user can choose where a request is processed: local model, own key or managed cloud.
Nothing may silently route a Local chat, file or session to own key or Cloud; a Local-to-own-key move is an explicit fork with consent and a visible provider label.
Security behaviour fails closed.

acceptance_criteria: A model outside the plan is refused by the server with a 403 and code model_not_available that names the plan, even if the request bypasses the UI.
A workspace policy that blocks a model refuses the request on each app, and an unreadable policy returns 503 with Retry-After.
If the training opt-out cannot be read, only no-training models are used and a warning is logged.
A member who is not owner or admin sees the Workspace policy page read-only and the team API refuses their change.
Turning on US-only routing is saved, reloads as on, and the chat route receives usOnly in its routing policy.
In the CLI, /privacy-mode byok from a Local session changes nothing and tells the person to use /continue-with-byok.
A mobile capability the server does not list keeps its shipped value when the server is unreachable.
A person under 18 is refused at sign-up or first run.
inferred: The mobile fail-open for unlisted capabilities is safe only because the server still refuses the request [inferred].
The same plan decision should appear on all six apps because every app fetches /api/me [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add the own-key leg to the mobile and web composer path chooser, or record that it is not offered there.
[proposed] Give CLI, VS Code and Chrome the same capability document reader as web and mobile so one resolver serves all six apps.

steps.what_happens: App fetches /api/me for its surface and stores the capability document.
Controls read the document; if it is missing they use the shipped platform matrix.
Person picks a model or path; picker computes locks from plan.
Server reads workspace model policy, training opt-out, US-only and region before routing.
Server checks plan access for the named model and refuses with model_not_available.
Server evaluates workspace policy on the chosen model and fallbacks; refuses with the policy code.
Provider call is made by the managed route, or by the CLI directly with the person's own key.
CLI moves a Local chat to BYOK or Cloud only through a reviewable draft with secret scan and consent.

A refusal record is kept and only clearAgeGate lifts it (ageGate.ts:128-140)

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Model access is decided by the model registry and plan tier, never by a provider name in the gate. Managed Cloud routes are chosen server side; own-key requests go straight to the provider chosen with --provider on the CLI. Workspace policy can name providers and models (apps/web/lib/services/model-policy-gate.ts). Training opt-out limits routing to providers that keep inputs out of training (request-processor.ts:4696-4698). Local models run through the device runtime.

access_and_usage.account: Cloud capability needs a signed-in account. CLI usage and plan need an AGI credential, otherwise the session runs local or BYOK (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:343-356). Mobile refresh needs an account epoch (Capabilities.tsx:39-45).
access_and_usage.permissions: Owner or admin changes workspace policy; others read only (WorkspacePolicySection.tsx:314-319). Server refuses non-admin team changes (team/route.ts:139).
access_and_usage.subscription: Plan tier decides model roster and gated features. CLI maps Free, Basic and own-key to the 'free' bucket, Pro and Team to 'pro', Max tiers to 'max' (tier_cache.rs:244-251). US-only needs an eligible plan (UsOnlyRoutingPanel.tsx:24-33).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: none found in the code for the gate itself; allowance is covered in F078-04.
access_and_usage.flags: Server feature_flags in /api/me; remote capability switches are named 'capability.<snake_case>' and read by mobile (apps/mobile/src/lib/Capabilities.tsx:36, 47-49, 81-86). Rollout rings also appear in feature_flags (apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts:278-283).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Model entitlement uses the registry minimum tier per model (request-processor.ts:5335). Auto aliases are admitted by plan (model-plan-admission.ts:25-31).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Workspace model policy can block provider or model; US-only and zero-data-retention and no-training narrow providers (request-processor.ts:4709-4715).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Local inference is not gated by plan in the code opened: mobile local models are listed without a plan check (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/service.ts:227) and CLI usage says local or BYOK sessions have no account usage (usage_summary.rs:343-356). Whether a sign-in is required for Local on each app is unknown. Mobile does not fetch the remote capability list in Local mode (Capabilities.tsx:39-45).

features.summary: Shows composer controls only when the chosen model supports them: effort levels, thinking, file types, image and video limits. The server refuses unsupported sampling values and clamps effort to what the model, plan and workspace allow. On web, a model change that strands attachments shows a banner with switch or remove.

purpose.what_it_does: Reads each model's capability record and shows only the effort marks, thinking switch, media options and attachment types it can take. The server checks the request again: it drops or clamps effort and refuses unsupported sampling parameters.
purpose.why_it_exists: A control that the model ignores is misleading, and a parameter a provider rejects makes the whole request fail. One catalog drives every screen so a model swap needs no screen edit (doc: AGENTS.md §4).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone choosing a model in the composer; developers calling the chat API; CLI users setting effort or temperature.
problems_solved: A slider offers effort levels the model rejects.
A model that cannot read images is sent an image.
Sampling values break a model that does not take them.
use_cases: Pick a model with an effort ladder on web: the slider shows only that model's marks.
Attach a PDF then switch to a text-only model: a banner offers Use Auto, Remove attachments or Choose a compatible model.
Send top_p to a model that rejects it through the API: 400 unsupported_parameter.
On the CLI set --temperature for a model that rejects sampling: the CLI leaves it out.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: composer footer model menu, effort slider and thinking switch (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFooter.tsx:1305-1321); attachment banner above the input (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:5434-5480).

Mobile: effort button 'Reasoning effort: <level>' and slider panel in the composer (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ComposerEffort.tsx:34-58); model row thinking toggle (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/components/ModelRow.tsx:72-74); Add to chat sheet for media.
CLI: model picker popup with an effort bar shown only for reasoning models (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/model_picker.rs:290-301).
VS Code: command 'Code: Set Reasoning Effort' and model switch warning (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:470-475; apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:1359-1370).
Chrome: effort control state from the managed model picker (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedModelPicker.ts:49-58, 337-339).
prerequisites: A selected model with catalog capability data.
For plan-gated effort levels, a known plan tier.
screens_and_controls: Effort marks, with plan-gated marks separated from allowed ones (ComposerFooter.tsx:1311-1314).
Thinking switch hidden for models that do not expose it (ComposerFooter.tsx:1321).
Attachment banner buttons 'Use Auto', 'Remove attachments', 'Choose a compatible model' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5459, 5469, 5477).
Free-model note 'This free model accepts images only...' (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5442-5443).
journey: 1. Person opens the model menu and picks a model.
2. The footer recomputes effort marks, thinking switch and media options from the catalog.
3. Person attaches files; unacceptable types are refused with a notice (web ChatComposerNew.tsx:2270-2287; mobile attachmentValidation.ts:98-123).
4. If the model later changes and attachments no longer fit, a banner appears and send is blocked (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3593).
5. Person chooses Use Auto, picks a compatible model, or removes the files.
6. On send the app sends effort and options; the server clamps effort and refuses unsupported parameters.
feedback_and_outputs: Banner text naming the problem, for example "The selected model can't read the attached image. Switch to Auto, choose an image-capable model, or remove the image." (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5445).
Toast 'Could not save the model for this conversation. The previous model remains active.' (ComposerFooter.tsx:1161-1163).
API error 400 unsupported_parameter with the parameter name (request-processor.ts:5159-5163).
settings: Per-conversation or global effort and thinking values (ComposerFooter.tsx:1014-1031; mobile useScopedEffort EffortSlider.tsx:57-76).
Workspace maximum reasoning effort (packages/contracts/types/src/enterprise/workspace-controls.ts:77-85).

working: Web effort marks come from the model's catalog ladder; marks the plan does not allow are separated and the control exists only with an explicit ladder (ComposerFooter.tsx:1311-1321).
Web attachment conflict is computed from image and PDF attachments against vision capability; send is blocked while it holds (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1542-1562, 3593).
Web banner gives three choices and does not delete attachments by itself (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5434-5480).
Web local model with attachments is a separate conflict (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1589).

Server refuses unsupported sampling parameters with 400 unsupported_parameter, built from the model's rejected list and the route's accepted list (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-parameters.ts:48-71; request-processor.ts:5153-5164).
Server drops effort the model does not support and clamps it to plan and workspace maximum (request-processor.ts:1826-1839, 5827-5835).
Server refuses too many images and unsupported image detail (request-processor.ts:5131-5146).
Models API publishes accepted request parameters per model (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/models/route.ts:60-61, 117-119).

Mobile effort steps come from the model's effort ladder only (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/components/EffortSlider.tsx:32-36) and the request maps thinking to thinking_mode (apps/mobile/services/streaming.ts:637-642).
Mobile attachments are checked by destination (device or Cloud) and by model image count (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/attachmentValidation.ts:154-180, 189-205).

Mobile image requests with a reference image check the image model's edit support and name capable models (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/actions/resolveMobileImageGenerationRequest.ts:177-190, 213-225).
CLI maps effort to the nearest supported level, sends it only where the route takes it, and drops temperature for models that reject sampling (apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:619-690).
CLI picker shows the effort bar only for reasoning models whose provider supports effort (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/model_picker.rs:290-301).

VS Code snaps effort to the model's levels and warns before a switch that loses image reading, tools or context (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/model-picker/modelConstants.ts:347-377; apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:1359-1370).
Chrome derives effort options and gated marks from the model reasoning record and plan (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedModelPicker.ts:337-339).
incomplete: Mobile file acceptance depends on destination (device or Cloud), not on the selected model's file types, apart from the image-count limit (attachmentValidation.ts:154-180). The brief marks it done.
VS Code gives a warning on model switch but no attachment keep or remove choice (commandSetup.ts:1359-1370).
Media settings (duration, size, aspect) were not opened in code for mobile, CLI and VS Code; brief says VS Code missing.
not_available: Attachment keep-or-remove choice after a model change on mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome (brief S78.25).
Attachment file-type gating and media settings on VS Code (brief S78.03, S78.06).
Chrome attachment-type gating (brief S78.03).

established.statement: Composer controls (effort, thinking, attachment options) appear, change or disappear by selected model.
Accepted file types depend on what the model can read.
Reasoning options match the model and unsupported levels are not sent.
Sampling options offered or sent depend on the model.
Media settings offered depend on the selected media model.
After switching to a model that cannot use the attachments, the user chooses to keep them (by switching model) or remove them.
Parameters the model cannot take are removed or corrected before sending.
Model IDs and capabilities come from the generated catalog, never typed into screens.

acceptance_criteria: Selecting a model with no effort ladder removes the effort slider on web, mobile and CLI.
Selecting a model with an effort ladder shows only its marks.
An image attached with a text-only model blocks send and shows the banner with the three choices on web.
'Remove attachments' empties the attachment list; 'Use Auto' switches the model and clears the banner.
An API call with top_p to a model that rejects it returns 400 unsupported_parameter naming top_p.
An effort above the plan or workspace maximum is sent reduced, not as typed.
The CLI request body has no temperature for a model that rejects sampling.
inferred: The brief wording 'the server strips' is only true for effort; for sampling the server refuses the request [inferred from request-processor.ts:5153-5164].
Mobile 'done' for accepted types likely means destination checks, not per-model checks [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Make the server and apps use the same message for an unsupported sampling parameter, or strip it, and state which.
[proposed] Add the attachment keep/remove choice to mobile and Chrome, or record that the banner is web-only.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: All options come from the model registry (capabilities, reasoning ladder, rejected sampling lists). Each provider adapter turns the same effort into its own wire field. The catalog, not the screen, is the source (doc: AGENTS.md §4).

features.summary: A control that can never apply here is left out. A control that applies but is blocked by plan, sign-in, key, environment or release state stays visible, disabled or locked, with a reason. Examples are locked model rows on web, mobile, CLI and VS Code.

purpose.what_it_does: Separates hidden controls (cannot apply) from locked or disabled controls (applies, but blocked) and shows the reason for the second kind.
purpose.why_it_exists: People discover what a plan would unlock, and nobody clicks a button that fails without a word.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who opens a model picker or composer; support staff explaining a locked item.
problems_solved: A blocked model disappears and the person never learns it exists.

features.summary: Each app reads the plan allowance left from the server usage summary and shows it. Free plans on web see only an Upgrade prompt. A failed read shows 'Unavailable' or an error, not a real-looking zero. Local and own-key use is not metered.

purpose.what_it_does: Fetches the server usage summary (percent used in session, weekly and period windows, credits, reset times) and shows how much is left.
purpose.why_it_exists: People should know before a limit stops them. The server owns the numbers so every app agrees (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:1-5).
purpose.who_uses_it: Paying subscribers on any app; support staff checking a limit complaint.
problems_solved: Surprise stop at a limit.
Different numbers on different apps.

Mobile user opens the cloud usage screen.
CLI user runs the usage command and sees plan, windows and history.
VS Code user sees usage in the sidebar.

features.summary: Finds out when a feature needs an account connection, a paired desktop or phone, or a runtime, says which is missing and offers a way forward. Web shows a connector checklist and a Continue on desktop link; mobile shows desktop pairing state; CLI and VS Code offer continue commands.

purpose.what_it_does: Detects a missing connector, device or runtime before the person relies on it, and gives an action to connect, pair, install or continue on another device.
purpose.why_it_exists: Features that depend on a connector, a paired computer or a local program fail in confusing ways unless the app checks first.
purpose.who_uses_it: People using plugins, code sessions, the phone companion, the CLI and VS Code.
problems_solved: A plugin that needs a connector fails halfway.
A person starts work on the web that fits the desktop better.
The CLI binary is missing in VS Code and nothing says so.
use_cases: Open a plugin page and see which connectors are still not connected.
Open the Code rail and choose 'Work with local code' to hand the session to the desktop app.
Open the mobile companion screen and see 'Not connected' or '<desktop>, offline'.
In the CLI run /continue-elsewhere to get the web link for the account chat.

CLI continue needs a Managed Cloud session saved to the account.

journey: 1. Person opens a page or action that needs a connector, device or runtime.
2. The app looks up what is connected (connectors list, devices list, local CLI probe).
3. If something is missing the app names it and offers Connect, a download link, Reconnect or a command.
4. For continue, the app opens a deep link or prints the web address.
5. The person finishes the work on the other device.

established.statement: The product detects when a feature needs an account connection that is missing and says which one.
The surface detects whether a required device is available and says so before the user relies on it.
The surface detects whether the needed runtime (sandbox, local model runtime, CLI) is available and gates the feature.
When a feature needs an account connection, the user is told which account and given a way to connect it.
When work fits another device better, the surface offers an action that continues it there.
Moving a Local chat to another trust boundary is an explicit fork with consent.

features.summary: When a feature needs a permission (microphone, camera, site access, agent autonomy, computer control), each app tells the person what the permission is for and how to change it later. There is no single shared component: Mobile, Desktop, Chrome, VS Code and CLI each have their own registry, dialog or prompt. Web dictation explains only after a denial.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the person a plain-words reason for each permission a feature needs, at or before the moment it is asked, and a way to see and change the answer later. Mobile keeps a registry of eight device permissions with a one-line purpose each and a status screen. Desktop shows a question dialog with a reason and a Settings list of answers and operating-system permissions. Chrome shows a site-access card before browser control starts. VS Code shows a modal warning before the Bypass Permissions agent mode. The CLI shows an approval prompt with a summary and detail lines before a tool runs. (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/permissions/registry.ts; apps/desktop/electron/runtime/permissionManager.ts; apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:1399; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/permissions/agentModeConsent.ts; apps/cli/src/tui/approval_broker.rs:220)
purpose.why_it_exists: An operating system or browser prompt says only 'allow microphone'. The person needs to know why AGI wants it and what it can do with it, so they can say yes with confidence and know where to undo it. The brief's requirement is that the explanation comes before or at the request, never only after a denial (brief S78.21). AGENTS.md section 9 also requires that an action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence (doc: AGENTS.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in or local user of the six apps who starts dictation, a camera or photo attach, browser control, computer control, or an agent mode that removes approval prompts. Testers and engineers use it to check that permission copy is complete.
problems_solved: A person is asked for the microphone, camera, calendar or notifications with no reason given.
A person denied a permission once and cannot find how to grant it later.
An agent mode that removes approval prompts is switched on without the person understanding the risk.
A site is granted to the browser agent without the person knowing what page content is sent to the cloud.
use_cases: Mobile: open Settings, Safety & Security, Permissions, and read 'Used for voice input and audio recording.' under Microphone, then tap it to see the status and an Open Settings button.
Chrome: the agent needs a site, so the side panel shows 'AGI needs access to <site>' with what is read, what is sent to AGI Cloud, and buttons to allow once, always allow or decline.
VS Code: switch the agent mode to Bypass Permissions and a modal 'Turn on Bypass Permissions?' lists what it removes before it is applied.
Desktop: the agent wants to control the mouse and keyboard, and a 'Permission required' dialog says what it wants to do and why, with Deny, Allow this session, or Always allow.

where_to_find_it: Mobile: Settings, Safety & Security, then Permissions (screen title 'Permissions', section 'App Permissions'); each row opens a detail screen. Also reachable from the Capabilities screen. (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/permissions/index.tsx)

Desktop (the Electron app showing the hosted web app): Settings section 'Permissions' with 'Your answers' and an operating-system group with an 'Open System Settings' button. (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopPermissionsSection.tsx:33-38)
Desktop: native 'Permission required' dialog raised when the agent first needs a capability. (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/permissionManager.ts)
Web: the microphone button in the chat composer (dictation). The only explanation is the error text shown after a denial. (apps/web/features/chat/stores/voice-input-store.ts:452)

Chrome: inline card in the side panel titled 'AGI needs access to <host>', plus a history-search card and a 'AGI wants to start a browser task' card. (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/bubbles.ts:1399; apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:4280)

VS Code: modal warning 'Turn on Bypass Permissions?' and 'Use Max reasoning with Bypass Permissions?' when the agent mode or effort is changed in the mode picker or Settings. (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/permissions/agentModeConsent.ts)

CLI: approval prompt in the terminal interface before a tool runs, including 'Workspace policy requires approval for <tool>'. (apps/cli/src/tui/approval_broker.rs; apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs)
prerequisites: Mobile: a device that reports the permission as available; Face ID, Speech Recognition, Photos & Files, Reminders rows show on iOS only, and the Face ID row only on a Face ID device. (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/permissions/registry.ts)
Desktop: the Electron host must be present, otherwise the Permissions section renders nothing. (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopPermissionsSection.tsx)
Chrome: the person is signed in and starts a browser task on a web page; account pages are refused. (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:14000)

steps.what_happens: Mobile: person opens Settings, Safety & Security, Permissions; the screen reads the status of each permission from the device and shows the registry text.

Mobile: person taps voice; the app reads the microphone and speech status and, if not granted, calls the system request; the system shows the build-time usage description. A denial throws 'mic-permission-denied' and an alert with Open Settings is shown.

Web: person clicks the microphone button; useDictation checks the Voice setting and the server kill switch, then the store calls getUserMedia, which raises the browser prompt. A denial maps to a text by error name.
Web: after recording stops, the audio is sent to the transcription endpoint on our servers; this is after the permission step and is not part of this feature.
Desktop: the agent asks requestPermission; if a stored decision exists it is returned, otherwise a native dialog is shown with the reason, and the answer is recorded.
Desktop: the Settings list reads decisions and operating-system status through the host bridge; focus and permission-changed events re-read it.
Chrome: the side panel builds the site-access card; on Allow it asks Chrome for the host permission and records a one-time or always grant.
VS Code: a mode change calls setAgentModeWithConsent, which shows the modal, then stores consent in workspace state and writes the setting.
CLI: a tool call reaches the policy gate and approval broker, which shows the request and returns allow or refuse to the tool runner.

aliases: Live updates after a plan, policy, connection, or device change
features.summary: After a plan, switch-off or sign-in change, gated controls should update without a restart. Each app refreshes from the account service by its own rule: mobile on resume and Cloud entry, VS Code and CLI on a five-minute cache, Chrome every three minutes while in use, web on specific events. Mobile, VS Code and web keep the last answer on error; CLI and Chrome differ.

purpose.what_it_does: Re-reads the person's plan and the server's list of allowed capabilities, and re-applies it to controls such as voice, file upload, connectors, models and dictation. Web reads /api/me into a billing store; mobile reads /api/me?surface=mobile on resume and on entering Cloud; VS Code marks the cached tier stale on a refused call and re-reads on the next use; the CLI re-reads when its on-disk cache is older than five minutes; Chrome re-reads the capability document every three minutes while the panel is active. (apps/web/shared/stores/web-auth-store.ts; apps/mobile/src/lib/capabilities.tsx; apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/tierResolver.ts; apps/cli/src/tier_cache.rs; apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:16157-16203)
purpose.why_it_exists: A person who upgrades, or an operator who switches a feature off for safety, should see the change without reinstalling or restarting, and a network error must not disable a working feature. The brief requires that a server switch-off takes effect on the next refresh with no store release (brief S78.28).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user of a managed plan; operators who throw a capability switch; testers checking upgrade and downgrade flows.
problems_solved: A person pays for a plan and the app still shows locked controls.
A faulty feature is paused by the operator but stays visible in an installed app until the next store release.
A short outage makes the app hide features the person has paid for.
A cached plan outlives a downgrade or a sign-out.
use_cases: Upgrade on the web: the pending-checkout component polls the billing store until the plan shows active, then moves to the confirmation page.
Operator pauses dictation: the web billing store receives it in disabled features on its next read and the microphone button is disabled with the reason text.
Mobile app is in the background while a capability is switched off; on return to the foreground the switch is applied.

acceptance_criteria: Web: after a successful upgrade, the plan label and the locked controls update within the polling window without a manual reload.
Web: with the network blocked during a refresh, the previous plan and controls remain and an error state is recorded, not cleared.
Mobile: switch a capability off on the server, background and foreground the app, and the capability's control is gone or shows the paused text without a new build.
Mobile: make the server unreachable and resume; every control keeps its previous state.
VS Code: after a 401 or quota refusal, the next tier read calls the account API; with the API unreachable, the model picker keeps the cached tier.
CLI: change the plan, wait past five minutes or trigger a 401, restart or continue, and the new tier shows; within five minutes the old tier shows.
Chrome: with the panel open and active, a capability change shows in the attach menu within the refresh window, and a failed summary request does not hide a permitted feature (target).
inferred: The CLI should keep its last known tier after cache expiry when the network fails, to match mobile and VS Code. [inferred from the required 'keeps the last answer' line]
Chrome should keep the last capability document when the account summary request fails. [inferred]
Web should refresh the billing store when the window regains focus, so a switch-off or plan change made elsewhere is applied without a trigger. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Add a focus and interval refresh of the web billing store with the same stale-while-failing rule the mobile store uses.
[proposed] Make the CLI read a stale cache as a fallback when the network call fails, marked as unverified.
[proposed] Make Chrome keep the previous document when the summary request fails.
[proposed] Share one refresh policy (triggers, keep-last, owner check) across apps in a contract.

steps.what_happens: A trigger fires on the device (app resume, window focus on a polling component, stale mark, cache age over five minutes, three-minute timer).
The app sends an authenticated GET to /api/me (mobile adds ?surface=mobile, Chrome ?surface=web).
The server builds the plan, feature flags, disabled features and the layered capability document from the account's entitlement and operator switches.
The app parses the response with the shared parser and stores it; controls re-render from the stored document.
On error the app keeps or discards its cache by app: web keeps (non-401), mobile keeps, VS Code keeps while signed in, CLI returns the default after expiry, Chrome sets the document to null.

features.summary: Auto is the default way to chat. For each message it picks one model and one provider route that the person's plan, workspace rules, region, credentials and remaining credits allow. If nothing qualifies it says so with reasons instead of guessing. Free plans get a fixed plan model, not Auto.

purpose.what_it_does: Auto looks at each message, lists the models the account may use, removes the ones that are retired, too costly for the remaining credits, blocked by workspace policy or region, or lacking a usable credential, ranks what is left and sends the message to one model on one provider route. [inferred from auto.ts:1340-1440, auto.ts:1722-1960]
purpose.why_it_exists: People should not need to know which model suits a task or which provider is healthy. Auto keeps cost and plan limits under control while still using a stronger model for hard work (brief S79.01, S79.04, S79.14, S79.15, S79.19).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person on a paid plan in Web, the Electron Desktop (which shows the hosted web app), Mobile, Chrome, VS Code and the CLI in Cloud mode; developers calling the public API with the Auto alias.
problems_solved: Choosing a model by hand for every task.
Paying for a strong model on a trivial question.
Failing a turn because one provider route is unhealthy.
Sending a request to a model the plan, workspace policy or region does not allow.
use_cases: A short greeting is answered on a cheap model; a coding question is moved to a stronger one.
A long chat stays on the same model while it remains eligible, which keeps the prompt cache warm.
A person near the end of their monthly credits keeps getting answers because costlier models are dropped.
A workspace that blocks one vendor never has Auto pick that vendor.

working: Eligibility filter before ranking: unknown or not-live or deprecated or past-deprecation model, tier admission, US-only policy, excluded providers, no-training, developer jurisdiction, no route for the trust mode, missing capability, too-small context (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1340-1435).
Route-level admission: workspace model policy, blocked commercial status, harness, zero data retention, no-training, regions (auto.ts:1060-1125).

Route ranking per model: healthy first, then has credential, observed-health penalty, expected cost, default route, route id; a warm-cache route wins unless it costs more than a ceiling multiple (auto.ts:1144-1196).

Plan clamp: tier maximum profile free/basic economy, pro balanced, max/enterprise/byok premium; Auto's profile per task (simple, general, creative economy; coding, reasoning, agentic, computer-use premium; long-context balanced) (routing-policies.json:416-440, auto.ts:1198-1216).

established.statement: Auto picks a model per request from the registry for the task, plan and constraints, on every app and the API.
Auto applies a task-specific routing profile, for example premium for coding and reasoning.
Candidates are filtered by capability, lifecycle, plan, policy, region and credentials before ranking.
Among eligible routes for a model one provider route is chosen by ranking on health, cost and cache.
Routing takes the user's remaining budget into account when choosing a route.
The founder wants Auto as the default and, on Mobile, the only routing choice.
Picker eligibility agrees with the server's effective plan, deployment, model and route policy; route failures identify the model actually executed.

acceptance_criteria: On Web with a paid plan and Auto selected, a one-line greeting and a long coding request can resolve to different models, and the answer shows the model used.
With a workspace policy that blocks a vendor, Auto never answers from that vendor.
With a nearly empty credit balance, Auto does not pick a model whose estimated cost exceeds the balance (except the fallback slot).
If no model qualifies, the person sees the 'Auto could not find a model' message and the API returns 422 model_route_unavailable.
On Free, selecting nothing special sends the plan's default model and the picker shows no Auto row.
In a CLI Cloud session started with --auto, the model name is printed at start and again when it changes.
--auto together with --model or --provider is rejected at parse time.
inferred: Mobile Auto should apply the same credit, training and policy rules as Web, because the product premise is one subscription system for every app.
Auto should never choose a Local on-device model, because Local, own-key and Cloud are separate boundaries (docs AGENTS.md §6).
proposed: [proposed] Send the Auto alias from Mobile (as Chrome does) so the server applies budget, training and policy rules, and keep the on-device call only for the picker preview.
[proposed] Add budget and training fields to the Rust resolver or document that own-key sessions have no credit budget.

steps.what_happens: Person picks Auto and sends a message on Web or Desktop; the client sends model 'auto' (an alias) to the chat completions API.

Server classifies the text, attachments and history, applies tool toggles, reads the credit balance, workspace policy, zero-retention rule, training opt-out, region and route health, then builds the routing request.
resolveAutoRoute filters, ranks and returns a selected route or an unavailable decision.
Selected model is written to the request; the call goes to the provider route through the managed adapters, with failover to other candidates before the first byte.
Mobile and Chrome run the same TypeScript router on the device first; Mobile sends the chosen model, Chrome sends the Auto alias.
CLI Cloud session sends 'auto' with an optional routing_profile to the gateway; CLI own-key session picks a model locally with the Rust resolver every turn.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The router reads the generated model registry (models, routes, harnesses, policies). Routes are provider routes through managed adapters; which provider serves a request depends on credentials available to the deployment (availableProviderIds, request-processor.ts:4706). No model name is written in this page on purpose.

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account required for Cloud Auto on every app. CLI falls back to the free policy with a warning when sign-in is missing (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:8004-8030).
access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace model policy can refuse a model or a provider and the router honours it (auto.ts:1070-1081). Workspace allowed trust modes exist in the router but no production caller sets them.
access_and_usage.subscription: Tier decides allowed slots and the highest band: free economy, basic economy, pro balanced, max/enterprise/byok premium (routing-policies.json:433-440). Auto alias minimum tier is basic (routing-policies.json:544). VS Code needs the developer_surfaces plan capability (modelConstants.ts:70).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Remaining credits drop costlier candidates when credits are allocated (request-processor.ts:4600-4616, auto.ts:1682). Credits are reserved per request (request-processor.ts:6160-6180 managed usage reservation). Rate limits: none found specific to Auto.
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_ROUTING_TASK_FAMILY_STAGE, AGI_ROUTING_OBSERVED_HEALTH, AGI_ROUTING_CANARY, AGI_ROUTING_SHADOW (default on), AGI_ROUTING_GATEWAY_ROUTES (apps/web/lib/services/gateway-routing.ts:13).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Capability, context window and harness features are checked per task (auto.ts:1415-1435). Image attachments need a multimodal-capable model through the task requirements.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Excluded providers for US-only (max and enterprise tiers), no-training, zero retention, workspace policy and region residency all remove routes (auto.ts:1060-1125, 1355-1385).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Auto never picks a Local on-device model; it resolves with trust mode managed_cloud (routing-request.ts:107). On Mobile a Local Mode chat refuses Cloud models (chatExecutionStore.ts:2262-2270). Desktop (Electron) answers every chat in the cloud (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:3235-3243).

Unhealthy routes rank last and failover rotates to the next candidate before the first byte.

features.summary: Beside Auto, a paid person can bias routing toward speed (Instant), capability (Best) or low cost (Economy). The choice only narrows the cost band and ordering; it never lets a model past plan or workspace limits. Web, Desktop, VS Code, the CLI and the API have it; Chrome has a Quick toggle; Mobile removed it by decision.

purpose.what_it_does: Sends a routing_profile of speed, quality or cost with the Auto request. The server swaps the Auto alias for the economy or premium alias and, for speed, asks the router to look at the fastest slots first. [inferred from request-processor.ts:3633-3637, 4769]
purpose.why_it_exists: Some people want a faster answer, the strongest model, or the cheapest model for a turn without picking one model by name (brief S79.05, S79.06, S79.07).
purpose.who_uses_it: Paid-plan people on Web and Desktop, VS Code users, CLI users with a saved Cloud session, Chrome users who want quicker cheaper answers, API callers.
problems_solved: Waiting on a heavy model for a simple question.
Overpaying for a simple task.
Needing the strongest model for one hard task without leaving Auto.
use_cases: Choose Instant for summaries.
Choose Best before a hard design question.
Choose Economy for bulk low-stakes questions.
In the CLI run /route speed before a quick lookup.

established.statement: A speed-first profile prefers the fastest eligible route.
A quality-first profile prefers the most capable eligible route.
A cost-first profile prefers the cheapest eligible route.
Web and desktop still offer Instant, Best and Economy under Auto; Mobile uses filters instead.
Chrome Quick is a per-turn Auto Economy override that keeps the saved selection and passes normal admission.

acceptance_criteria: On a paid Web plan, choosing Instant sends routing_profile 'speed' and the answering model is one of the faster slots the plan allows.
Choosing Best on a plan whose ceiling is premium sends routing_profile 'quality' and uses the premium band.
Choosing Auto sends no routing_profile.
On Free, the three rows are not shown.
In the CLI, /route bogus answers 'Unknown routing profile' and lists auto, speed, quality, cost.
In Chrome, Quick on does not change the saved model selection.
No profile ever returns a model the workspace policy forbids.
inferred: Best on a plan that cannot use the premium band should say so rather than silently use a lower band. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Hide or label the Best row when the tier ceiling is economy, as VS Code already locks rows by plan.

features.summary: Every message is labelled by kind (coding, research, agentic, image, long and so on) with fixed word patterns, attachments, length and the person's toggles. The label picks which models Auto may use. There is no model-based classifier. When nothing matches the default is general.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns a message plus its history, attachments and switches into one routing task type and, separately, a structural task family. Admission and ranking in Auto read these labels. [inferred from classify.ts:137-205, task-family.ts:173]
purpose.why_it_exists: Auto needs to know what the work is to pick a fit model: vision for images, large context for long chats, search-capable handling for current events (brief S79.09 to S79.13, S79.30).
purpose.who_uses_it: Nobody calls it directly; every Auto and every named-model request passes through it on all six apps.
problems_solved: Sending images to a model that cannot read them.
Sending a very long chat to a small context window.
Using a weak model for code.
Failing when the message type cannot be determined.
use_cases: Attach a photo: the request is routed to a multimodal-capable model.
Ask for 'the latest news today': treated as research.
Turn on Research: the request is research whatever the words say.
Paste a stack trace: treated as coding.

where_to_find_it: No control. It runs on every send in Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome, VS Code and CLI.
Toggles that override the text: Research, Work mode, office creation, code execution (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:1032-1043).
Response field x_agi_workforce.routing.task_type and task_confidence (response-builder.ts:409-413).
prerequisites: None.
screens_and_controls: Composer attachments and the Research, Work and code toggles (names as they appear per app were not collected).
journey: Type, attach files or images, and optionally switch on Research or Work.
Send.
The label is computed and used to route.
The answer comes from a model that fits the label.
feedback_and_outputs: API response carries task_type and task_confidence; Web turn logs include the classification (request-processor.ts:4512-4548).
CLI turn notice 'Auto route: <Task> -> <provider>/<model>' when an own-key session changes model (agent/chat.rs:725-729).
settings: Kill switch for the family stage: AGI_ROUTING_TASK_FAMILY_STAGE (task-family-routing.ts:71).

working: Priority-ordered classifier: separate-image-resource request gives agentic; image-generation intent gives image_generation; screenshot plus an action word gives computer-use; image or video attachment gives multimodal; over 50,000 estimated tokens gives long_context; browser action wording gives computer-use; code fence or code keywords give coding; reasoning verbs or arithmetic give reasoning; agent or tool wording gives agentic; research words give research; story or email drafting gives creative_writing; weak code words give coding; short text gives simple_chat; otherwise general at confidence 0.5 (packages/ai/routing/src/classify.ts:137-205).
Research words: latest, today, 2026, current, recent news, search the web, cite sources (classify.ts:97).
Conversation context: over 50,000 cumulative tokens forces long_context; a stable mode over the last 3 turns boosts confidence; a result at or above 0.85 may pivot (classify.ts:229-290).

Tool toggles override: research true gives research; work mode agiwork or office creation gives agentic; code execution gives coding; otherwise the classified type if the Web runtime serves it, else agentic when tools exist, else general (request-processor.ts:1020-1043).
Classification also switches tools on: research or search intent sets web_search; office and code-execution wording set their toggles (request-processor.ts:974-1010).
Task family: twelve families from structural signals only, no prose; unclear signals return null and Auto runs unchanged (packages/ai/routing/src/task-family.ts:68-215).
The family stage only reorders already admitted candidates and is on unless switched off (task-family-routing.ts:1-83, routing-stages.ts).

Surfaces: Web, Desktop and API classify on the server (request-processor.ts:4512-4548); Mobile and Chrome import the TypeScript classifier (cloudDispatchRouting.ts:49-58, managedChatRouting.ts:38-41); VS Code calls it per turn on text and images (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/routingTask.ts:17-27); CLI uses a hand-kept Rust mirror (apps/cli/src/routing/classify.rs:1-9).
incomplete: VS Code classifies with no history, so long-context and sticky logic do not apply there (routingTask.ts:26-27).
CLI mirror treats image attachments as images, never screenshots (routing/classify.rs:1-9).
disconnected_or_disabled: Confidence is advisory: nothing branches on it except the sticky pivot inside the classifier (classify.ts header 1-20).
Indic script detection only logs a line for a future pool (request-processor.ts:4585-4596).
not_available: No model-based classifier and no pluggable adapter; decided not to build (docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md D-2026-09-28-07).
Chrome: task family stage reached only through the server.

established.statement: Each request's task intent is classified and used for routing.
Which tools a request needs (research, agentic work, code execution) changes the routing task.
Attached images or video route the request to a multimodal-capable model.
Requests are classified by complexity so routing can set a quality floor or effort.
Requests needing current information are detected and routed to search-capable handling.
When classification fails or is ambiguous, routing falls back to a safe default.
A classification adapter such as Jev is not built.

acceptance_criteria: A message with an image attachment resolves to task type multimodal unless it is an image-generation request or a screenshot with an action word.
A conversation whose estimated tokens exceed 50,000 resolves to long_context.
With the Research toggle on, the task type is research whatever the text says.
With Work mode agiwork, the task type is agentic.
A message that matches nothing resolves to general (or simple_chat if under 80 characters and 15 words).
When the structural signals are unclear, no task family is set and the Auto result is the same as with the stage off.
inferred: Prompts in languages other than English get few keyword matches, so most fall to general. [inferred from the English-only patterns in classify.ts:20-100]
proposed: [proposed] Replace the hard-coded year in the research pattern with a rule that does not expire.
[proposed] Fix the header comment that says 5-turn while the code uses 3 (classify.ts:229).

steps.what_happens: Client sends text, attachments (image parts) and history with toggle fields.
Server classifies the last user text with history and attachments, applies conversation context, then toggle overrides.
Server builds structural signals and, if the stage is on, classifies a task family.
Task type feeds admission (required capabilities, context floor) and slot order; family reorders admitted candidates by cost above a floor.
Mobile and Chrome classify on the device before their own resolve call; CLI own-key sessions classify with the Rust mirror each turn.

features.summary: A person can pin one named model so the request runs on it, with the same eligibility checks as Auto. If it fails the answer is a refusal with reasons, not a swap. A provider route can be pinned in the data model, but no screen sets it, and a decision says there is no provider or route lock for customers.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person choose a specific model from the picker (or --model in the CLI) and keeps the request on it; the router only picks among that model's provider routes. [inferred from auto.ts:1760-1850]
purpose.why_it_exists: Some work needs one known model. Customers choose a model, never a supplier (docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md D-2026-09-28-07).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who wants a particular model; CLI users who force a provider for own-key or local use.
problems_solved: Getting a different model than the one chosen.
Hidden provider changes for a named model.
use_cases: Pick a model in the Web picker for one conversation.
Run agi --model <id> in a script.
Run agi --provider ollama for a local server (provider names listed in the flag help).
Start a chat on the project's default model (F079-05).

CLI --auto conflicts with --model and --provider (lib.rs:477).
incomplete: Mobile and Chrome pass fallbackToAutoForCapabilityMismatch true, so a named model that lacks a needed capability is answered by Auto with reason capability_fallback (cloudDispatchRouting.ts:94; managedChatRouting.ts:55; auto.ts:1822-1840). Web main chat does not set it.

Web out-of-credit path swaps a named model for a cheaper one unless a route is pinned, reporting fallback.original_model and reason insufficient_credits (request-processor.ts:6052-6113; response-builder.ts:424-428).
Chrome reconciles a stored selection not in the admitted list back to 'auto' (managedModelPicker.ts:273-287).
disconnected_or_disabled: Provider pin and route pin have storage, API fields and an error message but no picker control; setSelectedModelId(id, routeId) has no UI caller (grep of apps/web features and app).
Mobile, VS Code and Chrome have no provider or route lock (brief S79.17, S79.18); decision D-2026-09-28-07 says none on web, desktop, API or CLI managed routes.

steps.what_happens: Person selects a model; Web stores it and, on first message, creates the conversation with model and optional route.
Server reads the conversation's selected_route_id and builds the routing request with requiredRouteId.
Router checks the named model (eligibility) and the pinned route if any; returns selected or an unavailable code.
Request goes to the provider route; on availability failure it rotates to another route of the same model only.
If credits run out and no route is pinned, a cheaper model may answer and the response says so.
CLI --model or --provider sets the model and provider for the session; a Local session blocks a model that routes elsewhere.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Any model in the registry that the plan, policy, region and credentials allow. Providers are chosen only among that model's declared routes. CLI --provider help lists anthropic, openai, google, ollama (lib.rs:194).

access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Same credit reservation as Auto; out-of-credit may swap a named model.
access_and_usage.flags: none found for the picker; AGI_ROUTING_GATEWAY_ROUTES affects route availability.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Missing capability or context gives a refusal on Web; Mobile and Chrome fall back to Auto instead.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Excluded-provider rule for Auto does not apply to a named model, but no-training, region, transport and workspace policy do (auto.ts:182-215, 1760-1775).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Local models are chosen from the same picker on Mobile; the Electron Desktop refuses on-device inference in chat (dispatcher.ts:3235-3243); CLI Local sessions block any model that routes outside Local (agent/mod.rs:1791-1825).

features.summary: A Managed Cloud project can store a default model. On Web a new chat in that project starts on it once; Mobile shows and applies it for Cloud chats; VS Code shows it and offers a button that opens the picker, but does not switch by itself. The CLI and Chrome have no project default.

purpose.who_uses_it: People with Managed Cloud projects on Web, Desktop, Mobile and VS Code.

Starting a project chat on whatever model was last used.
