aliases: Only use models that do not train on your chats
features.summary: There is no single privacy-first button. Privacy comes from three modes (Local, own key, Cloud), a workspace zero-data-retention rule, a per-person no-training opt-out and a US-only option. Routing then keeps only routes that pass, and fails with a clear message when none do. On Desktop, chat is Cloud-only in code.

purpose.what_it_does: Removes routes and models that would keep, train on or move data against the person's or workspace's rules, and refuses requests that would cross a trust boundary without consent. [inferred from auto.ts:1099-1115, request-processor.ts:4694-4700, apps/cli/src/agent/mod.rs:1791-1825]
purpose.why_it_exists: People and workspaces need to know where data goes. Local, own key and Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing may move a chat across silently (AGENTS.md §6; brief S79.08).
purpose.who_uses_it: Privacy-conscious people, workspace admins, regulated teams, CLI developers working on private code.
problems_solved: A chat being used to train a provider's model.
A Local session leaking to a cloud model.
A workspace using providers that keep data.
use_cases: Turn on 'Only use models that do not train on your chats'.

A CLI Local session refuses a cloud model and points to /continue-with-cloud.
A Mobile Local Mode chat refuses a Cloud model.

established.statement: A privacy-first profile keeps requests on local models or zero-retention routes.

Local, own key and Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing may silently route a Local chat, file or session to own key or managed cloud; a Local-to-own-key move is an explicit fork with consent and a visible provider label.
Security behaviour fails closed; routing never relies on registry membership to cross boundaries.
Avoid silent cloud routing in developer workflows.

steps.what_happens: Server reads training opt-out (and Health and Google-data conditions), zero-retention rule, workspace model policy and region in parallel before routing.
Managed providers are filtered to those that keep inputs out of training when the opt-out is on; none left gives 403.
Router drops routes without zero retention and routes or models that may train, for Auto and for named models.
Failover and the credit swap re-check the same rule on every hop.
CLI checks the session's trust mode against the model's provider before each turn and refuses on mismatch.
Mobile Local chats run on-device models and refuse Cloud ones; Cloud chats send to our servers.

features.summary: When a model route is failing, Auto ranks it lower, and the Cloud server moves a failing call to another route or model before any text reaches the person. Separately, apps show buttons that let the person pick another model. The CLI rotates down a user-written model chain on transient errors.

purpose.what_it_does: Two linked parts. (1) Health and fallback: Auto routing demotes routes with recent failures and builds a fallback plan of other hosts of the same model first, then other models (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:757-764, :937-960, :1581-1612). On Cloud the server rotates through that plan on availability failures (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/managed-failover.ts:1-58). The CLI rotates down a chain the user typed (apps/cli/src/routing/fallback.rs:20-116). (2) Switch offers: buttons that open or apply a different model after a refusal, a failure, a limit or a capability mismatch. The person always clicks; nothing flips by itself.
purpose.why_it_exists: One provider outage or rate limit should not end a turn, and a person who is blocked should see a way out in one click. Rotation only happens inside rules for trust, plan and data policy, so a fallback never crosses a boundary the person did not accept [inferred from the guards in managed-failover.ts:1-58 and apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:2114-2127].
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person using Auto or a pinned model on Web, Desktop (hosted web), Mobile, Chrome and VS Code on Cloud; CLI users who set a model chain; operators who tune the kill switches.
problems_solved: A failing or rate-limited provider route no longer ranks first for the next request.
A failed Cloud call can be answered by another route or another model before the first byte reaches the person.
A blocked person (image edit with a model that cannot edit, Local model with attachments, free limit reached, refusal) gets a one-click path to another model.
CLI users avoid the rate-limit cliff by naming backup models.
use_cases: A provider returns server errors; Auto answers on another host or model and the answer carries a notice that a backup answered.
On Web the person attaches an image in image mode with a model that cannot edit; the notice offers 'Use <model>'.
In the CLI the person runs agi with a comma list of models; a 429 on the first rotates to the second and prints a 'Falling back' line.
In VS Code a stream is interrupted; the error card shows 'Switch model' which opens the model picker.

AGI_ROUTE_HEALTH_*, AGI_ROUTE_BREAKER_*, AGI_MODEL_LOCKOUT_*, AGI_CREDENTIAL_COOLDOWN_* names tune windows and breaker thresholds (packages/ai/routing/src/route-health-store.ts:48-71). Values not recorded here.

working: Observed route health lowers a route's rank by failure band and latency band; it also penalises routes that did not honour a capability the request uses (auto.ts:900-960, :1285).
The fallback plan keeps up to 2 other hosts of the same model before a different model, up to 4 fallback routes (auto.ts:757-764, :1581-1612).
If the preferred route is parked, Auto picks a dispatchable slot with reason health_fallback (auto.ts:2076-2092).
Observed health is supplied from stored snapshots on the Cloud request path (apps/web/lib/server/managed-cloud-routing/routing-request.ts:127; request-processor.ts:2775-2800).
Cloud server rotates on availability failures before the first byte, across models only for Auto, never after tool-call ids bind the turn to a provider (managed-failover.ts:1-58).

CLI FallbackChain rotates on rate-limit, network, stream and 5xx errors by default, not on bad auth or bad requests (apps/cli/src/routing/fallback.rs:103-116); the loop refuses to move a Local session to a cloud provider and restores state (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:2114-2127).
CLI Auto on an own-key session installs a fallback chain built from the Auto selection (chat.rs:707-717).
Switch offers exist on Web (image edit, Local model, paywall), Mobile (blocked image request), VS Code (failure codes), Chrome (failure bubble) and CLI (error hints) as listed under user_experience.
incomplete: The CLI 'switch offer' is text telling the person to re-run with --fallback-model or /model; there is no button (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:549,619-623,648).
A chain given to the CLI rotates automatically without asking at each failure; the person opted in by writing the chain (fallback.rs:42-64) [inferred reading of 'explicit'].
Mobile: only the blocked-image switch offer was found; no failure-triggered switch button found (callers: apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:742,770; apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/chat.tsx:146).
disconnected_or_disabled: FallbackOn::RateLimit and FallbackOn::Any exist but the enum carries allow(dead_code) and parse only builds the default Transient value (apps/cli/src/routing/fallback.rs:14-24,42-54).
not_available: Desktop-specific (native Tauri) code for these buttons was not found; the public Desktop shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
Local mode on Mobile and Desktop: no automatic fallback to Cloud was found; the CLI explicitly refuses it (chat.rs:2114-2127). Mobile Local behaviour for failures is unknown.

established.statement: Observed health of each route lowers its rank; can be turned off with AGI_ROUTING_OBSERVED_HEALTH=0.
Same-model fallbacks come first, then another model.
CLI chain rotates only on rate-limit, network or server errors, not bad auth or bad requests.
Unhealthy routes are demoted and failed calls fall back to healthy alternatives.
When another model would work better, the user is offered an explicit one-click switch; nothing flips by itself.
Local, own key and Cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing silently routes a Local turn to another boundary.

acceptance_criteria: With observed health on, a route with a high recent failure rate ranks behind a healthy route for the same model request.
With AGI_ROUTING_OBSERVED_HEALTH set to off, the failure and latency penalty is zero.
A Cloud Auto request whose first route fails with an availability error is answered by another route or model and the response carries X-AGI-Fallback-Reason.
A CLI chain 'a,b' moves to b on a 429, 5xx or network error, and does not move on an authentication error.
A CLI Local session never moves to a cloud model through the chain; it stops with an error.
On Web, with an image attached in image mode and a model that cannot edit, the notice shows 'Use <model>' and clicking it changes the image model without sending.
On VS Code and Chrome, a failed turn of an eligible kind shows 'Switch model' and clicking opens the picker without changing the model by itself.
inferred: A fallback must stay inside the same trust mode and the same data policy (training opt-out, region, workspace policy) [inferred from managed-failover.ts:1-58].
A switch offer must name the model it will use when the app already knows it [inferred from 'Use <model>' wording].
proposed: [proposed] Give the CLI a one-keystroke 'switch model' prompt on a failed turn in the TUI instead of only text hints.
[proposed] Give Mobile a failure-time 'Switch model' action like VS Code and Chrome.

steps.what_happens: Cloud turn: the web route builds an Auto routing request with stored route and credential health snapshots.
The resolver ranks admissible routes, adds the observed penalty, and builds up to four fallback routes (same-model hosts first).
The request goes to the provider; on an availability failure before the first byte the server tries the next plan entry, re-checking plan, data policy and training opt-out per hop.
The provider answers the turn.
The outcome of each attempt is written back to the route health store so the next request is ranked with it.
Response headers carry the fallback reason; the client stores it in message metadata and shows a notice.
CLI turn with a chain: a failed call is classified; if the error is transient the loop rotates to the next model after validating the privacy boundary, and calls the provider again.
Switch button click in Web, Mobile, VS Code or Chrome only changes the selected model or opens the picker.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Models come from the generated catalog and the Auto policy slots, not from the feature code. The fallback plan draws only on slots the plan tier is allowed (auto.ts:693). Providers are tried by route; credentials can be cooled down (route-health-store.ts:64-71). The CLI chain holds model names the person typed; provider is detected from the name (apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs:75-86).

access_and_usage.account: Cloud fallback and Cloud switch offers need a signed-in Cloud turn. CLI chains work with own keys without sign-in; Managed Cloud in the CLI needs 'agi login' (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:621-624).
access_and_usage.permissions: Fallback candidates are re-checked at attempt time against plan tier, workspace model policy and provider training opt-out (managed-failover.ts:1-58). The CLI refuses a rotation that would cross the Local boundary (chat.rs:2114-2127).
access_and_usage.subscription: The fallback plan only uses slots the tier is allowed (auto.ts:693). The paywall card offers an alternative model not covered by the limit (InlinePaywallCard.tsx:457-470). Billing for a rotated Cloud turn is one reservation settled at the price of the model that served (managed-failover.ts:1-58).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: At most 4 fallback routes, 2 same-model hosts before another model (auto.ts:757-764). Concurrency limits belong to the plan (not this feature).
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_ROUTING_OBSERVED_HEALTH (kill switch, on by default); route health, breaker, lockout and credential cooldown variables listed under settings.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Capability fallback: a model that cannot handle the request is replaced with reason capability_fallback when the request allows it (auto.ts:1822-1834). The image-edit offer depends on the media catalogue saying a model supports edit (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1372-1376).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Candidates whose provider may train on inputs are skipped when the account opted out (managed-failover.ts:1-58). Which providers are tried: provider folders under packages/ai/providers; exact set per request comes from the registry.
access_and_usage.local_mode: No fallback to another boundary. Web shows 'Switch to a cloud model' as an explicit person-initiated switch for a Local model with attachments or a new project chat (ChatComposerNew.tsx:1588-1592,5311-5349). The CLI Local session restores state and stops rather than egress (chat.rs:2114-2127). Mobile and Desktop Local failure handling: unknown.

features.summary: Every answer names the model that wrote it. When Auto moves a chat to another model, a short grey line says 'Moved to <model>: <reason>'. Each Cloud routing decision is also stored with the routing policy version that made it, so a turn can be traced later.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows the served model on each answer, shows a one-time receipt when Auto changed the chat's model with a plain-language reason, and records a trace for every Cloud routing decision that includes the policy version (packages/ai/routing/src/routing-trace.ts:16,153-154).
purpose.why_it_exists: A person should never wonder which model answered or why it changed; Auto keeps a conversation on its model and moves only for a reason (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-05-living-decision-model.md, D-2026-09-05-06). Engineers need a trace to explain a turn later.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using Auto on Web, Desktop (hosted web), Mobile, Chrome and CLI; engineers and operators reading traces.
problems_solved: Silent model changes mid-chat.
Not knowing which model produced an answer.
No way to link a past decision to the routing rules in force.
use_cases: Person reads 'Moved to <model>: the model Auto would normally use was having trouble' under an answer.
Person checks the model name under an answer in VS Code.
CLI user sees 'Auto route: <task> -> <provider>/<model>' when an own-key Auto session changes model.
Engineer queries a request id in routing_decision_traces to see policyVersion in the trace.

established.statement: The user can see why Auto chose or moved to a model.
Each answer shows which model actually produced it.
Routing policies are versioned and each decision traces to its policy version.
The line is a receipt shown once after the answer finishes.
Auto stays on the conversation's model and escalates on a failure signal; quality moves up, never sideways or down.

acceptance_criteria: After a finished Auto answer served by a model other than the previous one, a 'Moved to <model>' line appears once; during streaming it does not.
A known reason code shows its plain phrase; an unknown code shows the raw code.
An answer on a pinned (manual) model shows no 'Moved to' line.
Every finished answer shows its served model on Web, Mobile, Chrome, CLI and VS Code.
A Cloud turn writes one routing_decision_traces row whose trace JSON has policyVersion equal to the registry release version.
A failed trace write never fails the turn.

Server builds the decision trace with policyVersion and starts an asynchronous write.

CLI own-key Auto session re-classifies each turn locally against the bundled registry and prints the notice.
Chrome compares the answered model with the previous answer's model and sets movedFromModel.

features.summary: Send one prompt to two or three models and read the answers side by side. Web has a Compare answers page; Mobile has a Compare Models screen for two models in Cloud mode. Tools and memory are switched off for these requests. A model that fails does not stop the others.

purpose.what_it_does: Streams the same prompt to several chosen models in parallel (within the plan's concurrency) and shows each answer with its state, time to first text and total time.
purpose.why_it_exists: People choose between models by reading real answers; this matches a feature leaders ship [inferred from the brief's parity framing; doc: AGENTS.md section 10].
purpose.who_uses_it: Web (and Desktop through the hosted app) and Mobile Cloud users.
problems_solved: Picking a model by name alone.
Copying a prompt between chats to compare.
One failing model ruining the comparison.
use_cases: Open /models/compare and compare three models on a draft email.
Select models in the catalogue and click 'Compare answers'.
On Mobile type /compare and compare two models on a question.
A free plan runs one answer at a time; the second starts when the first ends.

features.summary: In the CLI, a markdown file with front matter defines a custom agent. Running agi --agent <name> or choosing it with /agents applies its model, tool limits, turn limit, permission mode and a spend cap to the session. A cap can only lower an existing budget. Agents started by the model do not get their own model.

purpose.what_it_does: Loads agent definition files from user and project folders and applies them to a CLI session (apps/cli/src/agents.rs:80-139).
purpose.why_it_exists: To let a person keep named specialists with their own prompt, tools, model and cost cap, as other coding agents allow [inferred].
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI users, including teams that commit agent files to a repository.
problems_solved: Repeating the same instructions and tool limits.
Running a cheap model for a narrow job.
Capping spend for a role.
use_cases: A 'reviewer' agent limited to read tools and a small budget.
A project agent using a specific model for migrations.
A model-called helper agent narrowed to the parent's tools.

where_to_find_it: CLI flag --agent <name> (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:424-426).
REPL slash command /agents (apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:71).
Agent files in .agiworkforce/agents/ and .claude/agents/ in a trusted project, and ~/.agiworkforce/agents/ and ~/.claude/agents/ (agents.rs, discover_agents).
prerequisites: CLI installed. Project agents load only when the workspace is trusted to supply configuration (agents.rs trusted_project).
A model named in the file must be switchable in the session.
screens_and_controls: Front matter keys read: name, description, model, tools, disallowedTools (or disallowed_tools), maxTurns (or max_turns), permissionMode (or permission_mode), color, skills, mcpServers, maxBudgetUsd (or max_budget_usd); the rest of the file is the system prompt (agents.rs parse at ~1457-1520).
Editable fields in the /agents editor: description, model, color, tools, disallowedTools, skills, maxTurns, maxBudgetUsd, permissionMode, prompt (agents.rs:1117-1128).
Template written by create: name, description, model, color, tools, disallowedTools, skills, maxTurns 20, permissionMode default (agents.rs:1085).
journey: Create a markdown file with the front matter in an agents folder.
Run agi --agent <name>, or in the REPL run /agents and pick one.
The CLI loads the definition and applies it to the session.
If the model cannot be switched, a message 'Agent `<name>` model override ignored: ...' is printed and the session keeps its model (agents.rs:92-99).
feedback_and_outputs: Warning if agent not found: 'Agent `<x>` not found. Use `/agents` to list available agents.' (apps/cli/src/repl/mod.rs:621).
Message when the agent asks for a looser permission mode than the session: 'the session keeps <mode>' (agents.rs:163-170).
Spend cap applied silently; the session ends at the budget.
settings: Session budget (max_budget_usd) that the agent cap lowers.
Workspace trust setting that allows project agents.

working: apply_to_session switches model, intersects tools with the caller's allowlist, appends denylists, sets max turns, narrows permission mode, caps spend, injects the system prompt and preloads skills (agents.rs:80-139).
cap_spend takes the smaller of the agent cap and the existing budget (agents.rs:57-65).
Discovery order: user folders first, then trusted project folders; the first definition of a name wins (agents.rs discover_agents, users_before_project).
Plugin-provided agent paths are loaded if they stay within the plugin root (agents.rs discover_agents_from).
Model-called subagents use apply_to_subagent_session: tools intersected with the parent, max turns only lowered, spend capped, model and permission mode ignored (agents.rs:187-196).
incomplete: A model-spawned specialist cannot use its own model; the model override is deliberately withheld (agents.rs:187-196,495-497).
not_available: Mobile and Chrome: missing per brief; no code searched beyond the brief.
Web, Desktop, VS Code: not listed in the brief; custom agent files with their own model were not found in these apps in the files opened (not exhaustively searched).

established.statement: Work is delegated to specialist workers that can use their own models.
The file sets the session model, allowed tools and spend cap; the cap can only lower an existing budget.
A definition file cannot widen the session's authority: permission mode only narrows, tools stay within the caller's allowlist.

acceptance_criteria: Running agi --agent <name> with a model line switches the session model.
A tools list narrows the tools to the intersection with any command-line allowlist.
An agent with a looser permission mode than the session leaves the session mode unchanged and prints a message.
maxBudgetUsd 5 on a session with budget 2 leaves 2; on a session with no budget sets 5.
A model-called subagent never changes the session model.
An agent in an untrusted project folder is not loaded.
An unknown agent name prints the not-found message.
inferred: The CLI model override still obeys the trust boundary rules of switch_model [inferred from agents.rs:92-99 using session.switch_model].
proposed: [proposed] Allow a model-called specialist to pick a model only within the same trust mode and plan, with consent shown.
[proposed] Surface agents in VS Code through the same definition files.

features.summary: Four routing ideas the brief marks not applicable in every app: a worker asking a stronger advisor model, abstaining when unsure, a pluggable classifier adapter, and a routing evaluation dashboard. The code has related but different pieces: a heuristic classifier with no model fallback, a shadow decision provider, and operator views over routing traces.

purpose.what_it_does: Records what is not built as a product feature and what nearby code exists, so no one assumes more or less than the code shows.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief lists these four items so the product area is complete; the statuses say not applicable.
purpose.who_uses_it: Engineers and testers planning routing work; nobody uses these as features today.
problems_solved: Avoids false claims that the product has advisor escalation or abstention.
Points operators to the partial visibility that does exist.
use_cases: An engineer asks 'can a model ask a stronger model for help?'; answer: no such code found.
An operator asks 'where can I see routing outcomes?'; answer: the Operator dashboard rollout tab, observability panels and SLO catalogue.
A planner asks 'is Jev wired into routing?'; answer: a semantic decision transport exists, shadow-first, and does not select the model.

Operators: Operator dashboard tab 'rollout' showing 'Model rollout' (apps/web/features/admin/pages/OperatorDashboardPage.tsx:46,487; apps/web/features/admin/components/ModelRolloutPanel.tsx:46-50).
Observability dashboard definition 'Model routing' with panels 'Routing decisions by route' and 'Share of turns with no route' (apps/web/lib/observability/dashboards.ts:847-871).
prerequisites: Operator pages need a platform admin (apps/web/app/api/admin/model-rollout/route.ts:50-54).
screens_and_controls: Rollout panel reads GET /api/admin/model-rollout: stage switches (observed health, canary, shadow), canary and shadow slots, and recent benchmarks (route.ts:56-66).
journey: Operator opens the Operator dashboard, selects the rollout tab, reads stage flags, slots and benchmarks.
feedback_and_outputs: Benchmarks by model, lifecycle stage and cohort computed by a cron from routing_decision_traces (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/rollout-evaluation-service.ts; cron route apps/web/app/api/cron/evaluate-model-rollout/route.ts; schedule in vercel.json:182).
settings: AGI_ROLLOUT_WINDOW_MS, AGI_ROLLOUT_MIN_SAMPLES, AGI_ROLLOUT_FAILURE_RATE_INCREASE, AGI_ROLLOUT_LATENCY_RATIO, AGI_ROLLOUT_COST_RATIO (rollout-evaluation-service.ts:21-29).
TYPESAFE_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_BASE_URL, TYPESAFE_MODEL, TYPESAFE_INPUT_MICROUSD_PER_MTOK configure the decision transport; names only (apps/web/lib/services/semantic-decisions/config.ts:24-34).

working: Heuristic classifier with sticky pivot and token guard; it has no model fallback and every caller routes on type alone (packages/ai/routing/src/classify.ts:1-12).

steps.what_happens: The app renders plans from the catalog compiled into it (web, mobile, VS Code, Chrome via shared package; CLI via embedded text of the allowance file and a Rust capability table).
Web asks for regional prices and which plans can be checked out in the person's country.
A buyer starts checkout; the server resolves the purchasable plan, picks the regional Stripe price and sends the current catalog version in session metadata.
Stripe hosts payment and sends events to our webhook.
The webhook writes subscriptions.plan_catalog_version at purchase, keeps it on a same-price renewal and replaces it when the price changes.
On every request the entitlement bundle carries the plan and the version it was sold under.
Clients learn the plan from the account endpoint (mobile calls /api/me?surface=mobile) and cache it.

features.summary: Each plan has a managed-usage allowance counted in credits over a rolling 5-hour window, a rolling week and the billing month. Paid plans state how many times more usage they give than the plan below. A separate weekly cap, 30% of the week, covers the most capable models. Ultra has no 5-hour cap.

purpose.what_it_does: Defines credit allowances per plan and window (packages/contracts/types/src/managed-usage-limits.ts:31-87), derives the 'N times more usage than <plan>' copy from those numbers (lines 123-215), and refuses a Cloud request that would pass a window with a reset time (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-request-service.ts:442-460, 473).
purpose.why_it_exists: So the plans differ in a stated, checkable amount of usage, and a person who hits a limit is told which window and when it refills.
purpose.who_uses_it: People on a paid or Free Cloud plan; support staff explaining a refusal; engineers changing allowances; testers.

steps.what_happens: Client sends a Cloud chat turn with the account token.
The auth gate resolves the plan and entitlement; a lapsed paid plan is served as Free.
The reservation builds the 5-hour, weekly and flagship caps for the plan and its sold-under catalog version, scaled by the revenue ratio.
The database reserves credits for the turn or declines with a reason (session, weekly, flagship, monthly).
On decline the server returns 429 or 402 with a code and reset time; the client shows the message.
Clients read usage and windows from the usage endpoint and render meters.

data.where_stored: managed usage request records in the database (table name not read)

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Credits are charged from provider cost of the model used. A model's class (flagship or standard) decides whether the flagship weekly window also applies (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-request-service.ts:797). Credits are spent the same whichever provider serves the model; per-provider rates are in the model catalog (SYS-model-catalog-and-routing).

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in AGI account on a Cloud plan. Local and own-key use has no AGI allowance.
access_and_usage.permissions: Anyone on the plan can see their own usage. Team seat members see their own allowance; the workspace spend cap is set by an admin (see F081-05).
access_and_usage.subscription: All plans from Free up have an allowance. Enterprise is unlimited under contract (managed-usage-limits.ts:84).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Windows: 5 hours rolling, 7 days rolling, billing month; flagship weekly = 30% of weekly credits (managed-usage-limits.ts:27). Quota warnings at 80% and 95% (managed-usage-policy.ts:243-244). A reset grant can refill the 5-hour and weekly windows (UsageSection.tsx:479-482).
access_and_usage.flags: None found in the code that turn the windows on or off per environment; extra-usage credits are a separate opt-in (see other areas).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Flagship-class models are the only ones counted in the flagship weekly window; they need Max, Ultra, Team Premium or Enterprise to select (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:2196-2243).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: None found in the code; allowances are provider agnostic.
access_and_usage.local_mode: No AGI plan limit applies to Local or own-key requests (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:2318-2319). The catalog gives local-only and byok zero managed usage (managed-usage-limits.ts:31-34). The CLI 'usage' command reports the usage as unavailable in local-only mode (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:340-352,523).

steps.what_happens: After sign-in the server hands the client the plan's attachment limits in the account response.
The client blocks a file over the published size or count before upload.
The server admits the upload: plan size, daily count in a key-value store, then storage used plus incoming bytes against the plan limit.
A chat turn takes a concurrency slot keyed by user; over the limit returns 429.
The slot is released when the stream ends, errors or is cancelled, or ages out after 360 seconds.
The requested effort is clamped to the plan before the model call.

steps.what_happens: Token is verified; its signed claims decide the surface (web, Chrome, mobile, desktop shell, developer, API key).
The gate looks up the plan and subscription status; a lapsed paid plan is treated as Free.
The needed capability for that surface is checked against the table; a miss returns 403 with a code and the required plan.
Other features check their own capability on their route.
Apps read the granted capability list in the account response and lock controls.
The person sees the message and a link to web pricing or the paywall.

data.what: Plan and granted capabilities cached on the phone

data.synced: Refreshed from the server on use

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The capability table names no model or provider. Plan-gated features that call providers (image, video, research) are routed by the model catalog; access by plan is checked first (SYS-model-catalog-and-routing; SYS-agents-tools-and-automation).

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in AGI account for every gate; an unbound token or no credential is refused.
access_and_usage.permissions: Team admin needs the workspace admin role plus a team plan; SSO and SCIM need Enterprise (apps/web/app/api/settings/team/team-admin-access.ts; apps/web/lib/server/sso/sso-access.ts).
access_and_usage.subscription: See the capability table in billing-catalog.ts:343-364. A lapsed subscription is served as Free (auth-gate.ts:341-352).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Capability checks themselves do not meter. Image and video generation have their own usage rules (outside these six features).
access_and_usage.flags: Connector release state coming_soon; mobile FEATURES flags; surface release labels; server flags per feature (for example the remote control gate).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: A capability can be allowed by plan while the chosen model cannot do it; that check is separate (SYS-model-catalog-and-routing).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: None found in the code at the plan layer. Plan access does not depend on a provider.
access_and_usage.local_mode: No plan capability check runs for Local or own-key use. The catalog marks the local-only and byok tiers as free of charge with no managed capabilities (billing-catalog.ts:166-181,478-482).

steps.what_happens: A member's request resolves entitlement: own paid row first, then seat candidates from the workspace owner's subscription.
The seat is accepted if the owner's subscription is entitled and the member's join rank is within licensed seats.
A monthly ledger is created for the member sized by the seat plan's budget.
Each request reserves credits against the member's ledger and, when set, checks the workspace month-to-date cap.
On a crossing in block mode the server audits the event and returns 402.

features.summary: Individual plans are billed monthly; only Team offers monthly or annual. An upgrade is charged now with credit for unused time and shows the charge and next renewal before confirming. A downgrade is scheduled for the end of the period. Self-serve plans have no grace period: a failed renewal moves the account to Free until paid. Mobile store purchase is switched off.

features.summary: Four linked billing features of AGI Cloud. A plan can be a trial that ends and reverts to Free. Promotion codes and bonus credits give extra value. Bought top-up credits form a separate balance. An opt-in switch lets bought credits pay for turns after a plan limit stops you. It is built on web, and on the Tauri desktop only partly.

purpose.what_it_does: It lets an account (1) hold a trialing plan with an end date, (2) get a discount through a promotion code or extra bonus credits, (3) buy credit top-ups that sit in a purchased balance apart from the plan allowance, and (4) switch on overage, so purchased credits fund a turn once a 5-hour, weekly or flagship-weekly plan window is used up. Overage is off by default. The trial-end job moves ended code-granted trials to Free (apps/web/lib/services/code-trial-expiry.ts:14-31).
purpose.why_it_exists: Heavy users of a capped plan need a way to keep working without moving to a bigger plan. New users need a low-risk way to try a paid plan. Operators need a way to give goodwill value. The commercial document says the plan allowance and the purchased balance are two different entitlements (doc: docs/product/commercial.md:229-246).
purpose.who_uses_it: Paying individual subscribers billed by Stripe, Apple or Google (buy credits, switch overage). New or referred users (trial). Anyone with a promotion code. Operators (grant bonus credits, configure usage-limit promotions). A person on an organization-managed plan cannot buy or switch; the refusal names the plan manager (doc: docs/product/commercial.md:260-264).
problems_solved: A person who hits a rolling usage limit has no way to continue except waiting or upgrading
A trial must not turn into a free plan for ever
Bought money must not vanish at renewal, and must not be spent without the person's opt-in
Discounts and goodwill need to be visible to the person
use_cases: A Pro subscriber hits the 5-hour limit, buys credits and turns on 'Keep going after a usage limit'
A friend invited through a referral gets a 7-day Pro trial at checkout
A person types a promotion code on the upgrade screen and sees the discount before paying
An operator grants bonus credits to a customer as goodwill

established.statement: A plan can be granted as a time-limited trial that is shown as a trial and ends (reverts or bills) when its period is over.
Promotional entitlements (promo codes, bonus credits, invite grants) exist, are applied to the account and are visible to the user.
Users can buy credit top-ups that form a separate purchased balance, which carries over and is shown apart from the plan allowance.
Users can opt in to spending purchased credits past a plan limit (overage), off by default, and overage use is accounted separately from the plan windows.
Purchased credits are never spent while usage credits are off; a credit turn is tagged is_overage for its whole life and plan windows exclude it.
Only accounts billed by Stripe, Apple or Google buy and switch credits; others are told the plan manager controls them.
Purchased top-ups remain separate and usage never resets on upgrade.

acceptance_criteria: A new account has overage off; GET /api/billing/overage returns enabled=false.
PUT /api/billing/overage { enabled: true } on a plan returns enabled=true and a refusal on a Free account with no subscription row says to start a plan.
A top-up of 20 dollars completed in Stripe raises Purchased credits by 1000 credits and does not change the plan or renewal date.
With overage off, a turn past a rolling limit is refused with text that says to turn on credits; with overage on and enough credits, the turn is admitted and the 5-hour and weekly meters do not rise.
A trialing subscription with no store or Stripe id and a past end date becomes Free after the next job run; one with a Stripe id is not touched.
An invalid or expired promotion code shows an error and leaves the plan and the price unchanged.
Usage shows Bonus credits and Purchased credits as rows separate from the plan meters.

steps.what_happens: Person presses Buy in Settings > Billing; the web page (or the hosted page in the public Desktop) sends the amount.
Server checks CSRF, rate limit, plan-change gate, organization policy, amount, paid plan, USD billing and the daily cap, then creates a Stripe payment session with the credit metadata.
Person pays on the Stripe page.
Stripe webhook adds credits to the purchased balance and writes a 'purchase' ledger row and an expiring-lot row.
Person switches overage; PUT writes subscriptions.overage_enabled and records an audit event.

On each managed turn, a database function reserves cost under a per-user lock; if a rolling cap would be crossed and credit headroom covers the estimate it admits the turn as overage, else it refuses.
Hourly cron ends code-granted trials; daily crons expire bonus credits and local-law purchase lots; hourly cron sends trial reminders.

data.synced: Read by every app from the server; not stored on the device
Server is the source; apps read it through the usage and billing endpoints
data.retained_or_deleted: Carries across renewals; owner is immutable (doc: docs/product/commercial.md:264-267)
Credit history shown to the person; deleted with the account (apps/web/app/trust/page.tsx lists bonus and purchase tables in erasure)
Expire only under local-law rules via a daily job
Inherited by every ledger row of the request
Set to canceled and Free at expiry for code-granted trials

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The feature does not choose a model. Overage pays for managed (Cloud) turns made on provider routes chosen by routing; flagship-model caps are one of the windows overage can pass (migration 0281:224-237). access_and_usage.account: An AGI account signed in to Cloud is required. Only accounts billed by Stripe, Apple or Google can buy credits or switch overage (BillingSection.tsx:454-456; top-up/route.ts:149-158).

features.summary: Tells a signed-in person which plan their AGI Subscription account is on and when the current billing period ends or renews. The server computes the plan on every read. Web, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome each show the plan in their own layout. Only web Billing and mobile Billing show period dates.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows the plan name and the billing period or renewal date taken from the server. The managed usage summary endpoint returns plan_tier, effective_plan_tier, subscription_status, period_start and period_end (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-summary-service.ts:211-221). Each app turns those fields into its own labels.
purpose.why_it_exists: A person must know what they are paying for and when it renews before they judge a limit or a charge. The brief says every signed-in surface shows the current plan read from the server and that users can see when it renews or ends (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/082-usage-dashboard-and-limit-ui.md, S82.01 and S82.02). The plan is never kept as a saved copy on the client.
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in account on Cloud mode. Free, paid individual and workspace-contract accounts all see it, in different forms.
problems_solved: A person cannot tell which plan limits apply to them.
A lapsed or unpaid subscription looks like a working one. The CLI prints a status line and the reason (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:639-671).
Different apps could show different plans if each kept its own copy. All of them read the same server answer.
use_cases: A subscriber opens Settings, Billing on web and reads 'Renews on' with the date (apps/web/features/settings/sections/BillingSection.tsx:822-826).
A mobile user opens Usage and sees '<plan> plan' above the period meter (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:1212).
A CLI user runs the usage command and reads 'Plan:' and 'Subscription:' lines (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:564-567).
A VS Code user opens the account menu and sees the plan label in the usage group (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:2236-2240).

where_to_find_it: Web and desktop (the public Desktop shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5): Settings, Usage shows the plan inside the allowance line under the heading 'Plan usage limits' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1245-1254, 1313-1315). The plan card with 'Free plan' or '<plan> plan', and the rows 'Renews on', 'Ends on', 'Trial ends on' or 'Current period ends', are on Settings, Billing (apps/web/features/settings/sections/BillingSection.tsx:67-72, 737-739, 822-826).

Mobile: Settings, Usage ('Usage' title) shows '<plan> plan' in a card header and 'Resets <date>' under the period meter (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:937-939, 1212). Settings, Cloud billing shows 'Renews', 'Trial ends' or 'Access ends' with a date (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-billing/index.tsx:367-370).
CLI: the usage command and the /usage slash command print 'Account usage', 'Plan: ...' and 'Subscription: ...' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1057, 7679-7685; apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:564-567).

VS Code extension: the account quick pick and the settings panel show the plan label (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:2236-2240; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/settings/SettingsPanel.ts:88-92).

working: The server builds plan_tier from the subscription row and effective_plan_tier from the entitlement bundle, plus seat type, period_start, period_end and subscription_status (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-summary-service.ts:68-90, 211-221).
GET /api/usage is authenticated, rate limited under the 'credits-balance' key and accepts API keys with the usage:read scope (apps/web/app/api/usage/route.ts:15-40).
Web reads the summary through one shared hook for all components on a page and re-reads it every 5 minutes while the user is active (apps/web/lib/hooks/useManagedUsageSummary.ts:22, 44-108).
Web Billing shows the plan card and the period row with trial, ends, renews or period wording (apps/web/features/settings/sections/BillingSection.tsx:67-72, 616-620, 822-826).

Mobile Usage shows the plan label from the summary (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:937, 1212) and Cloud billing shows the renewal date from the tier store, which reads /api/me?surface=mobile (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/store.ts:67-80; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-billing/index.tsx:126, 173-185).
CLI prints plan and subscription status, and explains payment-failed, paused and ended subscriptions (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:564-567, 639-671).

Chrome reads /api/usage together with its account call and keeps subscriptionTier and accountPlanTier from the summary (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/freeTrialClient.ts:116, 267-355).
incomplete: The web Usage page does not render the plan name as its own line or the period start and end dates. Dates are on Billing only (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1268-1315 has no period_start or period_end render).
The CLI response type has no period_start or period_end fields, so the CLI shows no period dates (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:66-93).

On mobile, the Usage screen shows the period reset date for the meter, and Billing shows the renewal date. The two are on separate screens (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:938-939; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-billing/index.tsx:367-370).
Chrome shows no persistent plan card or period date that was found. The brief marks Chrome 'done' but the product matrix marks it unverified (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:249).
disconnected_or_disabled: The Tauri desktop settings has its own UsageDashboard built from local stores (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/UsageDashboard.tsx:1-20). It is retained internal code, not the public Desktop (doc: AGENTS.md section 5). No read of /api/usage was found in that file.
not_available: Free plan on web and mobile: the Usage page shows only 'Upgrade for higher capacity' and an Upgrade button, no plan line or dates (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1313, 1319-1329; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:969-1021).
Workspace contract-priced plans on web: the Usage page says allowances are set by the contract and links to 'View workspace usage' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1330-1339).
Local and own-key modes have no AGI plan to show on CLI (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:343-357) or mobile Usage (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:1038).

established.statement: Every signed-in surface shows the account's current plan, read from the server.
Users can see the current billing period: when it renews or ends.
Settings must include usage settings with current session, weekly limits and current balance.
Plan, usage, invoices and limits must reconcile with authoritative records.
A failed read must not claim a full allowance; the last good reading stays and is marked stale.

acceptance_criteria: After a plan change on the server, a fresh read of Usage on web shows the new plan within one refresh, with no reinstall or re-login.
A paid account sees a renewal, end or trial date on web Billing and on mobile Cloud billing.
A failed read shows an error and a retry action. No bar shows a full allowance.
A lapsed paid period shows the 'has not renewed yet' message instead of a full meter.
A Free account on web and mobile sees only the upgrade prompt on Usage.
In Local or own-key mode the CLI refuses the read with a reason and sends no request.
inferred: All apps should show the same plan name for the same account, because all read the same fields [inferred from the shared service and shared type].
Chrome needs a visible plan or period element to match the other apps [inferred from the matrix marking Chrome unverified].
proposed: [proposed] Show plan name and period dates in one block at the top of the web and mobile Usage pages, so a reader does not have to switch to Billing.
[proposed] Add period_start and period_end to the CLI AccountUsage type and print 'Period: <start> to <end>'.
[proposed] Add a read-only plan line to the Chrome side panel account area.

steps.what_happens: Person opens Usage or Billing in an app.
The app sends GET /api/usage with the session cookie (web) or bearer token (CLI, mobile, VS Code, Chrome).
The server resolves the user, reads the credit balance, entitlement bundle, spendable credits and prepaid balances in parallel, and builds the summary.
The server returns plan_tier, effective_plan_tier, seat type, period_start, period_end and subscription_status.
The app parses the body with the shared parser (web, mobile, VS Code, Chrome) or a Rust struct (CLI) and renders labels.
Mobile Cloud billing separately reads /api/me?surface=mobile for the renewal date.

data.where_stored: Server database (subscription and credit balance rows, table names not opened). Client keeps it in memory only on web (module state) and in a zustand store on mobile.

data.retained_or_deleted: Invalidated when the server answers 401, 402 or 403 (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:480-490).

features.summary: Shows how full each usage window is and when it resets. The windows are a rolling session window, a rolling week, a weekly share for the most capable models, and the billing period. Web, mobile, CLI and VS Code show them. Chrome uses the same readings for warnings and a blocked state, not for meters.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns the server's usage percentages, credit windows and reset times into bars, text and warnings. The window labels are 'Current session', 'This week', 'Most capable models' and 'This billing period' (packages/contracts/types/src/usage-vocabulary.ts:34-62).
purpose.why_it_exists: A person on a metered plan needs to see how close they are to a limit and how long until it frees up, before work is blocked. The brief requires an overall usage meter and a reset countdown for each window (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/082-usage-dashboard-and-limit-ui.md, S82.03 and S82.17).
purpose.who_uses_it: Paid subscribers (not contract-priced workspace plans) using Cloud mode who ask how much they have left and when it resets.

established.statement: An overall usage meter shows how much of the plan allowance is used.
Each usage window shows how long until it resets.
Usage settings include current session and weekly limits.
The meter keeps its last value and is marked stale when a background read fails.
Meters never show dollars, tokens or internal ledger operands; values are in credits.

acceptance_criteria: Each shown window displays percent or credits used and a reset time.
The status sentence changes to 'Getting close' at 90 percent and 'Limit reached' at 100 percent.
A plan with no session cap shows no session bar.
A failed refresh leaves the last numbers on screen with '(refresh failed)' on web.
After 5 minutes of activity, web re-reads /api/usage without a click; a hidden tab does not poll.
On mobile the info button opens a sheet that lists the window descriptions and closes with Done.

steps.what_happens: Page mounts the shared hook, which starts one read and a 5 minute timer that only fires while the browser is active.
Server reads rolling session and weekly usage, applies uplifts, computes percentages and reset times from the oldest usage in each window.
For a Free plan the server uses the free-trial reading and its reset times.
Client parses, clamps percent to 0 to 100 and renders bars and text.
Client formats time to reset with the shared formatter.

data.what: Usage reading (percentages, credit windows, reset times)
data.where_stored: Computed from the server usage ledger rows (table managed_usage_requests is used by history; the rolling store was not opened). Client: module memory on web, zustand store on mobile.
data.retained_or_deleted: Client copy is dropped on close or account change.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The reading counts spend across models. The flagship window covers the most capable models only (packages/contracts/types/src/usage-vocabulary.ts:49-54). No provider is called to read it.

access_and_usage.account: Signed in. API key scope usage:read also works (apps/web/app/api/usage/route.ts:18).
access_and_usage.permissions: User-scoped database read of own data.
access_and_usage.subscription: Paid, non-contract plans see meters on web. Free sees upgrade only. Contract plans see a workspace link (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1319-1339).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Windows: 5-hour rolling session, 7-day rolling week, weekly flagship share, billing period (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-summary-service.ts:118-156). Caps come from the plan policy (managed-usage-policy.ts). Refresh interval 300000 ms (apps/web/lib/hooks/useManagedUsageSummary.ts:22).
access_and_usage.flags: limit_promotions presence; usage_allocation 'pending' or 'provisioned' (packages/contracts/types/src/managed-usage-balance.ts:90-106).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Flagship bucket concerns the most capable models. Which models count is decided in the model catalog and policy, not here (see SYS-model-catalog-and-routing).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: None found in the code for display.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Local mode is not metered. CLI refuses in Local and own-key modes (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:343-357). Mobile says 'Local mode keeps working' in the explainer (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:737-738).

purpose.what_it_does: Reads GET /api/usage/history and renders totals, periods, a product-area list, a model list and a project list in credits (apps/web/lib/services/account-usage-history-service.ts:197-250; apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1139-1153).
purpose.why_it_exists: The meters say how much is left. This says where it went, so a person can change habits or check a bill. The brief requires per-model, per-feature, coding and work, and per-project breakdowns (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/082-usage-dashboard-and-limit-ui.md, S82.04, S82.05, S82.10, S82.19).
purpose.who_uses_it: Paid subscribers who want to know which models, areas or projects used their credits.
problems_solved: No way to tell whether research, code or chat used the credits.
No way to link spend to a project.
Totals that include requests still in flight. The page counts only settled requests and says how many are still settling (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1154-1167).

A user reads 'By product area' to see how much Deep Research cost against chat.
A team member reads 'By project' to see which project used the most credits.
A CLI user reads 'By model' lines to compare models (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:805-822).

Empty: 'No settled usage in this period.' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1124-1126).

working: Server returns totals, periods, byWorkload, byModel, byProject and freshness from settled rows of managed_usage_requests for the user (apps/web/lib/services/account-usage-history-service.ts:104-250).
Granularity defaults to day, with 30 days, 12 weeks, 12 months of periods (apps/web/lib/services/account-usage-history-service.ts:31-59).
Window is clamped to the retained range (366 days max, 30 default) (apps/web/lib/services/usage-aggregation.ts:176-205).
Workload parameter accepts chat, work, research, code, browser and rejects others with a validation error (apps/web/app/api/usage/history/route.ts:23-27; apps/web/lib/billing/usage-attribution.ts:1).

Chat usage is tagged work, research or browser by mode; other chat is chat; code sessions are tagged code (apps/web/lib/billing/usage-attribution.ts:30-37; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-agent-service.ts:687).

Breakdowns are capped at 50 rows by the server (apps/web/lib/services/usage-aggregation.ts:49) and 8 rows on screen on web and mobile (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:60; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:198).

Web shows by product area, by model, by project (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1139-1153). Mobile shows product area and model (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:712-721).
CLI renders product area, model and day list; VS Code renders the same via summarizeUsageHistory (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:776-860; apps/extension-vscode/src/data/usagePresentation.ts:115-139).
incomplete: Mobile has no project breakdown (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:712-721).
CLI type has no by_project field, so projects are not shown (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:136-146).

VS Code parses byProject in its tests but summarizeUsageHistory does not render it (apps/extension-vscode/src/data/usagePresentation.ts:115-139; apps/extension-vscode/src/__tests__/usagePresentation.test.ts:29).
No UI control for the workload filter on any app. The web screen requests only granularity (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1079).
CLI and VS Code request the history with no granularity, so only the default day grouping is shown (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:9, 437-440; apps/extension-vscode/src/utils/api.ts:1555).
disconnected_or_disabled: The brief's code reference for research (request-processor.ts:4303) points at a context error branch, not at research attribution. The research tag comes from resolveChatWorkload (apps/web/lib/billing/usage-attribution.ts:30-37; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:6163).
not_available: Chrome has no usage history view (no history read found under apps/extension).
Free plan on web and mobile shows no history (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1451).

Users can see usage by feature or product area (chat, work, research, code, browser).
Users can see how much usage went to coding and agentic work.
Users can see usage broken down by project.
Users can review history by day, week and month.
An unknown workload name is refused before any read.
Totals count settled requests only and say how many are still settling.

A request with workload=research returns only research usage; workload=foo returns a validation error.
By project lists projects the user's workspace knows by name, and 'Project not in this workspace' otherwise.
An account with no settled usage sees 'No settled usage in this period.' and not an error.
A failed read shows 'Could not load your usage history.' and a retry that works.
Mobile shows product area and model lists and no project list.
Unsettled requests show a 'still settling' notice and are not in the totals.

proposed: [proposed] Add the project list to mobile, CLI and VS Code.
[proposed] Add a product-area filter control that calls the existing workload parameter.
[proposed] Let CLI and VS Code request week and month groupings.

steps.what_happens: Person opens the history card or switches grouping.
App sends GET /api/usage/history?granularity=<day|week|month>.
Server checks sign-in and the usage:read scope, validates workload, computes the window.
Server runs six aggregate queries in parallel on settled rows for the user.
Client parses with the shared parser, refuses a body that is not a history, and renders.

features.summary: Shows what each agent run or work task cost once it settles: credits, tokens and model calls, on web, desktop and mobile. The CLI and VS Code show billed credits per turn or session instead. Usage by device or surface is not built on any app or in the API.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores settled usage on each cloud agent run and shows it in the Tasks list and task detail (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TaskDetailPanel.tsx:336-385), and in the mobile run sheet (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/components/CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx:376-392).
purpose.why_it_exists: Long agent runs can use many credits. A person needs to see what one run cost. The brief requires usage per task and, where useful, by device or surface (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/082-usage-dashboard-and-limit-ui.md, S82.20 and S82.21).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who run Work, Research or code tasks in the cloud and want to judge each task's cost.
problems_solved: No link between a task and its credits.
A cost shown as zero while the task is still running. The panel says costs settle later (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TaskDetailPanel.tsx:378-380).
Charging language for a free-trial run. The panel says it was metered against the free trial allowance (same file:350-353).
use_cases: Web: open Tasks, pick a task, read 'Cost and usage'.
Mobile: open a cloud run and read 'Cost' and 'Usage' rows.
CLI: after a turn, read '<credits> billed' (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:428-441).
VS Code: open the account menu and read 'Billed this session' (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:2287).

where_to_find_it: Web and hosted Desktop: Tasks page list rows show cost after the model and time; the detail panel has the section 'Cost and usage' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TasksPage.tsx:752-758; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TaskDetailPanel.tsx:336-385, 728).
Mobile: cloud run detail sheet, rows 'Cost' and 'Usage' (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/components/CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx:376-392).
CLI: line after a turn and in the report (apps/cli/src/output.rs:834-838; apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:8696-8699).
VS Code: account quick pick rows 'Rough session estimate' and 'Billed this session' (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:2283-2288).
Chrome: not found.

CLI and VS Code: Cloud mode with a stored AGI credential (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:343-357).
screens_and_controls: Web Tasks list row cost text, with test id task-cost-<id>, shown only when a cost exists (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TasksPage.tsx:752-758).
Task detail section with credits, tokens in and out, reasoning tokens, model calls (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TaskDetailPanel.tsx:348-372).

working: recordCloudAgentRunSettledUsage writes one usage entry per billing key into cloud_agent_runs.settled_usage, with provider calls, tokens and cost in cents (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:605-614, 1137-1170).
mapSettledUsage sums the entries and returns a null cost when no entry was charged (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:616-640).

The writer is called from the managed agent stream and workflow settlement (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/managed-agent-stream.ts; apps/web/lib/workflows/steps/settle-workflow-invocation.ts).

Shared task UI shows cost in the list and detail (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TasksPage.tsx:752-758; TaskDetailPanel.tsx:336-385). The same package is used by web and desktop (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
Mobile shows Cost and Usage rows (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/components/CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx:376-392).
CLI polls /api/usage/turns/<id> up to four times and prints billed credits or 'not settled yet' (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:376-441).
VS Code settles queued billing and shows billed credits for the session (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:2205-2210, 2287).
incomplete: The mobile row shows tokens as a plain sum with no credits-per-call breakdown (apps/mobile/src/features/tasks/components/CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx:391).
CLI and VS Code show per-turn or per-session cost, not per task (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:401-441; apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:2287).
The brief cites TasksPage.tsx:591 and CloudRunDetailSheet.tsx:179-185 for cost. Those lines are other code. The cost lines are the ones listed above.

not_available: Usage by device or surface: no grouping by device or surface exists in the history service (apps/web/lib/services/account-usage-history-service.ts:104-250) or the history type. The brief records it missing on web, desktop, mobile and API (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/082-usage-dashboard-and-limit-ui.md, S82.21).
Chrome shows no per-task cost (no file found).

established.statement: Users can see usage per task (agent run or work session).
Where useful, users can see usage broken down by device or surface. Status is missing everywhere.
After a task finishes, the user sees what it actually cost.
A live run shows pending cost, not a false zero. A free-trial run shows no invented charge.

acceptance_criteria: A settled run shows credits in the Tasks list and the detail panel.
A running task says cost is recorded when it settles, or shows the settled-so-far figure with the growing-total note.
A free-trial run shows the free trial message and no price.
Mobile run sheet shows Cost and Usage rows for a run with usage and none for a run without.
CLI prints '<n> credits billed' after a settled turn and a 'not settled yet' note otherwise.
No app presents a per-device or per-surface table.
inferred: Cost in cents on the run is rounded from the ledger, so it may differ slightly from the history total [inferred from costCents integer in apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:605-612].
proposed: [proposed] Record the surface (web, desktop, mobile, CLI, IDE, extension) in the usage attribution json and add a 'By app' breakdown to the history API.
[proposed] Add a per-task total to CLI and VS Code run lists.

steps.what_happens: A managed agent run makes billed provider calls.
When a step settles, the server writes a usage entry (calls, tokens, cost in cents, time) into settled_usage under the billing key.
The app loads the run list or one run; the server maps settled_usage to run.usage.
The Tasks page or mobile sheet renders cost and tokens.
CLI asks the server for each turn's settlement and prints the result.

access_and_usage.subscription: Any plan with cloud runs. Free-trial runs store a null cost and show the free-trial message (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/tasks/TaskDetailPanel.tsx:350-353).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Settled amounts feed the same ledger as the meters. This feature only displays them.

access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: none found in the code.

features.summary: Shows usage of the non-text allowances: voice minutes, images, video seconds and computer-use requests under 'This month', plus how many responses run now, and file storage. Web and mobile show the monthly card and running count. Only mobile shows a storage card. Research appears in the history. CLI, VS Code and Chrome show none of this.

purpose.what_it_does: GET /api/usage/limits returns the plan, period reset, metered units, monthly image usage, running response count and file storage in one reply (apps/web/app/api/usage/limits/route.ts:85-101). Web and mobile render parts of it.
purpose.why_it_exists: Voice, image and video draw on separate allowances and storage has its own cap. A person needs to see them to avoid a refusal. The brief requires voice, image, video, research, storage and active job count (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/082-usage-dashboard-and-limit-ui.md, S82.06 to S82.09, S82.11, S82.12).
purpose.who_uses_it: Paid subscribers who use voice, image or video generation, upload files, or run several responses at once.
problems_solved: Refusals that came with no warning.
Not knowing why a new response is queued: 'Responses running now' shows the concurrency ceiling.
Upload failures when storage is full.
use_cases: A user reads 'Voice 12 of 60 minutes' under 'This month' (format at apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:763-784).
A user reads 'Responses running now 2 of 3 at a time' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:815-825).
A mobile user reads 'File storage' with a meter (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:577-603).
A user reads 'About N minutes of voice left at today's price' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:786-812).

where_to_find_it: Web and hosted Desktop: Settings, Usage. The card 'This month' (units and images) and the rows 'Voice' estimate and 'Responses running now' inside 'Plan usage limits' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:839-844, 1405-1409). There is no storage card on the web Usage page; project storage is on the knowledge files panel (apps/web/features/projects/components/KnowledgeFilesPanel.tsx).
Mobile: Settings, Usage. Cards 'This month', 'File storage' and the row 'Responses running now' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:522-603).
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: none.
prerequisites: Paid non-contract plan, Cloud mode. Web requests the limits only for those accounts (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1227-1231). Mobile requests them for a non-Free signed-in Cloud account (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:910-917).
screens_and_controls: Rows with labels 'Voice', 'Video', 'Computer use', 'Images' and a bar when a monthly cap exists, else '<n> <unit>, no monthly cap' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:763-784, 855-863).
Retry link when this month's read fails (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:848).
journey: Open Usage as a paid user.
The page requests /api/usage/limits in addition to the summary.
Read 'This month' with its reset date.
Read the running-response row and the voice estimate in the plan card.
On mobile, scroll to 'File storage' and read used and limit.
feedback_and_outputs: 'Resets <date and time>' under 'This month'.
'<used> of <limit> <unit> used' with a progress bar.
Image row: '<n> images · <credits>'.
Storage: '<used> of <limit>' with a meter, or used only when no limit.
settings: None.

working: The limits route returns planTier, periodStart, resetAt, units, images, responses, storage and voiceMinuteCredits and sets Cache-Control no-store (apps/web/app/api/usage/limits/route.ts:85-102).

Units are voice minutes, video seconds and computer-use requests with consumed, soft and hard limit per plan (apps/web/lib/services/tier-unit-quota-service.ts:274-291; packages/contracts/types/src/account-usage-client.ts:11-17).
On a plan with a free voice allowance, consumed voice minutes come from that allowance (apps/web/app/api/usage/limits/route.ts:79-96).
Images are counted for the current calendar month from settled image requests (apps/web/lib/services/account-usage-history-service.ts:299-327).
The running count reads the live turn slots and returns null when it cannot (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:1445-1461; apps/web/app/api/usage/limits/route.ts:44-54).
Storage is the file storage meter for the user or organization; each half is null if its read failed (apps/web/lib/server/file-storage.ts:77-91).

Web shows units, images, running responses and a voice estimate (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:786-869, 1405-1409). Mobile shows units, images, running responses and a storage card (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:522-603).
The web card hides rows with no limit and no use, and hides the whole card when empty (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:831-836).
Research usage is a workload row in the history (apps/web/lib/billing/usage-attribution.ts:34-35; apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1139-1143).
incomplete: The web Usage page has no storage display, although the API returns it (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx has no storage render).
Mobile 'This month' shows no voice estimate row (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:522-575).
Research has no allowance meter, only a share in the history (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1139-1143).

The Free voice allowance is computed by the API but web and mobile do not request limits for Free accounts (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1228; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:910-911).
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile Usage-credits card and store-sold items depend on the build flag nativePurchases, currently false (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePurchases.json:2). This does not hide the allowance cards.
not_available: CLI, VS Code and Chrome: no allowances, storage or running count (no reads of /api/usage/limits found in those apps).
Running count is null when no key-value store is configured or the plan has no limit (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:1449-1452).

established.statement: Users can see voice usage, image usage and video usage against any allowance.
Users can see how much usage went to research.
Users can see storage used against the plan storage limit.
Users can see how many jobs or responses are running now, ideally against the plan's concurrent limit.
An unreadable running count is reported as unknown, not zero.
A Free account's voice minutes come from its monthly allowance, not the paid ledger.

acceptance_criteria: As a paid user, 'This month' shows each unit with a limit and its reset date.
A unit with no cap reads 'no monthly cap'.
When the running-count read fails, the API returns responses null and the UI shows no running row.
Mobile shows a 'File storage' card with used and limit when the server returns bytes.
If the storage read fails, the storage card is hidden.
The API refuses a caller who is not signed in.
Images appear only after at least one image request this month.
inferred: The web Usage page should show storage, because the brief marks web 'done' for S82.11 [inferred from the brief; current code shows none].
proposed: [proposed] Add a 'File storage' card on web using the same limits reply.
[proposed] Add the voice estimate row to mobile.
[proposed] Show research as a named allowance if the plan ever gives one.

steps.what_happens: Usage page opens for a paid account and requests /api/usage/limits.
Server resolves the entitled plan, then reads units, images, running turns and storage in parallel.
If the plan has a free voice allowance, the server replaces voice consumed with the allowance reading.
The server sends the reply with no-store caching.
The client parses with the shared parser and renders cards, hiding empty ones.

features.summary: Shows credits left and keeps three kinds apart: the plan's included credits, purchased credits and bonus credits from referrals or promotions, each with its expiry rule. Web shows bonus and purchased on a 'Credit balances' card. Mobile shows included credits, and bonus and purchased only when store purchases are on, which they are not now.

purpose.what_it_does: The summary reply carries credit windows for the plan, a purchased balance that is null when unknown, bonus credits with their next expiry, and purchase expiry information (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-summary-service.ts:163-209). Apps render them in their own layouts.
purpose.why_it_exists: Credits are spent in a set order and expire by different rules. A person needs to know what they hold and when it lapses. The brief requires remaining credits, purchased versus included, promotional credits and expiry (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/082-usage-dashboard-and-limit-ui.md, S82.13 to S82.16).
purpose.who_uses_it: Subscribers who buy extra credits, get referral or promotional credits, or ask how much they can still spend.
problems_solved: Mistaking an unknown balance for zero. The server returns null when the read fails (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-summary-service.ts:56-66, 195).
Not knowing which credits are used first. The card says bonus credits go first, soonest expiring, then bought credits (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:425-427).
Surprise credit loss. Each bonus grant shows its next expiry date.
use_cases: A user with a referral reward reads 'Bonus credits 40' and 'Next expiry <date>' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:380-385).
A buyer reads 'Purchased credits' and that some expire where local law requires (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:398-404).
A CLI user reads 'Purchased credits: 25, overage on' (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:695-706).
A VS Code user reads 'Credits' with a note on whether they can be spent (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:2323-2329).

where_to_find_it: Web and hosted Desktop: Settings, Usage, card 'Credit balances' with rows 'Bonus credits' and 'Purchased credits' and a 'Buy credits' link to Billing (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:407-435). Included plan credits show in the plan bars and the allowance line (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1245-1254, 1393-1404).

Mobile: Settings, Usage, card 'Credit balances' with 'Included in your plan'. 'Bonus credits' and 'Purchased credits' appear only when store purchases are available (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:411-434).
CLI: usage command line 'Purchased credits: <n>, overage on|off', and 'Add credits: <link>' (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:695-706, 584-587).
VS Code: row 'Credits' with a spendability note and 'Add credits' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/settings/SettingsPanel.ts:99-108; apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:2323-2329).
Chrome: no balance display found. The panel uses the purchased balance to decide whether work can continue and shows 'using purchased credits' (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:13222-13264).
prerequisites: Paid non-contract plan on web (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1445).
Mobile: Cloud mode, signed in, not Free.
