Grant sources are referral_referrer, referral_friend and promo (apps/web/lib/services/bonus-credit-service.ts:11).

getPrepaidCreditBalances reads two database functions for balances and lots and returns bonus, purchased, expiring purchased and next expiry dates (apps/web/lib/services/bonus-credit-service.ts:164-212).
A failed prepaid read is logged and reported as null for purchased and bonus (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-summary-service.ts:56-66, 195-207).

A daily cron expires due bonus lots, at most 500 accounts per run (apps/web/app/api/cron/expire-bonus-credits/route.ts; vercel.json:34-35; apps/web/app/api/cron/expire-bonus-credits/route.test.ts:55).
The summary also returns credit_balance_cents (spendable) and overage_enabled (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-summary-service.ts:235-236).
Web renders the Credit balances card with unknown, none and amount states (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:370-435).
Web helper spendableCreditsNow sums plan remaining, bonus and purchased (apps/web/lib/hooks/useManagedUsageSummary.ts:163-172).
CLI prints a purchased line with 'unknown' when null (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:695-706).
VS Code shows the spendable balance and whether it will be spent (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/settings/SettingsPanel.ts:99-108).
Chrome derives balance, overage and spendable from purchased credits (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/usageWindows.ts:116-125).
incomplete: Mobile hides bonus and purchased rows when nativePurchases is false, which is the current setting (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:419-421; apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePurchases.json:2).
The CLI struct has no bonus or purchase-expiry fields, so it shows no bonus credits or expiry (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:41-48).
VS Code shows one 'Credits' figure (credit_balance_cents), not the included, purchased and bonus split (apps/extension-vscode/src/utils/api.ts:1393-1394).
Chrome computes a purchased balance string but no code that shows it was found (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/usageWindows.ts:116-125; no use of .balance in side_panel.ts).
The brief marks promotional credits and expiry done on desktop and mobile; mobile currently hides them (see above).
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile bonus and purchased rows are compiled in but switched off by nativePurchases false (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:419-421).
not_available: CLI, VS Code and Chrome: no bonus credits or expiry display.
Free plan on web and mobile: no credit balances (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1445).

established.statement: Users can see how many credits remain (plan windows and purchased balance).
Users can tell purchased credits apart from the plan's included allowance.
Users can see promotional or bonus credits, how much remains and when they lapse.
Users can see when each kind of credit expires: plan reset, purchased lifetime, bonus lapse.
Settings must show current balance and usage credits.
An unreadable balance is shown as unknown, not zero.
Past a plan limit, bonus credits are spent first (soonest to expire), then bought credits.
Credits show in credits, never in currency.

acceptance_criteria: Web 'Credit balances' shows Bonus credits and Purchased credits as separate rows.
A grant of bonus credits shows its next expiry date, 90 days after the grant.
When the prepaid read fails, both rows read 'Unavailable', not 'None' or zero.
Purchased credits that expire show the amount and next date; others say they do not expire.
After the daily cron, expired bonus credits disappear from the card.
Mobile with store purchases off shows only 'Included in your plan'.
CLI shows 'unknown' for a purchased balance it cannot read.
inferred: Included credits reset with the plan period, so their expiry is the reset time on the monthly bar [inferred from creditWindow(..., usageResetAt) at managed-usage-summary-service.ts:165-171].
proposed: [proposed] Show bonus credits and expiry in CLI, VS Code and Chrome.
[proposed] Let mobile show bonus credits and their expiry even when it sells nothing, since they are read-only account facts.
[proposed] Add one line on the web card stating the plan credits and reset date next to bonus and purchased.

steps.what_happens: Usage page reads GET /api/usage.
Server reads the prepaid balances and lots through two database functions. On failure it logs and treats balances as unknown.
Server returns purchased.remaining (null when unknown), bonus.remaining and next_expiry_at, and purchase_expiry.
Client renders the rows, with 'Unavailable', 'None' or an amount.
Each day the cron expires bonus lots past their date.

data.where_stored: Server database lots read by prepaid_credit_lots_microusd; exact table names not opened.
data.synced: Server is the source. Apps read it.
data.retained_or_deleted: Bonus lots expire 90 days after grant and the daily sweep takes back lapsed amounts (apps/web/lib/services/bonus-credit-service.ts:7, 125-160). Purchased credits may expire where local law requires (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:402).

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model or provider reads this. Credits are an account balance. Spend is priced per model by the rate card elsewhere (see SYS-model-catalog-and-routing).

access_and_usage.account: Signed in. Credits belong to the user account (apps/web/lib/services/bonus-credit-service.ts:164-165).
access_and_usage.permissions: User-scoped read. Granting bonus credits is a server and admin action, not part of this page (apps/web/app/api/admin/usage-promotions/__tests__/route.test.ts exists; contents not opened).
access_and_usage.subscription: Paid non-contract plans on web. A purchase needs a plan that can buy credits; the CLI and others point to web billing. Billing sales are limited by the owner's decisions (see unknowns).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Bonus expiry 90 days. Cron processes at most 500 accounts per run (apps/web/app/api/cron/expire-bonus-credits/route.test.ts:55). Purchased expiry follows the account's region rules.
access_and_usage.flags: Mobile nativePurchases false (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePurchases.json:2). Summary field self_serve says whether the holder buys credits themselves (packages/contracts/types/src/managed-usage-balance.ts:53-55).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: none found in the code.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Purchases go through the billing provider or app stores; purchase detail is outside this feature (see SYS-subscriptions-entitlements-and-usage).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Local mode uses no credits. CLI refuses the read in Local and own-key modes (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:343-357). The support article says Local mode and own key do not draw on a managed allowance (doc: apps/web/content/support/usage-and-credits.md).

features.summary: A paid Cloud account can see its settled usage grouped by UTC day, week or month, download the same window as a CSV file, and file a billing-problem report that opens a support ticket with a usage record attached. Web and the hosted desktop app have all three. Mobile has history only. The CLI prints a default history.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows settled managed (Cloud) usage by period, product area, model and project. Exports one row per settled request as CSV. Lets the user file a billing or usage discrepancy as a support ticket that carries a server-built usage record.
purpose.why_it_exists: Users need to check what they were charged credits for and to dispute a charge. The brief asks for day, week and month history (S82.18), a downloadable report (S82.32) and a tracked discrepancy report (S82.33). A product decision keeps the discrepancy form off mobile and sends web-billed users to the web (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md, D-2026-09-28-27).
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in person on a paid, self-serve Cloud plan. The section is hidden for Free and contract-priced plans (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1451).
problems_solved: Cannot see where credits went
Cannot reconcile a charge with requests
No tracked path to report a wrong charge
use_cases: A user opens Settings > Usage, switches to Weeks, and sees spend per week and per model.
A finance-minded user downloads the CSV to check a request ID.
A user sees a credit total that looks wrong, picks one day, quotes an invoice reference and files a report.
A mobile user checks last month's usage by model on the phone.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings > Usage, card titled 'Where your usage went' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1101). Mounted by apps/web/features/settings/components/WebSettingsModal.tsx:291.

Desktop (public Electron app): the same hosted web page, because the Electron window shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5). The Tauri build's own usage section (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/DesktopCloudSettingsModal.tsx:447) has no history, export or report code (grep for history/export/discrepan in that file found none).
Mobile: Settings, cloud usage screen, card 'Where your usage went' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:638).
CLI: the account usage output lists 'Usage history' lines (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:776).
prerequisites: Signed in with a Cloud account on a paid plan that is not contract-priced (UsageSection.tsx:1451).
Mobile: Cloud mode active, signed in, not Free (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:909-911).
Discrepancy report: a confirmed reply email on the account (apps/web/app/api/usage/discrepancy/route.ts:13, 158).
screens_and_controls: Segmented control 'Group usage history by' with Days, Weeks, Months (UsageSection.tsx:120-124, 1110).
Totals line, then lists: By day/week/month, By product area, By model, By project (UsageSection.tsx:1131-1150).
Notice '{n} request(s) still settling and not counted above' (UsageSection.tsx:1152-1166).
'Download CSV' link and 'Report a billing problem' button (UsageSection.tsx:1176-1189).
Report form fields: Period, 'Request ID (optional)', 'Invoice or charge reference (optional)', 'What looks wrong', buttons 'File report' and 'Cancel' (UsageSection.tsx:902+).
Mobile: Days, Weeks, Months buttons; lists capped at 8 rows (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:180-198). No project list, no download, no report.
journey: Open Settings > Usage on web or desktop (or the cloud usage screen on mobile).
Scroll to 'Where your usage went'. History for Days loads first.
Pick Days, Weeks or Months. The list reloads for the new grouping and any open report form closes (UsageSection.tsx:1112-1115).
Optional: click 'Download CSV' to save the current grouping's window.

steps.what_happens: Person opens Settings > Usage; the page fetches GET /api/usage/history?granularity=<day|week|month> with the session.
Server resolves the window start (30 days / 12 weeks / 12 months), runs six parallel SQL reads over the user's settled managed_usage_requests, returns totals and breakdowns.
Download CSV: the browser requests GET /api/usage/export?granularity=...; the server reads up to 10,000 settled rows and streams a text/csv attachment.
File report: the browser POSTs /api/usage/discrepancy with CSRF header; server checks rate limit, validates, loads history, balances and the disputed request, then opens a ticket and notifies staff.
Mobile fetches the same history endpoint through its API client.

features.summary: Before and during a research run, web shows an approximate maximum credit cost worked out in the browser. After a turn or task is billed, web, mobile, CLI and VS Code show the real credits. A server estimate endpoint exists but nothing in the apps calls it.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a rough upfront credit cost for a research run and a real, settled cost afterwards for a chat turn or an agent task.
purpose.why_it_exists: Credits are consumed by usage; people want to know a run's size before it starts and what it cost afterwards. Briefs S82.22 and S82.23 ask for both.
purpose.who_uses_it: Cloud users on web or hosted desktop (estimate and actual), mobile (task cost), CLI and VS Code (billed credits).
problems_solved: Surprise cost on a long research run
Not knowing what a turn or task cost
Confusing partial amounts before settlement
use_cases: A user edits a research plan and reads 'Estimated cost: up to about N credits'.
A user hovers a message and sees tokens plus credits.
A user opens a finished task and sees Cost and usage.
A CLI user sees '<credits> billed' after a turn.

established.statement: Users can buy extra usage when they run out, from where they hit the limit.
Users can turn on automatic credit reload and configure it.
Buying is allowed only on an active paid plan with a payment source.
Auto-reload runs only when the payment processor is enabled; the consent text is versioned and must be accepted before saving.
A failed reload is recorded with a reason.
Plan-limit refusals offer top-up only when the plan is self-serve and billed by a payment source and credits clear the block.
The product sells no subscriptions on any surface before 2027-01-01.

acceptance_criteria: On an active Stripe-billed paid plan, Buy opens hosted checkout for the chosen whole-dollar amount.
On Free or a lapsed plan, the route answers 'Top-ups are available on active paid plans...'.
A purchase that would pass the daily cap is refused with the daily limit message.
Saving auto-reload with no card shows 'Add a card...' and does not save enabled.
Saving requires the consent dialog and sends the current consent version; an old version returns 'consent_outdated'.
A declined reload sets Auto-reload off, shows the reason, and creates a notification.
Turning auto-reload off saves without a dialog.
Auto-reload does nothing above the threshold, on a billing hold or above the daily purchase cap.

proposed: [proposed] Consider a bounded automatic retry for soft declines instead of switching off.
[proposed] Show auto-reload on Apple and Google billed plans only if the owner decides to support off-session charges there.

steps.what_happens: User picks an amount; the browser POSTs /api/billing/top-up with CSRF token and an Idempotency-Key.
Server checks plan, policy, daily cap, creates a hosted checkout session at the payment processor and returns its URL.
The browser is handed to the processor's checkout page, which collects payment, terms and tax.
A webhook credits the account (credit top-up handler).

Auto-reload: after a settled request or each sweep the server checks balance versus threshold, billing hold, daily cap, takes a lease, charges the saved card off-session and settles on the payment event.
On failure the server disables auto-reload, records the reason, notifies and emails.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Not model dependent. Credits are spent when a managed request is billed at the catalog price; top-up only changes the balance. Payment is made to the payment processor, not to a model provider.

features.summary: A workspace owner or admin can set a monthly credit limit with a mode of Off, Notify or Block. Only Block refuses members' Cloud turns once the month's spend reaches the limit. Decisions are cached for 60 seconds. A separate policy cap and a personal spend limit also exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Caps managed spend for a workspace per calendar month and optionally alerts at a percentage threshold.
purpose.why_it_exists: Finance owners need a budget ceiling (S82.31). Notify lets them watch before enforcing.
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners and admins who hold the policy.manage permission; members feel the refusals.
problems_solved: Uncontrolled team spend
No early warning before a budget is hit
use_cases: Owner sets a cap, 80 percent alert and Notify to observe first.
Owner switches to Block; members' new Cloud turns stop at the cap.
Owner raises the cap and members are freed at once.
Owner removes the limit.

Enforcement: evaluateSpendLimit allows unless configured, mode block and spend >= cap; decision cached 60 seconds; unreadable state is treated as allowed (apps/web/lib/services/spend-limit-service.ts:53-60, 161-206). A raised cap or delete clears the cache for this server process (lines 212-214, 245-275).

Gate applied before managed work in chat completions, embeddings, audio transcription, voice live sessions, image and video generation and resume routes (callers of buildSpendLimitGateResponse in apps/web/app/api/...); the gate answers 402 with type insufficient_quota (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:511-545).
Crossing announcements via dispatchSpendAlertIfDue (spend-limit-service.ts:205-210).
Separate policy cap in the managed request path: refusal writes audit event spend_cap_exceeded and throws organization_spend_cap_reached (managed-usage-request-service.ts:338-399, 779).
Web UI with confirm dialog for removal.
incomplete: The confirmation dialog covers only removing the limit. Saving a change to Block shows an inline warning note, not a dialog (WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:278-322). The brief says the change is confirmed by the dialog.

Only the policy-cap path writes an audit event per refused request. The Block path writes a warning log line only (managed-compute-gate.ts:527-530). The brief's line 'each refused request writes an audit event' is true only for the policy cap.
The 60-second cache is per server process (Map in memory, spend-limit-service.ts:67); across several instances enforcement lag can differ. This is read from the code, not tested [inferred].
not_available: Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no controls (brief n/a). They show the refusal text only. Mobile treats organization_spend_cap_reached as no model switch (apps/mobile/services/apiErrors.ts:109); how other apps treat code over_cap was not established.

established.statement: An owner can set a spending cap that stops managed usage once reached.
Modes are off, notify and block; only block refuses.
Decisions are cached 60 seconds, so enforcement is eventual and may overshoot by about one window of spend.
If spend cannot be read, the request is allowed.
Product requirement: Usage settings must include a monthly spend limit.
An action a user cannot undo asks first, naming the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: With mode Block and spend at or above the cap, a member's next Cloud turn is refused with status 402 and the monthly spend limit message.
With mode Notify or Off, turns continue even above the cap.
Raising the cap frees members immediately on that server.
A member cannot see the set or remove controls.
Removing the limit shows a confirmation naming the consequence and then removes it.
Changing to Block records a critical audit event.
If the spend lookup fails, the turn is allowed and an error is logged.
inferred: Overshoot of about a minute of spend is acceptable and is stated to the admin in the UI copy [inferred from WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:79].
proposed: [proposed] Put switching to Block behind the confirmation dialog, since it starts refusing work.
[proposed] Merge the two cap mechanisms (limit table and policy cap) or document which wins.
[proposed] Write an audit event on each Block refusal.

features.summary: When a Cloud usage window is spent, web and mobile offer 'Notify me when it resets'. The server schedules one push notification at the reset time, only if the user's usage-reset notification preference is not off. It is a reminder, not an automatic resume. The brief marks it missing, but the code exists on web and mobile.

purpose.what_it_does: Schedules a push notification for the moment a spent usage window resets, so the user knows they can send messages again.
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S82.28 asks for automatic resume or notification after reset.
purpose.who_uses_it: Cloud users blocked by a plan window, on web (browser push) or mobile (device push).
problems_solved: User must keep checking when they can work again
use_cases: Web user hits the 5-hour limit and clicks 'Notify me when it resets'.
Mobile user sees the warning banner with the action and taps it.
User turns the alert off in Notifications and gets nothing.

Mobile: inside the usage warning banner (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/UsageLimitBanner.tsx:66, 200-230).

Preference: web Settings > Notifications > Usage (apps/web/features/settings/sections/NotificationsSection.tsx:74-77); mobile Settings > Notifications switch (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/notifications/index.tsx:548-556).
prerequisites: Cloud account; a spent window with a known reset time within 8 days (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/usage-reset-reminder.ts:6; UsageLimitBanner.tsx:77-91).
Notification permission granted on the browser or device (asked when needed).

Mobile text button 'Notify me when it resets' (44 point target), then 'We'll notify you' (UsageLimitBanner.tsx:66-67, 200-230).

Outcome texts on web: 'We will notify you when it resets.', 'Notifications are blocked for this site in your browser settings.', 'This browser cannot receive notifications.', 'The reminder could not be set. Try again in a minute.' (apps/web/features/chat/lib/usage-reset-reminder.ts:10-15).

The app asks the server to schedule a reminder for the reset time.

At the reset time a push arrives: 'Your AGI usage limit has reset. You can send messages again.' Tapping opens /chat.

Mobile client: checks or requests push permission, POSTs, then turns the account push group on for the device (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/services/usageResetReminder.ts:19-32).

Server route /api/usage/reset-reminder: CSRF, rate limit key usage-reset-reminder (10 per hour), refuses when the preference is off, validates the time (future and within 8 days), de-duplicates per user and reset time, starts a durable workflow that sleeps to the reset and then pushes if the preference still allows (apps/web/app/api/usage/reset-reminder/route.ts:60-107; apps/web/lib/workflows/usage-reset-reminder-workflow.ts:10-17; send-usage-reset-reminder.ts:16-33; apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:292-296).

The mobile action appears only when some window is fully used (resetAt requires percentRemaining <= 0, UsageLimitBanner.tsx:77-91), not at the 25 percent warning.
The web action appears only after a refusal that carries a reset time (WebChatPage.tsx:1807-1817).
disconnected_or_disabled: Hidden inside the desktop host (isDesktopHost, WebChatPage.tsx:1816).
not_available: CLI, VS Code and Chrome: no reminder (brief n/a).
Automatic resume on all apps.

established.statement: Users can choose to have blocked work resume automatically, or be notified, once the limit resets.
The server route is rate limited under usage-reset-reminder and the workflow sends only if the user's preference allows.
The reminder is a notification, not an automatic resume.

acceptance_criteria: After a refusal with a reset time, web shows 'Notify me when it resets' (not in the desktop host).
Clicking asks for push permission if needed and then shows 'We will notify you when it resets.'
If the browser blocks notifications the text says so and no request is sent.
Asking twice for the same reset sends only one push.
A reset more than 8 days away or already past is refused.
With the Usage push preference off, the request is refused and no push is sent even if scheduled earlier.
On mobile, a fully spent window shows the action; tapping with notifications denied shows the blocked text.
inferred: Brief status 'missing' for web and mobile is out of date because the code is present and tested [inferred from the files above].
proposed: [proposed] Add an 'auto-resume' option that re-sends the blocked message after the reset, if the owner wants it.
[proposed] Offer the action on the desktop host if Electron can receive push.

The app POSTs the reset time to /api/usage/reset-reminder.
Server checks CSRF, rate limit, preference and time window, claims a de-duplication key, and starts the workflow.
The workflow sleeps until the reset time.
At reset, the step re-checks the preference and sends a push to the user's registered browsers and devices.
The push provider delivers to the device.

features.summary: When a renewal payment fails, AGI Workforce tells the person on every app that the plan is past due or unpaid and where to fix it. Web and Desktop (the hosted web app) offer 'Pay <amount> now' and 'Update payment method'. CLI, VS Code and Chrome point to web billing. Mobile shows a status sentence only.

purpose.what_it_does: Detects a subscription in the past_due or unpaid state and shows a clear message that paid features are paused, with the way to pay the open invoice or change the card. Also explains on a public page why a payment fails. Pricing and the upgrade page block new upgrades while payment is overdue and send the person to Billing. (apps/web/features/billing/components/BillingPlanNotices.tsx:115; apps/web/app/payment-failure/page.tsx:33; apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:502)
purpose.why_it_exists: A failed renewal otherwise looks like a silent loss of paid features. The brief (S83.14, S83.15) requires the person to be told clearly and to be able to retry from the product. Product policy ranks past_due and unpaid below active, so paid access stops until payment succeeds. (doc: docs/product/commercial.md:175-181)
purpose.who_uses_it: Paying subscribers whose card was declined at renewal, on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome. Support staff also point people to /payment-failure.
problems_solved: A person does not know why paid features stopped.
A person cannot find the open invoice to pay.
A person tries to upgrade while an unpaid invoice exists and gets confusing errors.
A person worries a failed new checkout charged them.
use_cases: A card expires; the renewal fails; the person opens Settings, Billing on the web and clicks 'Pay <amount> now'.
A CLI user runs the account usage summary and reads that the account is on Free until the payment is settled, with the billing link.
A Chrome side panel user sees the composer gate 'Update billing to restore Managed Cloud chat.' and clicks 'Manage billing'.
A person whose 3D Secure check closed during a new checkout reads /payment-failure and learns no subscription was created and no charge was made.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (Desktop shows the hosted web app): Settings, Billing: a red alert at the top of the plan block (apps/web/features/settings/sections/BillingSection.tsx:832; apps/web/features/billing/components/BillingPlanNotices.tsx:115).
Web and Desktop: public page /payment-failure titled 'Payment didn't go through.' with buttons 'Open billing' and 'See plans' (apps/web/app/payment-failure/page.tsx:33-46).

Web and Desktop: /pricing shows the alert 'Your last payment didn't go through...' and the plan buttons read 'Update payment' (apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:502-506,982-990); /upgrade shows 'Open billing' (apps/web/app/upgrade/UpgradeChooser.tsx:169-173).
Mobile: Settings, plan screen; the plan summary sentence 'Your <plan> subscription is past due. Paid capabilities are unavailable.' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-billing/index.tsx:167).
CLI: the account usage summary (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:639-662).
VS Code: account menu item 'Manage billing & subscription' with the description 'Restore paid Cloud access on Web' (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:2414-2417).
Chrome: side panel composer gate message with the button 'Manage billing' (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:13427-13438; apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:117,185).
prerequisites: Signed in with an account that has a paid plan whose status is past_due or unpaid.

For the Pay and Update buttons on Web and Desktop: the plan is billed through the web payment provider (subscription_source stripe) (apps/web/features/billing/components/BillingPlanNotices.tsx:117-118).
The notice is not shown for contract-priced Enterprise plans (apps/web/features/billing/components/BillingPlanNotices.tsx:115).
screens_and_controls: Web and Desktop red notice: first line 'Your last <plan> payment didn't go through, so the plan is past due' (or 'unpaid'); second paragraph 'Self-serve plans have no grace period: paid features stop at the first failed renewal and come back as soon as the payment succeeds. Your chats and files stay.' with the link 'why a payment fails and what to do' to /payment-failure (apps/web/features/billing/components/BillingPlanNotices.tsx:147-162).

Link 'Pay <amount> now': opens the hosted invoice in a new tab; only when an open invoice with a hosted link is in the loaded invoice list (BillingPlanNotices.tsx:121-133; BillingSection.tsx:606-613).
Button 'Update payment method': opens the billing portal (BillingPlanNotices.tsx:134-143; BillingSection.tsx:327-337).
Settings also keeps 'Manage billing' available when the Stripe plan is past due (test: apps/web/features/settings/sections/__tests__/BillingSection.test.tsx:573).

CLI: lines 'Subscription: past due', 'Your last payment did not go through, so this subscription is past due. Until it is settled this account is on Free, and plan features and purchased credits are paused.' and 'Update your payment method in Settings > Billing: <link>' (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:647,654-662).
Chrome: the button text 'Manage billing' (apps/extension/_locales/en/messages.json:117).
journey: 1. A renewal payment fails; the server stores the status past_due (the Settings test comment says invoice.payment_failed does this) (apps/web/features/settings/sections/__tests__/BillingSection.test.tsx:797; doc: docs/product/commercial.md:175-179).
2. The person opens an app. Each app reads the plan and status from the account (web: billing store; mobile: GET /api/me?surface=mobile) (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/store.ts:79).
3. The app shows its own notice (see where_to_find_it).
4. On Web or Desktop the person clicks 'Pay <amount> now' to pay the hosted invoice, or 'Update payment method' to open the portal and change the card.

5. When payment succeeds the status returns to active and paid features come back; the notice goes away on the next account read [inferred from the notice text 'come back as soon as the payment succeeds'] (BillingPlanNotices.tsx:152).
6. On CLI, VS Code, Chrome and Mobile the person is sent to web billing to do step 4.

/payment-failure page text: renewal failure pauses paid features; a failed new checkout created no subscription and no charge; usual causes are a decline by the card issuer, a 3D Secure check that closed before confirming, or a network error reaching the bank (apps/web/app/payment-failure/page.tsx:34-44).

established.statement: When a payment fails, the user is told clearly (checkout or renewal) and shown how to fix it, on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome.
After a failed payment the user can retry it (pay the open invoice or update the card) from the product; the brief marks this done on Web and Desktop only.
Status past_due and incomplete grant no paid features; remediation goes through the billing portal only. Access is monotonic and the effective tier falls to free below the active/trialing rank.
A failed new checkout creates no subscription and no charge, and the /payment-failure page must say so.

acceptance_criteria: A web-billed account with status past_due shows a red alert in Settings, Billing with 'Pay <amount> now' (when an open invoice exists) and 'Update payment method'.
The same alert for status unpaid says 'unpaid'; an Enterprise contract plan shows no such alert.
/pricing shows 'Update payment' on plan buttons and /upgrade shows 'Open billing' while the status is past_due or unpaid.
/payment-failure shows both the renewal text and the 'no subscription was created and you weren't charged' text.
CLI account usage prints 'Subscription: past due' and the billing link for past_due, unpaid and incomplete.
Chrome side panel for a past_due paid account shows 'Update billing to restore Managed Cloud chat.' and a 'Manage billing' button that opens web billing.
VS Code shows 'Restore paid Cloud access on Web' under 'Manage billing & subscription' for a non-entitled paid plan.
After the payment succeeds and the account is re-read, the alert is gone.
inferred: Mobile should offer an action to reach web billing for a past-due web-billed plan when store links are allowed [inferred from the brief claiming mobile 'done']
Chrome should word 'unpaid' as specifically as 'past_due' [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Show the same failed-payment sentence on every app from one shared copy source, so the six wordings cannot drift.
[proposed] Fetch the open invoice by status instead of from the latest 24, so 'Pay now' never goes missing.

steps.what_happens: The payment provider reports a failed renewal; the server stores status past_due or unpaid on the user's subscriptions row.
The app reads plan, status and billing source from the account (web store; mobile GET /api/me?surface=mobile; CLI and extensions read the account usage and plan data).
Web loads GET /api/billing/invoices; the server asks the payment provider for the last 24 invoices of the stored customer.
The browser picks the first open invoice with a hosted link and builds 'Pay <amount> now'.
'Update payment method' calls POST /api/portal; the server creates a portal session and the browser is handed to the provider's hosted page.
The person pays or updates the card on the provider's hosted page; the provider tells our webhook and the status returns to active.

features.summary: Lets a person look back at what they paid. Web and Desktop (hosted web app) list invoices, credit-purchase receipts, refunds with status, and a credit ledger, and a refund request form sits on /refund-policy. Mobile only sends people to the web. Credit notes and a dedicated auto-reload history do not exist.

(apps/web/lib/services/billing-invoice-service.ts:26; apps/web/features/billing/components/BillingPaymentHistory.tsx:63-236; apps/web/app/api/billing/credit-history/route.ts:106-120; apps/web/app/refund-policy/RefundRequestForm.tsx:20)

established.statement: Users can see a list of past bills (invoices and credit purchases).
Users can download an invoice (PDF) and a receipt for every payment, including one-off credit purchases.
Users can see credit notes issued against their invoices.
Users can see refund status (requested, processing, refunded).
Users can see a history of credit purchases and of automatic reloads.
Customers request refunds on /refund-policy and operators refund from /admin/refunds; both issue the refund in the payment provider.
Refund status labels come from the provider, empty states explain why, failures show an error with Try again.

A Free account sees 'Invoices appear here once you are billed on a paid plan.'
An Apple or Google billed account sees the store receipt message.
When the provider call fails, an error and 'Try again' appear and are not replaced by an empty state.
Credit history shows usage debits labelled 'Usage: <model name>' and hides allocation and reset rows.

steps.what_happens: The Settings page waits for the billing store, then fetches invoices and payment methods in parallel, and credit history separately.
The invoices route authenticates, applies the rate limit and reads the stored customer id from the subscriptions table.
The server lists invoices from the payment provider (limit 24) and returns them with hosted and PDF links.
Receipts and refunds routes read payment intents and refunds from the provider for the user's customer.
Credit history is a database query on credit_transactions filtered to user-facing types, newest first.
Clicking a View, PDF or receipt link opens the provider's hosted page in a new tab (system browser on Desktop).
A refund request is posted with CSRF and rate limit, assessed and stored; an audit event is recorded.

features.summary: A person on a web-billed paid plan can cancel at the end of the period, undo that, or schedule a switch to a smaller plan after reviewing price, usage and limits. Web and Desktop (hosted web app) do all of it. Mobile and VS Code only show the end date; CLI and Chrome show nothing.

purpose.what_it_does: Cancel opens the hosted portal's cancel step; the plan ends at period end. Resume calls POST /api/billing/resume-cancellation to keep the plan. 'Switch to a smaller plan' loads a preview from GET /api/billing/downgrade-preview, then POST schedules the switch for the end of the term. Notices explain what the person keeps until then. (apps/web/features/settings/sections/BillingSection.tsx:339-350,895-918; apps/web/app/api/billing/downgrade-preview/route.ts:49-98)
purpose.why_it_exists: People must be able to leave or shrink without contacting support, and must know what happens next (S83.04, S83.21-S83.24).
purpose.who_uses_it: Individual paying subscribers on web billing, on Web and Desktop. Mobile and VS Code users read the end date.
problems_solved: Surprise loss of access.
Cannot undo a cancel.
Cannot move to a smaller plan without losing the account.
Unclear what is kept after the end.
use_cases: A user clicks 'Cancel plan' and finishes the cancel in the portal; Settings then says the plan ends on a date.
A user changes their mind and clicks 'Resume <plan>'.
A user clicks 'Switch to a smaller plan', reads price, usage and limits, and confirms 'Switch on <date>'.
A VS Code user sees 'Access ends <date>; review or resume the plan on Web'.

journey: 1. Open Settings, Billing.
2. Cancel: click 'Cancel plan', finish in the hosted portal, return; the 'ends on' notice shows.
3. Resume: click 'Resume <plan>'; the app calls the server and shows the new state.
4. Downgrade: click 'Switch to a smaller plan', pick a target if more than one, review the rows, click 'Switch on <date>'.
5. Undo a scheduled switch: click 'Keep <plan>'.
6. At the end date the account moves to Free (cancel) or to the smaller plan (switch).

established.statement: Users can cancel their subscription themselves.
A user who scheduled a cancellation can resume before it ends.
A scheduled end-of-period cancellation is shown with its date.
After cancelling the user is told what they keep until the end and what happens after.
Before a downgrade the user reviews price, features, limits and when it applies, and confirms.
Mid-period tier changes do not claw back the already granted allowance; the smaller allowance applies at next renewal.
Cancellation stays with the channel that sold the subscription.

acceptance_criteria: Cancel plan appears only for a web-billed active or trialing plan with no pending change.
After cancel is scheduled the notice shows the end date and the sentence about moving to Free with chats, projects and files kept.
Resume sends POST /api/billing/resume-cancellation with an Idempotency-Key and the notice disappears with fresh state.
The downgrade dialog shows price, usage and limits and the date it applies before the confirm button is enabled.
Confirming schedules the switch; a failure shows a message that nothing changed.
A scheduled switch shows 'Keep <plan>' and clicking it removes the switch.
Apple, Google and organization-managed plans show no Cancel or Switch buttons.
inferred: Resume while a payment is overdue should not be offered; the code shows the Cancel button only when the status is active or trialing [inferred from BillingSection.tsx:424,903].
proposed: [proposed] Give mobile and VS Code a resume action that opens web billing at the right section.
[proposed] Update docs/product/commercial.md, which says downgrade is not a code path, to describe the scheduled downgrade.

steps.what_happens: Settings loads plan state (GET /api/billing/downgrade-preview) for a web-billed active or trialing plan.
'Cancel plan' posts to /api/portal with flow cancel; the server creates a portal session with a cancel deep link; the browser opens the hosted portal.
The person confirms the cancel in the provider's portal, which sets cancel at period end.
Resume posts with an Idempotency-Key; the server keeps the plan at the provider, writes cancel_at_period_end to subscriptions, audits and returns plan state.
Downgrade confirm posts the target plan; the server schedules the change at the provider under a user-bound idempotency key and returns state.
The browser adopts the returned state and re-renders the notices.

features.summary: Stops a person paying twice and tells them where a plan is billed. Web and Desktop (hosted web app) show 'Billed through' and a store manage link; checkout answers 409 if another channel already bills. Mobile has the warning alert and a Restore purchases row, but both are compiled off in the shipped build.

purpose.what_it_does: Works out the one billing owner of a subscription (web payment provider, Apple, Google, organization or unverified) and uses it to block second purchases, label the plan and link to the right management page. Mobile can re-check store purchases with a Restore control. (apps/web/lib/server/subscription-billing-owner.ts:42-87; apps/web/features/settings/sections/BillingSection.tsx:818-820,877-884)
purpose.why_it_exists: One user has one subscriptions row and exactly one billing owner; a second channel must not create a second bill (doc: docs/product/commercial.md:75-99).
purpose.who_uses_it: Subscribers who bought on the web, Apple or Google; people who reinstall the mobile app; support staff who handle double charges.
problems_solved: Paying through two channels for one plan.
Not knowing where to cancel.
A purchase that did not arrive after reinstall.
use_cases: An Apple-billed user opens Settings, Billing on the web and sees 'Billed through' Apple and 'Manage in the App Store'.
A user tries web checkout while already billed by Google and gets a 409 naming the owner.
On mobile (when purchases are on) the user taps 'Restore purchases' after reinstalling.
A mobile user taps Upgrade on a web-billed plan and reads 'Subscription managed elsewhere'.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: Settings, Billing: row 'Billed through' and the link 'Manage in the App Store' or 'Manage on Google Play' (BillingSection.tsx:818-820,877-884).

Mobile (full screen only): alert 'Subscription managed elsewhere'; row 'Restore purchases' with the value 'Subscriptions and unfinished purchases'; text 'A purchase that did not arrive' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-billing/index.tsx:300-305,803-871).
Mobile (shipped reduced screen): row 'Billing' with values such as 'Managed on the web' or 'Managed where you subscribed' (index.tsx:378-390).
prerequisites: Signed in with a plan whose subscription source is apple, google, stripe or manual.
Restore needs a build with native purchases on, store connection, Cloud mode and a signed-in account (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/useMobileIap.ts:630-637; storePurchases.json:2).
The server must enable the store catalog via MOBILE_IAP_ENABLED and product id settings (apps/web/lib/server/mobile-iap-catalog.ts:53-56).
screens_and_controls: Web: 'Billed through' row; store link buttons; copy for blocked plan change: 'Change or cancel this subscription with Apple before starting web billing.' (Google equivalent) (BillingSection.tsx:431-450).
Mobile alert text: 'This subscription is billed through <source>; manage it there to avoid paying twice.' with buttons OK and the manage action (cloud-billing/index.tsx:300-305).
Mobile restore outcomes: 'No purchases to restore', 'Purchases already restored', 'Restore purchases needs the store' (index.tsx:102-117).
Mobile text: 'Restore purchases re-checks it with the store and never charges you again.' (index.tsx:869).
journey: 1. Open Settings, Billing (web) and read 'Billed through'.
2. If store billed, click 'Manage in the App Store' or 'Manage on Google Play'; the store page opens in a new tab.
3. On web, trying to start checkout while another owner is live is refused with the owner named.
4. On mobile with purchases on: tap Upgrade; if billed elsewhere the alert appears with a manage action.
5. After reinstall tap 'Restore purchases'; the app re-checks the store and shows one of the three outcomes.
feedback_and_outputs: Checkout 409 messages: 'This subscription is billed by Apple. Manage or cancel it with Apple before starting web billing.' (Google, organization and unverified variants) (subscription-billing-owner.ts:121-160).

409 for a live provider subscription: 'This account already has an active subscription with our payment provider. Open Billing to manage it, or contact support if your plan is not showing yet.' (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts:70-71).
Mobile portal error title 'Billing managed elsewhere' on a 409 (index.tsx:76).
settings: storePurchases.json nativePurchases; server flag MOBILE_IAP_ENABLED; product id environment variables MOBILE_IAP_APPLE_PRODUCT_IDS_JSON and MOBILE_IAP_GOOGLE_PRODUCT_IDS_JSON (configuration names only).

working: Billing owner resolution: stripe, apple, google, manual, none or unverified; more than one owner id or a malformed provider id gives unverified, which blocks changes (apps/web/lib/server/subscription-billing-owner.ts:42-65,70-87).

Policy flags canOpenStripePortal, canApplyStripeUpgrade, canStartStripeCheckout (subscription-billing-owner.ts:102-113); checkout returns 409 through stripeBillingOwnershipMessage (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts:332-334).
Checkout also refuses when the provider already bills a live subscription for the stored customer (route.ts:376-415).
A store row past its paid-through date plus a 3-day grace is treated as expired so web checkout can start (subscription-billing-owner.ts:30,92-112).
Web and Desktop Settings show owner label, store links and the owner-specific blocked-change copy (BillingSection.tsx:413-450,877-884).
Mobile owner guard and alert code (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/subscriptionSource.ts:41-72; cloud-billing/index.tsx:287-305).
Mobile restore code: outcomes nothing-to-restore, already-restored, store-unavailable (useMobileIap.ts:44-45,630-650).
incomplete: Mobile restore in the shipped build: code complete but not reachable (see disconnected).
Whether restore also re-sends pending receipts for a user who is not in Cloud mode: restore requires a cloud account epoch (useMobileIap.ts:631-637).
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile Restore purchases row, the 'Subscription managed elsewhere' alert on Upgrade, 'Manage in <store>' rows and 'View invoices' are in the full screen, which is returned only when NATIVE_PURCHASES_AVAILABLE is true; the value read from storePurchases.json is false (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/nativePurchaseAvailability.ts:3; storePurchases.json:2; cloud-billing/index.tsx:351). The test 'ships with purchases switched off' confirms (apps/mobile/__tests__/NoPurchasesBilling.test.tsx:106).

The brief says the switch is FEATURES.billing; the code uses FEATURES.billing only for the portal row (cloud-billing/index.tsx:199; apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:6) and for a service that throws in v1 (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/service.ts:9). The actual purchase switch is storePurchases.json (doc: docs/product/commercial.md:66-70).
not_available: Store-billed management on CLI, VS Code and Chrome beyond a label: VS Code shows 'Apple App Store' or 'Google Play' as owner text (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/account-auth/accountPresentation.ts:24-38); no manage link seen.
Web restore control: not applicable.

established.statement: On mobile, users can restore store purchases without being charged again.
Users billed by Apple or Google are told to manage it in that store, with a link.
Before a purchase that would double-bill, the user is warned.
One subscriptions row has exactly one billing owner; while the recorded owner is entitled the second channel loses; the new purchase takes ownership only once the old owner is no longer entitled.
Mobile v1 sells nothing in the app; when store purchase is turned on it opens with no waitlist or access code.
Mixed or unreadable ids are 'unverified' and block changes.

acceptance_criteria: A row with a valid web subscription id resolves to stripe; with only an Apple id to apple; with only a Google token to google.
A row with two owner ids or a malformed web id resolves to unverified and checkout returns 409 with the unverified message.
Web checkout for an Apple-billed active user returns 409 naming Apple.
Web checkout when the provider already bills a live subscription for the customer returns 409.
Settings, Billing shows 'Billed through' and the store manage link for Apple or Google plans.
On a mobile build with native purchases on, Restore with no store purchases shows 'No purchases to restore' and never charges.
On the shipped mobile build no Restore row is shown.
inferred: Organization appears as 'manual' in the source and as 'organization' only in the separate billing owner value (subscription-billing-owner.ts:90-98) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Show the same owner explanation in CLI, VS Code and Chrome when they gate on a plan owned by a store.
[proposed] Correct the brief's switch-on instruction to the real flag.

steps.what_happens: The server reads the user's subscriptions row and resolves the billing owner from the three id columns.
Checkout refuses with 409 when the owner policy does not allow starting checkout, or when the provider already bills a live subscription.
The web Settings page reads the same source from the account and shows the label and store links.
Mobile asks the store (native library, an outside service) for available purchases on the device; with a token it sends them to our verify route; outcomes are set on the device.
The server verifies the receipt with Apple or Google (outside services) and records it, refusing a purchase that conflicts with an entitled owner.
Store renewal notifications arrive from Apple or Google and update the row unless it also holds a web subscription id.

features.summary: A team owner buys seats on the Business tab of /pricing and adds seats later through the upgrade dialog. The workspace console shows seats used out of seats licensed. Enterprise admins see a read-only contract, contacts, purchase order and invoices. Bank-transfer recording exists as an API only, with no screen.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a team owner choose standard and premium seat counts at checkout, raise the count through the upgrade route, see 'Seats used N of M' in the workspace console, and lets enterprise administrators read their contract, contacts, purchase-order reference and invoices. An API records offline payments (wire, check, bank transfer) against an invoice. (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts:208-216; apps/web/app/api/upgrade/route.ts:277-290; apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceBillingSummary.tsx:104-135; apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/billing-contract/route.ts:114-204)
purpose.why_it_exists: Teams pay per seat and enterprises pay by contract and invoice; admins need to see what they are licensed for and billed (S83.28-S83.31).
purpose.who_uses_it: Team owners, workspace administrators, enterprise finance and procurement contacts, and operators who reconcile bank transfers.
problems_solved: No way to size a team purchase.
Admins cannot see licensed versus used seats.
Procurement cannot find the PO number, terms or invoices.
Bank transfers cannot be matched to invoices safely.
use_cases: An owner types seat counts on /pricing, Business tab, and buys.
An admin sees 'Seats used 3 of 5' in the workspace console.
A finance contact reads the contract's payment terms and purchase order reference.
An operator reports a wire against an invoice with its bank reference through the API.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web app): /pricing, Business tab, seat inputs labelled by the 'seatCountLabel' text (apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:1104-1120).
Web and Desktop: Settings, Billing shows the plan price per Standard and Premium seat for a team (BillingSection.tsx:318-327 region 'per Standard seat').
Web and Desktop: workspace console, 'Plan and seats' section with rows 'Plan', 'Seats used', 'Members' (WorkspaceBillingSummary.tsx:99-135).
Web and Desktop: workspace console sections 'Enterprise contract', 'Contacts' and 'Invoices' for organization administrators (WorkspaceEnterpriseContract.tsx:253,270-312).

established.statement: A team owner can buy seats (choose a count at purchase and add seats later).
Admins can assign seats to members and see seats used versus licensed.
Enterprise admins can see billing and procurement contacts for their contract.
Enterprise customers can buy through purchase orders and invoices: PO numbers on invoices, invoice terms, offline payment reporting.

An invitation beyond the licensed seats is refused with the seat message.

steps.what_happens: The pricing page keeps seat counts in the browser and sends plan, interval, seats and premiumSeats to POST /api/checkout.
The server validates the body, resolves seat quantities, checks the owner policy and, for a first purchase, the upgrade-access gate (403 when missing).
The server creates the hosted checkout session at the payment provider and the person pays there.
Later seat increases call POST /api/upgrade, which changes the subscription item quantity at the payment provider and refuses reductions.
The console reads seat state from the organization (licensed and consumed seats).
Contract read checks admin access, billing.read, then reads contract, invoices and positions and logs the admin data access.
Offline payment report checks billing.contracts.manage, the agreement's allowed methods, then inserts a record unless the same bank reference exists.

features.summary: Lets a person choose light, dark or follow-the-device colours on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI and Chrome. Web and Mobile also save the choice to the signed-in account. The CLI has seven terminal themes. VS Code has no theme setting of its own.

purpose.what_it_does: Switches the colour palette of the app. Web, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome offer System, Light and Dark. The CLI offers seven terminal themes. The choice is kept on the device and, for signed-in Web and Mobile Cloud users, in the account.
purpose.why_it_exists: People work in bright rooms, dark rooms and terminals. Claude and ChatGPT both let the person choose, so the product must too (doc: docs/product/requirements.md, section 16.1 lists Theme under Appearance settings). Accessible palettes in the CLI help low-vision and colour-blind people (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/theme_picker.rs:40-57).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI and Chrome. People who need high contrast or a colour-blind palette use the CLI themes.
problems_solved: A bright screen at night, or a dark screen in sunlight.
A second device that does not match the first (Web and Mobile Cloud settings sync).
Native dialogs on Desktop that did not match the chosen theme (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:606-618).
A flash of the wrong colour before the page loads (apps/web/shared/components/seo/theme-init-script.ts:1-40).
use_cases: A person on Web switches from System to Dark in the evening, and the change shows at once.
A person signs in on a second browser and finds the same theme already applied.
A CLI user on a light terminal picks Auto or a high-contrast theme and the choice is still there next launch.
A Chrome user forces the side panel to Dark while the browser stays light.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: Settings, Appearance, row 'Theme' with three buttons System, Light, Dark (apps/web/features/settings/sections/AppearanceSection.tsx:23-27, 44-73). Desktop shows the same hosted page (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).

Mobile: Settings, group 'Device', row 'Appearance', screen 'Appearance' with System, Light, Dark (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:670-676; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/appearance/index.tsx:13-17).

CLI: type /theme with no argument to open the picker, or /theme <name> (apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:575-598, 793-799). Names: auto, dark, light, ansi, high-contrast-dark, high-contrast-light, colorblind (apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/theme_picker.rs:51-59). Also 'theme' as a config key (apps/cli/src/config.rs:1562-1570).

Chrome: extension Options page, section 'Appearance', row 'Theme' with System, Light, Dark (apps/extension/src/features/options/appearance-section.ts:36-70; apps/extension/src/features/appearance/themePreference.ts:5-9).
VS Code: no theme setting found in apps/extension-vscode/package.json; the only 'theme' key there is the marketplace banner (package.json:26).
prerequisites: None for the device choice. Web keeps it in browser storage even when signed out.
Account sync happens only when signed in on Web (apps/web/features/settings/components/CloudSettingsSync.tsx:192-201).
screens_and_controls: Web: three icon buttons labelled 'System theme', 'Light theme', 'Dark theme' with a pressed state (AppearanceSection.tsx:50-57).

Mobile: three rows each with a title, a one-line description ('Match this device.', 'Bright neutral interface.', 'Dark neutral interface.') and a check mark on the active one (appearance/index.tsx:13-17, 39-73).
CLI: an overlay list of seven themes with a code preview (theme_picker.rs header comment and ThemeChoice::ALL at line 51).

Chrome: a drop-down. While loading it is disabled. A status line under the label describes the choice: 'Always light.', 'Always dark.', or "Follows your device's appearance." (appearance-section.ts:20-24, 66-77; themePreference.ts:15-19).
journey: Open the settings screen of the app (or type /theme in the CLI).
Pick System, Light or Dark (CLI: pick one of seven).
The palette changes at once with no reload (web: AppearanceSection.tsx:53 calls setNextTheme; mobile: appearance/index.tsx:44).
The app saves the value on the device. Signed-in Web writes it to the account after 400 ms. Mobile Cloud mode pushes it in the next settings sync.
On the next launch the saved value is applied before or as the first screen paints.
feedback_and_outputs: The active choice shows as pressed or checked.
Web shows an alert 'error text + This device keeps your choice.' with a Retry button when the account save or read fails (apps/web/features/settings/components/SettingsPreferenceRow.tsx:8-26).
CLI prints 'Theme set to X, saved in <path>.' or 'Theme set to X for this session; it could not be saved: ...' (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:5232-5245).
Chrome shows 'Saving…', then the description; on failure 'Could not save your theme. Please try again.' and the old value returns (appearance-section.ts:14-16, 82-99).
settings: Web storage key 'theme' (apps/web/shared/components/ThemeConstants.ts:3).
Account namespace 'appearance', field theme (apps/web/features/settings/lib/appearance-namespace.ts:12, 109-111).
Mobile stores themeMode separately for Local and Cloud (apps/mobile/stores/settings/localSettingsStore.ts:75; apps/mobile/stores/settings/cloudSettingsStore.ts:71).
CLI config key ui.theme (apps/cli/src/config.rs:1562-1570).
Chrome storage key agi_theme_preference (themePreference.ts:3).
Related: Contrast row (System or High) on Web (AppearanceSection.tsx:155-172).

working: Web: next-themes provider with default System and storage key 'theme' (apps/web/shared/components/ThemeProvider.tsx:41-54; apps/web/shared/components/ThemeConstants.ts:3-7).
Web: the page gets data-theme and data-theme-preference attributes after each change (ThemeProvider.tsx:22-26).
Web: an inline script sets the theme from storage before first paint (apps/web/shared/components/seo/theme-init-script.ts:1-40).
Web: a stored value that is not light, dark or system is repaired to dark (ThemeProvider.tsx:18-20; ThemeConstants.ts:9-14).

Web: theme is part of the 'appearance' account namespace, saved after 400 ms and flushed on page hide (CloudSettingsSync.tsx:37, 259-298, 313-326). A theme set while the account read was in flight wins over the late account value (CloudSettingsSync.tsx:48-58, 214-221).

Desktop: the Electron preload watches the page's data-theme-preference and reports it to the main process (apps/desktop/electron/preload.ts:218-236). The main process sets nativeTheme.themeSource, repaints windows and saves 'appearance' in the shell settings file (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:613-619). At start it applies the saved value (main.ts:2604-2605).

Mobile: three modes, kept separately for Local and Cloud (appearance/index.tsx:21-29). The app sets the OS colour scheme from the active mode (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:553-561). Cloud theme is sent to the account in the settings sync (apps/mobile/services/cloudSettingsMapping.ts:130-137, 180-188).

CLI: seven themes. The saved slug is read before the first frame and defaults to Dark if missing or unknown (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:650-660). The picker and /theme <name> both save to the project config (tui_app.rs:5260-5268; slash_commands.rs:793-799; apps/cli/src/config.rs:1263-1266).
Chrome: Options saves to chrome.storage.local and applies at once; the side panel reads the value on load and on later changes (themePreference.ts:29-43; apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:16149).
incomplete: Desktop gets the account value only through the hosted web page [inferred from AGENTS.md section 5 and the CloudSettingsSync mount in apps/web/app/AppRuntimeMounts.tsx:18-20].

CLI persistence is per project (.agiworkforce/config.toml in the working folder) when set from the picker or /theme (apps/cli/src/config.rs:1162-1171, 1263-1266). The user-level key can be set with the config command (config.rs:1562-1570).
Chrome keeps the theme on one device only; nothing sends it to the account (themePreference.ts:29-43).
not_available: VS Code: no theme setting; no matching key in apps/extension-vscode/package.json. The extension has a script that checks its colours use editor theme tokens (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:1573) so it presumably follows the editor theme [inferred].
CLI has no 'system' value; Auto follows the terminal background instead (theme_picker.rs ThemeChoice::applied at line 123).

established.statement: The user can choose light, dark or system theme and it applies and persists.
Appearance settings are their own page and include Theme.
A stored value that is not valid falls back to dark on Web.
If syncing fails, the device keeps the choice and the person can retry.

acceptance_criteria: On Web, pressing Dark changes the page at once and a reload keeps Dark.
With System selected, changing the operating system appearance changes the app without a reload.
Signing in on a second browser shows the theme saved from the first.
On Desktop, a permission dialog drawn by the shell matches the chosen theme.
On Mobile, Local mode and Cloud mode can hold different themes.
In the CLI, choose High Contrast Dark, quit, start again in the same folder, and the theme is the same.
In Chrome Options, choose Light, then open the side panel: it is light.
inferred: A first frame before React loads should already show the right palette; the inline script is the mechanism [inferred from theme-init-script.ts:1-40].
The CLI should offer a user-wide default as well as a project value [inferred; only the project path is used by the picker].
proposed: [proposed] Store the CLI picker choice at user level by default, so one choice covers all folders.
[proposed] Sync Chrome's theme to the account like Web.
[proposed] Add an explicit theme note for VS Code stating it follows the editor theme.

steps.what_happens: Person presses a theme button; the hook passes the value to next-themes, which sets the page class and saves it in browser storage.
Desktop only: the preload sees the page attribute change and tells the main process, which sets the native theme and saves it in the shell settings file.
Signed-in Web: the sync component notices the change, waits 400 ms, then sends only the changed keys to the account settings endpoint.
The server merges the patch into the user's settings row.
On another Web device, after sign-in the sync component reads the namespace and sets the theme, unless the person changed it meanwhile.
Mobile Cloud mode: the theme is put in the settings snapshot and pushed with the sync engine; the pull applies it to the Cloud store.
CLI: the chosen slug is applied to the palette, then written to .agiworkforce/config.toml of the project.
Chrome: the Options page writes agi_theme_preference to chrome.storage.local; the side panel listens for storage changes.

features.summary: Lets a person pick the colour used on selected controls and highlights. Web and Desktop offer five colours, Mobile offers ten. Web and Mobile Cloud mode share the choice through the account for the colours both know. CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no accent setting.

purpose.what_it_does: Recolours the highlight colour of the interface. Web and Desktop set one attribute on the page root and the style sheet does the rest. Mobile replaces its main highlight colour at run time.
purpose.why_it_exists: Personal colour is a common appearance control in the leading chat apps, and the product requirement lists Accent colour under Appearance (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 16.1).
purpose.who_uses_it: People on Web, Desktop and Mobile who want a colour other than the default.
problems_solved: Highlight colour that clashes with taste or with a theme.
Having to set the same colour twice on two devices (shared through the account where names match).
use_cases: Pick Violet on Web; the buttons and highlights turn violet.
Pick Lime on Mobile in Cloud mode; Local mode keeps Neutral.
Return to AGI amber to reset to the brand colour.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: Settings, Appearance, row 'Accent colour' with round swatches (apps/web/features/settings/sections/AppearanceSection.tsx:87-114).
Mobile: Settings, group 'Device', row 'Accent Color', screen 'Accent Color' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:678-684; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/accent-color/index.tsx:39).
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: none.
prerequisites: None. Account sync needs a sign-in (Web) or Cloud mode (Mobile).
screens_and_controls: Web: five round swatches, each with a tooltip and the label '<name> accent', a check on the active one, a 44 px touch area on touch screens (AppearanceSection.tsx:94-110). Names: AGI amber, Green, Blue, Violet, Rose (apps/web/shared/stores/web-settings-store.ts:13-19).

Mobile: a list of ten rows with a swatch circle, name and check: Neutral, Blue, Cyan, Green, Lime, Yellow, Orange, Rose, Magenta, Violet (accent-color/index.tsx:13-24, 46-81). Intro text: 'Colors selected controls and highlights. Neutral is the default.' (accent-color/index.tsx:42).
journey: Open the settings screen.
Press a swatch (Web) or tap a row (Mobile).
The interface recolours at once.
The value is saved on the device and, when signed in, sent to the account.
feedback_and_outputs: The chosen swatch or row shows a check and a pressed or selected state.
Mobile settings root shows the current accent name as the row value (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:681).
Web shows the sync alert with Retry if the account save fails (SettingsPreferenceRow.tsx:8-26).
settings: Web: accentColor in the web settings store, persisted under 'agiworkforce-web-settings' (web-settings-store.ts:86, 137, 210).
Account: appearance.accentColor with web 'default' written as 'amber' (appearance-namespace.ts:56-62).
Mobile: accentColor in the Local and Cloud settings stores, default 'neutral' (localSettingsStore.ts:76; cloudSettingsStore.ts:72).
Related: Contrast, Motion and Chat font rows on Web (AppearanceSection.tsx:75-78).

working: Web: AppearancePreferences sets or clears data-accent on the page root (apps/web/shared/components/AppearancePreferences.tsx:33-37). The style sheet maps each value to colour variables (apps/web/app/globals.css:725-760).
Web: accent is a field of the account appearance namespace and is saved with the rest (appearance-namespace.ts:109-127; CloudSettingsSync.tsx:66, 259-298).
Web: a colour name web does not know, such as mobile's neutral, is skipped when the account value is loaded, so Web keeps its own colour (appearance-namespace.ts:53-55, 137-138).

Mobile: each mode has its own accent; the theme hook replaces the highlight colours with the chosen swatch for the current light or dark scheme (apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/useTheme.ts:20-34, 52-55). Neutral and high-contrast mode leave the base colours.
Mobile: Cloud accent is part of the settings sync (apps/mobile/services/cloudSettingsMapping.ts:130-137, 180-188).
Mobile: an unknown value becomes neutral (apps/mobile/src/ui/theme/tokens.ts:28-32).
incomplete: The vocabularies differ: Web has AGI amber and no Neutral, Mobile has Neutral and no amber. Web 'amber' reaches Mobile as an unknown token and becomes neutral (tokens.ts:28-32; keys in packages/ui/design-tokens/src/index.ts:939-953) [inferred]. Cyan, Lime, Yellow, Orange and Magenta from Mobile are ignored on Web (appearance-namespace.ts:64-70).
Web 'Green', 'Blue', 'Violet', 'Rose' match Mobile names and travel both ways (appearance-namespace.ts:56-70).
not_available: CLI: no accent setting found in the CLI config keys listed at apps/cli/src/config.rs:1619.
VS Code: no accent setting found in apps/extension-vscode/package.json.
Chrome: no accent row in the Options Appearance section, which holds only Theme (apps/extension/src/features/options/appearance-section.ts:36-70).

established.statement: Where offered, the user can pick an accent colour that recolours the interface.
Accent colour is on the Appearance page.
Web and Mobile share one account vocabulary; an unknown name must not repaint the other surface.

acceptance_criteria: On Web each of the five swatches changes the highlight colour and sets data-accent on <html> (none for AGI amber).
Reload keeps the colour.
On Mobile each of the ten rows changes the highlight colour in light and dark.
Picking Green on Web, then signing in on Mobile Cloud mode, shows Green.
Picking Lime on Mobile does not change Web.
In Local mode on Mobile, the accent does not reach the account.
inferred: The two apps should agree on one list or document the difference [inferred from the mismatch in vocabularies].
proposed: [proposed] Add 'amber' to the Mobile vocabulary or map it to a named Mobile accent so the default round-trips.
[proposed] Offer accent in the CLI with ANSI-safe colours if wanted.

features.summary: Web and Desktop let a person set chat text to Small, Default or Large and set Motion to System or Reduced. The CLI has a reduced-motion setting and plain mode. Chrome honours the device setting only. Interface density has no control or code anywhere. Mobile follows the device by decision.

purpose.what_it_does: Text size changes message and code text in chat. Motion reduces animation in the interface and replies. Density is meant to switch compact or comfortable spacing but does not exist.
purpose.why_it_exists: Readability and motion sensitivity. The brief lists text size, density and reduced motion as controls (S84.05 to S84.07). Chat font, contrast and motion are on the Appearance page in the requirements (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 16.1).
purpose.who_uses_it: People with low vision, motion sensitivity or a preference for denser text.
problems_solved: Small text in long chats.
Animations that cause discomfort.
A terminal spinner that is noisy for a screen reader (apps/cli/src/output.rs:19-25).
use_cases: A Web user sets Chat text size to Large for long reading.
A person who is motion-sensitive sets Motion to Reduced without changing the whole computer.
A CLI user sets ui.reduced-motion true.
A Chrome user with the operating system set to reduce motion gets calm scrolling in Options.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: Settings, Appearance, row 'Chat text size' (a drop-down with Small, Default, Large) and row 'Motion' (buttons System, Reduced) (apps/web/features/settings/sections/AppearanceSection.tsx:116-150, 210-228).
CLI: config key reduced-motion or ui.reduced-motion (apps/cli/src/config.rs:1572-1578), or plain mode (flag --plain or environment AGI_PLAIN, apps/cli/src/output.rs:30-52).
Chrome: no control; the pages follow the device preference (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:4622; apps/extension/src/options.ts:246, 1214-1218).

Mobile: no control. The decision says text size and reduced motion follow the device (doc: docs/decisions/2026-11-13-founder-decisions.md D-2026-11-13-04; docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md S84.05, S84.07).
Density: none.
prerequisites: None.
screens_and_controls: Chat text size: a drop-down labelled 'Chat text size' (AppearanceSection.tsx:215-225).
Motion: two buttons 'System' and 'Reduced' with the hint 'Less animation in replies and the interface. System follows your device.' (AppearanceSection.tsx:126-148).
There is no 'Full motion' option, on purpose (AppearancePreferences.tsx:45-48).
journey: Open Settings, Appearance.
Choose a text size or a motion value.
The change shows at once: text resizes; animations drop to near zero.
It is saved on the device and, when signed in on Web, to the account.
feedback_and_outputs: The current value is shown in the control.
Text in messages and code blocks changes size.
Sync alert with Retry if the account write fails (SettingsPreferenceRow.tsx:8-26).
settings: chatTextSize: 'small' | 'default' | 'large' and motion: 'system' | 'reduced' in the web store (web-settings-store.ts:9, 36, 119-120).
Account keys textSize and motion in appearance (appearance-namespace.ts:39-40, 114-115).
CLI ui.reduced_motion (config.rs:155).
Related: Contrast and Chat font rows (AppearanceSection.tsx:155-208).

working: Web: the text size is set as data-chat-text-size on <html>; default removes it (apps/web/shared/components/AppearancePreferences.tsx:17-21). Rules in globals.css change the size of prose and code blocks (apps/web/app/globals.css:932-935, 965-972).

Web: motion 'reduced' sets data-motion=reduced; System removes it (AppearancePreferences.tsx:49-53). One blanket rule shrinks animation and transition time and turns off smooth scrolling (apps/web/app/globals.css:1928-1935). Several media queries answer the device setting separately (globals.css comment at lines 1920-1927).
Web: both values are in the account namespace and sync (appearance-namespace.ts:114-115, 143-147).
CLI: reduced motion or plain mode holds the spinner and shimmer still (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7122-7124; apps/cli/src/tui/motion.rs:10-14).

Chrome: the side panel and Options style sheets have prefers-reduced-motion rules, and Options scrolls without animation when the device asks (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:4622; apps/extension/src/options.ts:246, 1214-1218).
incomplete: Chrome has no in-app motion control, and no text size control.
Desktop uses the same hosted screen; no separate check was made.
not_available: Interface density (compact or comfortable): no control and no code found on Web, Desktop, Mobile or Chrome. I read AppearanceSection.tsx in full and it has no density row.

Mobile: no text size or motion control in Appearance (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/appearance/index.tsx shows only theme). By decision, follows the device. Whether the app honours the device text scale and reduce-motion setting was not checked.
CLI and VS Code: no text size control found. VS Code motion: none found.

features.summary: Web and Desktop let a person switch the interface language from a list of native names with flags, but only English and Spanish are offered, and settings screens stay in English. The choice is saved on the device and in the account. Mobile has the screen but it is switched off in v1. CLI and VS Code have none.

purpose.what_it_does: Changes the language of the menus, navigation and pricing text. The hint beside the control says settings labels and conversations are not translated.
purpose.why_it_exists: People expect to use the product in their own language. The founders limited the list to languages that are complete and reviewed (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md, lines 66-73).
purpose.who_uses_it: Spanish speakers today on Web and Desktop; later any reviewed language.
problems_solved: English-only menus for Spanish speakers.
Half-finished translations being shown (incomplete languages are hidden).
use_cases: A Spanish-speaking user selects Español and the menus change at once.
A user signs in on a new browser and finds Español already chosen.
A right-to-left language, once released, flips direction on the page root.

features.summary: Sets what a new chat starts with. Web and Desktop have Default model, Reasoning effort and New chats start in (Chat or Work), all limited by plan. Mobile has a device-only default effort and remembers the last model per mode. VS Code has three settings. CLI has config values. A default workspace exists nowhere.

purpose.what_it_does: Web and Desktop: saves a default model to the account, an effort level on the device, and a Chat or Work start mode in the account. Other surfaces keep their own equivalents.
purpose.why_it_exists: People should not repick the same model, effort and mode for every chat. The brief lists default model, effort, mode and workspace (S84.10 to S84.13).
purpose.who_uses_it: Regular users on every app, and developers using VS Code or the CLI.
problems_solved: Repeating the same picks at the start of each chat.
Choosing a model or effort the plan does not include (shown as locked).
use_cases: Set a default model on Web and every new chat starts with it.
Set effort to High once.
Start new chats in Work for people on a plan that includes it.
In VS Code set the default agent mode to Plan.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: Settings, General, Preferences: rows 'Default model', 'Reasoning effort', 'New chats start in' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/GeneralSection.tsx:299-307; row definitions at lines 361, 460, 583).

Mobile: Settings, General: a 'Default effort' slider group labelled by settings:defaultEffort, and the row 'Models' that opens the model screen (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/general/index.tsx:156-183).
VS Code settings: agiWorkforce.model, agiWorkforce.agent.mode, agiWorkforce.agent.effort (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:1219, 1404, 1428).
CLI: config [default] model, reasoning_effort and permission_mode (apps/cli/src/config.rs:177, 200-202, 213-216); /effort saves the effort (apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:800-807).
Chrome: the effort last chosen in the side panel is remembered (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:11111, 11501-11503); no Options row.
Default workspace: none.
prerequisites: Web: billing information must be loaded before models and effort levels are shown as allowed or locked (GeneralSection.tsx:361-380, 470-478).
Default Work mode applies only if the plan allows Work (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:1062-1066, 1233-1237).
screens_and_controls: Default model: a drop-down with 'Last used' first, then models. Models above the plan show '<name> · Upgrade to use (<plan label>)' and cannot be saved; picking one shows 'X needs <plan>.' with an 'Upgrade to use' link (GeneralSection.tsx:410-430).

Reasoning effort: a drop-down 'Off' plus levels low, medium, high, xhigh, max; levels over the plan show '<label>, not on your plan' and are disabled; plus the note 'Each chat can change this in the composer.' (GeneralSection.tsx:448-520).
New chats start in: a drop-down with Chat and Work and a plan hint (GeneralSection.tsx:583-604).
Mobile: an effort slider (general/index.tsx:158-171). Intro: 'Local defaults. These apply to this device only, not AGI Cloud.' (general/index.tsx:101-104).
journey: Open Settings, General.
Pick a model, an effort and a start mode.
