features.summary: Lets a person choose how the message box sends (Enter or Cmd/Ctrl+Enter) and see, switch off or rebind keyboard shortcuts. Web and Desktop offer an on/off send switch and a shortcut sheet. VS Code has a three-way send setting. CLI uses a config file. Chrome lists its two shortcuts and opens the browser's own page.

purpose.what_it_does: Web and Desktop (the Desktop window shows the hosted web app): a 'Send with Enter' switch decides whether Enter sends or adds a new line, and a 'Keyboard' pane lists shortcuts, lets the person record a new key combination for four of them, switch app shortcuts off, and restore defaults. VS Code has the setting agiWorkforce.composer.enterBehavior with three values. The CLI reads [ui.keybindings] in config.toml for seven global actions. Chrome shows its two browser commands read-only and links to chrome://extensions/shortcuts.
purpose.why_it_exists: People type in different ways. Some want Enter to add a line and a modifier to send, for long prompts, or for IME (input method) typing. Some shortcut keys clash with other tools, so they need to be moved or turned off. The brief's S84.14 and S84.15 say the user can choose the send key and view and customise shortcuts.
purpose.who_uses_it: Keyboard-heavy chat users, developers in VS Code or the CLI, people typing in languages that use an input method editor, and people whose browser or OS already uses a default shortcut.
problems_solved: Accidental send when Enter is pressed to add a line
Shortcut clashes with other apps or the browser
Not knowing which shortcuts exist
Needing to undo many custom keys at once
use_cases: A person writing long multi-paragraph prompts turns Send with Enter off so Enter adds a line and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends.
A person whose copy-last-message shortcut clashes with another tool records a new combination in the Keyboard pane.
A VS Code user sets Cmd/Ctrl+Enter as the send key.
A CLI user moves the cycle-model action to another chord in config.toml.

steps.what_happens: Person flips the Send with Enter switch; the store updates sendWithEnter.
The store persists to localStorage.
The composer key handler reads sendWithEnter on each keydown and sends or inserts a line.
When signed in, CloudSettingsSync compares the projected values with the last acknowledged ones and writes the changed fields after 400 ms to the 'appearance' namespace.

Rebinding: the dialog turns a key press into a chord, checks it against reserved and existing chords, then writes shortcutBindings in the store; the key handler uses the bound chords.
VS Code: the setting is read by Config and sent to the sidebar webview state; a change event refreshes it.
CLI: config.toml is read at start and the bindings are parsed.

features.summary: Mobile has a 'Haptic Feedback' switch that gates touch vibrations app-wide. features.summary: Lets a person choose where each kind of notice goes (web: Off, Email, Browser, Push combinations; mobile: Push or Off per category) and set quiet hours, when non-critical notices are held. Quiet hours are enforced on our servers for push and schedule emails. Timezone is read-only: it follows the device.

purpose.what_it_does: Web and Desktop (hosted page): the 'Notifications' pane has one select per event; the 'Time and focus' pane holds a break reminder and quiet hours (days, start, end) saved to the account. Mobile: 'Notifications' lists categories with a Push or Off state and links to 'Quiet hours' on the 'Time and focus' screen. Servers hold non-critical push and schedule email during the window; critical types are exempt.
purpose.why_it_exists: People want alerts where they will see them and want silence at night. The brief's S84.18 and S84.19 require per-category channels and quiet hours. S84.02 asks for a visible timezone for schedules, reminders and quiet hours.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who uses scheduled tasks, agents or push alerts; people who work across timezones.
problems_solved: Alerts at the wrong time
Unwanted email or push for finished tasks
No way to see which timezone quiet hours use
Too much time in the app without a break
use_cases: A person sets quiet hours 22:00 to 07:00 on weekdays so a scheduled-task push waits until morning.
A person sets 'Scheduled task finished' to Email only.
A person turns off 'Reply ready' browser alerts.
A person on mobile turns off the 'Tasks' push category.

Quiet hours validation: at least one day, valid times, start different from end (TimeFocusSection.tsx:92-109). Overnight windows work (packages/contracts/types/src/time-focus.ts isMinuteWithinQuietHours).

Timezone: browser zone is detected and saved inside the quiet-hours object, shown as read-only text (TimeFocusSection.tsx:41-43, 375). Mobile uses the device zone (notificationPrefsStore.ts:204, 267).

Server holds notices: push delivery checks quiet hours per device and exempts four critical types (agent_failed, emergency_stop_triggered, agent_approval_needed, approval_pending_escalation) (apps/web/lib/services/push-notification-service.ts:88-110; packages/contracts/types/src/time-focus.ts:7-13).

Schedule email is delayed until the window ends and, if the saved quiet hours cannot be read, the notice is held and finally dropped on the last retry (apps/web/lib/jobs/job-handlers.ts:105-190; apps/web/lib/services/quiet-hours-service.ts:16-86).
Mobile registers its push delivery preferences, including quiet hours and exempt types, with the server (apps/mobile/services/pushPreferenceSync.ts:57-80).
Web reminder checks the window, remembers a dismissal in session storage, and handles missing storage (apps/web/features/time-focus/TimeFocusReminder.tsx:158-168).
Security alerts are always shown in-app, including quiet hours (NotificationsSection.tsx:46-61, subheading).
incomplete: The footer says reminders 'currently apply on the Website', but servers also hold push and schedule email, and mobile shows its own reminder, so the text is outdated for some behaviour (TimeFocusSection.tsx:375 vs job-handlers.ts:111).
Timezone is not chosen: there is no control, so someone travelling cannot set a zone different from the device (S84.02 'not applicable anywhere').

Desktop Electron has no quiet-hours rule of its own; its agent notifications use 'Agent notifications' modes only (agentNotifications.ts shouldNotify) [inferred from absence of quiet-hours reads in that file].
Mobile quiet hours sync only in Cloud mode while signed in; in Local mode they stay on the device (useTimeFocusSync.ts:30-38).

Per-channel choices on mobile beyond Push or Off per category (index.tsx:411-413).

features.summary: The public Desktop app (Electron) can start at login ('Run on startup' in Settings, or 'Launch at Login' in the app menu) and lets the person pick the Quick Ask shortcut from a short list. The quick-ask window cannot be switched off or moved. A choice of what the app opens to has no control on any app.

purpose.what_it_does: Desktop: starts the app when the person logs in to the computer, and sets the global shortcut that opens the small Quick Ask window from any app. The same settings page also sets five other global shortcuts (new chat, screenshot, window shot, voice, stop agents).
purpose.why_it_exists: Quick access from anywhere is the main reason to install a desktop app. Launch at login keeps it ready. The brief's S84.20 asks for a startup destination, S84.21 for launch at login and S84.22 for companion window options (enable, shortcut, placement).
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop people who want AGI one key press away.
problems_solved: Having to open the app each day
A default shortcut clashing with another app
Reaching AGI without switching windows
use_cases: A person turns on Run on startup so Desktop is waiting after login.
A person moves Quick Ask from the default to another listed shortcut because another app uses it.
A person turns Quick Ask off by choosing 'No shortcut'.

where_to_find_it: Desktop (Electron): Settings, group 'Desktop app', item 'General', section 'General desktop settings': row 'Run on startup' (hint 'Start Desktop when you log in to this computer.') and row 'Quick Ask shortcut' (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopSettingsSection.tsx:36, 92-96, 290-327; nav in packages/ui/ui/src/settings-nav.ts:296).

Desktop menu: on macOS the app menu has a check item 'Launch at Login' (apps/desktop/electron/appMenu.ts:139-145); other systems have it in another menu (line 221). File menu has item 'Quick Ask' showing the shortcut (appMenu.ts:183-187); the tray menu also has 'Quick Ask' (appMenu.ts:621).
Desktop (Tauri retained build): a 'Launch at login' setting (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/tabs/General/index.tsx:228-285).
Chrome: no companion window setting found; the brief's Chrome line points at approval code (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:7380-7392) which is unrelated.
Web, mobile, VS Code, CLI: nothing.
prerequisites: Desktop app running (the section appears only when the host bridge exists; DesktopSettingsSection returns null otherwise, line 275).
A shortcut can be registered only if the operating system and other apps have not taken it.

Select 'Quick Ask shortcut' with the listed choices plus 'No shortcut' (choices Alt+Shift+Space, CommandOrControl+Shift+Space, CommandOrControl+Alt+A per packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:162).

A note under the row when the shell reports 'Already used by another Desktop shortcut.', 'Already used by another app.' or 'Not a shortcut this computer can register.' (DesktopSettingsSection.tsx:158-168).
A confirmation dialog 'Open <product> at login?' with buttons 'Cancel' and 'Open at login' when turning it on (main.ts:2060-2073).
journey: Open Settings, then Desktop app, then General.
Turn on Run on startup; confirm 'Open at login'.
The switch shows what the system accepted.
Choose another Quick Ask shortcut in the select; the shell registers it.
Press the shortcut anywhere; the Quick Ask window opens near the top center of the display the pointer is on.
feedback_and_outputs: Switch reflects the system's answer, not only the request (launchAtLogin.ts:25-28).
A note appears when a shortcut could not be claimed; a native notification 'Shortcut unavailable' appears once with a menu fallback hint (shortcuts.ts:34-60).

working: Launch at login is opt-in. The system's answer is the truth: the app reads the login item state, aligns its stored value with it, and does not re-add the item at launch (apps/desktop/electron/launchAtLogin.ts:4-28).
Setting it saves the choice, asks the system, then stores what the system now reports (launchAtLogin.ts:23-28).
Turning it on asks for confirmation; turning it off does not (main.ts:2052-2075, 2185-2190). docs/decisions/wire-or-cut.md:759 records that asking on enable is intended.
The app menu check item calls the same setter and restores the check when the change fails (appMenu.ts:28-35).

The page may set a shortcut only to a listed choice, to 'No shortcut' where allowed, or to the value it already has (apps/desktop/electron/garnishCore.ts:192-199). Others are refused with a message (main.ts:2159-2166).
Shortcuts are registered with the system; a duplicate, taken or malformed chord is reported as a status, not silently dropped (apps/desktop/electron/shortcuts.ts:55-98).
Stop Agents can never be off or lost: if a change leaves it unregistered, the old chords are restored and the person is told (shortcuts.ts:130-169).
Quick Ask window opens centred in the upper part of the display nearest the pointer (apps/desktop/electron/quickAsk.ts:140-142).
incomplete: The brief expects enable and placement options for the companion window; only the shortcut is configurable. There is no way to switch the Quick Ask window off except choosing 'No shortcut', while the menu item still opens it (appMenu.ts:183-187) [inferred].
The shortcut select offers only a few listed chords, not any chord (host-bridge.ts:161-170).

features.summary: Lets a signed-in person see and change their display name and photo, change email through a separate flow, and ask for the whole account to be deleted. Deletion is scheduled with a 24-hour cancellation window, not done at once, and is refused in some billing or workspace-ownership cases.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows the account's name, photo and email. Saves name and photo to the account profile. Starts a scheduled, cancellable deletion of the account and its Cloud data after an explicit confirmation (apps/web/app/api/user/delete-account/route.ts:385-617).
purpose.why_it_exists: A person must be able to correct how the account identifies them and to leave the product and take their data with them. The product requirements list Delete account and a subscription warning before deletion (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:1283-1285).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on Web, Desktop (hosted web app), Mobile, VS Code (link only) and, for name display only, Chrome. Not available in the CLI.
problems_solved: A wrong or outdated name or photo shown in the product and in shared content.
No way to leave: erasure of the account, chats, projects, memory and artifacts.
Accidental or paid-plan-blind deletion: the route stops renewal or refuses when billing cannot be matched.
use_cases: A person changes their full name and uploads a photo in Settings > General on the web.
A mobile user opens Settings > Account > Email, edits the display name, then later schedules deletion and signs out.
A person who owns a plan scheduled to end deletes their account and is told the plan ends at erasure with no refund.
A sole owner of a workspace tries to delete and is told to hand the workspace over first.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop (Electron shows the hosted web app, ARCHITECTURE.md:51-54): Settings > General > Profile (apps/web/features/settings/sections/GeneralSection.tsx:242-276); Settings > Account has the Email row and the Delete account row (apps/web/features/settings/sections/AccountSection.tsx:443,510).

Mobile: Settings > Account section, row labelled 'Email' (EMAIL_SCREEN_TITLE) opens the cloud account screen (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:623); Personalization also edits the full name (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/personalization/index.tsx:421-428).
VS Code: account menu item 'Edit your profile on Web' (Name, photo and email) opens the web profile page (apps/extension-vscode/src/core/commandSetup.ts:2527-2530).
Chrome: no profile editor or delete control found in apps/extension/src; the extension only reads the display name from /api/me (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/capabilityDocument.ts:14,72).
CLI: none.
prerequisites: Signed in to an AGI Cloud account. On mobile an unsigned user sees a sign-in prompt instead (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-account/index.tsx:111-118).
Deletion needs a fresh step-up check (re-verification) (apps/web/app/api/user/delete-account/route.ts:462; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-account/index.tsx:533).
screens_and_controls: Web General > Profile: photo with 'Upload photo' or 'Change photo' and 'Remove'; email shown read-only; 'Full name' field (80 characters); 'Save profile' button; 'Saved' text (GeneralSection.tsx:218-276).

Web Account: 'Email' row with a 'Change email address' action; 'Delete account' row with 'Delete' button; a dialog 'Delete your account?' asking to type DELETE; after scheduling, 'Cancel deletion' appears with the deadline (AccountSection.tsx:443-564,964).

Mobile account screen: 'Change profile photo', 'Display name' edit field, 'Export Cloud Data', 'Delete Account', and a cancel-deletion alert with 'Keep deletion scheduled' and 'Cancel deletion' (index.tsx:722,757,916,1003; 622-632).
VS Code: quick-pick item only.
journey: Web profile: open Settings > General, edit Full name or pick a photo, press 'Save profile'; the profile consumers refresh and 'Saved' shows (GeneralSection.tsx:152-165).

Web deletion: open Settings > Account, press 'Delete', read the notice, type DELETE, confirm, complete the step-up check, read the receipt with the cancellation deadline, press Continue to sign out (AccountSection.tsx:895-960).

Mobile deletion: open the account screen, choose 'Delete Account', read the alert, confirm, pass step-up; the app forgets the remembered account, signs out and shows 'Account deletion scheduled' (index.tsx:513-545).
To keep the account: sign back in before the deadline and choose 'Cancel deletion' (AccountSection.tsx:492-504; index.tsx:607-632).
feedback_and_outputs: Receipt message with the cancellation deadline, status and status reason (delete-account/route.ts:84-110).
Plan notices: ending plan, renewal stopped, store-billed plan keeps charging until cancelled in the store (with a manage link), or granted plan (route.ts:134-147).
Errors in plain words: 409 for active-subscription or sole-owner refusal, 503 when billing or workspace ownership could not be checked, 500 when scheduling failed (route.ts:417,442,454,499,520-570).
settings: No setting controls this feature.
Related: Settings > Account > 'Cancel deletion' (pending state); Settings > Billing for plan changes (route.ts:508-512 message).

working: Web: display name saves through PATCH /api/me and photo through the settings service (apps/web/app/settings/_lib/preferences-client.ts:282-295; GeneralSection.tsx:108-148). PATCH /api/me accepts only display_name (1-120 chars) and avatar_url (apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts:129-132,409-474).
Web email change runs through its own component calling /api/settings/email (apps/web/features/settings/components/EmailAddressChange.tsx:36,249).

Delete route: rate limit, CSRF, auth, plan admission, sole-owner check, step-up, then writes deletion_requested_at and deletion_scheduled_for 24 hours ahead on the profile row and writes an audit event (apps/web/app/api/user/delete-account/route.ts:385-612).

Delete route refuses with 409 when a payment is still being collected, when the plan cannot be matched to a purchase we can cancel, when a plan change is scheduled, or when the account is the only owner of a workspace (route.ts:233-278,421-460,492-513).
Paid plans that can be handled do not block deletion: ending plans, store-billed plans (with a warning), web plans whose renewal is stopped, and granted plans (route.ts:233-278,134-147).
GET reports pending, canCancel, requestedAt, scheduledFor and status (route.ts:319-383); cancel is a separate POST route (apps/web/app/api/user/delete-account/cancel/route.ts:11).

Mobile edits the display name and photo and deletes the account with the same endpoint, handling the two 409 reasons (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-account/index.tsx:190-195,513-600; accountDeletionRefusal.ts:3-30).
VS Code opens the web profile page (commandSetup.ts:2527-2530).

Erasure after the deadline runs in a cron named purge-deleted-accounts whose contents were not opened (apps/web/app/api/cron/purge-deleted-accounts).

established.statement: The user can view and edit name, photo and email on the surface and the change is saved to the account.
The user can delete the account (and its data) from the surface after an explicit confirmation.
Account settings must include Delete account and a subscription cancellation warning before delete when applicable.
Deletion states match the configured grace period and billing policy, cancellation works only when allowed, and partial failures never report complete erasure.
If billing or workspace-ownership cannot be checked, nothing is deleted and a 503 asks the person to try again.

acceptance_criteria: Changing Full name and pressing Save profile on web shows 'Saved' and the new name appears after reload, and PATCH /api/me returns display_name.
Delete needs the typed word DELETE on web before the confirm button enables.
With a paid plan that is renewing through the web, deletion succeeds only after renewal is stopped and the receipt says the plan ends at erasure with no refund.
With a payment still being collected, the request returns 409 reason active_subscription and nothing is scheduled.
When the plan lookup is forced to fail, the response is 503 and profiles.deletion_scheduled_for stays null.
An account that is the only owner of a workspace gets 409 reason sole_organization_owner naming the workspace.
After scheduling, GET /api/user/delete-account returns pending true and canCancel true until the deadline, and Cancel deletion clears the schedule.
Mobile sign-out happens only after the server confirms scheduling.
inferred: [inferred] Deletion is two-stage: schedule now, erase after the 24-hour deadline; the first draft's description of immediate deletion is wrong.

[inferred] Local-mode data on the phone is not touched by deletion: the confirmation says Local Mode data stays on this device (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-account/deleteAccountConfirmation.ts:13-24).
proposed: [proposed] Add a CLI command to show and cancel a pending deletion, and to open the web deletion page.
[proposed] Add a profile editor or at least a link in Chrome, as VS Code has.

steps.what_happens: Person edits name or photo and presses Save profile; the app sends PATCH /api/me with a CSRF token.
Server validates the body, upserts the profiles row and returns display_name and avatar_url.
Person confirms deletion; the client calls DELETE /api/user/delete-account after a step-up check.
Server rate-limits, checks CSRF and identity, loads the subscription and decides admission: none, plan notice, stop web renewal, or refuse.
For a web-billed plan the server stops renewal at the payment provider before scheduling and reverses it if scheduling fails.

features.summary: A person writes standing instructions and details about themselves, and picks style, length, technical level, formatting, language and tone traits. The server adds them to later Cloud chats on that account. A project can opt out. Reset exists for the style block on web and mobile; one-action reset of everything does not exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores a profile (preferred name, work, about you), standing instructions and response-style choices on the account, and adds them as a block to the model request for later chats (apps/web/lib/server/user-identity.ts:160-205,250-292).
purpose.why_it_exists: People want the assistant to follow their preferences every time without repeating them, as Claude and ChatGPT allow.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone signed in on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI (style fields only) and VS Code (name, work and style, plus editor-local instructions).
problems_solved: Repeating the same preferences in every chat.
Replies with the wrong length, tone, language or formatting.
Project-specific needs that conflict with personal preferences.

working: Server builds one block with optional user_profile, response_style and user_instructions tags; the header says it is user preference, not system authority (apps/web/lib/server/user-identity.ts:160-205).

Two stored groups are read at send time: 'general' (web fields) and 'personalization' (mobile sliders and style); the comment records that mobile sliders were once stored and ignored (user-identity.ts:250-292).

Only the first active account instruction is used; web's block is read before mobile's, and a switched-off block is not a candidate (user-identity.ts:294-302; apps/web/lib/preferences/instruction-preferences.ts:55-62).

Web saves both namespaces with merge and handles version conflicts (apps/web/app/api/settings/preferences/route.ts:176-250).

established.statement: The user can write custom instructions on the surface and they apply to that surface's chats until changed or switched off.
The user can choose how the assistant communicates (tone, length, formatting) and replies follow it.
One action resets personalization (instructions, style, memory) to defaults after confirmation.
Every visible setting persists and changes behaviour; read or save failures expose retry; account switches invalidate cached preferences.
Saved instructions reach the model in a block wrapped in user_instructions tags.

acceptance_criteria: After saving instructions on web, the next Cloud chat request carries a block containing the text inside user_instructions tags.
Switching 'Apply instructions for AGI' off keeps the text and removes it from the next request.

Empty fields send no block (the function returns null).
A failed save shows 'Your personalization was not saved.' and Retry works.
'Reset response style' returns the style, length, level, formatting, language and trait fields to defaults.
/personalize set length shorter changes the stored value and /personalize show displays 'shorter'.
A Local or BYOK CLI session refuses /personalize.

steps.what_happens: Person edits fields; web autosaves two groups, 'general' and 'personalization', after 400 ms.
Server merges the patch into user_settings with a version check and returns the saved value.
On the next Cloud message the server reads both groups and the project's opt-out and builds the block.
The block is added to the model request and the model replies; the block is skipped for the api surface or when personalization is false.
On-device model chats on web and desktop fetch the block from the server (cached 60 s) and add it locally.
Mobile Local mode builds the block from the on-device settings with no network.

features.summary: On web and desktop, a person picks a preset style and length for one chat from the composer, or creates a named custom style with a pasted writing sample. purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person choose per chat a style (Default, Concise, Explanatory, Learning, Formal or a custom one) and length (Brief, Default, Thorough). A custom style carries a name, an instruction and an optional writing sample of up to 1200 characters (apps/web/features/chat/stores/style-store.ts:20-38,348).
purpose.why_it_exists: People want replies in their own voice, as Claude's styles feature allows, without rewriting instructions.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web and Desktop (hosted web) chat users.

features.summary: The assistant keeps short facts about the person and adds the relevant ones to later chats. The person can view, add, edit, delete, export, switch off, exclude terms, choose per project whether account memory applies, and import from another assistant. Temporary chats do not use memory. Coverage differs by app.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores memories per account (or per project or device), selects up to 30 and 8000 characters for each turn, and gives controls to manage them (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:67-71; apps/web/lib/services/turn-context-service.ts:124-127).
purpose.why_it_exists: Continuity across chats, as in Claude and ChatGPT memory (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:754-766).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using Cloud chat on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome; Mobile Local users with device-only memory.
problems_solved: Repeating facts about oneself.
Unwanted memories: delete, exclude, reset.
Moving over from another assistant.
use_cases: Add 'I use metric units' and see it used next chat.
Switch memory off for a month and keep the stored facts.
Make a project use only its own memories.
Import a list exported from another assistant.

established.statement: The user can see, add, edit and delete saved memories, turn memory on or off, and memories are used in that surface's chats.
The user can choose per project whether project chats also use account-wide memories or only the project's.
The user can import memories exported from another assistant and they become saved memories.
Memory add, edit, pin, exclude, pause, delete and import persist and affect the next applicable turn; project-only facts stay in their project; temporary chats neither read nor write memory.
Each memory entry needs scope, provenance, update time, user controls, deletion, export and incognito exclusion.
Temporary chats must not update or reference memory unless the user explicitly changes that behaviour.

With memory off, no memory block is sent and stored facts remain.
In a temporary chat no memory is read or written.
A dry-run import writes nothing; commit writes selected items with imported source and reports counts.
Items matching a never-remember term are excluded and counted.
A project with 'Use memories from outside this project' off sees only that project's memories.
A workspace that disallows memory disables the toggles and sends no memory.
CLI 'agi memory off' stops memory in Local and BYOK sessions on the same machine.

[inferred] The mobile cloud project memory choice applies on the server for chats created from mobile since the server reads the project flag.

features.summary: When switched on, the assistant can pull short excerpts from the person's other chats to answer a new question. Temporary chats are never used. It is off unless the person turns it on, needs memory not to be switched off, and is available on web, desktop and mobile; CLI and VS Code have none; Chrome is unknown.

purpose.what_it_does: Searches the person's earlier chats for text related to the new question and adds up to three short excerpts to the model request, with sources shown (apps/web/lib/services/past-chat-context-service.ts:459-493; apps/web/lib/services/__tests__/past-chat-context-service.test.ts:81).
purpose.why_it_exists: Continuity without re-explaining, like Claude's chat search and ChatGPT's chat history reference (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:754-766).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web, Desktop and Mobile users.
problems_solved: Having to paste earlier answers back in.
Control: the person can turn it off, and temporary chats stay out.
use_cases: Ask 'what did we decide about the budget last week?'
Switch it off before a sensitive chat.
Use in a project and see only that project's chats when account memory is off for it.

Mobile: Settings > Assistant > Memory > 'Search and reference chats' (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/components/MemoryControlsCard.tsx:75).
Chrome: no past-chat switch found in apps/extension/src (grep returned nothing); brief says done, so unknown.
CLI and VS Code: none.
prerequisites: Signed in for Cloud chats; Mobile Local uses on-device history. Memory must not be switched off at the chat level (memoryEnabled !== false) (turn-context-service.ts:128-129).
screens_and_controls: Web switch with description 'Let the assistant look up excerpts from your other conversations when answering. Never used in temporary chats.' (MemorySection.tsx:408-415).

Citation list on web replies (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/__tests__/CitationPastChats.test.tsx).

settings: capabilities.searchPastChats; workspace context policy can withdraw it (turn-context-service.ts:189).

Project chats are confined to their own project when global memory is off for the project (past-chat-context-service.test.ts:53).
Search and retrieval endpoints exclude temporary chats (apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts:324,375; apps/web/lib/services/retrieval-search-service.ts:270,363).
Mobile Cloud: the server assembles it (chatExecutionStore.ts:2800); mobile Local searches on-device history with no network call (apps/mobile/__tests__/past-chat-context.test.ts:98).

not_available: CLI: missing (brief).

features.summary: A temporary chat is not saved to history or search, does not use or write memory, and is removed after 30 days if any trace remains. On web the person can make new chats temporary by default (per browser). There is no general off switch for history on web. CLI has a history setting and flag; Chrome and mobile have per-chat toggles.

purpose.what_it_does: Marks a chat as temporary at creation so the server refuses to store its messages, search and memory skip it, and sharing is refused (apps/web/lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts:1-23; apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/persist-message.ts:80).
purpose.why_it_exists: People want private one-off chats, like ChatGPT temporary chat and Claude incognito (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:765).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone on Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI and Chrome. VS Code has none found.
problems_solved: Sensitive questions that should leave no history or memory.
Remembering to switch it on each time (web default).
use_cases: Turn on 'Start new chats as temporary' and chat privately by default.
Open one incognito chat from the composer.
Run the CLI with --no-session-persistence for one run.
Tap the eye icon on the phone to start a temporary chat.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: Settings > Privacy > 'Start new chats as temporary' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PrivacySection.tsx:717-726); composer menu 'Use incognito' / 'Exit incognito' (apps/web/lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts:3,5; test ChatComposerNew.temporaryChat.test.tsx:100).

Mobile: eye icon 'Enable temporary chat' in chat (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/TemporaryChatToggle.tsx:49); explainer banner with a 'Personalized' switch in Cloud mode (TemporaryChatBanner.tsx:17-18,100-110).
CLI: flag --no-session-persistence and config key history or keep-history (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:433; config.rs:205,1459,1528).
Chrome: temporary chat in the side panel (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:8939) labelled 'Temporary chat'.
VS Code: none found.
prerequisites: Web default is not available inside a project: project chats are saved (temporary-chat-policy.ts:56-66).
screens_and_controls: Web Privacy switch with text 'Not saved to history or search, and deleted after 30 days. Project chats are saved.' (PrivacySection.tsx:717-722).
Web end action 'End temporary chat' with confirm 'End and discard' (temporary-chat-policy.ts:40-51).
Mobile alert 'Turn on temporary chat?' with Cancel and 'Turn on' (TemporaryChatToggle.tsx:29-32).
Chrome notice with 'Turn off', 'End temporary chat', 'End and discard', 'Keep chatting' (_locales/en/messages.json lines 2230-2263).
journey: Web default: flip the Privacy switch; new non-project chats are created as temporary.
Or arm temporary chat for one chat from the composer.
Send messages; none are saved; a banner or label shows the state.
Ending a temporary chat discards it with no recovery.
feedback_and_outputs: Retention text on web: 'Won't be saved to your history or show up in search, and skips memory. Files you attach stay out of your Library, and a connector asks before every call even where you saved Always allow.' (temporary-chat-policy.ts:20-30).

Mobile cloud explainer 'Won't appear in history or use memory, and is normally deleted after 30 days.'; Local explainer 'Won't be saved or use memory, and attachments never leave this device.' (TemporaryChatBanner.tsx:12-15).
settings: Web newChatsTemporary (default false) in browser storage agiworkforce-web-settings (shared/stores/web-settings-store.ts:128,210).
Mobile temporaryChatPersonalized default true; isTemporaryChat is session only (apps/mobile/stores/settingsStore.ts:137-138,170).
CLI default.keep_history.

working: Web sends isTemporary at conversation creation when the default is on (apps/web/lib/hooks/useConversations.ts:645; WebChatPage.tsx:2468; desktop task runner use-dispatch-task-runner.ts:93).

Server refuses to store messages of a temporary conversation with the conflict 'Messages in a temporary chat are not saved.' (persist-message.ts:80; temporary-chat-policy.ts:10); the free-quota path returns early the same way (apps/web/lib/server/persist-free-offering-user.ts:33).
Search, list and retrieval filter temporary chats (conversations route test; apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts:324,375; retrieval-search-service.ts:270,363).
Memory and past-chat sources are withheld for temporary turns (turn-context-service.ts:124-130).
A nightly job deletes temporary chats and their files after 30 days, except under a legal hold (apps/web/app/api/cron/purge-temporary-chats/route.ts:24,38-47).
Projects refuse temporary chats; local-model chats are temporary (temporary-chat-policy.ts:53-58).
Mobile temporary toggle with confirmation, cloud 'Personalized' switch that sends personalization false when off (chatExecutionStore.ts:3453-3455); memory not read (chatExecutionStore.ts:2797-2798).
CLI: with keep_history false or the flag, sessions do not persist (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6068-6077,6198-6200).
Chrome: temporary chat per chat, deleting the server conversation on end if one exists (side_panel.ts:8959-8970).
incomplete: Web default is per browser: it lives in localStorage and is not saved to the account (web-settings-store.ts:210).
Mobile has no default-temporary preference; the toggle resets each session (settingsStore.ts:137,170).
Chrome has a per-chat toggle only; brief says missing, code disagrees.
disconnected_or_disabled: A web 'rememberChats' history switch was removed because nothing read it; the Privacy section says so in a code comment (PrivacySection.tsx:690-701; test temporary-by-default.test.ts).
not_available: A general 'keep chats in history' off switch for Cloud chats on web, desktop, mobile (use temporary chat instead).
VS Code temporary or history control (none found; brief says missing).

established.statement: The user can choose whether chats are kept in history (and synced) or not saved.
The user can make new chats temporary by default (not saved, not used for memory) and the preference is honoured.
Consent and temporary-chat choices affect the next applicable request.
Temporary chats neither read nor write memory.
A temporary chat and its attachments are removed after 30 days.

acceptance_criteria: With the web default on, a new non-project chat is created with isTemporary true and its first message is never stored.
Posting a message to a temporary conversation through the message endpoint returns a conflict.
A temporary chat does not appear in conversation list, title search or /api/search.
Memory and past-chat excerpts are absent from a temporary turn.
In a project, new chats are saved even with the default on.
The purge job removes a temporary chat older than 30 days and keeps one under legal hold.
CLI run with --no-session-persistence writes no session state.
Mobile temporary chat asks before turning on and shows the explainer.
inferred: [inferred] On the web the default does not follow the person to another browser, unlike account settings.
proposed: [proposed] Save the default to the account so it follows across browsers.
[proposed] Add a default-temporary preference on Mobile.
[proposed] State plainly in each app that there is no global off switch for history.

steps.what_happens: Person turns the default on; the value is stored in the browser.
When a chat is created outside a project, the client sends isTemporary true in the create call.
The server stores a conversation row flagged temporary and refuses any message write to it.
Chat turns run without saving; memory and past-chat reads are skipped.
A nightly cron deletes temporary chats older than 30 days and their files in batches.
Mobile Local temporary chats stay on the device and are not saved.
